text: In view of the success of these initial efforts, and to give more emphasis and continuity to this essential coordination, I shall request the Congress to appropriate funds for the support of an Office of Coordinator of Public Works in the Executive Office of the President.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A most significant element in our growing economy is an agriculture that is stable, prosperous and free.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The problems of our agriculture have evolved over many years and cannot be solved overnight; nevertheless, governmental actions last year hold great promise of fostering a better balance between production and markets and, consequently, a better and more stable income for our farmers.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Through vigorous administration and through new authority provided by the 83rd Congress, surplus farm products are now moving into consumption.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: From February 1953 through November 1954, the rate of increase of government-held surpluses has been reduced by our moving into use more than 2.3 billion dollars' worth of government-owned farm commodities; this amount is equal to more than seven percent of a year's production of all our farms and ranches.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Domestic consumption remains high, and farm exports will be higher than last year.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: As a result of the flexibility provided by the Agricultural Act of 1954, we can move toward less restrictive acreage controls.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Thus, farm production is gradually adjusting to markets, markets are being expanded, and stocks are moving into use.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We can now look forward to an easing of the influences depressing farm prices, to reduced government expenditures for purchase of surplus products, and to less Federal intrusion into the lives and plans of our farm people.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Agricultural programs have been redirected toward better balance, greater stability and sustained prosperity.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We are headed in the right direction.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I urgently recommend to the Congress that we continue resolutely on this road.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Greater attention must be directed to the needs of low-income farm families.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Twenty-eight per cent of our farm-operator families have net cash incomes of less than $1,000 per year.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Last year, at my request, careful studies were made of the problems of these farm people.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall later submit recommendations designed to assure the steady alleviation of their most pressing concerns.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Because drought also remains a serious agricultural problem, I shall recommend legislation to strengthen Federal disaster assistance programs.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This legislation will prescribe an improved appraisal of need, better adjustment of the various programs to local conditions, and a more equitable sharing of costs between the States and the Federal Government.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The prosperity of our small business enterprises is an indispensable element in the maintenance of our economic strength.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Creation of the Small Business Administration and recently enacted tax laws facilitating small business expansion are but two of many important steps we have taken to encourage our smaller enterprises.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I recommend that the Congress extend the Small Business Act of 1953 which is due to expire next June.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We come now to the third great purpose of our government--its concern for the health, productivity and well-being of all our people.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Every citizen wants to give full expression to his God-given talents and abilities and to have the recognition and respect accorded under our religious and political traditions.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Americans also want a good material standard of living--not simply to accumulate possessions, but to fulfill a legitimate aspiration for an environment in which their families may live meaningful and happy lives.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our people are committed, therefore, to the creation and preservation of opportunity for every citizen to lead a more rewarding life.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: They are equally committed to the alleviation of misfortune and distress among their fellow citizens.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The aspirations of most of our people can best be fulfilled through their own enterprise and initiative, without government interference.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This Administration, therefore, follows two simple rules: first, the Federal Government should perform an essential task only when it cannot otherwise be adequately performed; and second, in performing that task, our government must not impair the self-respect, freedom and incentive of the individual.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: So long as these two rules are observed, the government can fully meet its obligation without creating a dependent population or a domineering bureaucracy.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: During the past two years, notable advances were made in these functions of government.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Protection of old-age and survivors' insurance was extended to an additional ten million of our people, and the benefits were substantially increased.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Legislation was enacted to provide unemployment insurance protection to some four million additional Americans.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Stabilization of living costs and the halting of inflation protected the value of pensions and savings.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A broad program now helps to bring good homes within the reach of the great majority of our people.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: With the States, we are providing rehabilitation facilities and more clinics, hospitals, and nursing homes for patients with chronic illnesses.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Also with the States, we have begun a great and fruitful expansion in the restoration of disabled persons to employment and useful lives.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the areas of Federal responsibility, we have made historic progress in eliminating from among our people demeaning practices based on race or color.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: All of us may be proud of these achievements during the past two years.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Yet essential Federal tasks remain to be done.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: As part of our efforts to provide decent, safe and sanitary housing for low-income families, we must carry forward the housing program authorized during the 83rd Congress.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We must also authorize contracts for a firm program of 35,000 additional public housing units in each of the next two fiscal years.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This program will meet the most pressing obligations of the Federal Government into the 1958 fiscal year for planning and building public housing.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: By that time the private building industry, aided by the Housing Act of 1954, will have had the opportunity to assume its full role in providing adequate housing for our low-income families.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The health of our people is one of our most precious assets.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Preventable sickness should be prevented; knowledge available to combat disease and disability should be fully used.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Otherwise, we as a people are guilty not only of neglect of human suffering but also of wasting our national strength.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Constant advances in medical care are not available to enough of our citizens.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Clearly our nation must do more to reduce the impact of accident and disease.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Two fundamental problems confront us: first, high and ever-rising costs of health services; second, serious gaps and shortages in these services.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: By special message on January 24, I shall propose a coordinated program to strengthen and improve existing health services.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This program will continue to reject socialized medicine.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: It will emphasize individual and local responsibility.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Under it the Federal Government will neither dominate nor direct, but serve as a helpful partner.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Within this framework, the program can be broad in scope.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: My recommendations will include a Federal health reinsurance service to encourage the development of more and better voluntary health insurance coverage by private organizations.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall also recommend measures to improve the medical care of that group of our citizens who, because of need, receive Federal-State public assistance.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: These two proposals will help more of our people to meet the costs of health services.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: To reduce the gaps in these services, I shall propose: New measures to facilitate construction of needed health facilities and help reduce shortages of trained health personnel; Vigorous steps to combat the misery and national loss involved in mental illness; Improved services for crippled children and for maternal and child health; Better consumer protection under our existing pure food and drug laws; and, finally, Strengthened programs to combat the increasingly serious pollution of our rivers and streams and the growing problem of air pollution.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: These measures together constitute a comprehensive program holding rich promise for better health for all of our people.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Last year's expansion of social security coverage and our new program of improved medical care for public assistance recipients together suggest modification of the formula for Federal sharing in old age assistance payments.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I recommend modification of the formula where such payments will, in the future, supplement benefits received under the old age and survivors insurance system.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: It is the inalienable right of every person, from childhood on, to have access to knowledge.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In our form of society, this right of the individual takes on a special meaning, for the education of all our citizens is imperative to the maintenance and invigoration of America's free institutions.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Today, we face grave educational problems.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Effective and up-to-date analyses of these problems and their solutions are being carried forward through the individual State conferences and the White House Conference to be completed this year.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: However, such factors as population growth, additional responsibilities of schools, and increased and longer school attendance have produced an unprecedented classroom shortage.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This shortage is of immediate concern to all of our people.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Positive, affirmative action must be taken now.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Without impairing in any way the responsibilities of our States, localities, communities, or families, the Federal government can and should serve as an effective catalyst in dealing with this problem.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall forward a special message to the Congress on February 15, presenting an affirmative program dealing with this shortage.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: To help the States do a better and more timely job, we must strengthen their resources for preventing and dealing with juvenile delinquency.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall propose Federal legislation to assist the States to promote concerted action in dealing with this nationwide problem.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall carry forward the vigorous efforts of the Administration to improve the international control of the traffic in narcotics and, in cooperation with State and local agencies, to combat narcotic addiction in our country.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I should like to speak now of additional matters of importance to all our people and especially to our wage earners.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: During the past year certain industrial changes and the readjustment of the economy to conditions of peace brought unemployment and other difficulties to various localities and industries.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: These problems are engaging our most earnest attention.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: But for the overwhelming majority of our working people, the past year has meant good jobs.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Moreover, the earnings and savings of our wage earners are no longer depreciating in value.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Because of cooperative relations between labor and management, fewer working days were lost through strikes in 1954 than in any year in the past decade.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The outlook for our wage earners can be made still more promising by several legislative actions.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: First, in the past five years we have had economic growth which will support an increase in the Federal minimum wage.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the light of present economic conditions, I recommend its increase to ninety cents an hour.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I also recommend that many others, at present excluded, be given the protection of a minimum wage.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Second, I renew my recommendation of last year for amendment of the Labor Management Relations Act of 1947 to further the basic objectives of this statute.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I especially call to the attention of the Congress amendments dealing with the right of economic strikers to vote in representation elections and the need for equalizing the obligation under the Act to file disclaimers of Communist affiliation.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: applicable to Federal contractors.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Legislation will also be proposed respecting non-occupational disability insurance and unemployment compensation in the District of Columbia.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In considering human needs, the Federal Government must take special responsibility for citizens in its direct employ.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: On January 11 I shall propose a pay adjustment plan for civilian employees outside the Postal Field Service to correct inequities and increase individual pay rates.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall also recommend voluntary health insurance on a contributory basis for Federal employees and their dependents.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In keeping with the Group Life Insurance Act passed in the 83rd Congress, this protection should be provided on the group insurance principle and purchased from private facilities.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Also on January 11 I shall recommend a modern pay plan, including pay increases, for postal field employees.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: As part of this program, and to carry forward our progress toward elimination of the large annual postal deficit, I shall renew my request for an increase in postal rates.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Again I urge that in the future the fixing of rates be delegated to an impartial, independent body.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: More adequate training programs to equip career employees of the government to render improved public service will be recommended, as will improvements in the laws affecting employees serving on foreign assignments.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Needed improvements in survivor, disability, and retirement benefits for Federal civilian and military personnel have been extensively considered by the Committee on Retirement Policy for Federal personnel.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The Committee's proposals would strengthen and improve benefits for our career people in government, and I endorse their broad objectives.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Full contributory coverage under old-age and survivors' insurance should be made available to all Federal personnel, just as in private industry.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: For career military personnel, the protection of the old-age and survivors' insurance system would be an important and long-needed addition, especially to their present unequal and inadequate survivorship protection.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The military retirement pay system should remain separate and unchanged.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Certain adjustments in the present civilian personnel retirement systems will be needed to reflect the additional protection of old-age and survivors' insurance.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: However, these systems also are a basic part of a total compensation and should be separately and independently retained.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I also urge the Congress to approve a long overdue increase in the salaries of Members of the Congress and of the Federal judiciary to a level commensurate with their heavy responsibilities.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our concern for the individual in our country requires that we consider several additional problems.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We must continue our program to help our Indian citizens improve their lot and make their full contribution to national life.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Two years ago I advised the Congress of injustices under existing immigration laws.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Through humane administration, the Department of Justice is doing what it legally can to alleviate hardships.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Clearance of aliens before arrival has been initiated, and except for criminal offenders, the imprisonment of aliens awaiting admission or deportation has been stopped.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Certain provisions of law, however, have the effect of compelling action in respect to aliens which are inequitable in some instances and discriminatory in others.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: These provisions should be corrected in this session of the Congress.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: As the complex problems of Alaska are resolved, that Territory should expect to achieve statehood.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the meantime, there is no justification for deferring the admission to statehood of Hawaii.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I again urge approval of this measure.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We have three splendid opportunities to demonstrate the strength of our belief in the right of suffrage.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: First, I again urge that a Constitutional amendment be submitted to the States to reduce the voting age for Federal elections.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Second, I renew my request that the principle of self-government be extended and the right of suffrage granted to the citizens of the District of Columbia.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Third, I again recommend that we work with the States to preserve the voting rights of citizens in the nation's service overseas.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In our determination to keep faith with those who in the past have met the highest call of citizenship, we now have under study the system of benefits for veterans and for surviving dependents of deceased veterans and servicemen.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Studies will be undertaken to determine the need for measures to ease the readjustment to civilian life of men required to enter the armed forces for two years of service.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the advancement of the various activities which will make our civilization endure and flourish, the Federal Government should do more to give official recognition to the importance of the arts and other cultural activities.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall recommend the establishment of a Federal Advisory Commission on the Arts within the Department of Health, Education and Welfare, to advise the Federal Government on ways to encourage artistic endeavor and appreciation.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall also propose that awards of merit be established whereby we can honor our fellow citizens who make great contribution to the advancement of our civilization.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Every citizen rightly expects efficient and economical administration of these many government programs I have outlined today.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I strongly recommend extension of the Reorganization Act and the law establishing the Commission on Intergovernmental Relations, both of which expire this spring.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Thus the Congress will assure continuation of the excellent progress recently made in improving government organization and administration.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In this connection we are looking forward with great interest to the reports which will soon be going to the Congress from the Commission on Organization of the Executive Branch of the Government.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I am sure that these studies, made under the chairmanship of former President Herbert Hoover with the assistance of more than two hundred distinguished citizens, will be of great value in paving the way toward more efficiency and economy in the government.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: And now, I return to the point at which I began--the faith of our people.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The many programs here summarized are, I believe, in full keeping with their needs, interests and aspirations.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The obligations upon us are clear: To labor earnestly, patiently, prayerfully, for peace, for freedom, for justice, throughout the world; To keep our economy vigorous and free, that our people may lead fuller, happier lives; To advance, not merely by our words but by our acts, the determination of our government that every citizen shall have opportunity to develop to his fullest capacity.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: As we do these things, before us is a future filled with opportunity and hope.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: That future will be ours if in our time we keep alive the patience, the courage, the confidence in tomorrow, the deep faith, of the millions who, in years past, made and preserved us this nation.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A decade ago, in the death and desolation of European battlefields, I saw the courage and resolution, I felt the inspiration, of American youth.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In these young men I felt America's buoyant confidence and irresistible will-to-do.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In them I saw, too, a devout America, humble before God.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: And so, I know with all my heart--and I deeply believe that all Americans know--that, despite the anxieties of this divided world, our faith, and the cause in which we all believe, will surely prevail.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The opening of this new year must arouse in us all grateful thanks to a kind Providence whose protection has been ever present and whose bounty has been manifold and abundant.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The State of the Union today demonstrates what can be accomplished under God by a free people; by their vision, their understanding of national problems, their initiative, their self-reliance, their capacity for work--and by their willingness to sacrifice whenever sacrifice is needed.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the past three years, responding to what our people want their Government to do, the Congress and the Executive have done much in building a stronger, better America.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: There has been broad progress in fostering the energies of our people, in providing greater opportunity for the satisfaction of their needs, and in fulfilling their demands for the strength and security of the Republic.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our country is at peace.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our security posture commands respect.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A spiritual vigor marks our national life.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our economy, approaching the 400 billion dollar mark, is at an unparalleled level of prosperity.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The national income is more widely and fairly distributed than ever before.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The number of Americans at work has reached an all-time high.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: As a people, we are achieving consuming more, building more and investing more than ever before.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Virtually all sectors of our society are sharing in these good times.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our farm families, if we act wisely, imaginatively and promptly to strengthen our present farm programs, can also look forward to sharing equitably in the prosperity they have helped to create.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: War in Korea ended two and a half years ago.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The collective security system has been powerfully strengthened.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our defenses have been reinforced at sharply reduced costs.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Programs to expand world trade and to harness the atom for the betterment of mankind have been carried forward.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our economy has been freed from governmental wage and price controls.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Inflation has been halted; the cost of living stabilized.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Government spending has been cut by more than ten billion dollars.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Nearly three hundred thousand positions have been eliminated from the Federal payroll.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Taxes have been substantially reduced.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A balanced budget is in prospect.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Social security has been extended to ten million more Americans and unemployment insurance to four million more.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Unprecedented advances in civil rights have been made.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The long-standing and deep-seated problems of agriculture have been forthrightly attacked.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This record of progress has been accomplished with a self-imposed caution against unnecessary and unwise interference in the private affairs of our people, of their communities and of the several States.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: If we of the Executive and Legislative Branches, keeping this caution ever in mind, address ourselves to the business of the year before us-- and to the unfinished business of last year--with resolution, the outlook is bright with promise.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Many measures of great national importance recommended last year to the Congress still demand immediate attention--legislation for school and highway construction;

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Many new items of business likewise require our attention-- measures that will further promote the release of the energies of our people;

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Every political and economic guide supports a valid confidence that wise effort will be rewarded by an even more plentiful harvest of human benefit than we now enjoy.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our resources are too many, our principles too dynamic, our purposes too worthy and the issues at stake too immense for us to entertain doubt or fear.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: But our responsibilities require that we approach this year's business with a sober humility.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A heedless pride in our present strength and position would blind us to the facts of the past, to the pitfalls of the future.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We must walk ever in the knowledge that we are enriched by a heritage earned in the labor and sacrifice of our forebears;

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In this light the Administration has continued work on its program for the Republic, begun three years ago.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Because the vast spread of national and human interests is involved within it, I shall not in this Message attempt its detailed delineation.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Instead, from time to time during this Session, there will be submitted to the Congress specific recommendations within specific fields.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the comprehensive survey required for their preparation, the Administration is guided by enduring objectives.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The first is: THE DISCHARGE OF OUR WORLD RESPONSIBILITY.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our world policy and our actions are dedicated to the achievement of peace with justice for all nations.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: With this purpose, we move in a wide variety of ways and through many agencies to remove the pall of fear;  .

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: These national objectives are fully supported by both our political parties.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the past year, our search for a more stable and just peace has taken varied forms.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Among the most important were the two Conferences at Geneva, in July and in the fall of last year.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We explored the possibilities of agreement on critical issues that jeopardize the peace.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The July meeting of Heads of Government held out promise to the world of moderation in the bitterness, of word and action, which tends to generate conflict and war.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: All were in agreement that a nuclear war would be an intolerable disaster which must not be permitted to occur.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: But in October, when the Foreign Ministers met again, the results demonstrated conclusively that the Soviet leaders are not yet willing to create the indispensable conditions for a secure and lasting peace.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Nevertheless, it is clear that the conflict between international communism and freedom has taken on a new complexion.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We know the Communist leaders have often practiced the tactics of retreat and zigzag.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We know that Soviet and Chinese communism still poses a serious threat to the free world.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: And in the Middle East recent Soviet moves are hardly compatible with the reduction of international tension.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Yet Communist tactics against the free nations have shifted in emphasis from reliance on violence and the threat of violence to reliance on division, enticement and duplicity.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We must be well prepared to meet the current tactics which pose a dangerous though less obvious threat.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: At the same time, our policy must be dynamic as well as flexible, designed primarily to forward the achievement of our own objectives rather than to meet each shift and change on the Communist front.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We must act in the firm assurance that the fruits of freedom are more attractive and desirable to mankind in the pursuit of happiness than the record of Communism.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the face of Communist military power, we must, of course, continue to maintain an effective system of collective security.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This involves two things--a system which gives clear warning that armed aggression will be met by joint action of the free nations, and deterrent military power to make that warning effective.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Moreover, the awesome power of the atom must be made to serve as a guardian of the free community and of the peace.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the last year, the free world has seen major gains for the system of collective security: the accession to the North Atlantic Treaty Organization and Western European Union of the sovereign Federal German Republic;

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In our own hemisphere, the inter-American system has continued to show its vitality in maintaining peace and a common approach to world problems.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We now have security pacts with more than 40 other nations.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the pursuit of our national purposes, we have been steadfast in our support of the United Nations, now entering its second decade with a wider membership and ever-increasing influence and usefulness.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the release of our fifteen fliers from Communist China, an essential prelude was the world opinion mobilized by the General Assembly, which condemned their imprisonment and demanded their liberation.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The successful Atomic Energy Conference held in Geneva under United Nations auspices and our Atoms for Peace program have been practical steps toward the world-wide use of this new energy source.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our sponsorship of such use has benefited our relations with other countries.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Active negotiations are now in progress to create an International Agency to foster peaceful uses of atomic energy.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: During the past year the crucial problem of disarmament has moved to the forefront of practical political endeavor.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: At Geneva, I declared the readiness of the United States to exchange blueprints of the military establishments of our nation and the U.S.S.R., to be confirmed by reciprocal aerial reconnaissance.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: By this means, I felt mutual suspicions could be allayed and an atmosphere developed in which negotiations looking toward limitation of arms would have improved chances of success.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the United Nations Subcommittee on Disarmament last fall, this proposal was explored and the United States also declared itself willing to include reciprocal ground inspection of key points.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: By the overwhelming vote of 56 to 7, the United Nations on December 16 endorsed these proposals and gave them a top priority.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Thereby, the issue is placed squarely before the bar of world opinion.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We shall persevere in seeking a general reduction of armaments under effective inspection and control which are essential safeguards to ensure reciprocity and protect the security of all.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the coming year much remains to be done.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: While maintaining our military deterrent, we must intensify our efforts to achieve a just peace.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In Asia we shall continue to give help to nations struggling to maintain their freedom against the threat of Communist coercion or subversion.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In Europe we shall endeavor to increase not only the military strength of the North Atlantic Alliance but also its political cohesion and unity of purpose.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We shall give such assistance as is feasible to the recently renewed effort of Western European nations to achieve a greater measure of integration, such as in the field of peaceful uses of atomic energy.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the Near East we shall spare no effort in seeking to promote a fair solution of the tragic dispute between the Arab States and Israel, all of whom we want as our friends.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The United States is ready to do its part to assure enduring peace in that area.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We hope that both sides will make the contributions necessary to achieve that purpose.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In Latin America, we shall continue to cooperate vigorously in trade and other measures designed to assist economic progress in the area.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Strong economic ties are an essential element in our free world partnership.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Increasing trade and investment help all of us prosper together.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Gratifying progress has been made in this direction, most recently by the three-year extension of our trade agreements legislation.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I most earnestly request that the Congress approve our membership in the Organization for Trade Cooperation, which would assist the carrying out of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade to which we have been a party since 1948.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our membership in the OTC will provide the most effective and expeditious means for removing discriminations and restrictions against American exports and in making our trade agreements truly reciprocal.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: United States membership in the Organization will evidence our continuing desire to cooperate in promoting an expanded trade among the free nations.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Thus the Organization, as proposed, is admirably suited to our own interests and to those of like-minded nations in working for steady expansion of trade and closer economic cooperation.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Being strictly an administrative entity, the Organization for Trade Cooperation cannot, of course, alter the control by Congress of the tariff, import, and customs policies of the United States.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We need to encourage investment overseas by avoiding unfair tax duplications, and to foster foreign trade by further simplification and improvement of our customs legislation.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We must sustain and fortify our Mutual Security Program.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Because the conditions of poverty and unrest in less developed areas make their people a special target of international communism, there is a need to help them achieve the economic growth and stability necessary to preserve their independence against communist threats and enticements.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In order that our friends may better achieve the greater strength that is our common goal, they need assurance of continuity in economic assistance for development projects and programs which we approve and which require a period of years for planning and completion.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Accordingly, I ask Congress to grant limited authority to make longer-term commitments for assistance to such projects, to be fulfilled from appropriations to be made in future fiscal years.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: These various steps will powerfully strengthen the economic foundation of our foreign policy.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Together with constructive action abroad, they will maintain the present momentum toward general economic progress and vitality of the free world.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In all things, change is the inexorable law of life.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In much of the world the ferment of change is working strongly; but grave injustices are still uncorrected.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We must not, by any sanction of ours, help to perpetuate these wrongs.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I have particularly in mind the oppressive division of the German people, the bondage of millions elsewhere, and the exclusion of Japan from United Nations membership.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We shall keep these injustices in the forefront of human consciousness and seek to maintain the pressure of world opinion to right these vast wrongs in the interest both of justice and secure peace.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Injustice thrives on ignorance.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Because an understanding of the truth about America is one of our most powerful forces, I am recommending a substantial increase in budgetary support of the United States Information Agency.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The sum of our international effort should be this: the waging of peace, with as much resourcefulness, with as great a sense of dedication and urgency, as we have ever mustered in defense of our country in time of war.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In this effort, our weapon is not force.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our weapons are the principles and ideas embodied in our historic traditions, applied with the same vigor that in the past made America a living promise of freedom for all mankind.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: To accomplish these vital tasks, all of us should be concerned with the strength, effectiveness and morale of our State Department and our Foreign Service.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Another guide in the preparation of the Administration's program is: THE CONSTANT IMPROVEMENT OF OUR NATIONAL SECURITY.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Because peace is the keystone of our national policy, our defense program emphasizes an effective flexible type of power calculated to deter or repulse any aggression and to preserve the peace.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Short of war, we have never had military strength better adapted to our needs with improved readiness for emergency use.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The maintenance of this strong military capability for the indefinite future will continue to call for a large share of our national budget.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our military programs must meet the needs of today.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: To build less would expose the nation to aggression.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: To build excessively, under the influence of fear, could defeat our purposes and impair or destroy the very freedom and economic system our military defenses are designed to protect.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We have improved the effectiveness and combat readiness of our forces by developing and making operational new weapons and by integrating the latest scientific developments, including new atomic weapons, into our military plans.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We continue to push the production of the most modern military aircraft.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The development of long-range missiles has been on an accelerated basis for some time.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We are moving as rapidly as practicable toward nuclear-powered aircraft and ships.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Combat capability, especially in terms of firepower, has been substantially increased.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We have made the adjustments in personnel permitted by the cessation of the Korean War, the buildup of our allies and the introduction of new weapons.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The services are all planning realistically on a long-term basis.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: To strengthen our continental defenses the United States and Canada, in the closest cooperation, have substantially augmented early warning networks.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Great progress is being made in extending surveillance of the Arctic, the Atlantic and the Pacific approaches to North America.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the last analysis our real strength lies in the caliber of the men and women in our Armed Forces, active and Reserve.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Much has been done to attract and hold capable military personnel, but more needs to be done.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This year, I renew my request of last year for legislation to provide proper medical care for military dependents and a more equitable survivors' benefit program.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The Administration will prepare additional recommendations designed to achieve the same objectives, including career incentives for medical and dental officers and nurses, and increases in the proportion of regular officers.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Closely related to the mission of the Defense Department is the task of the Federal Civil Defense Administration.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A particular point of relationship arises from the fact that the key to civil defense is the expanded continental defense program, including the distant early warning system.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our Federal civil defense authorities have made progress in their program, and now comprehensive studies are being conducted jointly by the Federal Civil Defense Administration, the States, and critical target case of an atomic attack.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We must strengthen Federal assistance to the States and cities in devising the most effective common defense.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We have a broad and diversified mobilization base.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We have the facilities, materials, skills and knowledge rapidly to expand the production of things we need for our defense whenever they are required.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: But mobilization base requirements change with changing technology and strategy.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We must maintain flexibility to meet new requirements.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I am requesting, therefore, that the Congress once again extend the Defense Production Act.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Of great importance to our nation's security is a continuing alertness to internal subversive activity within or without our government.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This Administration will not relax its efforts to deal forthrightly and vigorously in protection of this government and its citizens against subversion, at the same time fully protecting the constitutional rights of all citizens.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A third objective of the Administration is: FISCAL INTEGRITY.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A public office is, indeed, a public trust.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: None of its aspects is more demanding than the proper management of the public finances.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I refer now not only to the indispensable virtues of plain honesty and trustworthiness but also to the prudent, effective and conscientious use of tax money.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I refer also to the attitude of mind that makes efficient and economical service to the people a watchword in our government.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Over the long term, a balanced budget is a sure index to thrifty management--in a home, in a business or in the Federal Government.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: When achievement of a balanced budget is for long put off in a business or home, bankruptcy is the result.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: But in similar circumstances a government resorts to inflation of the money supply.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This inevitably results in depreciation of the value of the money, and an increase in the cost of living.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Every investment in personal security is threatened by this process of inflation, and the real values of the people's savings, whether in the form of insurance, bonds, pension and retirement funds or savings accounts are thereby shriveled.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We have made long strides these past three years in bringing our Federal finances under control.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The deficit for fiscal year 1953 was almost 9 1/2 billion dollars.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Larger deficits seemed certain--deficits which would have depreciated the value of the dollar and pushed the cost of living still higher.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: But government waste and extravagance were searched out.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Nonessential activities were dropped.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Government expenses were carefully scrutinized.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Total spending was cut by 14 billion dollars below the amount planned by the previous Administration for the fiscal year 1954.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This made possible--and it was appropriate in the existing circumstances of transition to a peacetime economy--the largest tax cut in any year in our history.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Almost 7 1/2 billion dollars were released and every taxpayer in the country benefited.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Almost two-thirds of the savings went directly to individuals.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This tax cut also helped to build up the economy, to make jobs in industry and to increase the production of the many things desired to improve the scale of living for the great majority of Americans.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The strong expansion of the economy, coupled with a constant care for efficiency in government operations and an alert guard against waste and duplication, has brought us to a prospective balance between income and expenditure.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This is being done while we continue to strengthen our military security.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I expect the budget to be in balance during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1956.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall propose a balanced budget for the next fiscal year ending June 30, 1957.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: But the balance we are seeking cannot be accomplished without the continuing every-day effort of the Executive and Legislative Branches to keep expenditures under control.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: It will also be necessary to continue all of the present excise taxes without any reduction and the corporation income taxes at their present rates for another year beyond next April 1st.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: It is unquestionably true that our present tax level is very burdensome and, in the interest of long term and continuous economic growth, should be reduced when we prudently can.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: It is essential, in the sound management of the Government's finances, that we be mindful of our enormous national debt and of the obligation we have toward future Americans to reduce that debt whenever we can appropriately do so.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Under conditions of high peacetime prosperity, such as now exist, we can never justify going further into debt to give ourselves a tax cut at the expense of our children.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: So, in the present state of our financial affairs, I earnestly believe that a tax cut can be deemed justifiable only when it will not unbalance the budget, a budget which makes provision for some reduction, even though modest, in our national debt.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In this way we can best maintain fiscal integrity.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A fourth aim of our program is: TO FOSTER A STRONG ECONOMY.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our competitive enterprise system depends on the energy of free human beings, limited by prudent restraints in law, using free markets to plan, organize and distribute production, and spurred by the prospect of reward for successful effort.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This system has developed our resources.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: It has marvelously expanded our productive capacity.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Against the record of all other economic systems devised through the ages, this competitive system has proved the most creative user of human skills in the development of physical resources, and the richest rewarder of human effort.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This is still true in this era when improved living standards and rising national requirements are accompanied by swift advances in technology and rapid obsolescence in machines and methods.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Typical of these are the strides made in construction of plants to produce electrical energy from atomic power and of laboratories and installations for the application of this new force in industry, agriculture and the healing arts.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: These developments make it imperative--to assure effective functioning of our enterprise system--that the Federal Government concern itself with certain broad areas of our economic life.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Most important of these is: Agriculture.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our farm people are not sharing as they should in the general prosperity.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: They alone of all major groups have seen their incomes decline rather than rise.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: They are caught between two millstones-- rising production costs and declining prices.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Such harm to a part of the national economy so vitally important to everyone is of great concern to us all.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: No other resource is so indispensable as the land that feeds and clothes us.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: No group is more fundamental to our national life than our farmers.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In successful prosecution of the war, the nation called for the utmost effort of its farmers.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Their response was superb, their contribution unsurpassed.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Farmers are not now to be blamed for the mountainous, price-depressing surpluses produced in response to wartime policies and laws that were too long continued.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: War markets are not the markets of peacetime.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Failure to recognize that basic fact by a timely adjustment of wartime legislation brought its inevitable result in peacetime--surpluses, lower prices and lower incomes for our farmers.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The dimensions of government responsibility are as broad and complex as the farm problem itself.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We are here concerned not only with our essential continuing supplies of food and fiber, but also with a way of life.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Both are indispensable to the well-being and strength of the nation.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Consideration of these matters must be above and beyond politics.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our national farm policy, so vital to the welfare of farm people and all of us, must not become a field for political warfare.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Too much is at stake.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our farm people expect of us, who have responsibility for their government, understanding of their problems and the will to help solve them.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Our objective must be to help bring production into balance with existing and new markets, at prices that yield farmers a return for their work in line with what other Americans get.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: To reach this goal, deep-seated problems must be subjected to a stepped-up attack.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: There is no single easy solution.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Rather, there must be a many-sided assault on the stubborn problems of surpluses, prices, costs, and markets; and a steady, persistent, imaginative advance in the relationship between farmers and their government.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In a few days, by special message, I shall lay before the Congress my detailed recommendations for new steps that should be taken promptly to speed the transition in agriculture and thus assist our farmers to achieve their fair share of the national income.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Basic to this program will be a new attack on the surplus problem-- for even the best-conceived farm program cannot work under a multi-billion dollar weight of accumulated stocks.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall urge authorization of a soil bank program to alleviate the problem of diverted acres and an over-expanded agricultural plant.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This will include an acreage reserve to reduce current and accumulated surpluses of crops in most serious difficulty, and a conservation reserve to achieve other needed adjustments in the use of agricultural resources.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall urge measures to strengthen our surplus disposal activities.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall propose measures to strengthen individual commodity programs, to remove controls where possible, to reduce carryovers, and to stop further accumulations of surpluses.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall ask the Congress to provide substantial new funds for an expanded drive on the research front, to develop new markets, new crops, and new uses.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The Rural Development Program to better the lot of low-income farm families deserves full Congressional support.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The Great Plains Program must go forward vigorously.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Advances on these and other fronts will pull down the price-depressing surpluses and raise farm income.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In this time of testing in agriculture, we should all together, regardless of party, carry forward resolutely with a sound and forward looking program on which farm people may confidently depend, now and for years to come.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I shall briefly mention four other subjects directly related to the well-being of the economy, preliminary to their fuller discussion in the Economic Report and later communications.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Resources Conservation.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I wish to re-emphasize the critical importance of the wise use and conservation of our great natural resources of land, forests, minerals and water and their long-range development consistent with our agricultural policy.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Water in particular now plays an increasing role in industrial processes, in the irrigation of land, in electric power, as well as in domestic uses.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: At the same time, it has the potential of damage and disaster.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A comprehensive legislative program for water conservation will be submitted to the Congress during the Session.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The development of our water resources cannot be accomplished overnight.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The need is such that we must make faster progress and without delay.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Therefore, I strongly recommend that action be taken at this Session on such wholly Federal projects as the Colorado River Storage Project and the Fryingpan-Arkansas Project; on the John Day partnership project, and other projects which provide for cooperative action between the Federal Government and non-Federal interests; and on legislation, which makes provision for Federal participation in small projects under the primary sponsorship of agencies of State and local government.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: During the past year the areas of our National Parks have been expanded, and new wildlife refuges have been created.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The visits of our people to the Parks have increased much more rapidly than have the facilities to care for them.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The Administration will submit recommendations to provide more adequate facilities to keep abreast of the increasing interest of our people in the great outdoors.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Disaster Assistance A modern community is a complex combination of skills, specialized buildings, machines, communications and homes.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Most importantly, it involves human lives.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Disaster in many forms--by flood, frost, high winds, for instance--can destroy on a massive scale in a few hours the labor of many years.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Through the past three years the Administration has repeatedly moved into action wherever disaster struck.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The extent of State participation in relief activities, however, has been far from uniform and, in many cases, has been either inadequate or nonexistent.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Disaster assistance legislation requires overhauling and an experimental program of flood-damage indemnities should be undertaken.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The Administration will make detailed recommendations on these subjects.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Area Development: We must help deal with the pockets of chronic unemployment that here and there mar the nation's general industrial prosperity.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Economic changes in recent years have been often so rapid and far-reaching that areas committed to a single local resource or industrial activity have found themselves temporarily deprived of their markets and their livelihood.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Such conditions mean severe hardship for thousands of people as the slow process of adaptation to new circumstances goes on.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This process can be speeded up.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Last year I authorized a major study of the problem to find additional steps to supplement existing programs for the redevelopment of areas of chronic unemployment.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Recommendations will be submitted, designed to supplement, with Federal technical and loan assistance local efforts to get on with this vital job.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Improving such communities must, of course, remain the primary responsibility of the people living there and of their States.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: But a soundly conceived Federal partnership program can be of real assistance to them in their efforts.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Highway Legislation: Legislation to provide a modern, interstate highway system is even more urgent this year than last, for 12 months have now passed in which we have fallen further behind in road construction needed for the personal safety, the general prosperity, the national security of the American people.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: During the year, the number of motor vehicles has increased from 58 to 61 million.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: During the past year over 38,000 persons lost their lives in highway accidents, while the fearful toll of injuries and property damage has gone on unabated.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In my message of February 22, 1955, I urged that measures be taken to complete the vital 40,000 mile interstate system over a period of 10 years at an estimated Federal cost of approximately 25 billion dollars.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: No program was adopted.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: If we are ever to solve our mounting traffic problem, the whole interstate system must be authorized as one project, to be completed approximately within the specified time.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Only in this way can industry efficiently gear itself to the job ahead.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Only in this way can the required planning and engineering be accomplished without the confusion and waste unavoidable in a piecemeal approach.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Furthermore, as I pointed out last year, the pressing nature of this problem must not lead us to solutions outside the bounds of sound fiscal management.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: As in the case of other pressing problems, there must be an adequate plan of financing.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: To continue the drastically needed improvement in other national highway systems, I recommend the continuation of the Federal Aid Highway Program.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Aside from agriculture and the four subjects specifically mentioned, an integral part of our efforts to foster a strong and expanding free economy is keeping open the door of opportunity to new and small enterprises, checking monopoly, and preserving a competitive environment.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In this past year the steady improvement in the economic health of small business has reinforced the vitality of our competitive economy.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We shall continue to help small business concerns to obtain access to adequate financing and to competent counsel on management, production, and marketing problems.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Through measures already taken, opportunities for small-business participation in government procurement programs, including military procurement, are greatly improved.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The effectiveness of these measures will become increasingly apparent.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We shall continue to make certain that small business has a fair opportunity to compete and has an economic environment in which it may prosper.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In my message last year I referred to the appointment of an advisory committee to appraise and report to me on the deficiencies as well as the effectiveness of existing Federal transportation policies.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I have commended the fundamental purposes and objectives of the committee's report.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I earnestly recommend that the Congress give prompt attention to the committee's proposals.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Essential to a prosperous economic environment for all business, small and large--for agriculture and industry and commerce--is efficiency in Government.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: To that end, exhaustive studies of the entire governmental structure were made by the Commission on Intergovernmental Relations and the Commission on the Organization of the Executive Branch of the Government--the reports of these Commissions are now under intensive review and already in the process of implementation in important areas.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: One specific and most vital governmental function merits study and action by the Congress.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: As part of our program of promoting efficiency in Government and getting the fiscal situation in hand, the Post Office Department in the past three years has been overhauled.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Nearly one thousand new post offices have been provided.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Financial practices have been modernized, and transportation and operating methods are being constantly improved.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A new wage and incentive plan for the half million postal employees has been established.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Never before has the postal system handled so much mail so quickly and so economically.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The Post Office Department faces two serious problems.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: First, much of its physical plant--post offices and other buildings--is obsolete and inadequate.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Many new buildings and the modernization of present ones are essential if we are to have improved mail service.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The second problem is the Department's fiscal plight.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: It now faces an annual deficit of one-half billion dollars.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Recommendations on postal facilities and on additional postal revenues will be submitted to the Congress.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A final consideration in our program planning is: THE RESPONSE TO HUMAN CONCERNS.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A fundamental belief shines forth in this Republic.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We believe in the worth and dignity of the individual.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We know that if we are to govern ourselves wisely--in the tradition of America--we must have the opportunity to develop our individual capacities to the utmost.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: To fulfill the individual's aspirations in the American way of life, good education is fundamental.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Good education is the outgrowth of good homes, good communities, good churches, and good schools.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Today our schools face pressing problems--problems which will not yield to swift and easy solutions, or to any single action.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: They will yield only to a continuing, active, informed effort by the people toward achieving better schools.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This kind of effort has been spurred by the thousands of conferences held in recent months by half a million citizens and educators in all parts of the country, culminating in the White House Conference on Education.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In that Conference, some two thousand delegates, broadly representative of the nation, studied together the problems of the nation's schools.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: They concluded that the people of the United States must make a greater effort through their local, State, and Federal Governments to improve the education of our youth.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: This expression from the people must now be translated into action at all levels of government.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: So far as the Federal share of responsibility is concerned, I urge that the Congress move promptly to enact an effective program of Federal assistance to help erase the existing deficit of school classrooms.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Such a program, which should be limited to a five-year period, must operate to increase rather than decrease local and State support of schools and to give the greatest help to the States and localities with the least financial resources.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Federal aid should in no way jeopardize the freedom of local school systems.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: There will be presented to the Congress a recommended program of Federal assistance for school construction.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Such a program should be accompanied by action to increase services to the nation's schools by the Office of Education and by legislation to provide continuation of payments to school districts where Federal activities have impaired the ability of those districts to provide adequate schools.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Under the 1954 Amendments to the old-age and survivors' insurance program, protection was extended to some 10 million additional workers and benefits were increased.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The system now helps protect 9 out of 10 American workers and their families against loss of income in old age or on the death of the breadwinner.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The system is sound.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: It must be kept so.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In developing improvements in the system, we must give the most careful consideration to population and social trends, and to fiscal requirements.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: With these considerations in mind, the Administration will present its recommendations for further expansion of coverage and other steps which can be taken wisely at this time.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Other needs in the area of social welfare include increased child welfare services, extension of the program of aid to dependent children, intensified attack on juvenile delinquency, and special attention to the problems of mentally retarded children.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The training of more skilled workers for these fields and the quest for new knowledge through research in social welfare are essential.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Similarly the problems of our aged people need our attention.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The nation has made dramatic progress in conquering disease-- progress of profound human significance which can be greatly accelerated by an intensified effort in medical research.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: A well-supported, well-balanced program of research, including basic research, can open new frontiers of knowledge, prevent and relieve suffering, and prolong life.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Accordingly I shall recommend a substantial increase in Federal funds for the support of such a program.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: As an integral part of this effort, I shall recommend a new plan to aid construction of non-Federal medical research and teaching facilities and to help provide more adequate support for the training of medical research manpower.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Finally, we must aid in cushioning the heavy and rising costs of illness and hospitalization to individuals and families.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Provision should be made, by Federal reinsurance or otherwise, to foster extension of voluntary health insurance coverage to many more persons, especially older persons and those in rural areas.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Plans should be evolved to improve protection against the costs of prolonged or severe illness.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: These measures will help reduce the dollar barrier between many Americans and the benefits of modern medical care.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The Administration health program will be submitted to the Congress in detail.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The response of government to human concerns embraces, of course, other measures of broad public interest, and of special interest to our working men and women.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The need still exists for improvement of the Labor Management Relations Act.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The recommendations I submitted to the Congress last year take into account not only the interests of labor and management but also the public welfare.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The needed amendments should be enacted without further delay.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: We must also carry forward the job of improving the wage-hour law.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Last year I requested the Congress to broaden the coverage of the minimum wage.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I repeat that recommendation, and I pledge the full resources of the Executive Branch to assist the Congress in finding ways to attain this goal.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Moreover, as requested last year, legislation should be passed to clarify and strengthen the eight-hour laws for the benefit of workers who are subject to Federal wage standards on Federal and Federally-assisted construction and other public works.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The Administration will shortly propose legislation to assure adequate disclosure of the financial affairs of each employee pension and welfare plan and to afford substantial protection to their beneficiaries in accordance with the objectives outlined in my message of January 11, 1954.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Occupational safety still demands attention, as I pointed out last year, and legislation to improve the Longshoremen's and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act is still needed.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The improvement of the District of Columbia Unemployment Insurance Law and legislation to provide employees in the District with non-occupational disability insurance are no less necessary now than 12 months ago.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Legislation to apply the principle of equal pay for equal work without discrimination because of sex is a matter of simple justice.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I earnestly urge the Congress to move swiftly to implement these needed labor measures.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: In the field of human needs, we must carry forward the housing program, which is contributing so greatly to the well-being of our people and the prosperity of our economy.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: Home ownership is now advanced to the point where almost three of every five families in our cities, towns, and suburbs own the houses they live in.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: For the housing program, most of the legislative authority already exists.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: However, a firm program of public housing is essential until the private building industry has found ways to provide more adequate housing for low-income families.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: The Administration will propose authority to contract for 35 thousand additional public housing units in each of the next 2 fiscal years for communities which will participate in an integrated attack on slums and blight.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: To meet the needs of the growing number of older people, several amendments to the National Housing Act will be proposed to assist the private homebuilding industry as well as charitable and non-profit organizations.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: With so large a number of the American people desiring to modernize and improve existing dwellings, I recommend that the Title I program for permanent improvements in the home be liberalized.

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
text: I recommend increases in the general FHA mortgage insurance authority;

speaker: Dwight D. Eisenhower
