text: No longer can anyone wonder whether we are in the grip of historical decay.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We know that history is ours to make.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And if there is great danger, there is now also the excitement of great expectations.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: America and the communist nations:Yet we still live in a troubled and perilous world.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: There is no longer a single threat.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: There are many.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: They differ in intensity and in danger.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: They require different attitudes and different answers.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: With the Soviet Union we seek peaceful understandings that can lessen the danger to freedom.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Last fall I asked the American people to choose that course.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will carry forward their command.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: If we are to live together in peace, we must come to know each other better.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I am sure that the American people would welcome a chance to listen to the Soviet leaders on our television--as I would like the Soviet people to hear our leaders on theirs.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I hope the new Soviet leaders can visit America so they can learn about our country at firsthand.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In Eastern Europe restless nations are slowly beginning to assert their identity.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Your Government, assisted by the leaders in American labor and business, is now exploring ways to increase peaceful trade with these countries and with the Soviet Union.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will report our conclusions to the Congress.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In Asia, communism wears a more aggressive face.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We see that in Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Why are we there?

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We are there, first, because a friendly nation has asked us for help against the Communist aggression.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Ten years ago our President pledged our help.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Three Presidents have supported that pledge.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will not break it now.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Second, our own security is tied to the peace of Asia.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Twice in one generation we have had to fight against aggression in the Far East.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: To ignore aggression now would only increase the danger of a much larger war.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Our goal is peace in southeast Asia.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: That will come only when aggressors leave their neighbors in peace.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: What is at stake is the cause of freedom and in that cause America will never be found wanting.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The Non-Communist World:But communism is not the only source of trouble and unrest.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: There are older and deeper sources--in the misery of nations and in man's irrepressible ambition for liberty and a better life.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: With the free Republics of Latin America I have always felt--and my country has always felt--very special ties of interest and affection.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It will be the purpose of my administration to strengthen these ties.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Together we share and shape the destiny of the new world.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In the coming year I hope to pay a visit to Latin America.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And I will steadily enlarge our commitment to the Alliance for Progress as the instrument of our war against poverty and injustice in this hemisphere.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In the Atlantic community we continue to pursue our goal of 20 years--a Europe that is growing in strength, unity, and cooperation with America.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: A great unfinished task is the reunification of Germany through self-determination.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This European policy is not based on any abstract design.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It is based on the realities of common interests and common values, common dangers and common expectations.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: These realities will continue to have their way--especially, I think, in our expanding trade and especially in our common defense.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Free Americans have shaped the policies of the United States.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And because we know these realities, those policies have been, and will be, in the interest of Europe.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Free Europeans must shape the course of Europe.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And, for the same reasons, that course has been, and will be, in our interest and in the interest of freedom.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I found this truth confirmed in my talks with European leaders in the last year.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I hope to repay these visits to some of our friends in Europe this year.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In Africa and Asia we are witnessing the turbulent unfolding of new nations and continents.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We welcome them to the society of nations.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We are committed to help those seeking to strengthen their own independence, and to work most closely with those governments dedicated to the welfare of all of their people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We seek not fidelity to an iron faith, but a diversity of belief as varied as man himself.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We seek not to extend the power of America but the progress of humanity.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We seek not to dominate others but to strengthen the freedom of all people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will seek new ways to use our knowledge to help deal with the explosion in world population and the growing scarcity in world resources.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Finally, we renew our commitment to the continued growth and the effectiveness of the United Nations.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The frustrations of the United Nations are a product of the world that we live in, and not of the institution which gives them voice.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It is far better to throw these differences open to the assembly of nations than to permit them to fester in silent danger.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: These are some of the goals of the American Nation in the world in which we live.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For ourselves we seek neither praise nor blame, neither gratitude nor obedience.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We seek peace.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We seek freedom.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We seek to enrich the life of man.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For that is the world in which we will flourish and that is the world that we mean for all men to ultimately have.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Toward the Great Society: World affairs will continue to call upon our energy and our courage.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But today we can turn increased attention to the character of American life.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We are in the midst of the greatest upward surge of economic well-being in the history of any nation.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Our flourishing progress has been marked by price stability that is unequalled in the world.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Our balance of payments deficit has declined and the soundness of our dollar is unquestioned.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I pledge to keep it that way and I urge business and labor to cooperate to that end.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We worked for two centuries to climb this peak of prosperity.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But we are only at the beginning of the road to the Great Society.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Ahead now is a summit where freedom from the wants of the body can help fulfill the needs of the spirit.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We built this Nation to serve its people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We want to grow and build and create, but we want progress to be the servant and not the master of man.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We do not intend to live in the midst of abundance, isolated from neighbors and nature, confined by blighted cities and bleak suburbs, stunted by a poverty of learning and an emptiness of leisure.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The Great Society asks not how much, but how good; not only how to create wealth but how to use it; not only how fast we are going, but where we are headed.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It proposes as the first test for a nation: the quality of its people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This kind of society will not flower spontaneously from swelling riches and surging power.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It will not be the gift of government or the creation of presidents.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It will require of every American, for many generations, both faith in the destination and the fortitude to make the journey.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And like freedom itself, it will always be challenge and not fulfillment.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And tonight we accept that challenge.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: A National Agenda: I propose that we begin a program in education to ensure every American child the fullest development of his mind and skills.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I propose that we begin a massive attack on crippling and killing diseases.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I propose that we launch a national effort to make the American city a better and a more stimulating place to live.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I propose that we increase the beauty of America and end the poisoning of our rivers and the air that we breathe.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I propose that we carry out a new program to develop regions of our country that are now suffering from distress and depression.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I propose that we make new efforts to control and prevent crime and delinquency.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I propose that we eliminate every remaining obstacle to the right and the opportunity to vote.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I propose that we honor and support the achievements of thought and the creations of art.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I propose that we make an all-out campaign against waste and inefficiency.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The Task: Our basic task is threefold: First, to keep our economy growing;

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: to open for all Americans the opportunity that is now enjoyed by most Americans;

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: and to improve the quality of life for all.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In the next 6 weeks I will submit special messages with detailed proposals for national action in each of these areas.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Tonight I would like just briefly to explain some of my major recommendations in the three main areas of national need.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I. A GROWING ECONOMY BASIC POLICIES.First, we must keep our Nation prosperous.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We seek full employment opportunity for every American citizen.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will present a budget designed to move the economy forward.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: More money will be left in the hands of the consumer by a substantial cut in excise taxes.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will continue along the path toward a balanced budget in a balanced economy.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I confidently predict--what every economic sign tells us tonight-- the continued flourishing of the American economy.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But we must remember that fear of a recession can contribute to the fact of a recession.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The knowledge that our Government will, and can, move swiftly will strengthen the confidence of investors and business.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Congress can reinforce this confidence by insuring that its procedures permit rapid action on temporary income tax cuts.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And special funds for job-creating public programs should be made available for immediate use if recession threatens.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Our continued prosperity demands continued price stability.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Business, labor, and the consumer all have a high stake in keeping wages and prices within the framework of the guideposts that have already served the Nation so well.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Finding new markets abroad for our goods depends on the initiative of American business.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But we stand ready--with credit and other help--to assist the flow of trade which will benefit the entire Nation.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: On The Farms: Our economy owes much to the efficiency of our farmers.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We must continue to assure them the opportunity to earn a fair reward.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I have instructed the Secretary of Agriculture to lead a major effort to find new approaches to reduce the heavy cost of our farm programs and to direct more of our effort to the small farmer who needs the help the most.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Increased Prosperity: We can help insure continued prosperity through:--a regional recovery program to assist the development of stricken areas left behind by our national progress;

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: further efforts to provide our workers with the skills demanded by modern technology, for the laboring-man is an indispensable force in the American system;

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: the extension of the minimum wage to more than 2 million unprotected workers;

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The improvement and The modernization of The unemployment compensation system.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And as pledged in our 1960 and 1964 Democratic platforms, I will propose to Congress changes in the Taft-Hartley Act including section 14(b).

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will do so hoping to reduce the conflicts that for several years have divided Americans in various States of our Union.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In a country that spans a continent modern transportation is vital to continued growth.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Transportation for Growth: I will recommend heavier reliance on competition in transportation and a new policy for our merchant marine.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will ask for funds to study high-speed rail transportation between urban centers.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will begin with test projects between Washington and Boston.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: On high-speed trains, passengers could travel this distance in less than 4 hours.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Opportunity for all: Second, we must open opportunity to all our people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Most Americans enjoy a good life.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But far too many are still trapped in poverty and idleness and fear.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Let a just nation throw open to them the city of promise: --to the elderly, by providing hospital care under social security and by raising benefit payments to those struggling to maintain the dignity of their later years;

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: to the poor and the unfortunate, through doubling the war against poverty this year;

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: to Negro Americans, through enforcement of the civil rights law and elimination of barriers to the right to vote;

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: to those in other lands that are seeking the promise of America, through an immigration law based on the work a man can do and not where he was born or how he spells his name.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: To Enrich the Life of All: Our third goal is to improve the quality of American life.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Through Education: We begin with learning.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Every child must have the best education that this Nation can provide.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Thomas Jefferson said that no nation can be both ignorant and free.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Today no nation can be both ignorant and great.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In addition to our existing programs, I will recommend a new program for schools and students with a first year authorization of $1,500 million.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It will help at every stage along the road to learning.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For the preschool years we will help needy children become aware of the excitement of learning.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For the primary and secondary school years we will aid public schools serving low-income families and assist students in both public and private schools.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For the college years we will provide scholarships to high school students of the greatest promise and the greatest need and we will guarantee low-interest loans to students continuing their college studies.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: New laboratories and centers will help our schools--help them lift their standards of excellence and explore new methods of teaching.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: These centers will provide special training for those who need and those who deserve special treatment.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Through Better Health: Greatness requires not only an educated people but a healthy people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Our goal is to match the achievements of our medicine to the afflictions of our people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We already carry on a large program in this country for research and health.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In addition, regional medical centers can provide the most advanced diagnosis and treatment for heart disease and cancer and stroke and other major diseases.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: New support for medical and dental education will provide the trained people to apply our knowledge.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Community centers can help the mentally ill and improve health care for school-age children from poor families, including services for the mentally retarded.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Through Improving the World We Live in: The City An educated and healthy people require surroundings in harmony with their hopes.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In our urban areas the central problem today is to protect and restore man's satisfaction in belonging to a community where he can find security and significance.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The first step is to break old patterns--to begin to think and work and plan for the development of the entire metropolitan areas.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will take this step with new programs of help for the basic community facilities and for neighborhood centers of health and recreation.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: New and existing programs will be open to those cities which work together to develop unified long-range policies for metropolitan areas.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We must also make some very important changes in our housing programs if we are to pursue these same basic goals.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: So a Department of Housing and Urban Development will be needed to spearhead this effort in our cities.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Every citizen has the right to feel secure in his home and on the streets of his community.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: To help control crime, we will recommend programs: to train local law enforcement officers;

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: to put the best techniques of modern science at their disposal;

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: to discover the causes of crime and better ways to prevent it.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will soon assemble a panel of outstanding experts of this Nation to search out answers to the national problem of crime and delinquency, and I welcome the recommendations and the constructive efforts of the Congress.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The Beauty of America For over three centuries the beauty of America has sustained our spirit and has enlarged our vision.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We must act now to protect this heritage.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In a fruitful new partnership with the States and the cities the next decade should be a conservation milestone.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We must make a massive effort to save the countryside and to establish--as a green legacy for tomorrow--more large and small parks, more seashores and open spaces than have been created during any other period in our national history.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: A new and substantial effort must be made to landscape highways to provide places of relaxation and recreation wherever our roads run.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Within our cities imaginative programs are needed to landscape streets and to transform open areas into places of beauty and recreation.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will seek legal power to prevent pollution of our air and water before it happens.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will step up our effort to control harmful wastes, giving first priority to the cleanup of our most contaminated rivers.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will increase research to learn much more about the control of pollution.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We hope to make the Potomac a model of beauty here in the Capital, and preserve unspoiled stretches of some of our waterways with a Wild Rivers bill.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: More ideas for a beautiful America will emerge from a White House Conference on Natural Beauty which I will soon call.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Art and Science We must also recognize and encourage those who can be pathfinders for the Nation's imagination and understanding.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: To help promote and honor creative achievements, I will propose a National Foundation on the Arts.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: To develop knowledge which will enrich our lives and ensure our progress, I will recommend programs to encourage basic science, particularly in the universities--and to bring closer the day when the oceans will supply our growing need for fresh water.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The Government: For government to serve these goals it must be modern in structure, efficient in action, and ready for any emergency.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I am busy, currently, reviewing the structure of the entire executive branch of this Government.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I hope to reshape it and to reorganize it to meet more effectively the tasks of the 20th century.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Wherever waste is found, I will eliminate it.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Last year we saved almost $3,500 million by eliminating waste in the National Government.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And I intend to do better this year.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And very soon I will report to you on our progress and on new economies that your Government plans to make.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Even the best of government is subject to the worst of hazards.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will propose laws to insure the necessary continuity of leadership should the President become disabled or die.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In addition, I will propose reforms in the electoral college-- leaving undisturbed the vote by States--but making sure that no elector can substitute his will for that of the people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Last year, in a sad moment, I came here and I spoke to you after 33 years of public service, practically all of them here on this Hill.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This year I speak after 1 year as President of the United States.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Many of you in this Chamber are among my oldest friends.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have shared many happy moments and many hours of work, and we have watched many Presidents together.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Yet, only in the White House can you finally know the full weight of this Office.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The greatest burden is not running the huge operations of government-- or meeting daily troubles, large and small--or even working with the Congress.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: A President's hardest task is not to do what is right, but to know what is right.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Yet the Presidency brings no special gift of prophecy or foresight.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: You take an oath, you step into an office, and you must then help guide a great democracy.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The answer was waiting for me in the land where I was born.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It was once barren land.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The angular hills were covered with scrub cedar and a few large live oaks.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Little would grow in that harsh caliche soil of my country.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And each spring the Pedernales River would flood our valley.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But men came and they worked and they endured and they built.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And tonight that country is abundant; abundant with fruit and cattle and goats and sheep, and there are pleasant homes and lakes and the floods are gone.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Why did men come to that once forbidding land? Well, they were restless, of course, and they had to be moving on.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But there was more than that.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: There was a dream--a dream of a place where a free man could build for himself, and raise his children to a better life--a dream of a continent to be conquered, a world to be won, a nation to be made.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Remembering this, I knew the answer.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: A President does not shape a new and personal vision of America.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: He collects it from the scattered hopes of the American past.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It existed when the first settlers saw the coast of a new world, and when the first pioneers moved westward.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It has guided us every step of the way.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It sustains every President.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But it is also your inheritance and it belongs equally to all the people that we all serve.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It must be interpreted anew by each generation for its own needs; as I have tried, in part, to do tonight.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: a more perfect union.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This, then, is the state of the Union: Free and restless, growing and full of hope.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: So it was in the beginning.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: So it shall always be, while God is willing, and we are strong enough to keep the faith.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I come before you tonight to report on the State of the Union for the third time

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I come here to thank you and to add my tribute, once more, to the Nation's gratitude for this, the 89th Congress.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This Congress has already reserved for itself an honored chapter in the history of America.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Our Nation tonight is engaged in a brutal and bitter conflict in Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Later on I want to discuss that struggle in some detail with you.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It just must be the center of our concerns.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But we will not permit those who fire upon us in Vietnam to win a victory over the desires and the intentions of all the American people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This Nation is mighty enough, its society is healthy enough, its people are strong enough, to pursue our goals in the rest of the world while still building a Great Society here at home.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And that is what I have come here to ask of you tonight.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I recommend that you provide the resources to carry forward, with full vigor, the great health and education programs that you enacted into law last year.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I recommend that we prosecute with vigor and determination our war on poverty.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I recommend that you give a new and daring direction to our foreign aid program, designed to make a maximum attack on hunger and disease and ignorance in those countries that are determined to help themselves, and to help those nations that are trying to control population growth.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I recommend that you make it possible to expand trade between the United States and Eastern Europe and the Soviet Union.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I recommend to you a program to rebuild completely, on a scale never before attempted, entire central and slum areas of several of our cities in America.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I recommend that you attack the wasteful and degrading poisoning of our rivers, and, as the cornerstone of this effort, clean completely entire large river basins.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I recommend that you meet the growing menace of crime in the streets by building up law enforcement and by revitalizing the entire Federal system from prevention to probation.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I recommend that you take additional steps to insure equal justice to all of our people by effectively enforcing nondiscrimination in Federal and State jury selection, by making it a serious Federal crime to obstruct public and private efforts to secure civil rights, and by outlawing discrimination in the sale and rental of housing.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I recommend that you help me modernize and streamline the Federal Government by creating a new Cabinet level Department of Transportation and reorganizing several existing agencies.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In turn, I will restructure our civil service in the top grades so that men and women can easily be assigned to jobs where they are most needed, and ability will be both required as well as rewarded.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will ask you to make it possible for Members of the House of Representatives to work more effectively in the service of the Nation through a constitutional amendment extending the term of a Congressman to 4 years, concurrent with that of the President.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Because of Vietnam we cannot do all that we should, or all that we would like to do.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will ruthlessly attack waste and inefficiency.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will make sure that every dollar is spent with the thrift and with the commonsense which recognizes how hard the taxpayer worked in order to earn it.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will continue to meet the needs of our people by continuing to develop the Great Society.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Last year alone the wealth that we produced increased $47 billion, and it will soar again this year to a total over $720 billion.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Because our economic policies have produced rising revenues, if you approve every program that I recommend tonight, our total budget deficit will be one of the lowest in many years.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It will be only $18 billion next year.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Total spending in the administrative budget will be $1128 billion.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Revenues next year will be $111 billion.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: On a cash basis--which is the way that you and I keep our family budget--the Federal budget next year will actually show a surplus.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: That is to say, if we include all the money that your Government will take in and all the money that your Government will spend, your Government next year will collect one-half billion dollars more than it will spend in the year 1967.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I have not come here tonight to ask for pleasant luxuries or for idle pleasures.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I have come here to recommend that you, the representatives of the richest Nation on earth, you, the elected servants of a people who live in abundance unmatched on this globe, you bring the most urgent decencies of life to all of your fellow Americans.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: There are men who cry out: We must sacrifice.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Well, let us rather ask them: Who will they sacrifice?

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Are they going to sacrifice the children who seek the learning, or the sick who need medical care, or the families who dwell in squalor now brightened by the hope of home?

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Will they sacrifice opportunity for the distressed, the beauty of our land, the hope of our poor?

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Time may require further sacrifices.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And if it does, then we will make them.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But we will not heed those who wring it from the hopes of the unfortunate here in a land of plenty.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I believe that we can continue the Great Society while we fight in Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But if there are some who do not believe this, then, in the name of justice, let them call for the contribution of those who live in the fullness of our blessing, rather than try to strip it from the hands of those that are most in need.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And let no one think that the unfortunate and the oppressed of this land sit stifled and alone in their hope tonight.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Hundreds of their servants and their protectors sit before me tonight here in this great Chamber.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The Great Society leads us along three roads-growth and justice and liberation.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: (1) First is growth-the national prosperity which supports the well-being of our people and which provides the tools of our progress.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I can report to you tonight what you have seen for yourselves already-in every city and countryside.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This Nation is flourishing.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Workers are making more money than ever-with after-tax income in the past 5 years up 33 percent; in the last year alone, up 8 percent.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: More people are working than ever before in our history-an increase last year of 2 1/2 million jobs.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Corporations have greater after-tax earnings than ever in history.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For the past 5 years those earnings have been up over 65 percent, and last year alone they had a rise of 20 percent.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Average farm income is higher than ever.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Over the past 5 years it is up 40 percent, and over the past year it is up 22 percent alone.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I was informed this afternoon by the distinguished Secretary of the Treasury that his preliminary estimates indicate that our balance of payments deficit has been reduced from $28 billion in 1964 to $13 billion, or less, in 1965.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This achievement has been made possible by the patriotic voluntary cooperation of businessmen and bankers working with your Government.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We must now work together with increased urgency to wipe out this balance of payments deficit altogether in the next year.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And as our economy surges toward new heights we must increase our vigilance against the inflation which raises the cost of living and which lowers the savings of every family in this land.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It is essential, to prevent inflation, that we ask both labor and business to exercise price and wage restraint, and I do so again tonight.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I believe it desirable, because of increased military expenditures, that you temporarily restore the automobile and certain telephone excise tax reductions made effective only 12 days ago.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Without raising taxes-or even increasing the total tax bill paid-we should move to improve our withholding system so that Americans can more realistically pay as they go, speed up the collection of corporate taxes, and make other necessary simplifications of the tax structure at an early date.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I hope these measures will be adequate.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But if the necessities of Vietnam require it, I will not hesitate to return to the Congress for additional appropriations, or additional revenues if they are needed.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: (2) The second road is justice.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Justice means a man's hope should not be limited by the color of his skin.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I propose legislation to establish unavoidable requirements for nondiscriminatory jury selection in Federal and State courts-and to give the Attorney General the power necessary to enforce those requirements.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I propose legislation to strengthen authority of Federal courts to try those who murder, attack, or intimidate either civil rights workers or others exercising their constitutional rights-and to increase penalties to a level equal to the nature of the crime.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Legislation, resting on the fullest constitutional authority of the Federal Government, to prohibit racial discrimination in the sale or rental of housing

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For that other nation within a Nation-the poor-whose distress has now captured the conscience of America, I will ask the Congress not only to continue, but to speed up the war on poverty.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And in so doing, we will provide the added energy of achievement with the increased efficiency of experience.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: To improve the life of our rural Americans and our farm population, we will plan for the future through the establishment of several new Community Development Districts, improved education through the use of Teachers Corps teams, better health measures, physical examinations, and adequate and available medical resources.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For those who labor, I propose to improve unemployment insurance, to expand minimum wage benefits, and by the repeal of section 14(b) of the Taft-Hartley Act to make the labor laws in all our States equal to the laws of the 31 States which do not have tonight right-to-work measures.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And I also intend to ask the Congress to consider measures which, without improperly invading State and local authority, will enable us effectively to deal with strikes which threaten irreparable damage to the national interest

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: (3) The third path is the path of liberation.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It is to use our success for the fulfillment of our lives.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: A great nation is one which breeds a great people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: A great people flower not from wealth and power, but from a society which spurs them to the fullness of their genius

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: That alone is a Great Society.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Yet, slowly, painfully, on the edge of victory, has come the knowledge that shared prosperity is not enough.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In the midst of abundance modern man walks oppressed by forces which menace and confine the quality of his life, and which individual abundance alone will not overcome.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We can subdue and we can master these forces-bring increased meaning to our lives-if all of us, Government and citizens, are bold enough to change old ways, daring enough to assault new dangers, and if the dream is dear enough to call forth the limitless capacities of this great people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This year we must continue to improve the quality of American life.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Let us fulfill and improve the great health and education programs of last year, extending special opportunities to those who risk their lives in our Armed Forces.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I urge the House of Representatives to complete action on three programs already passed by the Senate-the Teacher Corps, rent assistance, and home rule for the District of Columbia.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In some of our urban areas we must help rebuild entire sections and neighborhoods containing, in some cases, as many as 100,000 people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Working together, private enterprise and government must press forward with the task of providing homes and shops, parks and hospitals, and all the other necessary parts of a flourishing community where our people can come to live the good life.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will offer other proposals to stimulate and to reward planning for the growth of entire metropolitan areas.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Of all the reckless devastations of our national heritage, none is really more shameful than the continued poisoning of our rivers and our air.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We must undertake a cooperative effort to end pollution in several river basins, making additional funds available to help draw the plans and construct the plants that are necessary to make the waters of our entire river systems clean, and make them a source of pleasure and beauty for all of our people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: To attack and to overcome growing crime and lawlessness, I think we must have a stepped-up program to help modernize and strengthen our local police forces

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Our people have a right to feel secure in their homes and on their streets-and that right just must be secured.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Nor can we fail to arrest the destruction of life and property on our highways

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will propose a Highway Safety Act of 1966 to seek an end to this mounting tragedy.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We must also act to prevent the deception of the American consumer-requiring all packages to state clearly and truthfully their contents-all interest and credit charges to be fully revealed-and keeping harmful drugs and cosmetics away from our stores.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It is the genius of our Constitution that under its shelter of enduring institutions and rooted principles there is ample room for the rich fertility of American political invention.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We must change to master change.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I propose to take steps to modernize and streamline the executive branch, to modernize the relations between city and State and Nation

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: A new Department of Transportation is needed to bring together our transportation activities.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The present structure-35 Government agencies, spending $5 billion yearly-makes it almost impossible to serve either the growing demands of this great Nation or the needs of the industry, or the right of the taxpayer to full efficiency and real frugality.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will propose in addition a program to construct and to flight-test a new supersonic transport airplane that will fly three times the speed of sound-in excess of 2,000 miles per hour.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I propose to examine our Federal system-the relation between city, State, Nation, and the citizens themselves.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We need a commission of the most distinguished scholars and men of public affairs to do this job.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will ask them to move on to develop a creative federalism to best use the wonderful diversity of our institutions and our people to solve the problems and to fulfill the dreams of the American people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: As the process of election becomes more complex and more costly, we must make it possible for those without personal wealth to enter public life without being obligated to a few large contributors.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Therefore, I will submit legislation to revise the present unrealistic restriction on contributions-to prohibit the endless proliferation of committees, bringing local and State committees under the act-to attach strong teeth and severe penalties to the requirement of full disclosure of contributions-and to broaden the participation of the people, through added tax incentives, to stimulate small contributions to the party and to the candidate of their choice

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: To strengthen the work of Congress I strongly urge an amendment to provide a 4-year term for Members of the House of Representatives-which should not begin before 1972.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The present 2-year term requires most Members of Congress to divert enormous energies to an almost constant process of campaigning-depriving this Nation of the fullest measure of both their skill and their wisdom.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Today, too, the work of government is far more complex than in our early years, requiring more time to learn and more time to master the technical tasks of legislating.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And a longer term will serve to attract more men of the highest quality to political life.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The Nation, the principle of democracy, and, I think, each congressional district, will all be better served by a 4-year term for Members of the House.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And I urge your swift action.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Tonight the cup of peril is full in Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: That conflict is not an isolated episode, but another great event in the policy that we have followed with strong consistency since World War II.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The touchstone of that policy is the interest of the United States-the welfare and the freedom of the people of the United States.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But nations sink when they see that interest only through a narrow glass.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In a world that has grown small and dangerous, pursuit of narrow aims could bring decay and even disaster.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: An America that is mighty beyond description-yet living in a hostile or despairing world-would be neither safe nor free to build a civilization to liberate the spirit of man.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In this pursuit we helped rebuild Western Europe.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We gave our aid to Greece and Turkey, and we defended the freedom of Berlin.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In this pursuit we have helped new nations toward independence.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have extended the helping hand of the Peace Corps and carried forward the largest program of economic assistance in the world.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And in this pursuit we work to build a hemisphere of democracy and of social justice.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In this pursuit we have defended against Communist aggression-in Korea under President Truman-in the Formosa Straits under President Eisenhower-in Cuba under President Kennedy-and again in Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Tonight Vietnam must hold the center of our attention, but across the world problems and opportunities crowd in on the American Nation

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will discuss them fully in the months to come, and I will follow the five continuing lines of policy that America has followed under its last four Presidents.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: (1) The first principle is strength.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Tonight I can tell you that we are strong enough to keep all of our commitments.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will need expenditures of $58.3 billion for the next fiscal year to maintain this necessary defense might.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: While special Vietnam expenditures for the next fiscal year are estimated to increase by $58 billion, I can tell you that all the other expenditures put together in the entire Federal budget will rise this coming year by only $6 billion.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This is true because of the stringent cost-conscious economy program inaugurated in the Defense Department, and followed by the other departments of Government

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: (2) A second principle of policy is the effort to control, and to reduce, and to ultimately eliminate the modern engines of destruction.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will vigorously pursue existing proposals-and seek new ones-to control arms and to stop the spread of nuclear weapons

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: (3) A third major principle of our foreign policy is to help build those associations of nations which reflect the opportunities and the necessities of the modern world.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: By strengthening the common defense, by stimulating world commerce, by meeting new hopes, these associations serve the cause of a flourishing world

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will take new steps this year to help strengthen the Alliance for Progress, the unity of Europe, the community of the Atlantic, the regional organizations of developing continents, and that supreme association-the United Nations

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will work to strengthen economic cooperation, to reduce barriers to trade, and to improve international finance.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: (4) A fourth enduring strand of policy has been to help improve the life of man

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: From the Marshall plan to this very moment tonight, that policy has rested on the claims of compassion, and the certain knowledge that only a people advancing in expectation will build secure and peaceful lands.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This year I propose major new directions in our program of foreign assistance to help those countries who will help themselves.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will conduct a worldwide attack on the problems of hunger and disease and ignorance.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will place the matchless skill and the resources of our own great America, in farming and in fertilizers, at the service of those countries committed to develop a modern agriculture.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will aid those who educate the young in other lands, and we will give children in other continents the same head start that we are trying to give our own children.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: To advance these ends I will propose the International Education Act of 1966.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I will also propose the International Health Act of 1966 to strike at disease by a new effort to bring modern skills and knowledge to the uncared-for, those suffering in the world, and by trying to wipe out smallpox and malaria and control yellow fever over most of the world during this next decade;

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: to help countries trying to control population growth, by increasing our research-and we will earmark funds to help their efforts.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In the next year, from our foreign aid sources, we propose to dedicate $1 billion to these efforts, and we call on all who have the means to join us in this work in the world.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: (5) The fifth and most important principle of our foreign policy is support of national independence-the right of each people to govern themselves-and to shape their own institutions.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For a peaceful world order will be possible only when each country walks the way that it has chosen to walk for itself.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We follow this principle by encouraging the end of colonial rule.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We follow this principle, abroad as well as at home, by continued hostility to the rule of the many by the few--or the oppression of one race by another.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We follow this principle by building bridges to Eastern Europe.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And I will ask the Congress for authority to remove the special tariff restrictions which are a barrier to increasing trade between the East and the West.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The insistent urge toward national independence is the strongest force of today's world in which we live.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In Africa and Asia and Latin America it is shattering the designs of those who would subdue others to their ideas or their will.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It is eroding the unity of what was once a Stalinist empire.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In recent months a number of nations have cast out those who would subject them to the ambitions of mainland China.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: History is on the side of freedom and is on the side of societies shaped from the genius of each people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: History does not favor a single system or belief-unless force is used to make it so.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: That is why it has been necessary for us to defend this basic principle of our policy, to defend it in Berlin, in Korea, in Cuba-and tonight in Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For tonight, as so many nights before, young Americans struggle and young Americans die in a distant land.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Tonight, as so many nights before, the American Nation is asked to sacrifice the blood of its children and the fruits of its labor for the love of its freedom.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: How many times-in my lifetime and in yours-have the American people gathered, as they do now, to hear their President tell them of conflict and tell them of danger?

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Each time they have answered.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: They have answered with all the effort that the security and the freedom of this Nation required.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And they do again tonight in Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Not too many years ago Vietnam was a peaceful, if troubled, land.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In the North was an independent Communist government.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In the South a people struggled to build a nation, with the friendly help of the United States.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: There were some in South Vietnam who wished to force Communist rule on their own people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But their progress was slight.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Their hope of success was dim.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Then, little more than 6 years ago, North Vietnam decided on conquest.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And from that day to this, soldiers and supplies have moved from North to South in a swelling stream that is swallowing the remnants of revolution in aggression.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: As the assault mounted, our choice gradually became clear.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We could leave, abandoning South Vietnam to its attackers and to certain conquest, or we could stay and fight beside the people of South Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We stayed.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And we will stay until aggression has stopped.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will stay because a just nation cannot leave to the cruelties of its enemies a people who have staked their lives and independence on America's solemn pledge-a pledge which has grown through the commitments of three American Presidents.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will stay because in Asia and around the world are countries whose independence rests, in large measure, on confidence in America's word and in America's protection.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: To yield to force in Vietnam would weaken that confidence, would undermine the independence of many lands, and would whet the appetite of aggression.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We would have to fight in one land, and then we would have to fight in another-or abandon much of Asia to the domination of Communists.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And we do not intend to abandon Asia to conquest.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Last year the nature of the war in Vietnam changed again.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Swiftly increasing numbers of armed men from the North crossed the borders to join forces that were already in the South.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Attack and terror increased, spurred and encouraged by the belief that the United States lacked the will to continue and that their victory was near.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Despite our desire to limit conflict, it was necessary to act: to hold back the mounting aggression, to give courage to the people of the South, and to make our firmness clear to the North.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Thus we began limited air action against military targets in North Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We increased our fighting force to its present strength tonight of 190,000 men.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: These moves have not ended the aggression but they have prevented its success.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The aims of the enemy have been put out of reach by the skill and the bravery of Americans and their allies-and by the enduring courage of the South Vietnamese who, I can tell you, have lost eight men last year for every one of ours.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The enemy is no longer close to victory.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Time is no longer on his side.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: There is no cause to doubt the American commitment.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Our decision to stand firm has been matched by our desire for peace.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In 1965 alone we had 300 private talks for peace in Vietnam, with friends and adversaries throughout the world.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Since Christmas your Government has labored again, with imagination and endurance, to remove any barrier to peaceful settlement.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For 20 days now we and our Vietnamese allies have dropped no bombs in North Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Able and experienced spokesmen have visited, in behalf of America, more than 40 countries.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have talked to more than a hundred governments, all 113 that we have relations with, and some that we don't.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have talked to the United Nations and we have called upon all of its members to make any contribution that they can toward helping obtain peace.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In public statements and in private communications, to adversaries and to friends, in Rome and Warsaw, in Paris and Tokyo, in Africa and throughout this hemisphere, America has made her position abundantly clear.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We seek neither territory nor bases, economic domination or military alliance in Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We fight for the principle of self-determination-that the people of South Vietnam should be able to choose their own course, choose it in free elections without violence, without terror, and without fear.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The people of all Vietnam should make a free decision on the great question of reunification.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This is all we want for South Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It is all the people of South Vietnam want.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And if there is a single nation on this earth that desires less than this for its own people, then let its voice be heard.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have also made it clear-from Hanoi to New York-that there are no arbitrary limits to our search for peace.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We stand by the Geneva Agreements of 1954 and 1962.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will meet at any conference table, we will discuss any proposals-four points or fourteen or forty-and we will consider the views of any group.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will work for a cease-fire now or once discussions have begun.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will respond if others reduce their use of force, and we will withdraw our soldiers once South Vietnam is securely guaranteed the right to shape its own future.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have said all this, and we have asked-and hoped-and we have waited for a response.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: So far we have received no response to prove either success or failure.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have carried our quest for peace to many nations and peoples because we share this planet with others whose future, in large measure, is tied to our own action, and whose counsel is necessary to our own hopes.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have found understanding and support.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And we know they wait with us tonight for some response that could lead to peace.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I wish tonight that I could give you a blueprint for the course of this conflict over the coming months, but we just cannot know what the future may require.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We may have to face long, hard combat or a long, hard conference, or even both at once.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Until peace comes, or if it does not come, our course is clear.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will act as we must to help protect the independence of the valiant people of South Vietnam.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We will strive to limit the conflict, for we wish neither increased destruction nor do we want to invite increased danger.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But we will give our fighting men what they must have: every gun, and every dollar, and every decision-whatever the cost or whatever the challenge.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And we will continue to help the people of South Vietnam care for those that are ravaged by battle, create progress in the villages, and carry forward the healing hopes of peace as best they can amidst the uncertain terrors of war.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And let me be absolutely clear: The days may become months, and the months may become years, but we will stay as long as aggression commands us to battle.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: There may be some who do not want peace, whose ambitions stretch so far that war in Vietnam is but a welcome and convenient episode in an immense design to subdue history to their will.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But for others it must now be clear-the choice is not between peace and victory, it lies between peace and the ravages of a conflict from which they can only lose.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The people of Vietnam, North and South, seek the same things: the shared needs of man, the needs for food and shelter and education-the chance to build and work and till the soil, free from the arbitrary horrors of battle-the desire to walk in the dignity of those who master their own destiny.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For many painful years, in war and revolution and infrequent peace, they have struggled to fulfill those needs.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It is a crime against mankind that so much courage, and so much will, and so many dreams, must be flung on the fires of war and death.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: To all of those caught up in this conflict we therefore say again tonight: Let us choose peace, and with it the wondrous works of peace, and beyond that, the time when hope reaches toward consummation, and life is the servant of life.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In this work, we plan to discharge our duty to the people whom we serve.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This is the State of the Union.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But over it all-wealth, and promise, and expectation-lies our troubling awareness of American men at war tonight.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: How many men who listen to me tonight have served their Nation in other wars? How very many are not here to listen? The war in Vietnam is not like these other wars.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Yet, finally, war is always the same.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It is young men dying in the fullness of their promise.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It is trying to kill a man that you do not even know well enough to hate.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Therefore, to know war is to know that there is still madness in this world.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Many of you share the burden of this knowledge tonight with me.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But there is a difference.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For finally I must be the one to order our guns to fire, against all the most inward pulls of my desire.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For we have children to teach, and we have sick to be cured, and we have men to be freed.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: There are poor to be lifted up, and there are cities to be built, and there is a world to be helped.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Yet we do what we must.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I am hopeful, and I will try as best I can, with everything I have got, to end this battle and to return our sons to their desires.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Yet as long as others will challenge America's security and test the dearness of our beliefs with fire and steel, then we must stand or see the promise of two centuries tremble.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I believe tonight that you do not want me to try that risk.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And from that belief your President summons his strength for the trials that lie ahead in the days to come.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The work must be our work now.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Scarred by the weaknesses of man, with whatever guidance God may offer us, we must nevertheless and alone with our mortality, strive to ennoble the life of man on earth.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Thank you, and goodnight.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I share with all of you the grief that you feel at the death today of one of the most beloved, respected, and effective Members of this body, the distinguished Representative from Rhode Island, Mr. Fogarty.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I have come here tonight to report to you that this is a time of testing for our Nation.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: At home, the question is whether we will continue working for better opportunities for all Americans, when most Americans are already living better than any people in history.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Abroad, the question is whether we have the staying power to fight a very costly war, when the objective is limited and the danger to us is seemingly remote.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: So our test is not whether we shrink from our country's cause when the dangers to us are obvious and close at hand, but, rather, whether we carry on when they seem obscure and distant-and some think that it is safe to lay down our burdens.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I have come tonight to ask this Congress and this Nation to resolve that issue: to meet our commitments at home and abroad- to continue to build a better America-and to reaffirm this Nation's allegiance to freedom.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We must ask where we are, and whither we are tending.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The last 3 years bear witness to our determination to make this a better country.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have struck down legal barriers to equality.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have improved the education of 7 million deprived children and this year alone we have enabled almost 1 million students to go to college.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have brought medical care to older people who were unable to afford it.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Three and one-half million Americans have already received treatment under Medicare since July.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have built a strong economy that has put almost 3 million more Americans on the payrolls in the last year alone.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have included more than 9 million new workers under a higher minimum wage.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have launched new training programs to provide job skills for almost 1 million Americans.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have helped more than a thousand local communities to attack poverty in the neighborhoods of the poor.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have set out to rebuild our cities on a scale that has never been attempted before.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have begun to rescue our waters from the menace of pollution and to restore the beauty of our land and our countryside, our cities and our towns.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have given 1 million young Americans a chance to earn through the Neighborhood Youth Corps-or through Head Start, a chance to learn.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: So together we have tried to meet the needs of our people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And, we have succeeded in creating a better life for the many as well as the few.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Now we must answer whether our gains shall be the foundations of further progress, or whether they shall be only monuments to what might have been- abandoned now by a people who lacked the will to see their great work through.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I believe that our people do not want to quit-though the task is great, the work hard, often frustrating, and success is a matter not of days or months, but of years- and sometimes it may be even decades.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I have come here tonight to discuss with you five ways of carrying forward the progress of these last 3 years.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: These five ways concern programs, partnerships, priorities, prosperity, and peace.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: First, programs.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We must see to it, I think, that these new programs that we have passed work effectively and are administered in the best possible way.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Three years ago we set out to create these new instruments of social progress.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This required trial and error-and it has produced both.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But as we learn, through success and failure, we are changing our strategy and we are trying to improve our tactics.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: In the long run, these starts-some rewarding, others inadequate and disappointing-are crucial to success.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: One example is the struggle to make life better for the less fortunate among us.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The American people have decided that poverty is just as wasteful and just as unnecessary as preventable disease.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Many listened to President Truman that day here in this Chamber, but few understood what was required and did anything about it.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The executive branch and the Congress waited 15 long years before ever taking any action on that challenge, as it did on many other challenges that great President presented.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: It will not be a short or easy struggle- no single weapon will suffice-but we shall not rest until that war is won.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And I have come here to renew that pledge tonight.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I recommend that we intensify our efforts to give the poor a chance to enjoy and to join in this Nation's progress.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I shall propose certain administrative changes suggested by the Congress-as well as some that we have learned from our own trial and error.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I shall urge special methods and special funds to reach the hundreds of thousands of Americans that are now trapped in the ghettos of our big cities and, through Head Start, to try to reach out to our very young, little children.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The chance to learn is their brightest hope and must command our full determination.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: For learning brings skills; and skills bring jobs; and jobs bring responsibility and dignity, as well as taxes.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This war-like the war in Vietnam-is not a simple one.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: There is no single battle line which you can plot each day on a chart.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The enemy is not easy to perceive, or to isolate, or to destroy.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: There are mistakes and there are setbacks.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But we are moving, and our direction is forward.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This is true with other programs that are making and breaking new ground.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Some do not yet have the capacity to absorb well or wisely all the money that could be put into them.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Administrative skills and trained manpower are just as vital to their success as dollars.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And I believe those skills will come.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But it will take time and patience and hard work.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Success cannot be forced at a single stroke.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: So we must continue to strengthen the administration of every program if that success is to come-as we know it must.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We have done much in the space of 2 short years, working together.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I have recommended, and you, the Congress, have approved, 10 different reorganization plans, combining and consolidating many bureaus of this Government, and creating two entirely new Cabinet departments.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I have come tonight to propose that we establish a new department-a Department of Business and Labor.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: By combining the Department of Commerce with the Department of Labor and other related agencies, I think we can create a more economical, efficient, and streamlined instrument that will better serve a growing nation.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This is our goal throughout the entire Federal Government.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Every program will be thoroughly evaluated.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Grant-in-aid programs will be improved and simplified as desired by many of our local administrators and our Governors.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Where there have been mistakes, we will try very hard to correct them.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Where there has been progress, we will try to build upon it.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Our second objective is partnership-to create an effective partnership at all levels of government.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: And I should treasure nothing more than to have that partnership begin between the executive and the Congress.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The 88th and the 89th between the executive social and economic legislation than any two single Congresses in American history.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Most of you who were Members of those Congresses voted to pass most of those measures.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But your efforts will come to nothing unless it reaches the people.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Federal energy is essential.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But it is not enough.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Only a total working partnership among Federal, State, and local governments can succeed.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: The test of that partnership will be the concern of each public organization, each private institution, and each responsible citizen.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Each State, county, and city needs to examine its capacity for government in today's world, as we are examining ours in the executive department, and as I see you are examining yours.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Some will need to reorganize and reshape their methods of administration- as we are doing.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Others will need to revise their constitutions and their laws to bring them up to date-as we are doing.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Above all, I think we must work together and find ways in which the multitudes of small jurisdictions can be brought together more efficiently.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: During the past 3 years we have returned to State and local governments about $40 billion in grants-in-aid.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: This year alone, 70 percent of our Federal expenditures for domestic programs will be distributed through the State and local governments.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: With Federal assistance, State and local governments by 1970 will be spending close to $110 billion annually.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: These enormous sums must be used wisely, honestly, and effectively.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: We intend to work closely with the States and the localities to do exactly that.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Our third objective is priorities, to move ahead on the priorities that we have established within the resources that are available.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: I wish, of course, that we could do all that should be done-and that we could do it now.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: But the Nation has many commitments and responsibilities which make heavy demands upon our total resources.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: No administration would more eagerly utilize for these programs all the resources they require than the administration that started them.

speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
