text: Effective diplomacy is also essential in preventing conflict, in building world understanding.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The Vladivostok negotiations with the Soviet Union represent a major step in moderating strategic arms competition.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: My recent discussions with the leaders of the Atlantic community, Japan, and South Korea have contributed to meeting the common challenge.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But we have serious problems before us that require cooperation between the President and the Congress.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: By the Constitution and tradition, the execution of foreign policy is the responsibility of the President.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In recent years, under the stress of the Vietnam war, legislative restrictions on the President's ability to execute foreign policy and military decisions have proliferated.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: As a Member of the Congress, I opposed some and I approved others.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: As President, I welcome the advice and cooperation of the House and the Senate.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But if our foreign policy is to be successful, we cannot rigidly restrict in legislation the ability of the President to act.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The conduct of negotiations is ill-suited to such limitations.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Legislative restrictions, intended for the best motives and purposes, can have the opposite result, as we have seen most recently in our trade relations with the Soviet Union.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: For my part, I pledge this Administration will act in the closest consultation with the Congress as we face delicate situations and troubled times throughout the globe.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: When I became President only 5 months ago, I promised the last Congress a policy of communication, conciliation, compromise, and cooperation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I renew that pledge to the new Members of this Congress.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Let me sum it up.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: America needs a new direction, which I have sought to chart here today--a change of course which will: put the unemployed back to work;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: increase real income and production;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: restrain the growth of Federal Government spending;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: achieve energy independence;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: and advance the cause of world understanding.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have the ability.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have the know-how.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In partnership with the American people, we will achieve these objectives.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: As our 200th anniversary approaches, we owe it to ourselves and to posterity to rebuild our political and economic strength.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Let us make America once again and for centuries more to come what it has so long been--a stronghold and a beacon-light of liberty for the whole world.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Thank you.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. Vice President, Members of the 94th Congress, and distinguished guests: As we begin our Bicentennial, America is still one of the youngest nations in recorded history.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Long before our forefathers came to these shores, men and women had been struggling on this planet to forge a better life for themselves and their families.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In man's long, upward march from savagery and slavery--throughout the nearly 2,000 years of the Christian calendar, the nearly 6,000 years of Jewish reckoning--there have been many deep, terrifying valleys, but also many bright and towering peaks.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: One peak stands highest in the ranges of human history.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: One example shines forth of a people uniting to produce abundance and to share the good life fairly and with freedom.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: One union holds out the promise of justice and opportunity for every citizen: That union is the United States of America.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have not remade paradise on Earth.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We know perfection will not be found here.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But think for a minute how far we have come in 200 years.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We came from many roots, and we have many branches.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Yet all Americans across the eight generations that separate us from the stirring deeds of 1776, those who know no other homeland and those who just found refuge among our shores, say in unison: I am proud of America, and I am proud to be an American.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Life will be a little better here for my children than for me.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I believe this not because I am told to believe it, but because life has been better for me than it was for my father and my mother.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I know it will be better for my children because my hands, my brains, my voice, and my vote can help make it happen.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It has happened here in America.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It has happened to you and to me.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Government exists to create and preserve conditions in which people can translate their ideas into practical reality.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In the best of times, much is lost in translation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But we try.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Sometimes we have tried and failed.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Always we have had the best of intentions.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But in the recent past, we sometimes forgot the sound principles that guided us through most of our history.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We wanted to accomplish great things and solve age-old problems.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: And we became overconfident of our abilities.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We tried to be a policeman abroad and the indulgent parent here at home.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We thought we could transform the country through massive national programs, but often the programs did not work.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Too often they only made things worse.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In our rush to accomplish great deeds quickly, we trampled on sound principles of restraint and endangered the rights of individuals.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We unbalanced our economic system by the huge and unprecedented growth of Federal expenditures and borrowing.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: And we were not totally honest with ourselves about how much these programs would cost and how we would pay for them.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Finally, we shifted our emphasis from defense to domestic problems while our adversaries continued a massive buildup of arms.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The time has now come for a fundamentally different approach--for a new realism that is true to the great principles upon which this Nation was founded.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must introduce a new balance to our economy--a balance that favors not only sound, active government but also a much more vigorous, healthy economy that can create new jobs and hold down prices.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must introduce a new balance in the relationship between the individual and the government--a balance that favors greater individual freedom and self-reliance.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must strike a new balance in our system of federalism--a balance that favors greater responsibility and freedom for the leaders of our State and local governments.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must introduce a new balance between the spending on domestic programs and spending on defense--a balance that ensures we will fully meet our obligation to the needy while also protecting our security in a world that is still hostile to freedom.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: And in all that we do, we must be more honest with the American people, promising them no more than we can deliver and delivering all that we promise.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The genius of America has been its incredible ability to improve the lives of its citizens through a unique combination of governmental and free citizen activity.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: History and experience tells us that moral progress cannot come in comfortable and in complacent times, but out of trial and out of confusion.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Tom Paine aroused the troubled Americans of 1776 to stand up to the times that try men's souls because the harder the conflict, the more glorious the triumph.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Just a year ago I reported that the state of the Union was not good.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Tonight, I report that the state of our Union is better--in many ways a lot better--but still not good enough.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To paraphrase Tom Paine, 1975 was not a year for summer soldiers and sunshine patriots.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It was a year of fears and alarms and of dire forecasts-- most of which never happened and won't happen.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: As you recall, the year 1975 opened with rancor and with bitterness.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Political misdeeds of the past had neither been forgotten nor forgiven.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The longest, most divisive war in our history was winding toward an unhappy conclusion.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Many feared that the end of that foreign war of men and machines meant the beginning of a domestic war of recrimination and reprisal.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Friends and adversaries abroad were asking whether America had lost its nerve.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Finally, our economy was ravaged by inflation--inflation that was plunging us into the worse recession in four decades.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: At the same time, Americans became increasingly alienated from big institutions.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: They were steadily losing confidence, not just in big government but in big business, big labor, and big education, among others.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Ours was a troubled land.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: And so, 1975 was a year of hard decisions, difficult compromises, and a new realism that taught us something important about America.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It brought back a needed measure of common sense, steadfastness, and self-discipline.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Americans did not panic or demand instant but useless cures.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In all sectors, people met their difficult problems with the restraint and with responsibility worthy of their great heritage.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Add up the separate pieces of progress in 1975, subtract the setbacks, and the sum total shows that we are not only headed in a new direction, a direction which I proposed 12 months ago, but it turned out to be the right direction.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It is the right direction because it follows the truly revolutionary American concept of 1776, which holds that in a free society the making of public policy and successful problemsolving involves much more than government.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It involves a full partnership among all branches and all levels of government, private institutions, and individual citizens.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Common sense tells me to stick to that steady course.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Take the state of our economy.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Last January, most things were rapidly getting worse.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This January, most things are slowly but surely getting better.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The worst recession since World War II turned around in April.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The best cost-of-living news of the past year is that double-digit inflation of 12 percent or higher was cut almost in half.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The worst--unemployment remains far too high.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Today, nearly 1,700,000 more Americans are working than at the bottom of the recession.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: At year's end, people were again being hired much faster than they were being laid off.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Yet, let's be honest.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Many Americans have not yet felt these changes in their daily lives.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: They still see prices going up far too fast, and they still know the fear of unemployment.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We are also a growing nation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We need more and more jobs every year.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Today's economy has produced over 85 million jobs for Americans, but we need a lot more jobs, especially for the young.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: My first objective is to have sound economic growth without inflation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We all know from recent experience what runaway inflation does to ruin every other worthy purpose.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We are slowing it.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must stop it cold.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: For many Americans, the way to a healthy, noninflationary economy has become increasingly apparent.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The Government must stop spending so much and stop borrowing so much of our money.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: More money must remain in private hands where it will do the most good.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To hold down the cost of living, we must hold down the cost of government.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In the past decade, the Federal budget has been growing at an average rate of over 10 percent a year.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The budget I am submitting Wednesday cuts this rate of growth in half.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I have kept my promise to submit a budget for the next fiscal year of $395 billion.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In fact, it is $394.2 billion.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: By holding down the growth of Federal spending, we can afford additional tax cuts and return to the people who pay taxes more decisionmaking power over their own lives.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Last month I signed legislation to extend the 1975 tax reductions for the first 6 months of this year.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I now propose that effective July 1, 1976, we give our taxpayers a tax cut of approximately $10 billion more than Congress agreed to in December.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: My broader tax reduction would mean that for a family of four making $15,000 a year, there will be $227 more in take-home pay annually.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Hardworking Americans caught in the middle can really use that kind of extra cash.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: My recommendations for a firm restraint on the growth of Federal spending and for greater tax reduction are simple and straightforward.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: For every dollar saved in cutting the growth in the Federal budget, we can have an added dollar of Federal tax reduction.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We can achieve a balanced budget by 1979 if we have the courage and the wisdom to continue to reduce the growth of Federal spending.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: One test of a healthy economy is a job for every American who wants to work.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Government--our kind of government--cannot create that many jobs.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But the Federal Government can create conditions and incentives for private business and industry to make more and more jobs.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Five out of six jobs in this country are in private business and in industry.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Common sense tells us this is the place to look for more jobs and to find them faster.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I mean real, rewarding, permanent jobs.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To achieve this we must offer the American people greater incentives to invest in the future.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: My tax proposals are a major step in that direction.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To supplement these proposals, I ask that Congress enact changes in Federal tax laws that will speed up plant expansion and the purchase of new equipment.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: My recommendations will concentrate this job-creation tax incentive in areas where the unemployment rate now runs over 7 percent.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Legislation to get this started must be approved at the earliest possible date.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Within the strict budget total that I will recommend for the coming year, I will ask for additional housing assistance for 500,000 families.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: These programs will expand housing opportunities, spur construction, and help to house moderate- and low-income families.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We had a disappointing year in the housing industry in 1975.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But with lower interest rates and available mortgage money, we can have a healthy recovery in 1976.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: A necessary condition of a healthy economy is freedom from the petty tyranny of massive government regulation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We are wasting literally millions of working hours costing billions of taxpayers' and consumers' dollars because of bureaucratic redtape.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The American farmer, who now feeds 215 million Americans, but also millions worldwide, has shown how much more he can produce without the shackles of government control.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Now, we badly need reforms in other key areas in our economy: the airlines, trucking, railroads, and financial institutions.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I have submitted concrete plans in each of these areas, not to help this or that industry, but to foster competition and to bring prices down for the consumer.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This administration, in addition, will strictly enforce the Federal antitrust laws for the very same purposes.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Taking a longer look ail and gas is still declining.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Our dependence on foreign oil at high prices is still too great, draining jobs and dollars away from our own economy at the rate of $125 per year for every American.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Last month, I signed a compromise national energy bill which enacts a part of my comprehensive energy independence program.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This legislation was late, not the complete answer to energy independence, but still a start in the right direction.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I again urge the Congress to move ahead immediately on the remainder of my energy proposals to make America invulnerable to the foreign oil cartel.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: My proposals, as all of you know, would reduce domestic natural gas shortages;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: allow production from Federal petroleum reserves;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: stimulate effective conservation, including revitalization of our railroads and the expansion of our urban transportation systems;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: develop more and cleaner energy from our vast coal resources;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: expedite clean and safe nuclear power production;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: create a new national energy independence authority to stimulate vital energy investment;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: and accelerate development of technology to capture energy from the Sun and the Earth for this and future generations.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Also, I ask, for the sake of future generations, that we preserve the family farm and family-owned small business.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Both strengthen America and give stability to our economy.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I will propose estate tax changes so that family businesses and family farms can be handed down from generation to generation without having to be sold to pay taxes.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I propose tax changes to encourage people to invest in America's future, and their own, through a plan that gives moderate-income families income tax benefits if they make long-term investments in common stock in American companies.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The Federal Government must and will respond to clear-cut national needs--for this and future generations.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Hospital and medical services in America are among the best in the world, but the cost of a serious and extended illness can quickly wipe out a family's lifetime savings.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Increasing health costs are of deep concern to all and a powerful force pushing up the cost of living.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The burden of catastrophic illness can be borne by very few in our society.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must eliminate this fear from every family.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I propose catastrophic health insurance for everybody covered by Medicare.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To finance this added protection, fees for short-term care will go up somewhat, but nobody after reaching age 65 will have to pay more than $500 a year for covered hospital or nursing home care, nor more than $250 for 1 year's doctor bills.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We cannot realistically afford federally dictated national health insurance providing full coverage for all 215 million Americans.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The experience of other countries raises questions about the quality as well as the cost of such plans.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But I do envision the day when we may use the private health insurance system to offer more middle-income families high quality health services at prices they can afford and shield them also from their catastrophic illnesses.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Using resources now available, I propose improving the Medicare and other Federal health programs to help those who really need protection-- older people and the poor.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To help States and local governments give better health care to the poor, I propose that we combine 16 existing Federal programs, including Medicaid, into a single $10 billion Federal grant.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Funds would be divided among States under a new formula which provides a larger share of Federal money to those States that have a larger share of low-income families.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I will take further steps to improve the quality of medical and hospital care for those who have served in our Armed Forces.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Now let me speak about social security.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Our Federal social security system for people who have worked and contributed to it for all their lives is a vital part of our economic system.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Its value is no longer debatable.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In my budget for fiscal year 1977, I am recommending that the full cost-of-living increases in the social security benefits be paid during the coming year.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But I am concerned about the integrity of our Social Security Trust Fund that enables people--those retired and those still working who will retire--to count on this source of retirement income.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Younger workers watch their deductions rise and wonder if they will be adequately protected in the future.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must meet this challenge head on.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Simple arithmetic warns all of us that the Social Security Trust Fund is headed for trouble.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Unless we act soon to make sure the fund takes in as much as it pays out, there will be no security for old or for young.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I must, therefore, recommend a three-tenths of 1 percent increase in both employer and employee social security taxes effective January 1, 1977.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This will cost each covered employee less than 1 extra dollar a week and will ensure the integrity of the trust fund.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: As we rebuild our economy, we have a continuing responsibility to provide a temporary cushion to the unemployed.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: At my request, the Congress enacted two extensions and two expansions in unemployment insurance which helped those who were jobless during 1975.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: These programs will continue in 1976.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In my fiscal year 1977 budget, I am also requesting funds to continue proven job training and employment opportunity programs for millions of other Americans.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Compassion and a sense of community--two of America's greatest strengths throughout our history--tell us we must take care of our neighbors who cannot take care of themselves.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The host of Federal programs in this field reflect our generosity as a people.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But everyone realizes that when it comes to welfare, government at all levels is not doing the job well.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Too many of our welfare programs are inequitable and invite abuse.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Too many of our welfare programs have problems from beginning to end.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Worse, we are wasting badly needed resources without reaching many of the truly needy.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Complex welfare programs cannot be reformed overnight.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Surely we cannot simply dump welfare into the laps of the 50 States, their local taxpayers, or their private charities, and just walk away from it.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Nor is it the right time for massive and sweeping changes while we are still recovering from the recession.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Nevertheless, there are still plenty of improvements that we can make.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I will ask Congress for Presidential authority to tighten up the rules for eligibility and benefits.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Last year I twice sought long overdue reform of the scandal-riddled food stamp program.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This year I say again: Let's give food stamps to those most in need.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Let's not give any to those who don't need them.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Protecting the life and property of the citizen at home is the responsibility of all public officials, but is primarily the job of local and State law enforcement authorities.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Americans have always found the very thought of a Federal police force repugnant, and so do I.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But there are proper ways in which we can help to insure domestic tranquility as the Constitution charges us.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: My recommendations on how to control violent crime were submitted to the Congress last June with strong emphasis on protecting the innocent victims of crime.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To keep a convicted criminal from committing more crimes, we must put him in prison so he cannot harm more law-abiding citizens.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To be effective, this punishment must be swift and it must be certain.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Too often, criminals are not sent to prison after conviction but are allowed to return to the streets.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Some judges are reluctant to send convicted criminals to prison because of inadequate facilities.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To alleviate this problem at the Federal level, my new budget proposes the construction of four new Federal facilities.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To speed Federal justice, I propose an increase this year in the United States attorneys prosecuting Federal crimes and the reinforcement of the number of United States marshals.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Additional Federal judges are needed, as recommended by me and the Judicial Conference.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Another major threat to every American's person and property is the criminal carrying a handgun.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The way to cut down on the criminal use of guns is not to take guns away from the law-abiding citizen, but to impose mandatory sentences for crimes in which a gun is used, make it harder to obtain cheap guns for criminal purposes, and concentrate gun control enforcement in high-crime areas.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: My budget recommends 500 additional Federal agents in the 11 largest metropolitan high-crime areas to help local authorities stop criminals from selling and using handguns.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The sale of hard drugs is tragically on the increase again.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I have directed all agencies of the Federal Government to step up law enforcement efforts against those who deal in drugs.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In 1975, I am glad to report, Federal agents seized substantially more heroin coming into our country than in 1974.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: As President, I have talked personally with the leaders of Mexico, Colombia, and Turkey to urge greater efforts by their Governments to control effectively the production and shipment of hard drugs.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I recommended months ago that the Congress enact mandatory fixed sentences for persons convicted of Federal crimes involving the sale of hard drugs.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Hard drugs, we all know, degrade the spirit as they destroy the body of their users.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It is unrealistic and misleading to hold out the hope that the Federal Government can move into every neighborhood and clean up crime.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Under the Constitution, the greatest responsibility for curbing crime lies with State and local authorities.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: They are the frontline fighters in the war against crime.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: There are definite ways in which the Federal Government can help them.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I will propose in the new budget that Congress authorize almost $7 billion over the next 5 years to assist State and local governments to protect the safety and property of all their citizens.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: As President, I pledge the strict enforcement of Federal laws and--by example, support, and leadership--to help State and local authorities enforce their laws.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Together, we must protect the victims of crime and ensure domestic tranquility.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Last year I strongly recommended a 5-year extension of the existing revenue sharing legislation, which thus far has provided $23 1/2 billion to help State and local units of government solve problems at home.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This program has been effective with decisionmaking transferred from the Federal Government to locally elected officials.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Congress must act this year, or State and local units of government will have to drop programs or raise local taxes.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Including my health care program reforms, I propose to consolidate some 59 separate Federal programs and provide flexible Federal dollar grants to help States, cities, and local agencies in such important areas as education, child nutrition, and social services.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This flexible system will do the job better and do it closer to home.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The protection of the lives and property of Americans from foreign enemies is one of my primary responsibilities as President.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In a world of instant communications and intercontinental ballistic missiles, in a world economy that is global and interdependent, our relations with other nations become more, not less, important to the lives of Americans.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: America has had a unique role in the world since the day of our independence 200 years ago.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: And ever since the end of World War II, we have borne--successfully--a heavy responsibility for ensuring a stable world order and hope for human progress.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Today, the state of our foreign policy is sound and strong.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We are at peace, and I will do all in my power to keep it that way.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Our military forces are capable and ready.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Our military power is without equal, and I intend to keep it that way.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Our principal alliances with the industrial democracies of the Atlantic community and Japan have never been more solid.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: A further agreement to limit the strategic arms race may be achieved.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have an improving relationship with China, the world's most populous nation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The key elements for peace among the nations of the Middle East now exist.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Our traditional friendships in Latin America, Africa, and Asia continue.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have taken the role of leadership in launching a serious and hopeful dialog between the industrial world and the developing world.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have helped to achieve significant reform of the international monetary system.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We should be proud of what America, what our country, has accomplished in these areas, and I believe the American people are.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The American people have heard too much about how terrible our mistakes, how evil our deeds, and how misguided our purposes.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The American people know better.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The truth is we are the world's greatest democracy.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We remain the symbol of man's aspiration for liberty and well-being.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We are the embodiment of hope for progress.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I say it is time we quit downgrading ourselves as a nation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Of course, it is our responsibility to learn the right lesson from past mistakes.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It is our duty to see that they never happen again.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But our greater duty is to look to the future.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The world's troubles will not go away.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The American people want strong and effective international and defense policies.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In our constitutional system, these policies should reflect consultation and accommodation between the President and the Congress.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But in the final analysis, as the framers of our Constitution knew from hard experience, the foreign relations of the United States can be conducted effectively only if there is strong central direction that allows flexibility of action.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: That responsibility clearly rests with the President.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I pledge to the American people policies which seek a secure, just, and peaceful world.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I pledge to the Congress to work with you to that end.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must not face a future in which we can no longer help our friends, such as Angola, even in limited and carefully controlled ways.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must not lose all capacity to respond short of military intervention.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Some hasty actions of the Congress during the past year--most recently in respect to Angola--were, in my view, very shortsighted.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Unfortunately, they are still very much on the minds of our allies and our adversaries.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: A strong defense posture gives weight to our values and our views in international negotiations.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It assures the vigor of our alliances.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: And it sustains our efforts to promote settlements of international conflicts.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Only from a position of strength can we negotiate a balanced agreement to limit the growth of nuclear arms.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Only a balanced agreement will serve our interests and minimize the threat of nuclear confrontation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The defense budget I will submit to the Congress for fiscal year 1977 will show an essential increase over the current year.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It provides for real growth in purchasing power over this year's defense budget, which includes the cost of the all-volunteer force.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We are continuing to make economies to enhance the efficiency of our military forces.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But the budget I will submit represents the necessity of American strength for the real world in which we live.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: As conflict and rivalry persist in the world, our United States intelligence capabilities must be the best in the world.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The crippling of our foreign intelligence services increases the danger of American involvement in direct armed conflict.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Our adversaries are encouraged to attempt new adventures while our own ability to monitor events and to influence events short of military action is undermined.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Without effective intelligence capability, the United States stands blindfolded and hobbled.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In the near future, I will take actions to reform and strengthen our intelligence community.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I ask for your positive cooperation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It is time to go beyond sensationalism and ensure an effective, responsible, and responsive intelligence capability.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Tonight I have spoken about our problems at home and abroad.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I have recommended policies that will meet the challenge of our third century.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I have no doubt that our Union will endure, better, stronger, and with more individual freedom.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We can see forward only dimly--1 year, 5 years, a generation perhaps.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Like our forefathers, we know that if we meet the challenges of our own time with a common sense of purpose and conviction, if we remain true to our Constitution and to our ideals, then we can know that the future will be better than the past.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I see America today crossing a threshold, not just because it is our Bicentennial but because we have been tested in adversity.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have taken a new look at what we want to be and what we want our Nation to become.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I see America resurgent, certain once again that life will be better for our children than it is for us, seeking strength that cannot be counted in megatons and riches that cannot be eroded by inflation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I see these United States of America moving forward as before toward a more perfect Union where the government serves and the people rule.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We will not make this happen simply by making speeches, good or bad, yours or mine, but by hard work and hard decisions made with courage and with common sense.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I have heard many inspiring Presidential speeches, but the words I remember best were spoken by Dwight D.Eisenhower.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: America is not good because it is great, the President said.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: America is great because it is good.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: President Eisenhower was raised in a poor but religious home in the heart of America.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: right makes might.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: And Lincoln in turn evoked the silent image of George Washington kneeling in prayer at Valley Forge.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: So, all these magic memories which link eight generations of Americans are summed up in the inscription just above me.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Let us engrave it now in each of our hearts as we begin our Bicentennial.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr.Vice President, Members of the 95th Congress, and distinguished guests:

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In accordance with the Constitution, I come before you once again to report on the state of the Union.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This report will be my last--maybe--[laughter]--but for the Union it is only the first of such reports in our third century of independence, the close of which none of us will ever see.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We can be confident, however, that 100 years from now a freely elected President will come before a freely elected Congress chosen to renew our great Republic's pledge to the Government of the people, by the people, and for the people.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: For my part I pray the third century we are beginning will bring to all Americans, our children and their children's children, a greater measure of individual equality, opportunity, and justice, a greater abundance of spiritual and material blessings, and a higher quality of life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The state of the Union is a measurement of the many elements of which it is composed--a political union of diverse States, an economic union of varying interests, an intellectual union of common convictions, and a moral union of immutable ideals.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Taken in sum, I can report that the state of the Union is good.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: There is room for improvement, as always, but today we have a more perfect Union than when my stewardship began.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: As a people we discovered that our Bicentennial was much more than a celebration of the past;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: it became a joyous reaffirmation of all that it means to be Americans, a confirmation before all the world of the vitality and durability of our free institutions.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: our Constitution works;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: our great Republic is a Government of laws and not of men.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Here the people rule.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The people have spoken;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: they have chosen a new President and a new Congress to work their will.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I congratulate you--particularly the new Members--as sincerely as I did President-elect Carter.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In a few days it will be his duty to outline for you his priorities and legislative recommendations.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Tonight I will not infringe on that responsibility, but rather wish him the very best in all that is good for our country.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: During the period of my own service in this Capitol and in the White House, I can recall many orderly transitions of governmental responsibility--of problems as well as of position, of burdens as well as of power.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The genius of the American system is that we do this so naturally and so normally.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: There are no soldiers marching in the street except in the Inaugural Parade;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: no public demonstrations except for some of the dancers at the Inaugural Ball;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: the opposition party doesn't go underground, but goes on functioning vigorously in the Congress and in the country;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: and our vigilant press goes right on probing and publishing our faults and our follies, confirming the wisdom of the framers of the first amendment.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Because of the transfer of authority in our form of government affects the state of the Union and of the world, I am happy to report to you that the current transition is proceeding very well.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I was determined that it should;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I wanted the new President to get off on an easier start than I had.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: When I became President on August 9, 1974, our Nation was deeply divided and tormented.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In rapid succession the Vice President and the President had resigned in disgrace.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We were still struggling with the after-effects of a long, unpopular, and bloody war in Southeast Asia.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The economy was unstable and racing toward the worst recession in 40 years.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: People were losing jobs.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The cost of living was soaring.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The Congress and the Chief Executive were at loggerheads.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The integrity of our constitutional process and other institutions was being questioned.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: For more than 15 years domestic spending had soared as Federal programs multiplied, and the expense escalated annually.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: During the same period our national security needs were steadily shortchanged.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In the grave situation which prevailed in August 1974, our will to maintain our international leadership was in doubt.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I asked for your prayers and went to work.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In January 1975 I reported to the Congress that the state of the Union was not good.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I proposed urgent action to improve the economy and to achieve energy independence in 10 years.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I reassured America's allies and sought to reduce the danger of confrontation with potential adversaries.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I pledged a new direction for America.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: 1975 was a year of difficult decisions, but Americans responded with realism, common sense, and self-discipline.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: By January 1976 we were headed in a new direction, which I hold to be the right direction for a free society.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It was guided by the belief that successful problemsolving requires more than Federal action alone, that it involves a full partnership among all branches and all levels of government and public policies which nurture and promote the creative energies of private enterprises, institutions, and individual citizens.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: A year ago I reported that the state of the Union was better--in many ways a lot better--but still not good enough.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Common sense told me to stick to the steady course we were on, to continue to restrain the inflationary growth of government, to reduce taxes as well as spending, to return local decisions to local officials, to provide for long-range sufficiency in energy and national security needs.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I resisted the immense pressures of an election year to open the floodgates of Federal money and the temptation to promise more than I could deliver.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I told it as it was to the American people and demonstrated to the world that in our spirited political competition, as in this chamber, Americans can disagree without being disagreeable.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Now, after 30 months as your President, I can say that while we still have a way to go, I am proud of the long way we have come together.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I am proud of the part I have had in rebuilding confidence in the Presidency, confidence in our free system, and confidence in our future.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Once again, Americans believe in themselves, in their leaders, and in the promise that tomorrow holds for their children.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I am proud that today America is at peace.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: None of our sons are fighting and dying in battle anywhere in the world.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: And the chance for peace among all nations is improved by our determination to honor our vital commitments in defense of peace and freedom.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I am proud that the United States has strong defenses, strong alliances, and a sound and courageous foreign policy.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Our alliances with major partners, the great industrial democracies of Western Europe, Japan, and Canada, have never been more solid.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Consultations on mutual security, defense, and East-West relations have grown closer.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Collaboration has branched out into new fields such as energy, economic policy, and relations with the Third World.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have used many avenues for cooperation, including summit meetings held among major allied countries.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The friendship of the democracies is deeper, warmer, and more effective than at any time in 30 years.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We are maintaining stability in the strategic nuclear balance and pushing back the specter of nuclear war.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: A decisive step forward was taken in the Vladivostok Accord which I negotiated with General Secretary Brezhnev--joint recognition that an equal ceiling should be placed on the number of strategic weapons on each side.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: With resolve and wisdom on the part of both nations, a good agreement is well within reach this year.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The framework for peace in the Middle East has been built.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Hopes for future progress in the Middle East were stirred by the historic agreements we reached and the trust and confidence that we formed.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Thanks to American leadership, the prospects for peace in the Middle East are brighter than they have been in three decades.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The Arab states and Israel continue to look to us to lead them from confrontation and war to a new era of accommodation and peace.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have no alternative but to persevere, and I am sure we will.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The opportunities for a final settlement are great, and the price of failure is a return to the bloodshed and hatred that for too long have brought tragedy to all of the peoples of this area and repeatedly edged the world to the brink of war.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Our relationship with the People's Republic of China is proving its importance and its durability.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We are finding more and more common ground between our two countries on basic questions of international affairs.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In my two trips to Asia as President, we have reaffirmed America's continuing vital interest in the peace and security of Asia and the Pacific Basin, established a new partnership with Japan, confirmed our dedication to the security of Korea, and reinforced our ties with the free nations of Southeast Asia.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: An historic dialog has begun between industrial nations and developing nations.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Most proposals on the table are the initiatives of the United States, including those on food, energy, technology, trade, investment, and commodities.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We are well launched on this process of shaping positive and reliable economic relations between rich nations and poor nations over the long term.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have made progress in trade negotiations and avoided protectionism during recession.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We strengthened the international monetary system.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: During the past 2 years the free world's most important economic powers have already brought about important changes that serve both developed and developing economies.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The momentum already achieved must be nurtured and strengthened, for the prosperity of the rich and poor depends upon it.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In Latin America, our relations have taken on a new maturity and a sense of common enterprise.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In Africa the quest for peace, racial justice, and economic progress is at a crucial point.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The United States, in close cooperation with the United Kingdom, is actively engaged in this historic process.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Will change come about by warfare and chaos and foreign intervention?

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Or will it come about by negotiated and fair solutions, ensuring majority rule, minority rights, and economic advance?

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: America is committed to the side of peace and justice and to the principle that Africa should shape its own future, free of outside intervention.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: American leadership has helped to stimulate new international efforts to stem the proliferation of nuclear weapons and to shape a comprehensive treaty governing the use of oceans.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I am gratified by these accomplishments.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: They constitute a record of broad success for America and for the peace and prosperity of all mankind.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This administration leaves to its successor a world in better condition than we found.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We leave, as well, a solid foundation for progress on a range of issues that are vital to the well-being of America.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: What has been achieved in the field of foreign affairs and what can be accomplished by the new administration demonstrate the genius of Americans working together for the common good.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It is this, our remarkable ability to work together, that has made us a unique nation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It is Congress, the President, and the people striving for a better world.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I know all patriotic Americans want this Nation's foreign policy to succeed.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I urge members of my party in this Congress to give the new President loyal support in this area.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I express the hope that this new Congress will reexamine its constitutional role in international affairs.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The exclusive right to declare war, the duty to advise and consent on the part of the Senate, the power of the purse on the part of the House are ample authority for the legislative branch and should be jealously guarded.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But because we may have been too careless of these powers in the past does not justify congressional intrusion into, or obstruction of, the proper exercise of Presidential responsibilities now or in the future.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: There can be only one Commander in Chief.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In these times crises cannot be managed and wars cannot be waged by committee, nor can peace be pursued solely by parliamentary debate.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To the ears of the world, the President speaks for the Nation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: While he is, of course, ultimately accountable to the Congress, the courts, and the people, he and his emissaries must not be handicapped in advance in their relations with foreign governments as has sometimes happened in the past.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: At home I am encouraged by the Nation's recovery from the recession and our steady return to sound economic growth.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It is now continuing after the recent period of uncertainty, which is part of the price we pay for free elections.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Our most pressing need today and the future is more jobs-- productive, permanent jobs created by a thriving economy.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must revise our tax system both to ease the burden of heavy taxation and to encourage the investment necessary for the creation of productive jobs for all Americans who want to work.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Earlier this month I proposed a permanent income tax reduction of $10 billion below current levels, including raising the personal exemption from $750 to $1,000.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I also recommended a series of measures to stimulate investment, such as accelerated depreciation for new plants and equipment in areas of high unemployment, a reduction in the corporate tax rate from 48 to 46 percent, and eliminating the present double taxation of dividends.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I strongly urge the Congress to pass these measures to help create the productive, permanent jobs in the private economy that are so essential for our future.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: All the basic trends are good;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: we are not on the brink of another recession or economic disaster.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: If we follow prudent policies that encourage productive investment and discourage destructive inflation, we will come out on top, and I am sure we will.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have successfully cut inflation by more than half.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: When I took office, the Consumer Price Index was rising at 12.2 percent a year.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: During 1976 the rate of inflation was 5 percent.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have created more jobs--over 4 million more jobs today than in the spring of 1975.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Throughout this Nation today we have over 88 million people in useful, productive jobs--more than at any other time in our Nation's history.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But there are still too many Americans unemployed.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This is the greatest regret that I have as I leave office.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We brought about with the Congress, after much delay, the renewal of the general revenue sharing.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We expanded community development and Federal manpower programs.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We began a significant urban mass transit program.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Federal programs today provide more funds for our States and local governments than ever before--$70 billion for the current fiscal year.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Through these programs and others that provide aid directly to individuals, we have kept faith with our tradition of compassionate help for those who need it.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: As we begin our third century we can be proud of the progress that we have made in meeting human needs for all of our citizens.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have cut the growth of crime by nearly 90 percent.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Two years ago crime was increasing at the rate of 18 percent annually.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In the first three quarters of 1976, that growth rate had been cut to 2 percent.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But crime, and the fear of crime, remains one of the most serious problems facing our citizens.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have had some successes, and there have been some disappointments.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Bluntly, I must remind you that we have not made satisfactory progress toward achieving energy independence.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Energy is absolutely vital to the defense of our country, to the strength of our economy, and to the quality of our lives.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Two years ago I proposed to the Congress the first comprehensive national energy program--a specific and coordinated set of measures that would end our vulnerability to embargo, blockade, or arbitrary price increases and would mobilize U.S. technology and resources to supply a significant share of the free world's energy after 1985.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Of the major energy proposals I submitted 2 years ago, only half, belatedly, became law.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In 1973 we were dependent upon foreign oil imports for 36 percent of our needs.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Today, we are 40-percent dependent, and we'll pay out $34 billion for foreign oil this year.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Such vulnerability at present or in the future is intolerable and must be ended.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The answer to where we stand on our national energy effort today reminds me of the old argument about whether the tank is half full or half empty.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The pessimist will say we have half failed to achieve our 10-year energy goals;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: the optimist will say that we have half succeeded.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I am always an optimist, but we must make up for lost time.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have laid a solid foundation for completing the enormous task which confronts us.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I have signed into law five major energy bills which contain significant measures for conservation, resource development, stockpiling, and standby authorities.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have moved forward to develop the naval petroleum reserves;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: to build a 500-million barrel strategic petroleum stockpile;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: to phase out unnecessary Government allocation and price controls;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: to develop a lasting relationship with other oil consuming nations;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: to improve the efficiency of energy use through conservation in automobiles, buildings, and industry;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: and to expand research on new technology and renewable resources such as wind power, geothermal and solar energy.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: All these actions, significant as they are for the long term, are only the beginning.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I recently submitted to the Congress my proposals to reorganize the Federal energy structure and the hard choices which remain if we are serious about reducing our dependence upon foreign energy.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: These include programs to reverse our declining production of natural gas and increase incentives for domestic crude oil production.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I proposed to minimize environmental uncertainties affecting coal development, expand nuclear power generation, and create an energy independence authority to provide government financial assistance for vital energy programs where private capital is not available.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must explore every reasonable prospect for meeting our energy needs when our current domestic reserves of oil and natural gas begin to dwindle in the next decade.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I urgently ask Congress and the new administration to move quickly on these issues.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This Nation has the resources and the capability to achieve our energy goals if its Government has the will to proceed, and I think we do.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I have been disappointed by inability to complete many of the meaningful organizational reforms which I contemplated for the Federal Government, although a start has been made.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: For example, the Federal judicial system has long served as a model for other courts.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But today it is threatened by a shortage of qualified Federal judges and an explosion of litigation claiming Federal jurisdiction.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: the needs of the Federal Courts.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I especially endorse its proposals for a new commission on the judicial appointment process.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: While the judicial branch of our Government may require reinforcement, the budgets and payrolls of the other branches remain staggering.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I cannot help but observe that while the White House staff and the Executive Office of the President have been reduced and the total number of civilians in the executive branch contained during the 1970's, the legislative branch has increased substantially although the membership of the Congress remains at 535.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Congress now costs the taxpayers more than a million dollars per Member;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: the whole legislative budget has passed the billion dollar mark.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I set out to reduce the growth in the size and spending of the Federal Government, but no President can accomplish this alone.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The Congress sidetracked most of my requests for authority to consolidate overlapping programs and agencies, to return more decisionmaking and responsibility to State and local governments through block grants instead of rigid categorical programs, and to eliminate unnecessary redtape and outrageously complex regulations.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We have made some progress in cutting back the expansion of government and its intrusion into individual lives, but believe me, there is much more to be done--and you and I know it.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It can only be done by tough and temporarily painful surgery by a Congress as prepared as the President to face up to this very real political problem.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Again, I wish my successor, working with a substantial majority of his own party, the best of success in reforming the costly and cumbersome machinery of the Federal Government.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The task of self-government is never finished.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The problems are great;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: the opportunities are greater.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: America's first goal is and always will be peace with honor.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: America must remain first in keeping peace in the world.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We can remain first in peace only if we are never second in defense.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In presenting the state of the Union to the Congress and to the American people, I have a special obligation as Commander in Chief to report on our national defense.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Our survival as a free and independent people requires, above all, strong military forces that are well equipped and highly trained to perform their assigned mission.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I am particularly gratified to report that over the past 2 1/2 years, we have been able to reverse the dangerous decline of the previous decade in real resources this country was devoting to national defense.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This was an immediate problem I faced in 1974.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The evidence was unmistakable that the Soviet Union had been steadily increasing the resources it applied to building its military strength.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: During this same period the United States real defense spending declined.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In my three budgets we not only arrested that dangerous decline, but we have established the positive trend which is essential to our ability to contribute to peace and stability in the world.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The Vietnam war, both materially and psychologically, affected our overall defense posture.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The dangerous antimilitary sentiment discouraged defense spending and unfairly disparaged the men and women who serve in our Armed Forces.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The challenge that now confronts this country is whether we have the national will and determination to continue this essential defense effort over the long term, as it must be continued.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We can no longer afford to oscillate from year to year in so vital a matter;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: indeed, we have a duty to look beyond the immediate question of budgets and to examine the nature of the problem we will face over the next generation.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I am the first recent President able to address long-term, basic issues without the burden of Vietnam.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The war in Indo-china consumed enormous resources at the very time that the overwhelming strategic superiority we once enjoyed was disappearing.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In past years, as a result of decisions by the United States, our strategic forces leveled off, yet the Soviet Union continued a steady, constant buildup of its own forces, committing a high percentage of its national economic effort to defense.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The United States can never tolerate a shift in strategic balance against us or even a situation where the American people or our allies believe the balance is shifting against us.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The United States would risk the most serious political consequences if the world came to believe that our adversaries have a decisive margin of superiority.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To maintain a strategic balance we must look ahead to the 1980's and beyond.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The sophistication of modern weapons requires that we make decisions now if we are to ensure our security 10 years from now.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Therefore, I have consistently advocated and strongly urged that we pursue three critical strategic programs: the Trident missile launching submarine;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: the B-1 bomber, with its superior capability to penetrate modern air defenses;

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: and a more advanced intercontinental ballistic missile that will be better able to survive nuclear attack and deliver a devastating retaliatory strike.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In an era where the strategic nuclear forces are in rough equilibrium, the risks of conflict below the nuclear threshold may grow more perilous.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: A major, long-term objective, therefore, is to maintain capabilities to deal with, and thereby deter, conventional challenges and crises, particularly in Europe.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We cannot rely solely on strategic forces to guarantee our security or to deter all types of aggression.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must have superior naval and marine forces to maintain freedom of the seas, strong multipurpose tactical air forces, and mobile, modern ground forces.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Accordingly, I have directed a long-term effort to improve our worldwide capabilities to deal with regional crises.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I have submitted a 5-year naval building program indispensable to the Nation's maritime strategy.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Because the security of Europe and the integrity of NATO remain the cornerstone of American defense policy, I have initiated a special, long-term program to ensure the capacity of the Alliance to deter or defeat aggression in Europe.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: As I leave office I can report that our national defense is effectively deterring conflict today.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Our Armed Forces are capable of carrying out the variety of missions assigned to them.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Programs are underway which will assure we can deter war in the years ahead.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: But I also must warn that it will require a sustained effort over a period of years to maintain these capabilities.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: We must have the wisdom, the stamina, and the courage to prepare today for the perils of tomorrow, and I believe we will.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: As I look to the future--and I assure you I intend to go on doing that for a good many years--I can say with confidence that the state of the Union is good, but we must go on making it better and better.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This gathering symbolizes the constitutional foundation which makes continued progress possible, synchronizing the skills of three independent branches of Government, reserving fundamental sovereignty to the people of this great land.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It is only as the temporary representatives and servants of the people that we meet here, we bring no hereditary status or gift of infallibility, and none follows us from this place.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Like President Washington, like the more fortunate of his successors, I look forward to the status of private citizen with gladness and gratitude.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: To me, being a citizen of the United States of America is the greatest honor and privilege in this world.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: From the opportunities which fate and my fellow citizens have given me, as a Member of the House, as Vice President and President of the Senate, and as President of all the people, I have come to understand and place the highest value on the checks and balances which our founders imposed on government through the separation of powers among co-equal legislative, executive, and judicial branches.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: This often results in difficulty and delay, as I well know, but it also places supreme authority under God, beyond any one person, any one branch, any majority great or small, or any one party.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: The Constitution is the bedrock of all our freedoms.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Guard and cherish it, keep honor and order in your own house, and the Republic will endure.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It is not easy to end these remarks.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: In this Chamber, along with some of you, I have experienced many, many of the highlights of my life.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It was here that I stood 28 years ago with my freshman colleagues, as Speaker Sam Rayburn administered the oath.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I see some of you now-- Charlie Bennett, Dick Bolling, Carl Perkins, Pete Rodino, Harley Staggers, Tom Steed, Sid Yates, Clem Zablocki--and I remember those who have gone to their rest.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It was here we waged many, many a lively battle--won some, lost some, but always remaining friends.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It was here, surrounded by such friends, that the distinguished Chief Justice swore me in as Vice President on December 6, 1973.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: It was here I returned 8 months later as your President to ask not for a honeymoon, but for a good marriage.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I will always treasure those memories and your many, many kindnesses.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: I thank you for them all.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: My fellow Americans, I once asked you for your prayers, and now I give you mine: May God guide this wonderful country, its people, and those they have chosen to lead them.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: May our third century be illuminated by liberty and blessed with brotherhood, so that we and all who come after us may be the humble servants of thy peace.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Amen.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: Good night.

speaker: Gerald R. Ford
text: God bless you.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Two years ago today we had the first caucus in Iowa, and one year ago tomorrow, I walked from here to the White House to take up the duties of President of the United States.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I didn't know it then when I walked, but I've been trying to save energy ever since.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I return tonight to fulfill one of those duties of the Constitution: to give to the Congress, and to the Nation, information on the state of the Union.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Militarily, politically, economically, and in spirit, the state of our Union is sound.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are a great country, a strong country, a vital and dynamic country, and so we will remain.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are a confident people and a hardworking people, a decent and a compassionate people, and so we will remain.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I want to speak to you tonight about where we are and where we must go, about what we have done and what we must do.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And I want to pledge to you my best efforts and ask you to pledge yours.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Each generation of Americans has to face circumstances not of its own choosing, but by which its character is measured and its spirit is tested.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: There are times of emergency, when a nation and its leaders must bring their energies to bear on a single urgent task.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: That was the duty Abraham Lincoln faced when our land was torn apart by conflict in the War Between the States.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: That was the duty faced by Franklin Roosevelt when he led America out of an economic depression and again when he led America to victory in war.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: There are other times when there is no single overwhelming crisis, yet profound national interests are at stake.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: At such times the risk of inaction can be equally great.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It becomes the task of leaders to call forth the vast and restless energies of our people to build for the future.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: That is what Harry Truman did in the years after the Second World War, when we helped Europe and Japan rebuild themselves and secured an international order that has protected freedom from aggression.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We live in such times now, and we face such duties.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've come through a long period of turmoil and doubt, but we've once again found our moral course, and with a new spirit, we are striving to express our best instincts to the rest of the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: There is all across our land a growing sense of peace and a sense of common purpose.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This sense of unity cannot be expressed in programs or in legislation or in dollars.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It's an achievement that belongs to every individual American.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This unity ties together, and it towers over all our efforts here in Washington, and it serves as an inspiring beacon for all of us who are elected to serve.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This new atmosphere demands a new spirit, a partnership between those of us who lead and those who elect.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
