text: The foundations of this partnership are truth, the courage to face hard decisions, concern for one another and the common good over special interests, and a basic faith and trust in the wisdom and strength and judgment of the American people.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: For the first time in a generation, we are not haunted by a major international crisis or by domestic turmoil, and we now have a rare and a priceless opportunity to address persistent problems and burdens which come to us as a nation, quietly and steadily getting worse over the years.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: As President, I've had to ask you, the Members of Congress, and you, the American people, to come to grips with some of the most difficult and hard questions facing our society.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must make a maximum effort, because if we do not aim for the best, we are very likely to achieve little.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I see no benefit to the country if we delay, because the problems will only get worse.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We need patience and good will, but we really need to realize that there is a limit to the role and the function of government.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Government cannot solve our problems, it can't set our goals, it cannot define our vision.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Government cannot eliminate poverty or provide a bountiful economy or reduce inflation or save our cities or cure illiteracy or provide energy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And government cannot mandate goodness.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Only a true partnership between government and the people can ever hope to reach these goals.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Those of us who govern can sometimes inspire, and we can identify needs and marshal resources, but we simply cannot be the managers of everything and everybody.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We here in Washington must move away from crisis management, and we must establish clear goals for the future, immediate and the distant future, which will let us work together and not in conflict.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Never again should we neglect a growing crisis like the shortage of energy, where further delay will only lead to more harsh and painful solutions.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Every day we spend more than $120 million for foreign oil.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This slows our economic growth, it lowers the value of the dollar overseas, and it aggravates unemployment and inflation here at home.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Now we know what we must do, increase production.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must cut down on waste.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And we must use more of those fuels which are plentiful and more permanent.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must be fair to people, and we must not disrupt our Nation's economy and our budget.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Now, that sounds simple.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But I recognize the difficulties involved.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I know that it is not easy for the Congress to act.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But the fact remains that on the energy legislation, we have failed the American people.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Almost 5 years after the oil embargo dramatized the problem for us all, we still do not have a national energy program.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Not much longer can we tolerate this stalemate.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It undermines our national interest both at home and abroad.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must succeed, and I believe we will.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our main task at home this year, with energy a central element, is the Nation's economy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must continue the recovery and further cut unemployment and inflation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Last year was a good one for the United States.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We reached all of our major economic goals for 1977.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Four million new jobs were created, an all-time record, and the number of unemployed dropped by more than a million.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Unemployment right now is the lowest it has been since 1974, and not since World War II has such a high percentage of American people been employed.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The rate of inflation went down.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: There was a good growth in business profits and investments, the source of more jobs for our workers, and a higher standard of living for all our people.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: After taxes and inflation, there was a healthy increase in workers' wages.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And this year, our country will have the first $2 trillion economy in the history of the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Now, we are proud of this progress the first year, but we must do even better in the future.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We still have serious problems on which all of us must work together.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our trade deficit is too large.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Inflation is still too high, and too many Americans still do not have a job.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Now, I didn't have any simple answers for all these problems.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But we have developed an economic policy that is working, because it's simple, balanced, and fair.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It's based on four principles:   First, the economy must keep on expanding to produce   new jobs and better income, which our people need.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The   fruits of growth must be widely shared.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: More jobs must   be made available to those who have been bypassed   until now.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And the tax system must be made fairer and   simpler.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Secondly, private business and not the Government must   lead the expansion in the future.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Third, we must lower the rate of inflation and keep it   down.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Inflation slows down economic growth, and it's   the most cruel to the poor and also to the elderly and   others who live on fixed incomes.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And fourth, we must contribute to the strength of the   world economy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I will announce detailed proposals for improving our tax system later this week.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We can make our tax laws fairer, we can make them simpler and easier to understand, and at the same time, we can, and we will, reduce the tax burden on American citizens by $25 billion.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The tax reforms and the tax reductions go together.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Only with the long overdue reforms will the full tax cut be advisable.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Almost $17 billion in income tax cuts will go to individuals.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Ninety-six percent of all American taxpayers will see their taxes go down.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: For a typical family of four, this means an annual saving of more than $250 a year, or a tax reduction of about 20 percent.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: A further $2 billion cut in excise taxes will give more relief and also contribute directly to lowering the rate of inflation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And we will also provide strong additional incentives for business investment and growth through substantial cuts in the corporate tax rates and improvement in the investment tax credit.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Now, these tax proposals will increase opportunity everywhere in the Nation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But additional jobs for the disadvantaged deserve special attention.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've already passed laws to assure equal access to the voting booth and to restaurants and to schools, to housing, and laws to permit access to jobs.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But job opportunity, the chance to earn a decent living, is also a basic human right, which we cannot and will not ignore.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: A major priority for our Nation is the final elimination of the barriers that restrict the opportunities available to women and also to black people and Hispanics and other minorities.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've come a long way toward that goal.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But there is still much to do.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: What we inherited from the past must not be permitted to shackle us in the future.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I'll be asking you for a substantial increase in funds for public jobs for our young people, and I also am recommending that the Congress continue the public service employment programs at more than twice the level of a year ago.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: When welfare reform is completed, we will have more than a million additional jobs so that those on welfare who are able to work can work.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: However, again, we know that in our free society, private business is still the best source of new jobs.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Therefore, I will propose a new program to encourage businesses to hire young and disadvantaged Americans.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: These young people only need skills and a chance in order to take their place in our economic system.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Let's give them the chance they need.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: A major step in the right direction would be the early passage of a greatly improved Humphrey-Hawkins bill.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: My budget for 1979 addresses these national needs, but it is lean and tight.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I have cut waste wherever possible.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I am proposing an increase of less than 2 percent after adjusting for inflation, the smallest increase in the Federal budget in 4 years.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Lately, Federal spending has taken a steadily increasing portion of what Americans produce.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our new budget reverses that trend, and later I hope to bring the Government's toll down even further.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And with your help, we'll do that.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In time of high employment and a strong economy, deficit spending should not be a feature of our budget.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: As the economy continues to gain strength and as our unemployment rates continue to fall, revenues will grow.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: With careful planning, efficient management, and proper restraint on spending, we can move rapidly toward a balanced budget, and we will.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Next year the budget deficit will be only slightly less than this year.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But one-third of the deficit is due to the necessary tax cuts that I've proposed.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This year the right choice is to reduce the burden on taxpayers and provide more jobs for our people.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The third element in our program is a renewed attack on inflation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've learned the hard way that high unemployment will not prevent or cure inflation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Government can help us by stimulating private investment and by maintaining a responsible economic policy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Through a new top-level review process, we will do a better job of reducing Government regulation that drives up costs and drives up prices.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But again, Government alone cannot bring down the rate of inflation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: When a level of high inflation is expected to continue, then companies raise prices to protect their profit margins against prospective increases in wages and other costs, while workers demand higher wages as protection against expected price increases.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It's like an escalation in the arms race, and understandably, no one wants to disarm alone.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Now, no one firm or a group of workers can halt this process.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It's an effort that we must all make together.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I'm therefore asking government, business, labor, and other groups to join in a voluntary program to moderate inflation by holding wage and price increases in each sector of the economy during 1978 below the average increases of the last 2 years.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I do not believe in wage and price controls.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: A sincere commitment to voluntary constraint provides a way, perhaps the only way, to fight inflation without Government interference.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: As I came into the Capitol tonight, I saw the farmers, my fellow farmers, standing out in the snow.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I'm familiar with their problem, and I know from Congress' action that you are too.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: When I was running Carters Warehouse, we had spread on our own farms 5-10-15 fertilizer for about $40 a ton.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The last time I was home, the price was about $100 a ton.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The cost of nitrogen has gone up 150 percent, and the price of products that farmers sell has either stayed the same or gone down a little.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Now, this past year in 1977, you, the Congress, and I together passed a new agricultural act.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It went into effect October 1.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It'll have its first impact on the 1978 crops.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It will help a great deal.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It'll add $6 1/2 billion or more to help the farmers with their price supports and target prices.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Last year we had the highest level of exports of farm products in the history of our country, $24 billion.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We expect to have more this year.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We'll be working together.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But I think it's incumbent on us to monitor very carefully the farm situation and continue to work harmoniously with the farmers of our country.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: What's best for the farmers, the farm families, in the long run is also best for the consumers of our country.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Economic success at home is also the key to success in our international economic policy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: An effective energy program, strong investment and productivity, and controlled inflation will provide [improve] our trade balance and balance it, and it will help to protect the integrity of the dollar overseas.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: By working closely with our friends abroad, we can promote the economic health of the whole world, with fair and balanced agreements lowering the barriers to trade.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Despite the inevitable pressures that build up when the world economy suffers from high unemployment, we must firmly resist the demands for self-defeating protectionism.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But free trade must also be fair trade.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And I am determined to protect American industry and American workers against foreign trade practices which are unfair or illegal.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In a separate written message to Congress, I've outlined other domestic initiatives, such as welfare reform, consumer protection, basic education skills, urban policy, reform of our labor laws, and national health care later on this year.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I will not repeat these tonight.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But there are several other points that I would like to make directly to you.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: During these past years, Americans have seen our Government grow far from us.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: For some citizens, the Government has almost become like a foreign country, so strange and distant that we've often had to deal with it through trained ambassadors who have sometimes become too powerful and too influential, lawyers, accountants, and lobbyists.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This cannot go on.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must have what Abraham Lincoln wanted, a government for the people.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've made progress toward that kind of government.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: You've given me the authority I requested to reorganize the Federal bureaucracy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And I am using that authority.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've already begun a series of reorganization plans which will be completed over a period of 3 years.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We have also proposed abolishing almost 500 Federal advisory and other commissions and boards.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But I know that the American people are still sick and tired of Federal paperwork and red tape.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Bit by bit we are chopping down the thicket of unnecessary Federal regulations by which Government too often interferes in our personal lives and our personal business.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've cut the public's Federal paperwork load by more than 12 percent in less than a year.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And we are not through cutting.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've made a good start on turning the gobbledygook of Federal regulations into plain English that people can understand.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But we know that we still have a long way to go.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've brought together parts of 11 Government agencies to create a new Department of Energy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And now it's time to take another major step by creating a separate Department of Education.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But even the best organized Government will only be as effective as the people who carry out its policies.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: For this reason, I consider civil service reform to be absolutely vital.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Worked out with the civil servants themselves, this reorganization plan will restore the merit principle to a system which has grown into a bureaucratic maze.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It will provide greater management flexibility and better rewards for better performance without compromising job security.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Then and only then can we have a government that is efficient, open, and truly worthy of our people's understanding and respect.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I have promised that we will have such a government, and I intend to keep that promise.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In our foreign policy, the separation of people from government has been in the past a source of weakness and error.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In a democratic system like ours, foreign policy decisions must be able to stand the test of public examination and public debate.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: If we make a mistake in this administration, it will be on the side of frankness and openness with the American people.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In our modern world, when the deaths of literally millions of people can result from a few terrifying seconds of destruction, the path of national strength and security is identical to the path of peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Tonight, I am happy to report that because we are strong, our Nation is at peace with the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are a confident nation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've restored a moral basis for our foreign policy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The very heart of our identity as a nation is our firm commitment to human rights.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We stand for human rights because we believe that government has as a purpose to promote the well-being of its citizens.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This is true in our domestic policy; it's also true in our foreign policy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The world must know that in support of human rights, the United States will stand firm.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We expect no quick or easy results, but there has been significant movement toward greater freedom and humanity in several parts of the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Thousands of political prisoners have been freed.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The leaders of the world, even our ideological adversaries, now see that their attitude toward fundamental human rights affects their standing in the international community, and it affects their relations with the United States.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: To serve the interests of every American, our foreign policy has three major goals.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The first and prime concern is and will remain the security of our country.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Security is based on our national will, and security is based on the strength of our Armed Forces.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We have the will, and militarily we are very strong.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Security also comes through the strength of our alliances.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We have reconfirmed our commitment to the defense of Europe, and this year we will demonstrate that commitment by further modernizing and strengthening our military capabilities there.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Security can also be enhanced by agreements with potential adversaries which reduce the threat of nuclear disaster while maintaining our own relative strategic capability.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In areas of peaceful competition with the Soviet Union, we will continue to more than hold our own.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: At the same time, we are negotiating with quiet confidence, without haste, with careful determination, to ease the tensions between us and to ensure greater stability and security.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The strategic arms limitation talks have been long and difficult.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We want a mutual limit on both the quality and the quantity of the giant nuclear arsenals of both nations, and then we want actual reductions in strategic arms as a major step toward the ultimate elimination of nuclear weapons from the face of the Earth.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: If these talks result in an agreement this year, and I trust they will, I pledge to you that the agreement will maintain and enhance the stability of the world's strategic balance and the security of the United States.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: For 30 years, concerted but unsuccessful efforts have been made to ban the testing of atomic explosives, both military weapons and peaceful nuclear devices.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are hard at work with Great Britain and the Soviet Union on an agreement which will stop testing and will protect our national security and provide for adequate verification of compliance.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are now making, I believe, good progress toward this comprehensive ban on nuclear explosions.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are also working vigorously to halt the proliferation of nuclear weapons among the nations of the world which do not now have them and to reduce the deadly global traffic in conventional arms sales.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our stand for peace is suspect if we are also the principal arms merchant of the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: So, we've decided to cut down our arms transfers abroad on a year-by-year basis and to work with other major arms exporters to encourage their similar constraint.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Every American has a stake in our second major goal, a world at peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In a nuclear age, each of us is threatened when peace is not secured everywhere.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are trying to promote harmony in those parts of the world where major differences exist among other nations and threaten international peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In the Middle East, we are contributing our good offices to maintain the momentum of the current negotiations and to keep open the lines of communication among the Middle Eastern leaders.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The whole world has a great stake in the success of these efforts.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This is a precious opportunity for a historic settlement of a longstanding conflict, an opportunity which may never come again in our lifetime.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our role has been difficult and sometimes thankless and controversial.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But it has been constructive and it has been necessary, and it will continue.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our third major foreign policy goal is one that touches the life of every American citizen every day, world economic growth and stability.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This requires strong economic performance by the industrialized democracies like ourselves and progress in resolving the global energy crisis.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Last fall, with the help of others, we succeeded in our vigorous efforts to maintain the stability of the price of oil.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But as many foreign leaders have emphasized to me personally and, I am sure, to you, the greatest future contribution that America can make to the world economy would be an effective energy conservation program here at home.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We will not hesitate to take the actions needed to protect the integrity of the American dollar.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are trying to develop a more just international system.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And in this spirit, we are supporting the struggle for human development in Africa, in Asia, and in Latin America.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Finally, the world is watching to see how we act on one of our most important and controversial items of business, approval of the Panama Canal treaties.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The treaties now before the Senate are the result of the work of four administrations, two Democratic, two Republican.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: They guarantee that the canal will be open always for unrestricted use by the ships of the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our ships have the right to go to the head of the line for priority of passage in times of emergency or need.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We retain the permanent right to defend the canal with our own military forces, if necessary, to guarantee its openness and its neutrality.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The treaties are to the clear advantage of ourselves, the Panamanians, and the other users of the canal.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Ratifying the Panama Canal treaties will demonstrate our good faith to the world, discourage the spread of hostile ideologies in this hemisphere, and directly contribute to the economic well-being and the security of the United States.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I have to say that that's very welcome applause.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: There were two moments on my recent journey which, for me, confirmed the final aims of our foreign policy and what it always must be.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: One was in a little village in India, where I met a people as passionately attached to their rights and liberties as we are, but whose children have a far smaller chance for good health or food or education or human fulfillment than a child born in this country.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The other moment was in Warsaw, capital of a nation twice devastated by war in this century.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: There, people have rebuilt the city which war's destruction took from them.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But what was new only emphasized clearly what was lost.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: What I saw in those two places crystallized for me the purposes of our own Nation's policy: to ensure economic justice, to advance human rights, to resolve conflicts without violence, and to proclaim in our great democracy our constant faith in the liberty and dignity of human beings everywhere.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We Americans have a great deal of work to do together.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In the end, how well we do that work will depend on the spirit in which we approach it.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must seek fresh answers, unhindered by the stale prescriptions of the past.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It has been said that our best years are behind us.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But I say again that America's best is still ahead.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We have emerged from bitter experiences chastened but proud, confident once again, ready to face challenges once again, and united once again.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We come together tonight at a solemn time.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Last week the Senate lost a good and honest man, Lee Metcalf of Montana.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And today, the flag of the United States flew at half-mast from this Capitol and from American installations and ships all over the world, in mourning for Senator Hubert Humphrey.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Because he exemplified so well the joy and the zest of living, his death reminds us not so much of our own mortality, but of the possibilities offered to us by life.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: He always looked to the future with a special American kind of confidence, of hope and enthusiasm.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And the best way that we can honor him is by following his example.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: reconciliation, rebuilding, and rebirth.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Reconciliation of private needs and interests into a higher purpose.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Rebuilding the old dreams of justice and liberty, and country and community.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Rebirth of our faith in the common good.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Each of us here tonight, and all who are listening in your homes, must rededicate ourselves to serving the common good.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are a community, a beloved community, all of us.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our individual fates are linked, our futures intertwined.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And if we act in that knowledge and in that spirit, together, as the Bible says, we can move mountains.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Thank you very much.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Tonight I want to examine in a broad sense the state of our American Union--how we are building a new foundation for a peaceful and a prosperous world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our children who will be born this year will come of age in the 21st century.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: What kind of society, what kind of world are we building for them?

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Will we ourselves be at peace?

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Will our children enjoy a better quality of life?

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Will a strong and united America still be a force for freedom and prosperity around the world?

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Tonight, there is every sign that the state of our Union is sound.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our economy offers greater prosperity for more of our people than ever before.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Real per capita income and real business profits have risen substantially in the last 2 years.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Farm exports are setting an all-time record each year, and farm income last year, net farm income, was up more than 25 percent.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our liberties are secure.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our military defenses are strong and growing stronger.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And more importantly, tonight, America--our beloved country--is at peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our earliest national commitments, modified and reshaped by succeeding generations, have served us well.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But the problems that we face today are different from those that confronted earlier generations of Americans.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: They are more subtle, more complex, and more interrelated.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: At home, we are recognizing ever more clearly that government alone cannot solve these problems.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And abroad, few of them can be solved by the United States alone.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But Americans as a united people, working with our allies and friends, have never been afraid to face problems and to solve problems, either here or abroad.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The challenge to us is to build a new and firmer foundation for the future--for a sound economy, for a more effective government, for more political trust, and for a stable peace--so that the America our children inherit will be even stronger and even better than it is today.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We cannot resort to simplistic or extreme solutions which substitute myths for common sense.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In our economy, it is a myth that we must choose endlessly between inflation and recession.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Together, we build the foundation for a strong economy, with lower inflation, without contriving either a recession with its high unemployment or unworkable, mandatory government controls.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In our government, it is a myth that we must choose between compassion and competence.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Together, we build the foundation for a government that works, and works for people.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In our relations with our potential adversaries, it is a myth that we must choose between confrontation and capitulation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Together, we build the foundation for a stable world of both diversity and peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Together, we've already begun to build the foundation for confidence in our economic system.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: During the last 2 years, in bringing our economy out of the deepest recession since the 1930's, we've created 7,100,000 new jobs.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The unemployment rate has gone down 25 percent.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And now we must redouble our fight against the persistent inflation that has wracked our country for more than a decade.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: That's our important domestic issue, and we must do it together.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We know that inflation is a burden for all Americans, but it's a disaster for the poor, the sick, and the old.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: No American family should be forced to choose among food, warmth, health care, or decent housing because the cost of any of these basic necessities has climbed out of reach.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Three months ago, I outlined to the Nation a balanced anti-inflation program that couples responsible government restraint with responsible wage and price restraint.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It's based upon my knowledge that there is a more powerful force than government compulsion--the force created by the cooperative efforts of millions of Americans working toward a common goal.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Business and labor have been increasingly supportive.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It's imperative that we in government do our part.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must stop excessive government growth, and we must control government spending habits.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I've sent to this Congress a stringent but a fair budget, one that, since I ran for President in 1976, will have cut the Federal deficit in half.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And as a percentage of our gross national product, the deficit will have dropped by almost 75 percent.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This Congress had a good record last year, and I now ask the 96th Congress to continue this partnership in holding the line on excess Federal spending.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It will not be easy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But we must be strong, and we must be persistent.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This budget is a clear message that, with the help of you and the American people, I am determined, as President, to bring inflation under control.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The 1980 budget provides enough spending restraint to begin unwinding inflation, but enough support for our country to keep American workers productive and to encourage the investments that provide new jobs.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We will continue to mobilize our Nation's resources to reduce our trade deficit substantially this year and to maintain the strength of the American dollar.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've demonstrated in this restrained budget that we can build on the gains of the past 2 years to provide additional support to educate disadvantaged children, to care for the elderly, to provide nutrition and legal services for the poor, and to strengthen the economic base of our urban communities and, also, our rural areas.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This year, we will take our first steps to develop a national health plan.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must never accept a permanent group of unemployed Americans, with no hope and no stake in building our society.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: For those left out of the economy because of discrimination, a lack of skills, or poverty, we must maintain high levels of training, and we must continue to provide jobs.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: A responsible budget is not our only weapon to control inflation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must act now to protect all Americans from health care costs that are rising $1 million per hour, 24 hours a day, doubling every 5 years.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must take control of the largest contributor to that inflation: skyrocketing hospital costs.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: There will be no clearer test of the commitment of this Congress to the anti-inflation fight than the legislation that I will submit again this year to hold down inflation in hospital care.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Over the next 5 years, my proposals will save Americans a total of $60 billion, of which $25 billion will be savings to the American taxpayer in the Federal budget itself.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The American people have waited long enough.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This year we must act on hospital cost containment.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must also fight inflation by improvements and better enforcement of our antitrust laws and by reducing government obstacles to competition in the private sector.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must begin to scrutinize the overall effect of regulation in our economy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Through deregulation of the airline industry we've increased profits, cut prices for all Americans, and begun--for one of the few times in the history of our Nation--to actually dismantle a major Federal bureaucracy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This year, we must begin the effort to reform our regulatory processes for the railroad, bus, and the trucking industries.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: America has the greatest economic system in the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Let's reduce government interference and give it a chance to work.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I call on Congress to take other anti-inflation action--to expand our exports to protect American jobs threatened by unfair trade, to conserve energy, to increase production and to speed development of solar power, and to reassess our Nation's technological superiority.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: American workers who enlist in the fight against inflation deserve not just our gratitude, but they deserve the protection of the real wage insurance proposal that I have already made to the Congress.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: To be successful, we must change our attitudes as well as our policies.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We cannot afford to live beyond our means.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We cannot afford to create programs that we can neither manage nor finance, or to waste our natural resources, and we cannot tolerate mismanagement and fraud.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Above all, we must meet the challenges of inflation as a united people.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: With the support of the American people, government in recent decades has helped to dismantle racial barriers, has provided assistance for the jobless and the retired, has fed the hungry, has protected the safety, health, and bargaining rights of American workers, and has helped to preserve our natural heritage.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But it's not enough to have created a lot of government programs.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Now we must make the good programs more effective and improve or weed out those which are wasteful or unnecessary.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: With the support of the Congress, we've begun to reorganize and to get control of the bureaucracy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are reforming the civil service system, so that we can recognize and reward those who do a good job and correct or remove those who do not.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This year, we must extend major reorganization efforts to education, to economic development, and to the management of our natural resources.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We need to enact a sunshine [sunset] law that when government programs have outlived their value, they will automatically be terminated.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: There's no such thing as an effective and a noncontroversial reorganization and reform.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But we know that honest, effective government is essential to restore public faith in our public action.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: None of us can be satisfied when two-thirds of the American citizens chose not to vote last year in a national election.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Too many Americans feel powerless against the influence of private lobbying groups and the unbelievable flood of private campaign money which threatens our electoral process.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This year, we must regain the public's faith by requiring limited financial funds from public funds for congressional election campaigns.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: House bill 1 provides for this public financing of campaigns.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And I look forward with a great deal of anticipation to signing it at an early date.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: A strong economy and an effective government will restore confidence in America.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But the path of the future must be charted in peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must continue to build a new and a firm foundation for a stable world community.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are building that new foundation from a position of national strength--the strength of our own defenses, the strength of our friendships with other nations, and of our oldest American ideals.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: America's military power is a major force for security and stability in the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must maintain our strategic capability and continue the progress of the last 2 years with our NATO Allies, with whom we have increased our readiness, modernized our equipment, and stren than doubled, colonial empires have disappeared, and a hundred new nations have been born, and migration to the world's cities have all awakened new yearnings for economic justice and human rights among people everywhere.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This demand for justice and human rights is a wave of the future.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In such a world, the choice is not which super power will dominate the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: None can and none will.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The choice instead is between a world of anarchy and destruction, or a world of cooperation and peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In such a world, we seek not to stifle inevitable change, but to influence its course in helpful and constructive ways that enhance our values, our national interests, and the cause of peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Towering over this volatile, changing world, like a thundercloud on a summer day, looms the awesome power of nuclear weapons.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We will continue to help shape the forces of change, to anticipate emerging problems of nuclear proliferation and conventional arms sales, and to use our great strength parts of the world before they erupt and spread.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We have no desire to be the world's policeman.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But America does want to be the world's peacemaker.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are building the foundation for truly global cooperation, not only with Western and industrialized nations but with the developing countries as well.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our ties with Japan and our European allies are stronger than ever, and so are our friendly relations with the people of Latin America, Africa, and the Western Pacific and Asia.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've won new respect in this hemisphere with the Panama Canal treaties.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've gained new trust with the developing world through our opposition to racism, our commitment to human rights, and our support for majority rule in Africa.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The multilateral trade negotiations are now reaching a successful conclusion, and congressional approval is essential to the economic well-being of our own country and of the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This will be one of our top priorities in 1979.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are entering a hopeful era in our relations with one-fourth of the world's people who live in China.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The presence of Vice Premier Deng Xiaoping next week will help to inaugurate that new era.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And with prompt congressional action on authorizing legislation, we will continue our commitment to a prosperous, peaceful, and secure life for the people of Taiwan.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I'm grateful that in the past year, as in the year before, no American has died in combat anywhere in the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And in Iran, Nicaragua, Cyprus, Namibia, and Rhodesia, our country is working for peaceful solutions to dangerous conflicts.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In the Middle East, under the most difficult circumstances, we have sought to help ancient enemies lay aside deep-seated differences that have produced four bitter wars in our lifetime.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our firm commitment to Israel's survival and security is rooted in our deepest convictions and in our knowledge of the strategic importance to our own Nation of a stable Middle East.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: To promote peace and reconciliation in the region, we must retain the trust and the confidence both of Israel and also of the Arab nations that are sincerely searching for peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I am determined, as President, to use the full, beneficial influence of our country so that the precious opportunity for lasting peace between Israel and Egypt will not be lost.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The new foundation of international cooperation that we seek excludes no nation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Cooperation with the Soviet Union serves the cause of peace, for in this nuclear age, world peace must include peace between the super powers--and it must mean the control of nuclear arms.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Ten years ago, the United States and the Soviet Union made the historic decision to open the strategic arms limitations talks, or SALT.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The purpose of SALT, then as now, is not to gain a unilateral advantage for either nation, but to protect the security of both nations, to reverse the costly and dangerous momentum of the nuclear arms race, to preserve a stable balance of nuclear forces, and to demonstrate to a concerned world that we are determined to help preserve the peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The first SALT agreement was concluded in 1972.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And since then, during 6 years of negotiation by both Republican and Democratic leaders, nearly all issues of SALT II have been resolved.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: If the Soviet Union continues to negotiate in good faith, a responsible SALT agreement will be reached.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It's important that the American people understand the nature of the SALT process.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: SALT II is not based on sentiment; it's based on self-interest-- of the United States and of the Soviet Union.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Both nations share a powerful common interest in reducing the threat of a nuclear war.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I will sign no agreement which does not enhance our national security.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: SALT II does not rely on trust;

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: it will be verifiable.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We have very sophisticated, proven means, including our satellites, to determine for ourselves whether or not the Soviet Union is meeting its treaty obligations.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I will sign no agreement which cannot be verified.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The American nuclear deterrent will remain strong after SALT II.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: For example, just one of our relatively invulnerable Poseidon submarines--comprising less than 2 percent of our total nuclear force of submarines, aircraft, and land-based missiles--carries enough warheads to destroy every large- and medium-sized city in the Soviet Union.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our deterrent is overwhelming, and I will sign no agreement unless our deterrent force will remain overwhelming.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: A SALT agreement, of course, cannot substitute for wise diplomacy or a strong defense, nor will it end the danger of nuclear war.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But it will certainly reduce that danger.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It will strengthen our efforts to ban nuclear tests and to stop the spread of atomic weapons to other nations.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And it can begin the process of negotiating new agreements which will further limit nuclear arms.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The path of arms control, backed by a strong defense, the path our Nation and every President has walked for 30 years, can lead to a world of law and of international negotiation and consultation in which all peoples might live in peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In this year 1979, nothing is more important than that the Congress and the people of the United States resolve to continue with me on that path of nuclear arms control and world peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This is paramount.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I've outlined some of the changes that have transformed the world and which are continuing as we meet here tonight.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But we in America need not fear change.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The values on which our Nation was founded: individual liberty, self-determination, the potential for human fulfillment in freedom, all of these endure.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We find these democratic principles praised, even in books smuggled out of totalitarian nations and on wall posters in lands which we thought were closed to our influence.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our country has regained its special place of leadership in the worldwide struggle for human rights.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And that is a commitment that we must keep at home, as well as abroad.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The civil rights revolution freed all Americans, black and white, but its full promise still remains unrealized.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I will continue to work with all my strength for equal opportunity for all Americans--and for affirmative action for those who carry the extra burden of past denial of equal opportunity.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We remain committed to improving our labor laws to better protect the rights of American workers.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And our Nation must make it clear that the legal rights of women as citizens are guaranteed under the laws of our land by ratifying the equal rights amendment.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: As long as I'm President, at home and around the world America's examples and America's influence will be marshaled to advance the cause of human rights.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: To establish those values, two centuries ago a bold generation of Americans risked their property, their position, and life itself.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are their heirs, and they are sending us a message across the centuries.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The words they made so vivid are now growing faintly indistinct, because they are not heard often enough.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: love.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: These words remind us that the duty of our generation of Americans is to renew our Nation's faith, not focused just against foreign threats but against the threats of selfishness, cynicism, and apathy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The new foundation I've discussed tonight can help us build a nation and a world where every child is nurtured and can look to the future with hope, where the resources now wasted on war can be turned towards meeting human needs, where all people have enough to eat, a decent home, and protection against disease.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It can help us build a nation and a world where all people are free to seek the truth and to add to human understanding, so that all of us may live our lives in peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Tonight, I ask you, the Members of the Congress, to join me in building that new foundation, a better foundation, for our beloved country and our world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Thank you very much.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This last few months has not been an easy time for any of us.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: As we meet tonight, it has never been more clear that the state of our Union depends on the state of the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And tonight, as throughout our own generation, freedom and peace in the world depend on the state of our Union.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The 1980's have been born in turmoil, strife, and change.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This is a time of challenge to our interests and our values and it's a time that tests our wisdom and our skills.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: At this time in Iran, 50 Americans are still held captive, innocent victims of terrorism and anarchy.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Also at this moment, massive Soviet troops are attempting to subjugate the fiercely independent and deeply religious people of Afghanistan.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: These two acts--one of international terrorism and one of military aggression--present a serious challenge to the United States of America and indeed to all the nations of the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Together, we will meet these threats to peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I'm determined that the United States will remain the strongest of all nations, but our power will never be used to initiate a threat to the security of any nation or to the rights of any human being.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We seek to be and to remain secure--a nation at peace in a stable world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But to be secure we must face the world as it is.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Three basic developments have helped to shape our challenges: the steady growth and increased projection of Soviet military power beyond its own borders;

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: the overwhelming dependence of the Western democracies on oil supplies from the Middle East;

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: and the press of social and religious and economic and political change in the many nations of the developing world, exemplified by the revolution in Iran.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Each of these factors is important in its own right.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Each interacts with the others.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: All must be faced together, squarely and courageously.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We will face these challenges, and we will meet them with the best that is in us.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And we will not fail.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In response to the abhorrent act in Iran, our Nation has never been aroused and unified so greatly in peacetime.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our position is clear.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The United States will not yield to blackmail.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We continue to pursue these specific goals: first, to protect the present and long-range interests of the United States;

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: secondly, to preserve the lives of the American hostages and to secure, as quickly as possible, their safe release, if possible, to avoid bloodshed which might further endanger the lives of our fellow citizens;

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: to enlist the help of other nations in condemning this act of violence, which is shocking and violates the moral and the legal standards of a civilized world;

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: and also to convince and to persuade the Iranian leaders that the real danger to their nation lies in the north, in the Soviet Union and from the Soviet troops now in Afghanistan, and that the unwarranted Iranian quarrel with the United States hampers their response to this far greater danger to them.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: If the American hostages are harmed, a severe price will be paid.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We will never rest until every one of the American hostages are released.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But now we face a broader and more fundamental challenge in this region because of the recent military action of the Soviet Union.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Now, as during the last 3 1/2 decades, the relationship between our country, the United States of America, and the Soviet Union is the most critical factor in determining whether the world will live at peace or be engulfed in global conflict.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Since the end of the Second World War, America has led other nations in meeting the challenge of mounting Soviet power.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This has not been a simple or a static relationship.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Between us there has been cooperation, there has been competition, and at times there has been confrontation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In the 1940's we took the lead in creating the Atlantic Alliance in response to the Soviet Union's suppression and then consolidation of its East European empire and the resulting threat of the Warsaw Pact to Western Europe.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In the 1950's we helped to contain further Soviet challenges in Korea and in the Middle East, and we rearmed to assure the continuation of that containment.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In the 1960's we met the Soviet challenges in Berlin, and we faced the Cuban missile crisis.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And we sought to engage the Soviet Union in the important task of moving beyond the cold war and away from confrontation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And in the 1970's three American Presidents negotiated with the Soviet leaders in attempts to halt the growth of the nuclear arms race.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We sought to establish rules of behavior that would reduce the risks of conflict, and we searched for areas of cooperation that could make our relations reciprocal and productive, not only for the sake of our two nations but for the security and peace of the entire world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In all these actions, we have maintained two commitments: to be ready to meet any challenge by Soviet military power, and to develop ways to resolve disputes and to keep the peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Preventing nuclear war is the foremost responsibility of the two superpowers.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: That's why we've negotiated the strategic arms limitation treaties--SALT I and SALT II.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Especially now, in a time of great tension, observing the mutual constraints imposed by the terms of these treaties will be in the best interest of both countries and will help to preserve world peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I will consult very closely with the Congress on this matter as we strive to control nuclear weapons.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: That effort to control nuclear weapons will not be abandoned.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We superpowers also have the responsibility to exercise restraint in the use of our great military force.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The integrity and the independence of weaker nations must not be threatened.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: They must know that in our presence they are secure.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But now the Soviet Union has taken a radical and an aggressive new step.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It's using its great military power against a relatively defenseless nation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The implications of the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan could pose the most serious threat to the peace since the Second World War.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The vast majority of nations on Earth have condemned this latest Soviet attempt to extend its colonial domination of others and have demanded the immediate withdrawal of Soviet troops.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The Moslem world is especially and justifiably outraged by this aggression against an Islamic people.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: No action of a world power has ever been so quickly and so overwhelmingly condemned.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But verbal condemnation is not enough.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The Soviet Union must pay a concrete price for their aggression.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: While this invasion continues, we and the other nations of the world cannot conduct business as usual with the Soviet Union.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: That's why the United States has imposed stiff economic penalties on the Soviet Union.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I will not issue any permits for Soviet ships to fish in the coastal waters of the United States.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I've cut Soviet access to high-technology equipment and to agricultural products.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I've limited other commerce with the Soviet Union, and I've asked our allies and friends to join with us in restraining their own trade with the Soviets and not to replace our own embargoed items.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And I have notified the Olympic Committee that with Soviet invading forces in Afghanistan, neither the American people nor I will support sending an Olympic team to Moscow.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The Soviet Union is going to have to answer some basic questions: Will it help promote a more stable international environment in which its own legitimate, peaceful concerns can be pursued?

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Or will it continue to expand its military power far beyond its genuine security needs, and use that power for colonial conquest?

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The Soviet Union must realize that its decision to use military force in Afghanistan will be costly to every political and economic relationship it values.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The region which is now threatened by Soviet troops in Afghanistan is of great strategic importance: It contains more than two-thirds of the world's exportable oil.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The Soviet effort to dominate Afghanistan has brought Soviet military forces to within 300 miles of the Indian Ocean and close to the Straits of Hormuz, a waterway through which most of the world's oil must flow.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The Soviet Union is now attempting to consolidate a strategic position, therefore, that poses a grave threat to the free movement of Middle East oil.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: This situation demands careful thought, steady nerves, and resolute action, not only for this year but for many years to come.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It demands collective efforts to meet this new threat to security in the Persian Gulf and in Southwest Asia.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It demands the participation of all those who rely on oil from the Middle East and who are concerned with global peace and stability.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And it demands consultation and close cooperation with countries in the area which might be threatened.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Meeting this challenge will take national will, diplomatic and political wisdom, economic sacrifice, and, of course, military capability.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We must call on the best that is in us to preserve the security of this crucial region.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Let our position be absolutely clear: An attempt by any outside force to gain control of the Persian Gulf region will be regarded as an assault on the vital interests of the United States of America, and such an assault will be repelled by any means necessary, including military force.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: During the past 3 years, you have joined with me to improve our own security and the prospects for peace, not only in the vital oil-producing area of the Persian Gulf region but around the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've increased annually our real commitment for defense, and we will sustain this increase of effort throughout the Five Year Defense Program.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: It's imperative that Congress approve this strong defense budget for 1981, encompassing a 5-percent real growth in authorizations, without any reduction.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are also improving our capability to deploy U.S. military forces rapidly to distant areas.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've helped to strengthen NATO and our other alliances, and recently we and other NATO members have decided to develop and to deploy modernized, intermediate-range nuclear forces to meet an unwarranted and increased threat from the nuclear weapons of the Soviet Union.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are working with our allies to prevent conflict in the Middle East.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The peace treaty between Egypt and Israel is a notable achievement which represents a strategic asset for America and which also enhances prospects for regional and world peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We are now engaged in further negotiations to provide full autonomy for the people of the West Bank and Gaza, to resolve the Palestinian issue in all its aspects, and to preserve the peace and security of Israel.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Let no one doubt our commitment to the security of Israel.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In a few days we will observe an historic event when Israel makes another major withdrawal from the Sinai and when Ambassadors will be exchanged between Israel and Egypt.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've also expanded our own sphere of friendship.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our deep commitment to human rights and to meeting human needs has improved our relationship with much of the Third World.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our decision to normalize relations with the in the region of northeast Africa and the Persian Gulf.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We've reconfirmed our 1959 agreement to help Pakistan preserve its independence and its integrity.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The United States will take action consistent with our own laws to assist Pakistan in resisting any outside aggression.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And I'm asking the Congress specifically to reaffirm this agreement.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I'm also working, along with the leaders of other nations, to provide additional military and economic aid for Pakistan.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: That request will come to you in just a few days.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Finally, we are prepared to work with other countries in the region to share a cooperative security framework that respects differing values and political beliefs, yet which enhances the independence, security, and prosperity of all.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: All these efforts combined emphasize our dedication to defend and preserve the vital interests of the region and of the nation which we represent and those of our allies--in Europe and the Pacific, and also in the parts of the world which have such great strategic importance to us, stretching especially through the Middle East and Southwest Asia.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: With your help, I will pursue these efforts with vigor and with determination.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: You and I will act as necessary to protect and to preserve our Nation's security.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The men and women of America's Armed Forces are on duty tonight in many parts of the world.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I'm proud of the job they are doing, and I know you share that pride.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I believe that our volunteer forces are adequate for current defense needs, and I hope that it will not become necessary to impose a draft.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: However, we must be prepared for that possibility.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: For this reason, I have determined that the Selective Service System must now be revitalized.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I will send legislation and budget proposals to the Congress next month so that we can begin registration and then meet future mobilization needs rapidly if they arise.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We also need clear and quick passage of a new charter to define the legal authority and accountability of our intelligence agencies.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We will guarantee that abuses do not recur, but we must tighten our controls on sensitive intelligence information, and we need to remove unwarranted restraints on America's ability to collect intelligence.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The decade ahead will be a time of rapid change, as nations everywhere seek to deal with new problems and age-old tensions.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But America need have no fear.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We can thrive in a world of change if we remain true to our values and actively engaged in promoting world peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We will continue to work as we have for peace in the Middle East and southern Africa.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We will continue to build our ties with developing nations, respecting and helping to strengthen their national independence which they have struggled so hard to achieve.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And we will continue to support the growth of democracy and the protection of human rights.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In repressive regimes, popular frustrations often have no outlet except through violence.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But when peoples and their governments can approach their problems together through open, democratic methods, the basis for stability and peace is far more solid and far more enduring.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: That is why our support for human rights in other countries is in our own national interest as well as part of our own national character.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Peace--a peace that preserves freedom--remains America's first goal.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: In the coming years, as a mighty nation we will continue to pursue peace.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But to be strong abroad we must be strong at home.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: And in order to be strong, we must continue to face up to the difficult issues that confront us as a nation today.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The crises in Iran and Afghanistan have dramatized a very important lesson: Our excessive dependence on foreign oil is a clear and present danger to our Nation's security.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The need has never been more urgent.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: At long last, we must have a clear, comprehensive energy policy for the United States.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: As you well know, I have been working with the Congress in a concentrated and persistent way over the past 3 years to meet this need.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: We have made progress together.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: But Congress must act promptly now to complete final action on this vital energy legislation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Our Nation will then have a major conservation effort, important initiatives to develop solar power, realistic pricing based on the true value of oil, strong incentives for the production of coal and other fossil fuels in the United States, and our Nation's most massive peacetime investment in the development of synthetic fuels.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: The American people are making progress in energy conservation.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Last year we reduced overall petroleum consumption by 8 percent and gasoline consumption by 5 percent below what it was the year before.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: Now we must do more.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: After consultation with the Governors, we will set gasoline conservation goals for each of the 50 States, and I will make them mandatory if these goals are not met.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I've established an import ceiling for 1980 of 8.2 million barrels a day--well below the level of foreign oil purchases in 1977.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I expect our imports to be much lower than this, but the ceiling will be enforced by an oil import fee if necessary.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: I'm prepared to lower these imports still further if the other oil-consuming countries will join us in a fair and mutual reduction.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
text: If we have a serious shortage, I will not hesitate to impose mandatory gasoline rationing immediately.

speaker: Jimmy (James E.) Carter
