text: Through compromise and cooperation, the members of the Commission overcame their differences and achieved a fair, workable plan.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: They proved that, when it comes to the national welfare, Americans can still pull together for the common good.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Tonight, I'm especially pleased to join with the Speaker and the Senate majority leader in urging the Congress to enact this plan by Easter.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: There are elements in it, of course, that none of us prefers, but taken together it performs a package that all of us can support.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It asks for some sacrifice by all-- the self-employed, beneficiaries, workers, government employees, and the better-off among the retired-- but it imposes an undue burden on none.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And, in supporting it, we keep an important pledge to the American people: The integrity of the Social Security system will be preserved, and no one's payments will be reduced.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The Commission's plan will do the job; indeed, it must do the job.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We owe it to today's older Americans and today's younger workers.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: So, before we go any further, I ask you to join with me in saluting the members of the Commission who are here tonight and Senate Majority Leader Howard Baker and Speaker Tip O'Neill for a job well done.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I hope and pray the bipartisan spirit that guided you in this endeavor will inspire all of us as we face the challenges of the year ahead.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Nearly half a century ago, in this Chamber, another American President, Franklin Delano Roosevelt, in his second State of the Union message, urged America to look to the future, to meet the challenge of change and the need for leadership that looks forward, not backward.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: change is the order of the day.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In every nation economic problems long in the making have brought crises to [of] many kinds for which the masters of old practice and theory were unprepared.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: He also reminded us that the future lies with those wise political leaders who realize that the great public is interested more in Government than in politics.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: So, let us, in these next 2 years-- men and women of both parties, every political shade-- concentrate on the long-range, bipartisan responsibilities of government, not the short-range or short-term temptations of partisan politics.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The problems we inherited were far worse than most inside and out of government had expected;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: the recession was deeper than most inside and out of government had predicted.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Curing those problems has taken more time and a higher toll than any of us wanted.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Unemployment is far too high.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Projected Federal spending-- if government refuses to tighten its own belt-- will also be far too high and could weaken and shorten the economic recovery now underway.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This recovery will bring with it a revival of economic confidence and spending for consumer items and capital goods-- the stimulus we need to restart our stalled economic engines.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The American people have already stepped up their rate of saving, assuring that the funds needed to modernize our factories and improve our technology will once again flow to business and industry.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The inflationary expectations that led to a 21 1/2-percent interest prime rate and soaring mortgage rates 2 years ago are now reduced by almost half.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Leaders have started to realize that double-digit inflation is no longer a way of life.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I misspoke there.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: lenders.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: So, interest rates have tumbled, paving the way for recovery in vital industries like housing and autos.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The early evidence of that recovery has started coming in.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Housing starts for the fourth quarter of 1982 were up 45 percent from a year ago, and housing permits, a sure indicator of future growth, were up a whopping 60 percent.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We're witnessing an upsurge of productivity and impressive evidence that American industry will once again become competitive in markets at home and abroad, ensuring more jobs and better incomes for the Nation's work force.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But our confidence must also be tempered by realism and patience.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Quick fixes and artificial stimulants repeatedly applied over decades are what brought us the inflationary disorders that we've now paid such a heavy price to cure.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The permanent recovery in employment, production, and investment we seek won't come in a sharp, short spurt.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It'll build carefully and steadily in the months and years ahead.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In the meantime, the challenge of government is to identify the things that we can do now to ease the massive economic transition for the American people.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The Federal budget is both a symptom and a cause of our economic problems.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Unless we reduce the dangerous growth rate in government spending, we could face the prospect of sluggish economic growth into the indefinite future.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Failure to cope with this problem now could mean as much as a trillion dollars more in national debt in the next 4 years alone.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: That would average $4,300 in additional debt for every man, woman, child, and baby in our nation.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: To assure a sustained recovery, we must continue getting runaway spending under control to bring those deficits down.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: If we don't, the recovery will be too short, unemployment will remain too high, and we will leave an unconscionable burden of national debt for our children.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: That we must not do.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Let's be clear about where the deficit problem comes from.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Contrary to the drumbeat we've been hearing for the last few months, the deficits we face are not rooted in defense spending.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Taken as a percentage of the gross national product, our defense spending happens to be only about four-fifths of what it was in 1970.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Nor is the deficit, as some would have it, rooted in tax cuts.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Even with our tax cuts, taxes as a fraction of gross national product remain about the same as they were in 1970.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The fact is, our deficits come from the uncontrolled growth of the budget for domestic spending.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: During the 1970's the share of our national income devoted to this domestic spending increased by more than 60 percent, from 10 cents out of every dollar produced by the American people to 16 cents.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In spite of all our economies and efficiencies, and without adding any new programs, basic, necessary domestic spending provided for in this year's budget will grow to almost a trillion dollars over the next 5 years.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The deficit problem is a clear and present danger to the basic health of our Republic.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We need a plan to overcome this danger-- a plan based on these principles.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It must be bipartisan.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Conquering the deficits and putting the Government's house in order will require the best effort of all of us.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It must be fair.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Just as all will share in the benefits that will come from recovery, all would share fairly in the burden of transition.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It must be prudent.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The strength of our national defense must be restored so that we can pursue prosperity and peace and freedom while maintaining our commitment to the truly needy.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And finally, it must be realistic.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We can't rely on hope alone.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: With these guiding principles in mind, let me outline a four-part plan to increase economic growth and reduce deficits.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: First, in my budget message, I will recommend a Federal spending freeze.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I know this is strong medicine, but so far, we have only cut the rate of increase in Federal spending.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The Government has continued to spend more money each year, though not as much more as it did in the past.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Taken as a whole, the budget I'm proposing for the fiscal year will increase no more than the rate of inflation.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In other words, the Federal Government will hold the line on real spending.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Now, that's far less than many American families have had to do in these difficult times.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I will request that the proposed 6-month freeze in cost-of-living adjustments recommended by the bipartisan Social Security Commission be applied to other government-related retirement programs.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I will, also, propose a 1-year freeze on a broad range of domestic spending programs, and for Federal civilian and military pay and pension programs.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And let me say right here, I'm sorry, with regard to the military, in asking that of them, because for so many years they have been so far behind and so low in reward for what the men and women in uniform are doing.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But I'm sure they will understand that this must be across the board and fair.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Second, I will ask the Congress to adopt specific measures to control the growth of the so-called uncontrollable spending programs.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: These are the automatic spending programs, such as food stamps, that cannot be simply frozen and that have grown by over 400 percent since 1970.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: They are the largest single cause of the built-in or structural deficit problem.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our standard here will be fairness, ensuring that the taxpayers' hard-earned dollars go only to the truly needy;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: that none of them are turned away, but that fraud and waste are stamped out.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And I'm sorry to say, there's a lot of it out there.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In the food stamp program alone, last year, we identified almost $1.1 billion in overpayments.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The taxpayers aren't the only victims of this kind of abuse.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The truly needy suffer as funds intended for them are taken not by the needy, but by the greedy.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: For everyone's sake, we must put an end to such waste and corruption.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Third, I will adjust our program to restore America's defenses by proposing $55 billion in defense savings over the next 5 years.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: These are savings recommended to me by the Secretary of Defense, who has assured me they can be safely achieved and will not diminish our ability to negotiate arms reductions or endanger America's security.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We will not gamble with our national survival.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And fourth, because we must ensure reduction and eventual elimination of deficits over the next several years, I will propose a standby tax, limited to no more than 1 percent of the gross national product, to start in fiscal 1986.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It would last no more than 3 years, and it would start only if the Congress has first approved our spending freeze and budget control program.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And there are several other conditions also that must be met, all of them in order for this program to be triggered.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Now, you could say that this is an insurance policy for the future, a remedy that will be at hand if needed but only resorted to if absolutely necessary.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In the meantime, we'll continue to study ways to simplify the tax code and make it more fair for all Americans.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This is a goal that every American who's ever struggled with a tax form can understand.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: At the same time, however, I will oppose any efforts to undo the basic tax reforms that we've already enacted, including the 10-percent tax break coming to taxpayers this July and the tax indexing which will protect all Americans from inflationary bracket creep in the years ahead.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Now, I realize that this four-part plan is easier to describe than it will be to enact.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But the looming deficits that hang over us and over America's future must be reduced.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The path I've outlined is fair, balanced, and realistic.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: If enacted, it will ensure a steady decline in deficits, aiming toward a balanced budget by the end of the decade.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It's the only path that will lead to a strong, sustained recovery.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Let us follow that path together.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: No domestic challenge is more crucial than providing stable, permanent jobs for all Americans who want to work.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The recovery program will provide jobs for most, but others will need special help and training for new skills.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Shortly, I will submit to the Congress the Employment Act of 1983, designed to get at the special problems of the long-term unemployed, as well as young people trying to enter the job market.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I'll propose extending unemployment benefits, including special incentives to employers who hire the long-term unemployed, providing programs for displaced workers, and helping federally funded and State-administered unemployment insurance programs provide workers with training and relocation assistance.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Finally, our proposal will include new incentives for summer youth employment to help young people get a start in the job market.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must offer both short-term help and long-term hope for our unemployed.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I hope we can work together on this.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I hope we can work together as we did last year in enacting the landmark Job Training Partnership Act.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Regulatory reform legislation, a responsible clean air act, and passage of enterprise zone legislation will also create new incentives for jobs and opportunity.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: One out of every five jobs in our country depends on trade.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: So, I will propose a broader strategy in the field of international trade-- one that increases the openness of our trading system and is fairer to America's farmers and workers in the world marketplace.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must have adequate export financing to sell American products overseas.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I will ask for new negotiating authority to remove barriers and to get more of our products into foreign markets.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must strengthen the organization of our trade agencies and make changes in our domestic laws and international trade policy to promote free trade and the increased flow of American goods, services, and investments.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our trade position can also be improved by making our port system more efficient.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Better, more active harbors translate into stable jobs in our coalfields, railroads, trucking industry, and ports.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: After 2 years of debate, it's time for us to get together and enact a port modernization bill.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Education, training, and retraining are fundamental to our success as are research and development and productivity.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Labor, management, and government at all levels can and must participate in improving these tools of growth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Tax policy, regulatory practices, and government programs all need constant reevaluation in terms of our competitiveness.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Every American has a role and a stake in international trade.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We Americans are still the technological leaders in most fields.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must keep that edge, and to do so we need to begin renewing the basics--starting with our educational system.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: While we grew complacent, others have acted.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Japan, with a population only about half the size of ours, graduates from its universities more engineers than we do.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: If a child doesn't receive adequate math and science teaching by the age of 16, he or she has lost the chance to be a scientist or an engineer.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must join together-- parents, teachers, grassroots groups, organized labor, and the business community-- to revitalize American education by setting a standard of excellence.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In 1983 we seek four major education goals: a quality education initiative to encourage a substantial upgrading of math and science instruction through block grants to the States;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: establishment of education savings accounts that will give middle- and lower-income families an incentive to save for their children's college education and, at the same time, encourage a real increase in savings for economic growth;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: passage of tuition tax credits for parents who want to send their children to private or religiously affiliated schools;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: a constitutional amendment to permit voluntary school prayer.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: God should never have been expelled from America's classrooms in the first place.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our commitment to fairness means that we must assure legal and economic equity for women, and eliminate, once and for all, all traces of unjust discrimination against women from the United States Code.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We will not tolerate wage discrimination based on sex, and we intend to strengthen enforcement of child support laws to ensure that single parents, most of whom are women, do not suffer unfair financial hardship.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We will also take action to remedy inequities in pensions.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: These initiatives will be joined by others to continue our efforts to promote equity for women.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Also in the area of fairness and equity, we will ask for extension of the Civil Rights Commission, which is due to expire this year.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The Commission is an important part of the ongoing struggle for justice in America, and we strongly support its reauthorization.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Effective enforcement of our nation's fair housing laws is also essential to ensuring equal opportunity.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In the year ahead, we'll work to strengthen enforcement of fair housing laws for all Americans.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The time has also come for major reform of our criminal justice statutes and acceleration of the drive against organized crime and drug trafficking.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It's high time that we make our cities safe again.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This administration hereby declares an all-out war on big-time organized crime and the drug racketeers who are poisoning our young people.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We will also implement recommendations of our Task Force on Victims of Crime, which will report to me this week.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: American agriculture, the envy of the world, has become the victim of its own successes.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: With one farmer now producing enough food to feed himself and 77 other people, America is confronted with record surplus crops and commodity prices below the cost of production.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must strive, through innovations like the payment-in-kind crop swap approach and an aggressive export policy, to restore health and vitality to rural America.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Meanwhile, I have instructed the Department of Agriculture to work individually with farmers with debt problems to help them through these tough times.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Over the past year, our Task Force on Private Sector Initiatives has successfully forged a working partnership involving leaders of business, labor, education, and government to address the training needs of American workers.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Thanks to the Task Force, private sector initiatives are now underway in all 50 States of the Union, and thousands of working people have been helped in making the shift from dead-end jobs and low-demand skills to the growth areas of high technology and the service economy.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Additionally, a major effort will be focused on encouraging the expansion of private community child care.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The new advisory council on private sector initiatives will carry on and extend this vital work of encouraging private initiative in 1983.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In the coming year, we will also act to improve the quality of life for Americans by curbing the skyrocketing cost of health care that is becoming an unbearable financial burden for so many.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And we will submit legislation to provide catastrophic illness insurance coverage for older Americans.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I will also shortly submit a comprehensive federalism proposal that will continue our efforts to restore to States and local governments their roles as dynamic laboratories of change in a creative society.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: During the next several weeks, I will send to the Congress a series of detailed proposals on these and other topics and look forward to working with you on the development of these initiatives.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: So far, now, I've concentrated mainly on the problems posed by the future.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But in almost every home and workplace in America, we're already witnessing reason for great hope-- the first flowering of the manmade miracles of high technology, a field pioneered and still led by our country.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: To many of us now, computers, silicon chips, data processing, cybernetics, and all the other innovations of the dawning high technology age are as mystifying as the workings of the combustion engine must have been when that first Model T rattled down Main Street, U.S.A.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But as surely as America's pioneer spirit made us the industrial giant of the 20th century, the same pioneer spirit today is opening up on another vast front of opportunity, the frontier of high technology.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In conquering the frontier we cannot write off our traditional industries, but we must develop the skills and industries that will make us a pioneer of tomorrow.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This administration is committed to keeping America the technological leader of the world now and into the 21st century.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But let us turn briefly to the international arena.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: America's leadership in the world came to us because of our own strength and because of the values which guide us as a society: free elections, a free press, freedom of religious choice, free trade unions, and above all, freedom for the individual and rejection of the arbitrary power of the state.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: These values are the bedrock of our strength.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: They unite us in a stewardship of peace and freedom with our allies and friends in NATO, in Asia, in Latin America, and elsewhere.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: They are also the values which in the recent past some among us had begun to doubt and view with a cynical eye.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Fortunately, we and our allies have rediscovered the strength of our common democratic values, and we're applying them as a cornerstone of a comprehensive strategy for peace with freedom.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In London last year, I announced the commitment of the United States to developing the infrastructure of democracy throughout the world.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We intend to pursue this democratic initiative vigorously.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The future belongs not to governments and ideologies which oppress their peoples, but to democratic systems of self-government which encourage individual initiative and guarantee personal freedom.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But our strategy for peace with freedom must also be based on strength- - economic strength and military strength.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: A strong American economy is essential to the well-being and security of our friends and allies.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The restoration of a strong, healthy American economy has been and remains one of the central pillars of our foreign policy.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The progress I've been able to report to you tonight will, I know, be as warmly welcomed by the rest of the world as it is by the American people.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must also recognize that our own economic well-being is inextricably linked to the world economy.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We export over 20 percent of our industrial production, and 40 percent of our farmland produces for export.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We will continue to work closely with the industrialized democracies of Europe and Japan and with the International Monetary Fund to ensure it has adequate resources to help bring the world economy back to strong, non-inflationary growth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: As the leader of the West and as a country that has become great and rich because of economic freedom, America must be an unrelenting advocate of free trade.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: As some nations are tempted to turn to protectionism, our strategy cannot be to follow them, but to lead the way toward freer trade.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: To this end, in May of this year America will host an economic summit meeting in Williamsburg, Virginia.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: As we begin our third year, we have put in place a defense program that redeems the neglect of the past decade.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We have developed a realistic military strategy to deter threats to peace and to protect freedom if deterrence fails.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our Armed Forces are finally properly paid; after years of neglect are well trained and becoming better equipped and supplied.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And the American uniform is once again worn with pride.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Most of the major systems needed for modernizing our defenses are already underway, and we will be addressing one key system, the MX missile, in consultation with the Congress in a few months.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: America's foreign policy is once again based on bipartisanship, on realism, strength, full partnership, in consultation with our allies, and constructive negotiation with potential adversaries.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: From the Middle East to southern Africa to Geneva, American diplomats are taking the initiative to make peace and lower arms levels.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We should be proud of our role as peacemakers.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In the Middle East last year, the United States played the major role in ending the tragic fighting in Lebanon and negotiated the withdrawal of the PLO from Beirut.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Last September, I outlined principles to carry on the peace process begun so promisingly at Camp David.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: All the people of the Middle East should know that in the year ahead we will not flag in our efforts to build on that foundation to bring them the blessings of peace.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In Central America and the Caribbean Basin, we are likewise engaged in a partnership for peace, prosperity, and democracy.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Final passage of the remaining portions of our Caribbean Basin Initiative, which passed the House last year, is one of this administration's top legislative priorities for1983.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The security and economic assistance policies of this administration in Latin America and elsewhere are based on realism and represent a critical investment in the future of the human race.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This undertaking is a joint responsibility of the executive and legislative branches, and I'm counting on the cooperation and statesmanship of the Congress to help us meet this essential foreign policy goal.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: At the heart of our strategy for peace is our relationship with the Soviet Union.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The past year saw a change in Soviet leadership.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We're prepared for a positive change in Soviet-American relations.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But the Soviet Union must show by deeds as well as words a sincere commitment to respect the rights and sovereignty of the family of nations.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Responsible members of the world community do not threaten or invade their neighbors.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And they restrain their allies from aggression.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: For our part, we're vigorously pursuing arms reduction negotiations with the Soviet Union.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Supported by our allies, we've put forward draft agreements proposing significant weapon reductions to equal and verifiable lower levels.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We insist on an equal balance of forces.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And given the overwhelming evidence of Soviet violations of international treaties concerning chemical and biological weapons, we also insist that any agreement we sign can and will be verifiable.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In the case of intermediate-range nuclear forces, we have proposed the complete elimination of the entire class of land-based missiles.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We're also prepared to carefully explore serious Soviet proposals.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: At the same time, let me emphasize that allied steadfastness remains a key to achieving arms reductions.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: With firmness and dedication, we'll continue to negotiate.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Deep down, the Soviets must know it's in their interest as well as ours to prevent a wasteful arms race.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And once they recognize our unshakable resolve to maintain adequate deterrence, they will have every reason to join us in the search for greater security and major arms reductions.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: When that moment comes-- and I'm confident that it will-- we will have taken an important step toward a more peaceful future for all the world's people.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: A very wise man, Bernard Baruch, once said that America has never forgotten the nobler things that brought her into being and that light her path.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our country is a special place, because we Americans have always been sustained, through good times and bad, by a noble vision-- a vision not only of what the world around us is today but what we as a free people can make it be tomorrow.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We're realists; we solve our problems instead of ignoring them, no matter how loud the chorus of despair around us.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But we're also idealists, for it was an ideal that brought our ancestors to these shores from every corner of the world.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Right now we need both realism and idealism.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Millions of our neighbors are without work.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It is up to us to see they aren't without hope.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This is a task for all of us.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And may I say, Americans have rallied to this cause, proving once again that we are the most generous people on Earth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We who are in government must take the lead in restoring the economy.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And here all that time, I thought you were reading the paper.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The single thing-- the single thing that can start the wheels of industry turning again is further reduction of interest rates.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Just another 1 or 2 points can mean tens of thousands of jobs.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Right now, with inflation as low as it is, 3.9 percent, there is room for interest rates to come down.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Only fear prevents their reduction.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: A lender, as we know, must charge an interest rate that recovers the depreciated value of the dollars loaned.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And that depreciation is, of course, the amount of inflation.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Today, interest rates are based on fear-- fear that government will resort to measures, as it has in the past, that will send inflation zooming again.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We who serve here in this Capital must erase that fear by making it absolutely clear that we will not stop fighting inflation; that, together, we will do only those things that will lead to lasting economic growth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Yes, the problems confronting us are large and forbidding.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And, certainly, no one can or should minimize the plight of millions of our friends and neighbors who are living in the bleak emptiness of unemployment.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But we must and can give them good reason to be hopeful.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Back over the years, citizens like ourselves have gathered within these walls when our nation was threatened;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: sometimes when its very existence was at stake.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Always with courage and common sense, they met the crises of their time and lived to see a stronger, better, and more prosperous country.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The present situation is no worse and, in fact, is not as bad as some of those they faced.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Time and again, they proved that there is nothing we Americans cannot achieve as free men and women.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Yes, we still have problems-- plenty of them.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But it's just plain wrong-- unjust to our country and unjust to our people-- to let those problems stand in the way of the most important truth of all: America is on the mend.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We owe it to the unfortunate to be aware of their plight and to help them in every way we can.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: No one can quarrel with that.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must and do have compassion for all the victims of this economic crisis.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Americans who never make the headlines and will never be interviewed-- are laying the foundation, not just for recovery from our present problems but for a better tomorrow for all our people.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: From coast to coast, on the job and in classrooms and laboratories, at new construction sites and in churches and community groups, neighbors are helping neighbors.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And they've already begun the building, the research, the work, and the giving that will make our country great again.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I believe this, because I believe in them-- in the strength of their hearts and minds, in the commitment that each one of them brings to their daily lives, be they high or humble.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The challenge for us in government is to be worthy of them-- to make government a help, not a hindrance to our people in the challenging but promising days ahead.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: If we do that, if we care what our children and our children's children will say of us, if we want them one day to be thankful for what we did here in these temples of freedom, we will work together to make America better for our having been here-- not just in this year or this decade but in the next century and beyond.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Thank you, and God bless you.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Once again, in keeping with time-honored tradition, I have come to report to you on the state of the Union, and I'm pleased to report that America is much improved, and there's good reason to believe that improvement will continue through the days to come.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: You and I have had some honest and open differences in the year past.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But they didn't keep us from joining hands in bipartisan cooperation to stop a long decline that had drained this nation's spirit and eroded its health.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: There is renewed energy and optimism throughout the land.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: America is back, standing tall, looking to the eighties with courage, confidence, and hope.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The problems we're overcoming are not the heritage of one person, party, or even one generation.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It's just the tendency of government to grow, for practices and programs to become the nearest thing to eternal life we'll ever see on this Earth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: With a little more power and a little more money, we could do so much for the people.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: For a time we forgot the American dream isn't one of making government bigger; it's keeping faith with the mighty spirit of free people under God.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: As we came to the decade of the eighties, we faced the worst crisis in our postwar history.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In the seventies were years of rising problems and falling confidence.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: There was a feeling government had grown beyond the consent of the governed.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Families felt helpless in the face of mounting inflation and the indignity of taxes that reduced reward for hard work, thrift, and risk-taking.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: All this was overlaid by an ever-growing web of rules and regulations.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: On the international scene, we had an uncomfortable feeling that we'd lost the respect of friend and foe.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Some questioned whether we had the will to defend peace and freedom.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But America is too great for small dreams.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: There was a hunger in the land for a spiritual revival; if you will, a crusade for renewal.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The American people said: Let us look to the future with confidence, both at home and abroad.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Let us give freedom a chance.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Americans were ready to make a new beginning, and together we have done it.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We're confronting our problems one by one.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Hope is alive tonight for millions of young families and senior citizens set free from unfair tax increases and crushing inflation.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Inflation has been beaten down from 12.4 to 3.2 percent, and that's a great victory for all the people.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The prime rate has been cut almost in half, and we must work together to bring it down even more.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Together, we passed the first across-the-board tax reduction for everyone since the Kennedy tax cuts.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Next year, tax rates will be indexed so inflation can't push people into higher brackets when they get cost-of-living pay raises.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Government must never again use inflation to profit at the people's expense.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Today, a working family earning $25,000 has $1,100 more in purchasing power than if tax and inflation rates were still at the 1980 levels.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Real after-tax income increased 5 percent last year.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And economic deregulation of key industries like transportation has offered more chances-or choices, I should say, to consumers and new changes-or chances for entrepreneurs and protecting safety.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Tonight, we can report and be proud of one of the best recoveries in decades.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Send away the handwringers and the doubting Thomases.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Hope is reborn for couples dreaming of owning homes and for risk takers with vision to create tomorrow's opportunities.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The spirit of enterprise is sparked by the sunrise industries of high-tech and by small business people with big ideas-people like Barbara Proctor, who rose from a ghetto to build a multimillion-dollar advertising agency in Chicago;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Carlos Perez, a Cuban refugee, who turned $27 and a dream into a successful importing business in Coral Gables, Florida.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: People like these are heroes for the eighties.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: They helped 4 million Americans find jobs in 1983.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: More people are drawing paychecks tonight than ever before.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In 1983 women filled 73 percent of all the new jobs in managerial, professional, and technical fields.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But we know that many of our fellow countrymen are still out of work, wondering what will come of their hopes and dreams.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Can we love America and not reach out to tell them: You are not forgotten;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: we will not rest until each of you can reach as high as your God-given talents will take you.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The heart of America is strong; it's good and true.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The cynics were wrong; America never was a sick society.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We're seeing rededication to bedrock values of faith, family, work, neighborhood, peace, and freedom--values that help bring us together as one people, from the youngest child to the most senior citizen.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The Congress deserves America's thanks for helping us restore pride and credibility to our military.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And I hope that you're as proud as I am of the young men and women in uniform who have volunteered to man the ramparts in defense of freedom and whose dedication, valor, and skill increases so much our chance of living in a world at peace.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: People everywhere hunger for peace and a better life.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The tide of the future is a freedom tide, and our struggle for democracy cannot and will not be denied.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This nation champions peace that enshrines liberty, democratic rights, and dignity for every individual.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: America's new strength, confidence, and purpose are carrying hope and opportunity far from our shores.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: A world economic recovery is underway.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It began here.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We've journeyed far, but we have much farther to go.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Civilization can not go back; civilization must not stand still.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We have undertaken new methods.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It is our task to perfect, to improve, to alter when necessary, but in all cases to go forward.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It's time to move forward again, time for America to take freedom's next step.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Let us unite tonight behind four great goals to keep America free, secure, and at peace in the eighties together.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We can ensure steady economic growth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We can develop America's next frontier.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We can strengthen our traditional values.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And we can build a meaningful peace to protect our loved ones and this shining star of faith that has guided millions from tyranny to the safe harbor of freedom, progress, and hope.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Doing these things will open wider the gates of opportunity, provide greater security for all, with no barriers of bigotry or discrimination.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The key to a dynamic decade is vigorous economic growth, our first great goal.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We might well begin with common sense in Federal budgeting: government spending no more than government takes in.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must bring Federal deficits down.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But how we do that makes all the difference.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We can begin by limiting the size and scope of government.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Under the leadership of Vice President Bush, we have reduced the growth of Federal regulations by more than 25 percent and cut well over 300 million hours of government-required paperwork each year.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This will save the public more than $150 billion over the next 10 years.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The Grace commission--the Grace commission has given us some 2,500 recommendations for reducing wasteful spending, and they're being examined throughout the administration.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Federal spending growth has been cut from 17.4 percent in 1980 to less than half of that today, and we have already achieved over $300 billion in budget savings for the period of 1982 to '86.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But that's only a little more than half of what we sought.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Government is still spending too large a percentage of the total economy.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Now, some insist that any further budget savings must be obtained by reducing the portion spent on defense.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This ignores the fact that national defense is solely the responsibility of the Federal Government; indeed, it is its prime responsibility.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And yet defense spending is less than a third of the total budget.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: During the years of President Kennedy and of the years before that, defense was almost half the total budget.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And then came several years in which our military capability was allowed to deteriorate to a very dangerous degree.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We are just now restoring, through the essential modernization of our conventional and strategic forces, our capability to meet our present and future security needs.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We dare not shirk our responsibility to keep America free, secure, and at peace.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The last decade saw domestic spending surge literally out of control.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But the basis for such spending had been laid in previous years.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: A pattern of overspending has been in place for half a century.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: As the national debt grew, we were told not to worry, that we owed it to ourselves.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Now we know that deficits are a cause for worry.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But there's a difference of opinion as to whether taxes should be increased, spending cut, or some of both.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Fear is expressed that government borrowing to fund the deficit could inhibit the economic recovery by taking capital needed for business and industrial expansion.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Well, I think that debate is missing an important point.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Whether government borrows or increases taxes, it will be taking the same amount of money from the private sector, and, either way, that's too much.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Simple fairness dictates that government must not raise taxes on families struggling to pay their bills.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The root of the problem is that government's share is more than we can afford if we're to have a sound economy.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must bring down the deficits to ensure continued economic growth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In the budget that I will submit on February 1st, I will recommend measures that will reduce the deficit over the next 5 years.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Many of these will be unfinished business from last year's budget.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Some could be enacted quickly if we could join in a serious effort to address this problem.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I spoke today with Speaker of the House O'Neill, Senate Majority Leader Baker, Senator Minority Leader Byrd, and House Minority Leader Michel.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I asked them if they would designate congressional representatives to meet with representatives of the administration to try to reach prompt agreement on a bipartisan deficit reduction plan.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I know it would take a long, hard struggle to agree on a full-scale plan.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: So, what I have proposed is that we first see if we can agree on a down payment.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Now, I believe there is basis for such an agreement, one that could reduce the deficits by about a hundred billion dollars over the next 3 years.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We could focus on some of the less contentious spending cuts that are still pending before the Congress.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: These could be combined with measures to close certain tax loopholes, measures that the Treasury Department has previously said to be worthy of support.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In addition, we could examine the possibility of achieving further outlay savings based on the work of the Grace commission.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: If the congressional leadership is willing, my representatives will be prepared to meet with theirs at the earliest possible time.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I would hope the leadership might agree on an expedited timetable in which to develop and enact the down payment.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But a down payment alone is not enough to break us out of the deficit problem.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It could help us start on the right path.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Yet, we must do more.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: So, I propose that we begin exploring how together we can make structural reforms to curb the built-in growth of spending.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I also propose improvements in the budgeting process.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Some 43 of our 50 States grant their Governors the right to veto individual items in appropriation bills without having to veto the entire bill.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: California is one of those 43 States.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: As Governor, I found this line-item veto was a powerful tool against wasteful or extravagant spending.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It works in 43 States.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Let's put it to work in Washington for all the people.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It would be most effective if done by constitutional amendment.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The majority of Americans approve of such an amendment, just as they and I approve of an amendment mandating a balanced Federal budget.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Many States also have this protection in their constitutions.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: To talk of meeting the present situation by increasing taxes is a Band-Aid solution which does nothing to cure an illness that's been coming on for half a century-to say nothing of the fact that it poses a real threat to economic recovery.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Let's remember that a substantial amount of income tax is presently owed and not paid by people in the underground economy.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It would be immoral to make those who are paying taxes pay more to compensate for those who aren't paying their share.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: There's a better way.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Let us go forward with an historic reform for fairness, simplicity, and incentives for growth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I am asking Secretary Don Regan for a plan for action to simplify the entire tax code, so all taxpayers, big and small, are treated more fairly.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And I believe such a plan could result in that underground economy being brought into the sunlight of honest tax compliance.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And it could make the tax base broader, so personal tax rates could come down, not go up.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I've asked that specific recommendations, consistent with those objectives, be presented to me by December 1984.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our second great goal is to build on America's pioneer spirit-I said something funny?

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I said America's next frontier-and that's to develop that frontier.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: A sparkling economy spurs initiatives, sunrise industries, and makes older ones more competitive.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Nowhere is this more important than our next frontier: space.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Nowhere do we so effectively demonstrate our technological leadership and ability to make life better on Earth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The Space Age is barely a quarter of a century old.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But already we've pushed civilization forward with our advances in science and technology.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Opportunities and jobs will multiply as we cross new thresholds of knowledge and reach deeper into the unknown.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our progress in space-taking giant steps for all mankind-is a tribute to American teamwork and excellence.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our finest minds in government, industry, and academia have all pulled together.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And we can be proud to say: We are first; we are the best; and we are so because we're free.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: America has always been greatest when we dared to be great.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We can reach for greatness again.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We can follow our dreams to distant stars, living and working in space for peaceful, economic, and scientific gain.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Tonight, I am directing NASA to develop a permanently manned space station and to do it within a decade.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: A space station will permit quantum leaps in our research in science, communications, in metals, and in lifesaving medicines which could be manufactured only in space.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We want our friends to help us meet these challenges and share in their benefits.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: NASA will invite other countries to participate so we can strengthen peace, build prosperity, and expand freedom for all who share our goals.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Just as the oceans opened up a new world for clipper ships and Yankee traders, space holds enormous potential for commerce today.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The market for space transportation could surpass our capacity to develop it.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Companies interested in putting payloads into space must have ready access to private sector launch services.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The Department of Transportation will help an expendable launch services industry to get off the ground.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We'll soon implement a number of executive initiatives, develop proposals to ease regulatory constraints, and, with NASA's help, promote private sector investment in space.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And as we develop the frontier of space, let us remember our responsibility to preserve our older resources here on Earth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Preservation of our environment is not a liberal or conservative challenge, it's common sense.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Though this is a time of budget constraints, I have requested for EPA one of the largest percentage budget increases of any agency.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We will begin the long, necessary effort to clean up a productive recreational area and a special national resource-the Chesapeake Bay.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: To reduce the threat posed by abandoned hazardous waste dumps, EPA will spend $410 million.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And I will request a supplemental increase of 50 million.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And because the Superfund law expires in 1985, I've asked Bill Ruckelshaus to develop a proposal for its extension so there'll be additional time to complete this important task.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: On the question of acid rain, which concerns people in many areas of the United States and Canada, I'm proposing a research program that doubles our current funding.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And we'll take additional action to restore our lakes and develop new technology to reduce pollution that causes acid rain.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We have greatly improved the conditions of our natural resources.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We'll ask the Congress for $157 million beginning in 1985 to acquire new park and conservation lands.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The Department of the Interior will encourage careful, selective exploration and production on our vital resources in an Exclusive Economic Zone within the 200-mile limit off our coasts-but with strict adherence to environmental laws and with fuller State and public participation.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But our most precious resources, our greatest hope for the future, are the minds and hearts of our people, especially our children.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We can help them build tomorrow by strengthening our community of shared values.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This must be our third great goal.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: For us, faith, work, family, neighborhood, freedom, and peace are not just words;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: they're expressions of what America means, definitions of what makes us a good and loving people.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Families stand at the center of our society.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And every family has a personal stake in promoting excellence in education.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Excellence does not begin in Washington.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: A 600-percent increase in Federal spending on education between 1960 and 1980 was accompanied by a steady decline in Scholastic Aptitude Test scores.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Excellence must begin in our homes and neighborhood schools, where it's the responsibility of every parent and teacher and the right of every child.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our children come first, and that's why I established a bipartisan National Commission on Excellence in Education, to help us chart a commonsense course for better education.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And already, communities are implementing the Commission's recommendations.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Schools are reporting progress in math and reading skills.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But we must do more to restore discipline to schools; and we must encourage the teaching of new basics, reward teachers of merit, enforce tougher standards, and put our parents back in charge.
