text: Now we're going to develop a permanently manned space station and new opportunities for free enterprise, because in the next decade Americans and our friends around the world will be living and working together in space.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In the zero gravity of space, we could manufacture in 30 days lifesaving medicines it would take 30 years to make on Earth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We can make crystals of exceptional purity to produce super computers, creating jobs, technologies, and medical breakthroughs beyond anything we ever dreamed possible.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: As we do all this, we'll continue to protect our natural resources.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We will seek reauthorization and expanded funding for the Superfund program to continue cleaning up hazardous waste sites which threaten human health and the environment.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Now, there's another great heritage to speak of this evening.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Of all the changes that have swept America the past 4 years, none brings greater promise than our rediscovery of the values of faith, freedom, family, work, and neighborhood.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We see signs of renewal in increased attendance in places of worship;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: renewed optimism and faith in our future;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: love of country rediscovered by our young, who are leading the way.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We've rediscovered that work is good in and of itself, that it ennobles us to create and contribute no matter how seemingly humble our jobs.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We've seen a powerful new current from an old and honorable tradition--American generosity.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: From thousands answering Peace Corps appeals to help boost food production in Africa, to millions volunteering time, corporations adopting schools, and communities pulling together to help the neediest among us at home, we have refound our values.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Private sector initiatives are crucial to our future.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I thank the Congress for passing equal access legislation giving religious groups the same right to use classrooms after school that other groups enjoy.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But no citizen need tremble, nor the world shudder, if a child stands in a classroom and breathes a prayer.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We ask you again, give children back a right they had for a century and a half or more in this country.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The question of abortion grips our nation.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Abortion is either the taking of a human life or it isn't.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And if it is-and medical technology is increasingly showing it is-it must be stopped.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It is a terrible irony that while some turn to abortion, so many others who cannot become parents cry out for children to adopt.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We have room for these children.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We can fill the cradles of those who want a child to love.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And tonight I ask you in the Congress to move this year on legislation to protect the unborn.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In the area of education, we're returning to excellence, and again, the heroes are our people, not government.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We're stressing basics of discipline, rigorous testing, and homework, while helping children become computer-smart as well.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: For 20 years Scholastic Aptitude Test scores of our high school students went down, but now they have gone up 2 of the last 3 years.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must go forward in our commitment to the new basics, giving parents greater authority and making sure good teachers are rewarded for hard work and achievement through merit pay.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Of all the changes in the past 20 years, none has more threatened our sense of national well-being than the explosion of violent crime.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: One does not have to be attacked to be a victim.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The woman who must run to her car after shopping at night is a victim.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The couple draping their door with locks and chains are victims;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: as is the tired, decent cleaning woman who can't ride a subway home without being afraid.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We do not seek to violate the rights of defendants.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But shouldn't we feel more compassion for the victims of crime than for those who commit crime?

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: For the first time in 20 years, the crime index has fallen 2 years in a row.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We've convicted over 7,400 drug offenders and put them, as well as leaders of organized crime, behind bars in record numbers.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But we must do more.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I urge the House to follow the Senate and enact proposals permitting use of all reliable evidence that police officers acquire in good faith.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: These proposals would also reform the habeus corpus laws and allow, in keeping with the will of the overwhelming majority of Americans, the use of the death penalty where necessary.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: There can be no economic revival in ghettos when the most violent among us are allowed to roam free.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It's time we restored domestic tranquility.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And we mean to do just that.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Just as we're positioned as never before to secure justice in our economy, we're poised as never before to create a safer, freer, more peaceful world.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our alliances are stronger than ever.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our economy is stronger than ever.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We have resumed our historic role as a leader of the free world.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And all of these together are a great force for peace.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Since 1981 we've been committed to seeking fair and verifiable arms agreements that would lower the risk of war and reduce the size of nuclear arsenals.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Now our determination to maintain a strong defense has influenced the Soviet Union to return to the bargaining table.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our negotiators must be able to go to that table with the united support of the American people.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: All of us have no greater dream than to see the day when nuclear weapons are banned from this Earth forever.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Each Member of the Congress has a role to play in modernizing our defenses, thus supporting our chances for a meaningful arms agreement.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Your vote this spring on the Peacekeeper missile will be a critical test of our resolve to maintain the strength we need and move toward mutual and verifiable arms reductions.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: For the past 20 years we've believed that no war will be launched as long as each side knows it can retaliate with a deadly counterstrike.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Well, I believe there's a better way of eliminating the threat of nuclear war.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It is a Strategic Defense Initiative aimed ultimately at finding a non-nuclear defense against ballistic missiles.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It's the most hopeful possibility of the nuclear age.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But it's not very well understood.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Some say it will bring war to the heavens, but its purpose is to deter war in the heavens and on Earth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Now, some say the research would be expensive.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Perhaps, but it could save millions of lives, indeed humanity itself.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And some say if we build such a system, the Soviets will build a defense system of their own.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Well, they already have strategic defenses that surpass ours; a civil defense system, where we have almost none; and a research program covering roughly the same areas of technology that we're now exploring.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And finally some say the research will take a long time.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Let's get started.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Harry Truman once said that, ultimately, our security and the world's hopes for peace and human progress lie not in measures of defense or in the control of weapons, but in the growth and expansion of freedom and self-government.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And tonight, we declare anew to our fellow citizens of the world: Freedom is not the sole prerogative of a chosen few; it is the universal right of all God's children.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Look to where peace and prosperity flourish today.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It is in homes that freedom built.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Victories against poverty are greatest and peace most secure where people live by laws that ensure free press, free speech, and freedom to worship, vote, and create wealth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our mission is to nourish and defend freedom and democracy, and to communicate these ideals everywhere we can.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: America's economic success is freedom's success;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: it can be repeated a hundred times in a hundred different nations.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Many countries in east Asia and the Pacific have few resources other than the enterprise of their own people.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But through low tax rates and free markets they've soared ahead of centralized economies.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And now China is opening up its economy to meet its needs.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We need a stronger and simpler approach to the process of making and implementing trade policy, and we'll be studying potential changes in that process in the next few weeks.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We've seen the benefits of free trade and lived through the disasters of protectionism.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Tonight I ask all our trading partners, developed and developing alike, to join us in a new round of trade negotiations to expand trade and competition and strengthen the global economy--and to begin it in this next year.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: There are more than 3 billion human beings living in Third World countries with an average per capita income of $650 a year.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Many are victims of dictatorships that impoverished them with taxation and corruption.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Let us ask our allies to join us in a practical program of trade and assistance that fosters economic development through personal incentives to help these people climb from poverty on their own.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We cannot play innocents abroad in a world that's not innocent;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: nor can we be passive when freedom is under-siege.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Without resources, diplomacy cannot succeed.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our security assistance programs help friendly governments defend themselves and give them confidence to work for peace.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And I hope that you in the Congress will understand that, dollar for dollar, security assistance contributes as much to global security as our own defense budget.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must stand by all our democratic allies.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And we must not break faith with those who are risking their lives--on every continent, from Afghanistan to Nicaragua--to defy Soviet-supported aggression and secure rights which have been ours from birth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The Sandinista dictatorship of Nicaragua, with full Cuban-Soviet bloc support, not only persecutes its people, the church, and denies a free press, but arms and provides bases for Communist terrorists attacking neighboring states.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Support for freedom fighters is self-defense and totally consistent with the OAS and U.N. Charters.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It is essential that the Congress continue all facets of our assistance to Central America.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I want to work with you to support the democratic forces whose struggle is tied to our own security.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And tonight, I've spoken of great plans and great dreams.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: They're dreams we can make come true.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Two hundred years of American history should have taught us that nothing is impossible.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Ten years ago a young girl left Vietnam with her family, part of the exodus that followed the fall of Saigon.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: They came to the United States with no possessions and not knowing a word of English.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Ten years ago--the young girl studied hard, learned English, and finished high school in the top of her class.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And this May, May 22d to be exact, is a big date on her calendar.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Just 10 years from the time she left Vietnam, she will graduate from the United States Military Academy at West Point.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I thought you might like to meet an American hero named Jean Nguyen.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Now, there's someone else here tonight, born 79 years ago.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: She lives in the inner city, where she cares for infants born of mothers who are heroin addicts.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The children, born in withdrawal, are sometimes even dropped on her doorstep.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: She helps them with love.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Go to her house some night, and maybe you'll see her silhouette against the window as she walks the floor talking softly, soothing a child in her arms--Mother Hale of Harlem, and she, too, is an American hero.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Jean, Mother Hale, your lives tell us that the oldest American saying is new again: Anything is possible in America if we have the faith, the will, and the heart.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: History is asking us once again to be a force for good in the world.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Let us begin in unity, with justice, and love.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Thank you, and God bless you.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. President, distinguished members of the Congress, honored guests and fellow citizens, thank you for allowing me to delay my address until this evening.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We paused together to mourn and honor the valor of our seven Challenger heroes .

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And I hope that we are now ready to do what they would want us to do--go forward America and reach for the stars.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We will never forget those brave seven, but we shall go forward.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Mr. Speaker, before I begin my prepared remarks, may I point out that tonight marks the 10th and last State of the Union message that you've presided over.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And on behalf of the American people, I want to salute you for your service to Congress and country.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I have come to review with you the progress of our Nation, to speak of unfinished work, and to set our sights on the future.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I am pleased to report the state of our Union is stronger than a year ago, and growing stronger each day.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Tonight, we look out on a rising America--firm of heart, united in spirit, powerful in pride and patriotism--America is on the move! But, it wasn't long ago that we looked out on a different land--locked factory gates, long gasoline lines, intolerable prices and interest rates turning the greatest country on earth into a land of broken dreams.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Government growing beyond our consent had become a lumbering giant, slamming shut the gates of opportunity, threatening to crush the very roots of our freedom.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: What brought America back?

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The American people brought us back--with quiet courage and common sense;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: with undying faith that in this Nation under God the future will be ours, for the future belongs to the free.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Tonight the American people deserve our thanks--for 37 straight months of economic growth;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: for sunrise firms and modernized industries creating 9 million new jobs in 3 years;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: interest rates cut in half, inflation falling over from 12 percent in 1980 to under 4 today;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: and a mighty river of good works, a record $74 billion in voluntary giving just last year alone.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And despite the pressures of our modern world, family and community remain the moral core of our society, guardians of our values and hopes for the future.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Family and community are the co-stars of this Great American Comeback.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: They are why we say tonight: Private values must be at the heart of public policies.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: What is true for families in America is true for America in the family of free nations.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: History is no captive of some inevitable force.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: History is made by men and women of vision and courage.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Tonight, freedom is on the march.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The United States is the economic miracle, the model to which the world once again turns.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We stand for an idea whose time is now: Only by lifting the weights from the shoulders of all can people truly prosper and can peace among all nations be secure.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Teddy Roosevelt said that a nation that does great work lives forever.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We have done well, but we cannot stop at the foothills when Everest beckons.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It's time for America to be all that we can be.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: an agenda for a safer, more secure world.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And we speak about the necessities for actions to steel us for the challenges of growth, trade and security in the next decade and the year 2000.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And we will do it--not by breaking faith with bedrock principles, but by breaking free from failed policies.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Let us begin where storm clouds loom darkest--right here in Washington, D.C.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This week I will send you our detailed proposals;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: tonight, let us speak of our responsibility to redefine government's role: Not to control, not to demand or command, not to contain us;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: but to help in times of need, and above all, to create a ladder of opportunity to full employment so that all Americans can climb toward economic power and justice on their own.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But we cannot win the race to the future shackled to a system that can't even pass a federal budget.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We cannot win that race held back by horse-and-buggy programs that waste tax dollars and squander human potential.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We cannot win that race if we're swamped in a sea of red ink.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Now, Mr. Speaker, you know, I know, and the American people know the federal budget system is broken.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It doesn't work.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Before we leave this city, let's you and I work together to fix it.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And then we can finally given the American people a balanced budget.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Members of Congress, passage of Gramm-Rudman-Hollings gives us an historic opportunity to achieve what has eluded our national leadership for decades, forcing federal government to live within its means.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Your schedule now requires that the budget resolution be passed by April 15th, the very day America's families have to foot the bill for the budgets that you produce.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: How often we read of a husband and wife both working, struggling from paycheck to paycheck to raise a family, meet a mortgage, pay their taxes and bills.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And yet, some in Congress say taxes must be raised.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Well, I'm sorry--they're asking the wrong people to tighten their belts.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It's time we reduce the federal budget and left the family budget alone.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We do not face large deficits because American families are under taxed; we face those deficits because the federal government overspends.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The detailed budget that we will submit will meet the Gramm-Rudman-Hollings target for deficit reductions, meet our commitment to ensure a strong national defense, meet our commitment to protect Social Security and the truly less fortunate, and, yes, meet our commitment to not raise taxes.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: How should we accomplish this?

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Well, not by taking from those in need.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: As families take care of their own, government must provide shelter and nourishment for those who cannot provide for themselves.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But we must revise or replace programs enacted in the name of compassion that degrade the moral worth of work, encourage family breakups, and drive entire communities into a bleak and heartless dependency.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Gramm-Rudman-Hollings can mark a dramatic improvement.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But experience shows that simply setting deficit targets does not assure they'll be met.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must proceed with Grace Commission reforms against waste.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And tonight, I ask you to give me what 43 Governors have--give me a line-item veto this year.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Give me the authority to veto waste, and I'll take the responsibility, I'll make the cuts, I'll take the heat.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This authority would not give me any monopoly power, but simply prevent spending measures from sneaking through that could not pass on their own merit.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And you can sustain or override my veto--that's, that's the way the system should work.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Once we've made the hard choices, we should lock in our gains with a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I mentioned that we will meet our commitment to national defense.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must meet it.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Defense is not just another budget expense.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Keeping America strong, free, and at peace is solely the responsibility of the Federal Government;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: it is Government's prime responsibility.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We have devoted five years trying to narrow a dangerous gap born of illusion and neglect.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And we've made important gains.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Yet the threat from Soviet forces, conventional and strategic, from the Soviet drive for domination, from the increase in espionage and state terror remains great.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This is reality.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Closing our eyes will not make reality disappear.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We pledge together to hold real growth in defense spending to the bare minimum.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: My budget honors that pledge.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And I'm now asking you, the Congress, to keep its end of the bargain.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The Soviets must know that if America reduces her defenses, it will be because of a reduced threat, not a reduced resolve.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Keeping America strong is as vital to the national security as controlling Federal spending is to our economic security.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But, as I have said before, the most powerful force we can enlist against the Federal deficit is an ever-expanding American economy, unfettered and free.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The magic of opportunity--unreserved, unfailing, unrestrained--isn't this the calling that unites us?

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I believe our tax rate cuts for the people have done more to spur a spirit of risk-taking and help America's economy break free than any program since John Kennedy's tax cut almost a quarter century ago.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Now history calls us to press on, to complete efforts for an historic tax reform providing new opportunity for all and ensuring that all pay their fair share--but no more.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We've come this far.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Will you join me now and we'll walk this last mile together?

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: You know my views on this.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We cannot and we will not accept tax reform that is a tax increase in disguise.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: True reform must be an engine of productivity and growth, and that means a top personal rate no higher than 35 percent.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: True reform must be truly fair and that means raising personal exemptions to $2,000.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: True reform means a tax system that at long last is pro-family, pro-jobs, pro-future, and pro-America.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: As we knock down the barriers to growth, we must redouble our efforts for freer and fairer trade.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We have already taken actions to counter unfair trading practices to pry open closed foreign markets.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We will continue to do so.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We will also oppose legislation touted as providing protection that in reality pits one American worker against another, one industry against another, one community against another, and that raises prices for us all.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: If the United States can trade with other nations on a level playing field, we can out-produce, out-compete, and out-sell anybody, anywhere in the world.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: The constant expansion of our economy and exports requires a sound and stable dollar at home and reliable exchange rates around the world.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must never gain permit wild currency swings to cripple our farmers and other exporters.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Farmers, in particular, have suffered from past unwise government policies.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: They must not be abandoned with problems they did not create and cannot control.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We've begun coordinating economic and monetary policy among our major trading partners.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But there's more to do, and tonight I am directing Treasury Secretary Jim Baker to determine if the nations of the world should convene to discuss the role and relationship of our currencies.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Confident in our future, and secure in our values, Americans are striving forward to embrace the future.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We see it not only in our recovery, but in three straight years of falling crime rates, as families and communities band together to fight pornography, drugs, and lawlessness, and to give back to their children the safe and, yes, innocent childhood they deserve.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We see it in the renaissance in education, the rising SAT scores for three years--last year's increase the greatest since 1963.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It wasn't government and Washington lobbies that turned education around, it was the American people who, in reaching for excellence, knew to reach back to basics.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must continue the advance by supporting discipline in our schools;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: vouchers that give parents freedom of choice;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: and we must give back to our children their lost right to acknowledge God in their classrooms.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We are a nation of idealists, yet today there is a wound in our national conscience;

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: America will never be whole as long as the right to life granted by our Creator is denied to the unborn.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: For the rest of my time, I shall do what I can to see that this wound is one day healed.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: As we work to make the American Dream real for all, we must also look to the condition of America's families.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Struggling parents today worry how they will provide their children the advantages that their parents gave them.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In the welfare culture, the breakdown of the family, the most basic support system, has reached crisis proportions--in female and child poverty, child abandonment, horrible crimes and deteriorating schools.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: After hundreds of billions of dollars in poverty programs, the plight of the poor grows more painful.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But the waste in dollars and cents pales before the most tragic loss--the sinful waste of human spirit and potential.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We can ignore this terrible truth no longer.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Welfare is a narcotic, a subtle destroyer of the human spirit.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And we must now escape the spider's web of dependency.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Tonight I am charging the White House Domestic Council to present me by December 1, 1986, an evaluation of programs and a strategy for immediate action to meet the financial, educational, social, and safety concerns of poor families.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I am talking about real and lasting emancipation, because the success of welfare should be judged by how many of its recipients become independent of welfare.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Further, after seeing how devastating illness can destroy the financial security of the family, I am directing the Secretary of Health and Human Services, Dr. Otis Bowen, to report to me by year end with recommendations on how the private sector and government can work together to address the problems of affordable insurance for those whose life savings would otherwise be threatened when catastrophic illness strikes.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And tonight I want to speak directly to America's younger generation, because you hold the destiny of our nation in your hands.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: With all the temptations young people face it sometimes seems the allure of the permissive society requires superhuman feats of self-control.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But the call of the future is too strong, the challenge too great to get lost in the blind alleyways of dissolution, drugs, and despair.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Never has there been a more exciting time to be alive--a time of rousing wonder and heroic achievement.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Where we are going, we don't need roads.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Well, today physicists peering into the infinitely small realms of subatomic particles find reaffirmations of religious faith.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Yes, everywhere we see a swelling freedom tide across the world--freedom fighters rising up in Cambodia and Angola, fighting and dying for the same democratic liberties we hold sacred.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Their cause is our cause.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Freedom.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Yet, even as we work to expand world freedom, we must build a safer peace and reduce the danger of nuclear war.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But let's have no illusions.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Three years of steady decline in the value of our annual defense investment have increased the risk of our most basic security interests, jeopardizing earlier hard-won goals.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must face squarely the implications of this negative trend and make adequate, stable defense spending a top goal both this year and in the future.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: This same concern applies to economic and security assistance programs as well.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But the resolve of America and its NATO allies has opened the way for unprecedented achievement in arms reduction.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our recently signed INF Treaty is historic because it reduces nuclear arms and establishes the most stringent verification regime in arms control history, including several forms of short-notice, on-site inspection.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: I submitted the treaty today, and I urge the Senate to give its advice and consent to ratification of this landmark agreement.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Thank you very much.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: In addition to the INF Treaty, we're within reach of an even more significant START agreement that will reduce U.S. and Soviet long-range missile or strategic arsenals by half.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But let me be clear--our approach is not to seek agreement for agreement's sake, but to settle only for agreements that truly enhance our national security and that of our allies.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We will never put our security at risk--or that of our allies--just to reach an agreement with the Soviets.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: No agreement is better than a bad agreement.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: As I mentioned earlier, our efforts are to give future generations what we never had--a future free of nuclear terror.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Reduction of strategic offensive arms is one step.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: SDI another.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Our funding request for our Strategic Defense Initiative is less than two percent of the total defense budget.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: SDI funding is money wisely appropriated and money well spent.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: SDI has the same purpose and supports the same goals of arms reduction.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It reduces the risk of war and the threat of nuclear weapons to all mankind.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Strategic defenses that threaten no one could offer the world a safer, more stable basis for deterrence.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We must also remember that SDI is our insurance policy against a nuclear accident--a Chernobyl of the sky--or an accidental launch, or some madman who might come along.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We've seen such changes in the world in seven years--as totalitarianism struggles to avoid being overwhelmed by the forces of economic advance and the aspiration for human freedom, it is the free nations that are resilient and resurgent.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: As the global democratic revolution has put totalitarianism on the defensive, we have left behind the days of retreat--America is again a vigorous leader of the free world, a nation that acts decisively and firmly in the furtherance of her principles and vital interests.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: No legacy would make me more proud than leaving in place a bipartisan consensus for the cause of world freedom, a consensus that prevents a paralysis of American power from ever occurring again.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: But my thoughts tonight go beyond this.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And I hope you'll let me end this evening with a personal reflection.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: You know, the world could never be quite the same again after Jacob Shallus, a trustworthy and dependable clerk of the Pennsylvania General Assembly, took his pen and engrossed those words about representative government in the Preamble of our Constitution.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: And in a quiet but final way, the course of human events was forever altered when, on a ridge overlooking the Emmitsburg Pike in an obscure Pennsylvania town called Gettysburg, Lincoln spoke of our duty to government of and by the people and never letting it perish from the Earth.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: At the start of this decade, I suggested that we lived in equally momentous times--that it is up to us now to decide whether our form of government would endure and whether history still had a place of greatness for a quiet, pleasant, greening land called America.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Not everything has been made perfect in seven years--nor will it be made perfect in seven times 70 years--but before us, this year and beyond, are great prospects for the cause of peace and world freedom.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: It means, too, that the young Americans I spoke of seven years ago, as well as those who might be coming along the Virginia or Maryland shores this night and seeing for the first time the lights of this capital city, the lights that cast their glow on our great halls of government and the monuments to the memory of our great men--it means those young Americans will find a city of hope in a land that is free.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: We can be proud that for them and for us as those lights along the Potomac are still seen this night--signaling, as they have for nearly two centuries and as we pray God they always will, that another generation of Americans has protected and passed on lovingly this place called America, this shining city on a hill, this government of, by, and for the people.

speaker: Ronald W. Reagan
text: Thank you and God bless you.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. President, and distinguished Members of the House and Senate, honored guests, and fellow citizens: Less than 3 weeks ago, I joined you on the West Front of this very building and, looking over the monuments to our proud past, offered you my hand in filling the next page of American history with a story of extended prosperity and continued peace.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And tonight I'm back to offer you my plans as well.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The hand remains extended; the sleeves are rolled up; America is waiting; and now we must produce.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Together, we can build a better America.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: It is comforting to return to this historic Chamber.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Here, 22 years ago, I first raised my hand to be sworn into public life.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: So, tonight I feel as if I'm returning home to friends.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I intend, in the months and years to come, to give you what friends deserve: frankness, respect, and my best judgment about ways to improve America's future.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: In return, I ask for an honest commitment to our common mission of progress.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: If we seize the opportunities on the road before us, there'll be praise enough for all.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The people didn't send us here to bicker, and it's time to govern.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And many Presidents have come to this Chamber in times of great crisis: war and depression, loss of national spirit.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And 8 years ago, I sat in that very chair as President Reagan spoke of punishing inflation and devastatingly high interest rates and people out of work -- American confidence on the wane.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And our challenge is different.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We're fortunate -- a much changed landscape lies before us tonight.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: So, I don't propose to reverse direction.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We're headed the right way, but we cannot rest.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We're a people whose energy and drive have fueled our rise to greatness.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And we're a forward-looking nation -- generous, yes, but ambitious, not for ourselves but for the world.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Complacency is not in our character -- not before, not now, not ever.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And so, tonight we must take a strong America and make it even better.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must address some very real problems.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must establish some very clear priorities.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And we must make a very substantial cut in the Federal budget deficit.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Some people find that agenda impossible, but I'm presenting to you tonight a realistic plan for tackling it.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: My plan has four broad features: attention to urgent priorities, investment in the future, an attack on the deficit, and no new taxes.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: This budget represents my best judgment of how we can address our priorities.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: There are many areas in which we would all like to spend more than I propose;

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I understand that.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But we cannot until we get our fiscal house in order.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Next year alone, thanks to economic growth, without any change in the law, the Federal Government will take in over $80 billion more than it does this year.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: That's right -- over $80 billion in new revenues, with no increases in taxes.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And our job is to allocate those new resources wisely.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We can afford to increase spending by a modest amount, but enough to invest in key priorities and still cut the deficit by almost 40 percent in 1 year.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And that will allow us to meet the targets set forth in the Gramm-Rudman-Hollings law.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But to do that, we must recognize that growth above inflation in Federal programs is not preordained, that not all spending initiatives were designed to be immortal.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I make this pledge tonight: My team and I are ready to work with the Congress, to form a special leadership group, to negotiate in good faith, to work day and night -- if that's what it takes -- to meet the budget targets and to produce a budget on time.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We cannot settle for business as usual.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Government by continuing resolution, or government by crisis, will not do.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I ask the Congress tonight to approve several measures which will make budgeting more sensible.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We could save time and improve efficiency by enacting 2-year budgets.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Forty-three Governors have the line-item veto.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Presidents should have it, too.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And at the very least, when a President proposes to rescind Federal spending, the Congress should be required to vote on that proposal instead of killing it by inaction.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I ask the Congress to honor the public's wishes by passing a constitutional amendment to require a balanced budget.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Such an amendment, once phased in, will discipline both the Congress and the executive branch.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Several principles describe the kind of America I hope to build with your help in the years ahead.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We will not have the luxury of taking the easy, spendthrift approach to solving problems because higher spending and higher taxes put economic growth at risk.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Economic growth provides jobs and hope.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Economic growth enables us to pay for social programs.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Economic growth enhances the security of the Nation, and low tax rates create economic growth.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I believe in giving Americans greater freedom and greater choice.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I will work for choice for American families, whether in the housing in which they live, the schools to which they send their children, or the child care they select for their young.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: You see, I believe that we have an obligation to those in need, but that government should not be the provider of first resort for things that the private sector can produce better.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I believe in a society that is free from discrimination and bigotry of any kind.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I will work to knock down the barriers left by past discrimination and to build a more tolerant society that will stop such barriers from ever being built again.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I believe that family and faith represent the moral compass of the Nation.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I believe in giving people the power to make their own lives better through growth and opportunity.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And together, let's put power in the hands of people.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Three weeks ago, we celebrated the bicentennial inaugural, the 200th anniversary of the first Presidency.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And if you look back, one thing is so striking about the way the Founding Fathers looked at America.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: They didn't talk about themselves.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: They talked about posterity.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: They talked about the future.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And we, too, must think in terms bigger than ourselves.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must take actions today that will ensure a better tomorrow.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must extend American leadership in technology, increase long-term investment, improve our educational system, and boost productivity.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: These are the keys to building a better future, and here are some of my recommendations: I propose almost $2.2 billion for the National Science Foundation to promote basic research and keep us on track to double its budget by 1993.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I propose to make permanent the tax credit for research and development.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I've asked Vice President Quayle to chair a new Task Force on Competitiveness.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I request funding for NASA [National Aeronautics and Space Administration] and a strong space program, an increase of almost $2.4 billion over the current fiscal year.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must have a manned space station; a vigorous, safe space shuttle program;

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: and more commercial development in space.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: full throttle up.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And that's not just our ambition;

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: it's our destiny.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I propose that we cut the maximum tax rate on capital gains to increase long-term investment.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: History on this is clear -- this will increase revenues, help savings, and create new jobs.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We won't be competitive if we leave whole sectors of America behind.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: This is the year we should finally enact urban enterprise zones and bring hope to the inner cities.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But the most important competitiveness program of all is one which improves education in America.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: When some of our students actually have trouble locating America on a map of the world, it is time for us to map a new approach to education.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must reward excellence and cut through bureaucracy.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must help schools that need help the most.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must give choice to parents, students, teachers, and principals; and we must hold all concerned accountable.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: In education, we cannot tolerate mediocrity.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I want to cut that dropout rate and make America a more literate nation, because what it really comes down to is this: The longer our graduation lines are today, the shorter our unemployment lines will be tomorrow.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: So, tonight I'm proposing the following initiatives: the beginning of a $500 million program to reward America's best schools, merit schools;

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: the creation of special Presidential awards for the best teachers in every State, because excellence should be rewarded;

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: the establishment of a new program of National Science Scholars, one each year for every Member of the House and Senate, to give this generation of students a special incentive to excel in science and mathematics;

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: the expanded use of magnet schools, which give families and students greater choice;

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: and a new program to encourage alternative certification, which will let talented people from all fields teach in our classrooms.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Education President.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And tonight, I'd ask you to join me by becoming the Education Congress.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Just last week, as I settled into this new office, I received a letter from a mother in Pennsylvania who had been struck by my message in the Inaugural Address.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: my husband and I received word that our son was addicted to cocaine.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: He had the world at his feet.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Bright, gifted, personable -- he could have done anything with his life.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And now he has chosen cocaine.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: find a way to curb the supply of cocaine.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Get tough with the pushers.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Our son needs your help.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: My friends, that voice crying out for help could be the voice of your own neighbor, your own friend, your own son.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Over 23 million Americans used illegal drugs last year, at a staggering cost to our nation's well-being.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let this be recorded as the time when America rose up and said no to drugs.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The scourge of drugs must be stopped.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I am asking tonight for an increase of almost a billion dollars in budget outlays to escalate the war against drugs.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The war must be waged on all fronts.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Our new drug czar, Bill Bennett, and I will be shoulder to shoulder in the executive branch leading the charge.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Some money will be used to expand treatment to the poor and to young mothers.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: This will offer the helping hand to the many innocent victims of drugs, like the thousands of babies born addicted or with AIDS because of the mother's addiction.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Some will be used to cut the waiting time for treatment.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Some money will be devoted to those urban schools where the emergency is now the worst.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And much of it will be used to protect our borders, with help from the Coast Guard and the Customs Service, the Departments of State and Justice, and, yes, the U.S. military.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I mean to get tough on the drug criminals.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And let me be clear: This President will back up those who put their lives on the line every single day -- our local police officers.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: My budget asks for beefed-up prosecution, for a new attack on organized crime, and for enforcement of tough sentences -- and for the worst kingpins, that means the death penalty.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I also want to make sure that when a drug dealer is convicted there's a cell waiting for him.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And he should not go free because prisons are too full.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And so, let the word go out: If you're caught and convicted, you will do time.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But for all we do in law enforcement, in interdiction and treatment, we will never win this war on drugs unless we stop the demand for drugs.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: So, some of this increase will be used to educate the young about the dangers of drugs.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must involve the parents.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must involve the teachers.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must involve the communities.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And, my friends, we must involve ourselves, each and every one of us in this concern.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: One problem related to drug use demands our urgent attention and our continuing compassion, and that is the terrible tragedy of AIDS.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I'm asking for $1.6 billion for education to prevent the disease and for research to find a cure.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: If we're to protect our future, we need a new attitude about the environment.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must protect the air we breathe.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I will send to you shortly legislation for a new, more effective Clean Air Act.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: It will include a plan to reduce by date certain the emissions which cause acid rain, because the time for study alone has passed, and the time for action is now.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must make use of clean coal.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: My budget contains full funding, on schedule, for the clean coal technology agreement that we've made with Canada.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We've made that agreement with Canada, and we intend to honor that agreement.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must not neglect our parks.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: So, I'm asking to fund new acquisitions under the Land and Water Conservation Fund.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must protect our oceans.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I support new penalties against those who would dump medical waste and other trash into our oceans.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The age of the needle on the beaches must end.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And in some cases, the gulfs and oceans off our shores hold the promise of oil and gas reserves which can make our nation more secure and less dependent on foreign oil.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And when those with the most promise can be tapped safely, as with much of the Alaska National Wildlife Refuge, we should proceed.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But we must use caution; we must respect the environment.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And so, tonight I'm calling for the indefinite postponement of three lease sales which have raised troubling questions, two off the coast of California and one which could threaten the Everglades in Florida.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Action on these three lease sales will await the conclusion of a special task force set up to measure the potential for environmental damage.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I'm directing the Attorney General and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to use every tool at their disposal to speed and toughen the enforcement of our laws against toxic-waste dumpers.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I want faster cleanups and tougher enforcement of penalties against polluters.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: In addition to caring for our future, we must care for those around us.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: A decent society shows compassion for the young, the elderly, the vulnerable, and the poor.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Our first obligation is to the most vulnerable -- infants, poor mothers, children living in poverty -- and my proposed budget recognizes this.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I ask for full funding of Medicaid, an increase of over $3 billion, and an expansion of the program to include coverage of pregnant women who are near the poverty line.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I believe we should help working families cope with the burden of child care.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Our help should be aimed at those who need it most: low-income families with young children.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I support a new child care tax credit that will aim our efforts at exactly those families, without discriminating against mothers who choose to stay at home.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Now, I know there are competing proposals.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But remember this: The overwhelming majority of all preschool child care is now provided by relatives and neighbors and churches and community groups.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Families who choose these options should remain eligible for help.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Parents should have choice.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And for those children who are unwanted or abused or whose parents are deceased, we should encourage adoption.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I propose to reenact the tax deduction for adoption expenses and to double it to $3,000.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let's make it easier for these kids to have parents who love them.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We have a moral contract with our senior citizens.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And in this budget, Social Security is fully funded, including a full cost-of-living adjustment.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must honor our contract.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must care about those in the shadow of life, and I, like many Americans, am deeply troubled by the plight of the homeless.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The causes of homelessness are many; the history is long.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But the moral imperative to act is clear.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Thanks to the deep well of generosity in this great land, many organizations already contribute, but we in government cannot stand on the sidelines.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: In my budget, I ask for greater support for emergency food and shelter, for health services and measures to prevent substance abuse, and for clinics for the mentally ill.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I propose a new initiative involving the full range of government agencies.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must confront this national shame.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: There's another issue that I've decided to mention here tonight.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I've long believed that the people of Puerto Rico should have the right to determine their own political future.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Personally, I strongly favor statehood.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But I urge the Congress to take the necessary steps to allow the people to decide in a referendum.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Certain problems, the result of decades of unwise practices, threaten the health and security of our people.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Left unattended, they will only get worse.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But we can act now to put them behind us.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Earlier this week, I announced my support for a plan to restore the financial and moral integrity of our savings system.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I ask Congress to enact our reform proposals within 45 days.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must not let this situation fester.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We owe it to the savers in this country to solve this problem.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Certainly, the savings of Americans must remain secure.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let me be clear: Insured depositors will continue to be fully protected, but any plan to refinance the system must be accompanied by major reform.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Our proposals will prevent such a crisis from recurring.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The best answer is to make sure that a mess like this will never happen again.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The majority of thrifts in communities across the Nation have been honest.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: They've played a major role in helping families achieve the dream of home ownership.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But make no mistake, those who are corrupt, those who break the law, must be kicked out of the business; and they should go to jail.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We face a massive task in cleaning up the waste left from decades of environmental neglect at America's nuclear weapons plants.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Clearly, we must modernize these plants and operate them safely.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: That's not at issue; our national security depends on it.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But beyond that, we must clean up the old mess that's been left behind.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I propose in this budget to more than double our current effort to do so.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: This will allow us to identify the exact nature of the various problems so we can clean them up, and clean them up we will.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We've been fortunate during these past 8 years.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: America is a stronger nation than it was in 1980.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Morale in our Armed Forces has been restored; our resolve has been shown.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Our readiness has been improved, and we are at peace.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: There can no longer be any doubt that peace has been made more secure through strength.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And when America is stronger, the world is safer.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Most people don't realize that after the successful restoration of our strength, the Pentagon budget has actually been reduced in real terms for each of the last 4 years.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We cannot tolerate continued real reduction in defense.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: In light of the compelling need to reduce the deficit, however, I support a 1-year freeze in the military budget, something I proposed last fall in my flexible freeze plan.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And this freeze will apply for only 1 year, and after that, increases above inflation will be required.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I will not sacrifice American preparedness, and I will not compromise American strength.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I should be clear on the conditions attached to my recommendation for the coming year: The savings must be allocated to those priorities for investing in our future that I've spoken about tonight.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: This defense freeze must be a part of a comprehensive budget agreement which meets the targets spelled out in Gramm-Rudman-Hollings law without raising taxes and which incorporates reforms in the budget process.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I've directed the National Security Council to review our national security and defense policies and report back to me within 90 days to ensure that our capabilities and resources meet our commitments and strategies.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I'm also charging the Department of Defense with the task of developing a plan to improve the defense procurement process and management of the Pentagon, one which will fully implement the Packard commission report.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Many of these changes can only be made with the participation of the Congress, and so, I ask for your help.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We need fewer regulations.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We need less bureaucracy.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We need multiyear procurement and 2-year budgeting.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And frankly -- and don't take this wrong -- we need less congressional micromanagement of our nation's military policy.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I detect a slight division on that question, but nevertheless -- [laughter].

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Securing a more peaceful world is perhaps the most important priority I'd like to address tonight.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: You know, we meet at a time of extraordinary hope.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Never before in this century have our values of freedom, democracy, and economic opportunity been such a powerful and intellectual force around the globe.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Never before has our leadership been so crucial, because while America has its eyes on the future, the world has its eyes on America.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And it's a time of great change in the world, and especially in the Soviet Union.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Prudence and common sense dictate that we try to understand the full meaning of the change going on there, review our policies, and then proceed with caution.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But I've personally assured General Secretary Gorbachev that at the conclusion of such a review we will be ready to move forward.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We will not miss any opportunity to work for peace.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The fundamental facts remain that the Soviets retain a very powerful military machine in the service of objectives which are still too often in conflict with ours.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: So, let us take the new openness seriously, but let's also be realistic.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And let's always be strong.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: There are some pressing issues we must address.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I will vigorously pursue the Strategic Defense Initiative.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The spread, and even use, of sophisticated weaponry threatens global security as never before.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Chemical weapons must be banned from the face of the Earth, never to be used again.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And look, this won't be easy.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Verification -- extraordinarily difficult, but civilization and human decency demand that we try.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And the spread of nuclear weapons must be stopped.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I'll work to strengthen the hand of the International Atomic Energy Agency.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Our diplomacy must work every day against the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And around the globe, we must continue to be freedom's best friend.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And we must stand firm for self-determination and democracy in Central America, including in Nicaragua.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: It is my strongly held conviction that when people are given the chance they inevitably will choose a free press, freedom of worship, and certifiably free and fair elections.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We must strengthen the alliance of the industrial democracies, as solid a force for peace as the world has ever known.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And this is an alliance forged by the power of our ideals, not the pettiness of our differences.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: So, let's lift our sights to rise above fighting about beef hormones, to building a better future, to move from protectionism to progress.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I've asked the Secretary of State to visit Europe next week and to consult with our allies on the wide range of challenges and opportunities we face together, including East-West relations.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I look forward to meeting with our NATO partners in the near future.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I, too, shall begin a trip shortly to the far reaches of the Pacific Basin, where the winds of democracy are creating new hope and the power of free markets is unleashing a new force.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: When I served as our representative in China 14 or 15 years ago, few would have predicted the scope of the changes we've witnessed since then.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But in preparing for this trip, I was struck by something I came across from a Chinese writer.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: He was speaking of his country, decades ago, but his words speak to each of us in America tonight.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: we're afraid of the simple words like `goodness' and `mercy' and `kindness.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: My friends, if we're to succeed as a nation, we must rediscover those words.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: opportunity.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Lincoln once said: I hold that while man exists, it is his duty to improve not only his own condition but to assist in ameliorating that of mankind.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: It is this broader mission to which I call all Americans, because the definition of a successful life must include serving others.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And to the young people of America, who sometimes feel left out, I ask you tonight to give us the benefit of your talent and energy through a new program called YES, for Youth Entering Service to America.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: To those men and women in business, remember the ultimate end of your work: to make a better product, to create better lives.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I ask you to plan for the longer term and avoid that temptation of quick and easy paper profits.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: To the brave men and women who wear the uniform of the United States of America, thank you.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Your calling is a high one: to be the defenders of freedom and the guarantors of liberty.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And I want you to know that this nation is grateful for your service.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: To the farmers of America, we appreciate the bounty you provide.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We will work with you to open foreign markets to American agricultural products.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And to the parents of America, I ask you to get involved in your child's schooling.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Check on the homework, go to the school, meet the teachers, care about what is happening there.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: It's not only your child's future on the line, it's America's.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: To kids in our cities, don't give up hope.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Say no to drugs; stay in school.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Keep hope alive.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: To those 37 million Americans with some form of disability, you belong in the economic mainstream.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We need your talents in America's work force.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Disabled Americans must become full partners in America's opportunity society.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: To the families of America watching tonight in your living rooms, hold fast to your dreams because ultimately America's future rests in your hands.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And to my friends in this Chamber, I ask your cooperation to keep America growing while cutting the deficit.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: That's only fair to those who now have no vote: the generations to come.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let them look back and say that we had the foresight to understand that a time of peace and prosperity is not the time to rest but a time to press forward, a time to invest in the future.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And let all Americans remember that no problem of human making is too great to be overcome by human ingenuity, human energy, and the untiring hope of the human spirit.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I believe this.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I would not have asked to be your President if I didn't.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And tomorrow the debate on the plan I've put forward begins, and I ask the Congress to come forward with your own proposals.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let's not question each other's motives.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let's debate, let's negotiate; but let us solve the problem.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Recalling anniversaries may not be my specialty in speeches -- [laughter] -- but tonight is one of some note.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: On February 9th, 1941, just 48 years ago tonight, Sir Winston Churchill took to the airwaves during Britain's hour of peril.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Sail on, O Ship of State! Sail on, O Union, strong and great!

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And Churchill responded on this night by radio broadcast to a nation at war, but he directed his words to Franklin Roosevelt.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We shall not fail or falter, he said.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We shall not weaken or tire.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Give us the tools, and we will finish the job.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Tonight, almost half a century later, our peril may be less immediate, but the need for perseverance and clear-sighted fortitude is just as great.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Now, as then, there are those who say it can't be done.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: There are voices who say that America's best days have passed, that we're bound by constraints, threatened by problems, surrounded by troubles which limit our ability to hope.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Well, tonight I remain full of hope.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: We Americans have only begun on our mission of goodness and greatness.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Give us the tools, and we will do the job.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Thank you.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: God bless you, and God bless America.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Mr. President, Mr. Speaker, Members of the United States Congress: I return as a former President of the Senate and a former Member of this great House.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And now, as President, it is my privilege to report to you on the state of the Union.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Tonight I come not to speak about the state of the Government, not to detail every new initiative we plan for the coming year nor to describe every line in the budget.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I'm here to speak to you and to the American people about the state of the Union, about our world -- the changes we've seen, the challenges we face -- and what that means for America.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: There are singular moments in history, dates that divide all that goes before from all that comes after.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And many of us in this Chamber have lived much of our lives in a world whose fundamental features were defined in 1945;

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: and the events of that year decreed the shape of nations, the pace of progress, freedom or oppression for millions of people around the world.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Nineteen forty-five provided the common frame of reference, the compass points of the postwar era we've relied upon to understand ourselves.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And that was our world, until now.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The events of the year just ended, the Revolution of '89, have been a chain reaction, changes so striking that it marks the beginning of a new era in the world's affairs.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Think back -- think back just 12 short months ago to the world we knew as 1989 began.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: One year -- one year ago, the people of Panama lived in fear, under the thumb of a dictator.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Today democracy is restored;

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Panama is free.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Operation Just Cause has achieved its objective.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The number of military personnel in Panama is now very close to what it was before the operation began.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And tonight I am announcing that well before the end of February, the additional numbers of American troops, the brave men and women of our Armed Forces who made this mission a success, will be back home.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: A year ago in Poland, Lech Walesa declared that he was ready to open a dialog with the Communist rulers of that country;

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: and today, with the future of a free Poland in their own hands, members of Solidarity lead the Polish Government.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: A year ago, freedom's playwright, Vaclav Havel, languished as a prisoner in Prague.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And today it's Vaclav Havel, President of Czechoslovakia.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And 1 year ago, Erich Honecker of East Germany claimed history as his guide, and he predicted the Berlin Wall would last another hundred years.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: And today, less than 1 year later, it's the Wall that's history.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Remarkable events -- events that fulfill the long-held hopes of the American people; events that validate the longstanding goals of American policy, a policy based on a single, shining principle: the cause of freedom.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: America, not just the nation but an idea, alive in the minds of people everywhere.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: As this new world takes shape, America stands at the center of a widening circle of freedom -- today, tomorrow, and into the next century.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Our nation is the enduring dream of every immigrant who ever set foot on these shores, and the millions still struggling to be free.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: This nation, this idea called America, was and always will be a new world -- our new world.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
