text: We will put people to work right now and create half a million jobs: jobs that will rebuild our highways and airports, renovate housing, bring new life to our rural towns, and spread hope and opportunity among our nation's youth with almost 700,000 jobs for them this summer alone.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I invite America's business leaders to join us in this effort, so that together we can create a million summer jobs in cities and poor rural areas for our young people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Second, our plan looks beyond today's business cycle, because our aspirations extend into the next century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The heart of our plan deals with the long term.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It has an investment program designed to increase public and private investment in areas critical to our economic future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And it has a deficit reduction program that will increase savings available for private sector investment, lower interest rates, decrease the percentage of the federal budget claimed by interest payments, and decrease the risk of financial market disruptions that could adversely affect the economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Over the long run, all this should result in a higher rate of economic growth, improved productivity, higher wages, more high- quality jobs and an improved economic competitive position in the global economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In order to accomplish public investment and deficit reduction, government spending is being cut and taxes are being increased.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our spending cuts were carefully thought through to try to minimize any economic impact, to capture the peace dividend for investment purposes, and to switch the balance in the budget from consumption to investment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The tax increases and spending cuts were both designed to assure that the cost of this historic program to face and deal with our problems is borne by those who could most readily afford that cost.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our plan is designed to improve the health of American business through lower interest rates, improved infrastructure, better trained workers, and a stronger middle class.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because small businesses generate most of our nation's jobs, our plan includes the boldest targeted incentives for small business in history.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We propose a permanent investment tax credit for small business, and new rewards for entrepreneurs who take risks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will give small business access to the brilliant technologies of our time and to the credit they need to prosper and flourish.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With a new network of community development banks, and one billion dollars to make the dream of enterprise zones real, we will begin to bring new hope and new jobs to storefronts and factories from South Boston to South Texas to south-central Los Angeles.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our plan invests in our roads, bridges, transit facilities;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: in high- speed railways and high-tech information systems;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: and in the most ambitious environmental clean-up of our time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: On the edge of the new century, economic growth depends as never before on opening up new markets overseas.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And so we will insist on fair trade rules in international markets.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: NAFTA A part of our national economic strategy must be to expand trade on fair terms, including successful completion of the latest round of world trade talks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A North American Free Trade Agreement with appropriate safeguards for workers and the environment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: At the same time, we need an aggressive attempt to create the hi-tech jobs of the future; special attention to troubled industries like aerospace and airlines, and special assistance to displaced workers like those in our defense industry.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I pledge that business, government and labor will work together in a partnership to strengthen America for a change.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Health Care Reform But all of our efforts to strengthen the economy will fail unless we take bold steps to reform our health care system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America's businesses will never be strong; America's families will never be secure;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: and America's government will never be solvent until we tackle our health care crisis.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The rising costs and the lack of care are endangering both our economy and our lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Reducing health care costs will liberate hundreds of billions of dollars for investment and growth and new jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Over the long run, reforming health care is essential to reducing our deficit and expanding investment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Later this spring, I will deliver to Congress a comprehensive plan for health care reform that will finally get costs under control.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will provide security to all our families, so that no one will be denied the coverage they need.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will root out fraud and outrageous charges, and make sure that paperwork no longer chokes you or your doctor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we will maintain American standards - the highest quality medical care in the world and the choices we demand and deserve.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The American people expect us to deal with health care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we must deal with it now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Perhaps the most fundamental change our new direction offers is its focus on the future and the investments we seek in our children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Each day we delay carries a dear cost.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Half our two-year-olds don't receive immunizations against deadly diseases.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our plan will provide them for every eligible child.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we'll save ten dollars for every one we'll spend by eliminating preventable childhood diseases.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The Women, Infants, and Children nutrition program will be expanded so that every expectant mother who needs our help receives it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Education Head Start - a program that prepares children for school - is a success story.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It saves money, but today it reaches only one-third of all eligible children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Under our plan, we will cover every eligible child.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Investing in Head Start and WIC is not only the right thing, it's the smart thing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For every dollar we invest today, we save three tomorrow.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America must ask more of our students, our teachers, and our schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we must give them the resources they need to meet high standards.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will bring together business and schools to establish new apprenticeships, and give young people the skills they need today to find productive jobs tomorrow.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Lifelong learning will benefit workers throughout their careers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must create a new unified worker training system, so that workers receive training regardless of why they lost their jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our national service program will make college loans available to all Americans, and challenge them to give something back to their country - as teachers, police officers, community service workers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This will be an historic change on a scale with the creation of the Land Grant Colleges and the G.I. Bill.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A hundred years from now, historians who owe their education to our plan for national service will salute your vision.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We believe in jobs, we believe in learning, and we believe in rewarding work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We believe in restoring the values that make America special.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There is dignity in all work, and there must be dignity for all workers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To those who heal our sick, care for our children, and do our most tiring and difficult jobs, our new direction makes this solemn commitment: By expanding the Earned Income Tax Credit, we will make history: We will help reward work for millions of working poor Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our new direction aims to realize a principle as powerful as it is simple: If you work full time, you should not be poor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Welfare Later this year, we will offer a plan to end welfare as we know it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: No one wants to change the welfare system as much as those who are trapped by the welfare system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will offer people on welfare the education, training, child care and health care they need to get back on their feet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Then, after two years, they must get back to work - in private business if possible; in public service, if necessary.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's time to end welfare as a way of life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Strengthening Families Our next great goal is to strengthen American families.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We'll ask fathers and mothers to take more responsibility for their children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we'll crack down on deadbeat parents who won't pay their child support.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Crime We want to protect our families against violent crime which terrorizes our people and tears apart our communities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must pass a tough crime bill.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need to put 100,000 more police on the street, provide boot camps for first-time non-violent offenders, and put hardened criminals behind bars.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have a duty to keep guns out of the hands of criminals.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If you pass the Brady Bill, I'll sign it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Reform To make government work for middle-class taxpayers and not the special interests, we must reform our political system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'm asking Congress to enact real campaign finance reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's reduce the power of special interests and increase the participation of the people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should end the tax deduction for special interest lobbying and use the money to help clean up the political system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we should quickly enact legislation to force lobbyists to disclose their activities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But to revolutionize government we have to insure that it lives within its means.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And that starts at the top - with the White House.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the last few weeks, I have cut the White House staff by twenty-five percent, saving ten million dollars.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ordered administrative cuts in the budgets of agencies and departments, I cut the federal bureaucracy by 100,000 positions, for combined savings of nine billion dollars.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's time for government to be as frugal as any household in America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why I congratulate the Congress for taking similar steps to cut its costs today.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Together, we can show the American people that we have heard their call for change.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we can go further.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I call for an across-the-board freeze in federal government salaries for one year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thereafter, federal salaries will rise at a rate lower than the rate of inflation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must reinvent government to make it work again.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We'll push innovative education reform to improve learning, not just spend more money.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We'll use the Superfund to clean up pollution, not just increase lawyers' incomes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We'll use federal banking regulators, not just to protect the security and safety of our financial institutions, but to break the credit crunch.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we'll change the whole focus of our poverty programs from entitlement to empowerment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Deficit Reduction For years, there has been a lot of talk about the deficit, but very few credible efforts to deal with it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This plan does.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our plan tackles the budget deficit - seriously and over the long term.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will put in place one of the biggest deficit reductions and the biggest change of federal priorities in our history at the same time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are not cutting the deficit because the experts tell us to do so.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are cutting the deficit so that your family can afford a college education for your children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are cutting the deficit so that your children will someday be able to buy a home of their own.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are cutting the deficit so that your company can invest in retraining its workers and retooling its factories.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are cutting the deficit so that government can make the investments that help us become stronger and smarter and safer.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we do not act now, we will not recognize this country ten years from now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Ten years from now, the deficit will have grown to 635 billion dollars a year; the national debt will be almost 80 percent of our gross domestic product.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Paying the interest on that debt will be the costliest government program of all, and we will continue to be the world's largest debtor, depending on foreign funds for a large part of our nation's investments.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Budget Our budget will, by 1997, cut 140 billion dollars from the deficit - one of the greatest real spending cuts by an American president.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are making more than 150 difficult, painful reductions which will cut federal spending by 246 billion dollars.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are eliminating programs that are no longer needed, such as nuclear power research and development.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are slashing subsidies and canceling wasteful projects.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Many of these programs were justified in their time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But if we're going to start new plans, we must eliminate old ones.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Government has been good at building programs, now we must show that we can limit them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Defense As we restructure American military forces to meet the new threats of the post-Cold War world, we can responsibly reduce our defense budget.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But let no one be in any doubt: The men and women who serve under the American flag will be the best trained, best equipped, best prepared fighting force in the world, so long as I am President.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Backed by a leaner and more effective national defense and a stronger economy, our nation will be prepared to lead a world challenged by ethnic conflict, the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, the global democratic revolution, and the health of our environment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Taxes Our economic plan is ambitious, but it is necessary for the continued greatness of our country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And it will be paid for fairly -- by cutting government, by asking the most of those who benefited most in the past - by asking more Americans to contribute today so that all Americans can do better tomorrow.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For the wealthiest - those earning more than 180,000 dollars per year, I ask you to raise the top rate for federal income taxes from 31 percent to 36 percent.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our plan recommends a ten percent surtax on incomes over 250,000 dollars a year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we will close the loopholes that let some get away without paying any tax at all.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For businesses with taxable incomes over ten million dollars, we will raise the corporate tax rate to 36 percent.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we will cut the deduction for business entertainment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our plan attacks tax subsidies that reward companies that ship jobs overseas.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we will ensure that, through effective tax enforcement, foreign corporations who make money in America pay the taxes they owe to America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Middle-class Americans should know: You're not going alone any more;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: you're not going first;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: and you're no longer going to pay more and get less.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Ninety-eight point eight percent of America's families will have no increase in their income tax rates.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Only the wealthiest one point two percent will see their rates rise.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Medicare Let me be clear: There will be no new cuts in benefits from Medicare for beneficiaries.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There will be cuts in payments to providers: doctors, hospitals, and labs, as a way of controlling health care costs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These cuts are only a stop-gap until we reform the whole health care system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let me repeat that, because it matters to me, as I know it matters to you: This plan will not make new cuts in Medicare benefits for any beneficiary.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Social Security The only change we are making in Social Security is to ask those older Americans with higher incomes, who do not rely solely on Social Security to get by, to contribute more.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This change will not affect eighty percent of Social Security recipients.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If you do not pay taxes on Social Security now, you will not pay taxes on Social Security under this plan.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our plan includes a tax on energy as the best way to provide us with new revenue to lower the deficit and invest in our people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Moreover, unlike other taxes, this one reduces pollution, increases energy efficiency, and eases our dependence on oil from unstable regions of the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Taken together, these measures will cost an American family earning 40 thousand dollars a year less than 17 dollars a month.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And because of other programs we will propose, families earning less than 30,000 dollars a year will pay virtually no additional tax at all.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because of our publicly stated determination to reduce the deficit, interest rates have fallen since the election.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That means that, for the middle class, the increases in energy costs will be more than offset by lower interest costs for mortgages, consumer loans and credit cards.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is a wise investment for you and for your country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask all Americans to consider the cost of not changing, of not choosing a new direction.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Unless we have the courage to start building our future and stop borrowing from it, we are condemning ourselves to years of stagnation, interrupted only by recession; to slow growth in jobs, no growth in incomes, and more debt and disappointment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Worse yet - unless we change, unless we reduce the deficit, increase investment, and raise productivity so we can generate jobs - we will condemn our children and our children's children to a lesser life and a diminished destiny.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, the American people know we must change.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But they are also likely to ask whether we have the fortitude to make those changes happen.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They know that, as soon as we leave this Chamber, the special interests will be out in force, trying to stop the changes we seek.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The forces of conventional wisdom will offer a thousand reasons why it can't be done.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And our people will be watching and wondering to see if it's going to be business as usual again.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So we must scale the walls of their skepticism, not with our words, but by our deeds.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: After so many years of gridlock and indecision, after so many hopeful beginnings and so few promising results, Americans will be harsh in their judgments of us if we fail to seize this moment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This economic plan cannot please everybody.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If this package is picked apart, there will be something that will anger each of us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But, if it is taken as a whole, it will help all of us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Resist the temptation to focus only on a spending cut you don't like or some investment not made.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And nobody likes tax increases.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But let's face facts: For 20 years incomes have stalled.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For years, debt has exploded.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can no longer afford to deny reality.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must play the hand we were dealt.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The test of our program cannot simply be: What's in it for me?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The question must be: What's in it for us?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we work hard - and work together - if we rededicate ourselves to strengthening families, creating jobs, rewarding work, and reinventing government, we can lift America's fortunes once again.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight I ask everyone in this Chamber - and every American - to look into their hearts, spark their hopes, and fire their imaginations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There is so much good, so much possibility, so much excitement in our nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we act boldly, as leaders should, our legacy will be one of progress and prosperity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This, then, is America's new direction.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us summon the courage to seize the day.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you very much.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Good night.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And may God bless America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you very much.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. President, members of the 103rd Congress, my fellow Americans:

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'm not at all sure what speech is in the TelePrompter tonight -- but I hope we can talk about the state of the Union.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to begin by recalling the memory of the giant who presided over this Chamber with such force and grace.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And he surely was that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But, even more, he was a man of the people, a bricklayer's son who helped to build the great American middle class.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tip O'Neill never forgot who he was, where he came from, or who sent him here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight he's smiling down on us for the first time from the Lord's Gallery.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But in his honor, may we, too, always remember who we are, where we come from, and who sent us here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we do that we will return over and over again to the principle that if we simply give ordinary people equal opportunity, quality education, and a fair shot at the American Dream, they will do extraordinary things.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We gather tonight in a world of changes so profound and rapid that all nations are tested.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our American heritage has always been to master such change, to use it to expand opportunity at home and our leadership abroad.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But for too long, and in too many ways, that heritage was abandoned, and our country drifted.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For 30 years, family life in America has been breaking down.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For 20 years, the wages of working people have been stagnant or declining.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For the 12 years of trickle-down economics, we built a false prosperity on a hollow base as our national debt quadrupled.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: From 1989 to 1992, we experienced the slowest growth in a half century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For too many families, even when both parents were working, the American Dream has been slipping away.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In 1992, the American people demanded that we change.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A year ago I asked all of you to join me in accepting responsibility for the future of our country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Well, we did.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We replaced drift and deadlock with renewal and reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I want to thank every one of you here who heard the American people, who broke gridlock, who gave them the most successful teamwork between a President and a Congress in 30 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This Congress produced a budget that cut the deficit by half a trillion dollars, cut spending and raised income taxes on only the wealthiest Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This Congress produced tax relief for millions of low income workers to reward work over welfare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It produced NAFTA.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It produced the Brady bill, now the Brady law.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And thank you, Jim Brady, for being here, and God bless you, sir.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This Congress produced tax cuts to reduce the taxes of nine out of 10 small businesses who use the money to invest more and create jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It produced more research and treatment for AIDS, more childhood immunizations, more support for women's health research, more affordable college loans for the middle class.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A new national service program for those who want to give something back to their country and their communities for higher education.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A dramatic increase in high-tech investments to move us from a defense to a domestic high-tech economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This Congress produced a new law, the Motor Voter bill, to help millions of people register to vote.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It produced Family and Medical Leave.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All passed.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All signed into law with not one single veto.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These accomplishments were all commitments I made when I sought this office.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And, in fairness, they all had to be passed by you in this Congress.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I am persuaded that the real credit belongs to the people who sent us here, who pay our salaries, who hold our feet to the fire.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But what we do here is really beginning to change lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let me just give you one example.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I will never forget what the Family and Medical Leave law meant to just one father I met early one Sunday morning in the White House.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It was unusual to see a family there touring early Sunday morning, but he had his wife and his three children there, one of them in a wheelchair.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Mr. President, let me tell you something.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My little girl here is desperately ill.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: She's probably not going to make it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But because of the Family Leave law, I was able to take time off to spend with her -- the most important time I ever spent in my life -- without losing my job and hurting the rest of my family.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It means more to me than I will ever be able to say.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Don't you people up here ever think what you do doesn't make a difference.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It does.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Though we are making a difference, our work has just begun.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Many Americans still haven't felt the impact of what we've done.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The recovery still hasn't touched every community or created enough jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Incomes are still stagnant.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There's still too much violence and not enough hope in too many places.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Abroad, the young democracies we are strongly supporting still face very difficult times and look to us for leadership.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And so tonight, let us resolve to continue the journey of renewal.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To create more and better jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To guarantee health security for all.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To reward work over welfare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To promote democracy abroad.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to begin to reclaim our streets from violent crime and drugs and gangs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To renew our own American community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year we began to put our house in order by tackling the budget deficit that was driving us toward bankruptcy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We cut $255 billion in spending, including entitlements, and over 340 separate budget items.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We froze domestic spending and used honest budget numbers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Led by the Vice President, we launched a campaign to reinvent government.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We cut staff, cut perks, even trimmed the fleet of federal limousines.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: After years of leaders whose rhetoric attacked bureaucracy but whose actions expanded it, we will actually reduce it by 252,000 people over the next five years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: By the time we have finished, the federal bureaucracy will be at its lowest point in 30 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because the deficit was so large and because they benefitted from tax cuts in the 1980s, we did ask the wealthiest Americans to pay more to reduce the deficit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So on April 15th, the American people will discover the truth about what we did last year on taxes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Only the top 1 -- yes, listen -- the top 1.2 percent of Americans, as I said all along, will pay higher income tax rates.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let me repeat -- Only the wealthiest 1.2 percent of Americans will face higher income tax rates and no one else will.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And that is the truth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Of course, there were, as there always are in politics, naysayers who said this plan wouldn't work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But they were wrong.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When I became President the experts predicted that next year's deficit would be $300 billion.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But because we acted, those same people now say the deficit is going to be under $180 billion -- 40 percent lower then was previously predicted.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our economic program has helped to produce the lowest core inflation rate and the lowest interest rates in 20 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And because those interest rates are down, business investment and equipment is growing at seven times the rate of the previous four years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Auto sales are way up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Home sales are at a record high.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Millions of Americans have refinanced their homes, and our economy has produced 1.6 million private sector jobs in 1993 -- more than were created in the previous four years combined.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The people who supported this economic plan should be proud of its early results, proud.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But everyone in this chamber should know and acknowledge that there is more to do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Next month I will send you one of the toughest budgets ever presented to Congress.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It will cut spending in more than 300 programs, eliminate 100 domestic programs, and reform the ways in which governments buy goods and services.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year we must again make the hard choices to live within the hard spending ceilings we have set.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have proved we can bring the deficit down without choking off recovery, without punishing seniors of the middle class, and without putting our national security at risk.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If you will stick with this plan, we will post three consecutive years of declining deficits for the first time since Harry Truman lived in the White House.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And once again, the buck stops here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our economic plan also bolsters our strength and our credibility around the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Once we reduce the deficit and put the steel back into our competitive edge, the world echoed with the sound of falling trade barriers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In one year, with NAFTA, with GATT, with our efforts in Asia and the National Export Strategy, we did more to open world markets to American products than at any time in the last two generations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That means more jobs and rising living standards for the American people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Low deficits.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Low inflation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Low interest rates.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Low trade barriers and high investments.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These are the building blocks of our recovery.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But if we want to take full advantage of the opportunities before us in the global economy, you all know we must do more.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As we reduce defense spending, I ask Congress to invest more in the technologies of tomorrow.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Defense conversion will keep us strong militarily and create jobs for our people here at home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As we protect our environment, we must invest in the environmental technologies of the future which will create jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year we will fight for a revitalized Clean Water Act and a Safe Drinking Water Act and a reformed Superfund program.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And the Vice President is right -- we must also work with the private sector to connect every classroom, every clinic, every library, every hospital in America into a national information super highway by the year 2000.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Think of it -- instant access to information will increase productivity, will help to educate our children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It will provide better medical care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It will create jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I call on the Congress to pass legislation to establish that information super highway this year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As we expand opportunity and create jobs, no one can be left out.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must continue to enforce fair lending and fair housing and all civil rights laws, because America will never be complete in its renewal until everyone shares in its bounty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we all know, too, we can do all these things -- put our economic house in order, expand world trade, target the jobs of the future, guarantee equal opportunity -- but if we're honest, we'll all admit that this strategy still cannot work unless we also give our people the education, training and skills they need to seize the opportunities of tomorrow.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must set tough, world-class academic and occupational standards for all our children and give our teachers and students the tools they need to meet them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our Goals 2000 proposal will empower individual school districts to experiment with ideas like chartering their schools to be run by private corporations, or having more public school choice -- to do whatever they wish to do as long as we measure every school by one high standard: Are our children learning what they need to know to compete and win in the global economy?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Goals 2000 links world-class standards to grass-roots reforms.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I hope Congress will pass it without delay.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our School to Work Initiative will for the first time link school to the world of work, providing at least one year of pprenticeship beyond high school.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: After all, most of the people we're counting on to build our economic future won't graduate from college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's time to stop ignoring them and start empowering them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must literally transform our out-dated unemployment system into a new reemployment system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The old unemployment system just sort of kept you going while you waited for your old job to come back.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've got to have a new system to move people into new and better jobs because most of those old jobs just don't come back.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we know that the only way to have real job security in the future, to get a good job with a growing income, is to have real skills and the ability to learn new ones.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So we've got to streamline today's patchwork of training programs and make them a source of new skills for our people who lose their jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Reemployment, not unemployment, must become the centerpiece of our economic renewal.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I urge you to pass it in this session of Congress.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And just as we must transform our unemployment system, so must we also revolutionize our welfare system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It doesn't work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It defies our values as a nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we value work, we can't justify a system that makes welfare more attractive than work if people are worried about losing their health care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we value responsibility, we can't ignore the $34 billion in child support absent parents ought to be paying to millions of parents who are taking care of their children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we value strong families, we can't perpetuate a system that actually penalizes those who stay together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Can you believe that a child who has a child gets more money from the government for leaving home than for staying home with a parent or a grandparent?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's not just bad policy, it's wrong.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we ought to change it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I worked on this problem for years before I became President, with other governors and with members of Congress of both parties and with the previous administration of another party.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I worked on it with people who were on welfare -- lots of them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I want to say something to everybody here who cares about this issue.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The people who most want to change this system are the people who are dependent on it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They want to get off welfare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They want to go back to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They want to do right by their kids.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I once had a hearing when I was a governor and I brought in people on welfare from all over America who had found their way to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The woman from my state who testified was asked this question: What's the best thing about being off welfare and in a job?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These people want a better system and we ought to give it to them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year we began this.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We gave the states more power to innovate because we know that a lot of great ideas come from outside Washington, and many states are already using it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Then this Congress took a dramatic step.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Instead of taxing people with modest incomes into poverty, we helped them to work their way out of poverty by dramatically increasing the earned income tax credit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It will lift 15 million working families out of poverty, rewarding work over welfare, making it possible for people to be successful workers and successful parents.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now that's real welfare reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But there is more to be done.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This spring I will send you a comprehensive welfare reform bill that builds on the Family Support Act of 1988 and restores the basic values of responsibility.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We'll say to teenagers, if you have a child out of wedlock, we will no longer give you a check to set up a separate household.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We want families to stay together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Say to absent parents who aren't paying their child support, if you're not providing for your children, we'll garnish your wages, suspend your license, track you across state lines, and if necessary, make some of you work off what you owe.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: People who bring children into this world cannot and must not walk away from them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But to all those who depend on welfare, we should offer ultimately a simple compact.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We'll provide the support, the job training, the child care you need for up to two years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But after that, anyone who can work must -- in the private sector, wherever possible.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In community services, if necessary.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's the only way we'll ever make welfare what it ought to be -- a second chance, not a way of life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know it will be difficult to tackle welfare reform in 1994 at the same time we tackle health care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But let me point out, I think it is inevitable and imperative.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It is estimated that one million people are on welfare today because it's the only way they can get health care coverage for their children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Those who choose to leave welfare for jobs without health benefits -- and many entry jobs don't have health benefits -- find themselves in the incredible position of paying taxes that help to pay for health care coverage for those who made the other choice to stay on welfare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: No wonder people leave work and go back to welfare to get health care coverage.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have got to solve the health care problem to have real welfare reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So this year, we will make history by reforming the health care system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I would say to you, all of you, my fellow public servants, this is another issue where the people are way ahead of the politicians.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That may not be popular with either party, but it happens to be the truth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, the First Lady has received now almost a million letters from people all across America and from all walks of life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'd like to share just one of them with you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Richard Anderson of Reno, Nevada, lost his job and, with it, his health insurance.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Two weeks later, his wife, Judy, suffered a cerebral aneurysm.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He rushed her to the hospital, where she stayed in intensive care for 21 days.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The Andersons' bills were over $120,000.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Although Judy recovered and Richard went back to work, at $8 an hour, the bills were too much for them and they were literally forced into bankruptcy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It was to help the Richard and Judy Andersons of America that the First Lady and so many others have worked so hard and so long on this health care reform issue.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We owe them our thanks and our action.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know there are people here who say there's no health care crisis.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tell it to Richard and Judy Anderson.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tell it to the 58 million Americans who have no coverage at all for some time each year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tell it to the 81 million Americans with those preexisting conditions -- those folks are paying more or they can't get insurance at all, or they can't ever change their jobs because they or someone in their family has one of those preexisting conditions.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tell it to the small businesses burdened by the skyrocketing cost of insurance.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Most small businesses cover their employees, and they pay on average 35 percent more in premiums than big businesses or government.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Or tell it to the 76 percent of insured Americans, three out of four whose policies have lifetime limits.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And that means they can find themselves without any coverage at all just when they need it the most.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So if any of you believe there's no crisis, you tell it to those people -- because I can't.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There are some people who literally do not understand the impact of this problem on people's lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And all you have to do is go out and listen to them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Just go talk to them anywhere in any congressional district in this country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They're Republicans and Democrats and independents -- it doesn't have a lick to do with party.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They think we don't get it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And it's time we show them that we do get it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: From the day we began, our health care initiative has been designed to strengthen what is good about our health care system: the world's best health care professionals, cutting edge research and wonderful research institutions, Medicare for older Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: None of this -- none of it should be put at risk.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we're paying more and more money for less and less care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every year fewer and fewer Americans even get to choose their doctors.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every year doctors and nurses spend more time on paperwork and less time with patients because of the absolute bureaucratic nightmare the present system has become.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This system is riddled with inefficiency, with abuse, with fraud, and everybody knows it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In today's health care system, insurance companies call the shots.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They pick whom they cover and how they cover them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They can cut off your benefits when you need your coverage the most.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They are in charge.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: What does it mean?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It means every night millions of well-insured Americans go to bed just an illness, an accident or a pink slip away from having no coverage or financial ruin.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It means every morning millions of Americans go to work without any health insurance at all -- something the workers in no other advanced country in the world do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It means that every year, more and more hard-working people are told to pick a new doctor because their boss has had to pick a new plan.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And countless others turn down better jobs because they know if they take the better job, they will lose their health insurance.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we just let the health care system continue to drift, our country will have people with less care, fewer choices and higher bills.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, our approach protects the quality of care and people's choices.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It builds on what works today in the private sector -- to expand employer-based coverage, to guarantee private insurance for every American.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I might say, employer-based private insurance for every American was proposed 20 years ago by President Richard Nixon to the United States Congress.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It was a good idea then, and it's a better idea today.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Why do we want guaranteed private insurance?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because right now nine out of 10 people who have insurance get it through their employers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And that should continue.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And if your employer is providing good benefits at reasonable prices, that should continue, too.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That ought to make the Congress and the President feel better.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our goal is health insurance everybody can depend on --comprehensive benefits that cover preventive care and prescription drugs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Health premiums that don't just explode when yo get sick or you get older.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The power no matter how small your business is to choose dependable insurance at the same competitive rates governments and big business get today.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: One simple form for people who are sick.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And, most of all, the freedom to choose a plan and the right to choose your own doctor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our approach protects older Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every plan before the Congress proposes to slow the growth of Medicare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The difference is this: We believe those savings should be used to improve health care for senior citizens.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Medicare must be protected, and it should cover prescription drugs, and we should take the first steps in covering long-term care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To those who would cut Medicare without protecting seniors, I say the solution to today's squeeze on middle-class working people's health care is not to put the squeeze on middle-class retired people's health care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can do better than that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When it's all said and done, it's pretty simple to me.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Insurance ought to mean what it used to mean -- you pay a fair price for

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: security, and when you get sick, health care's always there, no matter what.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Along with the guarantee of health security, we all have to admit, too, there must be more responsibility on the part of all of us in how we use this system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: People have to take their kids to get immunized.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should all take advantage of preventive care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must all work together to stop the violence that explodes our emergency rooms.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have to practice better health habits, and we can't abuse the system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And those who don't have insurance under our approach will get coverage, but they'll have to pay something for it, too.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The minority of businesses that provide no insurance at all, and in so doing, shift the cost of the care of their employees to others, should contribute something.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: People who smoke should pay more for a pack of cigarettes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Everybody can contribute something if we want to solve the health care crisis.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There can't be any more something for nothing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It will not be easy but it can be done.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, in the coming months I hope very much to work both Democrats and Republicans to reform a health care system by using the market to bring down costs and to achieve lasting health security.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But if you look at history we see that for 60 years this country has tried to reform health care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: President Roosevelt tried.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: President Truman tried.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: President Nixon tried.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: President Carter tried.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every time the special interests were powerful enough to defeat them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But not this time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know that facing up to these interests will require courage.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It will raise critical questions about the way we finance our campaigns and how lobbyists yield their influence.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The work of change, frankly, will never get any easier until we limit the influence of well-financed interest who profit from this current system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I also must now to call on you to finish the job both Houses began last year by passing tough and meaningful campaign finance reform and lobby reform legislation this year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, my fellow Americans, this is really a test for all of us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The Amerian people provide those of us in government service with terrific health care benefits at reasonable costs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have health care that's always there.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think we need to give every hard-working, tax-paying American the same health care security they have already given to us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to make this very clear.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I am open, as I have said repeatedly, to the best ideas of concerned members of both parties.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have no special brief for any specific approach, even in our own bill, except this: If you send me legislation that does not guarantee every American private health insurance that can never be taken away, you will force me to take this pen, veto the legislation, and we'll come right back here and start all over again.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I don't think that's going to happen.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think we're ready to act now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I believe that you're ready to act now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And if you're ready to guarantee every American the same health care that you have, health care that can never be taken away, now -- not next year or the year after -- now is the time to stand with the people who sent us here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As we take these steps together to renew our strength at home, we cannot turn away from our obligation to renew our leadership abroad.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is a promising moment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because of the agreements we have reached this year, last year, Russia's strategic nuclear missiles soon will no longer be pointed at the United States, nor will we point ours at them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Instead of building weapons in space, Russian scientists will help us to build the international space station.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Of course, there are still dangers in the world --rampant arms proliferation, bitter regional conflicts, ethnic and nationalist tensions in many new democracies, severe environmental degradation the world over, and fanatics who seek to cripple the world's cities with terror.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As the world's greatest power, we must, therefore, maintain our defenses and our responsibilities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, we secured indictments against terrorists and sanctions against those who harbor them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We worked to promote environmentally sustainable economic growth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We achieved agreements with Ukraine, with Belarus, with Kazahkstan to eliminate completely their nuclear arsenal.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are working to achieve a Korean Peninsula free of nuclear weapons.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will seek early ratification of a treaty to ban chemical weapons worldwide.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And earlier today, we joined with over 30 nations to begin negotiations on a comprehensive ban to stop all nuclear testing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But nothing, nothing is more important to our security than our nation's armed forces.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We honor their contributions, including those who are carrying out the longest humanitarian air lift in history in Bosnia.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Those who will complete their mission in Somalia this year and their brave comrades who gave their lives there.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our forces are the finest military our nation has ever had.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I have pledged that as long as I am President, they will remain the best equipped, the best trained and the best prepared fighting force on the face of the Earth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year I proposed a defense plan that maintains our post-Cold War security at a lower cost.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year many people urged me to cut our defense spending further to pay for other government programs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I said, no.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The budget I send to Congress draws the line against further defense cuts.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It protects the readiness and quality of our forces.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Ultimately, the best strategy is to do that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must not cut defense further.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope the Congress without regard to party will support that position.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Ultimately, the best strategy to ensure our security and to build a durable peace is to support the advance of democracy elsewhere.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Democracies don't attack each other, they make better trading partners and partners in diplomacy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is why we have supported, you and I, the democratic reformers in Russia and in the other states of the former Soviet bloc.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I applaud the bipartisan support this Congress provided last year for our initiatives to help Russia, Ukraine, and the other states through their epic transformations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our support of reform must combine patience for the enormity of the task and vigilance for our fundamental interest and values.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will continue to urge Russia and the other states to press ahead with economic reforms.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we will seek to cooperate with Russia to solve regional problems, while insisting that if Russian troops operate in neighboring states, they do so only when those states agree to their presence and in strict accord with international standards.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we must also remember as these nations chart their own futures -- and they must chart their own futures -- how much more secure and more prosperous our own people will be if democratic and market reform succeed all across the former communist bloc.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our policy has been to support that move and that has been the policy of the Congress.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should continue it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is why I went to Europe earlier this month -- to work with our Europeans partners, to help to integrate all the former communist countries into a Europe that has a possibility of becoming unified for the first time in its entire history -- its entire history -- based on the simple commitments of all nations in Europe to democracy, to free markets and to respect for existing borders.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With our allies we have created a Partnership For Peace that invites states from the former Soviet bloc and other non-NATO members to work with NATO in military cooperation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When I met with Central Europe's leaders including Lech Walesa and Vaclav Havel, men who put their lives on the line for freedom, I told them that the security of their region is important to our country's security.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year we must also do more to support democratic renewal and human rights and sustainable development all around the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will ask Congress to ratify the new GATT accord.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will continue standing by South Africa as it works its way through its bold and hopeful and difficult transition to democracy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will convene a summit of the Western Hemisphere's leaders from Canada to the tip of South America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we will continue to press for the restoration of true democracy in Haiti.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And as we build a more constructive relationship with China, we must continue to insist on clear signs of improvement in that nation's human right record.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will also work for new progress toward the Middle East peace.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year the world watched Yitzhak Rabin and Yassir Arafat at the White House when they had their historic handshake of reconciliation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But there is a long, hard road ahead.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And on that road I am determined that I and our administration will do all we can to achieve a comprehensive and lasting peace for all the peoples of the region.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, there are some in our country who argue that with the Cold War, America should turn its back on the rest of the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Many around the world were afraid we would do just that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I took this office on a pledge that had no partisan tinge to keep our nation secure by remaining engaged in the rest of the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And this year, because of our work together -- enacting NAFTA, keeping our military strong and prepared, supporting democracy abroad -- we have reaffirmed America's leadership, America's engagement.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And as a result, the American people are more secure than they were before.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But while Americans are more secure from threats abroad, I think we all know that in many ways we are less secure from threats here at home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every day the national peace is shattered by crime.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In Petaluma, California, an innocent slumber party gives way to agonizing tragedy for the family of Polly Klaas.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: An ordinary train ride on Long Island ends in a hail of 9-millimeter rounds.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A tourist in Florida is nearly burned alive by bigots simply because he is black.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Right here in our Nation's Capital, a brave young man named Jason White, a policeman, the son and grandson of policemen, is ruthlessly gunned down.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Violent crime and the fear it provokes are crippling our society, limiting personal freedom and fraying the ties that bind us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The crime bill before Congress gives you a chance to do something about it -- a chance to be tough and smart.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: What does that mean?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let me begin by saying, I care a lot about this issue.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Many years ago, when I started out in public life, I was the attorney general of my state.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I served as a governor for a dozen years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know what it's like to sign laws increasing penalties, to build more prison cells, to carry out the death penalty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I understand this issue.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And it is not a simple thing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: First, we must recognize that most violent crimes are committed by a small percentage of criminals who too often break the laws even when they are on parole.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now those who commit crimes should be punished.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And those who commit repeated, violent crimes should be told, when you commit a third violent crime, you will be put away, and put away for good.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Three strikes, and you are out.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Second, we must take serious steps to reduce violence and prevent crime, beginning with more police officers and more community policing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We know right now that police who work the streets, know the folks, have the respect of the neighborhood kids, focus on high crime areas -- we know that they are more likely to prevent crime as well as catch criminals.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Look at the experience of Houston, where the crime rate dropped 17 percent in one year when that approach was taken.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Here tonight is one of those community policeman -- a brave, young detective, Kevin Jett, whose beat is eight square blocks in one of the toughest neighborhoods in New York.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every day he restores some sanity and safety and a sense of values and connections to the people whose lives he protects.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'd like to ask him to stand up and be recognized tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you, sir.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You will be given a chance to give the children of this country, the law-abiding working people of this country -- and don't forget, in the toughest neighborhoods in this country, in the highest crime neighborhoods in this country, the vast majority of people get up every day and obey the law, pay their taxes, do their best to raise their kids.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They deserve people like Kevin Jett.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And you're going to be given a chance to give the American people another 100,000 of them well trained.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I urge you to do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You have before you crime legislation which also establishes a police corps to encourage young people to get an education and pay it off by serving as police officers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Which encourages retiring military personnel to move into police forces, an inordinate resource for our country -- one which has a safe schools provision which will give our young people the chance to walk to school in safety and to be in school in safety instead of dodging bullets.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These are important things.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The third thing we have to do is to build on the Brady Bill -- the Brady Law.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To take further steps to keep guns out of the hands of criminals.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to say something about this issue.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Hunters must always be free to hunt.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Law-abiding adults should always be free to own guns to protect their homes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I respect that part of our culture, I grew up in it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I want to ask the sportsmen and others who lawfully own guns to join us in this campaign to reduce gun violence.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I say to you, I know you didn't create this problem, but we need your help to solve it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There is no sporting purpose on Earth that should stop the United States Congress from banishing assault weapons that out-gun police and cut down children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Fourth, we must remember that drugs are a factor in an enormous percentage of crimes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Recent studies indicate, sadly, that drug use is on the rise again among our young people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The crime bill contains -- all the crime bills contain -- more money for drug treatment for criminal addicts, and boot camps for youthful offenders that include incentives to get off drugs and to stay off drugs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our administration's budget with all its cuts can paint a large increase in funding for drug treatment and drug education.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You must pass them both.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need them desperately.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, the problem of violence is an American problem.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It has no partisan or philosophical element.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Therefore, I urge you to find ways as quickly as possible to set aside partisan differences and pass a strong, smart, tough crime bill.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But further, I urge you to consider this: As you demand tougher penalties for those who choose violence, let us also remember how we came to this sad point.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In our toughest neighborhoods, on our meanest streets, in our poorest rural areas, we have seen a stunning and simultaneous breakdown of community, family and work -- the heart and soul of civilized society.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This has created a vast vacuum which has been filled by violence and drugs and gangs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I ask you to remember that even as we say no to crime, we must give people -- especially our young people -- something to say yes to.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Many of our initiatives -- from job training to welfare reform to health care to national service -- will help to rebuild distressed

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: communities, to strengthen families, to provide work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But more needs to be done.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's what our community empowerment agenda is all about -- challenging businesses to provide more investment through empowerment zones.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Ensuring banks will make loans in the same communities their deposits come from.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Passing legislation to unleash the power of capital through community development banks to create jobs -- opportunity and hope where they're needed most.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think you know that to really solve this problem, we'll all have to put our heads together, leave our ideological armor aside and find some new ideas to do even more.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And let's be honest.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
