text: We all know something else too: Our problems go way beyond the reach of government.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They're rooted in the lose of values, in the disappearance of work and the breakdown of our families and our communities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, we can cut the deficit, create jobs, promote democracy around the world, pass welfare reform and health care, pass the toughest crime bill in history, but still leave too many of our people behind.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The American people have got to want to change from within if we're going to bring back work and family and community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We cannot renew our country when within a decade more than half of the children will be born into families where there has been no marriage.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We cannot renew this country when 13-year-old boys get semi-automatic weapons to shoot 9-year-olds for kicks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can't renew our country when children are having children and the fathers walk away as if the kids don't amount to anything.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can't renew the country when our businesses eagerly look for new investments and new customers abroad, but ignore those people right here at home who would give anything to have their jobs and would gladly buy their products if they had the money to do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can't renew our country unless more of us -- I mean all of us -- are willing to join the churches and the other good citizens -- people like of the black ministers I've worked with over the years, or the priests and the nuns I met at Our Lady of Help in East Los Angeles, or my good friend, Tony Campollo in Philadelphia -- unless we're willing to work with people like that, people who are saving kids, adopting schools, making streets safer -- all of us can do that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can't renew our country until we realize that governments don't raise children, parents do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Parents who know their children's teachers and turn off the television and help with the homework and teach their kids right from wrong -- those kinds of parents can make all the difference.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know, I had one.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'm telling you, we have got to stop pointing our fingers at these kids who have no future, and reach our hands out to them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our country needs it, we need it, and they deserve it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I say to you tonight, let's give our children a future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us take away their guns and give them books.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us overcome their despair and replace it with hope.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us, by our example, teach them to obey the law, respect our neighbors, and cherish our values.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us weave these sturdy threads into a new American community that can once more stand strong against the forces of despair and evil because everybody has a chance to walk into a better tomorrow.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Oh, there will be naysayers who fear that we won't be equal to the challenges of this time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But they misread our history, our heritage.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Even today's headlines -- all those things tell us we can and we will overcome any challenge.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When the earth shook and fires raged in California, when I saw the Mississippi deluge the farmlands of the Midwest in a 500-year flood, when the century's bitterest cold swept from North Dakota to Newport News, it seemed as though the world itself was coming apart at the seams.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But the American people -- they just came together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They rose to the occasion, neighbor helping neighbor, strangers risking life and limb to save total strangers -- showing the better angels of our nature.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us not reserve the better angels only for natural disasters, leaving our deepest and most profound problems to petty political fighting.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us instead be true to our spirit -- facing facts, coming together, bringing hope and moving forward.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, my fellow Americans, we are summoned to answer a question as old as the republic itself: What is the state of our union? It is growing stronger, but it must be stronger still.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With your help, and God's help, it will be.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you and God bless America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Mr. President, Mr. Speaker, members of the 104th Congress, my fellow Americans: Again we are here in the sanctuary of democracy, and once again, our democracy has spoken.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So let me begin by congratulating all of you here in the 104th Congress, and congratulating you, Mr. Speaker.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we agree on nothing else tonight, we must agree that the American people certainly voted for change in 1992 and in 1994.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And as I look out at you, I know how some of you must have felt in 1992.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: 'WE HEARD AMERICA SHOUTING': I must say that in both years we didn't hear America singing, we heard America shouting.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And now all of us, Republicans and Democrats alike, must say: We hear you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will work together to earn the jobs you have given us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For we are the keepers of the sacred trust, and we must be faithful to it in this new and very demanding era.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It has fallen to every generation since then to preserve that idea -- the American idea -- and to deepen and expand its meaning to new and different times: To Lincoln and his Congress, to preserve the Union and to end slavery.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To Theodore Roosevelt and Woodrow Wilson, to restrain the abuses and excesses of the Industrial Revolution, and to assert our leadership in the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To Franklin Roosevelt, to fight the failure and pain of the Great Depression, and to win our country's great struggle against fascism.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to all our presidents since, to fight the Cold War.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Especially, I recall two who struggled to fight that Cold War in partnership with congresses where the majority was of a different party.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To Harry Truman, who summoned us to unparalleled prosperity at home, and who built the architecture of the Cold War.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to Ronald Reagan, whom we wish well tonight, and who exhorted us to carry on until the twilight struggle against communism was won.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In another time of change and challenge, I had the honor to be the first president to be elected in the post-Cold War era, an era marked by the global economy, the information revolution, unparalleled change and opportunity and insecurity for the American people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I came to this hallowed chamber two years ago on a mission -- to restore the American Dream for all our people and to make sure that we move into the 21st century still the strongest force for freedom and democracy in the entire world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I was determined then to tackle the tough problems too long ignored.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In this effort I am frank to say that I have made my mistakes, and I have learned again the importance of humility in all human endeavor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I am also proud to say tonight that our country is stronger than it was two years ago.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Record numbers -- record numbers of Americans are succeeding in the new global economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are at peace and we are a force for peace and freedom throughout the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have almost six million new jobs since I became president, and we have the lowest combined rate of unemployment and inflation in 25 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our businesses are more productive and here we have worked to bring the deficit down, to expand trade, to put more police on our streets, to give our citizens more of the tools they need to get an education and to rebuild their own communities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But the rising tide is not lifting all boats.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: While our nation is enjoying peace and prosperity, too many of our people are still working harder and harder, for less and less.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: While our businesses are restructuring and growing more productive and competitive, too many of our people still can't be sure of having a job next year or even next month.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And far more than our material riches are threatened.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Things far more precious too us -- ourchildren, our families, our values.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our civil life is suffering in America today.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Citizens are working together less and shouting at each other more.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The common bonds of community which have been the great strength of our country from its very beginning are badly frayed.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: What are we to do about it?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And from that simple proposition, he shaped the New Deal, which helped to restore our nation to prosperity and define the relationship between our people and their government for half a century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That approach worked in its time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we today, we face a very different time and very different conditions.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are moving from an Industrial Age built on gears and sweat to an Information Age demanding skills and learning and flexibility.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our government, once a champion of national purpose, is now seen by many as simply a captive of narrow interests, putting more burdens on our citizens rather than equipping them to get ahead.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The values that used to hold us all together seem to be coming apart.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So tonight, we must forge a new social compact to meet the challenges of this time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As we enter a new era, we need a new set of understandings, not just with government, but even more important, with one another as Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: FORGING THE 'NEW COVENANT': That's what I want to talk with you about tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I call it the New Covenant.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But it's grounded in a very, very old idea -- that all Americans have not just a right, but a solid responsibility to rise as far as their God-given talents and determination can take them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to give something back to their communities and their country in return.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Opportunity and responsibility: They go hand in hand.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can't have one without the other.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And our national community can't hold together without both.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our New Covenant is a new set of understandings for how we can equip our people to meet the challenges of a new economy, how we can change the way our government works to fit a different time, and, above all, how we can repair the damaged bonds in our society and come together behind our common purpose.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must have dramatic change in our economy, our government and ourselves.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, without regard to party, let us rise to the occasion.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us put aside partisanship and pettiness and pride.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As we embark on this new course, let us put our country first, remembering that regardless of party label, we are all Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And let the final test of everything we do be a simple one: Is it good for the American people?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let me begin by saying that we cannot ask Americans to be better citizens if we are not better servants.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You made a good start by passing that law which applies to Congress all the laws you put on the private sector, and I was proud to sign it yesterday.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we have a lot more to do before people really trust the way things work around here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Three times as many lobbyists are in the streets and corridors of Washington as were here 20 years ago.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The American people look at their capital and they see a city where the well-connected and the well-protected can work the system, but the interests of ordinary citizens are often left out.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As the new Congress opened its doors, lobbyists were still doing business as usual -- the gifts, the trips, all the things that people are concerned about haven't stopped.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Twice this month you missed opportunities to stop these practices.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know there were other considerations in those votes, but I want to use something that I've heard my Republican friends say from time to time -- there doesn't have to be a law for everything.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So tonight, I ask you to just stop taking the lobbyists' perks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Just stop.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We don't have to wait for legislation to pass to send a strong signal to the American people that things are really changing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I also hope you will send me the strongest possible lobby reform bill, and I'll sign that, too.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should require lobbyists to tell the people for whom they work what they're spending, what they want.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should also curb the role of big money in elections by capping the cost of campaigns and limiting the influence of PACs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And as I have said for three years, we should work to open the airwaves so that they can be an instrument of democracy, not a weapon of destruction by giving free TV time to candidates for public office.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When the last Congress killed political reform last year, it was reported in the press that the lobbyists actually stood in the halls of this sacred building and cheered.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, let's give the folks at home something to cheer about.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: More important, I think we all agree that we have to change the way the government works.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's make it smaller, less costly and smaller -- leaner, not meaner.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I just told the Speaker the equal time doctrine is alive and well.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The New Covenant approach to governing is as different from the old bureaucratic way as the computer is from the manual typewriter.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The old way of governing around here protected organized interests.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should look out for the interests of ordinary people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The old way divided us by interest, constituency or class.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The New Covenant way should unite us behind a common vision of what's best for our country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The old way dispensed services through large, top-down, inflexible bureaucracies.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The New Covenant way should shift these resources and decision-making from bureaucrats to citizens, injecting choice and competition and individual responsibility into national policy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The old way of governing around here actually seemed to reward failure.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The New Covenant way should have built-in incentives to reward success.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The old way was centralized here in Washington.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The New Covenant way must take hold in the communities all across America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we should help them to do that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our job here is to expand opportunity, not bureaucracy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To empower people to make the most of their own lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to enhance our security here at home and abroad.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must not ask government to do what we should do for ourselves.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should rely on government as a partner to help us to do more for ourselves and for each other.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: BEYOND YESTERDAY'S GOVERNMENT:  I hope very much that as we debate these specific and exciting matters, we can go beyond the sterile discussion between the illusion that there is somehow a program for every problem on the one hand, and the other illusion that the government is a source of every problem we have.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our job is to get rid of yesterday's government so that our own people can meet today's and tomorrow's needs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we ought to do it together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, for years before I became president, I heard others say they would cut government and how bad it was.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But not much happened.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We actually did it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We cut over a quarter of a trillion dollars in spending, more than 300 domestic programs, more than 100,000 positions from the federal bureaucracy in the last two years alone.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Based on decisions already made, we will have cut a total of more than a quarter of a million positions from the federal government, making it the smallest it has been since John Kennedy was president, by the time I come here again next year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Under the leadership of Vice President Gore, our initiatives have already saved taxpayers $63 billion.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The age of the $500 hammer and the ashtray you can break on David Letterman is gone.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Deadwood programs, like mohair subsidies, are gone.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've streamlined the Agriculture Department by reducing it by more than 1,200 offices.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've slashed the small business loan form from an inch thick to a single page.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've thrown away the government's 10,000-page personnel manual.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And the government is working better in important ways: FEMA, the Federal Emergency Management Agency, has gone from being a disaster to helping people in disasters.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You can ask the farmers in the Middle West who fought the flood there or the people in California who have dealt with floods and earthquakes and fires, and they'll tell you that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Government workers, working hand in hand with private business, rebuilt Southern California's fractured freeways in record time and under budget.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And because the federal government moved fast, all but one of the 5,600 schools damaged in the earthquake are back in business.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, there are a lot of other things that I could talk about.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to just mention one because it will be discussed here in the next few weeks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: University administrators all over the country have told me that they are saving weeks and weeks of bureaucratic time now because of our direct college loan program, which makes college loans cheaper and more affordable, with better repayment terms for students, costs the government less, and cuts out paperwork and bureaucracy for the government and for the universities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We shouldn't cap that program.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should give every college in America the opportunity to be a part of it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: MORE REINVENTING AHEAD: Previous government programs gather dust.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The reinventing government report is getting results.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we're not through.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There's going to be a second round of reinventing government.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We propose to cut $130 billion in spending by shrinking departments, extending our freeze on domestic spending, cutting 60public housing programs down to three, getting rid of over 100 programs we do not need, like the Interstate Commerce Commission and the Helium Reserve Program.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we're working on getting rid of unnecessary regulations and making them more sensible.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The programs and regulations that have outlived their usefulness should go.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have to cut yesterday's government to help solve tomorrow's problems.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we need to get government closer to the people its meant to serve.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need to help move programs down to the point where states and communities and private citizens in the private sector can do a better job.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If they can do it, we ought to let them do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should get out of the way and let them do what they can do better.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Taking power away from federal bureaucracies and giving it back to communities and individuals is something everyone should be able to be for.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's time for Congress to stop passing on to the state the cost of decisions we make here in Washington.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know there are still serious differences over the details of the unfunded mandates legislation, but I want to work with you to make sure we pass a reasonable bill which will protect the national interests and give justified relief where we need to give it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For years, Congress concealed in the budget scores of pet spending projects.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year was no different.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There was a $1 million to study stress in plants, and $12 million for a tick removal program that didn't work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's hard to remove ticks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Those of us who have had them know.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But, I'll tell you something.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If you'll give me the line-item veto, I'll remove some of that nnecessary spending.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I think we should all remember, and almost all of us would agree, that government still has important responsibilities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our young people -- we should think of this when we cut -- our young people hold our future in their hands.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We still owe a debt to our veterans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And our senior citizens have made us what we are.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, my budget cuts a lot.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But it protects education, veterans, Social Security and Medicare -- and I hope you will do the same thing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You should, and I hope you will.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And when we give more flexibility to the states, let us remember that there are certain fundamental national needs that should be addressed in every state, north and south, east and west -- immunization against childhood disease -- school lunches in all our schools -- Head Start, medical care and nutrition for pregnant women and infants -- medical care and nutrition for pregnant women and infants.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All these things -- all these things are in the national interest.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I applaud your desire to get rid of costly and unnecessary regulations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But when we deregulate, let's remember what national action in the national interest has given us: safer foods for our families, safer toys for our children, safer nursing homes for our parents, safer cars and highways, and safer workplaces, clean air and cleaner water.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Do we need common sense and fairness in our regulations?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You bet we do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we can have common sense and still provide for safe drinking water.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can have fairness and still clean up toxic dumps, and we ought to do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Should we cut the deficit more?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Well, of course, we should.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Of course, we should.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we can bring it down in a way that still protects our economic recovery and does not unduly punish people who should not be punished, but instead should be helped.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: CUTTING THE BUDGET:  I know many of you in this chamber support the balanced budget amendment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I certainly want to balance the budget.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our administration has done more to bring the budget down and to save money than any in a very, very long time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If you believe passing this amendment is the right thing to do, then you have to be straight with the American people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They have a right to know what you're going to cut, what taxes you're going to raise, and how it's going to affect them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should be doing things in the open around here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For example, everybody ought to know if this proposal is going to endanger Social Security.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I would oppose that, and I think most Americans would.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Nothing is done more to undermine our sense of common responsibility than our failed welfare system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is one of the problems we have to face here in Washington in our New Covenant.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It rewards welfare over work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It undermines family values.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It lets millions of parents get away without paying their child support.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It keeps a minority, but a significant minority of the people on welfare trapped on it for a very long time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I've worked on this problem for a long time, nearly 15 years now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As a governor I had the honor of working with the Reagan administration to write the last welfare reform bill back in 1988.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the last two years we made a good start in continuing the work of welfare reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our administration gave two dozen states the right to slash through federal rules and regulations to reform their own welfare systems, and to try to promote work and responsibility over welfare and dependency.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year I introduced the most sweeping welfare reform plan ever presented by an administration.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have to make welfare what it was meant to be -- a second chance, not a way of life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have to help those on welfare move to work as quickly as possible, to provide child care and teach them skills if that's what they need for up to two years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And after that, there ought to be a simple hard rule: anyone who can work must go to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If a parent isn't paying child support, they should be forced to pay.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should suspend drivers' licenses, track the across state lines, make them work off what they owe.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is what we should do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Governments do not raise children, people do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And the parents must take responsibility for the children they bring into this world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to work with you, with all of you, to pass welfare reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But our goal must be to liberate people and lift them up, from dependence to independence, from welfare to work, from mere childbearing to responsible parenting.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our goal should not be to punish them because they happen to be poor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should -- we should require work and mutual responsibility.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we shouldn't cut people off just because they're poor, they're young, or even because they're unmarried.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should promote responsibility by requiring young mothers to live at home with their parents or in other supervised settings, by requiring them to finish school.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we shouldn't put them and their children out on the street.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I know all the arguments, pro and con, and I have read and thought about this for a long time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I still don't think we can in good conscious punish poor children for the mistakes of their parents.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, every single survey shows that all the American people care about this without regard to party or race or region.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So let this be the year we end welfare as we know it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But also let this be the year that we are all able to stop using this issue to divide America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: No one is more eager to end welfare -- I may be the only president who has actually had the opportunity to sit in a welfare office, who's actually spent hours and hours talking to people on welfare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I am telling you, people who are trapped on it know it doesn't work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They also want to get off.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So we can promote together education and work and good parenting.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have no problem with punishing bad behavior or the refusal to be a worker or a student, or a responsible parent.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I just don't want to punish poverty and past mistakes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All of us have made our mistakes, and none of us can change our yesterdays.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But every one of us can change our tomorrows.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And America's best example of that may be Lynn Woolsey, who worked her way off welfare to become a congresswoman from the state of California.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know the members of this Congress are concerned about crime, as are all the citizens of our country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I remind you that last year, we passed a very tough crime bill -- longer sentences, three strikes and you're out, almost 60 new capital punishment offenses, more prisons, more prevention, 100,000 more police.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we paid for it all by reducing the size of the federal bureaucracy and giving the money back to local communities to lower the crime rate.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There may be other things we can do to be tougher on crime, to be smarter with crime, to help to lower that rate first.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Well, if there are, let's talk about them and let's do them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But let's not go back on the things that we did last year that we know work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That we know work because the local law enforcement officers tell us that we did the right things, because local community leaders who have worked for years and years to lower the crime rate tell us that they work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's look at the experience of our cities and our rural areas where the crime rate has gone down and ask the people who did it how they did it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And if what we did last year supports the decline in the crime rate -- and I am convinced that it does -- let us not go back on it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's stick with it, implement it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've got four more hard years of work to do to do that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: THE BRADY BILL: I don't want to destroy the good atmosphere in the room or in the country tonight, but I have to mention one issue that divided this body greatly last year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The last Congress also passed the Brady Bill and, in the crime bill, the ban on 19 assault weapons.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I don't think it's a secret to anybody in this room that several members of the last Congress who voted for that aren't here tonight because they voted for it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I know, therefore, that some of you who are here because they voted for it are under enormous pressure to repeal it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I just have to tell you how I feel about it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The members of Congress who voted for that bill and I would never do anything to infringe on the right to keep and bear arms to hunt and to engage in other appropriate sporting activities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I've done it since I was a boy, and I'm going to keep right on doing it until I can't do it anymore.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But a lot of people laid down their seats in Congress so that police officers and kids wouldn't have to lay down their lives under a hail of assault weapon attack -- and I will not let that be repealed.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I will not let it be repealed.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'd like to talk about a couple of other issues we have to deal with.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want us to cut more spending, but I hope we won't cut government programs that help to prepare us for the new economy, promote responsibility and are organized from the grass roots up, not by federal bureaucracy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The very best example of this is the National Service Corps -- AmeriCorps.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It passed with strong bipartisan support.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And now there are 20,000 Americans, more than every served in one year in the Peace Corps, working all over this country, helping people person to person in local, grass-roots volunteer groups, solving problems and, in the process, earning some money for their education.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is citizenship at its best.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's good for the AmeriCorps members, but it's good for the rest of us, too.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's the essence of the New Covenant, and we shouldn't stop it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All Americans, not only in the states most heavily affected, but in every place in this country, are rightly disturbed by the large numbers of illegal aliens entering our country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The jobs they hold might otherwise be held by citizens or legal immigrants.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The public service they use impose burdens on our taxpayers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why our administration has moved aggressively to secure our borders more by hiring a record number of new border guards, by deporting twice as many criminal aliens as ever before, by cracking down on illegal hiring, by barring welfare benefits to illegal aliens.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the budget I will present to you we will try to do more to speed the deportation of illegal aliens who are arrested for crimes, to better identify illegal aliens in the workplace as recommended by the commission headed by former Congresswoman Barbara Jordan.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are a nation of immigrants.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we are also a nation of laws.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It is wrong and ultimately self-defeating for a nation of immigrants to permit the kind of abuse of our immigration laws we have seen in recent years, and we must do more to stop it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: EXPANDING THE MIDDLE CLASS: The most important job of our government in this new era is to empower the American people to succeed in the global economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America has always been a land of opportunity, a land where, if you work hard, you can get ahead.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've become a great middle class country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Middle class values sustain us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must expand that middle class, and shrink the underclass, even as we do everything we can to support the millions of Americans who are already successful in the new economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America is once again the world's strongest economic power, almost six million new jobs in the last two years, exports booming, inflation down, high-wage jobs are coming back.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A record number of American entrepreneurs are living the American Dream.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we want it to stay that way, those who work and lift our nation must have more of its benefits.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, too many of those people are being left out.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They're working harder for less.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They have less security, less income, less certainty that they can even afford a vacation, much less college for their kids or retirement for themselves.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We cannot let this continue.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we don't act, our economy will probably keep doing what it's been doing since about 1978, when the income growth began to go to those at the very top of our economic scale and the people in the vast middle got very little growth, and people who worked like crazy but were on the bottom then fell even further and further behind in the years afterward -- no matter how hard they worked.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've got to have a government that can be a real partner in making this new economy work for all of our people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A government that helps each and every one of us to get an education, and to have the opportunity to renew our skills.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why we worked so hard to increase educational opportunities in the last two years -- from Head Start to public schools, to apprenticeships for young people who don't go to college, to making college loans more available and more affordable.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's the first thing we have to do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've got to do something to empower people to improve their skills.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: LOWERING TAXES: The second thing we ought to do is to help people raise their incomes immediately by lowering their taxes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We took the first step in 1993 with a working family tax cut for 15 million families with incomes under $27,000.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A tax cut that this year will average about $1,000 a family.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we also gave tax reductions to most small and new businesses.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Before we could do more than that, we first had to bring down the deficit we inherited, and we had to get economic growth up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now we've done both.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And now we can cut taxes in a more comprehensive way.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But tax cuts should reinforce and promote our first obligation -- to empower our citizens through education and training to make the most of their own lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The spotlight should shine on those who make the right choices for themselves, their families and their communities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have proposed the Middle Class Bill of Rights, which should properly be called the Bill of Rights and Responsibilities because its provisions only benefit those who are working to educate and raise their children and to educate themselves.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It will, therefore, give needed tax relief and raise incomes in both the short run and the long run in a way that benefits all of us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There are four provisions.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: First, a tax deduction for all education and training after high school.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If you think about it, we permit businesses to deduct their investment, we permit individuals to deduct interest on their home mortgages, but today an education is even more important to the economic well-being of our whole country than even those things are.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should do everything we can to encourage it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I hope you will support it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Second, we ought to cut taxes, $500 for families with children under 13.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Third, we ought to foster more savings and personal responsibility by permitting people to establish an Individual Retirement Account and withdraw from it tax free for the cost of education, health care, first-time home-buying or the care of a parent.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And fourth, we should pass a G.I. Bill for America's workers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We propose to collapse nearly 70 federal programs and not give the money to the states, but give the money directly to the American people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Offer vouchers to them so that they, if they're laid off or if they're working for a very low wage, can get a voucher worth $2,600 a year for up to two years to go to their local community colleges or wherever else they want to get the skills they need to improve their lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's empower people in this way.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Move it from the government directly to the workers of America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, any one of us can call for a tax cut, but I won't accept one that explodes the deficit or puts our recovery at risk.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We ought to pay for our tax cuts fully and honestly.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Just two years ago, it was an open question whether we would find the strength to cut the deficit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thanks to the courage of the people who were here then, many of whom didn't return, we did cut the deficit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We began to do what others said would not be done.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We cut the deficit by over $600 billion, about $10,000 for every family in this country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's coming down three years in a row for the first time since Mr.Truman was president, and I don't think anybody in America wants us to let it explode again

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the budget I will send you, the Middle Class Bill of Rights is fully paid for by budget cuts in bureaucracy, cuts in programs, cuts in special interest subsidies.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And the spending cuts will more than double the tax cuts.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My budget pays for the Middle Class Bill of Rights without any cuts in Medicare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I will oppose any attempts to pay for tax cuts with Medicare cuts.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's not the right thing to do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know that a lot of you have your own ideas about tax relief, and some of them I find quite interesting.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I really want to work with all of you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My test for our proposals will be: Will it create jobs and raise incomes?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Will it strengthen our families and support our children?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Is it paid for?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Will it build the middle class and shrink the underclass?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If it does, I'll support it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But if it doesn't, I won't.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: RAISING THE MINIMUM WAGE:  The goal of building the middle class and shrinking the underclass is also why I believe that you should raise the minimum wage.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It rewards work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Two and a half million Americans -- 2.5 million Americans, often women with children, are working out there today for $4.25 an hour.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In terms of real buying power, by next year that minimum wage will be at a 40-year low.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's not my idea of how the new economy ought to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, I've studied the arguments and the evidence for and against a minimum wage increase.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I believe the weight of the evidence is that a modest increase does not cost jobs, and may even lure people back into the job market.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But the most important thing is, you can't make a living on $4.25 an hour.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Especially if you have children, even with the working families tax cut we passed last year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the past, the minimum wage has been a bipartisan issue, and I think it should be again.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I want to challenge you to have honest hearings on this.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To get together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To find a way to make the minimum wage a living wage.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Members of Congress have been here less than a month, but by the end of the week, 28 days into the new year, every member of Congress will have earned as much in congressional salary as a minimum wage worker makes all year long.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Everybody else here, including the President, has something else that too many Americans do without, and that's health care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, last year, we almost came to blows over health care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we didn't do anything.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And the cold, hard fact is that, since last year, since I was here, another 1.1 million Americans in working families have lost their health care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And the cold, hard fact is that many millions more, most of them farmers and small businesspeople and self-employed people, have seen their premiums skyrocket, their co-pays and deductibles go up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There's a whole bunch of people in this country that, in the statistics have health insurance, but really what they've got is a piece of paper that says they won't lose their home if they get sick.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: HEALTH SECURITY: Now, I still believe our country has got to move toward providing health security for every American family.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I know that last year, as the evidence indicates, we bit off more than we could chew.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I'm asking you that we work together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's do it step by step.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's do whatever we have to do to get something done.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's at least pass meaningful insurance reform so that no American risks losing coverage for facing skyrocketing prices.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That nobody loses their coverage because they face high prices or unavailable insurance, when they change jobs and lose a job, or a family member gets sick.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to work together with all of you who have an interest in this -- with the Democrats who worked on it last time, with the Republican leaders like Senator Dole who has a longtime commitment to health care reform and made some constructive proposals in this area last year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We ought to make sure that self-employed people in small businesses can buy insurance at more affordable rates through voluntary purchasing pools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We ought to help families provide long-term care for a sick parent or a disabled child.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can work to help workers who lose their jobs at least keep their health insurance coverage for a year while they look for work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we can find a way -- it may take some time, but we can find a way -- to make sure that our children have health care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, I think everybody in this room, without regard to party, can be proud of the fact that our country was rated as having the world's most productive economy for the first time in nearly a decade.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we can't be proud of the fact that we're the only wealthy country in the world that has a smaller percentage of the work force and their children with health insurance today than we did 10 years ago, the last time we were the most productive economy in the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So let's work together on this.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It is too important for politics as usual.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: SECURITY ABROAD:  Much of what the American people are thinking about tonight is what we've already talked about.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A lot of people think that the security concerns of America today are entirely internal to our borders.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They relate to the security of our jobs and our homes, and our incomes and our children, our streets, our health and protecting those borders.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now that the Cold War has passed, it's tempting to believe that all the security issues, with the possible exception of trade, reside here at home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But it's not so.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our security still depends upon our continued world leadership for peace and freedom and democracy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We still can't be strong at home unless we're strong abroad.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The financial crisis in Mexico is a case in point.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know it's not popular to say it tonight, but we have to act.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Not for the Mexican people, but for the sake of the millions of Americans whose livelihoods are tied to Mexico's well-being.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we want to secure American jobs, preserve American exports, safeguard America's borders, then we must pass the stabilization program and help to put Mexico back on track.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now let me repeat: it's not a loan, it's not foreign aid, it's not a bail out.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will be given a guarantee like co-signing a note with good collateral that will cover our risks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This legislation is the right thing for America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why the bipartisan leadership has supported it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I hope you in Congress will pass it quickly.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It is in our interest, and we can explain it to the American people, because we're going to do it in the right way.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, tonight, this is the first State of the Union address ever delivered since the beginning of the Cold War when not a single Russian missile is pointed at the children of America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And along with the Russians, we're on the way to destroying the missiles and the bombers that carry 9,000 nuclear warheads.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've come so far so fast in this post-Cold War world that it's easy to take the decline of the nuclear threat for granted.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But it's still there, and we aren't finished yet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year I'll ask the Senate to approve START II, to eliminate weapons that carry 5,000 more warheads.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The United States will lead the charge to extend indefinitely the nuclear Nonproliferation Treaty -- to enact a comprehensive nuclear test ban -- and to eliminate chemical weapons.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To stop and roll back North Korea's potentially deadly nuclear program, we'll continue to implement the agree we have reached with that nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's smart.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's tough.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's a deal based on continuing inspection with safeguards for our allies and ourselves.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year I'll submit to Congress comprehensive legislation to strengthen our hand in combatting terrorists --whether they strike at home or abroad.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As the coward's who bombed the World Trade Center found out, this country will hunt down terrorists and bring them to justice.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Just this week, another horrendous terrorist act in Israel killed 19 and injured scores more.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: On behalf of the American people and all of you, I send our deepest sympathy to the families of the victims.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know that in the face of such evil, it is hard for the people in the Middle East to go forward.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But the terrorists represent the past, not the future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must and we will pursue a comprehensive peace between Israel and all her neighbors in the Middle East.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Accordingly, last night I signed an executive order that will block the assets in the United States of terrorist organizations that threaten to disrupt the peace process.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It prohibits financial transactions with these groups.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And tonight I call on our allies and peace-loving nations throughout the world to join us with renewed fervor in a global effort to combat terrorism.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We cannot permit the future to be marred by terror and fear and paralysis.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: MILITARY PREPAREDNESS:  From the day I took the oath of office, I pledged that our nation would maintain the best-equipped, best-trained and best-prepared military on Earth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have, and they are.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They have managed the dramatic downsizing of our forces after the Cold War with remarkable skill and spirit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But to make sure our military is ready for action, and to provide the pay and the quality of life the military and their families deserve, I'm asking the Congress to add $25 billion in defense spending over the next six years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have visited many bases at home and around the world, since I became president.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I repeat that request with renewed conviction.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We ask a very great deal of our Armed Forces.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now that they are smaller in number, we ask more of them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They go out more often to more different places and stay longer.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They are called to service in many, many ways.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we must give them and their families what the times demand and what they have earned.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Just think about what our troops have done in the last year, showing America at its best -- helping to save hundreds of thousands of people in Rwanda, moving with lightning speech to head off another threat to Kuwait, giving freedom and democracy back to the people of Haiti.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have proudly supported peace and prosperity and freedom from South Africa to Northern Ireland, from Central and Eastern Europe to Asia, from Latin America to the Middle East.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All these endeavors are good in those places, but they make our future more confident and more secure.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Well, my fellow Americans, that's my agenda for America's future: Expanding opportunity, not bureaucracy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Enhancing security at home and abroad.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Empowering our people to make the most of their own lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's ambitious and achievable, but it's not enough.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We even need more than new ideas for changing the world or equipping Americans to compete in the new economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: More than a government that's smaller, smarter and wiser.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: More than all the changes we can make in government and in the private sector from the outside in.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our fortunes and our posterity also depend upon our ability to answer some questions from within -- from the values and voices that speak to our hearts as well as our heads.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Voices that tell us we have to do more to accept responsibility for ourselves and our families, for our communities, and, yes, for our fellow citizens.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We see our families and our communities all over this country coming apart.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we feel the common ground shifting from under us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The PTA, the town hall meeting, the ball park -- it's hard for a lot of overworked parents to find the time and space for those things that strengthen the bonds of trust and cooperation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Too many of our children don't even have parents and grandparents who can give them those experiences that they need to build their own character and their sense of identity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: MAKING A DIFFERENCE:  We all know what while we here in this chamber can make a difference on those things, that the real differences will be made by our fellow citizens -- where they work and where they live.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And it will be made almost without regard to party.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When I used to go to the softball park in Little Rock to watch my daughter's league, and people would come up to me, fathers and mothers, and talk to me, I can honestly say I had no idea whether 90 percent of them were Republicans or Democrats.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, why?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can't wait for disasters to act the way we used to act every day.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because as we move into this next century, everybody matters.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We don't have a person to waste.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And a lot of people are losing a lot of chances to do better.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That means that we need a New Covenant for everybody.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For our corporate and business leaders, we're going to work here to keep bringing the deficit down, to expand markets, to support their success in every possible way.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But they have an obligation when they're doing well to keep jobs in our communities and give their workers a fair share of the prosperity they generate.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For people in the entertainment industry in this country, we applaud your creativity and your world-wide success, and we support your freedom of expression.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But you do have a responsibility to assess the impact of your work and to understand the damage that comes from the incessant, repetitive, mindless violence and irresponsible conduct that permeates our media all the time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've got to ask our community leaders and all kinds of organizations to help us stop our most serious social problem: the epidemic of teen pregnancies and births where there is no marriage.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have sent to Congress a plan to targets schools all over this country with anti-pregnancy programs that work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But government can only do so much.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I call on parents and leaders all across this country to join together in a national campaign against teen pregnancy to make a difference.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can do this, and we must.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I would like to say a special word to our religious leaders.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, I'm proud of the fact the United States has more houses of worship per capita than any country in the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These people who lead our houses of worship can ignite their congregations to carry their faith into action.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Can reach out to all of our children, to all of the people in distress, to those who have been savaged by the breakdown of all we hold dear.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because so much of what we've done must come from the inside out, and our religious leaders and their congregations can make all the difference.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They have a role in the New Covenant as well.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There must be more responsibility for all of our citizens.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, it takes a lot of people to help all the kids in trouble stay off the streets and in school.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It takes a lot of people to build the Habitat for Humanity houses that the Speaker celebrates on his lapel pin.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It takes a lot of people to provide the people power for all of the civic organizations in this country that made our communities mean so much to most of us when we were kids.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It takes every parent to teach the children the difference between right and wrong and to encourage them to learn and grow.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to say no to the wrong things, but also to believe that they can be whatever they want to be.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know it's hard when you're working harder for less, when you're under great stress to do these things.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A lot of our people don't have the time or the emotional stress they think to do the work of citizenship.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Most of us in politics haven't helped very much.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For years, we've mostly treated citizens like they were consumers or spectators, sort of political couch potatoes who were supposed to watch the TV ads, either promise them something for nothing or play on their fears and frustrations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And more and more of our citizens now get most of their information in very negative and aggressive ways that are hardly conducive to honest and open conversations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But the truth is, we have got to stop seeing each other as enemies, just because we have different views.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If you go back to the beginning of this country, the great strength of America, as de Tocqueville pointed out when he came here a long time ago, has always been our ability to associate with people who were different from ourselves and to work together to find common ground.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And in this day, everybody has a responsibility to do more of that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We simply cannot wait for a tornado, a fire, or a flood to behave like Americans ought to behave in dealing with one another.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: HONORING CITIZENS:  I want to finish up here by pointing out some folks that are up with the First Lady that represent what I'm trying to talk about -- citizens

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have no idea what their party affiliation is or who they voted for in the last election.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But they represent what we ought to be doing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Cindy Perry teaches second graders to read in AmeriCorps in rural Kentucky.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: She gains when she gives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: She's a mother of four.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: She says that her service inspired her to get her high school equivalency last year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: She was married when she was a teenager.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Stand up, Cindy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: She was married when she was a teenager.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: She had four children, but she had time to serve other people, to get her high school equivalency.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And she's going to use her AmeriCorps money to go back to college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Stephen Bishop is the police chief of Kansas City.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He's been a national leader.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Stand up -- He's been a national leader in using more police in community policing, and he's worked with AmeriCorps to do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And the crime rate in Kansas City has gone down as a result of what he did.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Corporal Gregory Depestre went to Haiti as part of his adopted country's force to help secure democracy in his native land.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I might add, we must be the only country in the world that could have gone to Haiti and taken aitian-Americans there who could speak the language and talk to the people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And he was one of them, and we're proud of him.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The next two folks I've had the honor of meeting and getting to know a little bit, the Reverend John and the Reverend Diana Cherry of the AME Zion Church in Temple Hills, Maryland.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'd like to ask them to stand.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to tell you about them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the early '80s, they left government service and formed a church in a small living room in a small house, in the early '80s.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today that church has 17,000 members.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It is one of the three or four biggest churches in the entire United States.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It grows by 200 a month.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They do it together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And the special focus of their ministry is keeping families together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Two things they did make a big impression on me.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I visited their church once, and I learned they were building a new sanctuary closer to the Washington, D.C., line in a higher crime, higher drug rate area because they thought it was part of their ministry to change the lives of the people who needed them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The second thing I want to say is, that once Reverend Cherry was at a meeting at the White House with some other religious leaders, and he left early to go back to his church to minister to 150 couples that he had brought back to his church from all over America to convince them to come back together, to save their marriages, and to raise their kids.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is the kind of work that citizens are doing in America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need more of it, and it ought to be lifted up and supported.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The last person I want to introduce is Jack Lucas from Hattiesburg, Mississippi.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Jack, would you stand up?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Fifty years ago, in the sands of Iwo Jima, Jack Lucas taught and learned the lessons of citizenship.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: On February the 20th, 1945, he and three of his buddies encountered the enemy and two grenades at their feet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Jack Lucas threw himself on both of them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In that moment, he saved the lives of his companions, and miraculously in the next instant, a medic saved his life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He gained a foothold for freedom, and at the age of 17, just a year older than his grandson, who is up there with him today, and his son, who is a West Point graduate and a veteran, at 17, Jack Lucas became the youngest Marine in history and the youngest soldier in this century to win the Congressional Medal of Honor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It didn't matter where you were from or who you were, you relied on one another.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We all gain when we give, and we reap what we sow.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's at the heart of this New Covenant -- responsibility, opportunity and citizenship.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: More than stale chapters in some remote civics book.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They're still the virtue by which we can fulfill ourselves and reach our God-given potential and be like them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And also to fulfill the eternal promise of this country -- the enduring dream from that first and most sacred covenant.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I believe every person in this country still believes that we are created equal, and given by our Creator, the right to life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is a very, very great country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And our best days are still to come.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you, and God bless you all.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Mr Speaker Vice President, members of the 104th Congress, distinguished guests, my fellow Americans all across our land:

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let me begin tonight by saying to our men and women in uniform around the world, and especially those helping peace take root in Bosnia and to their families, I thank you

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America is very, very proud of you

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My duty tonight is to report on the state of the Union -- not the state of our government, but of our American community

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to set forth our responsibilities, in the words of our Founders, to form a more perfect union

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The state of the Union is strong

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our economy is the healthiest it has been in three decades

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have the lowest combined rates of unemployment and inflation in 27 years

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have created nearly 8 million new jobs, over a million of them in basic industries, like construction and automobiles

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America is selling more cars than Japan for the first time since the 1970s

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And for three years in a row, we have had a record number of new businesses started in our country

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our leadership in the world is also strong, bringing hope for new peace

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And perhaps most important, we are gaining ground in restoring our fundamental values

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The crime rate, the welfare and food stamp rolls, the poverty rate and the teen pregnancy rate are all down

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And as they go down, prospects for America's future go up

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: AN AGE OF POSSIBILITY':  We live in an age of possibility.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A hundred years ago we moved from farm to factory

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now we move to an age of technology, information, and global competition

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These changes have opened vast new opportunities for our people, but they have also presented them with stiff challenges

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: While more Americans are living better, too many of our fellow citizens are working harder just to keep up, and they are rightly concerned about the security of their families

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must answer here three fundamental questions: First, how do we make the American dream of opportunity for all a reality for all Americans who are willing to work for it?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Second, how do we preserve our old and enduring values as we move into the future?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And, third, how do we meet these challenges together, as one America?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We know big government does not have all the answers

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We know there's not a program for every problem
