speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We know and we have worked to give the American people a smaller, less bureaucratic government in Washington

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we have to give the American people one that lives within its means

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The era of big government is over

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we cannot go back to the time when our citizens were left to fend for themselves

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must go forward as one America -- one nation working together to meet the challenges we face together

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Self-reliance and teamwork are not opposing virtues

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must have both

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I believe our new, smaller government must work in an old-fashioned American way, together with all of our citizens through state and local governments, in the workplace, in religious, charitable and civic associations

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our goal must be to enable all our people to make the most of their own lives -- with stronger families, more educational opportunity, economic security, safer streets, a cleaner environment in a safer world

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To improve the state of our Union, we must ask more of ourselves, we must expect more of each other, and we must face our challenges together

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Here, in this place, our responsibility begins with balancing the budget in a way that is fair to all Americans

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There is now broad bipartisan agreement that permanent deficit spending must come to an end

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I compliment the Republican leadership and the membership for the energy and determination you have brought to this task of balancing the budget

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I thank the Democrats for passing the largest deficit reduction plan in history in 1993, which has already cut the deficit nearly in half in three years

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Since 1993, we have all begun to see the benefits of deficit reduction

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Lower interest rates have made it easier for businesses to borrow and to invest and to create new jobs

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Lower interest rates have brought down the cost of home mortgages, car payments and credit card rates to ordinary citizens

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, it is time to finish the job and balance the budget

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Though differences remain among us which are significant, the combined total of the proposed savings that are common to both plans is more than enough, using the numbers from your Congressional Budget Office to balance the budget in seven years and to provide a modest tax cut

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These cuts are real

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They will require sacrifice from everyone

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But these cuts do not undermine our fundamental obligations to our parents, our children, and our future, by endangering Medicare, or Medicaid, or education, or the environment, or by raising taxes on working families

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have said before, and let me say again, many good ideas have come out of our negotiations

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have learned a lot about the way both Republicans and Democrats view the debate before us

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have learned a lot about the good ideas that we could all embrace

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We ought to resolve our remaining differences

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I am willing to work to resolve them

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I am ready to meet tomorrow

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I ask you to consider that we should at least enact these savings that both plans have in common and give the American people their balanced budget, a tax cut, lower interest rates, and a brighter future

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should do that now, and make permanent deficits yesterday's legacy

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: CHILDREN AND FAMILIES: Now it is time for us to look also to the challenges of today and tomorrow, beyond the burdens of yesterday

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The challenges are significant, bout our nation was built on challenges.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America was built on challenges, not promises

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And when we work together to meet them, we never fail

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is the key to a more perfect Union

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our individual dreams must be realized by our common efforts

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight I want to speak to you about the challenges we all face as a people

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our first challenge is to cherish our children and strengthen America's families

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Family is the foundation of American life

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we have stronger families, we will have a stronger America

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Before I go on, I would like to take just a moment to thank my own family, and to thank the person who has taught me more than anyone else over 25 years about the importance of families and children -- a wonderful wife, a magnificent mother and a great First Lady

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you, Hillary

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All strong families begin with taking more responsibility for our children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have heard Mrs Gore say that it's hard to be a parent today, but it's even harder to be a child

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So all of us, not just as parents, but all of us in our other roles -- our media, our schools, our teachers, our communities, our churches and synagogues, our businesses, our governments -- all of us have a responsibility to help our children to make it and to make the most of their lives and their God-given capacities

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To the media: I say you should create movies and CDs and television shows you'd want your own children and grandchildren to enjoy

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I call on Congress to pass the requirement for a V-chip in TV sets so that parents can screen out programs they believe are inappropriate for their children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When parents control what their young children see, that is not censorship

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is enabling parents to assume more personal responsibility for their children's upbringing

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I urge them to do it

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The V-chip requirement is part of the important telecommunications bill now pending in this Congress

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It has bipartisan support, and I urge you to pass it now

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To make the V-chip work, I challenge the broadcast industry to do what movies have done -- to identify your programming in ways that help parents to protect their children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I invite the leaders of major media corporations in the entertainment industry to come to the White House next month to work with us in a positive way on concrete ways to improve what our children see on television

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I am ready to work with you

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I say to those who make and market cigarettes: every year a million children take up smoking, even though it is against the law

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Three hundred thousand of them will have their lives shortened as a result

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our administration has taken steps to stop the massive marketing campaigns that appeal to our children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are simply saying: Market your products to adults, if you wish, but draw the line on children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I say to those who are on welfare, and especially to those who have been trapped on welfare for a long time: For too long our welfare system has undermined the values of family and work, instead of supporting them

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The Congress and I are near agreement on sweeping welfare reform

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We agree on time limits, tough work requirements, and the toughest possible child support enforcement

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I believe we must also provide child care so that mothers who are required to go to work can do so without worrying about what is happening to their children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge this Congress to send me a bipartisan welfare reform bill that will really move people from welfare to work and do the right thing by our children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I will sign it immediately

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But let us be candid about this difficult problem

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Passing a law, even the best possible law, is only a first step

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The next step is to make it work

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge people on welfare to make the most of this opportunity for independence

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge American businesses to give people on welfare the chance to move into the work force

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I applaud the work of religious groups and others who care for the poor

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: More than anyone else in our society, they know the true difficulty of the task before us, and they are in a position to help

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every one of us should join them

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is the only way we can make real welfare for american people

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To strengthen the family we must do everything we can to keep the teen pregnancy rate going down

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I am gratified, as I'm sure all Americans are, that it has dropped for two years in a row

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we all know it is still far too high

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight I am pleased to announce that a group of prominent Americans is responding to that challenge by forming an organization that will support grass-roots community efforts all across our country in a national campaign against teen pregnancy

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I challenge all of us and every American to join their efforts

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I call on American men and women in families to give greater respect to one another

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must end the deadly scourge of domestic violence in our country

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I challenge America's families to work harder to stay together

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For families who stay together not only do better economically, their children do better as well

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In particular, I challenge the fathers of this country to love and care for their children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If your family has separated, you must pay your child support

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are doing more than ever to make sure you do, and we're going to do more, but let's all admit something about that, too: A check will not substitute for a parent's love and guidance

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And only you -- only you can make the decision to help raise your children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: No matter who you are, how low or high your station in life, it is the most basic human duty of every American to do that job to the best of his or her ability

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES:  Our second challenge is to provide Americans with the educational opportunities we will all need for this new century

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In our schools, every classroom in America must be connected to the information superhighway, with computers and good software, and well-trained teachers

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are working with the telecommunications industry, educators and parents to connect 20 percent of California's classrooms by this spring, and every classroom and every library in the entire United States by the year 2000

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask Congress to support this education technology initiative so that we can make sure this national partnership succeeds

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every diploma ought to mean something

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge every community, every school and every state to adopt national standards of excellence

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To measure whether schools are meeting those standards

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To cut bureaucratic red tape so that schools and teachers have more flexibility for grass-roots reform

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to hold them accountable for results

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's what our Goals 2000 initiative is all about

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge every state to give all parents the right to choose which public school their children will attend

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to let teachers form new schools with a charter they can keep only if they do a good job

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge all our schools to teach character education, to teach good values and good citizenship

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And if it means that teenagers will stop killing each other over designer jackets, then our public schools should be able to require their students to wear school uniforms

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge our parents to become their children's first teachers

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Turn off the TV

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: See that the homework is done

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And visit your children's classroom

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: No program, no teacher, no one else can do that for you

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, higher education is more important today than ever before

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've created a new student loan program that's made it easier to borrow and repay those loans, and we have dramatically cut the student loan default rate

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's something we should all be proud of, because it was unconscionably high just a few years ago

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Through AmeriCorps, our national service program, this year 25,000 young people will earn college money by serving their local communities to improve the lives of their friends and neighbors

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These initiatives are right for America and we should keep them going

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we should also work hard to open the doors of college even wider

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge Congress to expand work-study and help one million young Americans work their way through college by the year 2000

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To provide a $1000 merit scholarship for the top five percent of graduates in every high school in the United States

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To expand Pell Grant scholarships for deserving and needy students

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to make up to $10,000 a year of college tuition tax deductible

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's a good idea for America

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: ECONOMIC SECURITY: Our third challenge is to help every American who is willing to work for it, achieve economic security in this new age

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: People who work hard still need support to get ahead in the new economy

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They need education and training for a lifetime

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They need more support for families raising children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They need retirement security

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They need access to health care

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: More and more Americans are finding that the education of their childhood simply doesn't last a lifetime

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I challenge Congress to consolidate 70 overlapping, antiquated job-training programs into a simple voucher worth $2,600 for unemployed or underemployed workers to use as they please for community college tuition or other training

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is a G.I. Bill for America's workers we should all be able to agree on

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: More and more Americans are working hard without a raise

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Congress sets the minimum wage

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Within a year, the minimum wage will fall to a 40-year low in purchasing power

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Four dollars and 25 cents an hour is no longer a living wage, but millions of Americans and their children are trying to live on it

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge you to raise their minimum wage

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In 1993, Congress cut the taxes of 15 million hard-pressed working families to make sure that no parents who work full-time would have to raise their children in poverty, and to encourage people to move from welfare to work

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This expanded earned income tax credit is now worth about $1,800 a year to a family of four living on $20,000

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The budget bill I vetoed would have reversed this achievement and raised taxes on nearly 8 million of these people

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should not do that

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I also agree that the people who are helped under this initiative are not all those in our country who are working hard to do a good job raising their children and at work

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I agree that we need a tax credit for working families with children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's one of the things most of us in this Chamber, I hope, can agree on

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know it is strongly supported by the Republican majority

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And it should be part of any final budget agreement

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to challenge every business that can possibly afford it to provide pensions for your employees

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I challenge Congress to pass a proposal recommended by the White House Conference on Small Business that would make it easier for small businesses and farmers to establish their own pension plans

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is something we should all agree on

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should also protect existing pension plans

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Two years ago, with bipartisan support that was almost unanimous on both sides of the aisle, we moved to protect the pensions of 8 million working people and to stabilize the pensions of 32 million more

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Congress should not now let companies endanger those workers's pension funds

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know the proposal to liberalize the ability of employers to take money out of pension funds for other purposes would raise money for the treasury

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I believe it is false economy

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I vetoed that proposal last year, and I would have to do so again

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Finally, if our working families are going to succeed in the new economy, they must be able to buy health insurance policies that they do not lose when they change jobs or when someone in their family gets sick

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Over the past two years, over one million Americans in working families have lost their health insurance

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have to do more to make health care available to every American

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And Congress should start by passing the bipartisan bill sponsored by Senator Kennedy and Senator Kassebaum that would require insurance companies to stop dropping people when they switch jobs, and stop denying coverage for preexisting conditions

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's all do that

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And even as we enact savings in these programs, we must have a common commitment to preserve the basic protections of Medicare and Medicaid -- not just to the poor, but to people in working families, including children, people with disabilities, people with AIDS, and senior citizens in nursing homes

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the past three years, we've saved $15 billion just by fighting health care fraud and abuse

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have all agreed to save much more

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have all agreed to stabilize the Medicare Trust Fund

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we must not abandon our fundamental obligations to the people who need Medicare and Medicaid

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America cannot become stronger if they become weaker

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The G.I. Bill for workers, tax relief for education and child rearing, pension availability and protection, access to health care, preservation of Medicare and Medicaid -- these things, along with the Family and Medical Leave Act passed in 1993 -- these things will help responsible, hard-working American families to make the most of their own lives

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But employers and employees must do their part, as well, as they are doing in so many of our finest companies -- working together, putting the long-term prosperity ahead of the short-term gain

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As workers increase their hours and their productivity, employers should make sure they get the skills they need and share the benefits of the good years, as well as the burdens of the bad ones

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When companies and workers work as a team they do better, and so does America

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: TAKE BACK THE STREETS:  Our fourth great challenge is to take our streets back from crime and gangs and drugs

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: At last we have begun to find a way to reduce crime, forming community partnerships with local police forces to catch criminals and prevent crime

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This strategy, called community policing, is clearly working

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Violent crime is coming down all across America

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In New York City murders are down 25percent

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In St. Louis, 18 percent

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In Seattle, 32 percent

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we still have a long way to go before our streets are safe and our people are free from fear

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The Crime Bill of 1994 is critical to the success of community policing

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It provides funds for 100,000 new police in communities of all sizes

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We're already a third of the way there

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I challenge the Congress to finish the job

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us stick with a strategy that's working and keep the crime rate coming down

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Community policing also requires bonds of trust between citizens and police

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask all Americans to respect and support our law enforcement officers

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to our police, I say, our children need you as role models and heroes

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Don't let them down

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The Brady Bill has already stopped 44,000 people with criminal records from buying guns

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The assault weapons ban is keeping 19 kinds of assault weapons out of the hands of violent gangs

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge the Congress to keep those laws on the books

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our next step in the fight against crime is to take on gangs the way we once took on the mob

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'm directing the FBI and other investigative agencies to target gangs that involve juveniles in violent crime, and to seek authority to prosecute as adults teenagers who maim and kill like adults

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I challenge local housing authorities and tenant associations: Criminal gang members and drug dealers are destroying the lives of decent tenants

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: From now on, the rule for residents who commit crime and peddle drugs should be one strike and you're out

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge every state to match federal policy to assure that serious violent criminals serve at least 85 percent of their sentence

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: More police and punishment are important, but they're not enough

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have got to keep more of our young people out of trouble, with prevention strategies not dictated by Washington, but developed in communities

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge all of our communities, all of our adults, to give our children futures to say yes to

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I challenge Congress not to abandon the Crime Bill's support of these grass-roots prevention efforts

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Finally, to reduce crime and violence we have to reduce the drug problem

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The challenge begins in our homes, with parents talking to their children openly and firmly

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It embraces our churches and synagogues, our youth groups and our schools

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge Congress not to cut our support for drug-free schools

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: People like the D.A.R.E. officers are making a real impression on grade schoolchildren that will give them the strength to say no when the time comes

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Meanwhile, we continue our efforts to cut the flow of drugs into America

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For the last two years, one man in particular has been on the front lines of that effort

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight I am nominating him -- a hero of the Persian Gulf War and the Commander in Chief of the United States Military Southern Command -- General Barry McCaffrey, as America's new Drug Czar

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: General McCaffrey has earned three Purple Hearts and two Silver Stars fighting for this country

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight I ask that he lead our nation's battle against drugs at home and abroad

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To succeed, he needs a force far larger than he has ever commanded before

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He needs all of us

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every one of us has a role to play on this team

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you, General McCaffrey, for agreeing to serve your country one more time

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: COMMITMENT TO THE ENVIRONMENT:  Our fifth challenge: to leave our environment safe and clean for the next generation

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because of a generation of bipartisan effort we do have cleaner water and air, lead levels in children's blood has been cut by 70 percent, toxic emissions from factories cut in half

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Lake Erie was dead, and now it's a thriving resource

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But 10 million children under 12 still live within four miles of a toxic waste dump

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A third of us breathe air that endangers our health

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And in too many communities, the water is not safe to drink

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We still have much to do

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Yet Congress has voted to cut environmental enforcement by 25 percent

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That means more toxic chemicals in our water, more smog in our air, more pesticides in our food

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Lobbyists for polluters have been allowed to write their own loopholes into bills to weaken laws that protect the health and safety of our children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Some say that the taxpayer should pick up the tab for toxic waste and let polluters who can afford to fix it off the hook

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge Congress to reexamine those policies and to reverse them

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This issue has not been a partisan issue

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The most significant environmental gains in the last 30 years were made under a Democratic Congress and President Richard Nixon

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can work together

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have to believe some basic things

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Do you believe we can expand the economy without hurting the environment?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I do

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Do you believe we can create more jobs over the long run by cleaning the environment up?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know we can

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That should be our commitment

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must challenge businesses and communities to take more initiative in protecting the environment, and we have to make it easier for them to do it

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To businesses this administration is saying: If you can find a cheaper, more efficient way than government regulations require to meet tough pollution standards, do it -- as long as you do it right

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To communities we say: We must strengthen community right-to-know laws requiring polluters to disclose their emissions, but you have to use the information to work with business to cut pollution

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: People do have a right to know that their air and their water are safe

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: AMERICAN WORLD LEADERSHIP:  Our sixth challenge is to maintain America's leadership in the fight for freedom and peace throughout the world

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because of American leadership, more people than ever before live free and at peace

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And Americans have known 50 years of prosperity and security

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We owe thanks especially to our veterans of World War II

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I would like to say to Senator Bob Dole and to all others in this Chamber who fought in World War II, and to all others on both sides of the aisle who have fought bravely in all our conflicts since: I salute your service, and so do the American people

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All over the world, even after the Cold War, people still look to us and trust us to help them seek the blessings of peace and freedom

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But as the Cold War fades into memory, voices of isolation say America should retreat from its responsibilities

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I say they are wrong

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The threats we face today as Americans respect no nation's borders

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Think of them: terrorism, the spread of weapons of mass destruction, organized crime, drug trafficking, ethnic and religious hatred, aggression by rogue states, environmental degradation

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we fail to address these threats today, we will suffer the consequences in all our tomorrows

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Of course, we can't be everywhere

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Of course, we can't do everything

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But where our interests and our values are at stake, and where we can make a difference, America must lead

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must not be isolationist

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must not be the world's policeman

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we can and should be the world's very best peacemaker

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: By keeping our military strong, by using diplomacy where we can and force where we must, by working with others to share the risk and the cost of our efforts, America is making a difference for people here and around the world

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For the first time since the dawn of the nuclear age, there is not a single Russian missile pointed at America's children

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: North Korea has now frozen its dangerous nuclear weapons program

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In Haiti, the dictators are gone, democracy has a new day, the flow of desperate refugees to our shores has subsided

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Through tougher trade deals for America -- over 80 of them -- we have opened markets abroad, and now exports are at an all-time high, growing faster than imports and creating good American jobs

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We stood with those taking risks for peace: In Northern Ireland, where Catholic and Protestant children now tell their parents, violence must never return

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the Middle East, where Arabs and Jews who once seemed destined to fight forever now share knowledge and resources, and even dreams

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we stood up for peace in Bosnia

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Remember the skeletal prisoners, the mass graves, the campaign to rape and torture, the endless lines of refugees, the threat of a spreading war

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All these threats, all these horrors have now begun to give way to the promise of peace

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, our troops and a strong NATO, together with our new partners from Central Europe and elsewhere, are helping that peace to take hold

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As all of you know, I was just there with a bipartisan congressional group, and I was so proud not only of what our troops were doing, but of the pride they evidenced in what they were doing

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They knew what America's mission in this world is, and they were proud to be carrying it out

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Through these efforts, we have enhanced the security of the American people

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But make no mistake about it: important challenges remain

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The START II Treaty with Russia will cut our nuclear stockpiles by another 25 percent

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I urge the Senate to ratify it -- now

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must end the race to create new nuclear weapons by signing a truly comprehensive nuclear test ban treaty -- this year

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As we remember what happened in the Japanese subway, we can outlaw poison gas forever if the Senate ratifies the Chemical Weapons Convention -- this year

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can intensify the fight against terrorists and organized criminals at home and abroad if Congress passes the anti-terrorism legislation I proposed after the Oklahoma City bombing -- now

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can help more people move from hatred to hope all across the world in our own interest if Congress gives us the means to remain the world's leader for peace

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: RE-INVENTING GOVERNMENT:  My fellow Americans, the six challenges I have just discussed are for all of us

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our seventh challenge is really America's challenge to those of us in this hallowed hall tonight: to reinvent our government and make our democracy work for them

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year this Congress applied to itself the laws it applies to everyone else

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This Congress banned gifts and meals from lobbyists

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This Congress forced lobbyists to disclose who pays them and what legislation they are trying to pass or kill

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This Congress did that, and I applaud you for it

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now I challenge Congress to go further -- to curb special interest influence in politics by passing the first truly bipartisan campaign reform bill in a generation

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You, Republicans and Democrats alike, can show the American people that we can limit spending and open the airwaves to all candidates

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I also appeal to Congress to pass the line-item veto you promised the American people

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our administration is working hard to give the American people a government that works better and costs less

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thanks to the work of Vice President Gore, we are eliminating 16,000 pages of unnecessary rules and regulations, shifting more decision-making out of Washington, back to states and local communities

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As we move into the era of balanced budgets and smaller government, we must work in new ways to enable people to make the most of their own lives

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are helping America's communities, not with more bureaucracy, but with more opportunities

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Through our successful Empowerment Zones and Community Development Banks, we are helping people to find jobs, to start businesses

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And with tax incentives for companies that clean up abandoned industrial property, we can bring jobs back to places that desperately, desperately need them

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But there are some areas that the federal government should not leave and should address and address strongly

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: One of these areas is the problem of illegal immigration

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: After years of neglect, this administration has taken a strong stand to stiffen the protection of our borders

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are increasing border controls by 50 percent

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are increasing inspections to prevent the hiring of illegal immigrants

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And tonight, I announce I will sign an executive order to deny federal contracts to businesses that hire illegal immigrants

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let me be very clear about this: We are still a nation of immigrants

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: we should be proud of it

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should honor every legal immigrant here, working hard to become a new citizen

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we are also a nation of laws

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to say a special word now to those who work for our federal government

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today our federal government is 200,000 employees smaller than it was the day I took office as President

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our federal government today is the smallest it has been in 30 years, and it's getting smaller every day

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Most of our fellow Americans probably don't know that

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And there is a good reason: The remaining federal work force is composed of Americans who are now working harder and working smarter than ever before, to make sure the quality of our services does not decline

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'd like to give you one example

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: His name is Richard Dean

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He is a 49 year-old Vietnam veteran who's worked for the Social Security Administration for 22 years now

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year he was hard at work in the Federal Building in Oklahoma City when the blast killed 169 people and brought the rubble down all around him

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He reentered that building four times

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He saved the lives of three women

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He's here with us this evening, and I want to recognize Richard and applaud both his public service and his extraordinary personal heroism

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But Richard Dean's story doesn't end there

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This last November, he was forced out of his office when the government shut down

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And the second time the government shut down he continued helping Social Security recipients, but he was working without pay

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: On behalf of Richard Dean and his family, and all the other people who are out there working every day doing a good job for the American people, I challenge all of you in this Chamber: Never, ever shut the federal government down again

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: On behalf of all Americans, especially those who need their Social Security payments at the beginning of March, I also challenge the Congress to preserve the full faith and credit of the United States -- to honor the obligations of this great nation as we have for 220 years

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To rise above partisanship and pass a straightforward extension of the debt limit and show people America keeps its word

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know that this evening I have asked a lot of Congress, and even more from America

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I am confident: When Americans work together in their homes, their schools, their churches, their synagogues, their civic groups, their workplace, they can meet any challenge

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: TORCH OF CITIZENSHIP:  I say again: the era of big government is over

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we can't go back to the era of fending for yourself

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have to go forward to the era of working together as a community, as a team, as one America, with all of us reaching across these lines that divide us -- the division, the discrimination, the rancor -- we have to reach across it to find common ground

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have got to work together if we want America to work

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want you to meet two more people tonight who do just that

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Lucius Wright is a teacher in the Jackson, Mississippi, public school system

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A Vietnam veteran, he has created groups to help inner-city children turn away from gangs and build futures they can believe in

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And Sergeant Jennifer Rodgers is a police officer in Oklahoma City

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Like Richard Dean, she helped to pull her fellow citizens out of the rubble and deal with that awful tragedy

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: She reminds us that in their response to that atrocity the people of Oklahoma City lifted all of us with their basic sense of decency and community

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Lucius Wright and Jennifer Rodgers are special Americans

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I have the honor to announce tonight that they are the very first of several thousand Americans who will be chosen to carry the Olympic torch on its long journey from Los Angeles to the centennial of the modern Olympics in Atlanta this summer -- not because they are star athletes, but because they are star citizens, community heroes meeting America's challenges

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They are our real champions

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, each of us must hold high the torch of citizenship in our own lives

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: None of us can finish the race alone

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can only achieve our destiny together -- one hand, one generation, one American connecting to another

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There have always been things we could do together -- dreams we could make real -- which we could never have done on our own

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We Americans have forged our identity, our very union, from every point of view and every point on the planet, every different opinion

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we must be bound together by a faith more powerful than any doctrine that divides us -- by our belief in progress, our love of liberty, and our relentless search for common ground

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America has always sought and always risen to every challenge

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Who would say that, having come so far together, we will not go forward from here?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Who would say that this age of possibility is not for all Americans?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our country is and always has been a great and good nation

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But the best is yet to come, if we all do our part

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you, God bless you and God bless the United States of America

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Speaker, Mr. Vice President, members of the 105th Congress, distinguished guests, and my fellow Americans:

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think I should start by saying, thanks for inviting me back.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I come before you tonight with a challenge as great as any in our peacetime history, and a plan of action to meet that challenge, to prepare our people for the bold new world of the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have much to be thankful for.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With four years of growth, we have won back the basic strength of our economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With crime and welfare rolls declining, we are winning back our optimism, the enduring faith that we can master any difficulty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With the Cold War receding and global commerce at record levels, we are helping to win unrivaled peace and prosperity all across the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, the state of our union is strong.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But now we must rise to the decisive moment, to make a nation and a world better than any we have ever known.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The new promise of the global economy, the Information Age, unimagined new work, life-enhancing technology -- all these are ours to seize.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is our honor and our challenge.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must be shapers of events, not observers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For if we do not act, the moment will pass -- and we will lose the best possibilities of our future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We face no imminent threat, but we do have an enemy -- the enemy of our time is inaction.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So, tonight, I issue a call to action -- action by this Congress, action by our states, by our people, to prepare America for the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Action to keep our economy and our democracy strong and working for all our people;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: action to strengthen education and harness the forces of technology and science;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: action to build stronger families and stronger communities and a safer environment;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: action to keep America the world's strongest force for peace, freedom and prosperity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And above all, action to build a more perfect union here at home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The spirit we bring to our work will make all the difference.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must be committed to the pursuit of opportunity for all Americans, responsibility from all Americans, in a community of all Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we must be committed to a new kind of government -- not to solve all our problems for us, but to give our people -- all our people -- the tools they need to make the most of their own lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we must work together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The people of this nation elected us all.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They want us to be partners, not partisans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They put us all right here in the same boat, they gave us all oars, and they told us to row.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, here is the direction I believe we should take.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: BALANCED BUDGET:  First, we must move quickly to complete the unfinished business of our country -- to balance our budget, renew our democracy, and finish the job of welfare reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Over the last four years, we have brought new economic growth by investing in our people, expanding our exports, cutting our deficits, creating over 11 million new jobs, a four-year record.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now we must keep our economy the strongest in the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We here tonight have an historic opportunity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let this Congress be the Congress that finally balances the budget.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In two days, I will propose a detailed plan to balance the budget by 2002.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This plan will balance the budget and invest in our people while protecting Medicare, Medicaid, education, and the environment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It will balance the budget and build on the Vice President's efforts to make our government work better, even as it costs less.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It will balance the budget and provide middle class tax relief to pay for education and health care, to help to raise a child, to buy and sell a home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Balancing the budget requires only your vote and my signature.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It does not require us to rewrite our Constitution.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I believe it is both unnecessary and unwise to adopt a balanced budget amendment that could cripple our country in time of crisis, and force unwanted results, such as judges halting Social Security checks or increasing taxes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us at least agree, we should not pass any measure -- no measure should be passed that threatens Social Security.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We don

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Whatever our differences, we should balance the budget now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And then, for the long-term health of our society, we must agree to a bipartisan process to preserve Social Security and reform Medicare for the long run, so that these fundamental programs will be as strong for our children as they are for our parents.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And let me say something that's not in my script tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know this is not going to be easy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I really believe one of the reasons the American people gave me a second term was to take the tough decisions in the next four years that will carry our country through the next 50 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know it is easier for me than for you to say or do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But another reason I was elected is to support all of you, without regard to party, to give you what is necessary to join in these decisions.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We owe it to our country and to our future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: CAMPAIGN FINANCE REFORM:  Our second piece of unfinished business requires us to commit ourselves tonight, before the eyes of America, to finally enacting bipartisan campaign finance reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, Senators McCain and Feingold, Representatives Shays and Meehan, have reached across party lines here to craft tough and fair reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Their proposal would curb spending, reduce the role of special interests, create a level playing field between challengers and incumbents, and ban contributions from noncitizens, all corporate sources, and the other large soft money contributions that both parties receive.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know and I know that this can be delayed.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And you know and I know the delay will mean the death of reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So let's set our own deadline.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's work together to write bipartisan campaign finance reform into law and pass McCain-Feingold by the day we celebrate the birth of our democracy -- July the 4th.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: FROM WELFARE TO WORK: There is a third piece of unfinished business.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Over the last four years, we moved a record 2.25 million people off the welfare rolls

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Then last year, Congress enacted landmark welfare reform legislation, demanding that all able-bodied recipients assume the responsibility of moving from welfare to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now each and every one of us has to fulfill our responsibility -- indeed, our moral obligation -- to make sure that people who now must work, can work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And now we must act to meet a new goal: 2 million more people off the welfare rolls by the year 2000.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Here is my plan: Tax credits and other incentives for businesses that hire people off welfare; incentives for job placement firms and states to create more jobs for welfare recipients; training, transportation, and child care to help people go to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now I challenge every state: Turn those welfare checks into private sector paychecks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge every religious congregation, every community nonprofit, every business to hire someone off welfare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I'd like to say especially to every employer in our country who ever criticized the old welfare system, you can't blame that old system anymore, we have torn it down.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now do your part.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Give someone on welfare the chance to go to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I am pleased to announce that five major corporations -- Sprint, Monsanto, UPS, Burger King and United Airlines -- will be the first to join in a new national effort to marshal America's businesses, large and small, to create jobs so that people can move from welfare to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We passed welfare reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All of you know I believe we were right to do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But no one can walk out of this chamber with a clear conscience unless you are prepared to finish the job.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we must join together to do something else, too -- something both Republican and Democratic governors have asked us to do -- to restore basic health and disability benefits when misfortune strikes immigrants who came to this country legally, who work hard, pay taxes and obey the law.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To do otherwise is simply unworthy of a great nation of immigrants.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: EDUCATION: Now, looking ahead, the greatest step of all -- the high threshold of the future we now must cross -- and my number one priority for the next four years is to ensure that all Americans have the best education in the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's work together to meet these three goals: Every 8-year-old must be able to read;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: every 12-year-old must be able to log on to the Internet;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: every 18-year-old must be able to go to college;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: and every adult American must be able to keep on learning for a lifetime.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My balanced budget makes an unprecedented commitment to these goals -- $51 billion next year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But far more than money is required.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have a plan, a Call to Action for American Education, based on these 10 principles.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: First, a national crusade for education standards -- not federal government standards, but national standards, representing what all our students must know to succeed in the knowledge economy of the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every state and school must shape the curriculum to reflect these standards, and train teachers to lift students up to them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To help schools meet the standards and measure their progress, we will lead an effort over the next two years to develop national tests of student achievement in reading and math.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I issue a challenge to the nation: Every state should adopt high national standards, and by 1999, every state should test every 4th grader in reading and every 8th grader in math to make sure these standards are met.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Raising standards will not be easy, and some of our children will not be able to meet them at first.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The point is not to put our children down, but to lift them up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Good tests will show us who needs help, what changes in teaching to make, and which schools need to improve.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They can help us to end social promotion.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For no child should move from grade school to junior high, or junior high to high school until he or she is ready.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: took the Third International Math and Science Study.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's a test that reflects the world-class standards our children must meet for the new era.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And those students in Illinois tied for first in the world in science and came in second in math.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Two of them, Kristin Tanner and Chris Getsla, are here tonight, along with their teacher, Sue Winski.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They're up there with the First Lady, and they prove that when we aim high and challenge our students, they will be the best in the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's give them a hand.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Stand up, please.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Second, to have the best schools, we must have the best teachers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Most of us in this chamber would not be here tonight without the help of those teachers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know that I wouldn't be here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For years, many of our educators, led by North Carolina's Governor Jim Hunt and the National Board for Professional Teaching Standards, have worked very hard to establish nationally accepted credentials for excellence in teaching.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Just 500 of these teachers have been certified since 1995.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My budget will enable 100,000 more to seek national certification as master teachers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should reward and recognize our best teachers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And as we reward them, we should quickly and fairly remove those few who don't measure up, and we should challenge more of our finest young people to consider teaching as a career.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Third, we must do more to help all our children read.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Forty percent -- forty percent -- of our 8-year-olds cannot read on their own.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why we have just launched the America Reads initiative -- to build a citizen army of one million volunteer tutors to make sure every child can read independently by the end of the 3rd grade.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will use thousands of AmeriCorps volunteers to mobilize this citizen army.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We want at least 100,000 college students to help.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And tonight I am pleased that 60 college presidents have answered my call, pledging that thousands of their work-study students will serve for one year as reading tutors.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is also a challenge to every teacher and every principal.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You must use these tutors to help students read.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And it is especially a challenge to our parents.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You must read with your children every night.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This leads to the fourth principle: Learning begins in the first days of life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Scientists are now discovering how young children develop emotionally and intellectually from their very first days, and how important it is for parents to begin immediately talking, singing, even reading to their infants.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The First Lady has spent years writing about this issue, studying it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And she and I are going to convene a White House Conference on Early Learning and the Brain this spring, to explore how parents and educators can best use these startling new findings.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We already know we should start teaching children before they start school.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why this balanced budget expands Head Start to one million children by 2002.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And that is why the Vice President and Mrs.Gore will host their annual family conference this June on what we can do to make sure that parents are an active part of their children's learning all the way through school.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They've done a great deal to highlight the importance of family in our life, and now they're turning their attention to getting more parents involved in their children's learning all the way through school.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I thank you, Mr. Vice President, and I thank you especially, Tipper, for what you're doing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Fifth, every state should give parents the power to choose the right public school for their children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Their right to choose will foster competition and innovation that can make public schools better.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should also make it possible for more parents and teachers to start charter schools, schools that set and meet the highest standards, and exist only as long as they do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our plan will help America to create 3,000 of these charter schools by the next century -- nearly seven times as there are in the country today -- so that parents will have even more choices in sending their children to the best schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Sixth, character education must be taught in our schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must teach our children to be good citizens.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we must continue to promote order and discipline, supporting communities that introduce school uniforms, impose curfews enforce truancy laws, remove disruptive students from the classroom, and have zero tolerance for guns and drugs in school.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Seventh, we cannot expect our children to raise themselves up in schools that are literally falling down.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With the student population at an all-time high, and record numbers of school buildings falling into disrepair, this has now become a serious national concern.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Therefore, my budget includes a new initiative --$5 billion to help communities finance $20 billion in school construction over the next four years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Eighth: We must make the 13th and 14th years of education -- at least two years of college -- just as universal in America by the 21st century as a high school education is today, and we must open the doors of college to Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To do that, I propose America's HOPE Scholarship, basedon Georgia's pioneering program: two years of a $1,500 tax credit for college tuition, enough to pay for the typical community college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I also propose a tax deduction of up to $10,000 a year for all tuition after high school; an expanded IRA you can withdraw from tax free for education; and the largest increase in Pell Grant scholarships in 20 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, this plan will give most families the ability to pay no taxes on money they save for college tuition.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to pass it -- and give every American who works hard the chance to go to college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Ninth: In the 21st century, we must expand the frontiers of learning across a lifetime.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All our people, of whatever age, must have a chance to learn new skills.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Most Americans live near a community college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The roads that take them there can be paths to a better future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My G. I. Bill for America's Workers will transform the confusing tangle of federal training programs into a simple skill grant to go directly into eligible workers' hands.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For too long, this bill has been sitting on that desk there without action -- I ask you to pass it now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's give more of our workers the ability to learn and to earn for a lifetime.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tenth: We must bring the power of the Information Age into all our schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, I challenged America to connect every classroom and library to the Internet by the year 2000, so that, for the first time in our history, children in the most isolated rural towns, the most comfortable suburbs, the poorest inner city schools, will have the same access to the same universe of knowledge.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is my plan -- a Call to Action for American Education.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Some may say that it is unusual for a President to pay this kind of attention to education.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Some may say it is simply because the President and his wonderful wife have been obsessed with this subject for more years than they can recall.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is not what is driving these proposals.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must understand the significance of this endeavor: One of the greatest sources of our strength throughout the Cold War was a bipartisan foreign policy;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: because our future was at stake, politics stopped at the water's edge.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now I ask you -- and I ask all our nation's governors;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask parents, teachers, and citizens all across America -- for a new nonpartisan commitment to education -- because education is a critical national security issue for our future, and politics must stop at the schoolhouse door.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: HARNESSING TECHNOLOGY:  To prepare America for the 21st century we must harness the powerful forces of science and technology to benefit all Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is the first State of the Union carried live in video over the Internet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we've only begun to spread the benefits of a technology revolution that should become the modern birthright of every citizen.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our effort to connect every classroom is just the beginning.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, we should connect every hospital to the Internet, so that doctors can instantly share data about their patients with the best specialists in the field.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I challenge the private sector tonight to start by connecting every children's hospital as soon as possible, so that a child in bed can stay in touch with school, family and friends.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A sick child need no longer be a child alone.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must build the second generation of the Internet so that our leading universities and national laboratories can communicate in speeds 1,000 times faster than today, to develop new medical treatments, new sources of energy, new ways of working together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we cannot stop there.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As the Internet becomes our new town square, a computer in every home -- a teacher of all subjects, a connection to all cultures -- this will no longer be a dream, but a necessity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And over the next decade, that must be our goal.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must continue to explore the heavens -- pressing on with the Mars probes and the international space station, both of which will have practical applications for our everyday living.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must speed the remarkable advances in medical science.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The human genome project is now decoding the genetic mysteries of life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: American scientists have discovered genes linked to breast cancer and ovarian cancer, and medication that stops a stroke in progress and begins to reverse its effect, and treatments that dramatically lengthen the lives of people with HIV and AIDS.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Since I took office, funding for AIDS research at the National Institutes of Health has increased dramatically -- to $1.5 billion.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With new resources, NIH will now become the most powerful discovery engine for an AIDS vaccine, working with other scientists to finally end the threat of AIDS.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Remember that every year -- every year we move up the discovery of an AIDS vaccine will save millions of lives around the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must reinforce our commitment to medical science.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To prepare America for the 21st century, we must build stronger families.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Over the past four years, the Family and Medical Leave law has helped millions of Americans to take time off to be with their families.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With new pressures on people in the way they work and live, I believe we must expand family leave so that workers can take time off for teacher conferences and a child's medical checkup.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should pass flex-time, so workers can choose to be paid for overtime in income or trade it in for time off to be with their families.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must continue -- we must continue, step by step, to give more families access to affordable, quality health care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Forty million Americans still lack health insurance.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Ten million children still lack health insurance -- 80 percent of them have working parents who pay taxes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is wrong.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My balanced budget will extend health coverage to up to 5 million of those children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Since nearly half of all children who lose their insurance do so because their parents lose or change a job, my budget will also ensure that people who temporarily lose their jobs can still afford to keep their health insurance.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: No child should be without a doctor just because a parent is without a job.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My Medicare plan modernizes Medicare, increases the life of the trust fund to 10 years, provides support for respite care for the many families with loved ones afflicted with Alzheimer's.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And for the first time, it would fully pay for annual mammograms.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Just as we ended drive-through deliveries of babies last year, we must now end the dangerous and demeaning practice of forcing women home from the hospital only hours after a mastectomy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask your support for bipartisan legislation to guarantee that a woman can stay in the hospital for 48 hours after a mastectomy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With us tonight is Dr. Kristen Zarfos, a Connecticut surgeon whose outrage at this practice spurred a national movement and inspired this legislation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'd like her to stand so we thank her for her efforts.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Dr. Zarfos, thank you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the last four years, we have increased child support collections by 50 percent.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now we should go further and do better by making it a felony for any parent to cross a state line in an attempt to flee from this, his or her most sacred obligation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Finally, we must also protect our children by standing firm in our determination to ban the advertising and marketing of cigarettes that endanger their lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: BUILDING STRONGER COMMUNITIES:  To prepare America for the 21st century, we must build stronger communities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should start with safe streets.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Serious crime has dropped five years in a row.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The key has been community policing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must finish the job of putting 100,000 community police on the streets of the United States.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should pass the Victims Rights Amendment to the Constitution.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I ask you to mount a full-scale assault on juvenile crime, with legislation that declares war on gangs, with new prosecutors and tougher penalties;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: extends the Brady Bill so violent teen criminals will not be able to buy handguns;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
