text: requires child safety locks on handguns to prevent unauthorized use;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: and helps to keep our schools open after hours, on weekends, and in the summer, so our young people will have someplace to go and something to say yes to.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This balanced budget includes the largest antidrug effort ever: to stop drugs at their source, punish those who push them, and teach our young people that drugs are wrong, drugs are illegal, and drugs will kill them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope you will support it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our growing economy has helped to revive poor urban and rural neighborhoods.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we must do more to empower them to create the conditions in which all families can flourish and to create jobs through investment by business and loans by banks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should double the number of empowerment zones.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They've already brought so much hope to communities like Detroit, where the unemployment rate has been cut in half in four years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should restore contaminated urban land and buildings to productive use.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should expand the network of community development banks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And together we must pledge tonight that we will use this empowerment approach -- including private sector tax incentives -- to renew our Capital City, so that Washington is a great place to work and live, and once again the proud face America shows to world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must protect our environment in every community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the last four years, we cleaned up 250 toxic waste sites, as many as in the previous 12.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, we should clean up 500 more, so that our children grow up next to parks, not poison.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I urge you to pass my proposal to make big polluters live by a simple rule: If you pollute our environment, you should pay to clean it up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the last four years, we strengthened our nation's safe food and clean drinking water laws;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: we protected some of America's rarest, most beautiful land in Utah's Red Rocks region;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: created three new national parks in the California desert;

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: and began to restore the Florida Everglades.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now we must be as vigilant with our rivers as we are with our lands.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I announce that this year I will designate 10 American Heritage Rivers, to help communities alongside them revitalize their waterfronts and clean up pollution in the rivers, proving once again that we can grow the economy as we protect the environment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must also protect our global environment, working to ban the worst toxic chemicals and to reduce the greenhouse gases that challenge our health even as they change our climate.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, we all know that in all of our communities, some of our children simply don't have what they need to grow and learn in their own homes, or schools or neighborhoods.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And that means the rest of us must do more, for they are our children, too.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why President Bush, General Colin Powell, former Housing Secretary Henry Cisneros will join the Vice President and me to lead the President's Summit of Service in Philadelphia in April.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our national service program, AmeriCorps, has already helped 70,000 young people to work their way through college as they serve America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now we intend to mobilize millions of Americans to serve in thousands of ways.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Citizen service is an American responsibility which all Americans should embrace, and I ask your support for that endeavor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'd like to make just one last point about our national community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our economy is measured in numbers and statistics, and it's very important.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But the enduring worth of our nation lies in our shared values and our soaring spirit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So instead of cutting back on our modest efforts to support the arts and humanities, I believe we should stand by them and challenge our artists, musicians, and writers -- challenge our museums, libraries and theaters -- we should -- we should challenge all Americans in the arts and humanities to join with our fellow citizens to make the year 2000 a national celebration of the American spirit in every community -- a celebration of our common culture in the century that has passed, and in the new one to come in a new millennium, so that we can remain the world's beacon not only of liberty, but of creativity, long after the fireworks have faded.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: WORLD LEADERSHIP:  To prepare America for the 21st century we must master the forces of change in the world and keep American leadership strong and sure for an uncharted time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Fifty years ago, a farsighted America led in creating the institutions that secured victory in the Cold War and built a growing world economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As a result, today more people than ever embrace our ideals and share our interests.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Already, we have dismantled many of the blocs and barriers that divided our parents' world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For the first time, more people live under democracy than dictatorship, including every nation in our own hemisphere, but one -- and its day, too, will come.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, we stand at another moment of change and choice --and another time to be farsighted, to bring America 50 more years of security and prosperity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In this endeavor, our first task is to help to build, for the first time, an undivided, democratic Europe.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When Europe is stable, prosperous and at peace, America is more secure.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To that end, we must expand NATO by 1999, so that countries that were once our adversaries can become our allies.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: At the special NATO summit this summer, that is what we will begin to do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must strengthen NATO's Partnership for Peace with non-member allies.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we must build a stable partnership between NATO and a democratic Russia.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: An expanded NATO is good for America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And a Europe in which all democracies define their future not in terms of what they can do to each other, but in terms of what they can do together for the good of all -- that kind of Europe is good for America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Second, America must look to the East no less than to the West.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our security demands it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Americans fought three wars in Asia in this century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our prosperity requires it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: More than two million American jobs depend upon trade with Asia.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There, too, we are helping to shape an Asian Pacific community of cooperation, not conflict.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But let our progress there not mask the peril that remains.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Together with South Korea, we must advance peace talks with North Korea and bridge the Cold War's last divide.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I call on Congress to fund our share of the agreement under which North Korea must continue to freeze and then dismantle its nuclear weapons program.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must pursue a deeper dialogue with China -- for the sake of our interests and our ideals.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: An isolated China is not good for America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A China playing its proper role in the world is.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I will go to China, and I have invited China's President to come here, not because we agree on everything, but because engaging China is the best way to work on our common challenges like ending nuclear testing, and to deal frankly with our fundamental differences like human rights.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The American people must prosper in the global economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've worked hard to tear down trade barriers abroad so that we can create good jobs at home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I am proud to say that today, America is once again the most competitive nation and the number one exporter in the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now we must act to expand our exports, especially to Asia and Latin America -- two of the fastest growing regions on Earth -- or be left behind as these emerging economies forge new ties with other nations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is why we need the authority now to conclude new trade agreements that open markets to our goods and services even as we preserve our values.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need not shrink form the challenge of the global economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: After all, we have the best workers and the best products.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In a truly open market, we can out-compete anyone, anywhere on Earth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But this is about more than economics.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: By expanding trade, we can advance the cause of freedom and democracy around the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There is no better example of this truth than Latin America where democracy and open markets are on the march together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is why I will visit there in the spring to reinforce our important tie.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should all be proud that America led the effort to rescue our neighbor, Mexico, from its economic crises.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we should all be proud that last month Mexico repaid the United States -- three full years ahead of schedule -- with half a billion dollar profit to us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America must continue to be an unrelenting force for peace --- from the Middle East to Haiti, from Northern Ireland to Africa.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Taking reasonable risks for peace keeps us from being drawn into far more costly conflicts later.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With American leadership, the killing has stopped in Bosnia.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now the habits of peace must take hold.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The new NATO force will allow reconstruction and reconciliation to accelerate.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I ask Congress to continue its strong support for our troops.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They are doing a remarkable job there for America, and America must do right by them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Fifth, we must move strongly against new threats to our security.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the past four years, we agreed to ban -- we led the way to a worldwide agreement to ban nuclear testing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With Russia, we dramatically cut nuclear arsenals and we stopped targeting each others citizens.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are acting to prevent nuclear materials from falling into the wrong hands and to rid the world of land mines.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are working with other nations with renewed intensity to fight drug traffickers and to stop terrorists before they act, and hold them fully accountable if they do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, we must rise to a new test of leadership: ratifying the Chemical Weapons Convention.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Make no mistake about it, it will make our troops safer from chemical attack; it will help us to fight terrorism.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have no more important obligations -- especially in the wake of what we now know about the Gulf War.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This treaty has been bipartisan from the beginning -- supported by Republican and Democratic administrations and Republican and Democratic members of Congress -- and already approved by 68 nations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But if we do not act by April the 29th -- when this Convention goes into force, with or without us -- we will lose the chance to have Americans leading and enforcing this effort.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Together we must make the Chemical Weapons Convention law, so that at last we can begin to outlaw poison gas from the Earth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Finally, we must have the tools to meet all these challenges.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must maintain a strong and ready military.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must increase funding for weapons modernization by the year 2000, and we must take good care of our men and women in uniform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They are the world's finest.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must also renew our commitment to America's diplomacy, and pay our debts and dues to international financial institutions like the World Bank, and to a reforming United Nations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every dollar we devote to preventing conflicts, to promoting democracy, to stopping the spread of disease and starvation, brings a sure return in security and savings.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Yet international affairs spending today is just one percent of the federal budget -- a small fraction of what America invested in diplomacy to choose leadership over escapism at the start of the Cold War.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If America is to continue to lead the world, we here who lead America simply must find the will to pay our way.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A farsighted America moved the world to a better place over these last 50 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And so it can be for another 50 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But a shortsighted America will soon find its words falling on deaf ears all around the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Almost exactly 50 years ago, in the first winter of the Cold War, President Truman stood before a Republican Congress and called upon our country to meet its responsibilities of leadership.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we falter, we may endanger the peace of the world, and we shall surely endanger the welfare of this nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That Congress, led by Republicans like Senator Arthur Vandenberg, answered President Truman's call.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Together, they made the commitments that strengthened our country for 50 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now let us do the same.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us do what it takes to remain the indispensable nation -- to keep America strong, secure and prosperous for another 50 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: STRENGTH THROUGH DIVERSITY:  In the end, more than anything else, our world leadership grows out of the power of our example here at home, out of our ability to remain strong as one America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All over the world, people are being torn asunder by racial, ethnic, and religious conflicts that fuel fanaticism and terror.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are the world's most diverse democracy, and the world looks to us to show that it is possible to live and advance together across those kinds of differences.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America has always been a nation of immigrants.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: From the start, a steady stream of people, in search of freedom and opportunity, have left their own lands to make this land their home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We started as an experiment in democracy fueled by Europeans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have grown into an experiment in democratic diversity fueled by openness and promise.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, we must never, ever believe that our diversity is a weakness -- it is our greatest strength.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Americans speak every language, know every county.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: People on every continent can look to us and see the reflection of their own great potential -- and they always will, as long as we strive to give all of our citizens, whatever their background, an opportunity to achieve their own greatness.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We're not there yet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We still see evidence of abiding bigotry and intolerance, in ugly words and awful violence, in burned churches and bombed buildings.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must fight against this, in our country and in our hearts.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Just a few days before my second Inauguration, one of country's best known pastors, Reverend Robert Schuller, suggested that I read Isaiah 58:12.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations, and thou shalt be called, the repairer of the breach, the restorer of paths to dwell in.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I placed my hand on that verse when I took the oath of office, on behalf of all Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For no matter what our differences -- in our faiths, our backgrounds, our politics -- we must all be repairers of the breach.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to say a word about two other Americans who show us how.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Congressman Frank Tejeda was buried yesterday, a proud American whose family came from Mexico.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He was only 51 years old.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He was awarded the Silver Star, the Bronze Star and the Purple Heart, fighting for his country in Vietnam.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And he went on to serve Texas and America fighting for our future in this chamber.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are grateful for his service and honored that his mother, Lillie Tejeda, and his sister, Mary Alice, have come from Texas to be with us here tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we welcome you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Gary Locke, the newly elected Governor of Washington State, is the first Chinese-American governor in the history of our country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He's the proud son of two of the millions of Asian-American immigrants who have strengthened America with their hard work, family values and good citizenship.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He represents the future we can all achieve.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you, Governor, for being here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Please stand up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Reverend Schuller, Congressman Tejeda, Governor Locke, along with Kristin Tanner and Chris Getsla, Sue Winski and Dr.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Kristen Zarfos -- they're all Americans from different roots, whose lives reflect the best of what we can become when we are one America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We may not share a common past, but we surely do share a common future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: of every other strength we must build for this new century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Money cannot buy it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Power cannot compel it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Technology cannot create it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It can only come from the human spirit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America is far more than a place.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It is an idea, the most powerful idea in the history of nations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And all of us in this chamber, we are now the bearers of that idea, leading a great people into a new world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A child born tonight will have almost no memory of the 20th century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Everything that child will know about America will be because of what we do now to build a new century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We don't have a moment to waste.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tomorrow there will be just over 1,000 days until the year 2000.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: One thousand days to prepare our people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: One thousand days to work together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: One thousand days to build a bridge to a land of new promise.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, we have work to do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us seize those days and the century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you, God bless you and God bless America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. Vice President, members of the 105th Congress, distinguished guests, my fellow Americans:

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Since the last time we met in this chamber, America has lost two patriots and fine public servants.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Though they sat on opposite sides of the aisle, Representatives Walter Capps and Sonny Bono shared a deep love for this House and an unshakable commitment to improving the lives of all our people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the past few weeks they've both been eulogized.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I think we should begin by sending a message to their families and their friends that we celebrate their lives and give thanks for their service to our nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For 209 years it has been the President's duty to report to you on the state of the Union.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because of the hard work and high purpose of the American people, these are good times for America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have more than 14 million new jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The lowest unemployment in 24 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The lowest core inflation in 30 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Incomes are rising.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we have the highest homeownership in history.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Crime has dropped for a record five years in a row.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And the welfare rolls are at their lowest levels in 27 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our leadership in the world is unrivaled.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Ladies and gentlemen, the state of our Union is strong.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But with barely 700 days left in the 20th century, this is not a time to rest.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It is a time to build, to build the America within reach: an America where everybody has a chance to get ahead with hard work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Where every citizen can live in a safe community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Where families are strong, schools are good and all young people can go to college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: An America where scientists find cures for diseases from diabetes to Alzheimer's to AIDS.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: An America where every child can stretch a hand across a keyboard and reach every book ever written, every painting ever painted, every symphony ever composed.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Where government provides opportunity and citizens honor the responsibility to give something back to their communities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: An America which leads the world to new heights of peace and prosperity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is the America we have begun to build.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is the America we can leave to our children -- if we join together to finish the work at hand.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us strengthen our nation for the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Rarely have Americans lived through so much change, in so many ways, in so short a time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Quietly, but with gathering force, the ground has shifted beneath our feet as we have moved into an Information Age, a global economy, a truly new world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For five years now we have met the challenge of these changes as Americans have at every turning point -- by renewing the very idea of America: widening the circle of opportunity, deepening the meaning of our freedom, forging a more perfect union.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We shaped a new kind of government for the Information Age.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I thank the Vice President for his leadership and the Congress for its support in building a government that is leaner, more flexible, a catalyst for new ideas -- and most of all, a government that gives the American people the tools they need to make the most of their own lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have moved past the sterile debate between those who say government is the enemy and those who say government is the answer.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, we have found a third way.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have the smallest government in 35 years, but a more progressive one.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have a smaller government, but a stronger nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are moving steadily toward an even stronger America in the 21st century: an economy that offers opportunity, a society rooted in responsibility and a nation that lives as a community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: BALANCED BUDGET:  First, Americans in this chamber and across our nation have pursued a new strategy for prosperity: fiscal discipline to cut interest rates and spur growth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Investments in education and skills, in science and technology and transportation, to prepare our people for the new economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: New markets for American products and American workers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When I took office, the deficit for 1998 was projected to be $357 billion, and heading higher.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, our deficit is projected to be $10 billion, and heading lower.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For three decades, six Presidents have come before you to warn of the damage deficits pose to our nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I come before you to announce that the federal deficit -- once so incomprehensibly large that it had 11 zeroes -- will be, simply, zero.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I will submit to Congress for 1999 the first balanced budget in 30 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And if we hold fast to fiscal discipline, we may balance the budget this year -- four years ahead of schedule.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You can all be proud of that, because turning a sea of red ink into black is no miracle.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It is the product of hard work by the American people, and of two visionary actions in Congress -- the courageous vote in 1993 that led to a cut in the deficit of 90 percent and the truly historic bipartisan balanced budget agreement passed by this Congress.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Here's the really good news: If we maintain our resolve, we will produce balanced budgets as far as the eye can see.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must not go back to unwise spending or untargeted tax cuts that risk reopening the deficit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, together we enacted targeted tax cuts so that the typical middle class family will now have the lowest tax rates in 20 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My plan to balance the budget next year includes both new investments and new tax cuts targeted to the needs of working families: for education, for child care, for the environment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But whether the issue is tax cuts or spending, I ask all of you to meet this test: Approve only those priorities that can actually be accomplished without adding a dime to the deficit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: SOCIAL SECURITY:  Now, if we balance the budget for next year, it is projected that we'll then have a sizeable surplus in the years that immediately follow.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: What should we do with this projected surplus?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have a simple four-word answer: Save Social Security first.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I propose that we reserve 100 percent of the surplus -- that's every penny of any surplus -- until we have taken all the necessary measures to strengthen the Social Security system for the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us say to all Americans watching tonight -- whether you're 70 or 50, or whether you just started paying into the system -- Social Security will be there when you need it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us make this commitment: Social Security first.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's do that together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I also want to say that all the American people who are watching us tonight should be invited to join in this discussion, in facing these issues squarely, and forming a true consensus on how we should proceed.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We'll start by conducting nonpartisan forums in every region of the country -- and I hope that lawmakers of both parties will participate.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We'll hold a White House Conference on Social Security in December.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And one year from now I will convene the leaders of Congress to craft historic, bipartisan legislation to achieve a landmark for our generation -- a Social Security system that is strong in the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: MINIMUM WAGE:  In an economy that honors opportunity, all Americans must be able to reap the rewards of prosperity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because these times are good, we can afford to take one simple, sensible step to help millions of workers struggling to provide for their families: We should raise the minimum wage.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: EDUCATION:  The Information Age is, first and foremost, an education age, in which education must start at birth and continue throughout a lifetime.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, from this podium, I said that education has to be our highest priority.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I laid out a 10-point plan to move us forward and urged all of us to let politics stop at the schoolhouse door.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Since then, this Congress, across party lines, and the American people have responded, in the most important year for education in a generation -- expanding public school choice, opening the way to 3,000 new charter schools, working to connect every classroom in the country to the Information Superhighway, committing to expand Head Start to a million children, launching America Reads, sending literally thousands of college students into our elementary schools to make sure all our eight-year-olds can read.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year I proposed, and you passed, 220,000 new Pell Grant scholarships for deserving students.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Student loans, already less expensive and easier to repay, now you get to deduct the interest.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Families all over America now can put their savings into new tax-free education IRAs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And this year, for the first two years of college, families will get a $1,500 tax credit -- a HOPE Scholarship that will cover the cost of most community college tuition.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And for junior and senior year, graduate school, and job training, there is a lifetime learning credit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You did that and you should be very proud of it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: COLLEGE FOR ALL:  And because of these actions, I have something to say to every family listening to us tonight: Your children can go on to college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If you know a child from a poor family, tell her not to give up -- she can go on to college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If you know a young couple struggling with bills, worried they won't be able to send their children to college, tell them not to give up -- their children can go on to college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If you know somebody who's caught in a dead-end job and afraid he can't afford the classes necessary to get better jobs for the rest of his life, tell him not to give up -- he can go on to college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because of the things that have been done, we can make college as universal in the 21st century as high school is today.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And, my friends, that will change the face and future of America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have opened wide the doors of the world's best system of higher education.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now we must make our public elementary and secondary schools the world's best as well by raising standards, raising expectations, and raising accountability.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thanks to the actions of this Congress last year, we will soon have, for the very first time, a voluntary national test based on national standards in 4th grade reading and 8th grade math.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Parents have a right to know whether their children are mastering the basics.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And every parent already knows the key: good teachers and small classes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: SMALLER CLASSROOMS:  Tonight, I propose the first ever national effort to reduce class size in the early grades.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My balanced budget will help to hire 100,000 new teachers who have passed a state competency test.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, with these teachers -- listen -- with these teachers, we will actually be able to reduce class size in the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd grades to an average of 18 students a class, all across America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now if I've got the math right, more teachers teaching smaller classes requires more classrooms.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I also propose a school construction tax cut to help communities modernize or build 5,000 schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must also demand greater accountability.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When we promote a child from grade to grade who hasn't mastered the work, we don't do that child any favors.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It is time to end social promotion in America's schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, in Chicago, they made that decision -- not to hold our children back, but to lift them up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Chicago stopped social promotion, and started mandatory summer school, to help students who are behind to catch up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I propose to help other communities follow Chicago's lead.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's say to them: Stop promoting children who don't learn, and we will give you the tools to make sure they do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I also ask this Congress to support our efforts to enlist colleges and universities to reach out to disadvantaged children, starting in the 6th grade, so that they can get the guidance and hope they need so they can know that they, too, will be able to go on to college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: GLOBAL ECONOMICS:  As we enter the 21st century, the global economy requires us to seek opportunity not just at home, but in all the markets of the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must shape this global economy, not shrink from it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, record high exports account for fully one-third of our economic growth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to keep them going, because that's the way to keep America growing and to advance a safer, more stable world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now all of you know whatever your views are that I think this a great opportunity for America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I know there is opposition to more comprehensive trade agreements.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have listened carefully and I believe that the opposition is rooted in two fears: first, that our trading partners will have lower environmental and labor standards which will give them an unfair advantage in our market and do their own people no favors, even if there's more business.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And, second, that if we have more trade, more of our workers will lose their jobs and have to start over.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think we should seek to advance worker and environmental standards around the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have made it abundantly clear that it should be a part of our trade agenda.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we cannot influence other countries' decisions if we send them a message that we're backing away from trade with them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, I will send legislation to Congress, and ask other nations to join us, to fight the most intolerable labor practice of all -- abusive child labor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: JOB TRAINING:  We should also offer help and hope to those Americans temporarily left behind by the global marketplace or by the march of technology, which may have nothing to do with trade.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why we have more than doubled funding for training dislocated workers since 1993 -- and if my new budget is adopted, we will triple funding.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why we must do more, and more quickly, to help workers who lose their jobs for whatever reason.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, we help communities in a special way when their military base closes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We ought to help them in the same way if their factory closes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Again, I ask the Congress to continue its bipartisan work to consolidate the tangle of training programs we have today into one single G.I. Bill for Workers, a simple skills grant so people can, on their own, move quickly to new jobs, to higher incomes and brighter futures.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, we all know in every way in life change is not always easy, but we have to decide whether we're going to try to hold it back and hide from it or reap its benefits.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And remember the big picture here: While we've been entering into hundreds of new trade agreements, we've been creating millions of new jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So this year we will forge new partnerships with Latin America, Asia, and Europe.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we should pass the new African Trade Act -- it has bipartisan support.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: FAST TRACK:  I will also renew my request for the fast track negotiating authority necessary to open more new markets, create more new jobs, which every President has had for two decades.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, whether we like it or not, in ways that are mostly positive, the world's economies are more and more interconnected and interdependent.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, an economic crisis anywhere can affect economies everywhere.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Recent months have brought serious financial problems to Thailand, Indonesia, South Korea, and beyond.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, why should Americans be concerned about this?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: First, these countries are our customers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If they sink into recession, they won't be able to buy the goods we'd like to sell them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Second, they're also our competitors.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So if their currencies lose their value and go down, then the price of their goods will drop, flooding our market and others with much cheaper goods, which makes it a lot tougher for our people to compete.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And, finally, they are our strategic partners.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Their stability bolsters our security.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The American economy remains sound and strong, and I want to keep it that way.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But because the turmoil in Asia will have an impact on all the world's economies, including ours, making that negative impact as small as possible is the right thing to do for America -- and the right thing to do for a safer world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our policy is clear: No nation can recover if it does not reform itself.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But when nations are willing to undertake serious economic reform, we should help them do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I call on Congress to renew America's commitment to the International Monetary Fund.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I think we should say to all the people we're trying to represent here that preparing for a far-off storm that may reach our shores is far wiser than ignoring the thunder until the clouds are just overhead.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: WELFARE TO WORK:  A strong nation rests on the rock of responsibility.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A society rooted in responsibility must first promote the value of work, not welfare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can be proud that after decades of finger-pointing and failure, together we ended the old welfare system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we're now we replacing welfare checks with paychecks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, after a record four-year decline in welfare rolls, I challenged our nation to move 2 million more Americans off welfare by the year 2000.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'm pleased to report we have also met that goal, two full years ahead of schedule.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is a grand achievement, the sum of many acts of individual courage, persistence and hope.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For 13 years, Elaine Kinslow of Indianapolis, Indiana, was on and off welfare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, she's a dispatcher with the a van company.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: She's saved enough money to move her family into a good neighborhood, and she's helping other welfare recipients go to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Elaine Kinslow and all those like her are the real heroes of the welfare revolution.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There are millions like her all across America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I'm happy she could join the First Lady tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Elaine, we're very proud of you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Please stand up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We still have a lot more to do, all of us, to make welfare reform a success -- providing child care, helping families move closer to available jobs, challenging more companies to join our welfare-to-work partnership, increasing child support collections from deadbeat parents who have a duty to support their own children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I also want to thank Congress for restoring some of the benefits to immigrants who are here legally and working hard -- and I hope you will finish that job this year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: HEALTH CARE:  We have to make it possible for all hard-working families to meet their most important responsibilities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Two years ago, we helped guarantee that Americans can keep their health insurance when they change jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, we extended health care to up to 5 million children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, I challenge Congress to take the next historic steps.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: One hundred sixty million of our fellow citizens are in managed care plans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These plans save money and they can improve care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But medical decisions ought to be made by medical doctors, not insurance company accountants.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I urge this Congress to reach across the aisle and write into law a Consumer Bill of Rights that says this: You have the right to know all your medical options, not just the cheapest.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You have the right to choose the doctor you want for the care you need.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You have the right to emergency room care, wherever and whenever you need it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You have the right to keep your medical records confidential.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, traditional care or managed care, every American deserves quality care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Millions of Americans between the ages of 55 and 65 have lost their health insurance.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Some are retired.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Some are laid off.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Some lose their coverage when their spouses retire.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: After a lifetime of work, they are left with nowhere to turn.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I ask the Congress: Let these hard-working Americans buy into the Medicare system.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It won't add a dime to the deficit -- but the peace of mind it will provide will be priceless.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: TEEN SMOKING:  Next, we must help parents protect their children from the gravest health threat that they face: an epidemic of teen smoking, spread by multimillion-dollar marketing campaigns.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I challenge Congress: Let's pass bipartisan, comprehensive legislation that improve public health, protect our tobacco farmers, and change the way tobacco companies do business forever.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's do what it takes to bring teen smoking down.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's raise the price of cigarettes by up to $1.50 a pack over the next 10 years, with penalties on the tobacco industry if it keeps marketing to our children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now tomorrow, like every day, 3,000 children will start smoking, and 1,000 will die early as a result.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let this Congress be remembered as the Congress that saved their lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the new economy, most parents work harder than ever.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They face a constant struggle to balance their obligations to be good workers -- and their even more important obligations to be good parents.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The Family and Medical Leave Act was the very first bill I was privileged to sign into law as President in 1993.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Since then, about 15 million people have taken advantage of it, and I've met a lot of them all across this country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to extend that law to cover 10 million more workers, and to give parents time off when they have to go see their children's teachers or take them to the doctor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: CHILD CARE:  Child care is the next frontier we must face to enable people to succeed at home and at work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, I co-hosted the very first White House Conference on Child Care with one of our foremost experts, America's First Lady.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: From all corners of America, we heard the same message, without regard to region or income or political affiliation: We've got to raise the quality of child care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've got to make it safer.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've got to make it more affordable.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So here's my plan: Help families to pay for child care for a million more children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Scholarships and background checks for child care workers, and a new emphasis on early learning.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tax credits for businesses that provide child care for their employees.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And a larger child care tax credit for working families.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, if you pass my plan, what this means is that a family of four with an income of $35,000 and high child care costs will no longer pay a single penny of federal income tax.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, I think this is such a big issue with me because of my own personal experience.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have often wondered how my mother, when she was a young widow, would have been able to go away to school and get an education and come back and support me if my grandparents hadn't been able to take care of me.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: She and I were really very lucky.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: How many other families have never had that same opportunity?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we do know what the answer should be: Not a single American family should ever have to choose between the job they need and the child they love.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: LAW ENFORCEMENT:  A society rooted in responsibility must provide safe streets, safe schools, and safe neighborhoods.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We pursued a strategy of more police, tougher punishment, smarter prevention, with crime-fighting partnerships with local law enforcement and citizen groups, where the rubber hits the road.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I can report to you tonight that it's working.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Violent crime is down, robbery is down, assault is down, burglary is down -- for five years in a row, all across America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, we need to finish the job of putting 100,000 more police on our streets.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Again, I ask Congress to pass a juvenile crime bill that provides more prosecutors and probation officers, to crack down on gangs and guns and drugs, and bar violent juveniles from buying guns for life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I ask you to dramatically expand our support for after-school programs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think every American should know that most juvenile crime is committed between the hours of 3:00 in the afternoon and 8:00 at night.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can keep so many of our children out of trouble in the first place if we give them someplace to go other than the streets, and we ought to do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Drug use is on the decline.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I thank General McCaffrey for his leadership.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I thank this Congress for passing the largest antidrug budget in history.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now I ask you to join me in a ground-breaking effort to hire 1,000 new border patrol agents and to deploy the most sophisticated available new technologies to help close the door on drugs at our borders.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Police, prosecutors, and prevention programs, as good as they are, they can't work if our court system doesn't work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today there are large number of vacancies in the federal courts.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Here is what the Chief Justice of the United States wrote: Judicial vacancies cannot remain at such high levels indefinitely without eroding the quality of justice.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I simply ask the United States Senate to heed this plea, and vote on the highly qualified judicial nominees before you, up or down.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: FOREIGN FRIENDS AND FOES:  We must exercise responsibility not just at home, but around the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: On the eve of a new century, we have the power and the duty to build a new era of peace and security.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But, make no mistake about it, today's possibilities are not tomorrow's guarantees.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America must stand against the poisoned appeals of extreme nationalism.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must combat an unholy axis of new threats from terrorists, international criminals and drug traffickers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These 21st century predators feed on technology and the free flow of information and ideas and people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And they will be all the more lethal if weapons of mass destruction fall into their hands.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To meet these challenges, we are helping to write international rules of the road for the 21st century, protecting those who join the family of nations and isolating those who do not.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Within days, I will ask the Senate for its advice and consent to make Hungary, Poland, and the Czech Republic the newest members of NATO.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For 50 years, NATO contained communism and kept America and Europe secure.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now these three formerly communist countries have said yes to democracy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask the Senate to say yes to them -- our new allies.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: By taking in new members and working closely with new partners, including Russia and Ukraine, NATO can help to assure that Europe is a stronghold for peace in the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: BOSNIA MISSION:  Next, I will ask Congress to continue its support for our troops and their mission in Bosnia.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This Christmas, Hillary and I traveled to Sarajevo with Senator and Mrs.Dole and a bipartisan congressional delegation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We saw children playing in the streets, where two years ago they were hiding from snipers and shells.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The shops are filled with food.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The cafes were alive with conversation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The progress there is unmistakable -- but it is not yet irreversible.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To take firm root, Bosnia's fragile peace still needs the support of American and allied troops when the current NATO mission ends in June.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think Senator Dole actually said it best.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is like being ahead in the 4th quarter of a football game.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I wish all of you could have seen our troops in Tuzla.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They're very proud of what they're doing in Bosnia.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we're all very proud of them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: One of those brave soldiers is sitting with the First Lady tonight -- Army Sergeant Michael Tolbert.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: His father was a decorated Vietnam vet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: After college in Colorado, he joined the Army.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, he led an infantry unit that stopped mob of extremists from taking over a radio station that is a voice of democracy and tolerance in Bosnia.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you very much, Sergeant, for what you represent.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In Bosnia and around the world, our men and women in uniform always do their mission well.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our mission must be to keep them well-trained and ready, to improve their quality of life, and to provide the 21st century weapons they need to defeat any enemy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: WEAPONS TREATIES:  I ask Congress to join me in pursuing an ambitious agenda to reduce the serious threat of weapons of mass destruction.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, four decades after it was first proposed by President Eisenhower, a comprehensive nuclear test ban is within reach.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: By ending nuclear testing we can help to prevent the development of new and more dangerous weapons and make it more difficult for non-nuclear states to build them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I am pleased to announce four former Chairmen of the Joint Chiefs of Staff -- Generals John Shalikashvili, Colin Powell, and David Jones, and Admiral William Crowe -- have endorsed this treaty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I ask the Senate to approve it this year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Together, we also must also confront the new hazards of chemical and biological weapons, and the outlaw states, terrorists and organized criminals seeking to acquire them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: SADDAM HUSSEIN:  Saddam Hussein has spent the better part of this decade, and much of his nation's wealth, not on providing for the Iraqi people, but on developing nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons -- and the missiles to deliver them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The United Nations weapons inspectors have done a truly remarkable job, finding and destroying more of Iraq's arsenal than was destroyed during the entire Gulf War.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now Saddam Hussein wants to stop them from completing their mission.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: nan

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And when I say to him: You have used weapons of mass destruction before.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are determined to deny you the capacity to use them again.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, the Senate ratified the Chemical Weapons Convention to protect our soldiers and citizens from poison gas.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now we must act to prevent the use of disease as a weapon of war and terror.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The Biological Weapons Convention has been in effect for 23 years now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The rules are good, but the enforcement is weak.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must strengthen it with a new international inspection system to detect and deter cheating.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the months ahead, I will pursue our security strategy with old allies in Asia and Europe, and new partners from Africa to India and Pakistan, from South America to China.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And from Belfast, to Korea to the Middle East, America will continue to stand with those who stand for peace.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: UNITED NATIONS:  Finally, it's long past time to make good on our debt to the United Nations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: More and more, we are working with other nations to achieve common goals.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we want America to lead, we've got to set a good example.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As we see so clearly in Bosnia, allies who share our goals can also share our burdens.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In this new era, our freedom and independence are actually enriched, not weakened, by our increasing interdependence with other nations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we have to do our part.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To all of you I say it is a journey we can only make together -- living as one community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: CAMPAIGN FINANCE:  First, we have to continue to reform our government -- the instrument of our national community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Everyone knows elections have become too expensive, fueling a fundraising arms race.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, by March 6th, at long last the Senate will actually vote on bipartisan campaign finance reform proposed by Senators McCain and Feingold.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's be clear: A vote against McCain and Feingold is a vote for soft money and for the status quo.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to strengthen our democracy and pass campaign finance reform this year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But at least equally important, we have to address the real reason for the explosion in campaign costs -- the high cost of media advertising.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To the folks watching at home, those were the groans of pain in the audience.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I will formally request that the Federal Communications Commission act to provide free or reduced-cost television time for candidates who observe spending limits voluntarily.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The airwaves are a public trust, and broadcasters also have to help us in this effort to strengthen our democracy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Under the leadership of Vice President Gore, we've reduced the federal payroll by 300,000 workers, cut 16,000 pages of regulation, eliminated hundreds of programs and improved the operations of virtually every government agency.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we can do more.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: IRS OVERHAUL:  Like every taxpayer, I'm outraged by the reports of abuses by the IRS.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need some changes there -- new citizen advocacy panels, a stronger taxpayer advocate, phone lines open 24 hours a day, relief for innocent taxpayers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, by an overwhelming bipartisan margin, the House of Representatives passed sweeping IRS reforms.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This bill must not now languish in the Senate.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight I ask the Senate: follow the House, pass the bipartisan package as your first order of business.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: on, so I'll be out of trouble.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A nation that lives as a community must value all its communities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For the past five years, we have worked to bring the spark of private enterprise to inner city and poor rural areas -- with community development banks, more commercial loans in the poor neighborhoods, cleanup of polluted sites for development.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Under the continued leadership of the Vice President, we propose to triple the number of empowerment zones, to give business incentives to invest in those areas.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should also should give poor families more help to move into homes of their own, and we should use tax cuts to spur the construction of more low-income housing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, this Congress took strong action to help the District of Columbia.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us renew our resolve to make our capital city a great city for all who live and visit here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our cities are the vibrant hubs of great metropolitan areas.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They are still the gateways for new immigrants, from every continent, who come here to work for their own American Dreams.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's keep our cities going strong into the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They're a very important part of our future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES:  Our communities are only as healthy as the air our children breathe, the water they drink, the Earth they will inherit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, we put in place the toughest-ever controls on smog and soot.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We moved to protect Yellowstone, the Everglades, Lake Tahoe.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We expanded every community's right to know about the toxins that threaten their children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Just yesterday, our food safety plan took effect, using new science to protect consumers from dangers like E. coli and salmonella.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I ask you to join me in launching a new Clean Water Initiative, a far-reaching effort to clean our rivers, our lakes, our coastal waters for our children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our overriding environmental challenge tonight is the worldwide problem of climate change, global warming, the gathering crisis that requires worldwide action.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The vast majority of scientists have concluded unequivocally that if we don't reduce the emission of greenhouse gases, at some point in the next century we'll disrupt our climate and put our children and grandchildren at risk.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This past December, America led the world to reach a historic agreement committing our nation to reduce greenhouse gas emissions through market forces, new technologies, energy efficiency.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have it in our power to act right here, right now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I propose $6 billion in tax cuts and research and development to encourage innovation, renewable energy, fuel-efficient cars, energy-efficient homes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every time we have acted to heal our environment, pessimists have told us it would hurt the economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Well, today our economy is the strongest in a generation, and our environment is the cleanest in a generation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have always found a way to clean the environment and grow the economy at the same time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And when it comes to global warming, we'll do it again.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: RACIAL DISCRIMINATION:  Finally, community means living by the defining American value -- the ideal heard round the world that we are all created equal.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Throughout our history, we haven't always honored that ideal and we've never fully lived up to it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Often it's easier to believe that our differences matter more than what we have in common.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It may be easier, but it's wrong.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: What we have to do in our day and generation to make sure that America becomes truly one nation -- what do we have to do?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We're becoming more and more and more diverse.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Do you believe we can become one nation?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The answer cannot be to dwell on our differences, but to build on our shared values.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we all cherish family and faith, freedom and responsibility.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We all want our children to grow up in a world where their talents are matched by their opportunities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I've launched this national initiative on race to help us recognize our common interests and to bridge the opportunity gaps that are keeping us from becoming one America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us begin by recognizing what we still must overcome.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Discrimination against any American is un-American.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must vigorously enforce the laws that make it illegal.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask your help to end the backlog at the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Sixty thousand of our fellow citizens are waiting in line for justice, and we should act now to end their wait.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should also recognize that the greatest progress we can make toward building one America lies in the progress we make for all Americans, without regard to race.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When we open the doors of college to all Americans, when we rid all our streets of crime, when there are jobs available to people from all our neighborhoods, when we make sure all parents have the child care they need, we're helping to build one nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We, in this chamber and in this government, must do all we can to address the continuing American challenge to build one America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we'll only move forward if all our fellow citizens -- including every one of you at home watching tonight -- is also committed to this cause.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must work together, learn together, live together, serve together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: On the forge of common enterprise Americans of all backgrounds can hammer out a common identity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We see it today in the United States military, in the Peace Corps, in AmeriCorps.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Wherever people of all races and backgrounds come together in a shared endeavor and get a fair chance, we do just fine.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With shared values and meaningful opportunities and honest communication and citizen service, we can unite a diverse people in freedom and mutual respect.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are many.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must be one.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In that spirit, let us lift our eyes to the new millennium.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: How will we mark that passage?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It just happens once every thousand years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, Hillary and I launched the White House Millennium Program to promote America's creativity and innovation, and to preserve our heritage and culture into the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our culture lives in every community, and every community has places of historic value that tell our stories as Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should protect them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I am proposing a public-private partnership to advance our arts and humanities, and to celebrate the millennium by saving American's treasures, great and small.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH:  And while we honor the past, let us imagine the future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Think about this -- the entire store of human knowledge now doubles every five years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the 1980s, scientists identified the gene causing cystic fibrosis -- it took nine years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, scientists located the gene that causes Parkinson's Disease -- in only nine days.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: will offer a road map for prevention of illnesses throughout a lifetime.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Soon we'll be able to carry all the phone calls on Mother's Day on a single strand of fiber the width of a human hair.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A child born in 1998 may well live to see the 22nd century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, as part of our gift to the millennium, I propose a 21st Century Research Fund for path-breaking scientific inquiry -- the largest funding increase in history for the National Institutes of Health, the National Science Foundation, the National Cancer Institute.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have already discovered genes for breast cancer and diabetes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to support this initiative so ours will be the generation that finally wins the war against cancer, and begins a revolution in our fight against all deadly diseases.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As important as all this scientific progress is, we must continue to see that science serves humanity, not the other way around.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must prevent the misuse of genetic tests to discriminate against any American.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we must ratify the ethical consensus of the scientific and religious communities, and ban the cloning of human beings.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should enable all the world's people to explore the far reaches of cyberspace.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Think of this -- the first time I made a State of the Union speech to you, only a handful of physicists used the World Wide Web.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Literally, just a handful of people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, in schools, in libraries, homes and businesses, millions and millions of Americans surf the Net every day.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must give parents the tools they need to help protect their children from inappropriate material on the Internet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we also must make sure that we protect the exploding global commercial potential of the Internet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can do the kinds of things that we need to do and still protect our kids.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For one thing, I ask Congress to step up support for building the next generation Internet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's getting kind of clogged, you know.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And the next generation Internet will operate at speeds up to a thousand times faster than today.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: SPACE EXPLORATION:  Even as we explore this inner space in a new millennium we're going to open new frontiers in outer space.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Throughout all history, humankind has had only one place to call home -- our planet Earth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Beginning this year, 1998, men and women from 16 countries will build a foothold in the heavens -- the international space station.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With its vast expanses, scientists and engineers will actually set sail on an unchartered sea of limitless mystery and unlimited potential.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And this October, a true American hero, a veteran pilot of 149 combat missions and one, five-hour space flight that changed the world, will return to the heavens.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Godspeed, John Glenn.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: John, you will carry with you America's hopes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
