text: And on your uniform, once again, you will carry America's flag, marking the unbroken connection between the deeds of America's past and the daring of America's future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Nearly 200 years ago, a tattered flag, its broad stripes and bright stars still gleaming through the smoke of a fierce battle, moved Francis Scott Key to scribble a few words on the back of an envelope -- the words that became our national anthem.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, that Start Spangled Banner, along with the Declaration of Independence, the Constitution and the Bill of Rights, are on display just a short walk from here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They are America's treasures and we must also save them for the ages.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask all Americans to support our project to restore all our treasures so that the generations of the 21st century can see for themselves the images and the words that are the old and continuing glory of America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let that be our gift to the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: God bless you, and God bless the United States.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. Vice President, members of Congress, honored guests, my fellow Americans: Tonight, I have the honor of reporting to you on the State of the Union.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let me begin by saluting the new Speaker of the House, and thanking him, especially tonight, for extending an invitation to two special guests sitting in the gallery with Mrs. Hastert: Lyn Gibson and Wei Ling Chestnut are the widows of the two brave Capitol Hill police officers who gave their lives to defend freedom's house.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Mr. Speaker, at your swearing-in, you asked us all to work together in a spirit of civility and bipartisanship.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Mr. Speaker, let's do exactly that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I stand before you to report that America has created the longest peacetime economic expansion in our history -- with nearly 18 million new jobs, wages rising at more than twice the rate of inflation, the highest home ownership in history, the smallest welfare rolls in 30 years, and the lowest peacetime unemployment since 1957.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For the first time in three decades, the budget is balanced.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: From a deficit of $290 billion in 1992, we had a surplus of $70 billion last year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And now we are on course for budget surpluses for the next 25 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thanks to the pioneering leadership of all of you, we have the lowest violent crime rate in a quarter century and the cleanest environment in a quarter century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America is a strong force for peace from Northern Ireland to Bosnia to the Middle East.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thanks to the leadership of Vice President Gore, we have a government for the Information Age.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Once again, a government that is a progressive instrument of the common good, rooted in our oldest values of opportunity, responsibility and community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Devoted to fiscal responsibility.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Determined to give our people the tools they need to make the most of their own lives in the 21st century -- a 21st century government for 21st century America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, I stand before you tonight to report that the state of our union is strong.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America is working again.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The promise of our future is limitless.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we cannot realize that promise if we allow the hum of our prosperity to lull us into complacency.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: How we fare as a nation far into the 21st century depends upon what we do as a nation today.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So with our budget surplus growing, our economy expanding, our confidence rising, now is the moment for this generation to meet our historic responsibility to the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our fiscal discipline gives us an unsurpassed opportunity to address a remarkable new challenge -- the aging of America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: THE COMING 'SENIOR BOOM': With the number of elderly Americans set to double by 2030, the baby boom will become a senior boom.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So first, and above all, we must save Social Security for the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Early in this century, being old meant being poor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Even today, without Social Security, half our nation's elderly would be forced into poverty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, Social Security is strong.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But by 2013, payroll taxes will no longer be sufficient to cover monthly payments.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: By 2032, the trust fund will be exhausted and Social Security will be unable to pay the full benefits older Americans have been promised.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The best way to keep Social Security a rock-solid guarantee is not to make drastic cuts in benefits, not to raise payroll tax rates, not to drain resources from Social Security in the name of saving it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Instead, I propose that we make an historic decision to invest the surplus to save Social Security.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Specifically, I propose that we commit 60 percent of the budget surplus for the next 15 years to Social Security, investing a small portion in the private sector, just as any private or state government pension would do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This will earn a higher return and keep Social Security sound for 55 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we must aim higher.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should put Social Security on a sound footing for the next 75 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should reduce poverty among elderly women, who are nearly twice as likely to be poor as our other seniors.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we should eliminate the limits on what seniors on Social Security can earn.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, these changes will require difficult but fully achievable choices over and above the dedication of the surplus.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They must be made on a bipartisan basis.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They should be made this year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So let me say to you tonight, I reach out my hand to all of you in both Houses, in both parties, and ask that we join together in saying to the American people: We will save Social Security now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, last year we wisely reserved all of the surplus until we knew what it would take to save Social Security.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Again, I say, we shouldn't spend any of it -- not any of it -- until after Social Security is truly saved.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: First things first.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Second, once we have saved Social Security, we must fulfill our obligation to save and improve Medicare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Already, we have extended the life of the Medicare trust fund by 10 years -- but we should extend it for at least another decade.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I propose that we use one out of every $6 in the surplus for the next 15 years to guarantee the soundness of Medicare until the year 2020.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But, again, we should aim higher.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must be willing to work in a bipartisan way and look at new ideas, including the upcoming report of the bipartisan Medicare Commission.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we work together, we can secure Medicare for the next two decades and cover the greatest growing need of seniors -- affordable prescription drugs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Third, we must help all Americans, from their first day on the job -- to save, to invest, to create wealth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: From its beginning, Americans have supplemented Social Security with private pensions and savings.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Yet, today, millions of people retire with little to live on other than Social Security.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Americans living longer than ever simply must save more than ever.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: NEW PENSION INITIATIVE:  Therefore, in addition to saving Social Security and Medicare, I propose a new pension initiative for retirement security in the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I propose that we use a little over 11 percent of the surplus to establish universal savings accounts -- USA accounts -- to give all Americans the means to save.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With these new accounts Americans can invest as they choose and receive funds to match a portion of their savings, with extra help for those least able to save.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: USA accounts will help all Americans to share in our nation's wealth and to enjoy a more secure retirement.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to support them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Fourth, we must invest in long-term care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I propose a tax credit of $1,000 for the aged, ailing or disabled, and the families who care for them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Long-term care will become a bigger and bigger challenge with the aging of America, and we must do more to help our families deal with it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I was born in 1946, the first year of the baby boom.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I can tell you that one of the greatest concerns of our generation is our absolute determination not to let our growing old place an intolerable burden on our children and their ability to raise our grandchildren.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our economic success and our fiscal discipline now give us an opportunity to lift that burden from their shoulders, and we should take it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Saving Social Security, Medicare, creating USA accounts -- this is the right way to use the surplus.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we do so -- if we do so -- we will still have resources to meet critical needs in education and defense.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I want to point out that this proposal is fiscally sound.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Listen to this: If we set aside 60 percent of the surplus for Social Security and 16 percent for Medicare, over the next 15 years, that saving will achieve the lowest level of publicly-held debt since right before World War I, in 1917.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So with these four measures -- saving Social Security, strengthening Medicare, establishing the USA accounts, supporting long-term care -- we can begin to meet our generation's historic responsibility to establish true security for 21st century seniors.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, there are more children from more diverse backgrounds in our public schools than at any time in our history.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Their education must provide the knowledge and nurture the creativity that will allow our entire nation to thrive in the new economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today we can say something we couldn't say six years ago: With tax credits and more affordable student loans, with more work-study grants and more Pell grants, with education IRAs and the new HOPE Scholarship tax cut that more than five million Americans will receive this year, we have finally opened the doors of college to all Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With our support, nearly every state has set higher academic standards for public schools, and a voluntary national test is being developed to measure the progress of our students.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With over $1 billion in discounts available this year, we are well on our way to our goal of connecting every classroom and library to the Internet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last fall, you passed our proposal to start hiring 100,000 new teachers to reduce class size in the early grades.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now I ask you to finish the job.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, our children are doing better.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: SAT scores are up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Math scores have risen in nearly all grades.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But there's a problem.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: While our 4th graders outperform their peers in other countries in math and science, our 8th graders are around average, and our 12th graders rank near the bottom.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must do better.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, each year the national government invests more than $15 billion in our public schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I believe we must change the way we invest that money, to support what works and to stop supporting what does not work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: ACCOUNTABILITY IN EDUCATION:  First, later this year, I will send to Congress a plan that, for the first time, holds states and school districts accountable for progress and rewards them for results.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My Education Accountability Act will require every school district receiving federal help to take the following five steps.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: First, all schools must end social promotion.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, no child should graduate from high school with a diploma he or she can't read.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We do our children no favors when we allow them to pass from grade to grade without mastering the material.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we can't just hold students back because the system fails them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So my balanced budget triples the funding for summer school and after-school programs, to keep a million children learning.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If you doubt this will work, just look at Chicago, which ended social promotion and made summer school mandatory for those who don't master the basics.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Math and reading scores are up three years running -- with some of the biggest gains in some of the poorest neighborhoods.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It will work, and we should do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Second, all states and school districts must turn around their worst-performing schools -- or shut them down.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's the policy established in North Carolina by Governor Jim Hunt.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: North Carolina made the biggest gains in test scores in the nation last year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our budget includes $200 million to help states turn around their own failing schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Third, all states and school districts must be held responsible for the quality of their teachers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The great majority of our teachers do a fine job.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But in too many schools, teachers don't have college majors -- or even minors -- in the subjects they teach.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: New teachers should be required to pass performance exams, and all teachers should know the subjects they're teaching.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year's balanced budget contains resources to help them reach higher standards.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to attract talented young teachers to the toughest assignments, I recommend a sixfold increase in our program for college scholarships for students who commit to teach in the inner cities and isolated rural areas and Indian communities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us bring excellence in every part of America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Fourth, we must empower parents, with more information and more choices.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In too many communities, it's easier to get information on the quality of the local restaurants than on the quality of the local schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every school district should issue report cards on every school.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And parents should be given more choices in selecting their public schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When I became President, there was just one independent public charter school in all America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With our support, on a bipartisan basis, today there are 1,100.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My budget assures that early in the next century, there will be 3,000.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Fifth, to assure that our classrooms are truly places of learning, and to respond to what teachers have been asking us to do for years, we should say that all states and school districts must both adopt and implement sensible discipline policies.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, let's do one more thing for our children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, too many of our schools are so old they're falling apart, or so over-crowded students are learning in trailers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last fall, Congress missed the opportunity to change that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, with 53 million children in our schools, Congress must not miss that opportunity again.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to help our communities build or modernize 5,000 schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we do these things -- end social promotion.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Turn around failing schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Build modern ones.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Support qualified teachers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Promote innovation, competition and discipline -- then we will begin to meet our generation's historic responsibility to create 21st century schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, we also have to do more to support the millions of parents who give their all every day at home and at work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The most basic tool of all is a decent income.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So let's raise the minimum wage by a dollar an hour over the next two years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And let's make sure that women and men get equal pay for equal work by strengthening enforcement of equal pay laws.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That was encouraging, you know.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There was more balance on the seats.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I like that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's give them a hand.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's great.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Working parents also need quality child care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So, again this year, I ask Congress to support our plan for tax credits and subsidies for working families, for improved safety and quality, for expanded after-school programs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And our plan also includes a new tax credit for stay-at-home parents, too.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And our plan also includes a new tax credit for stay-at-home parents, too.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They need support, as well.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Parents should never have to worry about choosing between their children and their work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, the Family and Medical Leave Act -- the very first bill I signed into law -- has now, since 1993, helped millions and millions of Americans to care for a newborn baby or an ailing relative without risking their jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think it's time, with all the evidence that it has been so little burdensome to employers, to extend Family Leave to 10 million more Americans working for smaller companies.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I hope you will support it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Finally on the matter of work, parents should never have to face discrimination in the workplace.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I want to ask Congress to prohibit companies from refusing to hire or promote workers simply because they have children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is not right.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: PATIENTS' BILL OF RIGHTS':   America's families deserve the world's best medical care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thanks to bipartisan federal support for medical research, we are now on the verge of new treatments to prevent or delay diseases from Parkinson's to Alzheimer's, to arthritis to cancer.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But as we continue our advances in medical science, we can't let our medical system lag behind.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Managed care has literally transformed medicine in America -- driving down costs, but threatening to drive down quality as well.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think we ought to say to every American: You should have the right to know all your medical options -- not just the cheapest.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If you need a specialist, you should have the right to see one.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You have a right to the nearest emergency care if you're in an accident.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These are things that we ought to say.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I think we ought to say, you should have a right to keep your doctor during a period of treatment, whether it's a pregnancy or a chemotherapy treatment, or anything else.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I believe this.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, I've ordered these rights to be extended to the 85 millon Americans served by Medicare, Medicaid, and other federal health programs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But only Congress can pass a patients' bill of rights for all Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, last year, Congress missed that opportunity and we must not miss that opportunity again.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For the sake of our families, I ask us to join together across party lines and pass a strong, enforceable patients' bill of rights.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As more of our medical records are stored electronically, the threats to all our privacy increase.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because Congress has given me the authority to act if it does not do so by August, one way or another, we can all say to the American people, we will protect the privacy of medical records and we will do it this year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, two years ago, the Congress extended health coverage to up to five million children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, we should go beyond that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should make it easier for small businesses to offer health insurance.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should give people between the ages of 55 and 65 who lose their health insurance the chance to buy into Medicare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we should continue to ensure access to family planning.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: No one should have to choose between keeping health care and taking a job.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And, therefore, I especially ask you tonight to join hands to pass the landmark bipartisan legislation -- proposed by Senators Kennedy and Jeffords, Roth and Moynihan -- to allow people with disabilities to keep their health insurance when they go to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need to enable our public hospitals, our community, our university health centers to provide basic, affordable care for all the millions of working families who don't have any insurance.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They do a lot of that today, but much more can be done.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And my balanced budget makes a good down payment toward that goal.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope you will think about them and support that provision.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let me say we must step up our efforts to treat and prevent mental illness.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: No American should ever be afraid -- ever -- to address this disease.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, we will host a White House Conference on Mental Health.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With sensitivity, commitment and passion, Tipper Gore is leading our efforts here, and I'd like to thank her for what she's done.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As everyone knows, our children are targets of a massive media campaign to hook them on cigarettes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, I ask this Congress to resist the tobacco lobby, to reaffirm the FDA's authority to protect our children from tobacco, and to hold tobacco companies accountable while protecting tobacco farmers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: FEDERAL LITIGATION ON TOBACCO:   Smoking has cost taxpayers hundreds of billions of dollars under Medicare and other programs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, the states have been right about this -- taxpayers shouldn't pay for the cost of lung cancer, emphysema and other smoking-related illnesses -- the tobacco companies should.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So tonight I announce that the Justice Department is preparing a litigation plan to take the tobacco companies to court -- and with the funds we recover, to strengthen Medicare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, if we act in these areas -- minimum wage, family leave, child care, health care, the safety of our children -- then we will begin to meet our generation's historic responsibility to strengthen our families for the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, America is the most dynamic, competitive, job- creating economy in history.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we can do even better -- in building a 21st century economy that embraces all Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today's income gap is largely a skills gap.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, the Congress passed a law enabling workers to get a skills grant to choose the training they need.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I applaud all of you here who were part of that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, I recommend a five-year commitment in the new system so that we can provide, over the next five years, appropriate training opportunities for all Americans who lose their jobs, and expand rapid response teams to help all towns which have been really hurt when businesses close.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope you will support this.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Also, I ask your support for a dramatic increase in federal support for adult literacy, to mount a national campaign aimed at helping the millions and millions of working people who still read at less than a 5th grade level.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need to do this.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Here's some good news: In the past six years, we have cut the welfare rolls nearly in half.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Two years ago, from this podium, I asked five companies to lead a national effort to hire people off welfare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, our Welfare to Work Partnership includes 10,000 companies who have hired hundreds of thousands of people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And our balanced budget will help another 200,000 people move to the dignity and pride of work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope you will support it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must do more to bring the spark of private enterprise to every corner of America -- to build a bridge from Wall Street to Appalachia to the Mississippi Delta, to our Native American communities -- with more support for community development banks, for empowerment zones, for 100,000 more vouchers for affordable housing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I ask Congress to support our bold new plan to help businesses raise up to $15 billion in private sector capital to bring jobs and opportunities to our inner cities and rural areas -- with tax credits, loan guarantees, including the new American Private Investment Company, modeled on the Overseas Private Investment Company.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, for years and years and years, we've had this OPIC, this Overseas Private Investment Corporation, because we knew we had untapped markets overseas.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But our greatest untapped markets are not overseas -- they are right here at home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we should go after them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must work hard to help bring prosperity back to the family farm.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As this Congress knows very well, dropping prices and the loss of foreign markets have devastated too many family farms.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, the Congress provided substantial assistance to help stave off a disaster in American agriculture.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I am ready to work with lawmakers of both parties to create a farm safety net that will include crop insurance reform and farm income assistance.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to join with me and do this.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This should not be a political issue.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Everyone knows what an economic problem is going on out there in rural America today, and we need an appropriate means to address it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must strengthen our lead in technology.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It was government investment that led to the creation of the Internet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I propose a 28-percent increase in long-term computing research.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Y2K COMPUTER PROBLEM: We also must be ready for the 21st century from its very first moment, by solving the so-called Y2K computer problem.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We had one member of Congress stand up and applaud.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we may have about that ratio out there applauding at home, in front of their television sets.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Remember, this is a big, big problem.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we've been working hard on it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Already, we've made sure that the Social Security checks will come on time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I want all the folks at home listening to this to know that we need every state and local government, every business, large and small, to work with us to make sure that this Y2K computer bug will be remembered as the last headache of the 20th century, not the first crisis of the 21st.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, for our own prosperity, we must support economic growth abroad.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, until recently, a third of our economic growth came from exports.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But over the past year and a half, financial turmoil overseas has put that growth at risk.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, much of the world is in recession, with Asia hit especially hard.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is the most serious financial crisis in half a century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To meet it, the United States and other nations have reduced interest rates and strengthened the International Monetary Fund.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And while the turmoil is not over, we have worked very hard with other nations to contain it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: At the same time, we have to continue to work on the long-term project, building a global financial system for the 21st century that promotes prosperity and tames the cycle of boom and bust that has engulfed so much of Asia.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This June I will meet with other world leaders to advance this historic purpose.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I ask all of you to support our endeavors.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I also ask you to support creating a freer and fairer trading system for 21st century America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'd like to say something really serious to everyone in this chamber in both parties.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think trade has divided us, and divided Americans outside this chamber, for too long.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Somehow we have to find a common ground on which business and workers and environmentalists and farmers and government can stand together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I believe these are the things we ought to all agree on.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So let me try.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: First, we ought to tear down barriers, open markets, and expand trade.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But at the same time, we must ensure that ordinary citizens in all countries actually benefit from trade -- a trade that promotes the dignity of work, and the rights of workers, and protects the environment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must insist that international trade organizations be more open to public scrutiny, instead of mysterious, secret things subject to wild criticism.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When you come right down to it, now that the world economy is becoming more and more integrated, we have to do in the world what we spent the better part of this century doing here at home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have got to put a human face on the global economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, we must enforce our trade laws when imports unlawfully flood our nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have already informed the government of Japan that if that nation's sudden surge of steel imports into our country is not reversed, America will respond.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must help all manufacturers hit hard by the present crisis with loan guarantees and other incentives to increase American exports by nearly $2 billion.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'd like to believe we can achieve a new consensus on trade, based on these principles.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I ask the Congress again to join me in this common approach and to give the President the trade authority long used -- and now overdue and necessary -- to advance our prosperity in the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I also issue a call to the nations of the world to join the United States in a new round of global trade negotiations to expand exports of services, manufacturers and farm products.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight I say we will work with the International Labor Organization on a new initiative to raise labor standards around the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And this year, we will lead the international community to conclude a treaty to ban abusive child labor everywhere in the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we do these things -- invest in our people, our communities, our technology, and lead in the global economy -- then we will begin to meet our historic responsibility to build a 21st century prosperity for America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, no nation in history has had the opportunity and the responsibility we now have to shape a world that is more peaceful, more secure, more free.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: PEACEKEEPING AND ARMS CONTROL:  All Americans can be proud that our leadership helped to bring peace in Northern Ireland.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All Americans can be proud that our leadership has put Bosnia on the path to peace.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And with our NATO allies, we are pressing the Serbian government to stop its brutal repression in Kosovo -- to bring those responsible to justice, and to give the people of Kosovo the self-government they deserve.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All Americans can be proud that our leadership renewed hope for lasting peace in the Middle East.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Some of you were with me last December as we watched the Palestinian National Council completely renounce its call for the destruction of Israel.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now I ask Congress to provide resources so that all parties can implement the Wye Agreement -- to protect Israel's security, to stimulate the Palestinian economy, to support our friends in Jordan.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must not, we dare not, let them down.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope you will help.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As we work for peace, we must also meet threats to our nation's security -- including increased dangers from outlaw nations and terrorism.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will defend our security wherever we are threatened, as we did this summer when we struck at Osama bin Laden's network of terror.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The bombing of our embassies in Kenya and Tanzania reminds us again of the risks faced every day by those who represent America to the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So let's give them the support they need, the safest possible workplaces, and the resources they must have so America can continue to lead.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must work to keep terrorists from disrupting computer networks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must work to prepare local communities for biological and chemical emergencies, to support research into vaccines and treatments.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must increase our efforts to restrain the spread of nuclear weapons and missiles, from Korea to India and Pakistan.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must expand our work with Russia, Ukraine, and the other former Soviet nations to safeguard nuclear materials and technology so they never fall into the wrong hands.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our balanced budget will increase funding for these critical efforts by almost two-thirds over the next five years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With Russia, we must continue to reduce our nuclear arsenals.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The START II treaty and the framework we have already agreed to for START III could cut them by 80 percent from their Cold War height.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's been two years since I signed the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we don't do the right thing, other nations won't either.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask the Senate to take this vital step: Approve the treaty now, to make it harder for other nations to develop nuclear arms, and to make sure we can end nuclear testing forever.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For nearly a decade, Iraq has defied its obligations to destroy its weapons of terror and the missiles to deliver them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America will continue to contain Saddam -- and we will work for the day when Iraq has a government worthy of its people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, last month, in our action over Iraq, our troops were superb.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Their mission was so flawlessly executed that we risk taking for granted the bravery and the skill it required.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Captain Jeff Taliaferro, a 10-year veteran of the Air Force, flew a B-1B bomber over Iraq as we attacked Saddam's war machine.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He's here with us tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'd like to ask you to honor him and all the 33,000 men and women of Operation Desert Fox. Captain Taliaferro.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: BUILDING UP THE DEFENSE BUDGET:  It is time to reverse the decline in defense spending that began in 1985.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Since April, together we have added nearly $6 billion to maintain our military readiness.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My balanced budget calls for a sustained increase over the next six years for readiness, for modernization, and for pay and benefits for our troops and their families.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, we are the heirs of a legacy of bravery represented in every community in America by millions of our veterans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America's defenders today still stand ready at a moment's notice to go where comforts are few and dangers are many, to do what needs to be done as no one else can.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They always come through for America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must come through for them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The new century demands new partnerships for peace and security.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The United Nations plays a crucial role, with allies sharing burdens America might otherwise bear alone.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America needs a strong and effective U.N.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to work with this new Congress to pay our dues and our debts.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must continue to support security and stability in Europe and Asia -- expanding NATO and defining its new missions.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Maintaining our alliance with Japan, with Korea, without our other Asian allies.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And engaging China.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In China, last year, I said to the leaders and the people what I'd like to say again tonight: Stability can no longer be bought at the expense of liberty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I'd also like to say again to the American people: It's important not to isolate China.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The more we bring China into the world, the more the world will bring change and freedom to China.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last spring, with some of you, I traveled to Africa, where I saw democracy and reform rising, but still held back by violence and disease.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must fortify African democracy and peace by launching Radio Democracy for Africa, supporting the transition to democracy now beginning to take place in Nigeria, and passing the African Trade and Development Act.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must continue to deepen our ties to the Americas and the Caribbean.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our common work to educate children, fight drugs, strengthen democracy and increase trade.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In this hemisphere, every government but one is freely chosen by its people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are determined that Cuba, too, will know the blessings of liberty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The American people have opened their hearts and their arms to our Central American and Caribbean neighbors who have been so devastated by the recent hurricanes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Working with Congress, I am committed to help them rebuild.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When the First Lady and Tipper Gore visited the region, they saw thousands of our troops and thousands of American volunteers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the Dominican Republic, Hillary helped to rededicate a hospital that had been rebuilt by Dominicans and Americans, working side-by-side.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With her was someone else who has been very important to the relief efforts.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, sports records are made and, sooner or later, they're broken.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But making other people's lives better, and showing our children the true meaning of brotherhood -- that lasts forever.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So, for far more than baseball, Sammy Sosa, you're a hero in two countries tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I say to all of you, if we do these things -- if we pursue peace, fight terrorism, increase our strength, renew our alliances -- we will begin to meet our generation's historic responsibility to build a stronger 21st century America in a freer, more peaceful world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As the world has changed, so have our own communities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must make them safer, more livable and more united.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, we will reach our goal of 100,000 community police officers -- ahead of schedule and under budget.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The Brady Bill has stopped a quarter million felons, fugitives and stalkers from buying handguns.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And, now, the murder rate is the lowest in 30 years and the crime rate has dropped for six straight years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I propose a 21st century crime bill to deploy the latest technologies and tactics to make our communities even safer.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our balanced budget will help put up to 50,000 more police on the street, in the areas hardest hit by crime -- and then to equip them with new tools, from crime-mapping computers to digital mug shots.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must break the deadly cycle of drugs and crime.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our budget expands support for drug testing and treatment, saying to prisoners: If you stay on drugs, you have to stay behind bars.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to those on parole: If you want to keep your freedom, you must stay free of drugs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: GUN CONTROL:  I ask Congress to restore the five-day waiting period for buying a handgun -- and extend the Brady Bill to prevent juveniles who commit violent crimes from buying a gun.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must do more to keep our schools the safest places in our communities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, every American was horrified and heartbroken by the tragic killings in Jonesboro, Paducah, Pearl, Edinboro, Springfield.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We were deeply moved by the courageous parents now working to keep guns out of the hands of children and to make other efforts so that other parents don't have to live through their loss.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: After she lost her daughter, Suzann Wilson of Jonesboro, Arkansas, came here to the White House with a powerful plea.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Please, please, for the sake of your children, lock up your gun.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Don't let what happened in Jonesboro happen in your town.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's a message she is passionately advocating every day.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Suzann is here with us tonight, with the First Lady.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'd like to thank her for her courage and her commitment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In memory of all the children who lost their lives to school violence, I ask you to strengthen the Safe and Drug-Free School Act, to pass legislation to require child trigger locks, to do everything possible to keep our children safe.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: leaving this land even a better land for our descendants than it is for us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, we're restoring the Florida Everglades , saving Yellowstone, preserving the red rock canyons of Utah, protecting California's redwoods and our precious coasts.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But our most fateful new challenge is the threat of global warming.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: 1998 was the warmest year ever recorded.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year's heat waves, floods and storms are but a hint of what future generations may endure if we do not act now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight I propose a new clean air fund to help communities reduce greenhouse and other pollution, and tax incentives and investments to spur clean energy technology.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I want to work with members of Congress in both parties to reward companies that take early, voluntary action to reduce greenhouse gases.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, all our communities face a preservation challenge, as they grow and green space shrinks.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Seven thousand acres of farmland and open space are lost every day.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In response, I propose two major initiatives: First, a $1-billion Livability Agenda to help communities save open space, ease traffic congestion, and grow in ways that enhance every citizen's quality of life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And second, a $1-billion Lands Legacy Initiative to preserve places of natural beauty all across America -- from the most remote wilderness to the nearest city park.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These are truly landmark initiatives, which could not have been developed without the visionary leadership of the Vice President, and I want to thank him very much for his commitment here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, to get the most out of your community, you have to give something back.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why we created AmeriCorps -- our national service program that gives today's generation a chance to serve their communities and earn money for college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So far, in just four years, 100,000 young Americans have built low-income homes with Habitat for Humanity, helped to tutor children with churches, worked with FEMA to ease the burden of natural disasters, and performed countless other acts of service that have made America better.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask Congress to give more young Americans the chance to follow their lead and serve America in AmeriCorps.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must work to renew our national community as well for the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year the House passed the bipartisan campaign finance reform legislation sponsored by Representatives Shays and Meehan and Senators McCain and Feingold.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But a partisan minority in the Senate blocked reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I'd like to say to the House: Pass it again, quickly.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I'd like to say to the Senate: I hope you will say yes to a stronger American democracy in the year 2000.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: INITIATIVE ON RACE:  Since 1997, our Initiative on Race has sought to bridge the divides between and among our people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In its report last fall, the Initiative's Advisory Board found that Americans really do want to bring our people together across racial lines.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We know it's been a long journey.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For some, it goes back to before the beginning of our Republic.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For others, back since the Civil War.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For others, throughout the 20th century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But for most of us alive today, in a very real sense, this journey began 43 years ago, when a woman named Rosa Parks sat down on a bus in Alabama, and wouldn't get up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: She's sitting down with the First Lady tonight, and she may get up or not, as she chooses.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you, Rosa.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We know that our continuing racial problems are aggravated, as the Presidential Initiative said, by opportunity gaps.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The initiative I've outlined tonight will help to close them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we know that the discrimination gap has not been fully closed either.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Discrimination or violence because of race or religion, ancestry or gender, disability or sexual orientation, is wrong, and it ought to be illegal.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Therefore, I ask Congress to make the Employment Non-Discrimination Act and the Hate Crimes Prevention Act the law of the land.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, since every person in America counts, every American ought to be counted.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need a census that uses modern scientific methods to do that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our new immigrants must be part of our One America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: After all, they're revitalizing our cities, they're energizing our culture, they're building up our economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have a responsibility to make them welcome here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And they have a responsibility to enter the mainstream of American life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That means learning English and learning about our democratic system of government.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There are now long waiting lines of immigrants that are trying to do just that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Therefore, our budget significantly expands our efforts to help them meet their responsibility.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope you will support it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Whether our ancestors came here on the Mayflower, on slave ships, whether they came to Ellis Island or LAX in Los Angeles, whether they came yesterday or walked this land a thousand years ago -- our great challenge for the 21st century is to find a way to be One America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can meet all the other challenges if we can go forward as One America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, barely more than 300 days from now, we will cross that bridge into the new millennium.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I'd like to take just a minute to honor her.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For leading our Millennium Project, for all she's done for our children, for all she has done in her historic role to serve our nation and our best ideals at home and abroad, I honor her.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, I called on Congress and every citizen to mark the millennium by saving America's treasures.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Hillary has traveled all across the country to inspire recognition and support for saving places like Thomas Edison's Invention Factory or Harriet Tubman's home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now we have to preserve our treasures in every community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: by launching projects that save our history, promote our arts and humanities, prepare our children for the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Already, the response has been remarkable.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I want to say a special word of thanks to our private sector partners and to members in Congress of both parties for their support.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Just one example: Because of you, the Star-Spangled Banner will be preserved for the ages.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Six years ago, I came to office in a time of doubt for America, with our economy troubled, our deficit high, our people divided.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Some even wondered whether our best days were behind us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But across this country, in a thousand neighborhoods, I have seen -- even amidst the pain and uncertainty of recession -- the real heart and character of America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I knew then that we Americans could renew this country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: of our founders' dream.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: of the Cold War.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must all be profoundly grateful for the magnificent achievement of our forbearers in this century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Yet, perhaps, in the daily press of events, in the clash of controversy, we don't see our own time for what it truly is -- a new dawn for America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A hundred years from tonight, another American President will stand in this place and report on the State of the Union.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He -- or she -- he or she will look back on a 21st century shaped in so many ways by the decisions we make here and now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So let it be said of us then that we were thinking not only of our time, but of their time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That we reached as high as our ideals.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That we put aside our divisions and found a new hour of healing and hopefulness.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That we joined together to serve and strengthen the land we love.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, this is our moment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us lift our eyes as one nation, and from the mountaintop of this American Century, look ahead to the next one -- asking God's blessing on our endeavors and on our beloved country.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you and good evening.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. Vice President, members of Congress, honored guests, my fellow Americans: We are fortunate to be alive at this moment in history.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Never before has our nation enjoyed, at once, so much prosperity and social progress with so little internal crisis and so few external threats.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Never before have we had such a blessed opportunity -- and, therefore, such a profound obligation -- to build the more perfect union of our founders' dreams.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We begin the new century with over 20 million new jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The fastest economic growth in more than 30 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The lowest unemployment rates in 30 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The lowest poverty rates in 20 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The lowest African American and Hispanic unemployment rates on record.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The first back-to-back budget surpluses in 42 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And next month, America will achieve the longest period of economic growth in our entire history.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have built a new economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And our economic revolution has been matched by a revival of the American spirit: crime down by 20 percent, to its lowest level in 25 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Teen births down seven years in a row.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Adoptions up by 30 percent.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Welfare rolls cut in half to their lowest levels in 30 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, the state of our union is the strongest it has ever been.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: REINVENTING AMERICA:  As always, the real credit belongs to the American people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My gratitude also goes to those of you in this chamber who have worked with us to put progress over partisanship.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Eight years ago, it was not so clear to most Americans there would be much to celebrate in the year 2000.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Then our nation was gripped by economic distress, social decline, political gridlock.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: nan

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the best traditions of our nation, Americans determined to set things right.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We restored the vital center, replacing outmoded ideologies with a new vision anchored in basic, enduring values: opportunity for all, responsibility from all, a community of all Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We reinvented government, transforming it into a catalyst for new ideas that stress both opportunity and responsibility, and give our people the tools they need to solve their own problems.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With the smallest federal work force in 40 years, we turned record deficits into record surpluses, and doubled our investment in education.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We cut crime, with 100,000 community police and the Brady law, which has kept guns out of the hands of half a million criminals.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We ended welfare as we knew it -- requiring work while protecting health care and nutrition for children, and investing more in child care, transportation, and housing to help their parents go to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've helped parents to succeed at home and at work, with family leave, which 20 millions Americans have now used to care for a newborn child or a sick loved one.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have engaged 150,000 young Americans in citizen service through AmeriCorps, while helping them earn money for college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In 1992, we just had a road map.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, we have results.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But even more important, America again has the confidence to dream big dreams.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we must not let this confidence drift into complacency.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For we, all of us, will be judged by the dreams and deeds we pass on to our children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And on that score, we will be held to a high standard, indeed, because our chance to do good is so great.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: 21ST CENTURY REVOLUTION:  My fellow Americans, we have crossed the bridge we built to the 21st century.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, we must shape a 21st century American revolution -- of opportunity, responsibility and community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must be now, as we were in the beginning, a new nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It should be the growing nation with a future that takes the long look ahead.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So, tonight, let us take our long look ahead -- and set great goals for our nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To 21st century America, let us pledge these things: Every child will begin school ready to learn and graduate ready to succeed.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every family will be able to succeed at home and at work, and no child will be raised in poverty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will meet the challenge of the aging of America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will assure quality, affordable health care, at last, for all Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will make America the safest big country on Earth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will pay off our national debt for the first time since 1835.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will bring prosperity to every American community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will reverse the course of climate change and leave a safer, cleaner planet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: America will lead the world toward shared peace and prosperity, and the far frontiers of science and technology.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we will become at last what our founders pledged us to be so long ago -- one nation, under God, indivisible, with liberty and justice for all.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: GREAT GOALS:  These are great goals, worthy of a great nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We will not reach them all this year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Not even in this decade.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we will reach them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let us remember that the first American Revolution was not won with a single shot.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The continent was not settled in a single year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The lesson of our history -- and the lesson of the last seven years -- is that great goals are reached step by step, always building on our progress, always gaining ground.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Of course, you can't gain ground if you're standing still.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For too long this Congress has been standing still on some of our most pressing national priorities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So let's begin tonight with them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Again, I ask you to pass a real patients' bill of rights.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to pass common-sense gun safety legislation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to pass campaign finance reform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to vote up or down on judicial nominations and other important appointees.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And, again I ask you -- I implore you -- to raise the minimum wage.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, two years ago -- let me try to balance the seesaw here -- two years ago, as we reached across party lines to reach our first balanced budget, I asked that we meet our responsibility to the next generation by maintaining our fiscal discipline.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because we refused to stray from that path, we are doing something that would have seemed unimaginable seven years ago.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We are actually paying down the national debt.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we stay on this path, we can pay down the debt entirely in 13 just years now and make America debt-free for the first time since Andrew Jackson was President in 1835.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In 1993, we began to put our fiscal house in order with the Deficit Reduction Act, which you'll all remember won passages in both Houses by just a single vote.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Your former colleague, my first Secretary of the Treasury, led that effort and sparked our long boom.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He's here with us tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Lloyd Bentsen, you have served America well, and we thank you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Beyond paying off the debt, we must ensure that the benefits of debt reduction go to preserving two of the most important guarantees we make to every American -- Social Security and Medicare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I ask you to work with me to make a bipartisan down payment on Social Security reform by crediting the interest savings from debt reduction to the Social Security Trust Fund so that it will be strong and sound for the next 50 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But this is just the start of our journey.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must also take the right steps toward reaching our great goals.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: EDUCATIONAL GOALS:  First and foremost, we need a 21st century revolution in education, guided by our faith that every single child can learn.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Because education is more important than ever, more than ever the key to our children's future, we must make sure all our children have that key.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That means quality pre-school and after-school, the best trained teachers in the classroom, and college opportunities for all our children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For seven years now, we've worked hard to improve our schools, with opportunity and responsibility -- investing more, but demanding more in turn.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Reading, math, college entrance scores are up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Some of the most impressive gains are in schools in very poor neighborhoods.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But all successful schools have followed the same proven formula: higher standards, more accountability, and extra help so children who need it can get it to reach those standards.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have sent Congress a reform plan based on that formula.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It holds states and school districts accountable for progress, and rewards them for results.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Each year, our national government invests more than $15 billion in our schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It is time to support what works and stop supporting what doesn't.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, as we demand more from our schools, we should also invest more in our schools.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's double our investment to help states and districts turn around their worst-performing schools, or shut them down.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's double our investments in after-school and summer school programs, which boost achievement and keep people off the streets and out of trouble.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we do this, we can give every single child in every failing school in America -- everyone -- the chance to meet high standards.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Since 1993, we've nearly doubled our investment in Head Start and improved its quality.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I ask you for another $1 billion for Head Start, the largest increase in the history of the program.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We know that children learn best in smaller classes with good teachers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For two years in a row, Congress has supported my plan to hire 100,000 new qualified teachers to lower class size in the early grades.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I thank you for that, and I ask you to make it three in a row.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And to make sure all teachers know the subjects they teach, tonight I propose a new teacher quality initiative -- to recruit more talented people into the classroom, reward good teachers for staying there, and give all teachers the training they need.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We know charter schools provide real public school choice.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When I became President, there was just one independent public charter school in all America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, thanks to you, there are 1,700.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you now to help us meet our goal of 3,000 charter schools by next year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We know we must connect all our classrooms to the Internet, and we're getting there.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In 1994, only 3 percent of our classrooms were connected.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, with the help of the Vice President's E-rate program, more than half of them are.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And 90 percent of our schools have at least one Internet connection.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we cannot finish the job when a third of all our schools are in serious disrepair.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Many of them have walls and wires so old, they're too old for the Internet.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So tonight, I propose to help 5,000 schools a year make immediate and urgent repairs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And again, to help build or modernize 6,000 more, to get students out of trailers and into high-tech classrooms.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask all of you to help me double our bipartisan Gear-Up program, which provides mentors for disadvantaged young people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we double it, we can provide mentors for 1.4 million of them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's also offer these kids from disadvantaged backgrounds the same chance to take the same college test-prep courses wealthier students use to boost their test scores.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To make the American Dream achievable for all, we must make college affordable for all.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For seven years, on a bipartisan basis, we have taken action toward that goal: larger Pell grants, more affordable student loans, education IRAs, and our HOPE scholarships, which have already benefitted 5 million young people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, 67 percent of high school graduates are going on to college.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's up 10 percent since 1993.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Yet millions of families still strain to pay college tuition.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They need help.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: TAX CUTS FOR EDUCATION:  So I propose a landmark $30-billion college opportunity tax cut -- a middle class tax deduction for up to $10,000 in college tuition costs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The previous actions of this Congress have already made two years of college affordable for all.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's time to make four years of college affordable for all.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we take all these steps, we'll move a long way toward making sure every child starts school ready to learn and graduates ready to succeed.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need a 21st century revolution to reward work and strengthen families, by giving every parent the tools to succeed at work and at the most important work of all -- raising children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: HEALTH CARE:  That means making sure every family has health care and the support to care for aging parents, the tools to bring their children up right, and that no child grows up in poverty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: From my first days as President, we've worked to give families better access to better health care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In 1997, we passed the Children's Health Insurance Program -- CHIP -- so that workers who don't have coverage through their employers at least can get it for their children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So far, we've enrolled 2 million children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We're well on our way to our goal of 5 million.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But there are still more than 40 million of our fellow Americans without health insurance -- more than there were in 1993.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight I propose that we follow Vice President Gore's suggestion to make low income parents eligible for the insurance that covers their children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Together with our children's initiative -- think of this -- together with our children's initiative, this action would enable us to cover nearly a quarter of all the uninsured people in America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Again, I want to ask you to let people between the ages of 55 and 65 -- the fastest growing group of uninsured -- buy into Medicare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And this year I propose to give them a tax credit to make that choice an affordable one.
