speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope you will support that, as well.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When the baby boomers retire, Medicare will be faced with caring for twice as many of our citizens.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Yet, it is far from ready to do so.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My generation must not ask our children's generation to shoulder our burden.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We simply must act now to strengthen and modernize Medicare.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My budget includes a comprehensive plan to reform Medicare, to make it more efficient and competitive.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And it dedicates nearly $400 billion of our budget surplus to keep Medicare solvent past 2025.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And, at long last, it also provides funds to give every senior a voluntary choice of affordable coverage for prescription drugs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Lifesaving drugs are an indispensable part of modern medicine.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: No one creating a Medicare program today would even think of excluding coverage for prescription drugs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Yet more than three in five of our seniors now lack dependable drug coverage which can lengthen and enrich their lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The millions of older Americans who need prescription drugs the most pay the highest prices for them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In good conscience, we cannot let another year pass without extending to all our seniors this lifeline of affordable prescription drugs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Record numbers of Americans are providing for aging or ailing loved ones at home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's a loving, but a difficult and often very expensive choice.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, I proposed a $1,000 tax credit for long-term care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Frankly, it wasn't enough.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, let's triple it, to $3,000.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But this year, let's pass it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We also have to make needed investments to expand access to mental health care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to take a moment to thank the person who led our first White House Conference on Mental Health last year, and who for seven years has led all our efforts to break down the barriers to decent treatment of people with mental illness.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you, Tipper Gore.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Taken together, these proposals would mark the largest investment in health care in the 35 years since Medicare was created -- the largest investment in 35 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That would be a big step toward assuring quality health care for all Americans, young and old.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I ask you to embrace them and pass them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: EARNING THE TAX CREDIT:  We must also make investments that reward work and support families.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Nothing does that better than the Earned Income Tax Credit -- the EITC.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: in the EITC is about earning, working, taking responsibility and being rewarded for it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In my very first address to you, I asked Congress to greatly expand this credit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And you did.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As a result, in 1998 alone, the EITC helped more than 4.3 million Americans work their way out of poverty toward the middle class.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's double the number in 1993.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I propose another major expansion of the EITC: to reduce the marriage penalty, to make sure it rewards marriage as it rewards work -- and also, to expand the tax credit for families that have more than two children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It punishes people with more than two children today.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our proposal would allow families with three or more children to get up to $1,100 more in tax relief.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These are working families.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Their children should not be in poverty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We also can't reward work and family unless men and women get equal pay for equal work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, the female unemployment rate is the lowest it has been in 46 years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Yet, women still only earn about 75 cents for every dollar men earn.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must do better, by providing the resources to enforce present equal pay laws.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Training more women for high-paying, high-tech jobs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And passing the Paycheck Fairness Act.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Many working parents spend up to a quarter -- a quarter -- of their income on child care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, we helped parents provide child care for about 2 million children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My child care initiative, before you now, along with funds already secured in welfare reform, would make child care better, safer and more affordable for another 400,000 children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to pass that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They need it out there --

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For hard-pressed middle-income families, we should also expand the child care tax credit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I believe strongly we should take the next big step and make that tax credit refundable for low-income families.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For people making under $30,000 a year, that could mean up to $2,400 for child care costs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, we all say we're pro-work and pro-family.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Passing this proposal would prove it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tens of millions of Americans live from paycheck to paycheck.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As hard as they work, they still don't have the opportunity to save.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Too few can make use of IRAs and 401-K plans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should do more to help all working families save and accumulate wealth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's the idea behind the Individual Development Accounts, the IDAs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to take that idea to a new level, with new Retirement Savings Accounts that enable every low- and moderate-income family in America to save for retirement, a first home, a medical emergency, or a college education.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I propose to match their contributions, however small, dollar for dollar, every year they save.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I propose to give a major new tax credit to any small business that will provide a meaningful pension to its workers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Those people ought to have retirement as well as the rest of us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Nearly one in three American children grows up without a father.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These children are five times more likely to live in poverty than children with both parents at home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Clearly, demanding and supporting responsible fatherhood is critical to lifting all children out of poverty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've doubled child support collections since 1992.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I'm proposing to you tough new measures to hold still more fathers responsible.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we should recognize that a lot of fathers want to do right by their children, but need help to do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A FATHER'S RESPONSIBILITY:  Carlos Rosas of St. Paul, Minnesota, wanted to do right by his son, and he got the help to do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now he's got a good job and he supports his little boy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My budget will help 40,000 more fathers make the same choices Carlos Rosas did.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I thank him for being here tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Stand up, Carlos.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If there is any single issue on which we should be able to reach across party lines, it is in our common commitment to reward work and strengthen families, similar to what we did last year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We came together to help people with disabilities keep their health insurance when they go to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I thank you for that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thanks to overwhelming bipartisan support from this Congress, we have improved foster care.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've helped those young people who leave it when they turn 18, and we have dramatically increased the number of foster care children going into adoptive homes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I thank all of you for all of that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Of course, I am forever grateful to the person who has led our efforts from the beginning, and who's worked so tirelessly for children and families for 30 years now: my wife, Hillary.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I thank her.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we take the steps I've just discussed, we can go a long, long way toward empowering parents to succeed at home and at work, and ensuring that no child is raised in poverty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can make these vital investments in health care, education, support for working families, and still offer tax cuts to help pay for college, for retirement, to care for aging parents, to reduce the marriage penalty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can do these things without forsaking the path of fiscal discipline that got us to this point here tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Indeed, we must make these investments and these tax cuts in the context of a balanced budget that strengthens and extends the life of Social Security and Medicare and pays down the national debt.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Crime in America has dropped for the past seven years -- that's the longest decline on record -- thanks to a national consensus we helped to forge on community police, sensible gun safety laws, and effective prevention.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But nobody -- nobody here, nobody in America -- believes we're safe enough.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So again, I ask you to set a higher goal.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Let's make this country the safest big country in the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last fall, Congress supported my plan to hire, in addition to the 100,000 community police we've already funded, 50,000 more, concentrated in high-crime neighborhoods.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask your continued support for that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: GUN CONTROL:  Soon after the Columbine tragedy, Congress considered common-sense gun legislation, to require Brady background checks at the gun shows, child safety locks for new handguns, and a ban on the importation of large-capacity ammunition clips.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: With courage -- and a tie-breaking vote by the Vice President -- the Senate faced down the gun lobby, stood up for the American people, and passed this legislation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But the House failed to follow suit.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, we have all seen what happens when guns fall into the wrong hands.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Daniel Mauser was only 15 years old when he was gunned down at Columbine.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: He was an amazing kid -- a straight-A student, a good skier.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Like all parents who lose their children, his father Tom has borne unimaginable grief.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Somehow he has found the strength to honor his son by transforming his grief into action.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Earlier this month, he took a leave of absence from his job to fight for tougher gun safety laws.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I pray that his courage and wisdom will at long last move this Congress to make common-sense gun legislation the very next order of business.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tom Mauser, stand up.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We thank you for being here tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must strengthen our gun laws and enforce those already on the books better.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Federal gun crime prosecutions are up 16 percent since I took office.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we must do more.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I propose to hire more federal and local gun prosecutors and more ATF agents to crack down on illegal gun traffickers and bad-apple dealers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we must give them the enforcement tools that they need, tools to trace every gun and every bullet used in every gun crime in the United States.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to help us do that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Every state in this country already requires hunters and automobile drivers to have a license.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think they ought to do the same thing for handgun purchases.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, specifically, I propose a plan to ensure that all new handgun buyers must first have a photo license from their state showing they passed the Brady background check and a gun safety course, before they get the gun.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope you'll help me pass that in this Congress.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Listen to this -- listen to this.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The accidental gun rate -- the accidental gun death rate of children under 15 in the United States is nine times higher than in the other 25 industrialized countries combined.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, technologies now exist that could lead to guns that can only be fired by the adults who own them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask Congress to fund research into smart gun technology, to save these children's lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask responsible leaders in the gun industry to work with us on smart guns, and other steps to keep guns out of the wrong hands, to keep our children safe.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, every parent I know worries about the impact of violence in the media on their children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to begin by thanking the entertainment industry for accepting my challenge to put voluntary ratings on TV programs and video and Internet games.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But, frankly, the ratings are too numerous, diverse and confusing to be really useful to parents.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So tonight, I ask the industry to accept the First Lady's challenge to develop a single voluntary rating system for all children's entertainment that is easier for parents to understand and enforce.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The steps I outline will take us well on our way to making America the safest big country in the world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, to keep our historic economic expansion going -- the subject of a lot of discussion in this community and others -- I believe we need a 21st century revolution to open new markets, start new businesses, hire new workers right here in America -- in our inner cities, poor rural areas, and Native American reservations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our nation's prosperity hasn't yet reached these places.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Over the last six months, I've traveled to a lot of them, joined by many of you, and many far-sighted business people, to shine a spotlight on the enormous potential in communities from Appalachia to the Mississippi Delta, from Watts to the Pine Ridge Reservation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Everywhere I go, I meet talented people eager for opportunity, and able to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight I ask you, let's put them to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For business, it's the smart thing to do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For America, it's the right thing to do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And let me ask you something -- if we don't do this now, when in the wide world will we ever get around to it?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: So I ask Congress to give businesses the same incentives to invest in America's new markets they now have to invest in markets overseas.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I propose a large New Markets tax credit and other incentives to spur $22 billion in private-sector capital to create new businesses and new investments in our inner cities and rural areas.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I also -- because empowerment zones have been creating these opportunities for five years now, I also ask you to increase incentives to invest in them and to create more of them.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A COMMON GOAL:  And let me say to all of you again what I have tried to say at every turn -- this is not a Democratic or a Republican issue.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Giving people a chance to live their dreams is an American issue.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Mr. Speaker, it was a powerful moment last November when you joined Reverend Jesse Jackson and me in your home state of Illinois, and committed to working toward our common goal, by combining the best ideas from both sides of the aisle.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to thank you again, and to tell you, Mr.Speaker, I look forward to working with you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is a worthy, joint endeavor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I also ask you to make special efforts to address the areas of our nation with the highest rates of poverty -- our Native American reservations and the Mississippi Delta.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My budget includes $110-million initiative to promote economic development in the Delta, and a billion dollars to increase economic opportunity, health care, education and law enforcement for our Native American communities.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should begin this new century by honoring our historic responsibility to empower the first Americans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I want to thank tonight the leaders and the members from both parties who've expressed to me an interest in working with us on these efforts.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They are profoundly important.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: FARMING'S FUTURE:  There's another part of our American community in trouble tonight -- our family farmers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When I signed the Farm Bill in 1996, I said there was great danger it would work well in good times, but not in bad.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Well, droughts, floods, and historically low prices have made these times very bad for the farmers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must work together to strengthen the farm safety net, invest in land conservation, and create some new markets for them by expanding our programs for bio-based fuels and products.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Please, they need help -- let's do it together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Opportunity for all requires something else today -- having access to a computer and knowing how to use it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That means we must close the digital divide between those who've got the tools and those who don't.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, connecting classrooms and libraries to the Internet is crucial, but it's just a start.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My budget ensures that all new teachers are trained to teach 21st century skills, and it creates technology centers in 1,000 communities to serve adults.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This spring, I'll invite high-tech leaders to join me on another New Markets tour, to close the digital divide and open opportunity for our people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to thank the high-tech companies that already are doing so much in this area.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope the new tax incentives I have proposed will get all the rest of them to join us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is a national crusade.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have got to do this, and do it quickly.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, again I say to you, these are steps, but step by step, we can go a long way toward our goal of bringing opportunity to every community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To realize the full possibilities of this economy, we must reach beyond our own borders, to shape the revolution that is tearing down barriers and building new networks among nations and individuals, and economies and cultures: globalization.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's the central reality of our time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Of course, change this profound is both liberating and threatening to people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But there's no turning back.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And our open, creative society stands to benefit more than any other -- if we understand, and act on, the realities of interdependence.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have to be at the center of every vital global network, as a good neighbor and a good partner.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have to recognize that we cannot build our future without helping others to build theirs.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: TRADE INITIATIVES:  The first thing we have got to do is to forge a new consensus on trade.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, those of us who believe passionately in the power of open trade, we have to ensure that it lifts both our living standards and our values, never tolerating abusive child labor or a race to the bottom in the environment and worker protection.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But others must recognize that open markets and rule-based trade are the best engines we know of for raising living standards, reducing global poverty and environmental destruction, and assuring the free flow of ideas.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I believe as strongly tonight as I did the first day I got here, the only direction forward for America on trade -- the only direction for America on trade is to keep going forward.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to help me forge that consensus.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have to make developing economies our partners in prosperity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why I would like to ask you again to finalize our groundbreaking African and Caribbean Basin trade initiatives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But globalization is about more than economics.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Our purpose must be to bring together the world around freedom and democracy and peace, and to oppose those who would tear it apart.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Here are the fundamental challenges I believe America must meet to shape the 21st century world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: WORLD ECONOMICS:  First, we must continue to encourage our former adversaries, Russia and China, to emerge as stable, prosperous, democratic nations.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Both are being held back today from reaching their full potential: Russia by the legacy of communism, an economy in turmoil, a cruel and self-defeating war in Chechnya.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: China by the illusion that it can buy stability at the expense of freedom.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But think how much has changed in the past decade: 5,000 former Soviet nuclear weapons taken out of commission.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Russian soldiers actually serving with ours in the Balkans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Russian people electing their leaders for the first time in a thousand years.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And in China, an economy more open to the world than ever before.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Of course, no one, not a single person in this chamber tonight, can know for sure what direction these great nations will take.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we do know for sure that we can choose what we do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we should do everything in our power to increase the chance that they will choose wisely, to be constructive members of our global community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why we should support those Russians who are struggling for a democratic, prosperous future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Continue to reduce both our nuclear arsenals.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And help Russia to safeguard weapons and materials that remain.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And that's why I believe Congress should support the agreement we negotiated to bring China into the WTO, by passing Permanent Normal Trade Relations with China as soon as possible this year.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think you ought to do it for two reasons.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: First of all, our markets are already open to China.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This agreement will open China's markets to us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And, second, it will plainly advance the cause of peace in Asia and promote the cause of change in China.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: No, we don't know where it's going.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: All we can do is decide what we're going to do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But when all is said and done, we need to know we did everything we possibly could to maximize the chance that China will choose the right future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A second challenge we've got is to protect our own security from conflicts that pose the risk of wider war and threaten our common humanity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can't prevent every conflict or stop every outrage.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But where our interests are at stake and we can make a difference, we should be, and we must be, peacemakers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should be proud of our role in bringing the Middle East closer to a lasting peace.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Building peace in Northern Ireland.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Working for peace in East Timor and Africa.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Promoting reconciliation between Greece and Turkey and in Cyprus.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Working to defuse these crises between India and Pakistan.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In defending human rights and religious freedom.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we should be proud of the men and women of our Armed Forces and those of our allies who stopped the ethnic cleansing in Kosovo, enabling a million people to return to their homes.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: When Slobodan Milosevic unleashed his terror on Kosovo, Captain John Cherrey was one of the brave airmen who turned the tide.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And when another American plane was shot down over Serbia, he flew into the teeth of enemy air defenses to bring his fellow pilot home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thanks to our Armed Forces' skill and bravery, we prevailed in Kosovo without losing a single American in combat.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to introduce Captain Cherrey to you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We honor Captain Cherrey, and we promise you, Captain, we'll finish the job you began.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Stand up so we can see you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: SAFE TECHNOLOGY:  A third challenge we have is to keep this inexorable march of technology from giving terrorists and potentially hostile nations the means to undermine our defenses.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Keep in mind, the same technological advances that have shrunk cell phones to fit in the palms of our hands can also make weapons of terror easier to conceal and easier to use.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must meet this threat by making effective agreements to restrain nuclear and missile programs in North Korea.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Curbing the flow of lethal technology to Iran.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Preventing Iraq from threatening its neighbors.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Increasing our preparedness against chemical and biological attack.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Protecting our vital computer systems from hackers and criminals.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And developing a system to defend against new missile threats -- while working to preserve our ABM missile treaty with Russia.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must do all these things.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I predict to you, when most of us are long gone, but some time in the next 10 to 20 years, the major security threat this country will face will come from the enemies of the nation state: the narco-traffickers and the terrorists and the organized criminals, who will be organized together, working together, with increasing access to ever-more sophisticated chemical and biological weapons.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I want to thank the Pentagon and others for doing what they're doing right now to try to help protect us and plan for that, so that our defenses will be strong.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask for your support to ensure they can succeed.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I also want to ask you for a constructive bipartisan dialogue this year to work to build a consensus which I hope will eventually lead to the ratification of the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope we can also have a constructive effort to meet the challenge that is presented to our planet by the huge gulf between rich and poor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We cannot accept a world in which part of humanity lives on the cutting edge of a new economy, and the rest live on the bare edge of survival.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I think we have to do our part to change that -- with expanded trade, expanded aid, and the expansion of freedom.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is interesting -- from Nigeria to Indonesia, more people got the right to choose their leaders in 1999 than in 1989, when the Berlin Wall fell.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've got to stand by these democracies -- including, and especially tonight, Colombia, which is fighting narco-traffickers, for its own people's lives and our children's lives.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have proposed a strong two-year package to help Colombia win this fight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to thank the leaders in both parties in both Houses for listening to me and the President of Colombia about it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have got to pass this.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to ask your help.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: A lot is riding on it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And it's so important for the long-term stability of our country, and for what happens in Latin America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I also want you to know I'm going to send you new legislation to go after what these drug barons value the most -- their money.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I hope you'll pass that as well.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In a world where over a billion people live on less than a dollar a day, we also have got to do our part in the global endeavor to reduce the debts of the poorest countries, so they can invest in education, health care and economic growth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's what the Pope and other religious leaders have urged us to do.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And last year, Congress made a down payment on America's share.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to continue that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I thank you for what you did, and ask you to stay the course.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: FINAL CHALLENGES AND THANKS:  I also want to say that America must help more nations to break the bonds of disease.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year in Africa, 10 times as many people died from AIDS as were killed in wars -- 10 times.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The budget I give you invests $150 million more in the fight against this and other infectious killers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And today, I propose a tax credit to speed the development of vaccines for diseases like malaria, TB and AIDS.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask the private sector and our partners around the world to join us in embracing this cause.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can save millions of lives together, and we ought to do it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I also want to mention our final challenge, which, as always, is the most important.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to pass a national security budget that keeps our military the best-trained and best-equipped in the world, with heightened readiness and 21st century weapons.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Which raises salaries for our servicemen and women.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Which protects our veterans.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Which fully funds the diplomacy that keeps our soldiers out of war.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Which makes good on our commitment to pay our U.N. dues and arrears.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to pass this budget.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I also want to say something, if I might, very personal tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The American people watching us at home, with the help of all the commentators, can tell from who stands and who sits, and who claps and who doesn't, that there's still modest differences of opinion in this room.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But I want to thank you for something, every one of you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I want to thank you for the extraordinary support you have given -- Republicans and Democrats alike -- to our men and women in uniform.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I thank you for that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I also want to thank, especially, two people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: First, I want to thank our Secretary of Defense, Bill Cohen, for symbolizing our bipartisan commitment to national security.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you, sir.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Even more, I want to thank his wife, Janet, who, more than any other American citizen, has tirelessly traveled this world to show the support we all feel for our troops.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you, Janet Cohen.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I appreciate that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These are the challenges we have to meet so that we can lead the world toward peace and freedom in an era of globalization.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT:  I want to tell you that I am very grateful for many things as President.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But one of the things I'm grateful for is the opportunity that the Vice President and I have had to finally put to rest the bogus idea that you cannot grow the economy and protect the environment at the same time.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As our economy has grown, we've rid more than 500 neighborhoods of toxic waste, ensured cleaner air and water for millions of people.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the past three months alone, we've helped preserve 40 million acres of roadless lands in the national forests, created three new national monuments.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But as our communities grow, our commitment to conservation must continue to grow.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I propose creating a permanent conservation fund, to restore wildlife, protect coastlines, save natural treasures, from the California redwoods to the Florida Everglades.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This Lands Legacy endowment would represent by far the most enduring investment in land preservation ever proposed in this House.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope we can get together with all the people with different ideas and do this.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is a gift we should give to our children and our grandchildren for all time, across party lines.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can make an agreement to do this.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, the Vice President launched a new effort to make communities more liberal -- livable -- liberal, I know.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Wait a minute, I've got a punchline now.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's this year's agenda.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year was livable, right?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's what Senator Lott is going to say in the commentary afterwards.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To make our communities more livable.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is big business.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is a big issue.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: What does that mean?

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You ask anybody that lives in an unlivable community, and they'll tell you.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They want their kids to grow up next to parks, not parking lots.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The parents don't have to spend all their time stalled in traffic when they could be home with their children.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I ask you to support new funding for the following things, to make American communities for liberal -- livable.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: One -- I've done pretty well with this speech, but I can't say that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: One, I want you to help us to do three things.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need more funding for advanced transit systems.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need more funding for saving open spaces in places of heavy development.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we need more funding -- this ought to have bipartisan appeal -- we need more funding for helping major cities around the Great Lakes protect their waterways and enhance their quality of life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We need these things and I want you to help us.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, the greatest environmental challenge of the new century is global warming.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The scientists tell us the 1990s were the hottest decade of the entire millennium.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: If we fail to reduce the emission of greenhouse gases, deadly heat waves and droughts will become more frequent, coastal areas will flood, and economies will be disrupted.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is going to happen, unless we act.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Many people in the United States -- some people in this chamber -- and lots of folks around the world still believe you cannot cut greenhouse gas emissions without slowing economic growth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In the Industrial Age that may well have been true.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But in this digital economy, it is not true anymore.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: New technologies make it possible to cut harmful emissions and provide even more growth.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For example, just last week, automakers unveiled cars that get 70 to 80 miles a gallon -- the fruits of a unique research partnership between government and industry.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And before you know it, efficient production of bio-fuels will give us the equivalent of hundreds of miles from a gallon of gasoline.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To speed innovation in these kind of technologies, I think we should give a major tax incentive to business for the production of clean energy, and to families for buying energy-saving homes and appliances and the next generation of super-efficient cars when they hit the showroom floor.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I also ask the auto industry to use the available technologies to make all new cars more fuel-efficient right away.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I ask this Congress to do something else.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Please help us make more of our clean energy technology available to the developing world.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That will create cleaner growth abroad and a lot more new jobs here in the United States of America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, in the new century, innovations in science and technology will be the key not only to the health of the environment, but to miraculous improvements in the quality of our lives and advances in the economy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Later this year, researchers will complete the first draft of the entire human genome, the very blueprint of life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It is important for all our fellow Americans to recognize that federal tax dollars have funded much of this research, and that this and other wise investments in science are leading to a revolution in our ability to detect, treat, and prevent disease.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: For example, researchers have identified genes that cause Parkinson's, diabetes, and certain kinds of cancer -- they are designed precision therapies that will block the harmful effect of these genes for good.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Researchers already are using this new technique to target and destroy cells that cause breast cancer.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Soon, we may be able to use it to prevent the onset of Alzheimer's.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Scientists are also working on an artificial retina to help many blind people to see -- and listen to this -- microchips that would actually directly stimulate damaged spinal cords in a way that could allow people now paralyzed to stand up and walk.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These kinds of innovations are also propelling our remarkable prosperity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Information technology only includes 8 percent of our employment, but now it counts for a third of our economic growth -- along with jobs that pay, by the way, about 80 percent above the private sector average.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Again, we ought to keep in mind, government-funded research brought supercomputers, the Internet, and communications satellites into being.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Soon researchers will bring us devices that can translate foreign languages as fast as you can talk.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Materials 10 times stronger than steel at a fraction of the weight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And -- this is unbelievable to me -- molecular computers the size of a tear drop with the power of today's fastest supercomputers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: To accelerate the march of discovery across all these disciplines in science and technology, I ask you to support my recommendation of an unprecedented $3 billion in the 21st Century Research Fund, the largest increase in civilian research in a generation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We owe it to our future.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: TECHNOLOGY WITH VALUES:   Now, these new breakthroughs have to be used in ways that reflect our values.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: First and foremost, we have to safeguard our citizens' privacy.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, we proposed to protect every citizen's medical record.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This year, we will finalize those rules.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We've also taken the first steps to protect the privacy of bank and credit card records and other financial statements.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Soon I will send legislation to you to finish that job.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We must also act to prevent any genetic discrimination whatever by employers or insurers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I hope you will support that.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: These steps will allow us to lead toward the far frontiers of science and technology.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: They will enhance our health, the environment, the economy in ways we can't even imagine today.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we all know that at a time when science, technology and the forces of globalization are bringing so many changes into all our lives, it's more important than ever that we strengthen the bonds that root us in our local communities and in our national community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: No tie binds different people together like citizen service.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: There's a new spirit of service in America -- a movement we've tried to support with AmeriCorps, expanded Peace Corps, unprecedented new partnerships with businesses, foundations, community groups.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Partnerships, for example, like the one that enlisted 12,000 companies which have now moved 650,000 of our fellow citizens from welfare to work.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Partnerships to battle drug abuse, AIDS, teach young people to read, save America's treasures, strengthen the arts, fight teen pregnancy, prevent violence among young people, promote racial healing.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The American people are working together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But we should do more to help Americans help each other.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: First, we should help faith-based organizations to do more to fight poverty and drug abuse, and help people get back on the right track, with initiatives like Second Chance Homes that do so much to help unwed teen mothers.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Second, we should support Americans who tithe and contribute to charities, but don't earn enough to claim a tax deduction for it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Tonight, I propose new tax incentives that would allow low- and middle-income citizens who don't itemize to get that deduction.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: It's nothing but fair, and it will get more people to give.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should do more to help new immigrants to fully participate in our community.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's why I recommend spending more to teach them civics and English.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And since everybody in our community counts, we've got to make sure everyone is counted in this year's census.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now within 10 years -- just 10 years -- there will be no majority race in our largest state of California.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In a little more than 50 years, there will be no majority race in America.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: In a more interconnected world, this diversity can be our greatest strength.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Just look around this chamber.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Look around.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We have members in this Congress from virtually every racial, ethnic, and religious background.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I think you would agree that America is stronger because of it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But you also have to agree that all those differences you just clapped for all too often spark hatred and division even here at home.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Just in the last couple of years, we've seen a man dragged to death in Texas just because he was black.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We saw a young man murdered in Wyoming just because he was gay.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last year, we saw the shootings of African Americans, Asian Americans, and Jewish children just because of who they were.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This is not the American way, and we must draw the line.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I ask you to draw that line by passing without delay the Hate Crimes Prevention Act and the Employment Non-Discrimination Act.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And I ask you to reauthorize the Violence Against Women Act.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: CIVIL RIGHTS PROTECTION:  Finally tonight, I propose the largest-ever investment in our civil rights laws for enforcement, because no American should be subjected to discrimination in finding a home, getting a job, going to school, or securing a loan.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Protections in law should be protections in fact.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Last February, because I thought this was so important, I created the White House Office of One America to promote racial reconciliation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That's what one of my personal heroes, Hank Aaron, has done all his life.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: From his days as our all-time home run king to his recent acts of healing, he has always brought people together.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should follow his example, and we're honored to have him with us tonight.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Stand up, Hank Aaron.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I just want to say one more thing about this, and I want every one of you to think about this the next time you get mad at one of your colleagues on the other side of the aisle.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: This fall, at the White House, Hillary had one of her millennium dinners, and we had this very distinguished scientist there, who is an expert in this whole work in the human genome.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And he said that we are all, regardless of race, genetically 99.9 percent the same.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Now, you may find that uncomfortable when you look around here.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But it is worth remembering.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We can laugh about this, but you think about it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Modern science has confirmed what ancient faiths has always taught: the most important fact of life is our common humanity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Therefore, we should do more than just tolerate our diversity -- we should honor it and celebrate it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: My fellow Americans, every time I prepare for the State of the Union, I approach it with hope and expectation and excitement for our nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: But tonight is very special, because we stand on the mountain top of a new millennium.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Behind us we can look back and see the great expanse of American achievement.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And before us we can see even greater, grander frontiers of possibility.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should, all of us, be filled with gratitude and humility for our present progress and prosperity.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We should be filled with awe and joy at what lies over the horizon.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And we should be filled with absolute determination to make the most of it.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: You know, when the framers finished crafting our Constitution in Philadelphia, Benjamin Franklin stood in Independence Hall and he reflected on the carving of the sun that was on the back of a chair he saw.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: The sun was low on the horizon.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I've often wondered whether that sun was rising or setting.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: I have the happiness to know it's a rising sun.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Today, because each succeeding generation of Americans has kept the fire of freedom burning brightly, lighting those frontiers of possibility, we all still bask in the glow and the warmth of Mr. Franklin's rising sun.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: After 224 years, the American revolution continues.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: We remain a new nation.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: As long as our dreams outweigh our memories, America will be forever young.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: That is our destiny.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: And this is our moment.

speaker: Bill (William J. ) Clinton
text: Thank you, God bless you, and God bless America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I thank you for your invitation to speak here tonight.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I know Congress had to formally invite me, and it could have been a close vote.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So, Mr. Vice President, I appreciate you being here to break the tie.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I want to thank so many of you who have accepted my invitation to come to the White House to discuss important issues.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're off to a good start.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I will continue to meet with you and ask for your input.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You have been kind and candid, and I thank you for making a new President feel welcome.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The last time I visited the Capitol, I came to take an oath on the steps of this building.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On the steps of this building, I pledged to honor our Constitution and laws.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I asked you to join me in setting a tone of civility and respect in Washington.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I hope America is noticing the difference, because we're making progress.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Together, we are changing the tone in the Nation's Capital.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And this spirit of respect and cooperation is vital, because, in the end, we will be judged not only by what we say or how we say it, we will be judged by what we're able to accomplish.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America today is a nation with great challenges, but greater resources.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: An artist using statistics as a brush could paint two very different pictures of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One would have warning signs: increasing layoffs, rising energy prices, too many failing schools, persistent poverty, the stubborn vestiges of racism.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Another picture would be full of blessings: a balanced budget, big surpluses, a military that is second to none, a country at peace with its neighbors, technology that is revolutionizing the world, and our greatest strength -- concerned citizens who care for our country and care for each other.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Neither picture is complete in and of itself.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tonight I challenge and invite Congress to work with me to use the resources of one picture to repaint the other.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To direct the advantages of our time to solve the problems of our people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some of these resources will come from government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some, but not all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Year after year in Washington, budget debates seem to come down to an old, tired argument: on one side, those who want more government, regardless of the cost.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On the other, those who want less government, regardless of the need.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We should leave those arguments to the last century, and chart a different course.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Government has a role, and an important role.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet, too much government crowds out initiative and hard work, private charity and the private economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our new governing vision says government should be active, but limited.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Engaged, but not overbearing.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And my budget is based on that philosophy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It is reasonable, and it is responsible.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It meets our obligations, and funds our growing needs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We increase spending next year for Social Security and Medicare, and other entitlement programs, by $81 billion.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've increased spending for discretionary programs by a very responsible 4 percent, above the rate of inflation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My plan pays down an unprecedented amount of our national debt.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And then, when money is still left over, my plan returns it to the people who earned it in the first place.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A budget's impact is counted in dollars, but measured in lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Excellent schools, quality health care, a secure retirement, a cleaner environment, a stronger defense -- these are all important needs, and we fund them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The highest percentage increase in our budget should go to our children's education.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Education is not my top priority -- education is my top priority and, by supporting this budget, you'll make it yours, as well.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Reading is the foundation of all learning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So during the next five years, we triple spending, adding $5 billion to help every child in America learn to read.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Values are important, so we've tripled funding for character education to teach our children not only reading and writing, but right from wrong.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've increased funding to train and recruit teachers, because we know a good education starts with a good teacher.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I have a wonderful partner in this effort.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I like teachers so much, I married one.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Laura has begun a new effort to recruit Americans to the profession that will shape our future -- teaching.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: She will travel across America to promote sound teaching practices and early reading skills in our schools and in programs such as Head Start.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When it comes to our schools, dollars alone do not always make the difference.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Funding is important, and so is reform.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So we must tie funding to higher standards and accountability for results.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I believe in local control of schools.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We should not, and we will not, run public schools from Washington, D.C.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet when the federal government spends tax dollars, we must insist on results.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Children should be tested on basic reading and math skills every year between grades three and eight.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Measuring is the only way to know whether all our children are learning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I want to know, because I refuse to leave any child behind in America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Critics of testing contend it distracts from learning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They talk about teaching to the test.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But let's put that logic to the test.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If you test a child on basic math and reading skills, and you're teaching to the test, you're teaching math and reading.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And that's the whole idea.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As standards rise, local schools will need more flexibility to meet them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So we must streamline the dozens of federal education programs into five, and let states spend money in those categories as they see fit.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Schools will be given a reasonable chance to improve and the support to do so.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet, if they don't, if they continue to fail, we must give parents and students different options -- a better public school, a private school, tutoring or a charter school.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the end, every child in a bad situation must be given a better choice because, when it comes to our children, failure is simply not an option.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Another priority in my budget is to keep the vital promises of Medicare and Social Security, and together we will do so.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To meet the health care needs of all America's seniors, we double the Medicare budget over the next 10 years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My budget dedicates $238 billion to Medicare next year alone, enough to fund all current programs and to begin a new prescription drug benefit for low-income seniors.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: No senior in America should have to choose between buying food and buying prescriptions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To make sure the retirement savings of America's seniors are not diverted in any other program, my budget protects all $2.6 trillion of the Social Security surplus for Social Security, and for Social Security alone.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My budget puts a priority on access to health care, without telling Americans what doctor they have to see or what coverage they must choose.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many working Americans do not have health care coverage, so we will help them buy their own insurance with refundable tax credits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And to provide quality care in low-income neighborhoods, over the next five years we will double the number of people served at community health care centers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we will address the concerns of those who have health coverage, yet worry their insurance company doesn't care and won't pay.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Together this Congress and this President will find common ground to make sure doctors make medical decisions, and patients get the health care they deserve with a patients' bill of rights.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When it comes to their health, people want to get the medical care they need, not be forced to go to court because they didn't get it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will ensure access to the courts for those with legitimate claims.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But first, let's put in place a strong, independent review  so we promote quality health care, not frivolous lawsuits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My budget also increases funding for medical research, which gives hope to many who struggle with serious disease.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our prayers tonight are with one of your own who is engaged in his own fight against cancer -- a fine representative, and a good man, Congressman Joe Moakley.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I can think of no more appropriate tribute to Joe than to have the Congress finish the job of doubling the budget for the National Institutes of Health.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My new Freedom Initiative for Americans with Disabilities funds new technologies, expands opportunities to work, and makes our society more welcoming.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For the more than 50 million Americans with disabilities, we need to break down barriers to equality.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The budget I propose to you also supports the people who keep our country strong and free, the men and women who serve in the United States military.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I'm requesting $5.7 billion in increased military pay and benefits, and health care and housing.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our men and women in uniform give America their best and we owe them our support.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America's veterans honored their commitment to our country through their military service.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I will honor our commitment to them with a million-dollar increase to ensure better access to quality care and faster decisions on benefit claims.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My budget will improve our environment by accelerating the cleanup of toxic brownfields.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I propose we make a major investment in conservation by fully funding the Land and Water Conservation Fund.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our national parks have a special place in our country's life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our parks are places of great natural beauty and history.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As good stewards, we must leave them better than we found them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So I propose providing $4.9 billion over five years for the upkeep of these national treasures.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And my budget adopts a hopeful new approach to help the poor and the disadvantaged.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must encourage and support the work of charities and faith-based and community groups that offer help and love one person at a time.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These groups are working in every neighborhood in America to fight homelessness and addiction and domestic violence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To provide a hot meal or a mentor or a safe haven for our children.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Government should welcome these groups to apply for funds, not discriminate against them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Government cannot be replaced by charities or volunteers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Government should not fund religious activities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But our nation should support the good works of these good people who are helping their neighbors in need.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So I propose allowing all taxpayers, whether they itemize or not, to deduct their charitable contributions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Estimates show this could encourage as much as $14 billion a year in new charitable giving, money that will save and change lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our budget provides more than $700 million over the next 10 years for a federal compassion capital fund, with a focused and noble mission, to provide a mentor to the more than 100 million children with a parent in prison, and to support other local efforts to fight illiteracy, teen pregnancy, drug addiction and other difficult problems.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With us tonight is the Mayor of Philadelphia.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Please help me welcome Mayor John Street.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Mayor Street has encouraged faith-based and community organizations to make a significant difference in Philadelphia.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He's invited me to his city this summer to see compassionate action.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I'm personally aware of just how effective the Mayor is.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Mayor Street's a Democrat.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Let the record show, I lost his city, big time.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But some things are bigger than politics.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So I look forward to coming to your city, to see your faith-based programs in action.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As government promotes compassion, it also must promote justice.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Too many of our citizens have cause to doubt our nation's justice, when the law points a finger of suspicion at groups, instead of individuals.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: All our citizens are created equal, and must be treated equally.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Earlier today, I asked John Ashcroft, the Attorney General, to develop specific recommendations to end racial profiling.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It's wrong and we will end it in America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In so doing, we will not hinder the work of our nation's brave police officers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They protect us every day -- often at great risk.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But by stopping the abuses of a few, we will add to the public confidence our police officers earn and deserve.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My budget has funded a responsible increase in our ongoing operations.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It has funded our nation's important priorities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It has protected Social Security and Medicare.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And our surpluses are big enough that there is still money left over.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many of you have talked about the need to pay down our national debt.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I listened, and I agree.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We owe it to our children and grandchildren to act now, and I hope you will join me to pay down $2 trillion in debt during the next 10 years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: At the end of those 10 years, we will have paid down all the debt that is available to retire.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That is more debt, repaid more quickly than has ever been repaid by any nation at any time in history.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We should also prepare for the unexpected, for the uncertainties of the future.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We should approach our nation's budget as any prudent family would, with a contingency fund for emergencies or additional spending needs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For example, after a strategic review, we may need to increase defense spending.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We may need to increase spending for our farmers or additional money to reform Medicare.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And so, my budget sets aside almost a trillion dollars over 10 years for additional needs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That is one trillion additional reasons you can feel comfortable supporting this budget.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have increased our budget at a responsible 4 percent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have funded our priorities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We paid down all the available debt.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have prepared for contingencies.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we still have money left over.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: nan

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now, we come to a fork in the road.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have two choices.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Even though we have already met our needs, we could spend the money on more and bigger government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That's the road our nation has traveled in recent years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last year, government spending shot up 8 percent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That's far more than our economy grew, far more than personal income grew, and far more than the rate of inflation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If you continue on that road, you will spend the surplus and have to dip into Social Security to pay other bills.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Unrestrained government spending is a dangerous road to deficits, so we must take a different path.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The other choice is to let the American people spend their own money to meet their own needs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I hope you will join me in standing firmly on the side of the people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You see, the growing surplus exists because taxes are too high and government is charging more than it needs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The people of America have been overcharged and, on their behalf, I am here asking for a refund.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some say my tax plan is too big.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Others say it's too small.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I respectfully disagree.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This plan is just right.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I didn't throw darts at the board to come up with a number for tax relief.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I didn't take a poll or develop an arbitrary formula that might sound good.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I looked at problems in the Tax Code and calculated the cost to fix them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A tax rate of 15 percent is too high for those who earn low wages, so we must lower the rate to 10 percent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: No one should pay more than a third of the money they earn in federal income taxes, so we lowered the top rate to 33 percent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This reform will be welcome relief for America's small businesses, which often pay taxes at the highest rate.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And help for small business means jobs for Americans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We simplified the Tax Code by reducing the number of tax rates from the current five rates to four lower ones, 10 percent, 15, 25 and 33 percent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In my plan, no one is targeted in or targeted out.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Everyone who pays income taxes will get relief.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our government should not tax, and thereby discourage marriage, so we reduced the marriage penalty.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I want to help families rear and support their children, so we doubled the child credit to $1,000 per child.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It's not fair to tax the same earnings twice -- once when you earn them, and again when you die -- so we must repeal the death tax.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These changes add up to significant help.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A typical family with two children will save $1,600 a year on their federal income taxes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now, $1,600 may not sound like a lot to some, but it means a lot to many families: $1,600 buys gas for two cars for an entire year.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It pays tuition for a year at a community college.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It pays the average family grocery bill for three months.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That's real money.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With us tonight representing many American families are Steven and Josefina Ramos.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They are from Pennsylvania.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But they could be from any one of your districts.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Steven is the network administrator for a school district.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Josefina is a Spanish teacher at a charter school.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And they have a two-year-old daughter.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Steven and Josefina tell me they pay almost $8,000 a year in federal income taxes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My plan will save them more than $2,000.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Two thousand dollars a year means a lot to my family.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: nan

speaker: George W. Bush
text: After that, Steven and Josefina want to start saving for Lianna's college education.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My attitude is, government should never stand in the way of families achieving their dreams.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And as we debate this issue, always remember, the surplus is not the government's money, the surplus is the people's money.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For lower-income families, my tax plan restores basic fairness.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Right now, complicated tax rules punish hard work.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A waitress supporting two children on $25,000 a year can lose nearly half of every additional dollar she earns above the $25,000.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Her overtime, her hardest hours, are taxed at nearly 20 percent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This sends a terrible message: you'll never get ahead.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But America's message must be different.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must honor hard work, never punish it.

speaker: George W. Bush
