text: With tax relief, overtime will no longer be over-taxed time for the waitress.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: People with the smallest incomes will get the highest percentage of reductions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And millions of additional American families will be removed from the income tax rolls entirely.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tax relief is right and tax relief is urgent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The long economic expansion that began almost 10 years ago is faltering.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Lower interest rates will eventually help, but we cannot assume they will do the job all by themselves.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Forty years ago, and then 20 years ago, two Presidents, one Democrat, one Republican, John F.Kennedy and Ronald Reagan, advocated tax cuts to, in President Kennedy's words, get this country moving again.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They knew then what we must do now.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To create economic growth and opportunity, we must put money back into the hands of the people who buy goods and create jobs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must act quickly.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The Chairman of the Federal Reserve has testified before Congress that tax cuts often come too late to stimulate economic recovery.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So I want to work with you to give our economy an important jump-start by making tax relief retroactive.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must act now because it is the right thing to do.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must also act now because we have other things to do.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must show courage to confront and resolve tough challenges, to restructure our nation's defenses, to meet our growing need for energy, and to reform Medicare and Social Security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America has a window of opportunity to extend and secure our present peace by promoting a distinctly American internationalism.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will work with our allies and friends to be a force for good and a champion of freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will work for free markets, free trade and freedom from oppression.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Nations making progress toward freedom will find America is their friend.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will promote our values.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will promote the peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we need a strong military to keep the peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But our military was shaped to confront the challenges of the past.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So I've asked the Secretary of Defense to review America's Armed Forces and prepare to transform them to meet emerging threats.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My budget makes a down payment on the research and development that will be required.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet, in our broader transformation effort, we must put strategy first, then spending.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our defense vision will drive our defense budget, not the other way around.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our nation also needs a clear strategy to confront the threats of the 21st century -- threats that are more widespread and less certain.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They range from terrorists who threaten with bombs to tyrants in rogue nations intent upon developing weapons of mass destruction.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To protect our own people, our allies and friends, we must develop and we must deploy effective missile defenses.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And as we transform our military, we can discard Cold War relics, and reduce our own nuclear forces to reflect today's needs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A strong America is the world's best hope for peace and freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet the cause of freedom rests on more than our ability to defend ourselves and our allies.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Freedom is exported every day, as we ship goods and products that improve the lives of millions of people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Free trade brings greater political and personal freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Each of the previous five Presidents has had the ability to negotiate far reaching trade agreements.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I ask you to give me the strong hand of presidential trade promotion authority, and to do so quickly.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As we meet tonight, many citizens are struggling with the high cost of energy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have a serious energy problem that demands a national energy policy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The West is confronting a major energy shortage that has resulted in high prices and uncertainty.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I've asked federal agencies to work with California officials to help speed construction of new energy sources, and I have direct Vice President Cheney, Commerce Secretary Evans, Energy Secretary Abraham and other senior members in my administration to develop a national energy policy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our energy demand outstrips our supply.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We can produce more energy at home while protecting our environment, and we must.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We can produce more electricity to meet demand, and we must.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We can promote alternative energy sources and conservation, and we must.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America must become more energy-independent, and we will.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Perhaps the biggest test of our foresight and courage will be reforming Medicare and Social Security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Medicare's finances are strained and its coverage is outdated.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Ninety-nine percent of employer-provided health plans offer some form of prescription drug coverage.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Medicare does not.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The framework for reform has been developed by Senators Frist and Breaux and Congressman Thomas, and now is the time to act.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Medicare must be modernized, and we must make sure that every senior on Medicare can choose a health care plan that offers prescription drugs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Seven years from now, the baby boom generation will begin to claim Social Security benefits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Every one in this chamber knows that Social Security is not prepared to fully fund their retirement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we only have a couple of years to get prepared.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Without reform, this country will one day awaken to a stark choice: either a drastic rise in payroll taxes or a radical cut in retirement benefits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There is a better way.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This spring I will form a presidential commission to reform Social Security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The commission will make its recommendations by next fall.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Reform should be based on these principles: It must preserve the benefits of all current retirees and those nearing retirement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It must return Social Security to sound financial footing.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And it must offer personal savings accounts to younger workers who want them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Social Security now offers workers a return of less than 2 percent on the money they pay into the system.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To save the system, we must increase that by allowing younger workers to make safe, sound investments that yield a higher rate of return.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Ownership, access to wealth and independence should not be the privilege of the few.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They are the hope of every American, and we must make them the foundation of Social Security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By confronting the tough challenge of reform, by being responsible with our budget, we can earn the trust of the American people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we can add to that trust by enacting fair and balanced election and campaign reforms.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The agenda I have set before you tonight is worthy of a great nation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is a nation at peace, but not a nation at rest.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Much has been given to us, and much is expected.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Let us agree to bridge old divides.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But let us also agree that our goodwill must be dedicated to great goals.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Bipartisan is more than minding our matters.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It is doing our duty.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: No one can speak in this Capitol and not be awed by its history.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As so many turning points, debates in these chambers have reflected the collected or divided conscience of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And when we walk through Statuary Hall and see those men and women of marble, we're reminded of their courage and achievement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet America's purpose is never found only in statues or history.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America's purpose always stands before us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our generation must show courage in a time of blessing, as our nation has always shown in times of crisis.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And our courage, issue by issue, can gather to greatness and serve our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This is the privilege and responsibility we share.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And if we work together, we can prove that public service is noble.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We all came here for a reason.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We all have things we want to accomplish and promises to keep.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Juntos podemos -- together we can.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We can make Americans proud of their government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Together we can share in the credit of making our country more prosperous and generous and just, and earn from our conscience and from our fellow citizens the highest possible praise: Well done, good and faithful servants.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Thank you all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Good night and God bless.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Mr. Speaker, Vice President Cheney, members of Congress, distinguished guests, fellow citizens, as we gather tonight, our nation is at war, our economy is in recession and the civilized world faces unprecedented dangers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet the state of our union has never been stronger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We last met in an hour of shock and suffering.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In four short months, our nation has comforted the victims, begun to rebuild New York and the Pentagon, rallied a great coalition, captured, arrested and rid the world of thousands of terrorists, destroyed Afghanistan's terrorist training camps, saved a people from starvation and freed a country from brutal oppression.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The American flag flies again over our embassy in Kabul.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Terrorists who once occupied Afghanistan now occupy cells at Guantanamo Bay.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And terrorist leaders who urged followers to sacrifice their lives are running for their own.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America and Afghanistan are now allies against terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will be partners in rebuilding that country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And this evening we welcome the distinguished interim leader of a liberated Afghanistan: Chairman Hamid Karzai.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The last time we met in this chamber, the mothers and daughters of Afghanistan were captives in their own homes, forbidden from working or going to school.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Today women are free, and are part of Afghanistan's new government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we welcome the new minister of women's affairs, Dr.Sima Samar.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our progress is a tribute to the spirit of the Afghan people, to the resolve of our coalition and to the might of the United States military.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When I called our troops into action, I did so with complete confidence in their courage and skill.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tonight, thanks to them, we are winning the war on terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The men and women of our armed forces have delivered a message now clear to every enemy of the United States: Even 7,000 miles away, across oceans and continents, on mountaintops and in caves you will not escape the justice of this nation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For many Americans, these four months have brought sorrow and pain that will never completely go away.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Every day a retired firefighter returns to Ground Zero to feel closer to his two sons who died there.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: At a memorial in New York, a little boy left his football with a note for his lost father: Dear Daddy, please take this to Heaven.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I don't want to play football until I can play with you again someday.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: nan

speaker: George W. Bush
text: OUR CAUSE IS JUST':  Shannon is with us tonight.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Shannon, I assure you and all who have lost a loved one that our cause is just, and our country will never forget the debt we owe Micheal and all who gave their lives for freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our cause is just, and it continues.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our discoveries in Afghanistan confirmed our worst fears and showed us the true scope of the task ahead.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have seen the depth of our enemies' hatred in videos where they laugh about the loss of innocent life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And the depth of their hatred is equaled by the madness of the destruction they design.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have found diagrams of American nuclear power plants and public water facilities, detailed instructions for making chemical weapons, surveillance maps of American cities, and thorough descriptions of landmarks in America and throughout the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: What we have found in Afghanistan confirms that, far from ending there, our war against terror is only beginning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Most of the 19 men who hijacked planes on September the 11th were trained in Afghanistan's camps.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And so were tens of thousands of others.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Thousands of dangerous killers, schooled in the methods of murder, often supported by outlaw regimes, are now spread throughout the world like ticking time bombs, set to go off without warning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Thanks to the work of our law enforcement officials and coalition partners, hundreds of terrorists have been arrested, yet tens of thousands of trained terrorists are still at large.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These enemies view the entire world as a battlefield, and we must pursue them wherever they are.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So long as training camps operate, so long as nations harbor terrorists, freedom is at risk and America and our allies must not, and will not, allow it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our nation will continue to be steadfast, and patient and persistent in the pursuit of two great objectives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: First, we will shut down terrorist camps, disrupt terrorist plans and bring terrorists to justice.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And second, we must prevent the terrorists and regimes who seek chemical, biological or nuclear weapons from threatening the United States and the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our military has put the terror training camps of Afghanistan out of business, yet camps still exist in at least a dozen countries.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A terrorist underworld -- including groups like Hamas, Hezbollah, Islamic Jihad and Jaish-i-Mohammed -- operates in remote jungles and deserts, and hides in the centers of large cities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: While the most visible military action is in Afghanistan, America is acting elsewhere.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We now have troops in the Philippines helping to train that country's armed forces to go after terrorist cells that have executed an American and still hold hostages.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our soldiers, working with the Bosnian government, seized terrorists who were plotting to bomb our embassy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our Navy is patrolling the coast of Africa to block the shipment of weapons and the establishment of terrorist camps in Somalia.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My hope is that all nations will heed our call and eliminate the terrorist parasites who threaten their countries and our own.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many nations are acting forcefully.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Pakistan is now cracking down on terror, and I admire the strong leadership of President Musharraf.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But some governments will be timid in the face of terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And make no mistake about it: If they do not act, America will.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: AXIS OF EVIL:  Our second goal is to prevent regimes that sponsor terror from threatening America or our friends and allies with weapons of mass destruction.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some of these regimes have been pretty quiet since September 11, but we know their true nature.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: North Korea is a regime arming with missiles and weapons of mass destruction, while starving its citizens.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iran aggressively pursues these weapons and exports terror, while an unelected few repress the Iranian people's hope for freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iraq continues to flaunt its hostility toward America and to support terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The Iraqi regime has plotted to develop anthrax and nerve gas and nuclear weapons for over a decade.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This is a regime that has already used poison gas to murder thousands of its own citizens, leaving the bodies of mothers huddled over their dead children.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This is a regime that agreed to international inspections then kicked out the inspectors.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This is a regime that has something to hide from the civilized world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: States like these, and their terrorist allies, constitute an axis of evil, arming to threaten the peace of the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By seeking weapons of mass destruction, these regimes pose a grave and growing danger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They could provide these arms to terrorists, giving them the means to match their hatred.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They could attack our allies or attempt to blackmail the United States.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In any of these cases, the price of indifference would be catastrophic.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will work closely with our coalition to deny terrorists and their state sponsors the materials, technology and expertise to make and deliver weapons of mass destruction.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will develop and deploy effective missile defenses to protect America and our allies from sudden attack.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And all nations should know: America will do what is necessary to ensure our nation's security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We'll be deliberate, yet time is not on our side.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I will not wait on events while dangers gather.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I will not stand by as peril draws closer and closer.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The United States of America will not permit the world's most dangerous regimes to threaten us with the world's most destructive weapons.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our war on terror is well begun, but it is only begun.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This campaign may not be finished on our watch, yet it must be and it will be waged on our watch.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We can't stop short.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If we stopped now, leaving terror camps intact and terror states unchecked, our sense of security would be false and temporary.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: History has called America and our allies to action, and it is both our responsibility and our privilege to fight freedom's fight.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: BUDGET PRIORITIES:  Our first priority must always be the security of our nation, and that will be reflected in the budget I send to Congress.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My budget supports three great goals for America: We will win this war, we will protect our homeland, and we will revive our economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: September 11 brought out the best in America and the best in this Congress, and I join the American people in applauding your unity and resolve.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now Americans deserve to have this same spirit directed toward addressing problems here at home.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I am a proud member of my party.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet as we act to win the war, protect our people and create jobs in America, we must act first and foremost not as Republicans, not as Democrats, but as Americans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It costs a lot to fight this war.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have spent more than a billion dollars a month -- over $30 million a day -- and we must be prepared for future operations.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Afghanistan proved that expensive precision weapons defeat the enemy and spare innocent lives, and we need more of them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We need to replace aging aircraft and make our military more agile to put our troops anywhere in the world quickly and safely.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our men and women in uniform deserve the best weapons, the best equipment and the best training and they also deserve another pay raise.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My budget includes the largest increase in defense spending in two decades, because while the price of freedom and security is high, it is never too high.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Whatever it costs to defend our country, we will pay.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The next priority of my budget is to do everything possible to protect our citizens and strengthen our nation against the ongoing threat of another attack.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Time and distance from the events of September the 11th will not make us safer unless we act on its lessons.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is no longer protected by vast oceans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are protected from attack only by vigorous action abroad and increased vigilance at home.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My budget nearly doubles funding for a sustained strategy of homeland security, focused on four key areas: bioterrorism.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Emergency response.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Airport and border security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And improved intelligence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will develop vaccines to fight anthrax and other deadly diseases.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We'll increase funding to help states and communities train and equip our heroic police and firefighters.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will improve intelligence collection and sharing, expand patrols at our borders, strengthen the security of air travel, and use technology to track the arrivals and departures of visitors to the United States.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Homeland security will make America not only stronger but in many ways better.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Knowledge gained from bioterrorism research will improve public health.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Stronger police and fire departments will mean safer neighborhoods.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Stricter border enforcement will help combat illegal drugs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And as government works to better secure our homeland, America will continue to depend on the eyes and ears of alert citizens.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A few days before Christmas, an airline flight attendant spotted a passenger lighting a match.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The crew and passengers quickly subdued the man, who had been trained by al Qaeda and was armed with explosives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The people on that airplane were alert, and as a result likely saved nearly 200 lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tonight we welcome and thank flight attendants Hermis Moutardier and Christina Jones.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: ANTICIPATING A 'SHORT-TERM' DEFICIT:  Once we have funded our national security and our homeland security, the final great priority of my budget is economic security for the American people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To achieve these great national objectives -- to win the war, protect the homeland and revitalize our economy -- our budget will run a deficit that will be small and short term so long as Congress restrains spending and acts in a fiscally responsible way.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Americans who have lost their jobs need our help, and I support extending unemployment benefits and direct assistance for health care coverage.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet American workers want more than unemployment checks.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They want a steady paycheck.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When America works, America prospers, so my economic security plan can be summed up in one word: jobs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Good jobs begin with good schools, and here we've made a fine start.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Republicans and Democrats worked together to achieve historic education reform so that no child is left behind.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I was proud to work with members of both parties, Chairman John Boehner and Congressman George Miller, Senator Judd Gregg.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I was so proud of our work I even had nice things to say about my friend Ted Kennedy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A CALL FOR PERMANENT TAX CREDITS:  There's more to do.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We need to prepare our children to read and succeed in school with improved Head Start and early childhood development programs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must upgrade our teacher colleges and teacher training and launch a major recruiting drive with a great goal for America: a quality teacher in every classroom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Good jobs also depend on reliable and affordable energy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This Congress must act to encourage conservation, promote technology, build infrastructure, and it must act to increase energy production at home so America is less dependent on foreign oil.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Good jobs depend on expanded trade.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Selling into new markets creates new jobs, so I ask Congress to finally approve trade promotion authority.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On these two key issues, trade and energy, the House of Representatives has acted to create jobs and I urge the Senate to pass this legislation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Good jobs depend on sound tax policy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last year, some in this hall thought my tax relief plan was too small, some thought it was too big.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But when those checks arrived in the mail, most Americans thought tax relief was just about right.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Congress listened to the people and responded by reducing tax rates, doubling the child credit and ending the death tax.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For the sake of long-term growth, and to help Americans plan for the future, let's make these tax cuts permanent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The way out of this recession, the way to create jobs, is to grow the economy by encouraging investment in factories and equipment, and by speeding up tax relief so people have more money to spend.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For the sake of American workers, let's pass a stimulus package.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: ENSURING RETIREMENT SECURITY:  Good jobs must be the aim of welfare reform.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As we reauthorize these important reforms, we must always remember: The goal is to reduce dependency on government and offer every American the dignity of a job.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Americans know economic security can vanish in an instant without health security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask Congress to join me this year to enact a Patients' Bill of Rights to give uninsured workers credits to help buy health coverage, to approve an historic increase in spending for veterans' health and to give seniors a sound and modern Medicare system that includes coverage for prescription drugs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A good job job should lto security in retirement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask Congress to enact new safeguards for 401(k) and pension plans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Employees who have worked hard and saved all their lives should not have to risk losing everything if their company fails.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Through stricter accounting standards and tougher disclosure requirements, corporate America must be made more accountable to employees and shareholders and held to the highest standards of conduct.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Retirement security also depends upon keeping the commitments of Social Security, and we will.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must make Social Security financially stable and allow personal retirement accounts for younger workers who choose them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Members, you and I will work together in the months ahead on other issues: productive farm policy, a cleaner environment, broader home ownership, especially among minorities and ways to encourage the good work of charities and faith-based groups.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask you to join me on these important domestic issues in the same spirit of cooperation we have applied to our war against terrorism.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: During these last few months, I've been humbled and privileged to see the true character of this country in a time of testing.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our enemies believed America was weak and materialistic, that we would splinter in fear and selfishness.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They were as wrong as they are evil.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The American people have responded magnificently, with courage and compassion, strength and resolve.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As I have met the heroes, hugged the families and looked into the tired faces of rescuers, I have stood in awe of the American people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I hope you will join me in expressing thanks to one American for the strength and calm and comfort she brings to our nation in crisis: our first lady, Laura Bush.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: CREATING A 'FREEDOM CORPS':  None of us would ever wish the evil that was done on September 11th, yet after America was attacked, it was as if our entire country looked into a mirror and saw our better selves.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We were reminded that we are citizens, with obligations to each other, to our country and to history.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We began to think less of the goods we can accumulate and more about the good we can do.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For too long our culture has said, If it feels good, do it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now America is embracing a new ethic and a new creed: Let's roll.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the sacrifice of soldiers, the fierce brotherhood of firefighters, and the bravery and generosity of ordinary citizens, we have glimpsed what a new culture of responsibility could look like.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We want to be a Nation that serves goals larger than self.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have been offered a unique opportunity, and we must not let this moment pass.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My call tonight is for every American to commit at least two years, 4,000 hours over the rest of your lifetime, to the service of your neighbors and your nation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many are already serving and I thank you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If you aren't sure how to help, I've got a good place to start.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To sustain and extend the best that has emerged in America, I invite you to join the new USA Freedom Corps.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The Freedom Corps will focus on three areas of need: responding in case of crisis at home, rebuilding our communities, and extending American compassion throughout the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One purpose of the USA Freedom Corps will be homeland security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America needs retired doctors and nurses who can be mobilized in major emergencies.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: volunteers to help police and fire departments, transportation and utility workers well-trained in spotting danger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our country also needs citizens working to rebuild our communities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We need mentors to love children, especially children whose parents are in prison, and we need more talented teachers in troubled schools.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: USA Freedom Corps will expand and improve the good efforts of AmeriCorps and Senior Corps to recruit more than 200,000 new volunteers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And America needs citizens to extend the compassion of our country to every part of the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So we will renew the promise of the Peace Corps, double its volunteers over the next five years, and ask it to join a new effort to encourage development, and education, and opportunity in the Islamic world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This time of adversity offers a unique moment of opportunity, a moment we must seize to change our culture.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Through the gathering momentum of millions of acts of service and decency and kindness, I know: We can overcome evil with greater good.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we have a great opportunity during this time of war to lead the world toward the values that will bring lasting peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: All fathers and mothers, in all societies, want their children to be educated and live free from poverty and violence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: No people on Earth yearn to be oppressed, or aspire to servitude, or eagerly await the midnight knock of the secret police.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If anyone doubts this, let them look to Afghanistan, where the Islamic street greeted the fall of tyranny with song and celebration.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Let the skeptics look to Islam's own rich history -- with its centuries of learning, and tolerance, and progress.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: DEFENSE OF 'HUMAN DIGNITY':  America will lead by defending liberty and justice because they are right and true and unchanging for all people everywhere.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: No nation owns these aspirations, and no nation is exempt from them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have no intention of imposing our culture -- but America will always stand firm for the non-negotiable demands of human dignity: the rule of law.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Limits on the power of the state.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Respect for women.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Private property.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Free speech.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Equal justice.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And religious tolerance.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America will take the side of brave men and women who advocate these values around the world -- including the Islamic world -- because we have a greater objective than eliminating threats and containing resentment.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We seek a just and peaceful world beyond the war on terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In this moment of opportunity, a common danger is erasing old rivalries.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is working with Russia, China, and India in ways we never have before to achieve peace and prosperity.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In every region, free markets and free trade and free societies are proving their power to lift lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Together with friends and allies from Europe to Asia, from Africa to Latin America, we will demonstrate that the forces of terror cannot stop the momentum of freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The last time I spoke here, I expressed the hope that life would return to normal.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In some ways, it has.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In others, it never will.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Those of us who have lived through these challenging times have been changed by them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've come to know truths that we will never question: Evil is real, and it must be opposed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Beyond all differences of race or creed, we are one country, mourning together and facing danger together.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Deep in the American character, there is honor, and it is stronger than cynicism.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And many have discovered again that even in tragedy, especially in tragedy, God is near.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In a single instant, we realized that this will be a decisive decade in the history of liberty -- that we have been called to a unique role in human events.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Rarely has the world faced a choice more clear or consequential.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our enemies send other people's children on missions of suicide and murder.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They embrace tyranny and death as a cause and a creed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We stand for a different choice -- made long ago, on the day of our founding.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We affirm it again today.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We choose freedom and the dignity of every life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Steadfast in our purpose, we now press on.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have known freedom's price.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have shown freedom's power.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And in this great conflict, my fellow Americans, we will see freedom's victory.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Thank you, thank you all, and may God bless.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Mr. Speaker, Vice President Cheney, Members of Congress, distinguished citizens and fellow citizens: Every year, by law and by custom, we meet here to consider the state of the Union.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This year, we gather in this Chamber deeply aware of decisive days that lie ahead.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You and I serve our country in a time of great consequence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: During this session of Congress, we have the duty to reform domestic programs vital to our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have the opportunity to save millions of lives abroad from a terrible disease.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will work for a prosperity that is broadly shared, and we will answer every danger and every enemy that threatens the American people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In all these days of promise and days of reckoning, we can be confident.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In a whirlwind of change and hope and peril, our faith is sure;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: our resolve is firm;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: and our Union is strong.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This country has many challenges.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will not deny, we will not ignore, we will not pass along our problems to other Congresses, to other Presidents, and other generations.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will confront them with focus and clarity and courage.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: During the last 2 years, we have seen what can be accomplished when we work together.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To lift the standards of our public schools, we achieved historic education reform, which must now be carried out in every school and in every classroom so that every child in America can read and learn and succeed in life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To protect our country, we reorganized our Government and created the Department of Homeland Security, which is mobilizing against the threats of a new era.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To bring our economy out of recession, we delivered the largest tax relief in a generation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To insist on integrity in American business, we passed tough reforms, and we are holding corporate criminals to account.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some might call this a good record.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I call it a good start.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I ask the House and the Senate to join me in the next bold steps to serve our fellow citizens.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our first goal is clear: We must have an economy that grows fast enough to employ every man and woman who seeks a job.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: After recession, terrorist attacks, corporate scandals, and stock market declines, our economy is recovering.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet, it's not growing fast enough or strongly enough.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With unemployment rising, our Nation needs more small businesses to open, more companies to invest and expand, more employers to put up the sign that says, ``Help Wanted.''

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Jobs are created when the economy grows.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The economy grows when Americans have more money to spend and invest, and the best and fairest way to make sure Americans have that money is not to tax it away in the first place.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I am proposing that all the income-tax reductions set for 2004 and 2006 be made permanent and effective this year.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And under my plan, as soon as I've signed the bill, this extra money will start showing up in workers' paychecks.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Instead of gradually reducing the marriage penalty, we should do it now.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Instead of slowly raising the child credit to $1,000, we should send the checks to American families now.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The tax relief is for everyone who pays income taxes, and it will help our economy immediately: 92 million Americans will keep, this year, an average of almost $1,100 more of their own money;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: a family of 4 with an income of $40,000 would see their Federal income taxes fall from $1,178 to $45 per year;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: our plan will improve the bottom line for more than 23 million small businesses.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You, the Congress, have already passed all these reductions and promised them for future years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If this tax relief is good for Americans 3, or 5, or 7 years from now, it is even better for Americans today.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We should also strengthen the economy by treating investors equally in our tax laws.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It's fair to tax a company's profits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It is not fair to again tax the shareholder on the same profits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To boost investor confidence and to help the nearly 10 million seniors who receive dividend income, I ask you to end the unfair double taxation of dividends.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Lower taxes and greater investment will help this economy expand.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: More jobs mean more taxpayers and higher revenues to our Government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The best way to address the deficit and move toward a balanced budget is to encourage economic growth and to show some spending discipline in Washington, DC.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must work together to fund only our most important priorities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I will send you a budget that increases discretionary spending by 4 percent next year, about as much as the average family's income is expected to grow.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And that is a good benchmark for us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Federal spending should not rise any faster than the paychecks of American families.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A growing economy and a focus on essential priorities will be crucial to the future of Social Security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As we continue to work together to keep Social Security sound and reliable, we must offer younger workers a chance to invest in retirement accounts that they will control and they will own.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our second goal is high quality, affordable health for all Americans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The American system of medicine is a model of skill and innovation, with a pace of discovery that is adding good years to our lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet for many people, medical care costs too much, and many have no health coverage at all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These problems will not be solved with a nationalized health care system that dictates coverage and rations care.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Instead, we must work toward a system in which all Americans have a good insurance policy, choose their own doctors, and seniors and low-income Americans receive the help they need.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Instead of bureaucrats and trial lawyers and HMOs, we must put doctors and nurses and patients back in charge of American medicine.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Health care reform must begin with Medicare.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Medicare is the binding commitment of a caring society.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must renew that commitment by giving seniors access to preventive medicine and new drugs that are transforming health care in America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Seniors happy with the current Medicare system should be able to keep their coverage just the way it is.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And just like you, the Members of Congress, and your staffs and other Federal employees, all seniors should have the choice of a health care plan that provides prescription drugs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My budget will commit an additional $400 billion over the next decade to reform and strengthen Medicare.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Leaders of both political parties have talked for years about strengthening Medicare.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I urge the Members of this new Congress to act this year.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To improve our health care system, we must address one of the prime causes of higher cost, the constant threat that physicians and hospitals will be unfairly sued.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Because of excessive litigation, everybody pays more for health care, and many parts of America are losing fine doctors.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: No one has ever been healed by a frivolous lawsuit.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I urge the Congress to pass medical liability reform.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our third goal is to promote energy independence for our country, while dramatically improving the environment.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I have sent you a comprehensive energy plan to promote energy efficiency and conservation, to develop cleaner technology, and to produce more energy at home.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I have sent you Clear Skies legislation that mandates a 70-percent cut in air pollution from powerplants over the next 15 years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I have sent you a Healthy Forests Initiative, to help prevent the catastrophic fires that devastate communities, kill wildlife, and burn away millions of acres of treasured forests.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I urge you to pass these measures, for the good of both our environment and our economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Even more, I ask you to take a crucial step and protect our environment in ways that generations before us could not have imagined.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In this century, the greatest environmental progress will come about not through endless lawsuits or command-and-control regulations but through technology and innovation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I'm proposing $1.2 billion in research funding so that America can lead the world in developing clean,hydrogen-powered automobiles.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A simple chemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen generates energy, which can be used to power a car, producing only water, not exhaust fumes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With a new national commitment, our scientists and engineers will overcome obstacles to taking these cars from laboratory to showroom, so that the first car driven by a child born today could be powered by hydrogen and pollution-free.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Join me in this important innovation to make our air significantly cleaner and our country much less dependent on foreign sources of energy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our fourth goal is to apply the compassion of America to the deepest problems of America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For so many in our country, the homeless and the fatherless, the addicted, the need is great.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet there's power, wonder-working power, in the goodness and idealism and faith of the American people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Americans are doing the work of compassion every day, visiting prisoners, providing shelter for battered women, bringing companionship to lonely seniors.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These good works deserve our praise.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They deserve our personal support, and when appropriate, they deserve the assistance of the Federal Government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I urge you to pass both my Faith-Based Initiative and the Citizen Service Act, to encourage acts of compassion that can transform America,one heart and one soul at a time.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last year, I called on my fellow citizens to participate in the USA Freedom Corps, which is enlisting tens of thousands of new volunteers across America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I ask Congress and the American people to focus the spirit of service and the resources of Government on the needs of some of our most vulnerable citizens -- boys and girls trying to grow up without guidance and attention...and children who have to go through a prison gate to be hugged by their mom or their dad.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I propose a $450 million initiative to bring mentors to more than a million disadvantaged junior high students and children of prisoners.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Government will support the training and recruiting of mentors.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet it is the men and women of America who will fill the need.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One mentor, one person can change a life forever, and I urge you to be that one person.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Another cause of hopelessness is addiction to drugs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Addiction crowds out friendship, ambition, moral conviction and reduces all the richness of life to a single destructive desire.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As a government, we are fighting illegal drugs by cutting off supplies and reducing demand through antidrug education programs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet for those already addicted, the fight against drugs is a fight for their own lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Too many Americans in search of treatment cannot get it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So tonight I propose a new $600 million program to help an additional 300,000 Americans receive treatment over the next 3 years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our Nation is blessed with recovery programs that do amazing work.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One of them is found at the Healing Place Church in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A man in the program said, ``God does miracles in people's lives, and you never think it could be you.''

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight let us bring to all Americans who struggle with drug addiction this message of hope: The miracle of recovery is possible, and it could be you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By caring for children who need mentors and for addicted men and women who need treatment, we are building a more welcoming society, a culture that values every life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And in this work, we must not overlook the weakest among us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask you to protect infants at the very hour of their birth and end the practice of partial-birth abortion.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And because no human life should be started or ended as the object of an experiment, I ask you to set a high standard for humanity and pass a law against all human cloning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The qualities of courage and compassion that we strive for in America also determine our conduct abroad.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The American flag stands for more than our power and our interests.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our Founders dedicated this country to the cause of human dignity, the rights of every person, and the possibilities of every life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This conviction leads us into the world to help the afflicted and defend the peace and confound the designs of evil men.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In Afghanistan, we helped to liberate an oppressed people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we will continue helping them secure their country, rebuild their society, and educate all their children, boys and girls.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the Middle East, we will continue to seek peace between a secure Israel and a democratic Palestine.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Across the Earth, America is feeding the hungry.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: More than 60 percent of international food aid comes as a gift from the people of the United States.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As our Nation moves troops and builds alliances to make our world safer, we must also remember our calling as a blessed country is to make the world better.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Today, on the continent of Africa, nearly 30 million people have the AIDS virus, including 3 million children under the age 15.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There are whole countries in Africa where more than one-third of the adult population carries the infection.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: More than 4 million require immediate drug treatment.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet across that continent, only 50,000 AIDS victims--only 50,000--are receiving the medicine they need.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Because the AIDS diagnosis is considered a death sentence, many do not seek treatment.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Almost all who do are turned away.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A doctor in rural South Africa describes his frustration.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He says, ``We have no medicines.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many hospitals tell people, `You've got AIDS.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We can't help you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Go home and die.' ''

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In an age of miraculous medicines, no person should have to hear those words.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: AIDS can be prevented.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Antiretroviral drugs can extend life for many years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And the cost of those drugs has dropped from $12,000 a year to under $300 a year, which places a tremendous possibility within our grasp.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Ladies and gentlemen, seldom has history offered a greater opportunity to do so much for so many.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have confronted and will continue to confront HIV/AIDS in our own country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And to meet a severe and urgent crisis abroad, tonight I propose the Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief, a work of mercy beyond all current international efforts to help the people of Africa.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This comprehensive plan will prevent 7 million new AIDS infections, treat at least 2 million people with life-extending drugs, and provide humane care for millions of people suffering from AIDS and for children orphaned by AIDS.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask the Congress to commit $15 billion over the next 5 years, including nearly $10 billion in new money, to turn the tide against AIDS in the most afflicted nations of Africa and the Caribbean.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This Nation can lead the world in sparing innocent people from a plague of nature.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And this Nation is leading the world in confronting and defeating the manmade evil of international terrorism.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There are days when our fellow citizens do not hear news about the war on terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There's never a day when I do not learn of another threat or receive reports of operations in progress or give an order in this global war against a scattered network of killers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The war goes on, and we are winning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To date, we've arrested or otherwise dealt with many key commanders of Al Qaida.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They include a man who directed logistics and funding for the September the 11th attacks, the chief of Al Qaida operations in the Persian Gulf who planned the bombings of our embassies in east Africa and the U.S.S.Cole, an Al Qaida operations chief from S

speaker: George W. Bush
text: All told, more than 3,000 suspected terrorists have been arrested in many countries.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many others have met a different fate.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Let's put it this way: They are no longer a problem to the United States and our friends and allies.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are working closely with other nations to prevent further attacks.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America and coalition countries have uncovered and stopped terrorist conspiracies targeting the Embassy in Yemen, the American Embassy in Singapore, a Saudi military base, ships in the Straits of Hormuz and the Straits of Gibraltar.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've broken Al Qaida cells in Hamburg, Milan, Madrid, London, Paris, as well as Buffalo, New York.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have the terrorists on the run.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're keeping them on the run.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One by one, the terrorists are learning the meaning of American justice.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As we fight this war, we will remember where it began: Here, in our own country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This Government is taking unprecedented measures to protect our people and defend our homeland.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've intensified security at the borders and ports of entry, posted more than 50,000 newly trained Federal screeners in airports, begun inoculating troops and first-responders against smallpox, and are deploying the Nation's first early warning network o

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And this year, for the first time, we are beginning to field a defense to protect this Nation against ballistic missiles.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I thank the Congress for supporting these measures.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask you tonight to add to our future security with a major research and production effort to guard our people against bioterrorism, called Project BioShield.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The budget I send you will propose almost $6 billion to quickly make available effective vaccines and treatments against agents like anthrax, botulinum toxin, Ebola, and plague.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must assume that our enemies would use these diseases as weapons, and we must act before the dangers are upon us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Since September the 11th, our intelligence and law enforcement agencies have worked more closely than ever to track and disrupt the terrorists.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The FBI is improving its ability to analyze intelligence and is transforming itself to meet new threats.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I am instructing the leaders of the FBI, the CIA, the Homeland Security, and the Department of Defense to develop a Terrorist Threat Integration Center, to merge and analyze all threat information in a single location.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our Government must have the very best information possible, and we will use it to make sure the right people are in the right places to protect all our citizens.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our war against terror is a contest of will in which perseverance is power.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the ruins of two towers, at the western wall of the Pentagon, on a field in Pennsylvania, this Nation made a pledge, and we renew that pledge tonight: Whatever the duration of this struggle and whatever the difficulties, we will not permit the triumph

speaker: George W. Bush
text: free people will set the course of history.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Today, the gravest danger in the war on terror, the gravest danger facing America and the world, is outlaw regimes that seek and possess nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These regimes could use such weapons for blackmail, terror, and mass murder.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They could also give or sell those weapons to terrorist allies, who would use them without the least hesitation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This threat is new.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America's duty is familiar.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Throughout the 20th century, small groups of men seized control of great nations, built armies and arsenals, and set out to dominate the weak and intimidate the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In each case, their ambitions of cruelty and murder had no limit.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In each case, the ambitions of Hitlerism, militarism, and communism were defeated by the will of free peoples, by the strength of great alliances, and by the might of the United States of America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now, in this century, the ideology of power and domination has appeared again and seeks to gain the ultimate weapons of terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Once again, this Nation and all our friends are all that stand between a world at peace and a world of chaos and constant alarm.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Once again, we are called to defend the safety of our people and the hopes of all mankind.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we accept this responsibility.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is making a broad and determined effort to confront these dangers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have called on the United Nations to fulfill its charter and stand by its demand that Iraq disarm.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're strongly supporting the International Atomic Energy Agency in its mission to track and control nuclear materials aroundthe world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're working with other governments to secure nuclear materials in the former Soviet Union and to strengthen global treaties banning the production and shipment of missile technologies and weapons of mass destruction.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In all these efforts, however, America's purpose is more than to follow a process;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: it is to achieve a result, the end of terrible threats to the civilized world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: All free nations have a stake in preventing sudden and catastrophic attacks.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we're asking them to join us, and many are doing so.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet the course of this Nation does not depend on the decisions of others.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Whatever action is required, whenever action is necessary, I will defend the freedom and security of the American people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Different threats require different strategies.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In Iran, we continue to see a Government that represses its people, pursues weapons of mass destruction, and supports terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We also see Iranian citizens risking intimidation and death as they speak out for liberty and human rights and democracy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iranians, like all people, have a right to choose their own Government and determine their own destiny, and the United States supports their aspirations to live in freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On the Korean Peninsula, an oppressive regime rules a people living in fear and starvation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Throughout the 1990s, the United States relied on a negotiated framework to keep North Korea from gaining nuclear weapons.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We now know that that regime was deceiving the world and developing those weapons all along.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And today the North Korean regime is using its nuclear program to incite fear and seek concessions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America and the world will not be blackmailed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is working with the countries of the region, South Korea, Japan, China, and Russia, to find a peaceful solution and to show the

speaker: George W. Bush
text: North Korean Government that nuclear weapons will bring only isolation, economic stagnation, and continued hardship.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The North Korean regime will find respect in the world and revival for its people only when it turns away from its nuclear ambitions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our Nation and the world must learn the lessons of the Korean Peninsula and not allow an even greater threat to rise up in Iraq.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A brutal dictator, with a history of reckless aggression, with ties to terrorism, with great potential wealth, will not be permitted to dominate a vital region and threaten the United States.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Twelve years ago, Saddam Hussein faced the prospect of being the last casualty in a war he had started and lost.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To spare himself, he agreed to disarm of all weapons of mass destruction.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For the next 12 years, he systematically violated that agreement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He pursued chemical, biological, and nuclear weapons, even while inspectors were in his country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Nothing to date has restrained him from his pursuit of these weapons, not economic sanctions, not isolation from the civilized world, not even cruise missile strikes on his military facilities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Almost 3 months ago, the United Nations Security Council gave Saddam Hussein his final chance to disarm.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He has shown instead utter contempt for the United Nations and for the opinion of the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The 108 U.N.inspectors were sent to conduct--were not sent to conduct a scavenger hunt for hidden materials across a country the size of California.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The job of the inspectors is to verify that Iraq's regime is disarming.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It is up to Iraq to show exactly where it is hiding its banned weapons, lay those weapons out for the world to see, and destroy them as directed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Nothing like this has happened.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The United Nations concluded in 1999 that Saddam Hussein had biological weapons sufficient to produce over 25,000 liters of anthrax, enough doses to kill several million people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He hasn't accounted for that material.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He's given no evidence that he has destroyed it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The United Nations concluded that Saddam Hussein had materials sufficient to produce more than 38,000 liters of botulinum toxin, enough to subject millions of people to death by respiratory failure.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He hasn't accounted for that material.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He's given no evidence that he has destroyed it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our intelligence officials estimate that Saddam Hussein had the materials to produce as much as 500 tons of sarin, mustard, and VX nerve agent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In such quantities, these chemical agents could also kill untold thousands.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He's not accounted for these materials.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He has given no evidence that he has destroyed them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: U.S. intelligence indicates that Saddam Hussein had upwards of 30,000 munitions capable of delivering chemical agents.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Inspectors recently turned up 16 of them, despite Iraq's recent declaration denying their existence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Saddam Hussein has not accounted for the remaining 29,984 of these prohibited munitions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He's given no evidence that he has destroyed them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: From three Iraqi defectors we know that Iraq, in the late 1990s, had several mobile biological weapons labs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These are designed to produce germ warfare agents and can be moved from place to a place to evade inspectors.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Saddam Hussein has not disclosed these facilities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He's given no evidence that he has destroyed them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed in the 1990s that Saddam Hussein had an advanced nuclear weapons development program, had a design for a nuclear weapon, and was working on five different methods of enriching uranium for a bomb.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The British Government has learned that Saddam Hussein recently sought significant quantities of uranium from Africa.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our intelligence sources tell us that he has attempted to purchase high-strength aluminum tubes suitable for nuclear weapons production.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Saddam Hussein has not credibly explained these activities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He clearly has much to hide.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The dictator of Iraq is not disarming.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To the contrary, he is deceiving.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: From intelligence sources we know, for instance, that thousands of Iraqi security personnel are at work hiding documents and materials from the U.N.inspectors, sanitizing inspection sites, and monitoring the inspectors themselves.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iraqi officials accompany the inspectors in order to intimidate witnesses.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iraq is blocking U-2 surveillance flights requested by the United Nations.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iraqi intelligence officers are posing as the scientists inspectors are supposed to interview.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Real scientists have been coached by Iraqi officials on what to say.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Intelligence sources indicate that Saddam Hussein has ordered that scientists who cooperate with U.N. inspectors in disarming Iraq will be killed, along with their families.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Year after year, Saddam Hussein has gone to elaborate lengths, spent enormous sums, taken great risks to build and keep weapons of mass destruction.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But why?

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The only possible explanation, the only possible use he could have for those weapons, is to dominate, intimidate, or attack.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With nuclear arms or a full arsenal of chemical and biological weapons, Saddam Hussein could resume his ambitions of conquest in the

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Middle East and create deadly havoc in that region.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And this Congress and the American people must recognize another threat.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Evidence from intelligence sources, secret communications, and statements by people now in custody reveal that Saddam Hussein aids and protects terrorists, including members of Al Qaida.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Secretly and without fingerprints, he could provide one of his hidden weapons to terrorists or help them develop their own.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Before September the 11th, many in the world believed that Saddam Hussein could be contained.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But chemical agents, lethal viruses, and shadowy terrorist networks are not easily contained.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Imagine those 19 hijackers with other weapons and other plans, this time armed by Saddam Hussein.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It would take one vial, one canister, one crate slipped into this country to bring a day of horror like none we have ever known.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will do everything in our power to make sure that that day never comes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some have said we must not act until the threat is imminent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Since when have terrorists and tyrants announced their intentions, politely putting us on notice before they strike?

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If this threat is permitted to fully and suddenly emerge, all actions, all words, and all recriminations would come too late.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Trusting in the sanity and restraint of Saddam Hussein is not a strategy, and it is not an option.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The dictator who is assembling the world's most dangerous weapons has already used them on whole villages, leaving thousands of his own citizens dead, blind, or disfigured.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iraqi refugees tell us how forced confessions are obtained, by torturing children while their parents are made to watch.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: International human rights groups have cataloged other methods used in the torture chambers of Iraq: electric shock, burning with hot irons, dripping acid on the skin, mutilation with electric drills, cutting out tongues, and rape.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If this is not evil, then evil has no meaning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tonight I have a message for the brave and oppressed people of Iraq: Your enemy is not surrounding your country;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: your enemy is ruling your country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And the day he and his regime are removed from power will be the day of your liberation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The world has waited 12 years for Iraq to disarm.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America will not accept a serious and mounting threat to our country and our friends and our allies.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The United States will ask the U.N. Security Council to convene on February the 5th to consider the facts of Iraq's ongoing defiance of the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Secretary of State Powell will present information and intelligence about Iraqi's legal--Iraq's illegal weapons programs, its attempt to hide those weapons from inspectors, and its links to terrorist groups.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will consult.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But let there be no misunderstanding: If Saddam Hussein does not fully disarm, for the safety of our people and for the peace of the world, we will lead a coalition to disarm him.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I have a message for the men and women who will keep the peace, members of the American Armed Forces: Many of you are assembling in or near the Middle East, and some crucial hours may lay ahead.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In those hours, the success of our cause will depend on you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Your training has prepared you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Your honor will guide you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You believe in America, and America believes in you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Sending Americans into battle is the most profound decision a President can make.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The technologies of war have changed;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: the risks and suffering of war have not.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For the brave Americans who bear the risk, no victory is free from sorrow.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This Nation fights reluctantly, because we know the cost and we dread the days of mourning that always come.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We seek peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We strive for peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And sometimes peace must be defended.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A future lived at the mercy of terrible threats is no peace at all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If war is forced upon us, we will fight in a just cause and by just means, sparing, in every way we can, the innocent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And if war is forced upon us, we will fight with the full force and might of the United States military, and we will prevail.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And as we and our coalition partners are doing in Afghanistan, we will bring to the Iraqi people food and medicines and supplies and freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many challenges, abroad and at home, have arrived in a single season.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In 2 years, America has gone from a sense of invulnerability to an awareness of peril, from bitter division in small matters to calm unity in great causes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we go forward with confidence, because this call of history has come to the right country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Americans are a resolute people who have risen to every test of our time.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Adversity has revealed the character of our country, to the world and to ourselves.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is a strong nation and honorable in the use of our strength.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We exercise power without conquest, and we sacrifice for the liberty of strangers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Americans are a free people, who know that freedom is the right of every person and the future of every nation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The liberty we prize is not America's gift to the world, it is God's gift to humanity.

speaker: George W. Bush
