text: We Americans have faith in ourselves, but not in ourselves alone.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We do not know--we do not claim to know all the ways of providence, yet we can trust in them, placing our confidence in the loving God behind all of life and all of history.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: May He guide us now.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And may God continue to bless the United States of America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Mr.Speaker, Vice President Cheney, members of Congress, distinguished guests, and fellow citizens: America this evening is a nation called to great responsibilities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we are rising to meet them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As we gather tonight, hundreds of thousands of American servicemen and women are deployed across the world in the war on terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By bringing hope to the oppressed, and delivering justice to the violent, they are making America more secure.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Each day, law enforcement personnel and intelligence officers are tracking terrorist threats;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: analysts are examining airline passenger lists;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: the men and women of our new Homeland Security Department are patrolling our coasts and borders.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And their vigilance is protecting America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Americans are proving once again to be the hardest working people in the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The American economy is growing stronger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The tax relief you passed is working.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight, members of Congress can take pride in the great works of compassion and reform that skeptics had thought impossible.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You're raising the standards for our public schools, and you are giving our senior citizens prescription drug coverage under Medicare.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have faced serious challenges together, and now we face a choice: We can go forward with confidence and resolve, or we can turn back to the dangerous illusion that terrorists are not plotting and outlaw regimes are no threat to us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We can press on with economic growth, and reforms in education and Medicare, or we can turn back to old policies and old divisions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've not come all this way -- through tragedy, and trial and war -- only to falter and leave our work unfinished.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Americans are rising to the tasks of history, and they expect the same from us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In their efforts, their enterprise, and their character, the American people are showing that the state of our union is confident and strong.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our greatest responsibility is the active defense of the American people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Twenty-eight months have passed since September 11th, 2001 -- over two years without an attack on American soil.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And it is tempting to believe that the danger is behind us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That hope is understandable, comforting -- and false.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The killing has continued in Bali, Jakarta, Casablanca, Riyadh, Mombasa, Jerusalem, Istanbul,and Baghdad.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The terrorists continue to plot against America and the civilized world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And by our will and courage, this danger will be defeated.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Inside the United States, where the war began, we must continue to give our homeland security and law enforcement personnel every tool they need to defend us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And one of those essential tools is the Patriot Act, which allows federal law enforcement to better share information, to track terrorists, to disrupt their cells, and to seize their assets.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For years, we have used similar provisions to catch embezzlers and drug traffickers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If these methods are good for hunting criminals, they are even more important for hunting terrorists.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Key provisions of the Patriot Act are set to expire next year.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The terrorist threat will not expire on that schedule.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our law enforcement needs this vital legislation to protect our citizens.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You need to renew the Patriot Act.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is on the offensive against the terrorists who started this war.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last March, Khalid Shaikh Mohammed, a mastermind of September the 11th, awoke to find himself in the custody of U.S.and Pakistani authorities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last August the 11th brought the capture of the terrorist Hambali, who was a key player in the attack in Indonesia that killed over 200 people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're tracking al Qaeda around the world, and nearly two-thirds of their known leaders have now been captured or killed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Thousands of very skilled and determined military personnel are on the manhunt, going after the remaining killers who hide in cities and caves, and one by one, we will bring these terrorists to justice.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As part of the offensive against terror, we are also confronting the regimes that harbor and support terrorists, and could supply them with nuclear, chemical or biological weapons.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The United States and our allies are determined: We refuse to live in the shadow of this ultimate danger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The first to see our determination were the Taliban, who made Afghanistan the primary training base of al Qaeda killers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As of this month, that country has a new constitution, guaranteeing free elections and full participation by women.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Businesses are opening, health care centers are being established, and the boys and girls of Afghanistan are back in school.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With the help from the new Afghan army, our coalition is leading aggressive raids against the surviving members of the Taliban and al Qaeda.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The men and women of Afghanistan are building a nation that is free and proud and fighting terror -- and America is honored to be their friend.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Since we last met in this chamber, combat forces of the United States, Great Britain, Australia, Poland and other countries enforced the demands of the United Nations, ended the rule of Saddam Hussein, and the people of Iraq are free.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Having broken the Baathist regime, we face a remnant of violent Saddam supporters.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Men who ran away from our troops in battle are now dispersed and attack from the shadows.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These killers, joined by foreign terrorists, are a serious, continuing danger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet we're making progress against them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The once all-powerful ruler of Iraq was found in a hole, and now sits in a prison cell.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Of the top 55 officials of the former regime, we have captured or killed 45.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our forces are on the offensive, leading over 1,600 patrols a day and conducting an average of 180 raids a week.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are dealing with these thugs in Iraq, just as surely as we dealt with Saddam Hussein's evil regime.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The work of building a new Iraq is hard, and it is right.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And America has always been willing to do what it takes for what is right.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last January, Iraq's only law was the whim of one brutal man.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Today our coalition is working with the Iraqi Governing Council to draft a basic law, with a bill of rights.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're working with Iraqis and the United Nations to prepare for a transition to full Iraqi sovereignty by the end of June.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As democracy takes hold in Iraq, the enemies of freedom will do all in their power to spread violence and fear.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They are trying to shake the will of our country and our friends, but the United States of America will never be intimidated by thugs and assassins.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The killers will fail, and the Iraqi people will live in freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Month by month, Iraqis are assuming more responsibility for their own security and their own future.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tonight we are honored to welcome one of Iraq's most respected leaders: the current President of the Iraqi Governing Council, Adnan Pachachi.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Sir, America stands with you and the Iraqi people as you build a free and peaceful nation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Because of American leadership and resolve, the world is changing for the better.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last month, the leader of Libya voluntarily pledged to disclose and dismantle all of his regime's weapons of mass destruction programs, including a uranium enrichment project for nuclear weapons.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Colonel Qadhafi correctly judged that his country would be better off and far more secure without weapons of mass murder.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Nine months of intense negotiations involving the United States and Great Britain succeeded with Libya, while 12 years of diplomacy with Iraq did not.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And one reason is clear: For diplomacy to be effective, words must be credible, and no one can now doubt the word of America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Different threats require different strategies.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Along with nations in the region, we're insisting that North Korea eliminate its nuclear program.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America and the international community are demanding that Iran meet its commitments and not develop nuclear weapons.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is committed to keeping the world's most dangerous weapons out of the hands of the most dangerous regimes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When I came to this rostrum on September the 20th, 2001, I brought the police shield of a fallen officer, my reminder of lives that ended, and a task that does not end.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I gave to you and to all Americans my complete commitment to securing our country and defeating our enemies.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And this pledge, given by one, has been kept by many.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You in the Congress have provided the resources for our defense, and cast the difficult votes of war and peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our closest allies have been unwavering.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America's intelligence personnel and diplomats have been skilled and tireless.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And the men and women of the American military -- they have taken the hardest duty.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've seen their skill and their courage in armored charges and midnight raids, and lonely hours on faithful watch.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have seen the joy when they return, and felt the sorrow when one is lost.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I've had the honor of meeting our servicemen and women at many posts, from the deck of a carrier in the Pacific to a mess hall in Baghdad.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many of our troops are listening tonight.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I want you and your families to know: America is proud of you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And my administration, and this Congress, will give you the resources you need to fight and win the war on terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I know that some people question if America is really in a war at all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They view terrorism more as a crime, a problem to be solved mainly with law enforcement and indictments.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: After the World Trade Center was first attacked in 1993, some of the guilty were indicted and tried and convicted, and sent to prison.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But the matter was not settled.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The terrorists were still training and plotting in other nations, and drawing up more ambitious plans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: After the chaos and carnage of September the 11th, it is not enough to serve our enemies with legal papers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The terrorists and their supporters declared war on the United States, and war is what they got.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some in this chamber, and in our country, did not support the liberation of Iraq.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Objections to war often come from principled motives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But let us be candid about the consequences of leaving Saddam Hussein in power.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're seeking all the facts.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Already, the Kay Report identified dozens of weapons of mass destruction-related program activities and significant amounts of equipment that Iraq concealed from the United Nations.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Had we failed to act, the dictatator's weapons of mass destruction programs would continue to this day.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Had we failed to act, Security Council resolutions on Iraq would have been revealed as empty threats, weakening the United Nations and encouraging defiance by dictators around the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iraq's torture chambers would still be filled with victims, terrified and innocent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The killing fields of Iraq -- where hundreds of thousands of men and women and children vanished into the sands -- would still be known only to the killers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For all who love freedom and peace, the world without Saddam Hussein's regime is a better and safer place.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some critics have said our duties in Iraq must be internationalized.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This particular criticism is hard to explain to our partners in Britain, Australia, Japan, South Korea, the Philippines, Thailand, Italy, Spain, Poland, Denmark, Hungary, Bulgaria, Ukraine, Romania, the Netherlands, Norway, El Salvador, and the 17 other countries that have committed troops to Iraq.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As we debate at home, we must never ignore the vital contributions of our international partners, or dismiss their sacrifices.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: From the beginning, America has sought international support for our operations in Afghanistan and Iraq, and we have gained much support.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There is a difference, however, between leading a coalition of many nations, and submitting to the objections of a few.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America will never seek a permission slip to defend the security of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We also hear doubts that democracy is a realistic goal for the greater Middle East, where freedom is rare.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet it is mistaken, and condescending, to assume that whole cultures and great religions are incompatible with liberty and self-government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I believe that God has planted in every human heart the desire to live in freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And even when that desire is crushed by tyranny for decades, it will rise again.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As long as the Middle East remains a place of tyranny and despair and anger, it will continue to produce men and movements that threaten the safety of America and our friends.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So America is pursuing a forward strategy of freedom in the greater Middle East.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will challenge the enemies of reform, confront the allies of terror, and expect a higher standard from our friend.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To cut through the barriers of hateful propaganda, the Voice of America and other broadcast services are expanding their programming in Arabic and Persian -- and soon, a new television service will begin providing reliable news and information across the region.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I will send you a proposal to double the budget of the National Endowment for Democracy, and to focus its new work on the development of free elections, and free markets, free press, and free labor unions in the Middle East.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And above all, we will finish the historic work of democracy in Afghanistan and Iraq, so those nations can light the way for others, and help transform a troubled part of the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is a nation with a mission, and that mission comes from our most basic beliefs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have no desire to dominate, no ambitions of empire.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our aim is a democratic peace -- a peace founded upon the dignity and rights of every man and woman.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America acts in this cause with friends and allies at our side, yet we understand our special calling: This great republic will lead the cause of freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the last three years, adversity has also revealed the fundamental strengths of the American economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have come through recession, and terrorist attack, and corporate scandals, and the uncertainties of war.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And because you acted to stimulate our economy with tax relief, this economy is strong, and growing stronger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You have doubled the child tax credit from $500 to $1,000, reduced the marriage penalty, begun to phase out the death tax, reduced taxes on capital gains and stock dividends, cut taxes on small businesses, and you have lowered taxes for every American who pays income taxes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Americans took those dollars and put them to work, driving this economy forward.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The pace of economic growth in the third quarter of 2003 was the fastest in nearly 20 years;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: new home construction, the highest in almost 20 years;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: home ownership rates, the highest ever.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Manufacturing activity is increasing.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Inflation is low.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Interest rates are low.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Exports are growing.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Productivity is high, and jobs are on the rise.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These numbers confirm that the American people are using their money far better than government would have -- and you were right to return it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America's growing economy is also a changing economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As technology transforms the way almost every job is done, America becomes more productive, and workers need new skills.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Much of our job growth will be found in high-skilled fields like health care and biotechnology.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So we must respond by helping more Americans gain the skills to find good jobs in our new economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: All skills begin with the basics of reading and math, which are supposed to be learned in the early grades of our schools.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet for too long, for too many children, those skills were never mastered.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By passing the No Child Left Behind Act, you have made the expectation of literacy the law of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're providing more funding for our schools -- a 36-percent increase since 2001.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're requiring higher standards.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are regularly testing every child on the fundamentals.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are reporting results to parents, and making sure they have better options when schools are not performing.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are making progress toward excellence for every child in America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But the status quo always has defenders.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some want to undermine the No Child Left Behind Act by weakening standards and accountability.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet the results we require are really a matter of common sense: We expect third graders to read and do math at the third grade level -- and that's not asking too much.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Testing is the only way to identify and help students who are falling behind.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This nation will not go back to the days of simply shuffling children along from grade to grade without them learning the basics.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I refuse to give up on any child -- and the No Child Left Behind Act is opening the door of opportunity to all of America's children.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: At the same time, we must ensure that older students and adults can gain the skills they need to find work now.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many of the fastest growing occupations require strong math and science preparation, and training beyond the high school level.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So tonight, I propose a series of measures called Jobs for the 21st Century.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This program will provide extra help to middle and high school students who fall behind in reading and math, expand advanced placement programs in low-income schools, invite math and science professionals from the private sector to teach part-time in our high schools.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I propose larger Pell grants for students who prepare for college with demanding courses in high school.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I propose increasing our support for America's fine community colleges, so they can.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I do so, so they can train workers for industries that are creating the most new jobs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By all these actions, we'll help more and more Americans to join in the growing prosperity of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Job training is important, and so is job creation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must continue to pursue an aggressive, pro-growth economic agenda.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Congress has some unfinished business on the issue of taxes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The tax reductions you passed are set to expire.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Unless you act -- unless you act -- unless you act, the unfair tax on marriage will go back up.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Unless you act, millions of families will be charged $300 more in federal taxes for every child.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Unless you act, small businesses will pay higher taxes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Unless you act, the death tax will eventually come back to life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Unless you act, Americans face a tax increase.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: What Congress has given, the Congress should not take away.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For the sake of job growth, the tax cuts you passed should be permanent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our agenda for jobs and growth must help small business owners and employees with relief from needless federal regulation, and protect them from junk and frivolous lawsuits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Consumers and businesses need reliable supplies of energy to make our economy run -- so I urge you to pass legislation to modernize our electricity system, promote conservation, and make America less dependent on foreign sources of energy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My administration is promoting free and fair trade to open up new markets for America's entrepreneurs and manufacturers and farmers -- to create jobs for American workers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Younger workers should have the opportunity to build a nest egg by saving part of their Social Security taxes in a personal retirement account.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We should make the Social Security system a source of ownership for the American people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we should limit the burden of government on this economy by acting as good stewards of taxpayers' dollars.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In two weeks, I will send you a budget that funds the war, protects the homeland, and meets important domestic needs, while limiting the growth in discretionary spending to less than 4 percent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This will require that Congress focus on priorities, cut wasteful spending, and be wise with the people's money.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By doing so, we can cut the deficit in half over the next five years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight, I also ask you to reform our immigration laws so they reflect our values and benefit our economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I propose a new temporary worker program to match willing foreign workers with willing employers when no Americans can be found to fill the job.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This reform will be good for our economy because employers will find needed workers in an honest and orderly system.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A temporary worker program will help protect our homeland, allowing Border Patrol and law enforcement to focus on true threats to our national security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I oppose amnesty, because it would encourage further illegal immigration, and unfairly reward those who break our laws.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My temporary worker program will preserve the citizenship path for those who respect the law, while bringing millions of hardworking men and women out from the shadows of American life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our nation's health care system, like our economy, is also in a time of change.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Amazing medical technologies are improving and saving lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This dramatic progress has brought its own challenge, in the rising costs of medical care and health insurance.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Members of Congress, we must work together to help control those costs and extend the benefits of modern medicine throughout our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Meeting these goals requires bipartisan effort, and two months ago, you showed the way.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By strengthening Medicare and adding a prescription drug benefit, you kept a basic commitment to our seniors: You are giving them the modern medicine they deserve.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Starting this year, under the law you passed, seniors can choose to receive a drug discount card, saving them 10 to 25 percent off the retail price of most prescription drugs -- and millions of low-income seniors can get an additional $600 to buy medicine.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Beginning next year, seniors will have new coverage for preventive screenings against diabetes and heart disease, and seniors just entering Medicare can receive wellness exams.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In January of 2006, seniors can get prescription drug coverage under Medicare.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For a monthly premium of about $35, most seniors who do not have that coverage today can expect to see their drug bills cut roughly in half.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Under this reform, senior citizens will be able to keep their Medicare just as it is, or they can choose a Medicare plan that fits them best -- just as you, as members of Congress, can choose an insurance plan that meets your needs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And starting this year, millions of Americans will be able to save money tax-free for their medical expenses in a health savings account.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I signed this measure proudly, and any attempt to limit the choices of our seniors, or to take away their prescription drug coverage under Medicare, will meet my veto.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On the critical issue of health care, our goal is to ensure that Americans can choose and afford private health care coverage that best fits their individual needs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To make insurance more affordable, Congress must act to address rapidly rising health care costs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Small businesses should be able to band together and negotiate for lower insurance rates, so they can cover more workers with health insurance.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I urge you to pass association health plans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask you to give lower-income Americans a refundable tax credit that would allow millions to buy their own basic health insurance.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By computerizing health records, we can avoid dangerous medical mistakes, reduce costs, and improve care.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To protect the doctor-patient relationship, and keep good doctors doing good work, we must eliminate wasteful and frivolous medical lawsuits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tonight I propose that individuals who buy catastrophic health care coverage, as part of our new health savings accounts, be allowed to deduct 100 percent of the premiums from their taxes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A government-run health care system is the wrong prescription.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By keeping costs under control, expanding access, and helping more Americans afford coverage, we will preserve the system of private medicine that makes America's health care the best in the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are living in a time of great change -- in our world, in our economy, in science and medicine.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet some things endure -- courage and compassion, reverence and integrity, respect for differences of faith and race.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The values we try to live by never change.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And they are instilled in us by fundamental institutions, such as families and schools and religious congregations.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These institutions, these unseen pillars of civilization, must remain strong in America, and we will defend them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must stand with our families to help them raise healthy, responsible children.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When it comes to helping children make right choices, there is work for all of us to do.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One of the worst decisions our children can make is to gamble their lives and futures on drugs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our government is helping parents confront this problem with aggressive education, treatment, and law enforcement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Drug use in high school has declined by 11 percent over the last two years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Four hundred thousand fewer young people are using illegal drugs than in the year 2001.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In my budget, I proposed new funding to continue our aggressive, community-based strategy to reduce demand for illegal drugs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Drug testing in our schools has proven to be an effective part of this effort.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So tonight I proposed an additional $23 million for schools that want to use drug testing as a tool to save children's lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The aim here is not to punish children, but to send them this message: We love you, and we don't want to lose you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To help children make right choices, they need good examples.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Athletics play such an important role in our society, but, unfortunately, some in professional sports are not setting much of an example.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The use of performance-enhancing drugs like steroids in baseball, football, and other sports is dangerous, and it sends the wrong message -- that there are shortcuts to accomplishment, and that performance is more important than character.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So tonight I call on team owners, union representatives, coaches, and players to take the lead, to send the right signal, to get tough, and to get rid of steroids now.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To encourage right choices, we must be willing to confront the dangers young people face -- even when they're difficult to talk about.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Each year, about 3 million teenagers contract sexually-transmitted diseases that can harm them, or kill them, or prevent them from ever becoming parents.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In my budget, I propose a grassroots campaign to help inform families about these medical risks.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will double federal funding for abstinence programs, so schools can teach this fact of life: Abstinence for young people is the only certain way to avoid sexually-transmitted diseases.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Decisions children now make can affect their health and character for the rest of their lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: All of us -- parents and schools and government -- must work together to counter the negative influence of the culture, and to send the right messages to our children.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A strong America must also value the institution of marriage.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I believe we should respect individuals as we take a principled stand for one of the most fundamental, enduring institutions of our civilization.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Congress has already taken a stand on this issue by passing the Defense of Marriage Act, signed in 1996 by President Clinton.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That statute protects marriage under federal law as a union of a man and a woman, and declares that one state may not redefine marriage for other states.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Activist judges, however, have begun redefining marriage by court order, without regard for the will of the people and their elected representatives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On an issue of such great consequence, the people's voice must be heard.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If judges insist on forcing their arbitrary will upon the people, the only alternative left to the people would be the constitutional process.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our nation must defend the sanctity of marriage.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The outcome of this debate is important -- and so is the way we conduct it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The same moral tradition that defines marriage also teaches that each individual has dignity and value in God's sight.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It's also important to strengthen our communities by unleashing the compassion of America's religious institutions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Religious charities of every creed are doing some of the most vital work in our country -- mentoring children, feeding the hungry, taking the hand of the lonely.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet government has often denied social service grants and contracts to these groups, just because they have a cross or a Star of David or a crescent on the wall.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By executive order, I have opened billions of dollars in grant money to competition that includes faith-based charities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I ask you to codify this into law, so people of faith can know that the law will never discriminate against them again.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the past, we've worked together to bring mentors to children of prisoners, and provide treatment for the addicted, and help for the homeless.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I ask you to consider another group of Americans in need of help.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This year, some 600,000 inmates will be released from prison back into society.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We know from long experience that if they can't find work, or a home, or help, they are much more likely to commit crime and return to prison.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So tonight, I propose a four-year, $300 million prisoner re-entry initiative to expand job training and placement services, to provide transitional housing, and to help newly released prisoners get mentoring, including from faith-based groups.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is the land of second chance, and when the gates of the prison open, the path ahead should lead to a better lifeFor all Americans, the last three years have brought tests we did not ask for, and achievements shared by all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By our actions, we have shown what kind of nation we are.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In grief, we have found the grace to go on.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In challenge, we rediscovered the courage and daring of a free people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In victory, we have shown the noble aims and good heart of America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And having come this far, we sense that we live in a time set apart.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I've been witness to the character of the people of America, who have shown calm in times of danger, compassion for one another, and toughness for the long haul.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: All of us have been partners in a great enterprise.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And even some of the youngest understand that we are living in historic times.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last month a girl in Lincoln, Rhode Island, sent me a letter.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Dear George W. Bush.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: nan

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight, Ashley, your message to our troops has just been conveyed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And, yes, you have some duties yourself.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And, Ashley, while you do your part, all of us here in this great chamber will do our best to keep you and the rest of America safe and free.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My fellow citizens, we now move forward, with confidence and faith.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our nation is strong and steadfast.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The cause we serve is right, because it is the cause of all mankind.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The momentum of freedom in our world is unmistakable -- and it is not carried forward by our power alone.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We can trust in that greater power who guides the unfolding of the years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And in all that is to come, we can know that His purposes are just and true.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: May God continue to bless America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Mr. Speaker, Vice President Cheney, members of Congress, fellow citizens: As a new Congress gathers, all of us in the elected branches of government share a great privilege: We've been placed in office by the votes of the people we serve.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tonight that is a privilege we share with newly-elected leaders of Afghanistan, the Palestinian Territories, Ukraine, and a free and sovereign Iraq.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Two weeks ago, I stood on the steps of this Capitol and renewed the commitment of our nation to the guiding ideal of liberty for all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This evening I will set forth policies to advance that ideal at home and around the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight, with a healthy, growing economy, with more Americans going back to work, with our nation an active force for good in the world -- the state of our union is confident and strong.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our generation has been blessed -- by the expansion of opportunity, by advances in medicine, by the security purchased by our parents' sacrifice.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now, as we see a little gray in the mirror -- or a lot of gray -- and we watch our children moving into adulthood, we ask the question: What will be the state of their union?

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Members of Congress, the choices we make together will answer that question.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Over the next several months, on issue after issue, let us do what Americans have always done, and build a better world for our children and our grandchildren.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: First, we must be good stewards of this economy, and renew the great institutions on which millions of our fellow citizens rely.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America's economy is the fastest growing of any major industrialized nation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the past four years, we provided tax relief to every person who pays income taxes, overcome a recession, opened up new markets abroad, prosecuted corporate criminals, raised homeownership to its highest level in history, and in the last year alone, the United States has added 2.3 million new jobs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When action was needed, the Congress delivered -- and the nation is grateful.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now we must add to these achievements.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By making our economy more flexible, more innovative, and more competitive, we will keep America the economic leader of the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America's prosperity requires restraining the spending appetite of the federal government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I welcome the bipartisan enthusiasm for spending discipline.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I will send you a budget that holds the growth of discretionary spending below inflation, makes tax relief permanent, and stays on track to cut the deficit in half by 2009.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My budget substantially reduces or eliminates more than 150 government programs that are not getting results, or duplicate current efforts, or do not fulfill essential priorities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The principle here is clear: Taxpayer dollars must be spent wisely, or not at all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To make our economy stronger and more dynamic, we must prepare a rising generation to fill the jobs of the 21st century.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Under the No Child Left Behind Act, standards are higher, test scores are on the rise, and we're closing the achievement gap for minority students.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now we must demand better results from our high schools, so every high school diploma is a ticket to success.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will help an additional 200,000 workers to get training for a better career, by reforming our job training system and strengthening America's community colleges.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we'll make it easier for Americans to afford a college education, by increasing the size of Pell Grants.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To make our economy stronger and more competitive, America must reward, not punish, the efforts and dreams of entrepreneurs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Small business is the path of advancement, especially for women and minorities, so we must free small businesses from needless regulation and protect honest job-creators from junk lawsuits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Justice is distorted, and our economy is held back by irresponsible class-actions and frivolous asbestos claims -- and I urge Congress to pass legal reforms this year.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To make our economy stronger and more productive, we must make health care more affordable, and give families greater access to good coverage -- and more control over their health decisions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask Congress to move forward on a comprehensive health care agenda with tax credits to help low-income workers buy insurance, a community health center in every poor country, improved information technology to prevent medical error and needless costs, association health plans for small businesses and their employees -- expanded health savings accounts -- and medical liability reform that will reduce health care costs and make sure patients have the doctors and the care they need.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To keep our economy growing, we also need reliable supplies of affordable, environmentally responsible energy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Nearly four years ago, I submitted a comprehensive energy strategy that encourages conservation, alternative sources, a modernized electricity grid, and more production here at home -- including safe, clean nuclear energy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My Clear Skies legislation will cut power plant pollution and improve the health of our citizens.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And my budget provides strong funding for leading-edge technology -- from hydrogen-fueled cars, to clean coal, to renewable sources such as ethanol.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Four years of debate is enough: I urge Congress to pass legislation that makes America more secure and less dependent on foreign energy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: All these proposals are essential to expand this economy and add new jobs -- but they are just the beginning of our duty.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To build the prosperity of future generations, we must update institutions that were created to meet the needs of an earlier time.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Year after year, Americans are burdened by an archaic, incoherent federal tax code.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I've appointed a bipartisan panel to examine the tax code from top to bottom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And when their recommendations are delivered, you and I will work together to give this nation a tax code that is pro-growth, easy to understand, and fair to all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America's immigration system is also outdated -- unsuited to the needs of our economy and to the values of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We should not be content with laws that punish hardworking people who want only to provide for their families, and deny businesses willing workers, and invite chaos at our border.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It is time for an immigration policy that permits temporary guest workers to fill jobs Americans will not take, that rejects amnesty, that tells us who is entering and leaving our country, and that closes the border to drug dealers and terrorists.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One of America's most important institutions -- a symbol of the trust between generations -- is also in need of wise and effective reform.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Social Security was a great moral success of the 20th century, and we must honor its great purposes in this new century.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The system, however, on its current path, is headed toward bankruptcy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And so we must join together to strengthen and save Social Security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Today, more than 45 million Americans receive Social Security benefits, and millions more are nearing retirement -- and for them the system is sound and fiscally strong.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I have a message for every American who is 55 or older: Do not let anyone mislead you;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: for you, the Social Security system will not change in any way.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For younger workers, the Social Security system has serious problems that will grow worse with time.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Social Security was created decades ago, for a very different era.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In those days, people did not live as long.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Benefits were much lower than they are today.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And a half-century ago, about sixteen workers paid into the system for each person drawing benefits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our society has changed in ways the founders of Social Security could not have foreseen.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In today's world, people are living longer and, therefore, drawing benefits longer.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And those benefits are scheduled to rise dramatically over the next few decades.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And instead of sixteen workers paying in for every beneficiary, right now it's only about three workers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And over the next few decades that number will fall to just two workers per beneficiary.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With each passing year, fewer workers are paying ever-higher benefits to an ever-larger number of retirees.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So here is the result: Thirteen years from now, in 2018, Social Security will be paying out more than it takes in.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And every year afterward will bring a new shortfall, bigger than the year before.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For example, in the year 2027, the government will somehow have to come up with an extra $200 billion to keep the system afloat -- and by 2033, the annual shortfall would be more than $300 billion.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By the year 2042, the entire system would be exhausted and bankrupt.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If steps are not taken to avert that outcome, the only solutions would be dramatically higher taxes, massive new borrowing, or sudden and severe cuts in Social Security benefits or other government programs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I recognize that 2018 and 2042 may seem a long way off.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But those dates are not so distant, as any parent will tell you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If you have a five-year-old, you're already concerned about how you'll pay for college tuition 13 years down the road.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If you've got children in their 20s, as some of us do, the idea of Social Security collapsing before they retire does not seem like a small matter.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And it should not be a small matter to the United States Congress.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You and I share a responsibility.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must pass reforms that solve the financial problems of Social Security once and for all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Fixing Social Security permanently will require an open, candid review of the options.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some have suggested limiting benefits for wealthy retirees.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Former Congressman Tim Penny has raised the possibility of indexing benefits to prices rather than wages.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: During the 1990s, my predecessor, President Clinton, spoke of increasing the retirement age.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Former Senator John Breaux suggested discouraging early collection of Social Security benefits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The late Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan recommended changing the way benefits are calculated.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: All these ideas are on the table.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I know that none of these reforms would be easy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But we have to move ahead with courage and honesty, because our children's retirement security is more important than partisan politics.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I will work with members of Congress to find the most effective combination of reforms.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I will listen to anyone who has a good idea to offer.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must, however, be guided by some basic principles.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must make Social Security permanently sound, not leave that task for another day.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must not jeopardize our economic strength by increasing payroll taxes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must ensure that lower-income Americans get the help they need to have dignity and peace of mind in their retirement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must guarantee there is no change for those now retired or nearing retirement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we must take care that any changes in the system are gradual, so younger workers have years to prepare and plan for their future.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As we fix Social Security, we also have the responsibility to make the system a better deal for younger workers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And the best way to reach that goal is through voluntary personal retirement accounts.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Here is how the idea works.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Right now, a set portion of the money you earn is taken out of your paycheck to pay for the Social Security benefits of today's retirees.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If you're a younger worker, I believe you should be able to set aside part of that money in your own retirement account, so you can build a nest egg for your own future.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Here's why the personal accounts are a better deal.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Your money will grow, over time, at a greater rate than anything the current system can deliver -- and your account will provide money for retirement over and above the check you will receive from Social Security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In addition, you'll be able to pass along the money that accumulates in your personal account, if you wish, to your children and -- or grandchildren.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And best of all, the money in the account is yours, and the government can never take it away.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The goal here is greater security in retirement, so we will set careful guidelines for personal accounts.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We'll make sure the money can only go into a conservative mix of bonds and stock funds.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We'll make sure that your earnings are not eaten up by hidden Wall Street fees.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We'll make sure there are good options to protect your investments from sudden market swings on the eve of your retirement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We'll make sure a personal account cannot be emptied out all at once, but rather paid out over time, as an addition to traditional Social Security benefits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we'll make sure this plan is fiscally responsible, by starting personal retirement accounts gradually, and raising the yearly limits on contributions over time, eventually permitting all workers to set aside four percentage points of their payroll taxes in their accounts.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Personal retirement accounts should be familiar to federal employees, because you already have something similar, called the Thrift Savings Plan, which lets workers deposit a portion of their paychecks into any of five different broadly-based investment f

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It's time to extend the same security, and choice, and ownership to young Americans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our second great responsibility to our children and grandchildren is to honor and to pass along the values that sustain a free society.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So many of my generation, after a long journey, have come home to family and faith, and are determined to bring up responsible, moral children.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Government is not the source of these values, but government should never undermine them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Because marriage is a sacred institution and the foundation of society, it should not be re-defined by activist judges.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For the good of families, children, and society, I support a constitutional amendment to protect the institution of marriage.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Because a society is measured by how it treats the weak and vulnerable, we must strive to build a culture of life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Medical research can help us reach that goal, by developing treatments and cures that save lives and help people overcome disabilities -- and I thank the Congress for doubling the funding of the National Institutes of Health.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To build a culture of life, we must also ensure that scientific advances always serve human dignity, not take advantage of some lives for the benefit of others.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We should all be able to agree -- we should all be able to agree on some clear standards.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I will work with Congress to ensure that human embryos are not created for experimentation or grown for body parts, and that human life is never bought and sold as a commodity.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America will continue to lead the world in medical research that is ambitious, aggressive, and always ethical.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Because courts must always deliver impartial justice, judges have a duty to faithfully interpret the law, not legislate from the bench.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As President, I have a constitutional responsibility to nominate men and women who understand the role of courts in our democracy, and are well-qualified to serve on the bench -- and I have done so.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The Constitution also gives the Senate a responsibility: Every judicial nominee deserves an up or down vote.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Because one of the deepest values of our country is compassion, we must never turn away from any citizen who feels isolated from the opportunities of America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our government will continue to support faith-based and community groups that bring hope to harsh places.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now we need to focus on giving young people, especially young men in our cities, better options than apathy, or gangs, or jail.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I propose a three-year initiative to help organizations keep young people out of gangs, and show young men an ideal of manhood that respects women and rejects violence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Taking on gang life will be one part of a broader outreach to at-risk youth, which involves parents and pastors, coaches and community leaders, in programs ranging from literacy to sports.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I am proud that the leader of this nationwide effort will be our First Lady, Laura Bush.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Because HIV/AIDS brings suffering and fear into so many lives, I ask you to reauthorize the Ryan White Act to encourage prevention, and provide care and treatment to the victims of that disease.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And as we update this important law, we must focus our efforts on fellow citizens with the highest rates of new cases, African American men and women.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Because one of the main sources of our national unity is our belief in equal justice, we need to make sure Americans of all races and backgrounds have confidence in the system that provides justice.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In America we must make doubly sure no person is held to account for a crime he or she did not commit -- so we are dramatically expanding the use of DNA evidence to prevent wrongful conviction.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Soon I will send to Congress a proposal to fund special training for defense counsel in capital cases, because people on trial for their lives must have competent lawyers by their side.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our third responsibility to future generations is to leave them an America that is safe from danger, and protected by peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will pass along to our children all the freedoms we enjoy -- and chief among them is freedom from fear.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the three and a half years since September the 11th, 2001, we have taken unprecedented actions to protect Americans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've created a new department of government to defend our homeland, focused the FBI on preventing terrorism, begun to reform our intelligence agencies, broken up terror cells across the country, expanded research on defenses against biological and chemical attack, improved border security, and trained more than a half-million first responders.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Police and firefighters, air marshals, researchers, and so many others are working every day to make our homeland safer, and we thank them all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our nation, working with allies and friends, has also confronted the enemy abroad, with measures that are determined, successful, and continuing.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The al Qaeda terror network that attacked our country still has leaders -- but many of its top commanders have been removed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There are still governments that sponsor and harbor terrorists -- but their number has declined.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There are still regimes seeking weapons of mass destruction -- but no longer without attention and without consequence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our country is still the target of terrorists who want to kill many, and intimidate us all -- and we will stay on the offensive against them, until the fight is won.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Pursuing our enemies is a vital commitment of the war on terror -- and I thank the Congress for providing our servicemen and women with the resources they have needed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: During this time of war, we must continue to support our military and give them the tools for victory.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Other nations around the globe have stood with us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In Afghanistan, an international force is helping provide security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In Iraq, 28 countries have troops on the ground, the United Nations and the European Union provided technical assistance for the elections, and NATO is leading a mission to help train Iraqi officers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're cooperating with 60 governments in the Proliferation Security Initiative, to detect and stop the transit of dangerous materials.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're working closely with the governments in Asia to convince North Korea to abandon its nuclear ambitions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and nine other countries have captured or detained al Qaeda terrorists.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the next four years, my administration will continue to build the coalitions that will defeat the dangers of our time.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the long-term, the peace we seek will only be achieved by eliminating the conditions that feed radicalism and ideologies of murder.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If whole regions of the world remain in despair and grow in hatred, they will be the recruiting grounds for terror, and that terror will stalk America and other free nations for decades.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The only force powerful enough to stop the rise of tyranny and terror, and replace hatred with hope, is the force of human freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: of democracy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we've declared our own intention: America will stand with the allies of freedom to support democratic movements in the Middle East and beyond, with the ultimate goal of ending tyranny in our world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The United States has no right, no desire, and no intention to impose our form of government on anyone else.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That is one of the main differences between us and our enemies.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They seek to impose and expand an empire of oppression, in which a tiny group of brutal, self-appointed rulers control every aspect of every life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our aim is to build and preserve a community of free and independent nations, with governments that answer to their citizens, and reflect their own cultures.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And because democracies respect their own people and their neighbors, the advance of freedom will lead to peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That advance has great momentum in our time -- shown by women voting in Afghanistan, and Palestinians choosing a new direction, and the people of Ukraine asserting their democratic rights and electing a president.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are witnessing landmark events in the history of liberty.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And in the coming years, we will add to that story.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The beginnings of reform and democracy in the Palestinian territories are now showing the power of freedom to break old patterns of violence and failure.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tomorrow morning, Secretary of State Rice departs on a trip that will take her to Israel and the West Bank for meetings with Prime Minister Sharon and President Abbas.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: She will discuss with them how we and our friends can help the Palestinian people end terror and build the institutions of a peaceful, independent, democratic state.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To promote this democracy, I will ask Congress for $350 million to support Palestinian political, economic, and security reforms.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The goal of two democratic states, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace, is within reach -- and America will help them achieve that goal.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To promote peace and stability in the broader Middle East, the United States will work with our friends in the region to fight the common threat of terror, while we encourage a higher standard of freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Hopeful reform is already taking hold in an arc from Morocco to Jordan to Bahrain.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The government of Saudi Arabia can demonstrate its leadership in the region by expanding the role of its people in determining their future.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And the great and proud nation of Egypt, which showed the way toward peace in the Middle East, can now show the way toward democracy in the Middle East.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To promote peace in the broader Middle East, we must confront regimes that continue to harbor terrorists and pursue weapons of mass murder.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Syria still allows its territory, and parts of Lebanon, to be used by terrorists who seek to destroy every chance of peace in the region.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You have passed, and we are applying, the Syrian Accountability Act -- and we expect the Syrian government to end all support for terror and open the door to freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Today, Iran remains the world's primary state sponsor of terror -- pursuing nuclear weapons while depriving its people of the freedom they seek and deserve.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are working with European allies to make clear to the Iranian regime that it must give up its uranium enrichment program and any plutonium reprocessing, and end its support for terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And to the Iranian people, I say tonight: As you stand for your own liberty, America stands with you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our generational commitment to the advance of freedom, especially in the Middle East, is now being tested and honored in Iraq.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That country is a vital front in the war on terror, which is why the terrorists have chosen to make a stand there.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our men and women in uniform are fighting terrorists in Iraq, so we do not have to face them here at home.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And the victory of freedom in Iraq will strengthen a new ally in the war on terror, inspire democratic reformers from Damascus to Tehran, bring more hope and progress to a troubled region, and thereby lift a terrible threat from the lives of our children

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will succeed because the Iraqi people value their own liberty -- as they showed the world last Sunday.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Across Iraq, often at great risk, millions of citizens went to the polls and elected 275 men and women to represent them in a new Transitional National Assembly.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A young woman in Baghdad told of waking to the sound of mortar fire on election day, and wondering if it might be too dangerous to vote.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Hearing those explosions, it occurred to me -- the insurgents are weak, they are afraid of democracy, they are losing.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Americans recognize that spirit of liberty, because we share it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In any nation, casting your vote is an act of civic responsibility;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: for millions of Iraqis, it was also an act of personal courage, and they have earned the respect of us all.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One of Iraq's leading democracy and human rights advocates is Safia Taleb al-Suhail.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We were occupied for 35 years by Saddam Hussein.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Three days ago in Baghdad, Safia was finally able to vote for the leaders of her country -- and we are honored that she is with us tonight.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The terrorists and insurgents are violently opposed to democracy, and will continue to attack it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet, the terrorists' most powerful myth is being destroyed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The whole world is seeing that the car bombers and assassins are not only fighting coalition forces, they are trying to destroy the hopes of Iraqis, expressed in free elections.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And the whole world now knows that a small group of extremists will not overturn the will of the Iraqi people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will succeed in Iraq because Iraqis are determined to fight for their own freedom, and to write their own history.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That is the natural desire of an independent nation, and it is also the stated mission of our coalition in Iraq.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The new political situation in Iraq opens a new phase of our work in that country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: At the recommendation of our commanders on the ground, and in consultation with the Iraqi government, we will increasingly focus our efforts on helping prepare more capable Iraqi security forces -- forces with skilled officers and an effective command structure.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As those forces become more self-reliant and take on greater security responsibilities, America and its coalition partners will increasingly be in a supporting role.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the end, Iraqis must be able to defend their own country -- and we will help that proud, new nation secure its liberty.

speaker: George W. Bush

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He and all Iraqis can be certain: While our military strategy is adapting to circumstances, our commitment remains firm and unchanging.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are standing for the freedom of our Iraqi friends, and freedom in Iraq will make America safer for generations to come.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will not set an artificial timetable for leaving Iraq, because that would embolden the terrorists and make them believe they can wait us out.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are in Iraq to achieve a result: A country that is democratic, representative of all its people, at peace with its neighbors, and able to defend itself.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And when that result is achieved, our men and women serving in Iraq will return home with the honor they have earned.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Right now, Americans in uniform are serving at posts across the world, often taking great risks on my orders.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have given them training and equipment;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: and they have given us an example of idealism and character that makes every American proud.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The volunteers of our military are unrelenting in battle, unwavering in loyalty, unmatched in honor and decency, and every day they're making our nation more secure.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some of our servicemen and women have survived terrible injuries, and this grateful country will do everything we can to help them recover.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we have said farewell to some very good men and women, who died for our freedom, and whose memory this nation will honor forever.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One name we honor is Marine Corps Sergeant Byron Norwood of Pflugerville, Texas, who was killed during the assault on Fallujah.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: His mom, Janet, sent me a letter and told me how much Byron loved being a Marine, and how proud he was to be on the front line against terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When Byron was home the last time, I said that I wanted to protect him like I had since he was born.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He just hugged me and said, 'You've done your job, Mom.
