speaker: George W. Bush
text: Ladies and gentlemen, with grateful hearts, we honor freedom's defenders, and our military families, represented here this evening by Sergeant Norwood's mom and dad, Janet and Bill Norwood.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In these four years, Americans have seen the unfolding of large events.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have known times of sorrow, and hours of uncertainty, and days of victory.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In all this history, even when we have disagreed, we have seen threads of purpose that unite us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The attack on freedom in our world has reaffirmed our confidence in freedom's power to change the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are all part of a great venture: To extend the promise of freedom in our country, to renew the values that sustain our liberty, and to spread the peace that freedom brings.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: nan

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we live in the country where the biggest dreams are born.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The abolition of slavery was only a dream -- until it was fulfilled.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The liberation of Europe from fascism was only a dream -- until it was achieved.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The fall of imperial communism was only a dream -- until, one day, it was accomplished.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our generation has dreams of its own, and we also go forward with confidence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The road of Providence is uneven and unpredictable -- yet we know where it leads: It leads to freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Thank you, and may God bless America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Congress, members of the Supreme Court and Diplomatic Corps, distinguished guests and fellow citizens:   Today our Nation lost a beloved, graceful, courageous woman who called America to its founding ideals and carried on a noble dream.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight we are comforted by the hope of a glad reunion with the husband who was taken from her so long ago, and we are grateful for the good life of Coretta Scott King.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Every time I am invited to this rostrum, I am humbled by the privilege, and mindful of the history we have seen together.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have gathered under this Capitol dome in moments of national mourning and national achievement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have served America through one of the most consequential periods of our history, and it has been my honor to serve with you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In a system of two parties, two chambers, and two elected branches, there will always be differences and debate.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But even tough debates can be conducted in a civil tone, and our differences cannot be allowed to harden into anger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To confront the great issues before us, we must act in a spirit of good will and respect for one another, and I will do my part.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight the state of our Union is strong, and together we will make it stronger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In this decisive year, you and I will make choices that determine both the future and the character of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will choose to act confidently in pursuing the enemies of freedom, or retreat from our duties in the hope of an easier life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will choose to build our prosperity by leading the world economy, or shut ourselves off from trade and opportunity.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In a complex and challenging time, the road of isolationism and protectionism may seem broad and inviting, yet it ends in danger and decline.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The only way to protect our people, the only way to secure the peace, the only way to control our destiny is by our leadership, so the United States of America will continue to lead.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Abroad, our Nation is committed to a historic, long-term goal.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We seek the end of tyranny in our world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some dismiss that goal as misguided idealism.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In reality, the future security of America depends on it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On September 11, 2001, we found that problems originating in a failed and oppressive state 7,000 miles away could bring murder and destruction to our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Dictatorships shelter terrorists, feed resentment and radicalism, and seek weapons of mass destruction.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Democracies replace resentment with hope, respect the rights of their citizens and their neighbors, and join the fight against terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Every step toward freedom in the world makes our country safer, and so we will act boldly in freedom's cause.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Far from being a hopeless dream, the advance of freedom is the great story of our time.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In 1945, there were about two dozen lonely democracies in the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Today, there are 122.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we are writing a new chapter in the story of self-government, with women lining up to vote in Afghanistan, and millions of Iraqis marking their liberty with purple ink, and men and women from Lebanon to Egypt debating the rights of individuals and the necessity of freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: At the start of 2006, more than half the people of our world live in democratic nations.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we do not forget the other half, in places like Syria, Burma, Zimbabwe, North Korea, and Iran, because the demands of justice, and the peace of this world, require their freedom as well.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: No one can deny the success of freedom, but some men rage and fight against it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And one of the main sources of reaction and opposition is radical Islam, the perversion by a few of a noble faith into an ideology of terror and death.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Terrorists like bin Laden are serious about mass murder, and all of us must take their declared intentions seriously.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They seek to impose a heartless system of totalitarian control throughout the Middle East and arm themselves with weapons of  mass murder.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Their aim is to seize power in Iraq and use it as a safe haven to launch attacks against America and the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Lacking the military strength to challenge us directly, the terrorists have chosen the weapon of fear.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When they murder children at a school in Beslan, or blow up commuters in London, or behead a bound captive, the terrorists hope these horrors will break our will, allowing the violent to inherit the Earth.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But they have miscalculated: we love our freedom, and we will fight to keep it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In a time of testing, we cannot find security by abandoning our commitments and retreating within our borders.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If we were to leave these vicious attackers alone, they would not leave us alone.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They would simply move the battlefield to our own shores.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There is no peace in retreat.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And there is no honor in retreat.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By allowing radical Islam to work its will, by leaving an assaulted world to fend for itself, we would signal to all that we no longer believe in our own ideals, or even in our own courage.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But our enemies and our friends can be certain: the United States will not retreat from the world, and we will never surrender to evil.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America rejects the false comfort of isolationism.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are the Nation that saved liberty in Europe, and liberated death camps, and helped raise up democracies, and faced down an evil empire.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Once again, we accept the call of history to deliver the oppressed, and move this world toward peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We remain on the offensive against terror networks.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have killed or captured many of their leaders.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And for the others, their day will come.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We remain on the offensive in Afghanistan, where a fine president and national assembly are fighting terror while building the institutions of a new democracy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we are on the offensive in Iraq, with a clear plan for victory.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: First, we are helping Iraqis build an inclusive government, so that old resentments will be eased and the insurgency will be marginalized.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Second, we are continuing reconstruction efforts and helping the Iraqi government to fight corruption and build a modern economy, so all Iraqis can experience the benefits of freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Third, we are striking terrorist targets while we train Iraqi forces that are increasingly capable of defeating the enemy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iraqis are showing their courage every day, and we are proud to be their allies in the cause of freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our work in Iraq is difficult because our enemy is brutal.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But that brutality has not stopped the dramatic progress of a new democracy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In less than 3 years, that nation has gone from dictatorship, to liberation, to sovereignty, to a constitution, to national elections.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: At the same time, our coalition has been relentless in shutting off terrorist infiltration, clearing out insurgent strongholds, and turning over territory to Iraqi security forces.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I am confident in our plan for victory.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I am confident in the will of the Iraqi people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I am confident in the skill and spirit of our military.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Fellow citizens, we are in this fight to win, and we are winning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The road of victory is the road that will take our troops home.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As we make progress on the ground, and Iraqi forces increasingly take the lead, we should be able to further decrease our troop levels;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: but those decisions will be made by our military commanders, not by politicians in Washington D.C.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our coalition has learned from our experience in Iraq.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have adjusted our military tactics and changed our approach to reconstruction.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Along the way, we have benefited from responsible criticism and counsel offered by Members of Congress of both parties.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the coming year, I will continue to reach out and seek your good advice.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet there is a difference between responsible criticism that aims for success and defeatism that refuses to acknowledge anything but failure.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Hindsight alone is not wisdom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And second-guessing is not a strategy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With so much in the balance, those of us in public office have a duty to speak with candor.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A sudden withdrawal of our forces from Iraq would abandon our Iraqi allies to death and prison, put men like bin Laden and Zarqawi in charge of a strategic country, and show that a pledge from America means little.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Members of Congress: however we feel about the decisions and debates of the past, our Nation has only one option: we must keep our word, defeat our enemies, and stand behind the American military in its vital mission.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our men and women in uniform are making sacrifices and showing a sense of duty stronger than all fear.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They know what it is like to fight house to house in a maze of streets, to wear heavy gear in the desert heat, to see a comrade killed by a roadside bomb.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And those who know the costs also know the stakes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Marine Staff Sergeant Dan Clay was killed last month fighting in Fallujah.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He left behind a letter to his family, but his words could just as well be addressed to every American.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Here is what Dan wrote: ``I know what honor is.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It has been an honor to protect and serve all of you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I faced death with the secure knowledge that you would not have to.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Never falter.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: nan

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Staff Sergeant Dan Clay's wife, Lisa, and his mom and dad, Sara Jo and Bud, are with us this evening.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Welcome.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our Nation is grateful to the fallen, who live in the memory of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are grateful to all who volunteer to wear our Nation's uniform;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: and as we honor our brave troops, let us never forget the sacrifices of America's military families.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our offensive against terror involves more than military action.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Ultimately, the only way to defeat the terrorists is to defeat their dark vision of hatred and fear by offering the hopeful alternative of political freedom and peaceful change.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So the United States of America supports democratic reform across the broader Middle East.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Elections are vital, but they are only the beginning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Raising up a democracy requires the rule of law, protection of minorities, and strong, accountable institutions that last longer than a single vote.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The great people of Egypt have voted in a multiparty presidential election, and now their government should open paths of peaceful opposition that will reduce the appeal of radicalism.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The Palestinian people have voted in elections, and now the leaders of Hamas must recognize Israel, disarm, reject terrorism, and work for lasting peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Saudi Arabia has taken the first steps of reform.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now it can offer its people a better future by pressing forward with those efforts.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Democracies in the Middle East will not look like our own, because they will reflect the traditions of their own citizens.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet liberty is the future of every nation in the Middle East, because liberty is the right and hope of all humanity.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The same is true of Iran, a nation now held hostage by a small clerical elite that is isolating and repressing its people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The regime in that country sponsors terrorists in the Palestinian territories and in Lebanon, and that must come to an end.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The Iranian government is defying the world with its nuclear ambitions, and the nations of the world must not permit the Iranian regime to gain nuclear weapons.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America will continue to rally the world to confront these threats.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tonight, let me speak directly to the citizens of Iran: America respects you, and we respect your country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We respect your right to choose your own future and win your own freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And our Nation hopes one day to be the closest of friends with a free and democratic Iran.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To overcome dangers in our world, we must also take the offensive by encouraging economic progress, fighting disease, and spreading hope in hopeless lands.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Isolationism would not only tie our hands in fighting enemies;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: it would keep us from helping our friends in desperate need.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We show compassion abroad because Americans believe in the God-given dignity and worth of a villager with HIV/AIDS, or an infant with malaria, or a refugee fleeing genocide, or a young girl sold into slavery.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We also show compassion abroad because regions overwhelmed by poverty, corruption, and despair are sources of terrorism, organized crime, human trafficking, and the drug trade.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In recent years, you and I have taken unprecedented action to fight AIDS and malaria, expand the education of girls, and reward developing nations that are moving forward with economic and political reform.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For people everywhere, the United States is a partner for a better life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Shortchanging these efforts would increase the suffering and chaos of our world, undercut our long-term security, and dull the conscience of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I urge Members of Congress to serve the interests of America by showing the compassion of America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our country must also remain on the offensive against terrorism here at home.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The enemy has not lost the desire or capability to attack us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Fortunately, this Nation has superb professionals in law enforcement, intelligence, the military, and homeland security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These men and women are dedicating their lives to protecting us all, and they deserve our support and our thanks.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They also deserve the same tools they already use to fight drug trafficking and organized crime, so I ask you to reauthorize the PATRIOT Act.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It is said that prior to the attacks of September 11, our government failed to connect the dots of the conspiracy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We now know that two of the hijackers in the United States placed telephone calls to al Qaeda operatives overseas.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But we did not know about their plans until it was too late.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So to prevent another attack, based on authority given to me by the Constitution and by statute, I have authorized a terrorist surveillance program to aggressively pursue the international communications of suspected al Qaeda operatives and affiliates to and from America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Previous Presidents have used the same constitutional authority I have, and Federal courts have approved the use of that authority.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Appropriate Members of Congress have been kept informed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This terrorist surveillance program has helped prevent terrorist attacks.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It remains essential to the security of America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If there are people inside our country who are talking with al Qaeda, we want to know about it, because we will not sit back and wait to be hit again.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In all these areas, from the disruption of terror networks, to victory in Iraq, to the spread of freedom and hope in troubled regions, we need the support of our friends and allies.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To draw that support, we must always be clear in our principles and willing to act.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The only alternative to American leadership is a dramatically more dangerous and anxious world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet we also choose to lead because it is a privilege to serve the values that gave us birth.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: American leaders, from Roosevelt to Truman to Kennedy to Reagan, rejected isolation and retreat because they knew that America is always more secure when freedom is on the march.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our own generation is in a long war against a determined enemy, a war that will be fought by Presidents of both parties, who will need steady bipartisan support from the Congress.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tonight I ask for yours.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Together, let us protect our country, support the men and women who defend us, and lead this world toward freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Here at home, America also has a great opportunity: we will build the prosperity of our country by strengthening our economic leadership in the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our economy is healthy and vigorous and growing faster than other major industrialized nations.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the last 2 1/2 years, America has created 4.6 million new jobs, more than Japan and the European Union combined.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Even in the face of higher energy prices and natural disasters, the American people have turned in an economic performance that is the envy of the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The American economy is preeminent, but we cannot afford to be complacent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In a dynamic world economy, we are seeing new competitors like China and India.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This creates uncertainty, which makes it easier to feed people's fears.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And so we are seeing some old temptations return.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Protectionists want to escape competition, pretending that we can keep our high standard of living while walling off our economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Others say that the government needs to take a larger role in directing the economy, centralizing more power in Washington and increasing taxes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We hear claims that immigrants are somehow bad for the economy, even though this economy could not function without them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: All these are forms of economic retreat, and they lead in the same direction, toward a stagnant and second-rate economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I will set out a better path, an agenda for a Nation that competes with confidence, an agenda that will raise standards of living and generate new jobs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Americans should not fear our economic future, because we intend to shape it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Keeping America competitive begins with keeping our economy growing, and our economy grows when Americans have more of their own money to spend, save, and invest.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the last 5 years, the tax relief you passed has left $880 billion in the hands of American workers, investors, small businesses, and families;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: and they have used it to help produce more than 4 years of uninterrupted economic growth.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet the tax relief is set to expire in the next few years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If we do nothing, American families will face a massive tax increase they do not expect and will not welcome.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Because America needs more than a temporary expansion, we need more than temporary tax relief.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I urge the Congress to act responsibly and make the tax cuts permanent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Keeping America competitive requires us to be good stewards of tax dollars.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Every year of my Presidency, we have reduced the growth of nonsecurity discretionary spending, and last year you passed bills that cut this spending.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This year my budget will cut it again and reduce or eliminate more than 140 programs that are performing poorly or not fulfilling essential priorities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By passing these reforms, we will save the American taxpayer another $14 billion next year and stay on track to cut the deficit in half by 2009.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I am pleased that Members of Congress are working on earmark reform, because the Federal budget has too many special interest projects.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we can tackle this problem together, if you pass the line-item veto.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must also confront the larger challenge of mandatory spending, or entitlements.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This year, the first of about 78 million baby boomers turn 60, including two of my dad's favorite people, me and President Clinton.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This milestone is more than a personal crisis;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: it is a national challenge.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The retirement of the baby boom generation will put unprecedented strains on the Federal Government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By 2030, spending for Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid alone will be almost 60 percent of the entire Federal budget.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And that will present future Congresses with impossible choices, staggering tax increases, immense deficits, or deep cuts in every category of spending.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Congress did not act last year on my proposal to save Social Security;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: yet the rising cost of entitlements is a problem that is not going away.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And with every year we fail to act, the situation gets worse.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So tonight, I ask you to join me in creating a commission to examine the full impact of baby boom retirements on Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This commission should include Members of Congress of both parties, and offer bipartisan solutions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We need to put aside partisan politics, work together, and get this problem solved.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Keeping America competitive requires us to open more markets for all that Americans make and grow.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One out of every five factory jobs in America is related to global trade, and we want people everywhere to buy American.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With open markets and a level playing field, no one can outproduce or outcompete the American worker.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Keeping America competitive requires an immigration system that upholds our laws, reflects our values, and serves the interests of our economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our Nation needs orderly and secure borders.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To meet this goal, we must have stronger immigration enforcement and border protection.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we must have a rational, humane guest worker program that rejects amnesty, allows temporary jobs for people who seek them legally, and reduces smuggling and crime at the border.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Keeping America competitive requires affordable health care.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our government has a responsibility to help provide health care for the poor and the elderly, and we are meeting that responsibility.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For all Americans, we must confront the rising cost of care, strengthen the doctor-patient relationship, and help people afford the insurance coverage they need.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will make wider use of electronic records and other health information technology to help control costs and reduce dangerous medical errors.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will strengthen health savings accounts by making sure individuals and small business employees can buy insurance with the same advantages that people working for big businesses now get.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will do more to make this coverage portable, so workers can switch jobs without having to worry about losing their health insurance.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And because lawsuits are driving many good doctors out of practice, leaving women in nearly 1,500 American counties without a single OB-GYN, I ask the Congress to pass medical liability reform this year.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Keeping America competitive requires affordable energy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Here we have a serious problem: America is addicted to oil, which is often imported from unstable parts of the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The best way to break this addiction is through technology.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Since 2001, we have spent nearly $10 billion to develop cleaner, cheaper, and more reliable alternative energy sources;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: and we are on the threshold of incredible advances.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So tonight, I announce the Advanced Energy Initiative, a 22 percent increase in clean energy research at the Department of Energy, to push for breakthroughs in two vital areas.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To change how we power our homes and offices, we will invest more in zero-emission coal-fired plants;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: revolutionary solar and wind technologies;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: and clean, safe nuclear energy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must also change how we power our automobiles.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will increase our research in better batteries for hybrid and electric cars and in pollution-free cars that run on hydrogen.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will also fund additional research in cutting-edge methods of producing ethanol, not just from corn but from wood chips, stalks, or switch grass.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our goal is to make this new kind of ethanol practical and competitive within 6 years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Breakthroughs on this and other new technologies will help us reach another great goal: to replace more than 75 percent of our oil imports from the Middle East by 2025.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By applying the talent and technology of America, this country can dramatically improve our environment, move beyond a petroleum-based economy, and make our dependence on Middle Eastern oil a thing of the past.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And to keep America competitive, one commitment is necessary above all: we must continue to lead the world in human talent and creativity.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our greatest advantage in the world has always been our educated, hardworking, ambitious people;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: and we are going to keep that edge.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I announce the American Competitiveness Initiative, to encourage innovation throughout our economy and to give our Nation's children a firm grounding in math and science.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: First: I propose to double the Federal commitment to the most critical basic research programs in the physical sciences over the next 10 years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This funding will support the work of America's most creative minds as they explore promising areas such as nanotechnology, supercomputing, and alternative energy sources.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Second: I propose to make permanent the research and development tax credit, to encourage bolder private-sector investment in technology.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With more research in both the public and private sectors, we will improve our quality of life and ensure that America will lead the world in opportunity and innovation for decades to come.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Third: We need to encourage children to take more math and science and make sure those courses are rigorous enough to compete with other nations.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have made a good start in the early grades with the No Child Left Behind Act, which is raising standards and lifting test scores across our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight, I propose to train 70,000 high school teachers to lead advanced placement courses in math and science;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: bring 30,000 math and science professionals to teach in classrooms;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: and give early help to students who struggle with math, so they have a better chance at good high-wage jobs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If we ensure that America's children succeed in life, they will ensure that America succeeds in the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Preparing our Nation to compete in the world is a goal that all of us can share.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I urge you to support the American Competitiveness Initiative, and together we will show the world what the American people can achieve.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is a great force for freedom and prosperity.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet our greatness is not measured in power or luxuries, but by who we are and how we treat one another.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So we strive to be a compassionate, decent, hopeful society.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In recent years, America has become a more hopeful Nation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Violent crime rates have fallen to their lowest levels since the 1970s.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Welfare cases have dropped by more than half over the past decade.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Drug use among youth is down 19 percent since 2001.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There are fewer abortions in America than at any point in the last three decades, and the number of children born to teenage mothers has been falling for a dozen years in a row.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These gains are evidence of a quiet transformation, a revolution of conscience, in which a rising generation is finding that a life of personal responsibility is a life of fulfillment.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Government has played a role.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Wise policies such as welfare reform, drug education, and support for abstinence and adoption have made a difference in the character of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And everyone here tonight, Democrat and Republican, has a right to be proud of this record.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet many Americans, especially parents, still have deep concerns about the direction of our culture and the health of our most basic institutions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They are concerned about unethical conduct by public officials, and discouraged by activist courts that try to redefine marriage.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And they worry about children in our society who need direction and love, and about fellow citizens still displaced by natural disaster, and about suffering caused by treatable diseases.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As we look at these challenges, we must never give in to the belief that America is in decline or that our culture is doomed to unravel.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The American people know better than that.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have proven the pessimists wrong before, and we will do it again.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A hopeful society depends on courts that deliver equal justice under the law.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The Supreme Court now has two superb new members on its bench, Chief Justice John Roberts and Justice Sam Alito.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I thank the Senate for confirming both of them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I will continue to nominate men and women who understand that judges must be servants of the law, and not legislate from the bench.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Today marks the official retirement of a very special American.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For 24 years of faithful service to our Nation, the United States is grateful to Justice Sandra Day O'Connor.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A hopeful society has institutions of science and medicine that do not cut ethical corners and that recognize the matchless value of every life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight, I ask you to pass legislation to prohibit the most egregious abuses of medical research: human cloning in all its forms, creating or implanting embryos for experiments, creating human-animal hybrids, and buying, selling or patenting human embryos.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Human life is a gift from our Creator, and that gift should never be discarded, devalued, or put up for sale.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A hopeful society expects elected officials to uphold the public trust.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Honorable people in both parties are working on reforms to strengthen the ethical standards of Washington, and I support your efforts.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Each of us has made a pledge to be worthy of public responsibility, and that is a pledge we must never forget, never dismiss, and never betray.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As we renew the promise of our institutions, let us also show the character of America in our compassion and care for one another.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A hopeful society gives special attention to children who lack direction and love.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Through the Helping America's Youth Initiative, we are encouraging caring adults to get involved in the life of a child, and this good work is being led by our First Lady, Laura Bush.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This year we will add resources to encourage young people to stay in school, so more of America's youth can raise their sights and achieve their dreams.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A hopeful society comes to the aid of fellow citizens in times of suffering and emergency and stays at it until they are back on their feet.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So far the Federal Government has committed $85 billion to the people of the gulf coast and New Orleans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are removing debris, repairing highways, and building stronger levees.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are providing business loans and housing assistance.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet as we meet these immediate needs, we must also address deeper challenges that existed before the storm arrived.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In New Orleans and in other places, many of our fellow citizens have felt excluded from the promise of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The answer is not only temporary relief, but schools that teach every child and job skills that bring upward mobility and more opportunities to own a home and start a business.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As we recover from a disaster, let us also work for the day when all Americans are protected by justice, equal in hope, and rich in opportunity.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A hopeful society acts boldly to fight diseases like HIV/AIDS, which can be prevented and treated and defeated.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: More than a million Americans live with HIV, and half of all AIDS cases occur among African Americans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask Congress to reform and reauthorize the Ryan White Act and provide new funding to States so we end the waiting lists for AIDS medicines in America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will also lead a nationwide effort, working closely with African American churches and faith-based groups, to deliver rapid HIV tests to millions, end the stigma of AIDS, and come closer to the day when there are no new infections in America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Fellow citizens, we have been called to leadership in a period of consequence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have entered a great ideological conflict we did nothing to invite.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We see great changes in science and commerce that will influence all our lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And sometimes it can seem that history is turning in a wide arc, toward an unknown shore.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet the destination of history is determined by human action, and every great movement of history comes to a point of choosing.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Lincoln could have accepted peace at the cost of disunity and continued slavery.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Martin Luther King could have stopped at Birmingham or at Selma and achieved only half a victory over segregation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The United States could have accepted the permanent division of Europe and been complicit in the oppression of others.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Today, having come far in our own historical journey, we must decide: Will we turn back, or finish well?

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Before history is written down in books, it is written in courage.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Like Americans before us, we will show that courage, and we will finish well.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will lead freedom's advance.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will compete and excel in the global economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will renew the defining moral commitments of this land.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And so we move forward, optimistic about our country, faithful to its cause, and confident of the victories to come.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: May God bless America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Thank you very much.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight, I have a high privilege and distinct honor of my own--as the first President to begin the State of the Union message with these words: Madam Speaker.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In his day, the late Congressman Thomas D'Alesandro, Jr., from Baltimore, Maryland, saw Presidents Roosevelt and Truman at this rostrum.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But nothing could compare with the sight of his only daughter, Nancy, presiding tonight as Speaker of the House of Representatives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Congratulations, Madam Speaker.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Two Members of the House and Senate are not with us tonight, and we pray for the recovery and speedy return of Senator Tim Johnson and Congressman Charlie Norwood.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Madam Speaker, Vice President Cheney, Members of Congress, distinguished guests, and fellow citizens: This rite of custom brings us together at a defining hour, when decisions are hard and courage is tested.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We enter the year 2007 with large endeavors under way, and others that are ours to begin.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In all of this, much is asked of us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must have the will to face difficult challenges and determined enemies, and the wisdom to face them together.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some in this Chamber are new to the House and Senate, and I congratulate the Democratic majority.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Congress has changed, but our responsibilities have not.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Each of us is guided by our own convictions, and to these we must stay faithful.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet we are all held to the same standards and called to serve the same good purposes: to extend the Nation's prosperity, to spend the people's money wisely, to solve problems, not leave them to future generations, to guard America against all evil, and to keep faith with those we have sent forth to defend us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are not the first to come here with government divided and uncertainty in the air.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Like many before us, we can work through our differences and achieve big things for the American people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our citizens don't much care which side of the aisle we sit on, as long as we are willing to cross that aisle when there is work to be done.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our job is to make life better for our fellow Americans and help them to build a future of hope and opportunity, and this is the business before us tonight.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A future of hope and opportunity begins with a growing economy, and that is what we have.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are now in the 41st month of uninterrupted job growth, in a recovery that has created 7.2 million new jobs, so far.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Unemployment is low, inflation is low, and wages are rising.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The economy is on the move, and our job is to keep it that way, not with more government but with more enterprise.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Next week, I will deliver a full report on the state of our economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight, I want to discuss three economic reforms that deserve to be priorities for this Congress.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: First, we must balance the Federal budget.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We can do so without raising taxes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: What we need to do is impose spending discipline in Washington, D.C.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We set a goal of cutting the deficit in half by 2009, and met that goal 3 years ahead of schedule.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now let us take the next step.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the coming weeks, I will submit a budget that eliminates the Federal deficit within the next 5 years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask you to make the same commitment.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Together, we can restrain the spending appetite of the Federal Government and balance the Federal budget.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Next, there is the matter of earmarks.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These special interest items are often slipped into bills at the last hour, when not even C-SPAN is watching.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In 2005 alone, the number of earmarks grew to over 13,000 and totaled nearly $18 billion.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Even worse, over 90 percent of earmarks never make it to the floor of the House and Senate.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They are dropped into committee reports that are not even part of the bill that arrives on my desk.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You did not vote them into law.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I did not sign them into law.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet they are treated as if they have the force of law.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The time has come to end this practice.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So let us work together to reform the budget process, expose every earmark to the light of day and to a vote in Congress, and cut the number and cost of earmarks at least in half by the end of this session.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Finally, to keep this economy strong we must take on the challenge of entitlements.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Social Security and Medicare and Medicaid are commitments of conscience, and so it is our duty to keep them permanently sound.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet we are failing in that duty, and this failure will one day leave our children with three bad options: huge tax increases, huge deficits, or huge and immediate cuts in benefits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Everyone in this Chamber knows this to be true, yet somehow we have not found it in ourselves to act.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So let us work together and do it now.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With enough good sense and good will, you and I can fix Medicare and Medicaid, and save Social Security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Spreading opportunity and hope in America also requires public schools that give children the knowledge and character they need in life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Five years ago, we rose above partisan differences to pass the No Child Left Behind Act, preserving local control, raising standards, and holding those schools accountable for results.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And because we acted, students are performing better in reading and math, and minority students are closing the achievement gap.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now the task is to build on this success, without watering down standards, without taking control from local communities, and without back sliding and calling it reform.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We can lift student achievement even higher by giving local leaders flexibility to turn around failing schools, and by giving families with children stuck in failing schools the right to choose someplace better.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must increase funds for students who struggle, and make sure these children get the special help they need.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we can make sure our children are prepared for the jobs of the future, and our country is more competitive, by strengthening math and science skills.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The No Child Left Behind Act has worked for America's children, and I ask Congress to reauthorize this good law.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A future of hope and opportunity requires that all our citizens have affordable and available health care.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When it comes to health care, government has an obligation to care for the elderly, the disabled, and poor children, and we will meet those responsibilities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For all other Americans, private health care insurance is the best way to meet their needs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But many Americans cannot afford a health insurance policy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So tonight, I propose two new initiatives to help more Americans afford their own insurance.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: First, I propose a standard tax deduction for health insurance that will be like the standard tax deduction for dependents.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Families with health insurance will pay no income or payroll taxes on $15,000 of their income.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Single Americans with health insurance will pay no income or payroll taxes on $7,500 of their income.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With this reform, more than 100 million men, women, and children who are now covered by employer-provided insurance will benefit from lower tax bills.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: At the same time, this reform will level the playing field for those who do not get health insurance through their job.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For Americans who now purchase health insurance on their own, this proposal would mean a substantial tax savings, $4,500 for a family of four making $60,000 a year.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And for the millions of other Americans who have no health insurance at all, this deduction would help put a basic private health insurance plan within their reach.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Changing the Tax Code is a vital and necessary step to making health care affordable for more Americans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My second proposal is to help the States that are coming up with innovative ways to cover the uninsured.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: States that make basic private health insurance available to all their citizens should receive Federal funds to help them provide this coverage to the poor and the sick.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I have asked the Secretary of Health and Human Services to work with Congress to take existing Federal funds and use them to create ``Affordable Choices'' grants.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These grants would give our Nation's Governors more money and more flexibility to get private health insurance to those most in need.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There are many other ways that Congress can help.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We need to expand health savings accounts.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: *We need to help small businesses through association health plans, we need to reduce costs and medical errors with better information technology.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will encourage price transparency, and to protect good doctors from junk lawsuits we need to pass medical liability reform.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And in all we do, we must remember that the best health care decisions are made not by government and insurance companies, but by patients and their doctors.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Extending hope and opportunity in our country requires an immigration system worthy of America, with laws that are fair and borders that are secure.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When laws and borders are routinely violated, this harms the interests of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To secure our border, we are doubling the size of the Border Patrol, and funding new infrastructure and technology.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet even with all these steps, we cannot fully secure the border unless we take pressure off the border, and that requires a temporary worker program.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We should establish a legal and orderly path for foreign workers to enter our country to work on a temporary basis.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As a result, they won't have to try to sneak in, and that will leave border agents free to chase down drug smugglers and criminals and terrorists.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will enforce our immigration laws at the work site, and give employers the tools to verify the legal status of their workers, so there is no excuse left for violating the law.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We need to uphold the great tradition of the melting pot that welcomes and assimilates new arrivals.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We need to resolve the status of illegal immigrants who are already in our country, without animosity and without amnesty.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Convictions run deep in this Capitol when it comes to immigration.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Let us have a serious, civil, and conclusive debate, so that you can pass, and I can sign, comprehensive immigration reform into law.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Extending hope and opportunity depends on a stable supply of energy that keeps America's economy running and America's environment clean.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For too long our Nation has been dependent on foreign oil, and this dependence leaves us more vulnerable to hostile regimes, and to terrorists, who could cause huge disruptions of oil shipments, and raise the price of oil, and do great harm to our economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It is in our vital interest to diversify America's energy supply, and the way forward is through technology.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must continue changing the way America generates electric power, by even greater use of clean coal technology, solar and wind energy, and clean, safe nuclear power.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We need to press on with battery research for plug-in and hybrid vehicles and expand the use of clean diesel vehicles and biodiesel fuel.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must continue investing in new methods of producing ethanol, using everything from wood chips, to grasses, to agricultural wastes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have made a lot of progress, thanks to good policies here in Washington and the strong response of the market.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And now even more dramatic advances are within reach.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight, I ask Congress to join me in pursuing a great goal.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Let us build on the work we have done and reduce gasoline usage in the United States by 20 percent in the next 10 years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When we do that, we will be cutting our total imports by the equivalent of three-quarters of all the oil we now import from the Middle East.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To reach this goal, we must increase the supply of alternative fuels, by setting a mandatory fuels standard to require 35 billion gallons of renewable and alternative fuels in 2017.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And that is nearly five times the current target.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: At the same time, we need to reform and modernize fuel economy standards for cars the way we did for light trucks, and conserve up to 8 1/2 billion more gallons of gasoline by 2017.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Achieving these ambitious goals will dramatically reduce our dependence on foreign oil, but it is not going to eliminate it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So as we continue to diversify our fuel supply, we must also step up domestic oil production in environmentally sensitive ways.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And to further protect America against severe disruptions to our oil supply, I ask Congress to double the current capacity of the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is on the verge of technological breakthroughs that will enable us to live our lives less dependent on oil.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These technologies will help us become better stewards of the environment, and they will help us to confront the serious challenge of global climate change.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A future of hope and opportunity requires a fair, impartial system of justice.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The lives of our citizens across our Nation are affected by the outcome of cases pending in our Federal courts.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have a shared obligation to ensure that the Federal courts have enough judges to hear those cases and deliver timely rulings.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As president, I have a duty to nominate qualified men and women to vacancies on the Federal bench.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And the United States Senate has a duty as well, to give those nominees a fair hearing and a prompt up-or-down vote on the Senate floor.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For all of us in this room, there is no higher responsibility than to protect the people of this country from danger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Five years have come and gone since we saw the scenes and felt the sorrow that the terrorists can cause.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have had time to take stock of our situation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have added many critical protections to guard the homeland.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We know with certainty that the horrors of that September morning were just a glimpse of what the terrorists intend for us, unless we stop them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With the distance of time, we find ourselves debating the causes of conflict and the course we have followed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Such debates are essential when a great democracy faces great questions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet one question has surely been settled, that to win the war on terror we must take the fight to the enemy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: From the start, America and our allies have protected our people by staying on the offense.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The enemy knows that the days of comfortable sanctuary, easy movement, steady financing, and free-flowing communications are long over.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For the terrorists, life since 9/11 has never been the same.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our success in this war is often measured by the things that did not happen.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We cannot know the full extent of the attacks that we and our allies have prevents, but here is some of what we do know: we stopped an al Qaeda plot to fly a hijacked airplane into the tallest building on the west coast.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We broke up a Southeast Asian terrorist cell grooming operatives for attacks inside the United States.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We uncovered an al Qaeda cell developing anthrax to be used in attacks against America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And just last August, British authorities uncovered a plot to blow up passenger planes bound for America over the Atlantic Ocean.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For each life saved, we owe a debt of gratitude to the brave public servants who devote their lives to finding the terrorists and stopping them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Every success against the terrorists is a reminder of the shoreless ambitions of this enemy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The evil that inspired and rejoiced in 9/11 is still at work in the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And so long as that is the case, America is still a Nation at war.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the minds of the terrorists, this war began well before September 11 and will not end until their radical vision is fulfilled.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And these past 5 years have given us a much clearer view of the nature of this enemy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Al Qaeda and its followers are Sunni extremists, possessed by hatred and commanded by a harsh and narrow ideology.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Take almost any principle of civilization, and their goal is the opposite.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They preach with threats, instruct with bullets and bombs, and promise paradise for the murder of the innocent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our enemies are quite explicit about their intentions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They want to overthrow moderate governments and establish safe havens from which to plan and carry out new attacks on our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By killing and terrorizing Americans, they want to force our country to retreat from the world and abandon the cause of liberty.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They would then be free to impose their will and spread their totalitarian ideology.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: nan

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These men are not given to idle words, and they are just one camp in the Islamist radical movement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In recent times, it has also become clear that we face an escalating danger from Shia extremists who are just as hostile to America and are also determined to dominate the Middle East.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many are known to take direction from the regime in Iran, which is funding and arming terrorists like Hezbollah, a group second only to al Qaeda in the American lives it has taken.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The Shia and Sunni extremists are different faces of the same totalitarian threat.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Whatever slogans they chant, when they slaughter the innocent, they have the same wicked purposes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They want to kill Americans, kill democracy in the Middle East, and gain the weapons to kill on an even more horrific scale.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the sixth year since our Nation was attacked, I wish I could report to you that the dangers had ended.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They have not.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And so it remains the policy of this government to use every lawful and proper tool of intelligence, diplomacy, law enforcement, and military action to do our duty, to find these enemies, and to protect the American people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This war is more than a clash of arms.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It is a decisive ideological struggle, and the security of our Nation is in the balance.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To prevail, we must remove the conditions that inspire blind hatred, and drove 19 men to get onto airplanes and to come and kill us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: What every terrorist fears most is human freedom, societies where men and women make their own choices, answer to their own conscience, and live by their hopes instead of their resentments.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Free people are not drawn to violent and malignant ideologies, and most will choose a better way when they are given a chance.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So we advance our own security interests by helping moderates, reformers, and brave voices for democracy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The great question of our day is whether America will help men and women in the Middle East to build free societies and share in the rights of all humanity.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I say, for the sake of our own security, we must.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the last 2 years, we have seen the desire for liberty in the broader Middle East, and we have been sobered by the enemy's fierce reaction.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In 2005, the world watched as the citizens of Lebanon raised the banner of the Cedar Revolution.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They drove out the Syrian occupiers, and chose new leaders in free elections.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In 2005, the people of Afghanistan defied the terrorists and elected a democratic legislature.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And in 2005, the Iraqi people held three national elections, choosing a transitional government, adopting the most progressive, democratic constitution in the Arab world, and then electing a government under that constitution.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Despite endless threats from the killers in their midst, nearly 12 million Iraqi citizens came out to vote in a show of hope and solidarity we should never forget.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A thinking enemy watched all of these scenes, adjusted their tactics, and in 2006 they struck back.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In Lebanon, assassins took the life of Pierre Gemayel, a prominent participant in the Cedar Revolution.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Hezbollah terrorists, with support from Syria and Iran, sowed conflict in the region and are seeking to undermine Lebanon's legitimately elected government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In Afghanistan, Taliban and al Qaeda fighters tried to regain power by regrouping and engaging Afghan and NATO forces.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In Iraq, al Qaeda and other Sunni extremists blew up one of the most sacred places in Shia Islam, the Golden Mosque of Samarra.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This atrocity, directed at a Muslim house of prayer, was designed to provoke retaliation from Iraqi Shia, and it succeeded.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Radical Shia elements, some of whom receive support from Iran, formed death squads.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The result was a tragic escalation of sectarian rage and reprisal that continues to this day.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This is not the fight we entered in Iraq, but it is the fight we are in.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Every one of us wishes that this war were over and won.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet it would not be like us to leave our promises unkept, our friends abandoned, and our own security at risk.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Ladies and gentlemen, on this day, at this hour, it is still within our power to shape the outcome of this battle.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Let us find our resolve and turn events toward victory.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are carrying out a new strategy in Iraq, a plan that demands more from Iraq's elected government and gives our forces in Iraq the reinforcements they need to complete their mission.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our goal is a democratic Iraq that upholds the rule of law, respects the rights of its people, provides them security, and is an ally in the war on terror.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In order to make progress toward this goal, the Iraqi Government must stop the sectarian violence in its capital.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But the Iraqis are not yet ready to do this on their own.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So we are deploying reinforcements of more than 20,000 additional soldiers and marines to Iraq.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The vast majority will go to Baghdad, where they will help Iraqi forces to clear and secure neighborhoods, and serve as advisers embedded in Iraqi Army units.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With Iraqis in the lead, our forces will help secure the city by chasing down the terrorists, insurgents, and the roaming death squads.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And in Anbar province, where al Qaeda terrorists have gathered and local forces have begun showing a willingness to fight them, we are sending an additional 4,000 United States marines, with orders to find the terrorists and clear them out.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We did not drive al Qaeda out of their safe haven in Afghanistan only to let them set up a new safe haven in a free Iraq.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The people of Iraq want to live in peace, and now is the time for their government to act.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iraq's leaders know that our commitment is not open ended.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They have promised to deploy more of their own troops to secure Baghdad, and they must do so.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They have pledged that they will confront violent radicals of any faction or political party.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And they need to follow through and lift needless restrictions on Iraqi and Coalition forces so these troops can achieve their mission of bringing security to all of the people of Baghdad.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iraq's leaders have committed themselves to a series of benchmarks to achieve reconciliation, to share oil revenues among all of Iraq's citizens, to put the wealth of Iraq into the rebuilding of Iraq, to allow more Iraqis to reenter their nation's civic life, to hold local elections, and to take responsibility for security in every Iraqi province.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But for all of this to happen, Baghdad must be secured.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And our plan will help the Iraqi Government take back its capital and make good on its commitments.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My fellow citizens, our military commanders and I have carefully weighed the options.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We discussed every possible approach.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the end, I chose this course of action because it provides the best chance for success.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many in this Chamber understand that America must not fail in Iraq, because you understand that the consequences of failure would be grievous and far reaching.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If American forces step back before Baghdad is secure, the Iraqi Government would be overrun by extremists on all sides.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We could expect an epic battle between Shia extremists backed by Iran, and Sunni extremists aided by al Qaeda and supporters of the old regime.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A contagion of violence could spill out across the country, and in time the entire region could be drawn into the conflict.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For America, this is a nightmare scenario.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: For the enemy, this is the objective.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Chaos is their greatest ally in this struggle.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And out of chaos in Iraq would emerge an emboldened enemy with new safe havens, new recruits, new resources, and an even greater determination to harm America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To allow this to happen would be to ignore the lessons of September 11 and invite tragedy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And ladies and gentlemen, nothing is more important at this moment in our history than for America to succeed in the Middle East, to succeed in Iraq, and to spare the American people from this danger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This is where matters stand tonight, in the here and now.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I have spoken with many of you in person.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I respect you and the arguments you have made.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We went into this largely united, in our assumptions and in our convictions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And whatever you voted for, you did not vote for failure.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our country is pursuing a new strategy in Iraq, and I ask you to give it a chance to work.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I ask you to support our troops in the field, and those on their way.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The war on terror we fight today is a generational struggle that will continue long after you and I have turned our duties over to others.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That is why it is important to work together so our Nation can see this great effort through.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Both parties and both branches should work in close consultation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And this is why I propose to establish a special advisory council on the war on terror, made up of leaders in Congress from both political parties.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will share ideas for how to position America to meet every challenge that confronts us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we will show our enemies abroad that we are united in the goal of victory.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One of the first steps we can take together is to add to the ranks of our military, so that the American Armed Forces are ready for all the challenges ahead.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I ask the Congress to authorize an increase in the size of our active Army and Marine Corps by 92,000 in the next 5 years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A second task we can take on together is to design and establish a volunteer civilian reserve corps.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Such a corps would function much like our military reserve.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It would ease the burden on the Armed Forces by allowing us to hire civilians with critical skills to serve on missions abroad when America needs them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And it would give people across America who do not wear the uniform a chance to serve in the defining struggle of our time.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Americans can have confidence in the outcome of this struggle, because we are not in this struggle alone.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have a diplomatic strategy that is rallying the world to join in the fight against extremism.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In Iraq, multinational forces are operating under a mandate from the United Nations, and we are working with Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and the gulf states to increase support for Iraq's government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The United Nations has imposed sanctions on Iran and made it clear that the world will not allow the regime in Tehran to acquire nuclear weapons.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With the other members of the Quartet, the U.N., the Eurpoean Union and Russia, we are pursuing diplomacy to help bring peace to the Holy Land, and pursuing the establishment of a democratic Palestinian state living side by side with Israel in peace and security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In Afghanistan, NATO has taken the lead in turning back the Taliban and al Qaeda offensive, the first time the alliance has deployed forces outside the North Atlantic area.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Together with our partners in China, Japan, Russia, and South Korea, we are pursuing intensive diplomacy to achieve a Korean Peninsula free of nuclear weapons.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we will continue to speak out for the cause of freedom in places like Cuba, Belarus, and Burma, and continue to awaken the conscience of the world to save the people of Darfur.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: American foreign policy is more than a matter of war and diplomacy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our work in the world is also based on a timeless truth: to whom much is given, much is required.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We hear the call to take on the challenges of hunger and poverty and disease, and that is precisely what America is doing.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must continue to fight HIV/AIDS, especially on the continent of Africa.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Because you funded our Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief, the number of people receiving life-saving drugs has grown from 50,000 to more than 800,000 in 3 short years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask you to continue funding our efforts to fight HIV/AIDS, and I ask you to provide $1 billion over 5 years so we can combat malaria in 15 African countries.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask that you fund the Millennium Challenge Account so that American aid reaches the people who need it, in nations where democracy is on the rise and corruption is in retreat.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And let us continue to support the expanded trade and debt relief that are the best hope for lifting lives and eliminating poverty.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When America serves others in this way, we show the strength and generosity of our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These deeds reflect the character of our people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The greatest strength we have is the heroic kindness, courage, and self-sacrifice of the American people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: You see this spirit often if you know where to look, and tonight we need only look above to the gallery.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Dikembe Mutombo grew up in Africa amid great poverty and disease.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He came to Georgetown University on a scholarship to study medicine, but Coach John Thompson got a look at Dikembe and had a different idea.

text: Tommy Rieman was a teenager pumping gas in Independence, Kentucky, when he enlisted in the United States Army.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In December 2003, he was on a reconnaissance mission in Iraq when his team came under heavy enemy fire.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: From his Humvee, Sergeant Rieman returned fire.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He used his body as a shield to protect his gunner.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He was shot in the chest and arm, and received shrapnel wounds to his legs, yet he refused medical attention and stayed in the fight.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: He helped to repel a second attack, firing grenades at the enemy's position.

speaker: George W. Bush

speaker: George W. Bush

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Madam Speaker, Vice President Cheney, members of Congress, distinguished guests, and fellow citizens:

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Seven years have passed since I first stood before you at this rostrum.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In that time, our country has been tested in ways none of us could have imagined.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We faced hard decisions about peace and war, rising competition in the world economy, and the health and welfare of our citizens.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These issues call for vigorous debate, and I think it's fair to say we've answered the call.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet history will record that amid our differences, we acted with purpose.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And together, we showed the world the power and resilience of American self-government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: All of us were sent to Washington to carry out the people's business.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That is the purpose of this body.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It is the meaning of our oath.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It remains our charge to keep.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The actions of the 110th Congress will affect the security and prosperity of our nation long after this session has ended.

speaker: George W. Bush
