text: In this election year, let us show our fellow Americans that we recognize our responsibilities and are determined to meet them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Let us show them that Republicans and Democrats can compete for votes and cooperate for results at the same time.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: From expanding opportunity to protecting our country, we've made good progress.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet we have unfinished business before us, and the American people expect us to get it done.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the work ahead, we must be guided by the philosophy that made our nation great.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As Americans, we believe in the power of individuals to determine their destiny and shape the course of history.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We believe that the most reliable guide for our country is the collective wisdom of ordinary citizens.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And so in all we do, we must trust in the ability of free peoples to make wise decisions, and empower them to improve their lives for their futures.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To build a prosperous future, we must trust people with their own money and empower them to grow our economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As we meet tonight, our economy is undergoing a period of uncertainty.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America has added jobs for a record 52 straight months, but jobs are now growing at a slower pace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Wages are up, but so are prices for food and gas.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Exports are rising, but the housing market has declined.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: At kitchen tables across our country, there is a concern about our economic future.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the long run, Americans can be confident about our economic growth.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But in the short run, we can all see that that growth is slowing.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So last week, my administration reached agreement with Speaker Pelosi and Republican Leader Boehner on a robust growth package that includes tax relief for individuals and families and incentives for business investment.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The temptation will be to load up the bill.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That would delay it or derail it, and neither option is acceptable.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This is a good agreement that will keep our economy growing and our people working.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And this Congress must pass it as soon as possible.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have other work to do on taxes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Unless Congress acts, most of the tax relief we've delivered over the past seven years will be taken away.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Some in Washington argue that letting tax relief expire is not a tax increase.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Try explaining that to 116 million American taxpayers who would see their taxes rise by an average of $1,800.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Others have said they would personally be happy to pay higher taxes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I welcome their enthusiasm.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I'm pleased to report that the IRS accepts both checks and money orders.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Most Americans think their taxes are high enough.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With all the other pressures on their finances, American families should not have to worry about their federal government taking a bigger bite out of their paychecks.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There's only one way to eliminate this uncertainty:  Make the tax relief permanent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And members of Congress should know:  If any bill raises taxes reaches my desk, I will veto it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Just as we trust Americans with their own money, we need to earn their trust by spending their tax dollars wisely.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Next week, I'll send you a budget that terminates or substantially reduces 151 wasteful or bloated programs, totaling more than $18 billion.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The budget that I will submit will keep America on track for a surplus in 2012.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: American families have to balance their budgets;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: so should their government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The people's trust in their government is undermined by congressional earmarks -- special interest projects that are often snuck in at the last minute, without discussion or debate.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last year, I asked you to voluntarily cut the number and cost of earmarks in half.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I also asked you to stop slipping earmarks into committee reports that never even come to a vote.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Unfortunately, neither goal was met.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So this time, if you send me an appropriations bill that does not cut the number and cost of earmarks in half, I'll send it back to you with my veto.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tomorrow, I will issue an executive order that directs federal agencies to ignore any future earmark that is not voted on by Congress.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If these items are truly worth funding, Congress should debate them in the open and hold a public vote.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our shared responsibilities extend beyond matters of taxes and spending.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On housing, we must trust Americans with the responsibility of homeownership and empower them to weather turbulent times in the housing market.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My administration brought together the HOPE NOW alliance, which is helping many struggling homeowners avoid foreclosure.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And Congress can help even more.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight I ask you to pass legislation to reform Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, modernize the Federal Housing Administration, and allow state housing agencies to issue tax-free bonds to help homeowners refinance their mortgages.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These are difficult times for many American families, and by taking these steps, we can help more of them keep their homes.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To build a future of quality health care, we must trust patients and doctors to make medical decisions and empower them with better information and better options.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We share a common goal: making health care more affordable and accessible for all Americans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The best way to achieve that goal is by expanding consumer choice, not government control.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So I have proposed ending the bias in the tax code against those who do not get their health insurance through their employer.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This one reform would put private coverage within reach for millions, and I call on the Congress to pass it this year.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The Congress must also expand health savings accounts, create Association Health Plans for small businesses, promote health information technology, and confront the epidemic of junk medical lawsuits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With all these steps, we will help ensure that decisions about your medical care are made in the privacy of your doctor's office -- not in the halls of Congress.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On education, we must trust students to learn if given the chance, and empower parents to demand results from our schools.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In neighborhoods across our country, there are boys and girls with dreams -- and a decent education is their only hope of achieving them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Six years ago, we came together to pass the No Child Left Behind Act, and today no one can deny its results.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last year, fourth and eighth graders achieved the highest math scores on record.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Reading scores are on the rise.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: African American and Hispanic students posted all-time highs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now we must work together to increase accountability, add flexibility for states and districts, reduce the number of high school dropouts, provide extra help for struggling schools.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Members of Congress: The No Child Left Behind Act is a bipartisan achievement.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It is succeeding.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we owe it to America's children, their parents, and their teachers to strengthen this good law.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must also do more to help children when their schools do not measure up.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Thanks to the D.C. Opportunity Scholarships you approved, more than 2,600 of the poorest children in our Nation's Capital have found new hope at a faith-based or other non-public school.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Sadly, these schools are disappearing at an alarming rate in many of America's inner cities.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And to open the doors of these schools to more children, I ask you to support a new $300 million program called Pell Grants for Kids. We have seen how Pell Grants help low-income college students realize their full potential.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Together, we've expanded the size and reach of these grants. Now let us apply that same spirit to help liberate poor children trapped in failing public schools. (Applause.)

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So I will convene a White House summit aimed at strengthening these lifelines of learning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On trade, we must trust American workers to compete with anyone in the world and empower them by opening up new markets overseas.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Today, our economic growth increasingly depends on our ability to sell American goods and crops and services all over the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So we're working to break down barriers to trade and investment wherever we can.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're working for a successful Doha Round of trade talks, and we must complete a good agreement this year.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: At the same time, we're pursuing opportunities to open up new markets by passing free trade agreements.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I thank the Congress for approving a good agreement with Peru.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And now I ask you to approve agreements with Colombia and Panama and South Korea.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many products from these nations now enter America duty-free, yet many of our products face steep tariffs in their markets.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These agreements will level the playing field.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They will give us better access to nearly 100 million customers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: nan

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These agreements also promote America's strategic interests.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The first agreement that will come before you is with Colombia, a friend of America that is confronting violence and terror, and fighting drug traffickers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: If we fail to pass this agreement, we will embolden the purveyors of false populism in our hemisphere.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So we must come together, pass this agreement, and show our neighbors in the region that democracy leads to a better life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Trade brings better jobs and better choices and better prices.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet for some Americans, trade can mean losing a job, and the federal government has a responsibility to help.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I ask Congress to reauthorize and reform trade adjustment assistance, so we can help these displaced workers learn new skills and find new jobs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To build a future of energy security, we must trust in the creative genius of American researchers and entrepreneurs and empower them to pioneer a new generation of clean energy technology.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our security, our prosperity, and our environment all require reducing our dependence on oil

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last year, I asked you to pass legislation to reduce oil consumption over the next decade, and you responded.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Together we should take the next steps: Let us fund new technologies that can generate coal power while capturing carbon emissions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Let us increase the use of renewable power and emissions-free nuclear power.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Let us continue investing in advanced battery technology and renewable fuels to power the cars and trucks of the future.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Let us create a new international clean technology fund, which will help developing nations like India and China make greater use of clean energy sources.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And let us complete an international agreement that has the potential to slow, stop, and eventually reverse the growth of greenhouse gases.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This agreement will be effective only if it includes commitments by every major economy and gives none a free ride.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The United States is committed to strengthening our energy security and confronting global climate change.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And the best way to meet these goals is for America to continue leading the way toward the development of cleaner and more energy-efficient technology.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To keep America competitive into the future, we must trust in the skill of our scientists and engineers and empower them to pursue the breakthroughs of tomorrow.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last year, Congress passed legislation supporting the American Competitiveness Initiative, but never followed through with the funding.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This funding is essential to keeping our scientific edge.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So I ask Congress to double federal support for critical basic research in the physical sciences and ensure America remains the most dynamic nation on Earth.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On matters of life and science, we must trust in the innovative spirit of medical researchers and empower them to discover new treatments while respecting moral boundaries.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In November, we witnessed a landmark achievement when scientists discovered a way to reprogram adult skin cells to act like embryonic stem cells.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This breakthrough has the potential to move us beyond the divisive debates of the past by extending the frontiers of medicine without the destruction of human life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So we're expanding funding for this type of ethical medical research.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And as we explore promising avenues of research, we must also ensure that all life is treated with the dignity it deserves.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And so I call on Congress to pass legislation that bans unethical practices such as the buying, selling, patenting, or cloning of human life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On matters of justice, we must trust in the wisdom of our founders and empower judges who understand that the Constitution means what it says.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I've submitted judicial nominees who will rule by the letter of the law, not the whim of the gavel.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Many of these nominees are being unfairly delayed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They are worthy of confirmation, and the Senate should give each of them a prompt up-or-down vote.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In communities across our land, we must trust in the good heart of the American people and empower them to serve their neighbors in need.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Over the past seven years, more of our fellow citizens have discovered that the pursuit of happiness leads to the path of service.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Americans have volunteered in record numbers.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Charitable donations are higher than ever.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Faith-based groups are bringing hope to pockets of despair, with newfound support from the federal government.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And to help guarantee equal treatment of faith-based organizations when they compete for federal funds, I ask you to permanently extend Charitable Choice.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tonight the armies of compassion continue the march to a new day in the Gulf Coast.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America honors the strength and resilience of the people of this region.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We reaffirm our pledge to help them build stronger and better than before.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tonight I'm pleased to announce that in April we will host this year's North American Summit of Canada, Mexico, and the United States in the great city of New Orleans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: There are two other pressing challenges that I've raised repeatedly before this body, and that this body has failed to address: entitlement spending and immigration.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Every member in this chamber knows that spending on entitlement programs like Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid is growing faster than we can afford.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We all know the painful choices ahead if America stays on this path: massive tax increases, sudden and drastic cuts in benefits, or crippling deficits.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I've laid out proposals to reform these programs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Now I ask members of Congress to offer your proposals and come up with a bipartisan solution to save these vital programs for our children and our grandchildren.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The other pressing challenge is immigration.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America needs to secure our borders -- and with your help, my administration is taking steps to do so.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're increasing worksite enforcement, deploying fences and advanced technologies to stop illegal crossings.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: at the border, and by the end of this year, we will have doubled the number of border patrol agents.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet we also need to acknowledge that we will never fully secure our border until we create a lawful way for foreign workers to come here and support our economy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This will take pressure off the border and allow law enforcement to concentrate on those who mean us harm.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must also find a sensible and humane way to deal with people here illegally.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Illegal immigration is complicated, but it can be resolved.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And it must be resolved in a way that upholds both our laws and our highest ideals.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This is the business of our nation here at home.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet building a prosperous future for our citizens also depends on confronting enemies abroad and advancing liberty in troubled regions of the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our foreign policy is based on a clear premise: We trust that people, when given the chance, will choose a future of freedom and peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the last seven years, we have witnessed stirring moments in the history of liberty.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've seen citizens in Georgia and Ukraine stand up for their right to free and fair elections.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've seen people in Lebanon take to the streets to demand their independence.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've seen Afghans emerge from the tyranny of the Taliban and choose a new president and a new parliament.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've seen jubilant Iraqis holding up ink-stained fingers and celebrating their freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These images of liberty have inspired us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the past seven years, we've also seen images that have sobered us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've watched throngs of mourners in Lebanon and Pakistan carrying the caskets of beloved leaders taken by the assassin's hand.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've seen wedding guests in blood-soaked finery staggering from a hotel in Jordan, Afghans and Iraqis blown up in mosques and markets, and trains in London and Madrid ripped apart by bombs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On a clear September day, we saw thousands of our fellow citizens taken from us in an instant.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These horrific images serve as a grim reminder: The advance of liberty is opposed by terrorists and extremists -- evil men who despise freedom, despise America, and aim to subject millions to their violent rule.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Since 9/11, we have taken the fight to these terrorists and extremists.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will stay on the offense, we will keep up the pressure, and we will deliver justice to our enemies.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are engaged in the defining ideological struggle of the 21st century.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The terrorists oppose every principle of humanity and decency that we hold dear.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Yet in this war on terror, there is one thing we and our enemies agree on: In the long run, men and women who are free to determine their own destinies will reject terror and refuse to live in tyranny.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And that is why the terrorists are fighting to deny this choice to the people in Lebanon, Iraq, Afghanistan, Pakistan, and the Palestinian Territories.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And that is why, for the security of America and the peace of the world, we are spreading the hope of freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In Afghanistan, America, our 25 NATO allies, and 15 partner nations are helping the Afghan people defend their freedom and rebuild their country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Thanks to the courage of these military and civilian personnel, a nation that was once a safe haven for al Qaeda is now a young democracy where boys and girls are going to school, new roads and hospitals are being built, and people are looking to the future with new hope.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These successes must continue, so we're adding 3,200 Marines to our forces in Afghanistan, where they will fight the terrorists and train the Afghan Army and police.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Defeating the Taliban and al Qaeda is critical to our security, and I thank the Congress for supporting America's vital mission in Afghanistan.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In Iraq, the terrorists and extremists are fighting to deny a proud people their liberty, and fighting to establish safe havens for attacks across the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: One year ago, our enemies were succeeding in their efforts to plunge Iraq into chaos.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So we reviewed our strategy and changed course.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We launched a surge of American forces into Iraq.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We gave our troops a new mission: Work with the Iraqi forces to protect the Iraqi people, pursue the enemy in its strongholds, and deny the terrorists sanctuary anywhere in the country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The Iraqi people quickly realized that something dramatic had happened.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Those who had worried that America was preparing to abandon them instead saw tens of thousands of American forces flowing into their country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They saw our forces moving into neighborhoods, clearing out the terrorists, and staying behind to ensure the enemy did not return.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And they saw our troops, along with Provincial Reconstruction Teams that include Foreign Service officers and other skilled public servants, coming in to ensure that improved security was followed by improvements in daily life.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our military and civilians in Iraq are performing with courage and distinction, and they have the gratitude of our whole nation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The Iraqis launched a surge of their own.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: nan

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Over the past year, similar movements have spread across the country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And today, the grassroots surge includes more than 80,000 Iraqi citizens who are fighting the terrorists.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The government in Baghdad has stepped forward, as well -- adding more than 100,000 new Iraqi soldiers and police during the past year.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: While the enemy is still dangerous and more work remains, the American and Iraqi surges have achieved results few of us could have imagined just one year ago.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When we met last year, many said that containing the violence was impossible.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A year later, high profile terrorist attacks are down, civilian deaths are down, sectarian killings are down.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When we met last year, militia extremists -- some armed and trained by Iran -- were wreaking havoc in large areas of Iraq.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A year later, coalition and Iraqi forces have killed or captured hundreds of militia fighters.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And Iraqis of all backgrounds increasingly realize that defeating these militia fighters is critical to the future of their country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When we met last year, al Qaeda had sanctuaries in many areas of Iraq, and their leaders had just offered American forces safe passage out of the country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Today, it is al Qaeda that is searching for safe passage.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They have been driven from many of the strongholds they once held, and over the past year, we've captured or killed thousands of extremists in Iraq, including hundreds of key al Qaeda leaders and operatives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last month, Osama bin Laden released a tape in which he railed against Iraqi tribal leaders who have turned on al Qaeda and admitted that coalition forces are growing stronger in Iraq.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Ladies and gentlemen, some may deny the surge is working, but among the terrorists there is no doubt.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Al Qaeda is on the run in Iraq, and this enemy will be defeated.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: When we met last year, our troop levels in Iraq were on the rise.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: and the surge forces we sent to Iraq are beginning to come home.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This progress is a credit to the valor of our troops and the brilliance of their commanders.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This evening, I want to speak directly to our men and women on the front lines.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Soldiers and sailors, airmen, Marines, and Coast Guardsmen: In the past year, you have done everything we've asked of you, and more.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our nation is grateful for your courage.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are proud of your accomplishments.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tonight in this hallowed chamber, with the American people as our witness, we make you a solemn pledge: In the fight ahead, you will have all you need to protect our nation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I ask Congress to meet its responsibilities to these brave men and women by fully funding our troops.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our enemies in Iraq have been hit hard.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They are not yet defeated, and we can still expect tough fighting ahead.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our objective in the coming year is to sustain and build on the gains we made in 2007, while transitioning to the next phase of our strategy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: American troops are shifting from leading operations, to partnering with Iraqi forces, and, eventually, to a protective overwatch mission.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: As part of this transition, one Army brigade combat team and one Marine Expeditionary Unit have already come home and will not be replaced.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the coming months, four additional brigades and two Marine battalions will follow suit.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Taken together, this means more than 20,000 of our troops are coming home.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Any further drawdown of U.S. troops will be based on conditions in Iraq and the recommendations of our commanders.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Members of Congress: Having come so far and achieved so much, we must not allow this to happen.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the coming year, we will work with Iraqi leaders as they build on the progress they're making toward political reconciliation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: At the local level, Sunnis, Shia, and Kurds are beginning to come together to reclaim their communities and rebuild their lives.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Progress in the provinces must be matched by progress in Baghdad.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're seeing some encouraging signs.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The national government is sharing oil revenues with the provinces.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The parliament recently passed both a pension law and de-Baathification reform.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They're now debating a provincial powers law.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The Iraqis still have a distance to travel.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But after decades of dictatorship and the pain of sectarian violence, reconciliation is taking place -- and the Iraqi people are taking control of their future.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The mission in Iraq has been difficult and trying for our nation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But it is in the vital interest of the United States that we succeed.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A free Iraq will deny al Qaeda a safe haven.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A free Iraq will show millions across the Middle East that a future of liberty is possible.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: A free Iraq will be a friend of America, a partner in fighting terror, and a source of stability in a dangerous part of the world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By contrast, a failed Iraq would embolden the extremists, strengthen Iran, and give terrorists a base from which to launch new attacks on our friends, our allies, and our homeland.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The enemy has made its intentions clear.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: At a time when the momentum seemed to favor them, al Qaida's top commander in Iraq declared that they will not rest until they have attacked us here in Washington.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: My fellow Americans: We will not rest either.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will not rest until this enemy has been defeated.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must do the difficult work today, so that years from now people will look back and say that this generation rose to the moment, prevailed in a tough fight, and left behind a more hopeful region and a safer America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're also standing against the forces of extremism in the Holy Land, where we have new cause for hope.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Palestinians have elected a president who recognizes that confronting terror is essential to achieving a state where his people can live in dignity and at peace with Israel.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Israelis have leaders who recognize that a peaceful, democratic Palestinian state will be a source of lasting security.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This month in Ramallah and Jerusalem, I assured leaders from both sides that America will do, and I will do, everything we can to help them achieve a peace agreement that defines a Palestinian state by the end of this year.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The time has come for a Holy Land where a democratic Israel and a democratic Palestine live side-by-side in peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We're also standing against the forces of extremism embodied by the regime in Tehran.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iran's rulers oppress a good and talented people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And wherever freedom advances in the Middle East, it seems the Iranian regime is there to oppose it.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Iran is funding and training militia groups in Iraq, supporting Hezbollah terrorists in Lebanon, and backing Hamas' efforts to undermine peace in the Holy Land.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Tehran is also developing ballistic missiles of increasing range, and continues to develop its capability to enrich uranium, which could be used to create a nuclear weapon.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our message to the people of Iran is clear: We have no quarrel with you.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We respect your traditions and your history.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We look forward to the day when you have your freedom.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our message to the leaders of Iran is also clear: Verifiably suspend your nuclear enrichment, so negotiations can begin.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And to rejoin the community of nations, come clean about your nuclear intentions and past actions, stop your oppression at home, cease your support for terror abroad.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: But above all, know this: America will confront those who threaten our troops.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We will stand by our allies, and we will defend our vital interests in the Persian Gulf.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: On the home front, we will continue to take every lawful and effective measure to protect our country.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This is our most solemn duty.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We are grateful that there has not been another attack on our soil since 9/11.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This is not for the lack of desire or effort on the part of the enemy.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: In the past six years, we've stopped numerous attacks, including a plot to fly a plane into the tallest building in Los Angeles and another to blow up passenger jets bound for America over the Atlantic.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Dedicated men and women in our government toil day and night to stop the terrorists from carrying out their plans.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: These good citizens are saving American lives, and everyone in this chamber owes them our thanks.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And we owe them something more: We owe them the tools they need to keep our people safe.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And one of the most important tools we can give them is the ability to monitor terrorist communications.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: To protect America, we need to know who the terrorists are talking to, what they are saying, and what they're planning.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Last year, Congress passed legislation to help us do that.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Unfortunately, Congress set the legislation to expire on February the 1st.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: That means if you don't act by Friday, our ability to track terrorist threats would be weakened and our citizens will be in greater danger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Congress must ensure the flow of vital intelligence is not disrupted.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Congress must pass liability protection for companies believed to have assisted in the efforts to defend America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've had ample time for debate.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The time to act is now.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Protecting our nation from the dangers of a new century requires more than good intelligence and a strong military.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: It also requires changing the conditions that breed resentment and allow extremists to prey on despair.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So America is using its influence to build a freer, more hopeful, and more compassionate world.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This is a reflection of our national interest;

speaker: George W. Bush
text: it is the calling of our conscience.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America opposes genocide in Sudan.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We support freedom in countries from Cuba and Zimbabwe to Belarus and Burma.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is leading the fight against global poverty, with strong education initiatives and humanitarian assistance.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We've also changed the way we deliver aid by launching the Millennium Challenge Account.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: This program strengthens democracy, transparency, and the rule of law in developing nations, and I ask you to fully fund this important initiative.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is leading the fight against global hunger.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Today, more than half the world's food aid comes from the United States.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And tonight, I ask Congress to support an innovative proposal to provide food assistance by purchasing crops directly from farmers in the developing world, so we can build up local agriculture and help break the cycle of famine.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is leading the fight against disease.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: With your help, we're working to cut by half the number of malaria-related deaths in 15 African nations.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And our Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief is treating 1.4 million people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We can bring healing and hope to many more.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So I ask you to maintain the principles that have changed behavior and made this program a success.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And I call on you to double our initial commitment to fighting HIV/AIDS by approving an additional $30 billion over the next five years.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: America is a force for hope in the world because we are a compassionate people, and some of the most compassionate Americans are those who have stepped forward to protect us.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We must keep faith with all who have risked life and limb so that we might live in freedom and peace.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Over the past seven years, we've increased funding for veterans by more than 95 percent.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And as increase funding we must also reform our veterans system to meet the needs of a new war and a new generation.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: I call on the Congress to enact the reforms recommended by Senator Bob Dole and Secretary Donna Shalala, so we can improve the system of care for our wounded warriors and help them build lives of hope and promise and dignity.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our military families also sacrifice for America.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: They endure sleepless nights and the daily struggle of providing for children while a loved one is serving far from home.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: We have a responsibility to provide for them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So I ask you to join me in expanding their access to child care, creating new hiring preferences for military spouses across the federal government, and allowing our troops to transfer their unused education benefits to their spouses or children.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: Our military families serve our nation, they inspire our nation, and tonight our nation honors them.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: The strength -- the secret of our strength, the miracle of America, is that our greatness lies not in our government, but in the spirit and determination of our people.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: nan

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By trusting the people, our Founders wagered that a great and noble nation could be built on the liberty that resides in the hearts of all men and women.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: By trusting the people, succeeding generations transformed our fragile young democracy into the most powerful nation on Earth and a beacon of hope for millions.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: And so long as we continue to trust the people, our nation will prosper, our liberty will be secure, and the state of our Union will remain strong.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: So tonight, with confidence in freedom's power, and trust in the people, let us set forth to do their business.

speaker: George W. Bush
text: God bless America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To the Congress of the United States:

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've come here tonight not only to address the distinguished men and women in this great chamber, but to speak frankly and directly to the men and women who sent us here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know that for many Americans watching right now, the state of our economy is a concern that rises above all others.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And rightly so.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If you haven't been personally affected by this recession, you probably know someone who has--a friend;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: a neighbor;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: a member of your family.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You don't need to hear another list of statistics to know that our economy is in crisis, because you live it every day.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the worry you wake up with and the source of sleepless nights.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the job you thought you'd retire from but now have lost;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: the business you built your dreams upon that's now hanging by a thread;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: the college acceptance letter your child had to put back in the envelope.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The impact of this recession is real, and it is everywhere.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But while our economy may be weakened and our confidence shaken;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: though we are living through difficult and uncertain times, tonight I want every American to know this: We will rebuild, we will recover, and the United States of America will emerge stronger than before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The weight of this crisis will not determine the destiny of this Nation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The answers to our problems don't lie beyond our reach.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They exist in our laboratories and universities;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: in our fields and our factories;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: in the imaginations of our entrepreneurs and the pride of the hardest-working people on Earth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Those qualities that have made America the greatest force of progress and prosperity in human history we still possess in ample measure.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What is required now is for this country to pull together, confront boldly the challenges we face, and take responsibility for our future once more.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, if we're honest with ourselves, we'll admit that for too long, we have not always met these responsibilities--as a Government or as a people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I say this not to lay blame or look backwards, but because it is only by understanding how we arrived at this moment that we'll be able to lift ourselves out of this predicament.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The fact is, our economy did not fall into decline overnight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Nor did all of our problems begin when the housing market collapsed or the stock market sank.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have known for decades that our survival depends on finding new sources of energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Yet we import more oil today than ever before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The cost of health care eats up more and more of our savings each year, yet we keep delaying reform.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our children will compete for jobs in a global economy that too many of our schools do not prepare them for.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And though all these challenges went unsolved, we still managed to spend more money and pile up more debt, both as individuals and through our Government, than ever before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In other words, we have lived through an era where too often, short-term gains were prized over long-term prosperity;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: where we failed to look beyond the next payment, the next quarter, or the next election.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A surplus became an excuse to transfer wealth to the wealthy instead of an opportunity to invest in our future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Regulations were gutted for the sake of a quick profit at the expense of a healthy market.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: People bought homes they knew they couldn't afford from banks and lenders who pushed those bad loans anyway.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And all the while, critical debates and difficult decisions were put off for some other time on some other day.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Well that day of reckoning has arrived, and the time to take charge of our future is here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now is the time to act boldly and wisely--to not only revive this economy, but to build a new foundation for lasting prosperity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now is the time to jumpstart job creation, re-start lending, and invest in areas like energy, health care, and education that will grow our economy, even as we make hard choices to bring our deficit down.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is what my economic agenda is designed to do, and that's what I'd like to talk to you about tonight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's an agenda that begins with jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As soon as I took office, I asked this Congress to send me a recovery plan by President's Day that would put people back to work and put money in their pockets.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Not because I believe in bigger Government--I don't.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Not because I'm not mindful of the massive debt we've inherited--I am.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I called for action because the failure to do so would have cost more jobs and caused more hardships.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, a failure to act would have worsened our long-term deficit by assuring weak economic growth for years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why I pushed for quick action.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tonight, I am grateful that this Congress delivered, and pleased to say that the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act is now law.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Over the next 2 years, this plan will save or create 3.5 million jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More than 90 percent of these jobs will be in the private sector--jobs rebuilding our roads and bridges;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: constructing wind turbines and solar panels;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: laying broadband and expanding mass transit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because of this plan, there are teachers who can now keep their jobs and educate our kids.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Health care professionals can continue caring for our sick.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There are 57 police officers who are still on the streets of Minneapolis tonight because this plan prevented the layoffs their department was about to make.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because of this plan, 95 percent of the working households in America will receive a tax cut--a tax cut that you will see in your paychecks beginning on April 1st.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because of this plan, families who are struggling to pay tuition costs will receive a $2,500 tax credit for all four years of college.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And Americans who have lost their jobs in this recession will be able to receive extended unemployment benefits and continued health care coverage to help them weather this storm.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know there are some in this chamber and watching at home who are skeptical of whether this plan will work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I understand that skepticism.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Here in Washington, we've all seen how quickly good intentions can turn into broken promises and wasteful spending.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And with a plan of this scale comes enormous responsibility to get it right.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is why I have asked Vice President Biden to lead a tough, unprecedented oversight effort--because nobody messes with Joe

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I have told each member of my Cabinet as well as mayors and governors across the country that they will be held accountable by me and the American people for every dollar they spend.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I have appointed a proven and aggressive Inspector General to ferret out any and all cases of waste and fraud.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we have created a new website called recovery.gov so that every American can find out how and where their money is being spent.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So the recovery plan we passed is the first step in getting our economy back on track.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But it is just the first step.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because even if we manage this plan flawlessly, there will be no real recovery unless we clean up the credit crisis that has severely weakened our financial system.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want to speak plainly and candidly about this issue tonight, because every American should know that it directly affects you and your family's well-being.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You should also know that the money you've deposited in banks across the country is safe;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: your insurance is secure;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: and you can rely on the continued operation of our financial system.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is not the source of concern.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The concern is that if we do not re-start lending in this country, our recovery will be choked off before it even begins.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You see, the flow of credit is the lifeblood of our economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The ability to get a loan is how you finance the purchase of everything from a home to a car to a college education;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: how stores stock their shelves, farms buy equipment, and businesses make payroll.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But credit has stopped flowing the way it should.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Too many bad loans from the housing crisis have made their way onto the books of too many banks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With so much debt and so little confidence, these banks are now fearful of lending out any more money to households, to businesses, or to each other.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When there is no lending, families can't afford to buy homes or cars.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So businesses are forced to make layoffs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our economy suffers even more, and credit dries up even further.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is why this Administration is moving swiftly and aggressively to break this destructive cycle, restore confidence, and re-start lending.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will do so in several ways.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: First, we are creating a new lending fund that represents the largest effort ever to help provide auto loans, college loans, and small business loans to the consumers and entrepreneurs who keep this economy running.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Second, we have launched a housing plan that will help responsible families facing the threat of foreclosure lower their monthly payments and refinance their mortgages.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's a plan that won't help speculators or that neighbor down the street who bought a house he could never hope to afford, but it will help millions of Americans who are struggling with declining home values--Americans who will now be able to take advantage of the lower interest rates that this plan has already helped bring about.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, the average family who refinances today can save nearly $2,000 per year on their mortgage.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Third, we will act with the full force of the Federal Government to ensure that the major banks that Americans depend on have enough confidence and enough money to lend even in more difficult times.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And when we learn that a major bank has serious problems, we will hold accountable those responsible, force the necessary adjustments, provide the support to clean up their balance sheets, and assure the continuity of a strong, viable institution that can serve our people and our economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I understand that on any given day, Wall Street may be more comforted by an approach that gives banks bailouts with no strings attached, and that holds nobody accountable for their reckless decisions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But such an approach won't solve the problem.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And our goal is to quicken the day when we re-start lending to the American people and American business and end this crisis once and for all.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I intend to hold these banks fully accountable for the assistance they receive, and this time, they will have to clearly demonstrate how taxpayer dollars result in more lending for the American taxpayer.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This time, CEOs won't be able to use taxpayer money to pad their paychecks or buy fancy drapes or disappear on a private jet.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Those days are over.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Still, this plan will require significant resources from the Federal Government--and yes, probably more than we've already set aside.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But while the cost of action will be great, I can assure you that the cost of inaction will be far greater, for it could result in an economy that sputters along for not months or years, but perhaps a decade.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That would be worse for our deficit, worse for business, worse for you, and worse for the next generation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I refuse to let that happen.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I understand that when the last Administration asked this Congress to provide assistance for struggling banks, Democrats and Republicans alike were infuriated by the mismanagement and results that followed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So were the American taxpayers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So was I.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So I know how unpopular it is to be seen as helping banks right now, especially when everyone is suffering in part from their bad decisions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I promise you--I get it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I also know that in a time of crisis, we cannot afford to govern out of anger, or yield to the politics of the moment.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My job--our job--is to solve the problem.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our job is to govern with a sense of responsibility.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will not spend a single penny for the purpose of rewarding a single Wall Street executive, but I will do whatever it takes to help the small business that can't pay its workers or the family that has saved and still can't get a mortgage.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what this is about.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's not about helping banks--it's about helping people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because when credit is available again, that young family can finally buy a new home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And then some company will hire workers to build it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And then those workers will have money to spend, and if they can get a loan too, maybe they'll finally buy that car, or open their own business.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Investors will return to the market, and American families will see their retirement secured once more.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Slowly, but surely, confidence will return, and our economy will recover.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So I ask this Congress to join me in doing whatever proves necessary.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because we cannot consign our Nation to an open-ended recession.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And to ensure that a crisis of this magnitude never happens again, I ask the Congress to move quickly on legislation that will finally reform our outdated regulatory system.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is time to put in place tough, new common-sense rules of the road so that our financial market rewards drive and innovation, and punishes short-cuts and abuse.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The recovery plan and the financial stability plan are the immediate steps we're taking to revive our economy in the short-term.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But the only way to fully restore America's economic strength is to make the long-term investments that will lead to new jobs, new industries, and a renewed ability to compete with the rest of the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The only way this century will be another American century is if we confront at last the price of our dependence on oil and the high cost of health care;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: the schools that aren't preparing our children and the mountain of debt they stand to inherit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is our responsibility.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the next few days, I will submit a budget to the Congress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So often, we have come to view these documents as simply numbers on a page or laundry lists of programs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I see this document differently.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I see it as a vision for America--as a blueprint for our future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My budget does not attempt to solve every problem or address every issue.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It reflects the stark reality of what we've inherited--a trillion dollar deficit, a financial crisis, and a costly recession.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Given these realities, everyone in this chamber--Democrats and Republicans--will have to sacrifice some worthy priorities for which there are no dollars.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that includes me.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But that does not mean we can afford to ignore our long-term challenges.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I reject the view that says our problems will simply take care of themselves;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that says Government has no role in laying the foundation for our common prosperity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For history tells a different story.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: History reminds us that at every moment of economic upheaval and transformation, this Nation has responded with bold action and big ideas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the midst of civil war, we laid railroad tracks from one coast to another that spurred commerce and industry.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: From the turmoil of the Industrial Revolution came a system of public high schools that prepared our citizens for a new age.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the wake of war and depression, the GI Bill sent a generation to college and created the largest middle-class in history.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And a twilight struggle for freedom led to a nation of highways, an American on the moon, and an explosion of technology that still shapes our world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In each case, Government didn't supplant private enterprise;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: it catalyzed private enterprise.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It created the conditions for thousands of entrepreneurs and new businesses to adapt and to thrive.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are a Nation that has seen promise amid peril, and claimed opportunity from ordeal.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now we must be that nation again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is why, even as it cuts back on the programs we don't need, the budget I submit will invest in the three areas that are absolutely critical to our economic future: energy, health care, and education.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It begins with energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We know the country that harnesses the power of clean, renewable energy will lead the 21st century.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And yet, it is China that has launched the largest effort in history to make their economy energy efficient.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We invented solar technology, but we've fallen behind countries like Germany and Japan in producing it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: New plug-in hybrids roll off our assembly lines, but they will run on batteries made in Korea.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Well I do not accept a future where the jobs and industries of tomorrow take root beyond our borders--and I know you don't either.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is time for America to lead again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thanks to our recovery plan, we will double this Nation's supply of renewable energy in the next 3 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have also made the largest investment in basic research funding in American history--an investment that will spur not only new discoveries in energy, but breakthroughs in medicine, science, and technology.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will soon lay down thousands of miles of power lines that can carry new energy to cities and towns across this country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we will put Americans to work making our homes and buildings more efficient so that we can save billions of dollars on our energy bills.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But to truly transform our economy, protect our security, and save our planet from the ravages of climate change, we need to ultimately make clean, renewable energy the profitable kind of energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So I ask this Congress to send me legislation that places a market-based cap on carbon pollution and drives the production of more renewable energy in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And to support that innovation, we will invest $15 billion a year to develop technologies like wind power and solar power;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: advanced biofuels, clean coal, and more fuel-efficient cars and trucks built right here in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As for our auto industry, everyone recognizes that years of bad decision- making and a global recession have pushed our automakers to the brink.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should not, and will not, protect them from their own bad practices. But we are committed to the goal of a re-tooled, re-imagined auto industry that can compete and win.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Millions of jobs depend on it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Scores of communities depend on it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I believe the Nation that invented the automobile cannot walk away from it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: None of this will come without cost, nor will it be easy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But this is America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We don't do what's easy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We do what is necessary to move this country forward.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For that same reason, we must also address the crushing cost of health care.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This is a cost that now causes a bankruptcy in America every 30 seconds.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: By the end of the year, it could cause 1.5 million Americans to lose their homes.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the last 8 years, premiums have grown four times faster than wages.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in each of these years, one million more Americans have lost their health insurance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is one of the major reasons why small businesses close their doors and corporations ship jobs overseas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it's one of the largest and fastest-growing parts of our budget.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Given these facts, we can no longer afford to put health care reform on hold.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Already, we have done more to advance the cause of health care reform in the last thirty days than we have in the last decade.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When it was days old, this Congress passed a law to provide and protect health insurance for 11 million American children whose parents work full-time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our recovery plan will invest in electronic health records and new technology that will reduce errors, bring down costs, ensure privacy, and save

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It will launch a new effort to conquer a disease that has touched the life of nearly every American by seeking a cure for cancer in our time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it makes the largest investment ever in preventive care, because that is one of the best ways to keep our people healthy and our costs under control.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This budget builds on these reforms.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It includes an historic commitment to comprehensive health care reform

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's a commitment that's paid for in part by efficiencies in our system that are long overdue.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it's a step we must take if we hope to bring down our deficit in the years to come.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, there will be many different opinions and ideas about how to achieve reform, and that is why I'm bringing together businesses and workers, doctors and health care providers, Democrats and Republicans to begin work on this issue next week.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I suffer no illusions that this will be an easy process.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It will be hard.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I also know that nearly a century after Teddy Roosevelt first called for reform, the cost of our health care has weighed down our economy and the conscience of our Nation long enough.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let there be no doubt: health care reform cannot wait, it must not wait, and it will not wait another year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The third challenge we must address is the urgent need to expand the promise of education in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In a global economy where the most valuable skill you can sell is your knowledge, a good education is no longer just a pathway to opportunity--it is a prerequisite.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Right now, three-quarters of the fastest-growing occupations require more than a high school diploma.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And yet, just over half of our citizens have that level of education.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have one of the highest high school dropout rates of any industrialized nation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And half of the students who begin college never finish.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This is a prescription for economic decline, because we know the countries that out-teach us today will out-compete us tomorrow.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is why it will be the goal of this Administration to ensure that every child has access to a complete and competitive education--from the day they are born to the day they begin a career.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Already, we have made an historic investment in education through the economic recovery plan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have dramatically expanded early childhood education and will continue to improve its quality, because we know that the most formative learning comes in those first years of life.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have made college affordable for nearly seven million more students. And we have provided the resources necessary to prevent painful cuts and teacher layoffs that would set back our children's progress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we know that our schools don't just need more resources.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They need more reform.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is why this budget creates new incentives for teacher performance;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: pathways for advancement, and rewards for success.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll invest in innovative programs that are already helping schools meet high standards and close achievement gaps.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we will expand our commitment to charter schools.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is our responsibility as lawmakers and educators to make this system work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But it is the responsibility of every citizen to participate in it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And so tonight, I ask every American to commit to at least 1 year or more of higher education or career training.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This can be community college or a four-year school;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: vocational training or an apprenticeship.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But whatever the training may be, every American will need to get more than a high school diploma.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And dropping out of high school is no longer an option.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's not just quitting on yourself, it's quitting on your country--and this country needs and values the talents of every American.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is why we will provide the support necessary for you to complete college and meet a new goal: by 2020, America will once again have the highest proportion of college graduates in the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know that the price of tuition is higher than ever, which is why if you are willing to volunteer in your neighborhood or give back to your community or serve your country, we will make sure that you can afford a higher education.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And to encourage a renewed spirit of national service for this and future generations, I ask this Congress to send me the bipartisan legislation that bears the name of Senator Orrin Hatch as well as an American who has never stopped asking what he can do for his country--Senator Edward Kennedy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These education policies will open the doors of opportunity for our children.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But it is up to us to ensure they, walk through them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the end, there is no program or policy that can substitute for a mother or father who will attend those parent/teacher conferences, or help with homework after dinner, or turn off the TV, put away the video games, and read to their child.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I speak to you not just as a President, but as a father when I say that responsibility for our children's education must begin at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There is, of course, another responsibility we have to our children.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that is the responsibility to ensure that we do not pass on to them a debt they cannot pay.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With the deficit we inherited, the cost of the crisis we face, and the long-term challenges we must meet, it has never been more important to ensure that as our economy recovers, we do what it takes to bring this deficit down.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm proud that we passed the recovery plan free of earmarks, and I want to pass a budget next year that ensures that each dollar we spend reflects only our most important national priorities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Yesterday, I held a fiscal summit where I pledged to cut the deficit in half by the end of my first term in office.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My Administration has also begun to go line by line through the Federal budget in order to eliminate wasteful and ineffective programs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As you can imagine, this is a process that will take some time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we're starting with the biggest lines.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have already identified two trillion dollars in savings over the next decade.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In this budget, we will end education programs that don't work and end direct payments to large agribusinesses that don't need them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll eliminate the no-bid contracts that have wasted billions in Iraq, and reform our defense budget so that we're not paying for Cold War-era weapons systems we don't use.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will root out the waste, fraud, and abuse in our Medicare program that doesn't make our seniors any healthier, and we will restore a sense of fairness and balance to our tax code by finally ending the tax breaks for corporations that ship our jobs overseas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In order to save our children from a future of debt, we will also end the tax breaks for the wealthiest 2 percent of Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But let me be perfectly clear, because I know you'll hear the same old claims that rolling back these tax breaks means a massive tax increase on the American people: if your family earns less than $250,000 a year, you will not see your taxes increased a single dime.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I repeat: not one single dime.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, the recovery plan provides a tax cut--that's right, a tax cut--for 95 percent of working families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And these checks are on the way.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To preserve our long-term fiscal health, we must also address the growing costs in Medicare and Social Security.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Comprehensive health care reform is the best way to strengthen Medicare for years to come.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we must also begin a conversation on how to do the same for Social Security, while creating tax-free universal savings accounts for all Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Finally, because we're also suffering from a deficit of trust, I am committed to restoring a sense of honesty and accountability to our budget.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is why this budget looks ahead 10 years and accounts for spending that was left out under the old rules--and for the first time, that includes the full cost of fighting in Iraq and Afghanistan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For 7 years, we have been a nation at war.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No longer will we hide its price.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are now carefully reviewing our policies in both wars, and I will soon announce a way forward in Iraq that leaves Iraq to its people and responsibility ends this war.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And with our friends and allies, we will forge a new and comprehensive strategy for Afghanistan and Pakistan to defeat al Qaeda and combat extremism.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because I will not allow terrorists to plot against the American people from safe havens half a world away.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As we meet here tonight, our men and women in uniform stand watch abroad and more are readying to deploy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To each and every one of them, and to the families who bear the quiet burden of their absence, Americans are united in sending one message: we honor your service, we are inspired by your sacrifice, and you have our unyielding support.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To relieve the strain on our forces, my budget increases the number of our soldiers and Marines.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And to keep our sacred trust with those who serve, we will raise their pay, and give our veterans the expanded health care and benefits that they have earned.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To overcome extremism, we must also be vigilant in upholding the values our troops defend--because there is no force in the world more powerful than the example of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is why I have ordered the closing of the detention center at Guantanamo Bay, and will seek swift and certain justice for captured terrorists--because living our values doesn't make us weaker, it makes us safer and it makes us stronger.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that is why I can stand here tonight and say without exception or equivocation that the United States of America does not torture.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In words and deeds, we are showing the world that a new era of engagement has begun.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For we know that America cannot meet the threats of this century alone, but the world cannot meet them without America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We cannot shun the negotiating table, nor ignore the foes or forces that could do us harm.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are instead called to move forward with the sense of confidence and candor that serious times demand.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To seek progress toward a secure and lasting peace between Israel and her neighbors, we have appointed an envoy to sustain our effort.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To meet the challenges of the 21st century--from terrorism to nuclear proliferation;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: from pandemic disease to cyber threats to crushing poverty--we will strengthen old alliances, forge new ones, and use all elements of our national power.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And to respond to an economic crisis that is global in scope, we are working with the nations of the G-20 to restore confidence in our financial system, avoid the possibility of escalating protectionism, and spur demand for American goods in markets across the globe.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For the world depends on us to have a strong economy, just as our economy depends on the strength of the world's.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As we stand at this crossroads of history, the eyes of all people in all nations are once again upon us--watching to see what we do, with this moment; waiting for us to lead.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Those of us gathered here tonight have been called to govern in extraordinary times.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For in our hands lies the ability to shape our world for good or for ill.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know that it is easy to lose sight of this truth--to become cynical and doubtful;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: consumed with the petty and the trivial.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But in my life, I have also learned that hope is found in unlikely places;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that inspiration often comes not from those with the most power or celebrity, but from the dreams and aspirations of Americans who are anything but ordinary.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I think about Leonard Abess, the bank president from Miami who reportedly cashed out of his company, took a $60 million bonus, and gave it out to all 399 people who worked for him, plus another 72 who used to work for him.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: He didn't tell anyone, but when the local newspaper found out, he simply said, ``I knew some of these people since I was 7 years old.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I didn't feel right getting the money myself.''

speaker: Barack Obama
