text: I think about Greensburg, Kansas, a town that was completely destroyed by a tornado, but is being rebuilt by its residents as a global example of how clean energy can power an entire community--how it can bring jobs and businesses to a place where piles of bricks and rubble once lay.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: ``The tragedy was terrible,'' said one of the men who helped them rebuild.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: ``But the folks here know that it also provided an incredible opportunity.''

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I think about Ty'Sheoma Bethea, the young girl from that school I visited in Dillon, South Carolina--a place where the ceilings leak, the paint peels off the walls, and they have to stop teaching six times a day because the train barrels by their classroom.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She has been told that her school is hopeless, but the other day after class she went to the public library and typed up a letter to the people sitting in this room.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She even asked her principal for the money to buy a stamp.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The letter asks us for help, and says, ``We are just students trying to become lawyers, doctors, congressmen like yourself and one day president, so we can make a change to not just the state of South Carolina but also the world. We are not quitters.''

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are not quitters.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These words and these stories tell us something about the spirit of the people who sent us here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They tell us that even in the most trying times, amid the most difficult circumstances, there is a generosity, a resilience, a decency, and a determination that perseveres;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: a willingness to take responsibility for our future and for posterity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Their resolve must be our inspiration.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Their concerns must be our cause.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we must show them and all our people that we are equal to the task before us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know that we haven't agreed on every issue thus far, and there are surely times in the future when we will part ways.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But,I also know that every American who is sitting here tonight loves this country and wants it to succeed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That must be the starting point for every debate we have in the coming months, and where we return after those debates are done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is the foundation on which the American people expect us to build common ground.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if we do--if we come together and lift this Nation from the depths of this crisis;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: if we put our people back to work and restart the engine of our prosperity;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: if we confront without fear the challenges of our time and summon that enduring spirit of an America that does not quit, then someday years from now our children can tell their children that this was the time when we performed, in the words that are carved into this very chamber, ``something worthy to be remembered.''

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thank you, God Bless you, and may God Bless the United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Madam Speaker, Vice President Biden, Members of Congress, distinguished guests, and fellow Americans: Our Constitution declares that from time to time, the President shall give to Congress information about the state of our Union. For 220 years, our leaders have fulfilled this duty.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They've done so during periods of prosperity and tranquility, and they've done so in the midst of war and depression, at moments of great strife and great struggle.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's tempting to look back on these moments and assume that our progress was inevitable, that America was always destined to succeed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But when the Union was turned back at Bull Run and the Allies first landed at Omaha Beach, victory was very much in doubt.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When the market crashed on Black Tuesday and civil rights marchers were beaten on Bloody Sunday, the future was anything but certain.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These were the times that tested the courage of our convictions and the strength of our Union.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And despite all our divisions and disagreements, our hesitations and our fears, America prevailed because we chose to move forward as one Nation, as one people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Again, we are tested.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And again, we must answer history's call.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: One year ago, I took office amid two wars, an economy rocked by a severe recession, a financial system on the verge of collapse, and a Government deeply in debt.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Experts from across the political spectrum warned that if we did not act, we might face a second depression.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So we acted, immediately and aggressively.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And 1 year later, the worst of the storm has passed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But the devastation remains.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: One in 10 Americans still cannot find work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Many businesses have shuttered.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Home values have declined.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Small towns and rural communities have been hit especially hard.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And for those who'd already known poverty, life's become that much harder.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This recession has also compounded the burdens that America's families have been dealing with for decades: the burden of working harder and longer for less, of being unable to save enough to retire or help kids with college.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So I know the anxieties that are out there right now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're not new.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These struggles are the reason I ran for President.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These struggles are what I've witnessed for years, in places like Elkhart, Indiana;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Galesburg, Illinois.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I hear about them in the letters that I read each night.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The toughest to read are those written by children asking why they have to move from their home, asking when their mom or dad will be able to go back to work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For these Americans and so many others, change has not come fast enough.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some are frustrated, some are angry.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They don't understand why it seems like bad behavior on Wall Street is rewarded, but hard work on Main Street isn't, or why Washington has been unable or unwilling to solve any of our problems.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're tired of the partisanship and the shouting and the pettiness.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They know we can't afford it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Not now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So we face big and difficult challenges.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And what the American people hope, what they deserve, is for all of us, Democrats and Republicans, to work through our differences, to overcome the numbing weight of our politics.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For while the people who sent us here have different backgrounds, different stories, different beliefs, the anxieties they face are the same.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The aspirations they hold are shared: a job that pays the bills;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: a chance to get ahead;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: most of all, the ability to give their children a better life.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And you know what else they share? They share a stubborn resilience in the face of adversity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After one of the most difficult years in our history, they remain busy building cars and teaching kids, starting businesses and going back to school.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're coaching Little League and helping their neighbors.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: One woman wrote to me and said, We are strained but hopeful, struggling but encouraged.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's because of this spirit, this great decency and great strength, that I have never been more hopeful about America's future than I am tonight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Despite our hardships, our Union is strong.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We do not give up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We do not quit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We do not allow fear or division to break our spirit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In this new decade, it's time the American people get a Government that matches their decency, that embodies their strength.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tonight I'd like to talk about how together we can deliver on that promise.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It begins with our economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our most urgent task upon taking office was to shore up the same banks that helped cause this crisis.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It was not easy to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if there's one thing that has unified Democrats and Republicans and everybody in between, it's that we all hated the bank bailout.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I hated it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I hated it;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: you hated it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It was about as popular as a root canal.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] But when I ran for President, I promised I wouldn't just do what was popular;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I would do what was necessary.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if we had allowed the meltdown of the financial system, unemployment might be double what it is today.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More businesses would certainly have closed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More homes would have surely been lost.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So I supported the last administration's efforts to create the financial rescue program.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And when we took that program over, we made it more transparent and more accountable.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as a result, the markets are now stabilized, and we've recovered most of the money we spent on the banks-most but not all.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To recover the rest, I've proposed a fee on the biggest banks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, I know Wall Street isn't keen on this idea.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But if these firms can afford to hand out big bonuses again, they can afford a modest fee to pay back the taxpayers who rescued them in their time of need.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, as we stabilized the financial system, we also took steps to get our economy growing again, save as many jobs as possible, and help Americans who had become unemployed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we extended or increased unemployment benefits for more than 18 million Americans, made health insurance 65 percent cheaper for families who get their coverage through COBRA, and passed 25 different tax cuts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, let me repeat: We cut taxes.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We cut taxes for 95 percent of working families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We cut taxes for small businesses.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We cut taxes for first-time home buyers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We cut taxes for parents trying to care for their children.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We cut taxes for 8 million Americans paying for college.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Applause] I thought I'd get some applause on that one.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] As a result, millions of Americans had more to spend on gas and food and other necessities, all of which helped businesses keep more workers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we haven't raised income taxes by a single dime on a single person-not a single dime.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, because of the steps we took, there are about 2 million Americans working right now who would otherwise be unemployed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Two hundred thousand work in construction and clean energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Three hundred thousand are teachers and other education workers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tens of thousands are cops, firefighters, correctional officers, first-responders.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we're on track to add another 1

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The plan that has made all of this possible, from the tax cuts to the jobs, is the Recovery Act.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's right, the Recovery Act, also known as the stimulus bill.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Economists on the left and the right say this bill has helped save jobs and avert disaster.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But you don't have to take their word for it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Talk to the small business in Phoenix that will triple its workforce because of the Recovery Act.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Talk to the window manufacturer in Philadelphia who said he used to be skeptical about the Recovery Act, until he had to add two more work shifts just because of the business it created.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Talk to the single teacher raising two kids who was told by her principal in the last week of school that because of the Recovery Act, she wouldn't be laid off after all.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There are stories like this all across America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And after 2 years of recession, the economy is growing again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Retirement funds have started to gain back some of their value.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Businesses are beginning to invest again, and slowly some are starting to hire again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I realize that for every success story, there are other stories, of men and women who wake up with the anguish of not knowing where their next paycheck will come from, who send out resumes week after week and hear nothing in response.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is why jobs must be our number-one focus in 2010, and that's why I'm calling for a new jobs bill tonight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, the true engine of job creation in this country will always be America's businesses.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Applause] I agree, absolutely.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But Government can create the conditions necessary for businesses to expand and hire more workers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should start where most new jobs do, in small businesses, companies that begin when an entrepreneur takes a chance on a dream or a worker decides it's time she became her own boss.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Through sheer grit and determination, these companies have weathered the recession, and they're ready to grow.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But when you talk to small-business owners in places like Allentown, Pennsylvania, or Elyria, Ohio, you find out that even though banks on Wall Street are lending again, they're mostly lending to bigger companies.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Financing remains difficult for small-business owners across the country, even those that are making a profit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight I'm proposing that we take $30 billion of the money Wall Street banks have repaid and use it to help community banks give small businesses the credit they need to stay afloat.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm also proposing a new small business tax credit, one that will go to over 1 million small businesses who hire new workers or raise wages.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: While we're at it, let's also eliminate all capital gains taxes on small-business investment and provide a tax incentive for all large businesses and all small businesses to invest in new plants and equipment.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Next, we can put Americans to work today building the infrastructure of tomorrow.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: From the first railroads to the Interstate Highway System, our Nation has always been built to compete.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There's no reason Europe or China should have the fastest trains or the new factories that manufacture clean energy products.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tomorrow I'll visit Tampa, Florida, where workers will soon break ground on a new high-speed railroad funded by the Recovery Act.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There are projects like that all across this country that will create jobs and help move our Nation's goods, services, and information.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should put more Americans to work building clean energy facilities and give rebates to Americans who make their homes more energy efficient, which supports clean energy jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And to encourage these and other businesses to stay within our borders, it is time to finally slash the tax breaks for companies that ship our jobs overseas and give those tax breaks to companies that create jobs right here in the United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, the House has passed a jobs bill that includes some of these steps.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As the first order of business this year, I urge the Senate to do the same, and I know they will.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They will.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: People are out of work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're hurting.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They need our help.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I want a jobs bill on my desk without delay.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But the truth is, these steps won't make up for the 7 million jobs that we've lost over the last 2 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The only way to move to full employment is to lay a new foundation for long-term economic growth and finally address the problems that America's families have confronted for years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can't afford another so-called economic expansion like the one from the last decade, what some call the lost decade, where jobs grew more slowly than during any prior expansion, where the income of the average American household declined while the cost of health care and tuition reached record highs, where prosperity was built on a housing bubble and financial speculation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: From the day I took office, I've been told that addressing our larger challenges is too ambitious;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: such an effort would be too contentious.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've been told that our political system is too gridlocked and that we should just put things on hold for a while.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For those who make these claims, I have one simple question: How long should we wait? How long should America put its future on hold? You see, Washington has been telling us to wait for decades, even as the problems have grown worse.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Meanwhile, China's not waiting to revamp its economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Germany's not waiting.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: India's not waiting.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These nations are-they're not standing still.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These nations aren't playing for second place.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're putting more emphasis on math and science.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're rebuilding their infrastructure.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're making serious investments in clean energy because they want those jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Well, I do not accept second place for the United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As hard as it may be, as uncomfortable and contentious as the debates may become, it's time to get serious about fixing the problems that are hampering our growth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, one place to start is serious financial reform.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Look, I am not interested in punishing banks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm interested in protecting our economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A strong, healthy financial market makes it possible for businesses to access credit and create new jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It channels the savings of families into investments that raise incomes.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But that can only happen if we guard against the same recklessness that nearly brought down our entire economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to make sure consumers and middle class families have the information they need to make financial decisions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can't allow financial institutions, including those that take your deposits, to take risks that threaten the whole economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, the House has already passed financial reform with many of these changes, and the lobbyists are trying to kill it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we cannot let them win this fight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if the bill that ends up on my desk does not meet the test of real reform, I will send it back until we get it right.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've got to get it right.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Next, we need to encourage American innovation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last year, we made the largest investment in basic research funding in history, an investment that could lead to the world's cheapest solar cells or treatment that kills cancer cells but leaves healthy ones untouched.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And no area is more ripe for such innovation than energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You can see the results of last year's investments in clean energy in the North Carolina company that will create 1,200 jobs nationwide helping to make advanced batteries or in the California business that will put a thousand people to work making solar panels.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But to create more of these clean energy jobs, we need more production, more efficiency, more incentives.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that means building a new generation of safe, clean nuclear powerplants in this country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It means making tough decisions about opening new offshore areas for oil and gas development.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It means continued investment in advanced biofuels and clean coal technologies.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And, yes, it means passing a comprehensive energy and climate bill with incentives that will finally make clean energy the profitable kind of energy in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, I am grateful to the House for passing such a bill last year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And this year, I'm eager to help advance the bipartisan effort in the Senate.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know there have been questions about whether we can afford such changes in a tough economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know that there are those who disagree with the overwhelming scientific evidence on climate change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But here's the thing: Even if you doubt the evidence, providing incentives for energy efficiency and clean energy are the right thing to do for our future, because the nation that leads the clean energy economy will be the nation that leads the global economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And America must be that nation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Third, we need to export more of our goods, because the more products we make and sell to other countries, the more jobs we support right here in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight we set a new goal: We will double our exports over the next 5 years, an increase that will support 2 million jobs in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To help meet this goal, we're launching a National Export Initiative that will help farmers and small businesses increase their exports and reform export controls consistent with national security.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have to seek new markets aggressively, just as our competitors are.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If America sits on the sidelines while other nations sign trade deals, we will lose the chance to create jobs on our shores.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But realizing those benefits also means enforcing those agreements so our trading partners play by the rules.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why we'll continue to shape a Doha trade agreement that opens global markets and why we will strengthen our trade relations in Asia and with key partners like South Korea and Panama and Colombia.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Fourth, we need to invest in the skills and education of our people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, this year, we've broken through the stalemate between left and right by launching a national competition to improve our schools.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And the idea here is simple: Instead of rewarding failure, we only reward success.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Instead of funding the status quo, we only invest in reform, reform that raises student achievement, inspires students to excel in math and science, and turns around failing schools that steal the future of too many young Americans, from rural communities to the inner city.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the 21st century, the best antipoverty program around is a world-class education.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in this country, the success of our children cannot depend more on where they live than on their potential.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When we renew the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, we will work with Congress to expand these reforms to all 50 States.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Still, in this economy, a high school diploma no longer guarantees a good job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why I urge the Senate to follow the House and pass a bill that will revitalize our community colleges, which are a career pathway to the children of so many working families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To make college more affordable, this bill will finally end the unwarranted taxpayer subsidies that go to banks for student loans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Instead, let's take that money and give families a $10,000 tax credit for 4 years of college and increase Pell grants.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And let's tell another 1 million students that when they graduate, they will be required to pay only 10 percent of their income on student loans and all of their debt will be forgiven after 20 years

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And by the way, it's time for colleges and universities to get serious about cutting their own costs, because they too have a responsibility to help solve this problem.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, the price of college tuition is just one of the burdens facing the middle class.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why last year, I asked Vice President Biden to chair a task force on middle class families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we're nearly doubling the child care tax credit and making it easier to save for retirement by giving access to every worker a retirement account and expanding the tax credit for those who start a nest egg.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we're working to lift the value of a family's single largest investment, their home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The steps we took last year to shore up the housing market have allowed millions of Americans to take out new loans and save an average of $1,500 on mortgage payments.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This year, we will step up refinancing so that homeowners can move into more affordable mortgages.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it is precisely to relieve the burden on middle class families that we still need health insurance reform.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Yes, we do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, let's clear a few things up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I didn't choose to tackle this issue to get some legislative victory under my belt.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And by now it should be fairly obvious that I didn't take on health care because it was good politics.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] I took on health care because of the stories I've heard from Americans with preexisting conditions whose lives depend on getting coverage, patients who've been denied coverage, families, even those with insurance, who are just one illness away from financial ruin.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After nearly a century of trying-Democratic administration's, Republican administrations-we are closer than ever to bringing more security to the lives of so many Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The approach we've taken would protect every American from the worst practices of the insurance industry.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It would give small businesses and uninsured Americans a chance to choose an affordable health care plan in a competitive market.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It would require every insurance plan to cover preventive care.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And by the way, I want to acknowledge our First Lady, Michelle Obama, who this year is creating a national movement to tackle the epidemic of childhood obesity and make kids healthier.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Applause] Thank you, honey.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She gets embarrassed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] Our approach would preserve the right of Americans who have insurance to keep their doctor and their plan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It would reduce costs and premiums for millions of families and businesses.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And according to the Congressional Budget Office, the independent organization that both parties have cited as the official scorekeeper for Congress, our approach would bring down the deficit by as much as $1 trillion over the next two decades.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Still, this is a complex issue, and the longer it was debated, the more skeptical people became.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I take my share of the blame for not explaining it more clearly to the American people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I know that with all the lobbying and horse-trading, the process left most Americans wondering, What's in it for me? But I also know this problem is not going away.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: By the time I'm finished speaking tonight, more Americans will have lost their health insurance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Millions will lose it this year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our deficit will grow.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Premiums will go up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Patients will be denied the care they need.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Small-business owners will continue to drop coverage altogether.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will not walk away from these Americans, and neither should the people in this Chamber.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So, as temperatures cool, I want everyone to take another look at the plan we've proposed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There's a reason why many doctors, nurses, and health care experts who know our system best consider this approach a vast improvement over the status quo.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But if anyone from either party has a better approach that will bring down premiums, bring down the deficit, cover the uninsured, strengthen Medicare for seniors, and stop insurance company abuses, let me know.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let me know.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let me know.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm eager to see it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Here's what I ask Congress, though: Don't walk away from reform.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Not now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Not when we are so close.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let us find a way to come together and finish the job for the American people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's get it done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's get it done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, even as health care reform would reduce our deficit, it's not enough to dig us out of a massive fiscal hole in which we find ourselves.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's a challenge that makes all others that much harder to solve and one that's been subject to a lot of political posturing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let me start the discussion of Government spending by setting the record straight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At the beginning of the last decade, the year 2000, America had a budget surplus of over $200 billion.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: By the time I took office, we had a 1-year deficit of over $1 trillion and projected deficits of $8 trillion over the next decade.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Most of this was the result of not paying for two wars, two tax cuts, and an expensive prescription drug program.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: On top of that, the effects of the recession put a $3 trillion hole in our budget.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: All this was before I walked in the door.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] Now-applause-just stating the facts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, if we had taken office in ordinary times, I would have liked nothing more than to start bringing down the deficit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we took office amid a crisis.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And our efforts to prevent a second depression have added another $1 trillion to our national debt.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That too is a fact.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm absolutely convinced that was the right thing to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But families across the country are tightening their belts and making tough decisions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The Federal Government should do the same.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight I'm proposing specific steps to pay for the trillion dollars that it took to rescue the economy last year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Starting in 2011, we are prepared to freeze Government spending for 3 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Spending related to our national security, Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security will not be affected.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But all other discretionary Government programs will.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Like any cash-strapped family, we will work within a budget to invest in what we need and sacrifice what we don't.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if I have to enforce this discipline by veto, I will.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will continue to go through the budget, line by line, page by page, to eliminate programs that we can't afford and don't work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've already identified $20 billion in savings for next year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To help working families, we'll extend our middle class tax cuts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But at a time of record deficits, we will not continue tax cuts for oil companies, for investment fund managers, and for those making over $250,000 a year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We just can't afford it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, even after paying for what we spent on my watch, we'll still face the massive deficit we had when I took office.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More importantly, the cost of Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security will continue to skyrocket.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why I've called for a bipartisan fiscal commission, modeled on a proposal by Republican Judd Gregg and Democrat Kent Conrad.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This can't be one of those Washington gimmicks that lets us pretend we solve a problem.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The commission will have to provide a specific set of solutions by a certain deadline.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, yesterday the Senate blocked a bill that would have created this commission, so I'll issue an Executive order that will allow us to go forward, because I refuse to pass this problem on to another generation of Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And when the vote comes tomorrow, the Senate should restore the pay-as-you-go law that was a big reason for why we had record surpluses in the 1990s.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, I know that some in my own party will argue that we can't address the deficit or freeze Government spending when so many are still hurting.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I agree, which is why this freeze won't take effect until next year, when the economy is stronger.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's how budgeting works.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] But understand, if we don't take meaningful steps to rein in our debt, it could damage our markets, increase the cost of borrowing, and jeopardize our recovery, all of which would have an even worse effect on our job growth and family incomes.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: From some on the right, I expect we'll hear a different argument, that if we just make fewer investments in our people, extend tax cuts, including those for the wealthier Americans, eliminate more regulations, maintain the status quo on health care, our deficits will go away.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The problem is, that's what we did for 8 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what helped us into this crisis.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's what helped lead to these deficits.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can't do it again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Rather than fight the same tired battles that have dominated Washington for decades, it's time to try something new.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's invest in our people without leaving them a mountain of debt.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's meet our responsibility to the citizens who sent us here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's try common sense-laughter-a novel concept.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, to do that, we have to recognize that we face more than a deficit of dollars right now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We face a deficit of trust, deep and corrosive doubts about how Washington works that have been growing for years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To close that credibility gap, we have to take action on both ends of Pennsylvania Avenue to end the outsized influence of lobbyists, to do our work openly, to give our people the Government they deserve.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, that's what I came to Washington to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why, for the first time in history, my administration posts on-our White House visitors online.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we've excluded lobbyists from policymaking jobs or seats on Federal boards and commissions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we can't stop there.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's time to require lobbyists to disclose each contact they make on behalf of a client, with my administration or with Congress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's time to put strict limits on the contributions that lobbyists give to candidates for Federal office.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With all due deference to separation of powers, last week, the Supreme Court reversed a century of law that I believe will open the floodgates for special interests, including foreign corporations, to spend without limit in our elections.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I don't think American elections should be bankrolled by America's most powerful interests, or worse, by foreign entities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They should be decided by the American people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I'd urge Democrats and Republicans to pass a bill that helps correct some of these problems.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm also calling on Congress to continue down the path of earmark reform, Democrats and Republicans-Democrats and Republicans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Look, you've trimmed some of this spending, you've embraced some meaningful change, but restoring the public trust demands more.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For example, some Members of Congress post some earmark requests online.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight I'm calling on Congress to publish all earmark requests on a single web site before there's a vote so that the American people can see how their money is being spent.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, none of these reforms will even happen if we don't also reform how we work with one another.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, I'm not naive.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I never thought that the mere fact of my election would usher in peace and harmony and-[laughter]-some postpartisan era.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I knew that both parties have fed divisions that are deeply entrenched.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And on some issues, there are simply philosophical differences that will always cause us to part ways.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These disagreements, about the role of government in our lives, about our national priorities and our national security, they've been taking place for over 200 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're the very essence of our democracy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But what frustrates the American people is a Washington where every day is Election Day.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can't wage a perpetual campaign where the only goal is to see who can get the most embarrassing headlines about the other side, a belief that if you lose, I win.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Neither party should delay or obstruct every single bill just because they can.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The confirmation of-I'm speaking to both parties now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The confirmation of well-qualified public servants shouldn't be held hostage to the pet projects or grudges of a few individual Senators.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Washington may think that saying anything about the other side, no matter how false, no matter how malicious, is just part of the game.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But it's precisely such politics that has stopped either party from helping the American people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Worse yet, it's sowing further division among our citizens, further distrust in our Government.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So, no, I will not give up on trying to change the tone of our politics.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know it's an election year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And after last week, it's clear that campaign fever has come even earlier than usual.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we still need to govern.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To Democrats, I would remind you that we still have the largest majority in decades and the people expect us to solve problems, not run for the hills.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if the Republican leadership is going to insist that 60 votes in the Senate are required to do any business at all in this town-a supermajority-then the responsibility to govern is now yours as well.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Just saying no to everything may be good short-term politics, but it's not leadership.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We were sent here to serve our citizens, not our ambitions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's show the American people that we can do it together.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This week, I'll be addressing a meeting of the House Republicans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'd like to begin monthly meetings with both Democratic and Republican leadership.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know you can't wait.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] Now, throughout our history, no issue has united this country more than our security.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Sadly, some of the unity we felt after 9/11 has dissipated.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we can argue all we want about who's to blame for this, but I'm not interested in relitigating the past.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know that all of us love this country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: All of us are committed to its defense.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's put aside the schoolyard taunts about who's tough.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's reject the false choice between protecting our people and upholding our values.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's leave behind the fear and division and do what it takes to defend our Nation and forge a more hopeful future for America and for the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's the work we began last year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Since the day I took office, we've renewed our focus on the terrorists who threaten our Nation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've made substantial investments in our homeland security and disrupted plots that threatened to take American lives.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are filling unacceptable gaps revealed by the failed Christmas attack, with better airline security and swifter action on our intelligence.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've prohibited torture and strengthened partnerships from the Pacific to South Asia to the Arabian Peninsula.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in the last year, hundreds of Al Qaida's fighters and affiliates, including many senior leaders, have been captured or killed, far more than in 2008.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in Afghanistan, we're increasing our troops and training Afghan security forces so they can begin to take the lead in July of 2011 and our troops can begin to come home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will reward good governance, work to reduce corruption, and support the rights of all Afghans, men and women alike.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're joined by allies and partners who have increased their own commitments and who will come together tomorrow in London to reaffirm our common purpose.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There will be difficult days ahead, but I am absolutely confident we will succeed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As we take the fight to Al Qaida, we are responsibly leaving Iraq to its people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As a candidate, I promised that I would end this war, and that is what I am doing as President.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will have all of our combat troops out of Iraq by the end of this August.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will support the Iraqi Government as they hold elections, and we will continue to partner with the Iraqi people to promote regional peace and prosperity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But make no mistake: This war is ending, and all of our troops are coming home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight all of our men and women in uniform, in Iraq, in Afghanistan, and around the world, they have to know that we-that they have our respect, our gratitude, our full support.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And just as they must have the resources they need in war, we all have a responsibility to support them when they come home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we made the largest increase in investments for veterans in decades last year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we're building a 21st century VA.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why Michelle has joined with Jill Biden to forge a national commitment to support military families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, even as we prosecute two wars, we're also confronting perhaps the greatest danger to the American people, the threat of nuclear weapons.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've embraced the vision of John F. Kennedy and Ronald Reagan through a strategy that reverses the spread of these weapons and seeks a world without them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To reduce our stockpiles and launchers, while ensuring our deterrent, the United States and Russia are completing negotiations on the farthest reaching arms control treaty in nearly two decades.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And at April's Nuclear Security Summit, we will bring 44 nations together here in Washington, DC, behind a clear goal: securing all vulnerable nuclear materials around the world in 4 years so that they never fall into the hands of terrorists.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, these diplomatic efforts have also strengthened our hand in dealing with those nations that insist on violating international agreements in pursuit of nuclear weapons.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why North Korea now faces increased isolation and stronger sanctions, sanctions that are being vigorously enforced.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why the international community is more united and the Islamic Republic of Iran is more isolated.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as Iran's leaders continue to ignore their obligations, there should be no doubt: They too will face growing consequences.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is a promise.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's the leadership we are providing: engagement that advances the common security and prosperity of all people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're working through the G-20 to sustain a lasting global recovery.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're working with Muslim communities around the world to promote science and education and innovation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have gone from a bystander to a leader in the fight against climate change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're helping developing countries to feed themselves and continuing the fight against HIV/AIDS.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we are launching a new initiative that will give us the capacity to respond faster and more effectively to bioterrorism or an infectious disease, a plan that will counter threats at home and strengthen public health abroad.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As we have for over 60 years, America takes these actions because our destiny is connected to those beyond our shores.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we also do it because it is right.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why, as we meet here tonight, over 10,000 Americans are working with many nations to help the people of Haiti recover and rebuild.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we stand with the girl who yearns to go to school in Afghanistan, why we support the human rights of the women marching through the streets of Iran, why we advocate for the young man denied a job by corruption in Guinea.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For America must always stand on the side of freedom and human dignity-always.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Abroad, America's greatest source of strength has always been our ideals.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The same is true at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We find unity in our incredible diversity, drawing on the promise enshrined in our Constitution: The notion that we're all created equal;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that no matter who you are or what you look like, if you abide by the law, you should be protected by it;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: if you adhere to our common values, you should be treated no different than anyone else.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We must continually renew this promise.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My administration has a Civil Rights Division that is once again prosecuting civil rights violations and employment discrimination.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We finally strengthened our laws to protect against crimes driven by hate.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This year, I will work with Congress and our military to finally repeal the law that denies gay Americans the right to serve the country they love because of who they are.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the right thing to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're going to crackdown on violations of equal pay laws so that women get equal pay for an equal day's work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we should continue the work of fixing our broken immigration system, to secure our borders and enforce our laws and ensure that everyone who plays by the rules can contribute to our economy and enrich our Nation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the end, it's our ideals, our values that built America, values that allowed us to forge a nation made up of immigrants from every corner of the globe, values that drive our citizens still.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Every day, Americans meet their responsibilities to their families and their employers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Time and again, they lend a hand to their neighbors and give back to their country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They take pride in their labor and are generous in spirit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These aren't Republican values or Democratic values that they're living by, business values or labor values, they're American values.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Unfortunately, too many of our citizens have lost faith that our biggest institutions-our corporations, our media, and, yes, our Government-still reflect these same values.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Each of these institutions are full of honorable men and women doing important work that helps our country prosper.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But each time a CEO rewards himself for failure or a banker puts the rest of us at risk for his own selfish gain, people's doubts grow.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Each time lobbyists game the system or politicians tear each other down instead of lifting this country up, we lose faith.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The more that TV pundits reduce serious debates to silly arguments, big issues into sound bites, our citizens turn away.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No wonder there's so much cynicism out there.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No wonder there's so much disappointment.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I campaigned on the promise of change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Change we can believe in, the slogan went.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And right now I know there are many Americans who aren't sure if they still believe we can change or that I can deliver it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But remember this: I never suggested that change would be easy or that I could do it alone.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Democracy in a nation of 300 million people can be noisy and messy and complicated.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And when you try to do big things and make big changes, it stirs passions and controversy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's just how it is.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Those of us in public office can respond to this reality by playing it safe and avoid telling hard truths and pointing fingers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can do what's necessary to keep our poll numbers high and get through the next election, instead of doing what's best for the next generation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I also know this: If people had made that decision 50 years ago or 100 years ago or 200 years ago, we wouldn't be here tonight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The only reason we are here is because generations of Americans were unafraid to do what was hard, to do what was needed even when success was uncertain, to do what it took to keep the dream of this Nation alive for their children and their grandchildren.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, our administration has had some political setbacks this year, and some of them were deserved.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I wake up every day knowing that they are nothing compared to the setbacks that families all across this country have faced this year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And what keeps me going, what keeps me fighting, is that despite all these setbacks, that spirit of determination and optimism, that fundamental decency that has always been at the core of the American people, that lives on.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It lives on in the struggling small-business owner who wrote to me of his company, None of us, he said,are willing to consider, even slightly, that we might fail.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It lives on in the woman who said that even though she and her neighbors have felt the pain of recession, We are strong.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are resilient.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are American.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It lives on in the 8-year-old boy in Louisiana who just sent me his allowance and asked if I would give it to the people of Haiti.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it lives on in all the Americans who've dropped everything to go someplace they've never been and pull people they've never known from the rubble, prompting chants of U.S.A.! U.S.A! U.S.A! when another life was saved.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The spirit that has sustained this Nation for more than two centuries lives on in you, its people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have finished a difficult year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have come through a difficult decade.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But a new year has come.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A new decade stretches before us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We don't quit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I don't quit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's seize this moment to start anew, to carry the dream forward, and to strengthen our Union once more.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thank you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: God bless you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And God bless the United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. Vice President, Members of Congress, distinguished guests, and fellow Americans: Tonight I want to begin by congratulating the men and women of the 112th Congress, as well as your new Speaker, John Boehner.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as we mark this occasion, we're also mindful of the empty chair in this Chamber, and we pray for the health of our colleague and our friend Gabby Giffords.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's no secret that those of us here tonight have had our differences over the last 2 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The debates have been contentious;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: we have fought fiercely for our beliefs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's a good thing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what a robust democracy demands.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what helps set us apart as a nation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But there's a reason the tragedy in Tucson gave us pause.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Amid all the noise and passion and rancor of our public debate, Tucson reminded us that no matter who we are or where we come from, each of us is a part of something greater, something more consequential than party or political preference.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are part of the American family.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We believe that in a country where every race and faith and point of view can be found, we are still bound together as one people, that we share common hopes and a common creed, that the dreams of a little girl in Tucson are not so different than those of our own children, that they all deserve the chance to be fulfilled.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That too is what sets us apart as a nation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, by itself, this simple recognition won't usher in a new era of cooperation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What comes of this moment is up to us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What comes of this moment will be determined not by whether we can sit together tonight, but whether we can work together tomorrow.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I believe we can, and I believe we must.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what the people who sent us here expect of us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With their votes, they've determined that governing will now be a shared responsibility between parties.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: New laws will only pass with support from Democrats and Republicans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will move forward together or not at all, for the challenges we face are bigger than party and bigger than politics.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At stake right now is not who wins the next election.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After all, we just had an election.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At stake is whether new jobs and industries take root in this country or somewhere else.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's whether the hard work and industry of our people is rewarded.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's whether we sustain the leadership that has made America not just a place on a map, but the light to the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are poised for progress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Two years after the worst recession most of us have ever known, the stock market has come roaring back, corporate profits are up, the economy is growing again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we have never measured progress by these yardsticks alone.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We measure progress by the success of our people, by the jobs they can find and the quality of life those jobs offer, by the prospects of a small-business owner who dreams of turning a good idea into a thriving enterprise, by the opportunities for a better life that we pass on to our children.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's the project the American people want us to work on-together.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, we did that in December.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thanks to the tax cuts we passed, Americans' paychecks are a little bigger today.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Every business can write off the full cost of new investments that they make this year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And these steps, taken by Democrats and Republicans, will grow the economy and add to the more than 1 million private sector jobs created last year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we have to do more.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These steps we've taken over the last 2 years may have broken the back of this recession, but to win the future, we'll need to take on challenges that have been decades in the making.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Many people watching tonight can probably remember a time when finding a good job meant showing up at a nearby factory or a business downtown.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You didn't always need a degree, and your competition was pretty much limited to your neighbors.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If you worked hard, chances are you'd have a job for life, with a decent paycheck and good benefits and the occasional promotion.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Maybe you'd even have the pride of seeing your kids work at the same company.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That world has changed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And for many, the change has been painful.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've seen it in the shuttered windows of once booming factories and the vacant storefronts on once busy Main Streets.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've heard it in the frustrations of Americans who've seen their paychecks dwindle or their jobs disappear, proud men and women who feel like the rules have been changed in the middle of the game.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're right.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The rules have changed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In a single generation, revolutions in technology have transformed the way we live, work, and do business.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Steel mills that once needed 1,000 workers can now do the same work with 100.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, just about any company can set up shop, hire workers, and sell their products wherever there's an Internet connection.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Meanwhile, nations like China and India realized that with some changes of their own, they could compete in this new world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And so they started educating their children earlier and longer, with greater emphasis on math and science.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're investing in research and new technologies.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Just recently, China became the home to the world's largest private solar research facility and the world's fastest computer.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So yes, the world is changed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The competition for jobs is real.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But this shouldn't discourage us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It should challenge us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Remember, for all the hits we've taken these last few years, for all the naysayers predicting our decline, America still has the largest, most prosperous economy in the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No workers are more productive than ours.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No country has more successful companies or grants more patents to inventors and entrepreneurs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're the home to the world's best colleges and universities, where more students come to study than any place on Earth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What's more, we are the first nation to be founded for the sake of an idea: the idea that each of us deserves the chance to shape our own destiny.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why centuries of pioneers and immigrants have risked everything to come here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's why our students don't just memorize equations, but answer questions like What do you think of that idea? What would you change about the world? What do you want to be when you grow up? The future is ours to win.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But to get there, we can't just stand still.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As Robert Kennedy told us, The future is not a gift.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is an achievement.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Sustaining the American Dream has never been about standing pat.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It has required each generation to sacrifice and struggle and meet the demands of a new age.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And now it's our turn.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We know what it takes to compete for the jobs and industries of our time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to out-innovate, out-educate, and out-build the rest of the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have to make America the best place on Earth to do business.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to take responsibility for our deficit and reform our Government.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's how our people will prosper.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's how we'll win the future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tonight, I'd like to talk about how we get there.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The first step in winning the future is encouraging American innovation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: None of us can predict with certainty what the next big industry will be or where the new jobs will come from.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thirty years ago, we couldn't know that something called the Internet would lead to an economic revolution.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What we can do-what America does better than anyone else-is spark the creativity and imagination of our people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're the nation that put cars in driveways and computers in offices;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: the nation of Edison and the Wright brothers, of Google and Facebook.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In America, innovation doesn't just change our lives.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is how we make our living.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our free enterprise system is what drives innovation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But because it's not always profitable for companies to invest in basic research, throughout our history, our Government has provided cutting-edge scientists and inventors with the support that they need.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what planted the seeds for the Internet.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what helped make possible things like computer chips and GPS.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Just think of all the good jobs-from manufacturing to retail-that have come from these breakthroughs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Half a century ago, when the Soviets beat us into space with the launch of a satellite called Sputnik, we had no idea how we would beat them to the Moon.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The science wasn't even there yet.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: NASA didn't exist.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But after investing in better research and education, we didn't just surpass the Soviets;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: we unleashed a wave of innovation that created new industries and millions of new jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This is our generation's Sputnik moment.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Two years ago, I said that we needed to reach a level of research and development we haven't seen since the height of the space race.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in a few weeks, I will be sending a budget to Congress that helps us meet that goal.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll invest in biomedical research, information technology, and especially clean energy technology, an investment that will strengthen our security, protect our planet, and create countless new jobs for our people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Already, we're seeing the promise of renewable energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Robert and Gary Allen are brothers who run a small Michigan roofing company.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After September 11th, they volunteered their best roofers to help repair the Pentagon.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But half of their factory went unused, and the recession hit them hard.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, with the help of a Government loan, that empty space is being used to manufacture solar shingles that are being sold all across the country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: nan

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what Americans have done for over 200 years: reinvented ourselves.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And to spur on more success stories like the Allen Brothers, we've begun to reinvent our energy policy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're not just handing out money.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're issuing a challenge.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're telling America's scientists and engineers that if they assemble teams of the best minds in their fields and focus on the hardest problems in clean energy, we'll fund the Apollo projects of our time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At the California Institute of Technology, they're developing a way to turn sunlight and water into fuel for our cars.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At Oak Ridge National Laboratory, they're using supercomputers to get a lot more power out of our nuclear facilities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With more research and incentives, we can break our dependence on oil with biofuels and become the first country to have a million electric vehicles on the road by 2015.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to get behind this innovation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And to help pay for it, I'm asking Congress to eliminate the billions in taxpayer dollars we currently give to oil companies.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I don't know if you've noticed, but they're doing just fine on their own.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] So instead of subsidizing yesterday's energy, let's invest in tomorrow's.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, clean energy breakthroughs will only translate into clean energy jobs if businesses know there will be a market for what they're selling.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight I challenge you to join me in setting a new goal: By 2035, 80 percent of America's electricity will come from clean energy sources.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some folks want wind and solar.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Others want nuclear, clean coal, and natural gas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To meet this goal, we will need them all, and I urge Democrats and Republicans to work together to make it happen.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Maintaining our leadership in research and technology is crucial to America's success.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But if we want to win the future, if we want innovation to produce jobs in America and not overseas, then we also have to win the race to educate our kids.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Think about it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Over the next 10 years, nearly half of all new jobs will require education that goes beyond a high school education.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And yet as many as a quarter of our students aren't even finishing high school.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The quality of our math and science education lags behind many other nations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America has fallen to ninth in the proportion of young people with a college degree.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And so the question is whether all of us, as citizens and as parents, are willing to do what's necessary to give every child a chance to succeed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That responsibility begins not in our classrooms, but in our homes and communities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's family that first instills the love of learning in a child.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Only parents can make sure the TV is turned off and homework gets done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to teach our kids that it's not just the winner of the Super Bowl who deserves to be celebrated, but the winner of the science fair.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to teach them that success is not a function of fame or PR, but of hard work and discipline.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our schools share this responsibility.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When a child walks into a classroom, it should be a place of high expectations and high performance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But too many schools don't meet this test.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why instead of just pouring money into a system that's not working, we launched a competition called Race to the Top.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To all 50 States, we said, If you show us the most innovative plans to improve teacher quality and student achievement, we'll show you the money.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Race to the Top is the most meaningful reform of our public schools in a generation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For less than 1 percent of what we spend on education each year, it has led over 40 States to raise their standards for teaching and learning.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And these standards were developed, by the way, not by Washington, but by Republican and Democratic Governors throughout the country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And Race to the Top should be the approach we follow this year as we replace No Child Left Behind with a law that's more flexible and focused on what's best for our kids.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You see, we know what's possible from our children when reform isn't just a top-down mandate, but the work of local teachers and principals, school boards and communities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Take a school like Bruce Randolph in Denver.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Three years ago, it was rated one of the worst schools in Colorado, located on turf between two rival gangs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But last May, 97 percent of the seniors received their diploma.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: nan

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Most will be the first in their families to go to college.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what good schools can do, and we want good schools all across the country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's also remember that after parents, the biggest impact on a child's success comes from the man or woman at the front of the classroom.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In South Korea, teachers are known as nation builders.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Here in America, it's time we treated the people who educate our children with the same level of respect.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We want to reward good teachers and stop making excuses for bad ones.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And over the next 10 years, with so many baby boomers retiring from our classrooms, we want to prepare 100,000 new teachers in the fields of science and technology and engineering and math.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, to every young person listening tonight who's contemplating their career choice: If you want to make a difference in the life of our Nation, if you want to make a difference in the life of a child, become a teacher.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Your country needs you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, the education race doesn't end with a high school diploma.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To compete, higher education must be within the reach of every American.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we've ended the unwarranted taxpayer subsidies that went to banks and used the savings to make college affordable for millions of students.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And this year, I ask Congress to go further and make permanent our tuition tax credit, worth $10,000 for 4 years of college.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the right thing to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because people need to be able to train for new jobs and careers in today's fast-changing economy, we're also revitalizing America's community colleges.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last month, I saw the promise of these schools at Forsyth Tech in North Carolina.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Many of the students there used to work in the surrounding factories that have since left town.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: One mother of two, a woman named Kathy Proctor, had worked in the furniture industry since she was 18 years old.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And she told me she's earning her degree in biotechnology now, at 55 years old, not just because the furniture jobs are gone, but because she wants to inspire her children to pursue their dreams too.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As Kathy said, I hope it tells them to never give up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If we take these steps, if we raise expectations for every child and give them the best possible chance at an education, from the day they are born until the last job they take, we will reach the goal that I set 2 years ago: By the end of the decade, America will once again have the highest proportion of college graduates in the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: One last point about education: Today, there are hundreds of thousands of students excelling in our schools who are not American citizens.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some are the children of undocumented workers, who had nothing to do with the actions of their parents.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They grew up as Americans and pledge allegiance to our flag, and yet they live every day with the threat of deportation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Others come here from abroad to study in our colleges and universities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But as soon as they obtain advanced degrees, we send them back home to compete against us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It makes no sense.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, I strongly believe that we should take on, once and for all, the issue of illegal immigration.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I am prepared to work with Republicans and Democrats to protect our borders, enforce our laws, and address the millions of undocumented workers who are now living in the shadows.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know that debate will be difficult.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know it will take time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But tonight, let's agree to make that effort.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And let's stop expelling talented, responsible young people who could be staffing our research labs or starting a new business, who could be further enriching this Nation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The third step in winning the future is rebuilding America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To attract new businesses to our shores, we need the fastest, most reliable ways to move people, goods, and information, from high-speed rail to high-speed Internet.

speaker: Barack Obama
