text: Our infrastructure used to be the best, but our lead has slipped.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: South Korean homes now have greater Internet access than we do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Countries in Europe and Russia invest more in their roads and railways than we do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: China is building faster trains and newer airports.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Meanwhile, when our own engineers graded our Nation's infrastructure, they gave us a D.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have to do better.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America is the nation that built the transcontinental railroad, brought electricity to rural communities, constructed the Interstate Highway System.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The jobs created by these projects didn't just come from laying down track or pavement.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They came from businesses that opened near a town's new train station or the new off-ramp.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So over the last 2 years, we've begun rebuilding for the 21st century, a project that has meant thousands of good jobs for the hard-hit construction industry.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tonight I'm proposing that we redouble those efforts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll put more Americans to work repairing crumbling roads and bridges.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll make sure this is fully paid for, attract private investment, and pick projects based [on]* what's best for the economy, not politicians.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Within 25 years, our goal is to give 80 percent of Americans access to high-speed rail.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This could allow you to go places in half the time it takes to travel by car.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For some trips, it will be faster than flying, without the pat-down.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] As we speak, routes in California and the Midwest are already underway.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Within the next 5 years, we'll make it possible for businesses to deploy the next generation of high-speed wireless coverage to 98 percent of all Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Within the next 5 years, we'll make it possible for businesses to deploy the next generation of high-speed wireless coverage to 98 percent of all Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This isn't just about-this isn't about faster Internet or fewer dropped calls.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's about connecting every part of America to the digital age.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's about connecting every part of America to the digital age.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's about a rural community in Iowa or Alabama where farmers and small-business owners will be able to sell their products all over the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's about a firefighter who can download the design of a burning building onto a handheld device, a student who can take classes with a digital textbook, or a patient who can have face-to-face video chats with her doctor.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: All these investments, in innovation, education, and infrastructure, will make America a better place to do business and create jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But to help our companies compete, we also have to knock down barriers that stand in the way of their success.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For example, over the years, a parade of lobbyists has rigged the Tax Code to benefit particular companies and industries.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Those with accountants or lawyers to work the system can end up paying no taxes at all.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But all the rest are hit with one of the highest corporate tax rates in the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It makes no sense, and it has to change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight I'm asking Democrats and Republicans to simplify the system, get rid of the loopholes, level the playing field, and use the savings to lower the corporate tax rate for the first time in 25 years without adding to our deficit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It can be done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To help businesses sell more products abroad, we set a goal of doubling our exports by 2014.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because the more we export, the more jobs we create here at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Already, our exports are up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Recently, we signed agreements with India and China that will support more than 250,000 jobs here in the United States.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And last month, we finalized a trade agreement with South Korea that will support at least 70,000 American jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This agreement has unprecedented support from business and labor, Democrats and Republicans, and I ask this Congress to pass it as soon as possible.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, before I took office, I made it clear that we would enforce our trade agreements, and that I would only sign deals that keep faith with American workers and promote American jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what we did with Korea, and that's what I intend to do as we pursue agreements with Panama and Colombia and continue our Asia Pacific and global trade talks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To reduce barriers to growth and investment, I've ordered a review of Government regulations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When we find rules that put an unnecessary burden on businesses, we will fix them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I will not hesitate to create or enforce commonsense safeguards to protect the American people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what we've done in this country for more than a century.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's why our food is safe to eat, our water is safe to drink, and our air is safe to breathe.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's why we have speed limits and child labor laws.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's why last year, we put in place consumer protections against hidden fees and penalties by credit card companies and new rules to prevent another financial crisis.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it's why we passed reform that finally prevents the health insurance industry from exploiting patients.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, I have heard rumors that a few of you still have concerns about our new health care law.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] So let me be the first to say that anything can be improved.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If you have ideas about how to improve this law by making care better or more affordable, I am eager to work with you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can start right now by correcting a flaw in the legislation that has placed an unnecessary bookkeeping burden on small businesses.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What I'm not willing to do-what I'm not willing to do is go back to the days when insurance companies could deny someone coverage because of a preexisting condition.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm not willing to tell James Howard, a brain cancer patient from Texas, that his treatment might not be covered.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm not willing to tell Jim Houser, a small-business man from Oregon, that he has to go back to paying $5,000 more to cover his employees.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As we speak, this law is making prescription drugs cheaper for seniors and giving uninsured students a chance to stay on their patients'-parents' coverage.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So I say to this chamber tonight: Instead of refighting the battles of the last 2 years, let's fix what needs fixing, and let's move forward.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, the final critical step in winning the future is to make sure we aren't buried under a mountain of debt.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are living with a legacy of deficit spending that began almost a decade ago.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in the wake of the financial crisis, some of that was necessary to keep credit flowing, save jobs, and put money in people's pockets.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But now that the worst of the recession is over, we have to confront the fact that our Government spends more than it takes in.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is not sustainable.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Every day, families sacrifice to live within their means.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They deserve a Government that does the same.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight I am proposing that starting this year, we freeze annual domestic spending for the next 5 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, this would reduce the deficit by more than $400 billion over the next decade and will bring discretionary spending to the lowest share of our economy since Dwight Eisenhower was President.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This freeze will require painful cuts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Already, we've frozen the salaries of hard-working Federal employees for the next 2 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've proposed cuts to things I care deeply about, like community action programs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The Secretary of Defense has also agreed to cut tens of billions of dollars in spending that he and his generals believe our military can do without.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, I recognize that some in this Chamber have already proposed deeper cuts, and I'm willing to eliminate whatever we can honestly afford to do without.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But let's make sure that we're not doing it on the backs of our most vulnerable citizens.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And let's make sure that what we're cutting is really excess weight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Cutting the deficit by gutting our investments in innovation and education is like lightening an overloaded airplane by removing its engine.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It may make you feel like you're flying high at first, but it won't take long before you feel the impact.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] Now, most of the cuts and savings I've proposed only address annual domestic spending, which represents a little more than 12 percent of our budget.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To make further progress, we have to stop pretending that cutting this kind of spending alone will be enough.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It won't.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The bipartisan fiscal commission I created last year made this crystal clear.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I don't agree with all their proposals, but they made important progress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And their conclusion is that the only way to tackle our deficit is to cut excessive spending wherever we find it, in domestic spending, defense spending, health care spending, and spending through tax breaks and loopholes.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This means further reducing health care costs, including programs like Medicare and Medicaid, which are the single biggest contributor to our long-term deficit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The health insurance law we passed last year will slow these rising costs, which is part of the reason that nonpartisan economists have said that repealing the health care law would add a quarter of a trillion dollars to our deficit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Still, I'm willing to look at other ideas to bring down costs, including one that Republicans suggested last year: medical malpractice reform to rein in frivolous lawsuits.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To put us on solid ground, we should also find a bipartisan solution to strengthen Social Security for future generations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We must do it without putting at risk current retirees, the most vulnerable, or people with disabilities, without slashing benefits for future generations, and without subjecting Americans' guaranteed retirement income to the whims of the stock market.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if we truly care about our deficit, we simply can't afford a permanent extension of the tax cuts for the wealthiest 2 percent of Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Before we take money away from our schools or scholarships away from our students, we should ask millionaires to give up their tax break.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's not a matter of punishing their success, it's about promoting America's success.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, the best thing we could do on taxes for all Americans is to simplify the individual Tax Code.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This will be a tough job, but members of both parties have expressed an interest in doing this, and I am prepared to join them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So now is the time to act.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now is the time for both sides and both Houses of Congress, Democrats and Republicans, to forge a principled compromise that gets the job done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If we make the hard choices now to rein in our deficits, we can make the investments we need to win the future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let me take this one step further.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We shouldn't just give our people a Government that's more affordable, we should give them a Government that's more competent and more efficient.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can't win the future with a Government of the past.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We live and do business in the information age, but the last major reorganization of the Government happened in the age of black-and-white TV.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There are 12 different agencies that deal with exports.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There are at least five different agencies that deal with housing policy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Then there's my favorite example: The Interior Department is in charge of salmon while they're in fresh water, but the Commerce Department handles them when they're in saltwater.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] I hear it gets even more complicated once they're smoked.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] Now, we've made great strides over the last 2 years in using technology and getting rid of waste.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Veterans can now download their electronic medical records with a click of the mouse.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're selling acres of Federal office space that hasn't been used in years, and we'll cut through redtape to get rid of more.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we need to think bigger.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the coming months, my administration will develop a proposal to merge, consolidate, and reorganize the Federal Government in a way that best serves the goal of a more competitive America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will submit that proposal to Congress for a vote, and we will push to get it passed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the coming year, we'll also work to rebuild people's faith in the institution of Government.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because you deserve to know exactly how and where your tax dollars are being spent, you'll be able to go to a web site and get that information for the very first time in history.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because you deserve to know when your elected officials are meeting with lobbyists, I ask Congress to do what the White House has already done: put that information online.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And because the American people deserve to know that special interests aren't larding up legislation with pet projects, both parties in Congress should know this: If a bill comes to my desk with earmarks inside, I will veto it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will veto it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The 21st-century Government that's open and competent, a government that lives within its means, an economy that's driven by new skills and new ideas-our success in this new and changing world will require reform, responsibility, and innovation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It will also require us to approach that world with a new level of engagement in our foreign affairs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Just as jobs and businesses can now race across borders, so can new threats and new challenges.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No single wall separates East and West.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No one rival superpower is aligned against us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And so we must defeat determined enemies, wherever they are, and build coalitions that cut across lines of region and race and religion.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And America's moral example must always shine for all who yearn for freedom and justice and dignity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And because we've begun this work, tonight we can say that American leadership has been renewed and America's standing has been restored.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Look to Iraq, where nearly 100,000 of our brave men and women have left with their heads held high.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: American combat patrols have ended, violence is down, and a new Government has been formed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This year, our civilians will forge a lasting partnership with the Iraqi people, while we finish the job of bringing our troops out of Iraq.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America's commitment has been kept.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The Iraq war is coming to an end.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, as we speak, Al Qaida and their affiliates continue to plan attacks against us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thanks to our intelligence and law enforcement professionals, we're disrupting plots and securing our cities and skies.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as extremists try to inspire acts of violence within our borders, we are responding with the strength of our communities, with respect for the rule of law, and with the conviction that American Muslims are a part of our American family.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've also taken the fight to Al Qaida and their allies abroad.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In Afghanistan, our troops have taken Taliban strongholds and trained Afghan security forces.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our purpose is clear: By preventing the Taliban from reestablishing a stranglehold over the Afghan people, we will deny Al Qaida the safe haven that served as a launching pad for 9/11.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thanks to our heroic troops and civilians, fewer Afghans are under the control of the insurgency.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There will be tough fighting ahead, and the Afghan Government will need to deliver better governance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we are strengthening the capacity of the Afghan people and building an enduring partnership with them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This year, we will work with nearly 50 countries to begin a transition to an Afghan lead, and this July, we will begin to bring our troops home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In Pakistan, Al Qaida's leadership is under more pressure than at any point since 2001.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Their leaders and operatives are being removed from the battlefield.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Their safe havens are shrinking.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we've sent a message from the Afghan border to the Arabian Peninsula to all parts of the globe: We will not relent, we will not waver, and we will defeat you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: American leadership can also be seen in the effort to secure the worst weapons of war.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because Republicans and Democrats approved the new START Treaty, far fewer nuclear weapons and launchers will be deployed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because we rallied the world, nuclear materials are being locked down on every continent so they never fall into the hands of terrorists.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because of a diplomatic effort to insist that Iran meet its obligations, the Iranian Government now faces tougher sanctions, tighter sanctions than ever before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And on the Korean Peninsula, we stand with our ally South Korea and insist that North Korea keeps its commitment to abandon nuclear weapons.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This is just a part of how we're shaping a world that favors peace and prosperity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With our European allies, we revitalized NATO and increased our cooperation on everything from counterterrorism to missile defense.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've reset our relationship with Russia, strengthened Asian alliances, built new partnerships with nations like India.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This March, I will travel to Brazil, Chile, and El Salvador to forge new alliances across the Americas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Around the globe, we're standing with those who take responsibility, helping farmers grow more food, supporting doctors who care for the sick, and combating the corruption that can rot a society and rob people of opportunity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Recent events have shown us that what sets us apart must not just be our power-it must also be the purpose behind it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In south Sudan-with our assistance-the people were finally able to vote for independence after years of war.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thousands lined up before dawn.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: People danced in the streets.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: One man who lost four of his brothers at war summed up the scene around him.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This was a battlefield for most of my life, he said.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now we want to be free.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we saw that same desire to be free in Tunisia, where the will of the people proved more powerful than the writ of a dictator.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tonight let us be clear: The United States of America stands with the people of Tunisia and supports the democratic aspirations of all people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We must never forget that the things we've struggled for, and fought for, live in the hearts of people everywhere.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we must always remember that the Americans who have borne the greatest burden in this struggle are the men and women who serve our country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight let us speak with one voice in reaffirming that our Nation is united in support of our troops and their families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let us serve them as well as they've served us, by giving them the equipment they need, by providing them with the care and benefits that they have earned, and by enlisting our veterans in the great task of building our own Nation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our troops come from every corner of this country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're Black, White, Latino, Asian, Native American.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They are Christian and Hindu, Jewish and Muslim.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And yes, we know that some of them are gay.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Starting this year, no American will be forbidden from serving the country they love because of who they love.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And with that change, I call on all our college campuses to open their doors to our military recruiters and ROTC.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is time to leave behind the divisive battles of the past.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is time to move forward as one Nation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should have no illusions about the work ahead of us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Reforming our schools, changing the way we use energy, reducing our deficit, none of this will be easy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: All of it will take time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it will be harder because we will argue about everything: the costs, the details, the letter of every law.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, some countries don't have this problem.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If the central government wants a railroad, they build a railroad, no matter how many homes get bulldozed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If they don't want a bad story in the newspaper, it doesn't get written.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And yet, as contentious and frustrating and messy as our democracy can sometimes be, I know there isn't a person here who would trade places with any other nation on Earth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We may have differences in policy, but we all believe in the rights enshrined in our Constitution.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We may have different opinions, but we believe in the same promise that says this is a place where you can make it if you try.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We may have different backgrounds, but we believe in the same dream that says this is a country where anything is possible, no matter who you are, no matter where you come from.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That dream is why I can stand here before you tonight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That dream is why a working-class kid from Scranton can sit behind me.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] That dream is why someone who began by sweeping the floors of his father's Cincinnati bar can preside as Speaker of the House in the greatest nation on Earth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That dream-that American Dream-is what drove the Allen Brothers to reinvent their roofing company for a new era.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's what drove those students at Forsyth Tech to learn a new skill and work towards the future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that dream is the story of a small-business owner named Brandon Fisher.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Brandon started a company in Berlin, Pennsylvania, that specializes in a new kind of drilling technology.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And one day last summer, he saw the news that halfway across the world, 33 men were trapped in a Chilean mine, and no one knew how to save them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But Brandon thought his company could help.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And so he designed a rescue that would come to be known as Plan B.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: His employees worked around the clock to manufacture the necessary drilling equipment, and Brandon left for Chile.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Along with others, he began drilling a 2,000-foot hole into the ground, working 3 or 4 hour-3 or 4 days at a time without any sleep.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thirty-seven days later, Plan B succeeded, and the miners were rescued.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But because he didn't want all of the attention, Brandon wasn't there when the miners emerged.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: He'd already gone back home, back to work on his next project.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We do big things.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: nan

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We do big things.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: From the earliest days of our founding, America has been the story of ordinary people who dare to dream.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's how we win the future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: nan

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I might not come from a family of college graduates, but I will be the first to get my degree.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: nan

speaker: Barack Obama
text: nan

speaker: Barack Obama

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We do big things.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The idea of America endures.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our destiny remains our choice.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tonight more than two centuries later, it's because of our people that our future is hopeful, our journey goes forward, and the state of our Union is strong.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thank you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: God bless you, and may God bless the United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. Vice President, Members of Congress, distinguished guests, and fellow Americans: Last month, I went to Andrews Air Force Base and welcomed home some of our last troops to serve in Iraq.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Together, we offered a final, proud salute to the colors under which more than a million of our fellow citizens fought and several thousand gave their lives.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We gather tonight knowing that this generation of heroes has made the United States safer and more respected around the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For the first time in 9 years, there are no Americans fighting in Iraq.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For the first time in two decades, Usama bin Laden is not a threat to this country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Most of Al Qaida's top lieutenants have been defeated.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The Taliban's momentum has been broken, and some troops in Afghanistan have begun to come home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These achievements are a testament to the courage, selflessness, and teamwork of America's Armed Forces.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At a time when too many of our institutions have let us down, they exceed all expectations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're not consumed with personal ambition.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They don't obsess over their differences.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They focus on the mission at hand.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They work together.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Imagine what we could accomplish if we followed their example.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Think about the America within our reach: a country that leads the world in educating its people;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: an America that attracts a new generation of high-tech manufacturing and high-paying jobs;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: a future where we're in control of our own energy and our security and prosperity aren't so tied to unstable parts of the world;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: an economy built to last, where hard work pays off and responsibility is rewarded.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can do this.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know we can, because we've done it before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At the end of World War II, when another generation of heroes returned home from combat, they built the strongest economy and middle class the world has ever known.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My grandfather, a veteran of Patton's army, got the chance to go to college on the GI bill.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My grandmother, who worked on a bomber assembly line, was part of a workforce that turned out the best products on Earth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The two of them shared the optimism of a nation that had triumphed over a depression and fascism.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They understood they were part of something larger, that they were contributing to a story of success that every American had a chance to share, the basic American promise that if you worked hard, you could do well enough to raise a family, own a home, send your kids to college, and put a little away for retirement.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The defining issue of our time is how to keep that promise alive.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No challenge is more urgent.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No debate is more important.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can either settle for a country where a shrinking number of people do really well while a growing number of Americans barely get by.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Or we can restore an economy where everyone gets a fair shot and everyone does their fair share and everyone plays by the same set of rules.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What's at stake aren't Democratic values or Republican values, but American values.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we have to reclaim them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's remember how we got here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Long before the recession, jobs and manufacturing began leaving our shores.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Technology made businesses more efficient, but also made some jobs obsolete.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Folks at the top saw their incomes rise like never before, but most hard-working Americans struggled with costs that were growing, paychecks that weren't, and personal debt that kept piling up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In 2008, the house of cards collapsed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We learned that mortgages had been sold to people who couldn't afford or understand them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Banks had made huge bets and bonuses with other people's money.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Regulators had looked the other way or didn't have the authority to stop the bad behavior.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It was wrong, it was irresponsible, and it plunged our economy into a crisis that put millions out of work, saddled us with more debt, and left innocent, hard-working Americans holding the bag.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the 6 months before I took office, we lost nearly 4 million jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we lost another 4 million before our policies were in full effect.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Those are the facts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But so are these: In the last 22 months, businesses have created more than 3 million jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last year, they created the most jobs since 2005.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: American manufacturers are hiring again, creating jobs for the first time since the late 1990s.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Together, we've agreed to cut the deficit by more than $2 trillion.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we've put in place new rules to hold Wall Street accountable so a crisis like this never happens again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The state of our Union is getting stronger.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we've come too far to turn back now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As long as I'm President, I will work with anyone in this Chamber to build on this momentum.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I intend to fight obstruction with action, and I will oppose any effort to return to the very same policies that brought on this economic crisis in the first place.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No, we will not go back to an economy weakened by outsourcing, bad debt, and phony financial profits.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight I want to speak about how we move forward and lay out a blueprint for an economy that's built to last, an economy built on American manufacturing, American energy, skills for American workers, and a renewal of American values.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, this blueprint begins with American manufacturing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: On the day I took office, our auto industry was on the verge of collapse.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some even said we should let it die.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With a million jobs at stake, I refused to let that happen.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In exchange for help, we demanded responsibility.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We got workers and automakers to settle their differences.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We got the industry to retool and restructure.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, General Motors is back on top as the world's number-one automaker.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Chrysler has grown faster in the U.S. than any major car company.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Ford is investing billions in U.S. plants and factories.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And together, the entire industry added nearly a hundred and sixty thousand jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We bet on American workers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We bet on American ingenuity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tonight, the American auto industry is back.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What's happening in Detroit can happen in other industries.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It can happen in Cleveland and Pittsburgh and Raleigh.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can't bring every job back that's left our shore.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But right now it's getting more expensive to do business in places like China.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Meanwhile, America is more productive.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A few weeks ago, the CEO of Master Lock told me that it now makes business sense for him to bring jobs back home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, for the first time in 15 years, Master Lock's unionized plant in Milwaukee is running at full capacity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So we have a huge opportunity at this moment to bring manufacturing back.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we have to seize it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight my message to business leaders is simple: Ask yourselves what you can do to bring jobs back to your country, and your country will do everything we can to help you succeed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should start with our Tax Code.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Right now companies get tax breaks for moving jobs and profits overseas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Meanwhile, companies that choose to stay in America get hit with one of the highest tax rates in the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It makes no sense, and everyone knows it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's change it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: First, if you're a business that wants to outsource jobs, you shouldn't get a tax deduction for doing it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That money should be used to cover moving expenses for companies like Master Lock that decide to bring jobs home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Second, no American company should be able to avoid paying its fair share of taxes by moving jobs and profits overseas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: From now on, every multinational company should have to pay a basic minimum tax.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And every penny should go towards lowering taxes for companies that choose to stay here and hire here in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Third, if you're an American manufacturer, you should get a bigger tax cut.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If you're a high-tech manufacturer, we should double the tax deduction you get for making your products here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if you want to relocate in a community that was hit hard when a factory left town, you should get help financing a new plant, equipment, or training for new workers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So my message is simple: It is time to stop rewarding businesses that ship jobs overseas, and start rewarding companies that create jobs right here in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Send me these tax reforms, and I will sign them right away.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're also making it easier for American businesses to sell products all over the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Two years ago, I set a goal of doubling U.S. exports over 5 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With the bipartisan trade agreements we signed into law, we're on track to meet that goal ahead of schedule.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And soon there will be millions of new customers for American goods in Panama, Colombia, and South Korea.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Soon there will be new cars on the streets of Seoul imported from Detroit and Toledo and Chicago.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will go anywhere in the world to open new markets for American products.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I will not stand by when our competitors don't play by the rules.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've brought trade cases against China at nearly twice the rate as the last administration, and it's made a difference.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Over a thousand Americans are working today because we stopped a surge in Chinese tires.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we need to do more.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's not right when another country lets our movies, music, and software be pirated.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's not fair when foreign manufacturers have a leg up on ours only because they're heavily subsidized.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight I'm announcing the creation of a trade enforcement unit that will be charged with investigating unfair trading practices in countries like China.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There will be more inspections to prevent counterfeit or unsafe goods from crossing our borders.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And this Congress should make sure that no foreign company has an advantage over American manufacturing when it comes to accessing financing or new markets like Russia.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our workers are the most productive on Earth, and if the playing field is level, I promise you, America will always win.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I also hear from many business leaders who want to hire in the United States, but can't find workers with the right skills.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Growing industries in science and technology have twice as many openings as we have workers who can do the job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Think about that: openings at a time when millions of Americans are looking for work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's inexcusable, and we know how to fix it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Jackie Bray is a single mom from North Carolina who was laid off from her job as a mechanic.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Then Siemens opened a gas turbine factory in Charlotte and formed a partnership with Central Piedmont Community College.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The company helped the college design courses in laser and robotics training.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It paid Jackie's tuition, then hired her to help operate their plant.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want every American looking for work to have the same opportunity as Jackie did.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Join me in a national commitment to train 2 million Americans with skills that will lead directly to a job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My administration has already lined up more companies that want to help.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Model partnerships between businesses like Siemens and community colleges in places like Charlotte and Orlando and Louisville are up and running.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now you need to give more community colleges the resources they need to become community career centers, places that teach people skills that businesses are looking for right now, from data management to high-tech manufacturing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I want to cut through the maze of confusing training programs so that from now on, people like Jackie have one program, one web site, and one place to go for all the information and help that they need.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is time to turn our unemployment system into a reemployment system that puts people to work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These reforms will help people get jobs that are open today.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But to prepare for the jobs of tomorrow, our commitment to skills and education has to start earlier.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For less than 1 percent of what our Nation spends on education each year, we've convinced nearly every State in the country to raise their standards for teaching and learning, the first time that's happened in a generation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But challenges remain, and we know how to solve them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At a time when other countries are doubling down on education, tight budgets have forced States to lay off thousands of teachers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We know a good teacher can increase the lifetime income of a classroom by over $250,000.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A great teacher can offer an escape from poverty to the child who dreams beyond his circumstance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Every person in this Chamber can point to a teacher who changed the trajectory of their lives.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Most teachers work tirelessly, with modest pay, sometimes digging into their own pocket for school supplies, just to make a difference.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Teachers matter.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So instead of bashing them or defending the status quo, let's offer schools a deal.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Give them the resources to keep good teachers on the job and reward the best ones.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in return, grant schools flexibility to teach with creativity and passion, to stop teaching to the test, and to replace teachers who just aren't helping kids learn.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's a bargain worth making.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We also know that when students don't walk away from their education, more of them walk the stage to get their diploma.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When students are not allowed to drop out, they do better.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight I am proposing that every State-every State-requires that all students stay in high school until they graduate or turn 18.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When kids do graduate, the most daunting challenge can be the cost of college.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At a time when Americans owe more in tuition debt than credit card debt, this Congress needs to stop the interest rates on student loans from doubling in July.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Extend the tuition tax credit we started that saves millions of middle class families thousands of dollars and give more young people the chance to earn their way through college by doubling the number of work-study jobs in the next 5 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, it's not enough for us to increase student aid.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can't just keep subsidizing skyrocketing tuition;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: we'll run out of money.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: States also need to do their part by making higher education a higher priority in their budgets.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And colleges and universities have to do their part by working to keep costs down.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Recently, I spoke with a group of college presidents who have done just that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some schools redesign courses to help students finish more quickly.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some use better technology.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The point is, it's possible.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let me put colleges and universities on notice: If you can't stop tuition from going up, the funding you get from taxpayers will go down.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Higher education can't be a luxury.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is an economic imperative that every family in America should be able to afford.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's also remember that hundreds of thousands of talented, hard-working students in this country face another challenge: the fact that they aren't yet American citizens.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Many were brought here as small children, are American through and through, yet they live every day with the threat of deportation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Others came more recently, to study business and science and engineering, but as soon as they get their degree, we send them home to invent new products and create new jobs somewhere else.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That doesn't make sense.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I believe as strongly as ever that we should take on illegal immigration.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why my administration has put more boots on the border than ever before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why there are fewer illegal crossings than when I took office.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The opponents of action are out of excuses.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should be working on comprehensive immigration reform right now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But if election-year politics keeps Congress from acting on a comprehensive plan, let's at least agree to stop expelling responsible young people who want to staff our labs, start new businesses, defend this country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Send me a law that gives them the chance to earn their citizenship.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will sign it right away.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You see, an economy built to last is one where we encourage the talent and ingenuity of every person in this country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That means women should earn equal pay for equal work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It means we should support everyone who's willing to work and every risk taker and entrepreneur who aspires to become the next Steve Jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After all, innovation is what America has always been about.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Most new jobs are created in startups and small businesses.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's pass an agenda that helps them succeed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tear down regulations that prevent aspiring entrepreneurs from getting the financing to grow.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Expand tax relief to small businesses that are raising wages and creating good jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Both parties agree on these ideas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So put them in a bill and get it on my desk this year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Innovation also demands basic research.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, the discoveries taking place in our federally financed labs and universities could lead to new treatments that kill cancer cells, but leave healthy ones untouched, new lightweight vests for cops and soldiers that can stop any bullet.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Don't gut these investments in our budget.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Don't let other countries win the race for the future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Support the same kind of research and innovation that led to the computer chip and the Internet, to new American jobs and new American industries.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And nowhere is the promise of innovation greater than in American-made energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Over the last 3 years, we've opened millions of new acres for oil and gas exploration, and tonight I'm directing my administration to open more than 75 percent of our potential offshore oil and gas resources.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Right now-right now-American oil production is the highest that it's been in 8 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's right, 8 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Not only that, last year, we relied less on foreign oil than in any of the past 16 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But with only 2 percent of the world's oil reserves, oil isn't enough.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This country needs an all-out, all-of-the-above strategy that develops every available source of American energy, a strategy that's cleaner, cheaper, and full of new jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have a supply of natural gas that can last America nearly 100 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And my administration will take every possible action to safely develop this energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Experts believe this will support more than 600,000 jobs by the end of the decade.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I'm requiring all companies that drill for gas on public lands to disclose the chemicals they use.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because America will develop this resource without putting the health and safety of our citizens at risk.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The development of natural gas will create jobs and power trucks and factories that are cleaner and cheaper, proving that we don't have to choose between our environment and our economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And by the way, it was public research dollars, over the course of 30 years, that helped develop the technologies to extract all this natural gas out of shale rock, reminding us that Government support is critical in helping businesses get new energy ideas off the ground.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, what's true for natural gas is just as true for clean energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In 3 years, our partnership with the private sector has already positioned America to be the world's leading manufacturer of high-tech batteries.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because of Federal investments, renewable energy use has nearly doubled, and thousands of Americans have jobs because of it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When Bryan Ritterby was laid off from his job making furniture, he said he worried that at 55 no one would give him a second chance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But he found work at Energetx, a wind turbine manufacturer in Michigan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Before the recession, the factory only made luxury yachts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, it's hiring workers like Bryan, who said, I'm proud to be working in the industry of the future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our experience with shale gas, our experience with natural gas, shows us that the payoffs on these public investments don't always come right away.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some technologies don't pan out, some companies fail.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I will not walk away from the promise of clean energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will not walk away from workers like Bryan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will not cede the wind or solar or battery industry to China or Germany because we refuse to make the same commitment here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've subsidized oil companies for a century.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's long enough.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's time to end the taxpayer giveaways to an industry that rarely has been more profitable and double down on a clean energy industry that never has been more promising.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Pass clean energy tax credits.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Create these jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can also spur energy innovation with new incentives.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The differences in this Chamber may be too deep right now to pass a comprehensive plan to fight climate change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But there's no reason why Congress shouldn't at least set a clean energy standard that creates a market for innovation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So far, you haven't acted.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Well, tonight I will.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm directing my administration to allow the development of clean energy on enough public land to power 3 million homes.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I'm proud to announce that the Department of Defense, working with us, the world's largest consumer of energy, will make one of the largest commitments to clean energy in history, with the Navy purchasing enough capacity to power a quarter of a million homes a year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, the easiest way to save money is to waste less energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So here's a proposal: Help manufacturers eliminate energy waste in their factories and give businesses incentives to upgrade their buildings.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Their energy bills will be a hundred billion dollars lower over the next decade, and America will have less pollution, more manufacturing, more jobs for construction workers who need them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Send me a bill that creates these jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Building this new energy future should be just one part of a broader agenda to repair America's infrastructure.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So much of America needs to be rebuilt.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've got crumbling roads and bridges, a power grid that wastes too much energy, an incomplete high-speed broadband network that prevents a small-business owner in rural America from selling her products all over the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: During the Great Depression, America built the Hoover Dam and the Golden Gate Bridge.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After World War II, we connected our States with a system of highways.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Democratic and Republican administrations invested in great projects that benefited everybody, from the workers who built them to the businesses that still use them today.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the next few weeks, I will sign an Executive order clearing away the redtape that slows down too many construction projects.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But you need to fund these projects.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Take the money we're no longer spending at war, use half of it to pay down our debt, and use the rest to do some nation-building right here at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There's never been a better time to build, especially since the construction industry was one of the hardest hit when the housing bubble burst.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, construction workers weren't the only ones who were hurt.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So were millions of innocent Americans who've seen their home values decline.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And while Government can't fix the problem on its own, responsible homeowners shouldn't have to sit and wait for the housing market to hit bottom to get some relief.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why I'm sending this Congress a plan that gives every responsible homeowner the chance to save about $3,000 a year on their mortgage by refinancing at historically low rates.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No more redtape.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No more runaround from the banks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A small fee on the largest financial institutions will ensure that it won't add to the deficit and will give those banks that were rescued by taxpayers a chance to repay a deficit of trust.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's never forget: Millions of Americans who work hard and play by the rules every day deserve a Government and a financial system that do the same.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's time to apply the same rules from top to bottom.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No bailouts, no handouts, and no copouts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: An America built to last insists on responsibility from everybody.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've all paid the price for lenders who sold mortgages to people who couldn't afford them and buyers who knew they couldn't afford them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we need smart regulations to prevent irresponsible behavior.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Rules to prevent financial fraud or toxic dumping or faulty medical devices, these don't destroy the free market.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They make the free market work better.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There's no question that some regulations are outdated, unnecessary, or too costly.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, I've approved fewer regulations in the first 3 years of my Presidency than my Republican predecessor did in his.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've ordered every Federal agency to eliminate rules that don't make sense.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've already announced over 500 reforms, and just a fraction of them will save business and citizens more than $10 billion over the next 5 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We got rid of one rule from 40 years ago that could have forced some dairy farmers to spend $10,000 a year proving that they could contain a spill, because milk was somehow classified as an oil.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With a rule like that, I guess it was worth crying over spilled milk.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Laughter] Now, I'm confident a farmer can contain a milk spill without a Federal agency looking over his shoulder.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Absolutely.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I will not back down from making sure an oil company can contain the kind of oil spill we saw in the Gulf 2 years ago.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will not back down from protecting our kids from mercury poisoning or making sure that our food is safe and our water is clean.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will not go back to the days when health insurance companies had unchecked power to cancel your policy, deny your coverage, or charge women differently than men.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I will not go back to the days when Wall Street was allowed to play by its own set of rules.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The new rules we passed restore what should be any financial system's core purpose: getting funding to entrepreneurs with the best ideas and getting loans to responsible families who want to buy a home or start a business or send their kids to college.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So if you are a big bank or financial institution, you're no longer allowed to make risky bets with your customers' deposits.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You're required to write out a living will that details exactly how you'll pay the bills if you fail, because the rest of us are not bailing you out ever again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if you're a mortgage lender or a payday lender or a credit card company, the days of signing people up for products they can't afford with confusing forms and deceptive practices, those days are over.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, American consumers finally have a watchdog in Richard Cordray, with one job: to look out for them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll also establish a financial crimes unit of highly trained investigators to crack down on large-scale fraud and protect people's investments.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some financial firms violate major antifraud laws because there's no real penalty for being a repeat offender.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's bad for consumers, and it's bad for the vast majority of bankers and financial service professionals who do the right thing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So pass legislation that makes the penalties for fraud count.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tonight I'm asking my Attorney General to create a special unit of Federal prosecutors and leading State attorney general to expand our investigations into the abusive lending and packaging of risky mortgages that led to the housing crisis.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This new unit will hold accountable those who broke the law, speed assistance to homeowners, and help turn the page on an era of recklessness that hurt so many Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, a return to the American values of fair play and shared responsibility will help protect our people and our economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But it should also guide us as we look to pay down our debt and invest in our future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Right now our most immediate priority is stopping a tax hike on a hundred and sixty million working Americans while the recovery is still fragile.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: People cannot afford losing $40 out of each paycheck this year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There are plenty of ways to get this done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's agree right here, right now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No side issues.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No drama.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Pass the payroll tax cut without delay.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's get it done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When it comes to the deficit, we've already agreed to more than $2 trillion in cuts and savings.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we need to do more, and that means making choices.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Right now we're poised to spend nearly $1 trillion more on what was supposed to be a temporary tax break for the wealthiest 2 percent of Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Right now because of loopholes and shelters in the Tax Code, a quarter of all millionaires pay lower tax rates than millions of middle class households.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Right now Warren Buffett pays a lower tax rate than his secretary.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Do we want to keep these tax cuts for the wealthiest Americans? Or do we want to keep our investments in everything else, like education and medical research, a strong military and care for our veterans? Because if we're serious about paying down our debt, we can't do both.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The American people know what the right choice is.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So do I.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As I told the Speaker this summer, I'm prepared to make more reforms that rein in the long-term costs of Medicare and Medicaid and strengthen Social Security, so long as those programs remain a guarantee of security for seniors.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But in return, we need to change our Tax Code so that people like me, and an awful lot of Members of Congress, pay our fair share of taxes.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tax reform should follow the Buffett rule.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If you make more than a million dollars a year, you should not pay less than 30 percent in taxes.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And my Republican friend Tom Coburn is right: Washington should stop subsidizing millionaires.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, if you're earning a million dollars a year, you shouldn't get special tax subsidies or deductions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: On the other hand, if you make under $250,000 a year, like 98 percent of American families, your taxes shouldn't go up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You're the ones struggling with rising costs and stagnant wages.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You're the ones who need relief.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, you can call this class warfare all you want.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But asking a billionaire to pay at least as much as his secretary in taxes? Most Americans would call that common sense.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We don't begrudge financial success in this country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We admire it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When Americans talk about folks like me paying my fair share of taxes, it's not because they envy the rich.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's because they understand that when I get a tax break I don't need and the country can't afford, it either adds to the deficit or somebody else has to make up the difference, like a senior on a fixed income or a student trying to get through school or a family trying to make ends meet.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's not right.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Americans know that's not right.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They know that this generation's success is only possible because past generations felt a responsibility to each other and to the future of their country, and they know our way of life will only endure if we feel that same sense of shared responsibility.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's how we'll reduce our deficit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's an America built to last.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, I recognize that people watching tonight have differing views about taxes and debt, energy and health care.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But no matter what party they belong to, I bet most Americans are thinking the same thing right about now: Nothing will get done in Washington this year or next year or maybe even the year after that, because Washington is broken.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Can you blame them for feeling a little cynical? The greatest blow to our confidence in our economy last year didn't come from events beyond our control.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It came from a debate in Washington over whether the United States would pay its bills or not.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Who benefited from that fiasco? I've talked tonight about the deficit of trust between Main Street and Wall Street.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But the divide between this city and the rest of the country is at least as bad, and it seems to get worse every year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, some of this has to do with the corrosive influence of money in politics.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So together, let's take some steps to fix that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Send me a bill that bans insider trading by Members of Congress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will sign it tomorrow.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's limit any elected official from owning stocks in industries they impact.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's make sure people who bundle campaign contributions for Congress can't lobby Congress and vice versa, an idea that has bipartisan support, at least outside of Washington.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some of what's broken has to do with the way Congress does its business these days.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A simple majority is no longer enough to get anything-even routine busines-passed through the Senate.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Neither party has been blameless in these tactics.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now both parties should put an end to it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For starters, I ask the Senate to pass a simple rule that all judicial and public service nominations receive a simple up-or-down vote within 90 days.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The executive branch also needs to change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Too often, it's inefficient, outdated, and remote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why I've asked this Congress to grant me the authority to consolidate the Federal bureaucracy so that our Government is leaner, quicker, and more responsive to the needs of the American people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Finally, none of this can happen unless we also lower the temperature in this town.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to end the notion that the two parties must be locked in a perpetual campaign of mutual destruction, that politics is about clinging to rigid ideologies instead of building consensus around commonsense ideas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm a Democrat, but I believe what Republican Abraham Lincoln believed: That Government should do for people only what they cannot do better by themselves and no more.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why my education reform offers more competition and more control for schools and States.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we're getting rid of regulations that don't work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why our health care law relies on a reformed private market, not a Government program.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: On the other hand, even my Republican friends who complain the most about Government spending have supported federally financed roads and clean energy projects and Federal offices for the folks back home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The point is, we should all want a smarter, more effective Government.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And while we may not be able to bridge our biggest philosophical differences this year, we can make real progress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With or without this Congress, I will keep taking actions that help the economy grow.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I can do a whole lot more with your help.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because when we act together, there's nothing the United States of America can't achieve.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's the lesson we've learned from our actions abroad over the last few years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Ending the Iraq war has allowed us to strike decisive blows against our enemies.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: From Pakistan to Yemen, the Al Qaida operatives who remain are scrambling, knowing that they can't escape the reach of the United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: From this position of strength, we've begun to wind down the war in Afghanistan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Ten thousand of our troops have come home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Twenty-three thousand more will leave by the end of this summer.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This transition to Afghan lead will continue, and we will build an enduring partnership with Afghanistan so that it is never again a source of attacks against America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As the tide of war recedes, a wave of change has washed across the Middle East and North Africa, from Tunis to Cairo, from Sana'a to Tripoli.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A year ago, Qadhafi was one of the world's longest serving dictators, a murderer with American blood on his hands.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, he is gone.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in Syria, I have no doubt that the Asad regime will soon discover that the forces of change cannot be reversed and that human dignity cannot be denied.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: How this incredible transformation will end remains uncertain.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we have a huge stake in the outcome.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And while it's ultimately up to the people of the region to decide their fate, we will advocate for those values that have served our own country so well.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will stand against violence and intimidation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will stand for the rights and dignity of all human beings: men and women;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Christians, Muslims, and Jews.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will support policies that lead to strong and stable democracies and open markets, because tyranny is no match for liberty.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we will safeguard America's own security against those who threaten our citizens, our friends, and our interests.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Look at Iran.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Through the power of our diplomacy, a world that was once divided about how to deal with Iran's nuclear program now stands as one.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The regime is more isolated than ever before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Its leaders are faced with crippling sanctions, and as long as they shirk their responsibilities, this pressure will not relent.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let there be no doubt: America is determined to prevent Iran from getting a nuclear weapon, and I will take no options off the table to achieve that goal.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But a peaceful resolution of this issue is still possible, and far better.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if Iran changes course and meets its obligations, it can rejoin the community of nations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The renewal of American leadership can be felt across the globe.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our oldest alliances in Europe and Asia are stronger than ever.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our ties to the Americas are deeper.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our ironclad commitment-and I mean ironclad-to Israel's security has meant the closest military cooperatoin between our two countries in history.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've made it clear that America is a Pacific power, and a new beginning in Burma has lit a new hope.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: From the coalitions we've built to secure nuclear materials, to the missions we've led against hunger and disease, from the blows we've dealt to our enemies, to the enduring power of our moral example, America is back.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Anyone who tells you otherwise, anyone who tells you that America is in decline or that our influence has waned, doesn't know what they're talking about.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's not the message we get from leaders around the world who are eager to work with us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's not how people feel from Tokyo to Berlin, from Cape Town to Rio, where opinions of America are higher than they've been in years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Yes, the world is changing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No, we can't control every event.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But America remains the one indispensable nation in world affairs, and as long as I'm President, I intend to keep it that way.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why, working with our military leaders, I've proposed a new defense strategy that ensures we maintain the finest military in the world, while saving nearly half a trillion dollars in our budget.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To stay one step ahead of our adversaries, I've already sent this Congress legislation that will secure our country from the growing dangers of cyber threats.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Above all, our freedom endures because of the men and women in uniform who defend it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As they come home, we must serve them as well as they've served us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That includes giving them the care and the benefits they have earned, which is why we've increased annual VA spending every year I've been President.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it means enlisting our veterans in the work of rebuilding our Nation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With the bipartisan support of this Congress, we're providing new tax credits to companies that hire vets.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Michelle and Jill Biden have worked with American businesses to secure a pledge of 135,000 jobs for veterans and their families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tonight I'm proposing a veterans jobs corps that will help our communities hire veterans as cops and firefighters, so that America is as strong as those who defend her.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Which brings me back to where I began.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Those of us who've been sent here to serve can learn a thing or two from the service of our troops.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When you put on that uniform, it doesn't matter if you're Black or White, Asian, Latino, Native American;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: conservative, liberal;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: rich, poor;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: gay, straight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When you're marching into battle, you look out for the person next to you or the mission fails.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When you're in the thick of the fight, you rise or fall as one unit, serving one nation, leaving no one behind.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You know, one of my proudest possessions is the flag that the SEAL team took with them on the mission to get bin Laden.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: On it are each of their names.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some may be Democrats, some may be Republicans, but that doesn't matter.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Just like it didn't matter that day in the Situation Room, when I sat next to Bob Gates, a man who was George Bush's Defense Secretary, and Hillary Clinton, a woman who ran against me for President.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: All that mattered that day was the mission.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No one thought about politics.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No one thought about themselves.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: One of the young men involved in the raid later told me that he didn't deserve credit for the mission.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It only succeeded, he said, because every single member of that unit did their job: the pilot who landed the helicopter that spun out of control, the translator who kept others from entering the compound, the troops who separated the women and children from the fight, the SEALs who charged up the stairs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More than that, the mission only succeeded because every member of that unit trusted each other, because you can't charge up those stairs into darkness and danger unless you know that there's somebody behind you, watching your back.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So it is with America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Each time I look at that flag, I'm reminded that our destiny is stitched together like those 50 stars and those 13 stripes.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No one built this country on their own.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This Nation is great because we built it together.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This Nation is great because we worked as a team.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This Nation is great because we get each other's backs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if we hold fast to that truth, in this moment of trial, there is no challenge too great, no mission too hard.

speaker: Barack Obama
