text: As long as we are joined in common purpose, as long as we maintain our common resolve, our journey moves forward, and our future is hopeful, and the state of our Union will always be strong.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thank you, God bless you, and God bless the United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Please, everybody, have a seat.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. Vice President, Members of Congress, fellow Americans: Fifty-one years ago, John F. Kennedy declared to this Chamber that ""the Constitution makes us not rivals for power, but partners for progress."

speaker: Barack Obama
text: "It is my task," he said, "to report the state of the Union;to improve it is the task of us all."

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight, thanks to the grit and determination of the American people, there is much progress to report.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After a decade of grinding war, our brave men and women in uniform are coming home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After years of grueling recession, our businesses have created over 6 million new jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We buy more American cars than we have in 5 years and less foreign oil than we have in 20.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our housing market is healing, our stock market is rebounding, and consumers, patients, and homeowners enjoy stronger protections than ever before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So together, we have cleared away the rubble of crisis, and we can say with renewed confidence that the state of our Union is stronger.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we gather here knowing that there are millions of Americans whose hard work and dedication have not yet been rewarded.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our economy is adding jobs, but too many people still can't find full-time employment.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Corporate profits have skyrocketed to alltime highs, but for more than a decade, wages and incomes have barely budged.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is our generation's task, then, to reignite the true engine of America's economic growth: a rising, thriving middle class.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is our unfinished task to restore the basic bargain that built this country: the idea that if you work hard and meet your responsibilities, you can get ahead, no matter where you come from, no matter what you look like or who you love.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is our unfinished task to make sure that this Government works on behalf of the many, and not just the few;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that it encourages free enterprise, rewards individual initiative, and opens the doors of opportunity to every child across this great Nation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The American people don't expect government to solve every problem.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They don't expect those of us in this Chamber to agree on every issue.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But they do expect us to put the Nation's interests before party.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They do expect us to forge reasonable compromise where we can.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For they know that America moves forward only when we do so together and that the responsibility of improving this Union remains the task of us all.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, our work must begin by making some basic decisions about our budget, decisions that will have a huge impact on the strength of our recovery.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Over the last few years, both parties have worked together to reduce the deficit by more than $2.5 trillion, mostly through spending cuts, but also by raising tax rates on the wealthiest 1 percent of Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As a result, we are more than halfway towards the goal of $4 trillion in deficit reduction that economists say we need to stabilize our finances.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now we need to finish the job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And the question is, how?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In 2011, Congress passed a law saying that if both parties couldn't agree on a plan to reach our deficit goal, about a trillion dollars' worth of budget cuts would automatically go into effect this year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These sudden, harsh, arbitrary cuts would jeopardize our military readiness.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They'd devastate priorities like education and energy and medical research.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They would certainly slow our recovery and cost us hundreds of thousands of jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why Democrats, Republicans, business leaders, and economists have already said that these cuts-known here in Washington as the sequester-are a really bad idea.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, some in Congress have proposed preventing only the defense cuts by making even bigger cuts to things like education and job training, Medicare, and Social Security benefits.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That idea is even worse.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Yes, the biggest driver of our long-term debt is the rising cost of health care for an aging population.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And those of us who care deeply about programs like Medicare must embrace the need for modest reforms;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: otherwise, our retirement programs will crowd out the investments we need for our children and jeopardize the promise of a secure retirement for future generations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we can't ask senior citizens and working families to shoulder the entire burden of deficit reduction while asking nothing more from the wealthiest and the most powerful.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We won't grow the middle class simply by shifting the cost of health care or college onto families that are already struggling or by forcing communities to lay off more teachers and more cops and more firefighters.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Most Americans-Democrats, Republicans, and Independents-understand that we can't just cut our way to prosperity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They know that broad-based economic growth requires a balanced approach to deficit reduction, with spending cuts and revenue and with everybody doing their fair share.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's the approach I offer tonight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: On Medicare, I'm prepared to enact reforms that will achieve the same amount of health care savings by the beginning of the next decade as the reforms proposed by the bipartisan Simpson-Bowles Commission.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Already, the Affordable Care Act is helping to slow the growth of health care costs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And the reforms I'm proposing go even further.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll reduce taxpayer subsidies to prescription drug companies and ask more from the wealthiest seniors.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll bring down costs by changing the way our Government pays for Medicare, because our medical bills shouldn't be based on the number of tests ordered or days spent in the hospital;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: they should be based on the quality of care that our seniors receive.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I am open to additional reforms from both parties, so long as they don't violate the guarantee of a secure retirement.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our Government shouldn't make promises we cannot keep, but we must keep the promises we've already made.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To hit the rest of our deficit reduction target, we should do what leaders in both parties have already suggested and save hundreds of billions of dollars by getting rid of tax loopholes and deductions for the well-off and the well-connected.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After all, why would we choose to make deeper cuts to education and Medicare just to protect special interest tax breaks?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: How is that fair?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Why is it that deficit reduction is a big emergency justifying making cuts in Social Security benefits

speaker: Barack Obama
text: How does that promote growth?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now is our best chance for bipartisan, comprehensive tax reform that encourages job creation and helps bring down the deficit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can get this done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The American people deserve a Tax Code that helps small businesses spend less time filling out complicated forms and more time expanding and hiring;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: a Tax Code that ensures billionaires with high-powered accountants can't work the system and pay a lower rate than their hard-working secretaries;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: a Tax Code that lowers incentives to move jobs overseas and lowers tax rates for businesses and manufacturers that are creating jobs right here in the United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what tax reform can deliver.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what we can do together.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I realize that tax reform and entitlement reform will not be easy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The politics will be hard for both sides.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: None of us will get a hundred percent of what we want.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But the alternative will cost us jobs, hurt our economy, visit hardship on millions of hard-working Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's set party interests aside and work to pass a budget that replaces reckless cuts with smart savings and wise investments in our future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And let's do it without the brinksmanship that stresses consumers and scares off investors.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The greatest nation on Earth cannot keep conducting its business by drifting from one manufactured crisis to the next.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can't do it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's agree right here, right now to keep the people's Government open and pay our bills on time and always uphold the full faith and credit of the United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The American people have worked too hard, for too long, rebuilding from one crisis to see their elected officials cause another.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, most of us agree that a plan to reduce the deficit must be part of our agenda.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But let's be clear: Deficit reduction alone is not an economic plan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A growing economy that creates good, middle class jobs, that must be the north star that guides our efforts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Every day, we should ask ourselves three questions as a nation: How do we attract more jobs to our shores?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: How do we equip our people with the skills they need to get those jobs?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And how do we make sure that hard work leads to a decent living?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, a year and a half ago, I put forward an American Jobs Act that independent economists said would create more than 1 million new jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I thank the last Congress for passing some of that agenda.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I urge this Congress to pass the rest.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But tonight I'll lay out additional proposals that are fully paid for and fully consistent with the budget framework both parties agreed to just 18 months ago.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let me repeat: Nothing I'm proposing tonight should increase our deficit by a single dime.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is not a bigger Government we need, but a smarter Government that sets priorities and invests in broad-based growth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what we should be looking for.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our first priority is making America a magnet for new jobs and manufacturing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After shedding jobs for more than 10 years, our manufacturers have added about 500,000 jobs over the past 3.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Caterpillar is bringing jobs back from Japan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Ford is bringing jobs back from Mexico.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And this year, Apple will start making Macs in America again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There are things we can do right now to accelerate this trend.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last year, we created our first manufacturing innovation institute in Youngstown, Ohio.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A once-shuttered warehouse is now a state-of-the-art lab where new workers are mastering the 3-D printing that has the potential to revolutionize the way we make almost everything.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There's no reason this can't happen in other towns.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight I'm announcing the launch of three more of these manufacturing hubs, where businesses will partner with the Department of Defense and Energy to turn regions left behind by globalization into global centers of high-tech jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I ask this Congress to help create a network of 15 of these hubs and guarantee that the next revolution in manufacturing is made right here in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can get that done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, if we want to make the best products, we also have to invest in the best ideas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Every dollar we invested to map the human genome returned $140 to our economy-every dollar.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, our scientists are mapping the human brain to unlock the answers to Alzheimer's.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're developing drugs to regenerate damaged organs, devising new materials to make batteries 10 times more powerful.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now is not the time to gut these job-creating investments in science and innovation, now is the time to reach a level of research and development not seen since the height of the space race.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to make those investments.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, no area holds more promise than our investments in American energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After years of talking about it, we're finally poised to control our own energy future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We produce more oil at home than we have in 15 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have doubled the distance our cars will go on a gallon of gas and the amount of renewable energy we generate from sources like wind and solar, with tens of thousands of good American jobs to show for it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We produce more natural gas than ever before, and nearly everyone's energy bill is lower because of it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And over the last 4 years, our emissions of the dangerous carbon pollution that threatens our planet have actually fallen.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But for the sake of our children and our future, we must do more to combat climate change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, it's true that no single event makes a trend.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But the fact is, the 12 hottest years on record have all come in the last 15.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Heat waves, droughts, wildfires, floods-all are now more frequent and more intense.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can choose to believe that Superstorm Sandy and the most severe drought in decades and the worst wildfires some States have ever seen were all just a freak coincidence.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Or we can choose to believe in the overwhelming judgment of science and act before it's too late.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, the good news is we can make meaningful progress on this issue while driving strong economic growth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I urge this Congress to get together, pursue a bipartisan, market-based solution to climate change, like the one John McCain and Joe Lieberman worked on together a few years ago.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But if Congress won't act soon to protect future generations, I will.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I will direct my Cabinet to come up with executive actions we can take, now and in the future, to reduce pollution, prepare our communities for the consequences of climate change, and speed the transition to more sustainable sources of energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And 4 years ago, other countries dominated the clean energy market and the jobs that came with it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we've begun to change that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last year, wind energy added nearly half of all new power capacity in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's generate even more.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Solar energy gets cheaper by the year;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: let's drive down costs even further.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As long as countries like China keep going all in on clean energy, so must we.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, in the meantime, the natural gas boom has led to cleaner power and greater energy independence.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to encourage that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why my administration will keep cutting redtape and speeding up new oil and gas permits.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's got to be part of an all-of-the-above plan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I also want to work with this Congress to encourage the research and technology that helps natural gas burn even cleaner and protects our air and our water.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, much of our new-found energy is drawn from lands and waters that we, the public, own together.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight I propose we use some of our oil and gas revenues to fund an energy security trust that will drive new research and technology to shift our cars and trucks off oil for good.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If a nonpartisan coalition of CEOs and retired generals and admirals can get behind this idea, then so can we.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's take their advice and free our families and businesses from the painful spikes in gas prices we've put up with for far too long.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm also issuing a new goal for America: Let's cut in half the energy wasted by our homes and businesses over the next 20 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll work with the States to do it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Those States with the best ideas to create jobs and lower energy bills by constructing more efficient buildings will receive Federal support to help make that happen.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America's energy sector is just one part of an aging infrastructure badly in need of repair.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Ask any CEO where they'd rather locate and hire, a country with deteriorating roads and bridges or one with high-speed rail and Internet, high-tech schools, self-healing power grids.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The CEO of Siemens America-a company that brought hundreds of new jobs to North Carolina-said that if we upgrade our infrastructure, they'll bring even more jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's the attitude of a lot of companies all around the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I know you want these job-creating projects in your district.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've seen all those ribbon-cuttings.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight I propose a Fix-It-First program to put people to work as soon as possible on our most urgent repairs, like the nearly 70,000 structurally deficient bridges across the country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And to make sure taxpayers don't shoulder the whole burden, I'm also proposing a partnership to rebuild America that attracts private capital to upgrade what our businesses need most: modern ports to move our goods, modern pipelines to withstand a storm, modern schools worthy of our children.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's prove there's no better place to do business than here in the United States of America, and let's start right away.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can get this done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And part of our rebuilding effort must also involve our housing sector.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The good news is, our housing market is finally healing from the collapse of 2007.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Home prices are rising at the fastest pace in 6 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Home purchases are up nearly 50 percent, and construction is expanding again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But even with mortgage rates near a 50-year low, too many families with solid credit who want to buy a home are being rejected.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Too many families who never missed a payment and want to refinance are being told no.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's holding our entire economy back.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to fix it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Right now there's a bill in this Congress that would give every responsible homeowner in America the chance to save $3,000 a year by refinancing at today's rates.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Democrats and Republicans have supported it before, so what are we waiting for?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Take a vote and send me that bill.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Why are-why would we be against that?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Why would that be a partisan issue, helping folks refinance?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Right now overlapping regulations keep responsible young families from buying their first home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What's holding us back?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's streamline the process and help our economy grow.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These initiatives in manufacturing, energy, infrastructure, housing, all these things will help entrepreneurs and small-business owners expand and create new jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But none of it will matter unless we also equip our citizens with the skills and training to fill those jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that has to start at the earliest possible age.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Study after study shows that the sooner a child begins learning, the better he or she does down the road.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But today, fewer than 3 in 10 4-year-olds are enrolled in a high-quality preschool program.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Most middle class parents can't afford a few hundred bucks a week for a private preschool.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And for poor kids who need help the most, this lack of access to preschool education can shadow them for the rest of their lives.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight I propose working with States to make high-quality preschool available to every single child in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's something we should be able to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Every dollar we invest in high-quality early childhood education can save more than 7 dollars later on: by boosting graduation rates, reducing teen pregnancy, even reducing violent crime.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In States that make it a priority to educate our youngest children, like Georgia or Oklahoma, studies show students grow up more likely to read and do math at grade level, graduate high school, hold a job, form more stable families of their own.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We know this works.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's do what works and make sure none of our children start the race of life already behind.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's give our kids that chance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's also make sure that a high school diploma puts our kids on a path to a good job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Right now countries like Germany focus on graduating their high school students with the equivalent of a technical degree from one of our community colleges.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So those German kids, they're ready for a job when they graduate high school.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They've been trained for the jobs that are there.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now at schools like P-TECH in Brooklyn, a collaboration between New York Public Schools and City University of New York and IBM, students will graduate with a high school diploma and an associate's degree in computers or engineering.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to give every American student opportunities like this.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And 4 years ago, we started Race to the Top, a competition that convinced almost every State to develop smarter curricula and higher standards, all for about 1 percent of what we spend on education each year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight I'm announcing a new challenge to redesign America's high schools so they better equip graduates for the demands of a high-tech economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we'll reward schools that develop new partnerships with colleges and employers and create classes that focus on science, technology, engineering, and math: the skills today's employers are looking for to fill the jobs that are there right now and will be there in the future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, even with better high schools, most young people will need some higher education.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's a simple fact: The more education you've got, the more likely you are to have a good job and work your way into the middle class.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But today, skyrocketing costs price too many young people out of a higher education or saddle them with unsustainable debt.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Through tax credits, grants, and better loans, we've made college more affordable for millions of students and families over the last few years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But taxpayers can't keep on subsidizing higher and higher and higher costs for higher education.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Colleges must do their part to keep costs down, and it's our job to make sure that they do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight I ask Congress to change the Higher Education Act so that affordability and value are included in determining which colleges receive certain types of Federal aid.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tomorrow my administration will release a new college scorecard that parents and students can use to compare schools based on a simple criterion: where you can get the most bang for your educational buck.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, to grow our middle class, our citizens have to have access to the education and training that today's jobs require.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we also have to make sure that America remains a place where everyone who's willing to work-everybody who's willing to work hard-has the chance to get ahead.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our economy is stronger when we harness the talents and ingenuity of striving, hopeful immigrants.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And right now leaders from the business, labor, law enforcement, faith communities, they all agree that the time has come to pass comprehensive immigration reform.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now is the time to do it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now is the time to get it done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Applause] Now is the time to get it done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Real reform means stronger border security, and we can build on the progress my administration has already made: putting more boots on the southern border than at any time in our history and reducing illegal crossings to their lowest levels in 40 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Real reform means establishing a responsible pathway to earned citizenship, a path that includes passing a background check, paying taxes and a meaningful penalty, learning English, and going to the back of the line behind the folks trying to come here legally.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And real reform means fixing the legal immigration system to cut waiting periods and attract the highly skilled entrepreneurs and engineers that will help create jobs and grow our economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In other words, we know what needs to be done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as we speak, bipartisan groups in both Chambers are working diligently to draft a bill, and I applaud their efforts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's get this done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Send me a comprehensive immigration reform bill in the next few months, and I will sign it right away.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And America will be better for it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's get it done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Applause] Let's get it done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we can't stop there.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We know our economy is stronger when our wives, our mothers, our daughters can live their lives free from discrimination in the workplace and free from the fear of domestic violence.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today the Senate passed the "Violence Against Women's Act" that Joe Biden originally wrote almost 20 years ago.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I now urge the House to do the same.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Good job, Joe.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I ask this Congress to declare that women should earn a living equal to their efforts, and finally pass the ""Paycheck Fairness Act"" this year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We know our economy is stronger when we reward an honest day's work with honest wages.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But today, a full-time worker making the minimum wage earns $14,500 a year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Even with the tax relief we put in place, a family with two kids that earns the minimum wage still lives below the poverty line.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's wrong.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why, since the last time this Congress raised the minimum wage, 19 States have chosen to bump theirs even higher.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight let's declare that in the wealthiest nation on Earth, no one who works full-time should have to live in poverty and raise the Federal minimum wage to $9 an hour.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should be able to get that done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This single step would raise the incomes of millions of working families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It could mean the difference between groceries or the food bank, rent or eviction, scraping by or finally getting ahead.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For businesses across the country, it would mean customers with more money in their pockets.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And a whole lot of folks out there would probably need less help from government.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, working folks shouldn't have to wait year after year for the minimum wage to go up while CEO pay has never been higher.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So here's an idea that Governor Romney and I actually agreed on last year: Let's tie the minimum wage to the cost of living so that it finally becomes a wage you can live on.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight let's also recognize that there are communities in this country where no matter how hard you work, it is virtually impossible to get ahead: factory towns decimated from years of plants packing up;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: inescapable pockets of poverty, urban and rural, where young adults are still fighting for their first job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America is not a place where the chance of birth or circumstance should decide our destiny.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why we need to build new ladders of opportunity into the middle class for all who are willing to climb them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's offer incentives to companies that hire Americans who've got what it takes to fill that job opening, but have been out of work so long that no one will give them a chance anymore.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's put people back to work rebuilding vacant homes in rundown neighborhoods.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And this year, my administration will begin to partner with 20 of the hardest hit towns in America to get these communities back on their feet.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, we'll work with local leaders to target resources at public safety and education and housing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll give new tax credits to businesses that hire and invest.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we'll work to strengthen families by removing the financial deterrents to marriage for low-income couples and do more to encourage fatherhood, because what makes you a man isn't the ability to conceive a child, it's having the courage to raise one.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we want to encourage that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We want to help that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Stronger families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Stronger communities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A stronger America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is this kind of prosperity-broad, shared, built on a thriving middle class-that has always been the source of our progress at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's also the foundation of our power and influence throughout the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight we stand united in saluting the troops and civilians who sacrifice every day to protect us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because of them, we can say with confidence that America will complete its mission in Afghanistan and achieve our objective of defeating the core of Al Qaida.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Already, we have brought home 33,000 of our brave service men and women.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This spring, our forces will move into a support role, while Afghan security forces take the lead.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight I can announce that over the next year, another 34,000 American troops will come home from Afghanistan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This drawdown will continue, and by the end of next year, our war in Afghanistan will be over.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Beyond 2014, America's commitment to a unified and sovereign Afghanistan will endure, but the nature of our commitment will change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're negotiating an agreement with the Afghan Government that focuses on two missions: training and equipping Afghan forces so that the country does not again slip into chaos and counterterrorism efforts that allow us to pursue the remnants of Al Qaida and their affiliates.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, the organization that attacked us on 9/11 is a shadow of its former self.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's true, different Al Qaida affiliates and extremist groups have emerged, from the Arabian Peninsula to Africa.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The threat these groups pose is evolving.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But to meet this threat, we don't need to send tens of thousands of our sons and daughters abroad or occupy other nations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Instead, we'll need to help countries like Yemen and Libya and Somalia provide for their own security and help allies who take the fight to terrorists, as we have in Mali.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And where necessary, through a range of capabilities, we will continue to take direct action against those terrorists who pose the gravest threat to Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, as we do, we must enlist our values in the fight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why my administration has worked tirelessly to forge a durable legal and policy framework to guide our counterterrorism efforts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Throughout, we have kept Congress fully informed of our efforts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I recognize that in our democracy, no one should just take my word for it that we're doing things the right way.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So, in the months ahead, I will continue to engage Congress to ensure not only that our targeting, detention, and prosecution of terrorists remains consistent with our laws and system of checks and balances, but that our efforts are even more transparent to the American people and to the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, our challenges don't end with Al Qaida.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America will continue to lead the effort to prevent the spread of the world's most dangerous weapons.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The regime in North Korea must know they will only achieve security and prosperity by meeting their international obligations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Provocations of the sort we saw last night will only further isolate them, as we stand by our allies, strengthen our own missile defense, and lead the world in taking firm action in response to these threats.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Likewise, the leaders of Iran must recognize that now is the time for a diplomatic solution, because a coalition stands united in demanding that they meet their obligations, and we will do what is necessary to prevent them from getting a nuclear weapon.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At the same time, we'll engage Russia to seek further reductions in our nuclear arsenals and continue leading the global effort to secure nuclear materials that could fall into the wrong hands, because our ability to influence others depends on our willingness to lead and meet our obligations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America must also face the rapidly growing threat from cyber attacks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, we know hackers steal people's identities and infiltrate private e-mails.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We know foreign countries and companies swipe our corporate secrets.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now our enemies are also seeking the ability to sabotage our power grid, our financial institutions, our air traffic control systems.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We cannot look back years from now and wonder why we did nothing in the face of real threats to our security and our economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why, earlier today, I signed a new Executive order that will strengthen our cyber defenses by increasing information sharing and developing standards to protect our national security, our jobs, and our privacy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But now Congress must act as well, by passing legislation to give our Government a greater capacity to secure our networks and deter attacks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This is something we should be able to get done on a bipartisan basis.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, even as we protect our people, we should remember that today's world presents not just dangers, not just threats, it presents opportunities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To boost American exports, support American jobs and level the playing field in the growing markets of Asia, we intend to complete negotiations on a Trans-Pacific Partnership.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tonight I'm announcing that we will launch talks on a comprehensive transatlantic trade and investment partnership with the European Union, because trade that is fair and free across the Atlantic supports millions of good-paying American jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We also know that progress in the most impoverished parts of our world enriches us all, not only because it creates new markets, more stable order in certain regions of the world, but also because it's the right thing to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In many places, people live on little more than a dollar a day.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So the United States will join with our allies to eradicate such extreme poverty in the next two decades by connecting more people to the global economy, by empowering women, by giving our young and brightest minds new opportunities to serve and helping communities to feed and power and educate themselves, by saving the world's children from preventable deaths, and by realizing the promise of an AIDS-free generation, which is within our reach.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You see, America must remain a beacon to all who seek freedom during this period of historic change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I saw the power of hope last year in Rangoon, in Burma, when Aung San Suu Kyi welcomed an American President into the home where she had been imprisoned for years;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: when thousands of Burmese lined the streets, waving American flags, including a man who said: "There is justice and law in the United States.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want our country to be like that."

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In defense of freedom, we'll remain the anchor of strong alliances from the Americas to Africa, from Europe to Asia.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the Middle East, we will stand with citizens as they demand their universal rights and support stable transitions to democracy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We know the process will be messy, and we cannot presume to dictate the course of change in countries like Egypt, but we can and will insist on respect for the fundamental rights of all people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll keep the pressure on a Syrian regime that has murdered its own people and support opposition leaders that respect the rights of every Syrian.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we will stand steadfast with Israel in pursuit of security and a lasting peace.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These are the messages I'll deliver when I travel to the Middle East next month.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And all this work depends on the courage and sacrifice of those who serve in dangerous places at great personal risk: our diplomats, our intelligence officers, and the men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As long as I'm Commander in Chief, we will do whatever we must to protect those who serve their country abroad, and we will maintain the best military the world has ever known.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll invest in new capabilities, even as we reduce waste and wartime spending.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will ensure equal treatment for all servicemembers and equal benefits for their families, gay and straight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will draw upon the courage and skills of our sisters and daughters and moms, because women have proven under fire that they are ready for combat.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will keep faith with our veterans, investing in world-class care-including mental health care-for our wounded warriors, supporting our military families, giving our veterans the benefits and education and job opportunities that they have earned.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I want to thank my wife Michelle and Dr. Jill Biden for their continued dedication to serving our military families as well as they have served us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thank you, honey.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thank you, Jill.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Defending our freedom, though, is not just the job of our military alone.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We must all do our part to make sure our God-given rights are protected here at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That includes one of the most fundamental rights of a democracy: the right to vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, when any American, no matter where they live or what their party, are denied that right because they can't afford to wait for 5 or 6 or 7 hours just to cast their ballot, we are betraying our ideals.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight I'm announcing a nonpartisan commission to improve the voting experience in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it definitely needs improvement.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm asking two long-time experts in the field-who, by the way, recently served as the top attorneys for my campaign and for Governor Romney's campaign-to lead it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can fix this, and we will.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The American people demand it, and so does our democracy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, what I've said tonight matters little if we don't come together to protect our most precious resource: our children.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It has been 2 months since Newtown.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know this is not the first time this country has debated how to reduce gun violence.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But this time is different.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Overwhelming majorities of Americans-Americans who believe in the Second Amendment-have come together around commonsense reform, like background checks that will make it harder for criminals to get their hands on a gun.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Senators of both parties are working together on tough new laws to prevent anyone from buying guns for resale to criminals.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Police chiefs are asking our help to get weapons of war and massive ammunition magazines off our streets, because these police chiefs, they're tired of seeing their guys and gals being outgunned.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Each of these proposals deserves a vote in Congress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, if you want to vote no, that's your choice.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But these proposals deserve a vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because in the 2 months since Newtown, more than a thousand birthdays, graduations, anniversaries have been stolen from our lives by a bullet from a gun-more than a thousand.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: One of those we lost was a young girl named Hadiya Pendleton.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She was 15 years old.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She loved Fig Newtons and lip gloss.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She was a majorette.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She was so good to her friends, they all thought they were her best friend.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Just 3 weeks ago, she was here, in Washington, with her classmates, performing for her country at my Inauguration.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And a week later, she was shot and killed in a Chicago park after school, just a mile away from my house.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Hadiya's parents, Nate and Cleo, are in this Chamber tonight, along with more than two dozen Americans whose lives have been torn apart by gun violence.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They deserve a vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They deserve a vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: [Applause] They deserve a vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Gabby Giffords deserves a vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The families of Newtown deserve a vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The families of Aurora deserve a vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The families of Oak Creek and Tucson and Blacksburg, and the countless other communities ripped open by gun violence, they deserve a simple vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They deserve a simple vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our actions will not prevent every senseless act of violence in this country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, no laws, no initiatives, no administrative acts will perfectly solve all the challenges I've outlined tonight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we were never sent here to be perfect.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We were sent here to make what difference we can, to secure this Nation, expand opportunity, uphold our ideals through the hard, often frustrating, but absolutely necessary work of self-government.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We were sent here to look out for our fellow Americans the same way they look out for one another, every single day, usually without fanfare, all across this country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should follow their example.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should follow the example of a New York City nurse named Menchu Sanchez.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When Hurricane Sandy plunged her hospital into darkness, she wasn't thinking about how her own home was faring.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Her mind was on the 20 precious newborns in her care and the rescue plan she devised that kept them all safe.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should follow the example of a North Miami woman named Desiline Victor.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When Desiline arrived at her polling place, she was told the wait to vote might be 6 hours.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as time ticked by, her concern was not with her tired body or aching feet, but whether folks like her would get to have their say.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And hour after hour, a throng of people stayed in line to support her, because Desiline is 102 years old.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And they erupted in cheers when she finally put on a sticker that read, "I voted." [Applause] There's Desiline.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should follow the example of a police officer named Brian Murphy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When a gunman opened fire on a Sikh temple in Wisconsin and Brian was the first to arrive-and he did not consider his own safety.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: He fought back until help arrived and ordered his fellow officers to protect the safety of the Americans worshiping inside, even as he lay bleeding from 12 bullet wounds.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And when asked how he did that, Brian said, "That's just the way we're made."

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's just the way we're made.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We may do different jobs and wear different uniforms and hold different views than the person beside us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But as Americans, we all share the same proud title: We are citizens.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's a word that doesn't just describe our nationality or legal status.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It describes the way we're made.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It describes what we believe.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It captures the enduring idea that this country only works when we accept certain obligations to one another and to future generations;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that our rights are wrapped up in the rights of others;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: and that well into our third century as a nation, it remains the task of us all, as citizens of these United States, to be the authors of the next great chapter of our American story.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thank you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: God bless you, and God bless these United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. Vice President, Members of Congress, my fellow Americans:Today in America, a teacher spent extra time with a student who needed it, and did her part to lift America's graduation rate to its highest level in more than three decades.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: An entrepreneur flipped on the lights in her tech startup, and did her part to add to the more than eight million new jobs our businesses have created over the past four years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: An autoworker fine-tuned some of the best, most fuel-efficient cars in the world, and did his part to help America wean itself off foreign oil.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A farmer prepared for the spring after the strongest five-year stretch of farm exports in our history.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A rural doctor gave a young child the first prescription to treat asthma that his mother could afford.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A man took the bus home from the graveyard shift, bone-tired but dreaming big dreams for his son.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in tight-knit communities across America, fathers and mothers will tuck in their kids, put an arm around their spouse, remember fallen comrades, and give thanks for being home from a war that, after twelve long years, is finally coming to an end.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight, this chamber speaks with one voice to the people we represent: it is you, our citizens, who make the state of our union strong.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Here are the results of your efforts: The lowest unemployment rate in over five years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A rebounding housing market.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A manufacturing sector that's adding jobs for the first time since the 1990s.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More oil produced at home than we buy from the rest of the world , the first time that's happened in nearly twenty years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our deficits , cut by more than half.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And for the first time in over a decade, business leaders around the world have declared that China is no longer the world's number one place to invest;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America is.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why I believe this can be a breakthrough year for America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After five years of grit and determined effort, the United States is better-positioned for the 21st century than any other nation on Earth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The question for everyone in this chamber, running through every decision we make this year, is whether we are going to help or hinder this progress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For several years now, this town has been consumed by a rancorous argument over the proper size of the federal government.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's an important debate , one that dates back to our very founding.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But when that debate prevents us from carrying out even the most basic functions of our democracy , when our differences shut down government or threaten the full faith and credit of the United States , then we are not doing right by the American people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As President, I'm committed to making Washington work better, and rebuilding the trust of the people who sent us here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I believe most of you are, too.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last month, thanks to the work of Democrats and Republicans, this Congress finally produced a budget that undoes some of last year's severe cuts to priorities like education.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Nobody got everything they wanted, and we can still do more to invest in this country's future while bringing down our deficit in a balanced way.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But the budget compromise should leave us freer to focus on creating new jobs, not creating new crises.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the coming months, let's see where else we can make progress together.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's make this a year of action.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what most Americans want , for all of us in this chamber to focus on their lives, their hopes, their aspirations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And what I believe unites the people of this nation, regardless of race or region or party, young or old, rich or poor, is the simple, profound belief in opportunity for all , the notion that if you work hard and take responsibility, you can get ahead.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's face it: that belief has suffered some serious blows.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Over more than three decades, even before the Great Recession hit, massive shifts in technology and global competition had eliminated a lot of good, middle-class jobs, and weakened the economic foundations that families depend on.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, after four years of economic growth, corporate profits and stock prices have rarely been higher, and those at the top have never done better.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But average wages have barely budged.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Inequality has deepened.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Upward mobility has stalled.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The cold, hard fact is that even in the midst of recovery, too many Americans are working more than ever just to get by , let alone get ahead.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And too many still aren't working at all.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our job is to reverse these trends.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It won't happen right away, and we won't agree on everything.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But what I offer tonight is a set of concrete, practical proposals to speed up growth, strengthen the middle class, and build new ladders of opportunity into the middle class.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some require Congressional action, and I'm eager to work with all of you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But America does not stand still , and neither will I. So wherever and whenever I can take steps without legislation to expand opportunity for more American families, that's what I'm going to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As usual, our First Lady sets a good example.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Michelle's Let's Move partnership with schools, businesses, and local leaders has helped bring down childhood obesity rates for the first time in thirty years , an achievement that will improve lives and reduce health care costs for decades to come.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The Joining Forces alliance that Michelle and Jill Biden launched has already encouraged employers to hire or train nearly 400,000 veterans and military spouses.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Taking a page from that playbook, the White House just organized a College Opportunity Summit where already, 150 universities, businesses, and nonprofits have made concrete commitments to reduce inequality in access to higher education , and help every hardworking kid go to college and succeed when they get to campus.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Across the country, we're partnering with mayors, governors, and state legislatures on issues from homelessness to marriage equality.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The point is, there are millions of Americans outside Washington who are tired of stale political arguments, and are moving this country forward.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They believe, and I believe, that here in America, our success should depend not on accident of birth, but the strength of our work ethic and the scope of our dreams.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what drew our forebears here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's how the daughter of a factory worker is CEO of America's largest automaker;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: how the son of a barkeeper is Speaker of the House;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: how the son of a single mom can be President of the greatest nation on Earth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Opportunity is who we are.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And the defining project of our generation is to restore that promise.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We know where to start: the best measure of opportunity is access to a good job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With the economy picking up speed, companies say they intend to hire more people this year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And over half of big manufacturers say they're thinking of insourcing jobs from abroad.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's make that decision easier for more companies.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Both Democrats and Republicans have argued that our tax code is riddled with wasteful, complicated loopholes that punish businesses investing here, and reward companies that keep profits abroad.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's flip that equation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's work together to close those loopholes, end those incentives to ship jobs overseas, and lower tax rates for businesses that create jobs here at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Moreover, we can take the money we save with this transition to tax reform to create jobs rebuilding our roads, upgrading our ports, unclogging our commutes , because in today's global economy, first-class jobs gravitate to first-class infrastructure.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll need Congress to protect more than three million jobs by finishing transportation and waterways bills this summer.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I will act on my own to slash bureaucracy and streamline the permitting process for key projects, so we can get more construction workers on the job as fast as possible.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We also have the chance, right now, to beat other countries in the race for the next wave of high-tech manufacturing jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My administration has launched two hubs for high-tech manufacturing in Raleigh and Youngstown, where we've connected businesses to research universities that can help America lead the world in advanced technologies.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight, I'm announcing we'll launch six more this year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Bipartisan bills in both houses could double the number of these hubs and the jobs they create.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So get those bills to my desk and put more Americans back to work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's do more to help the entrepreneurs and small business owners who create most new jobs in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Over the past five years, my administration has made more loans to small business owners than any other.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And when ninety-eight percent of our exporters are small businesses, new trade partnerships with Europe and the Asia-Pacific will help them create more jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to work together on tools like bipartisan trade promotion authority to protect our workers, protect our environment, and open new markets to new goods stamped  Made in the USA.  China and Europe aren't standing on the sidelines.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Neither should we.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We know that the nation that goes all-in on innovation today will own the global economy tomorrow.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This is an edge America cannot surrender.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Federally-funded research helped lead to the ideas and inventions behind Google and smartphones.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why Congress should undo the damage done by last year's cuts to basic research so we can unleash the next great American discovery , whether it's vaccines that stay ahead of drug-resistant bacteria, or paper-thin material that's stronger than steel.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And let's pass a patent reform bill that allows our businesses to stay focused on innovation, not costly, needless litigation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, one of the biggest factors in bringing more jobs back is our commitment to American energy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The all-of-the-above energy strategy I announced a few years ago is working, and today, America is closer to energy independence than we've been in decades.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: One of the reasons why is natural gas , if extracted safely, it's the bridge fuel that can power our economy with less of the carbon pollution that causes climate change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Businesses plan to invest almost $100 billion in new factories that use natural gas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'll cut red tape to help states get those factories built, and this Congress can help by putting people to work building fueling stations that shift more cars and trucks from foreign oil to American natural gas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My administration will keep working with the industry to sustain production and job growth while strengthening protection of our air, our water, and our communities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And while we're at it, I'll use my authority to protect more of our pristine federal lands for future generations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's not just oil and natural gas production that's booming;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: we're becoming a global leader in solar, too.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Every four minutes, another American home or business goes solar;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: every panel pounded into place by a worker whose job can't be outsourced.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's continue that progress with a smarter tax policy that stops giving $4 billion a year to fossil fuel industries that don't need it, so that we can invest more in fuels of the future that do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And even as we've increased energy production, we've partnered with businesses, builders, and local communities to reduce the energy we consume.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When we rescued our automakers, for example, we worked with them to set higher fuel efficiency standards for our cars.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the coming months, I'll build on that success by setting new standards for our trucks, so we can keep driving down oil imports and what we pay at the pump.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Taken together, our energy policy is creating jobs and leading to a cleaner, safer planet.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Over the past eight years, the United States has reduced our total carbon pollution more than any other nation on Earth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we have to act with more urgency , because a changing climate is already harming western communities struggling with drought, and coastal cities dealing with floods.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why I directed my administration to work with states, utilities, and others to set new standards on the amount of carbon pollution our power plants are allowed to dump into the air.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The shift to a cleaner energy economy won't happen overnight, and it will require tough choices along the way.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But the debate is settled.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Climate change is a fact.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And when our children's children look us in the eye and ask if we did all we could to leave them a safer, more stable world, with new sources of energy, I want us to be able to say yes, we did.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Finally, if we are serious about economic growth, it is time to heed the call of business leaders, labor leaders, faith leaders, and law enforcement , and fix our broken immigration system.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Republicans and Democrats in the Senate have acted.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know that members of both parties in the House want to do the same.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Independent economists say immigration reform will grow our economy and shrink our deficits by almost $1 trillion in the next two decades.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And for good reason: when people come here to fulfill their dreams , to study, invent, and contribute to our culture , they make our country a more attractive place for businesses to locate and create jobs for everyone.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's get immigration reform done this year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The ideas I've outlined so far can speed up growth and create more jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But in this rapidly-changing economy, we have to make sure that every American has the skills to fill those jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The good news is, we know how to do it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Two years ago, as the auto industry came roaring back, Andra Rush opened up a manufacturing firm in Detroit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She knew that Ford needed parts for the best-selling truck in America, and she knew how to make them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She just needed the workforce.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So she dialed up what we call an American Job Center , places where folks can walk in to get the help or training they need to find a new job, or better job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She was flooded with new workers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And today, Detroit Manufacturing Systems has more than 700 employees.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What Andra and her employees experienced is how it should be for every employer , and every job seeker.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight, I've asked Vice President Biden to lead an across-the-board reform of America's training programs to make sure they have one mission: train Americans with the skills employers need, and match them to good jobs that need to be filled right now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That means more on-the-job training, and more apprenticeships that set a young worker on an upward trajectory for life.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It means connecting companies to community colleges that can help design training to fill their specific needs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if Congress wants to help, you can concentrate funding on proven programs that connect more ready-to-work Americans with ready-to-be-filled jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'm also convinced we can help Americans return to the workforce faster by reforming unemployment insurance so that it's more effective in today's economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But first, this Congress needs to restore the unemployment insurance you just let expire for 1.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: 6 million people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let me tell you why.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Misty DeMars is a mother of two young boys.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She'd been steadily employed since she was a teenager.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She put herself through college.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She'd never collected unemployment benefits.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In May, she and her husband used their life savings to buy their first home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A week later, budget cuts claimed the job she loved.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last month, when their unemployment insurance was cut off, she sat down and wrote me a letter , the kind I get every day.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are the face of the unemployment crisis,  she wrote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I am not dependent on the government

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Please give us this chance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Congress, give these hardworking, responsible Americans that chance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They need our help, but more important, this country needs them in the game.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why I've been asking CEOs to give more long-term unemployed workers a fair shot at that new job and new chance to support their families;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: this week, many will come to the White House to make that commitment real.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight, I ask every business leader in America to join us and to do the same , because we are stronger when America fields a full team.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, it's not enough to train today's workforce.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We also have to prepare tomorrow's workforce, by guaranteeing every child access to a world-class education.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Estiven Rodriguez couldn't speak a word of English when he moved to New York City at age nine.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But last month, thanks to the support of great teachers and an innovative tutoring program, he led a march of his classmates , through a crowd of cheering parents and neighbors , from their high school to the post office, where they mailed off their college applications.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And this son of a factory worker just found out he's going to college this fall.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Five years ago, we set out to change the odds for all our kids.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We worked with lenders to reform student loans, and today, more young people are earning college degrees than ever before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Race to the Top, with the help of governors from both parties, has helped states raise expectations and performance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Teachers and principals in schools from Tennessee to Washington, D.C. are making big strides in preparing students with skills for the new economy , problem solving, critical thinking, science, technology, engineering, and math.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some of this change is hard.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It requires everything from more challenging curriculums and more demanding parents to better support for teachers and new ways to measure how well our kids think, not how well they can fill in a bubble on a test.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But it's worth it , and it's working.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The problem is we're still not reaching enough kids, and we're not reaching them in time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That has to change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Research shows that one of the best investments we can make in a child's life is high-quality early education.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last year, I asked this Congress to help states make high-quality pre-K available to every four year-old.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As a parent as well as a President, I repeat that request tonight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But in the meantime, thirty states have raised pre-k funding on their own.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They know we can't wait.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So just as we worked with states to reform our schools, this year, we'll invest in new partnerships with states and communities across the country in a race to the top for our youngest children.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as Congress decides what it's going to do, I'm going to pull together a coalition of elected officials, business leaders, and philanthropists willing to help more kids access the high-quality pre-K they need.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last year, I also pledged to connect 99 percent of our students to high-speed broadband over the next four years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight, I can announce that with the support of the FCC and companies like Apple, Microsoft, Sprint, and Verizon, we've got a down payment to start connecting more than 15,000 schools and twenty million students over the next two years, without adding a dime to the deficit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're working to redesign high schools and partner them with colleges and employers that offer the real-world education and hands-on training that can lead directly to a job and career.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're shaking up our system of higher education to give parents more information, and colleges more incentives to offer better value, so that no middle-class kid is priced out of a college education.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're offering millions the opportunity to cap their monthly student loan payments to ten percent of their income, and I want to work with Congress to see how we can help even more Americans who feel trapped by student loan debt.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I'm reaching out to some of America's leading foundations and corporations on a new initiative to help more young men of color facing tough odds stay on track and reach their full potential.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The bottom line is, Michelle and I want every child to have the same chance this country gave us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we know our opportunity agenda won't be complete , and too many young people entering the workforce today will see the American Dream as an empty promise , unless we do more to make sure our economy honors the dignity of work, and hard work pays off for every single American.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, women make up about half our workforce.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But they still make 77 cents for every dollar a man earns.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is wrong, and in 2014, it's an embarrassment.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A woman deserves equal pay for equal work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She deserves to have a baby without sacrificing her job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A mother deserves a day off to care for a sick child or sick parent without running into hardship , and you know what, a father does, too.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's time to do away with workplace policies that belong in a  Mad Men  episode.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This year, let's all come together , Congress, the White House, and businesses from Wall Street to Main Street , to give every woman the opportunity she deserves.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because I firmly believe when women succeed, America succeeds.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, women hold a majority of lower-wage jobs , but they're not the only ones stifled by stagnant wages.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Americans understand that some people will earn more than others, and we don't resent those who, by virtue of their efforts, achieve incredible success.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But Americans overwhelmingly agree that no one who works full time should ever have to raise a family in poverty.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the year since I asked this Congress to raise the minimum wage, five states have passed laws to raise theirs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Many businesses have done it on their own.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Nick Chute is here tonight with his boss, John Soranno.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: John's an owner of Punch Pizza in Minneapolis, and Nick helps make the dough.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Only now he makes more of it: John just gave his employees a raise, to ten bucks an hour , a decision that eased their financial stress and boosted their morale.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight, I ask more of America's business leaders to follow John's lead and do what you can to raise your employees' wages.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To every mayor, governor, and state legislator in America, I say, you don't have to wait for Congress to act;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Americans will support you if you take this on.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as a chief executive, I intend to lead by example.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Profitable corporations like Costco see higher wages as the smart way to boost productivity and reduce turnover.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should too.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the coming weeks, I will issue an Executive Order requiring federal contractors to pay their federally-funded employees a fair wage of at least $10.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: 10 an hour , because if you cook our troops' meals or wash their dishes, you shouldn't have to live in poverty.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, to reach millions more, Congress needs to get on board.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, the federal minimum wage is worth about twenty percent less than it was when Ronald Reagan first stood here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tom Harkin and George Miller have a bill to fix that by lifting the minimum wage to $10.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This will help families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It will give businesses customers with more money to spend.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It doesn't involve any new bureaucratic program.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So join the rest of the country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Say yes.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Give America a raise.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There are other steps we can take to help families make ends meet, and few are more effective at reducing inequality and helping families pull themselves up through hard work than the Earned Income Tax Credit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Right now, it helps about half of all parents at some point.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I agree with Republicans like Senator Rubio that it doesn't do enough for single workers who don't have kids.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's work together to strengthen the credit, reward work, and help more Americans get ahead.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's do more to help Americans save for retirement.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, most workers don't have a pension.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A Social Security check often isn't enough on its own.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And while the stock market has doubled over the last five years, that doesn't help folks who don't have 401ks.

speaker: Barack Obama
