text: That's why, tomorrow, I will direct the Treasury to create a new way for working Americans to start their own retirement savings: MyRA. It's a new savings bond that encourages folks to build a nest egg.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: MyRA guarantees a decent return with no risk of losing what you put in.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if this Congress wants to help, work with me to fix an upside-down tax code that gives big tax breaks to help the wealthy save, but does little to nothing for middle-class Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Offer every American access to an automatic IRA on the job, so they can save at work just like everyone in this chamber can.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And since the most important investment many families make is their home, send me legislation that protects taxpayers from footing the bill for a housing crisis ever again, and keeps the dream of homeownership alive for future generations of Americans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: One last point on financial security.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For decades, few things exposed hard-working families to economic hardship more than a broken health care system.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in case you haven't heard, we're in the process of fixing that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A pre-existing condition used to mean that someone like Amanda Shelley, a physician assistant and single mom from Arizona, couldn't get health insurance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But on January 1st, she got covered.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: On January 3rd, she felt a sharp pain.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: On January 6th, she had emergency surgery.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Just one week earlier, Amanda said, that surgery would've meant bankruptcy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what health insurance reform is all about , the peace of mind that if misfortune strikes, you don't have to lose everything.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Already, because of the Affordable Care Act, more than three million Americans under age 26 have gained coverage under their parents' plans.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More than nine million Americans have signed up for private health insurance or Medicaid coverage.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And here's another number: zero.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because of this law, no American can ever again be dropped or denied coverage for a preexisting condition like asthma, back pain, or cancer.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No woman can ever be charged more just because she's a woman.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we did all this while adding years to Medicare's finances, keeping Medicare premiums flat, and lowering prescription costs for millions of seniors.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, I don't expect to convince my Republican friends on the merits of this law.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I know that the American people aren't interested in refighting old battles.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So again, if you have specific plans to cut costs, cover more people, and increase choice , tell America what you'd do differently.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's see if the numbers add up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But let's not have another forty-something votes to repeal a law that's already helping millions of Americans like Amanda.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The first forty were plenty.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We got it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We all owe it to the American people to say what we're for, not just what we're against.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if you want to know the real impact this law is having, just talk to Governor Steve Beshear of Kentucky, who's here tonight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Kentucky's not the most liberal part of the country, but he's like a man possessed when it comes to covering his commonwealth's families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They are our friends and neighbors,  he said.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They are people we shop and go to church with

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No one deserves to live that way.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Steve's right.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why, tonight, I ask every American who knows someone without health insurance to help them get covered by March 31st.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Moms, get on your kids to sign up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Kids, call your mom and walk her through the application.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It will give her some peace of mind , plus, she'll appreciate hearing from you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After all, that's the spirit that has always moved this nation forward.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the spirit of citizenship , the recognition that through hard work and responsibility, we can pursue our individual dreams, but still come together as one American family to make sure the next generation can pursue its dreams as well.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Citizenship means standing up for everyone's right to vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last year, part of the Voting Rights Act was weakened.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But conservative Republicans and liberal Democrats are working together to strengthen it;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: and the bipartisan commission I appointed last year has offered reforms so that no one has to wait more than a half hour to vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's support these efforts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It should be the power of our vote, not the size of our bank account, that drives our democracy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Citizenship means standing up for the lives that gun violence steals from us each day.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I have seen the courage of parents, students, pastors, and police officers all over this country who say  we are not afraid,  and I intend to keep trying, with or without Congress, to help stop more tragedies from visiting innocent Americans in our movie theaters, shopping malls, or schools like Sandy Hook.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Citizenship demands a sense of common cause;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: participation in the hard work of self-government;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: an obligation to serve to our communities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I know this chamber agrees that few Americans give more to their country than our diplomats and the men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight, because of the extraordinary troops and civilians who risk and lay down their lives to keep us free, the United States is more secure.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When I took office, nearly 180,000 Americans were serving in Iraq and Afghanistan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, all our troops are out of Iraq.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More than 60,000 of our troops have already come home from Afghanistan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With Afghan forces now in the lead for their own security, our troops have moved to a support role.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Together with our allies, we will complete our mission there by the end of this year, and America's longest war will finally be over.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: After 2014, we will support a unified Afghanistan as it takes responsibility for its own future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If the Afghan government signs a security agreement that we have negotiated, a small force of Americans could remain in Afghanistan with NATO allies to carry out two narrow missions: training and assisting Afghan forces, and counterterrorism operations to pursue any remnants of al Qaeda.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For while our relationship with Afghanistan will change, one thing will not: our resolve that terrorists do not launch attacks against our country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The fact is, that danger remains.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: While we have put al Qaeda's core leadership on a path to defeat, the threat has evolved, as al Qaeda affiliates and other extremists take root in different parts of the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In Yemen, Somalia, Iraq, and Mali, we have to keep working with partners to disrupt and disable these networks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In Syria, we'll support the opposition that rejects the agenda of terrorist networks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Here at home, we'll keep strengthening our defenses, and combat new threats like cyberattacks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as we reform our defense budget, we have to keep faith with our men and women in uniform, and invest in the capabilities they need to succeed in future missions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have to remain vigilant.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I strongly believe our leadership and our security cannot depend on our military alone.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As Commander-in-Chief, I have used force when needed to protect the American people, and I will never hesitate to do so as long as I hold this office.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I will not send our troops into harm's way unless it's truly necessary;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: nor will I allow our sons and daughters to be mired in open-ended conflicts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We must fight the battles that need to be fought, not those that terrorists prefer from us , large-scale deployments that drain our strength and may ultimately feed extremism.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So, even as we aggressively pursue terrorist networks , through more targeted efforts and by building the capacity of our foreign partners , America must move off a permanent war footing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why I've imposed prudent limits on the use of drones , for we will not be safer if people abroad believe we strike within their countries without regard for the consequence.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why, working with this Congress, I will reform our surveillance programs , because the vital work of our intelligence community depends on public confidence, here and abroad, that the privacy of ordinary people is not being violated.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And with the Afghan war ending, this needs to be the year Congress lifts the remaining restrictions on detainee transfers and we close the prison at Guantanamo Bay , because we counter terrorism not just through intelligence and military action, but by remaining true to our Constitutional ideals, and setting an example for the rest of the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You see, in a world of complex threats, our security and leadership depends on all elements of our power , including strong and principled diplomacy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: American diplomacy has rallied more than fifty countries to prevent nuclear materials from falling into the wrong hands, and allowed us to reduce our own reliance on Cold War stockpiles.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: American diplomacy, backed by the threat of force, is why Syria's chemical weapons are being eliminated, and we will continue to work with the international community to usher in the future the Syrian people deserve , a future free of dictatorship, terror and fear.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As we speak, American diplomacy is supporting Israelis and Palestinians as they engage in difficult but necessary talks to end the conflict there;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: to achieve dignity and an independent state for Palestinians, and lasting peace and security for the State of Israel , a Jewish state that knows America will always be at their side.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it is American diplomacy, backed by pressure, that has halted the progress of Iran's nuclear program , and rolled parts of that program back , for the very first time in a decade.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As we gather here tonight, Iran has begun to eliminate its stockpile of higher levels of enriched uranium.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is not installing advanced centrifuges.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Unprecedented inspections help the world verify, every day, that Iran is not building a bomb.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And with our allies and partners, we're engaged in negotiations to see if we can peacefully achieve a goal we all share: preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These negotiations will be difficult.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They may not succeed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are clear-eyed about Iran's support for terrorist organizations like Hezbollah, which threaten our allies;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: and the mistrust between our nations cannot be wished away.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But these negotiations do not rely on trust;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: any long-term deal we agree to must be based on verifiable action that convinces us and the international community that Iran is not building a nuclear bomb.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If John F. Kennedy and Ronald Reagan could negotiate with the Soviet Union, then surely a strong and confident America can negotiate with less powerful adversaries today.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The sanctions that we put in place helped make this opportunity possible.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But let me be clear: if this Congress sends me a new sanctions bill now that threatens to derail these talks, I will veto it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For the sake of our national security, we must give diplomacy a chance to succeed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If Iran's leaders do not seize this opportunity, then I will be the first to call for more sanctions, and stand ready to exercise all options to make sure Iran does not build a nuclear weapon.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But if Iran's leaders do seize the chance, then Iran could take an important step to rejoin the community of nations, and we will have resolved one of the leading security challenges of our time without the risks of war.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Finally, let's remember that our leadership is defined not just by our defense against threats, but by the enormous opportunities to do good and promote understanding around the globe , to forge greater cooperation, to expand new markets, to free people from fear and want.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And no one is better positioned to take advantage of those opportunities than America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our alliance with Europe remains the strongest the world has ever known.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: From Tunisia to Burma, we're supporting those who are willing to do the hard work of building democracy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In Ukraine, we stand for the principle that all people have the right to express themselves freely and peacefully, and have a say in their country's future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Across Africa, we're bringing together businesses and governments to double access to electricity and help end extreme poverty.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the Americas, we are building new ties of commerce, but we're also expanding cultural and educational exchanges among young people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we will continue to focus on the Asia-Pacific, where we support our allies, shape a future of greater security and prosperity, and extend a hand to those devastated by disaster , as we did in the Philippines, when our Marines and civilians rushed to aid those battered by a typhoon, and were greeted with words like,  We will never forget your kindness  and  God bless America!

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We do these things because they help promote our long-term security.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we do them because we believe in the inherent dignity and equality of every human being, regardless of race or religion, creed or sexual orientation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And next week, the world will see one expression of that commitment , when Team USA marches the red, white, and blue into the Olympic Stadium , and brings home the gold.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My fellow Americans, no other country in the world does what we do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: On every issue, the world turns to us, not simply because of the size of our economy or our military might , but because of the ideals we stand for, and the burdens we bear to advance them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No one knows this better than those who serve in uniform.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As this time of war draws to a close, a new generation of heroes returns to civilian life.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll keep slashing that backlog so our veterans receive the benefits they've earned, and our wounded warriors receive the health care , including the mental health care , that they need.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We'll keep working to help all our veterans translate their skills and leadership into jobs here at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we all continue to join forces to honor and support our remarkable military families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let me tell you about one of those families I've come to know.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I first met Cory Remsburg, a proud Army Ranger, at Omaha Beach on the 65th anniversary of D-Day.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Along with some of his fellow Rangers, he walked me through the program , a strong, impressive young man, with an easy manner, sharp as a tack.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We joked around, and took pictures, and I told him to stay in touch.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A few months later, on his tenth deployment, Cory was nearly killed by a massive roadside bomb in Afghanistan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: His comrades found him in a canal, face down, underwater, shrapnel in his brain.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For months, he lay in a coma.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The next time I met him, in the hospital, he couldn't speak;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: he could barely move.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Over the years, he's endured dozens of surgeries and procedures, and hours of grueling rehab every day.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Even now, Cory is still blind in one eye.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: He still struggles on his left side.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But slowly, steadily, with the support of caregivers like his dad Craig, and the community around him, Cory has grown stronger.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Day by day, he's learned to speak again and stand again and walk again , and he's working toward the day when he can serve his country again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My recovery has not been easy,  he says.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Nothing in life that's worth anything is easy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Cory is here tonight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And like the Army he loves, like the America he serves, Sergeant First Class Cory Remsburg never gives up, and he does not quit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My fellow Americans, men and women like Cory remind us that America has never come easy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our freedom, our democracy, has never been easy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Sometimes we stumble;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: we make mistakes;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: we get frustrated or discouraged.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But for more than two hundred years, we have put those things aside and placed our collective shoulder to the wheel of progress , to create and build and expand the possibilities of individual achievement;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: to free other nations from tyranny and fear;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: to promote justice, and fairness, and equality under the law, so that the words set to paper by our founders are made real for every citizen.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The America we want for our kids , a rising America where honest work is plentiful and communities are strong;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: where prosperity is widely shared and opportunity for all lets us go as far as our dreams and toil will take us , none of it is easy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But if we work together;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: if we summon what is best in us, with our feet planted firmly in today but our eyes cast towards tomorrow , I know it's within our reach.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Believe it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: God bless you, and God bless the United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: THE PRESIDENT:  Mr. Speaker, Mr. Vice President, Members of Congress, my fellow Americans: We are 15 years into this new century.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Fifteen years that dawned with terror touching our shores;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that unfolded with a new generation fighting two long and costly wars;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that saw a vicious recession spread across our nation and the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It has been, and still is, a hard time for many.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But tonight, we turn the page.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight, after a breakthrough year for America, our economy is growing and creating jobs at the fastest pace since 1999.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our unemployment rate is now lower than it was before the financial crisis.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More of our kids are graduating than ever before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More of our people are insured than ever before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we are as free from the grip of foreign oil as we've been in almost 30 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight, for the first time since 9/11, our combat mission in Afghanistan is over.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Six years ago, nearly 180,000 American troops served in Iraq and Afghanistan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, fewer than 15,000 remain.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we salute the courage and sacrifice of every man and woman in this 9/11 Generation who has served to keep us safe.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are humbled and grateful for your service.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America, for all that we have endured;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: for all the grit and hard work required to come back;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: for all the tasks that lie ahead, know this:  The shadow of crisis has passed, and the State of the Union is strong.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At this moment -- with a growing economy, shrinking deficits, bustling industry, booming energy production -- we have risen from recession freer to write our own future than any other nation on Earth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's now up to us to choose who we want to be over the next 15 years and for decades to come.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Will we accept an economy where only a few of us do spectacularly well?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Or will we commit ourselves to an economy that generates rising incomes and chances for everyone who makes the effort?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Will we approach the world fearful and reactive, dragged into costly conflicts that strain our military and set back our standing?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Or will we lead wisely, using all elements of our power to defeat new threats and protect our planet?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Will we allow ourselves to be sorted into factions and turned against one another?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Or will we recapture the sense of common purpose that has always propelled America forward?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In two weeks, I will send this Congress a budget filled with ideas that are practical, not partisan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in the months ahead, I'll crisscross the country making a case for those ideas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight, I want to focus less on a checklist of proposals, and focus more on the values at stake in the choices before us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It begins with our economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Seven years ago, Rebekah and Ben Erler of Minneapolis were newlyweds.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She waited tables.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: He worked construction.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Their first child, Jack, was on the way.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They were young and in love in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it doesn't get much better than that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We are a strong, tight-knit family who has made it through some very, very hard times.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America, Rebekah and Ben's story is our story.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They represent the millions who have worked hard and scrimped, and sacrificed and retooled.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You are the reason that I ran for this office.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You are the people I was thinking of six years ago today, in the darkest months of the crisis, when I stood on the steps of this Capitol and promised we would rebuild our economy on a new foundation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it has been your resilience, your effort that has made it possible for our country to emerge stronger.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We believed we could reverse the tide of outsourcing and draw new jobs to our shores.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And over the past five years, our businesses have created more than 11 million new jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We believed we could reduce our dependence on foreign oil and protect our planet.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And today, America is number one in oil and gas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America is number one in wind power.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Every three weeks, we bring online as much solar power as we did in all of 2008.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And thanks to lower gas prices and higher fuel standards, the typical family this year should save about $750 at the pump.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We believed we could prepare our kids for a more competitive world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And today, our younger students have earned the highest math and reading scores on record.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our high school graduation rate has hit an all-time high.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More Americans finish college than ever before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We believed that sensible regulations could prevent another crisis, shield families from ruin, and encourage fair competition.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, we have new tools to stop taxpayer-funded bailouts, and a new consumer watchdog to protect us from predatory lending and abusive credit card practices.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in the past year alone, about 10 million uninsured Americans finally gained the security of health coverage.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At every step, we were told our goals were misguided or too ambitious;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that we would crush jobs and explode deficits.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Instead, we've seen the fastest economic growth in over a decade, our deficits cut by two-thirds, a stock market that has doubled, and health care inflation at its lowest rate in 50 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This is good news, people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So the verdict is clear.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Middle-class economics works.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Expanding opportunity works.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And these policies will continue to work as long as politics don't get in the way.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can't slow down businesses or put our economy at risk with government shutdowns or fiscal showdowns.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can't put the security of families at risk by taking away their health insurance, or unraveling the new rules on Wall Street, or refighting past battles on immigration when we've got to fix a broken system.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if a bill comes to my desk that tries to do any of these things, I will veto it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It will have earned my veto.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, thanks to a growing economy, the recovery is touching more and more lives.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Wages are finally starting to rise again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We know that more small business owners plan to raise their employees' pay than at any time since 2007.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But here's the thing:  Those of us here tonight, we need to set our sights higher than just making sure government doesn't screw things up;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that government doesn't halt the progress we're making.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to do more than just do no harm.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight, together, let's do more to restore the link between hard work and growing opportunity for every American.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because families like Rebekah's still need our help.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: She and Ben are working as hard as ever, but they've had to forego vacations and a new car so that they can pay off student loans and save for retirement.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Friday night pizza, that's a big splurge.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Basic childcare for Jack and Henry costs more than their mortgage, and almost as much as a year at the University of Minnesota.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Like millions of hardworking Americans, Rebekah isn't asking for a handout, but she is asking that we look for more ways to help families get ahead.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in fact, at every moment of economic change throughout our history, this country has taken bold action to adapt to new circumstances and to make sure everyone gets a fair shot.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We set up worker protections, Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid to protect ourselves from the harshest adversity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We gave our citizens schools and colleges, infrastructure and the Internet -- tools they needed to go as far as their effort and their dreams will take them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what middle-class economics is -- the idea that this country does best when everyone gets their fair shot, everyone does their fair share, everyone plays by the same set of rules.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We don't just want everyone to share in America's success, we want everyone to contribute to our success.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So what does middle-class economics require in our time?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: First, middle-class economics means helping working families feel more secure in a world of constant change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That means helping folks afford childcare, college, health care, a home, retirement.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And my budget will address each of these issues, lowering the taxes of working families and putting thousands of dollars back into their pockets each year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Here's one example.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: During World War II, when men like my grandfather went off to war, having women like my grandmother in the workforce was a national security priority -- so this country provided universal childcare.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In today's economy, when having both parents in the workforce is an economic necessity for many families, we need affordable, high-quality childcare more than ever.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's not a nice-to-have -- it's a must-have.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So it's time we stop treating childcare as a side issue, or as a women's issue, and treat it like the national economic priority that it is for all of us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why my plan will make quality childcare more available and more affordable for every middle-class and low-income family with young children in America -- by creating more slots and a new tax cut of up to $3,000 per child, per year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Here's another example.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, we are the only advanced country on Earth that doesn't guarantee paid sick leave or paid maternity leave to our workers.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Forty-three million workers have no paid sick leave -- 43 million.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Think about that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that forces too many parents to make the gut-wrenching choice between a paycheck and a sick kid at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So I'll be taking new action to help states adopt paid leave laws of their own.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And since paid sick leave won where it was on the ballot last November, let's put it to a vote right here in Washington.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Send me a bill that gives every worker in America the opportunity to earn seven days of paid sick leave.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the right thing to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the right thing to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, nothing helps families make ends meet like higher wages.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why this Congress still needs to pass a law that makes sure a woman is paid the same as a man for doing the same work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We still need to make sure employees get the overtime they've earned.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And to everyone in this Congress who still refuses to raise the minimum wage, I say this:  If you truly believe you could work full-time and support a family on less than $15,000 a year, try it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If not, vote to give millions of the hardest-working people in America a raise.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, these ideas won't make everybody rich, won't relieve every hardship.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's not the job of government.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To give working families a fair shot, we still need more employers to see beyond next quarter's earnings and recognize that investing in their workforce is in their company's long-term interest.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We still need laws that strengthen rather than weaken unions, and give American workers a voice.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But you know, things like childcare and sick leave and equal pay;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: things like lower mortgage premiums and a higher minimum wage -- these ideas will make a meaningful difference in the lives of millions of families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's a fact.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's what all of us, Republicans and Democrats alike, were sent here to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Second, to make sure folks keep earning higher wages down the road, we have to do more to help Americans upgrade their skills.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America thrived in the 20th century because we made high school free, sent a generation of GIs to college, trained the best workforce in the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We were ahead of the curve.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But other countries caught on.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in a 21st century economy that rewards knowledge like never before, we need to up our game.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to do more.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: By the end of this decade, two in three job openings will require some higher education -- two in three.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And yet, we still live in a country where too many bright, striving Americans are priced out of the education they need.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's not fair to them, and it's sure not smart for our future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why I'm sending this Congress a bold new plan to lower the cost of community college -- to zero.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Keep in mind 40 percent of our college students choose community college.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some are young and starting out.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some are older and looking for a better job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some are veterans and single parents trying to transition back into the job market.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Whoever you are, this plan is your chance to graduate ready for the new economy without a load of debt.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Understand, you've got to earn it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You've got to keep your grades up and graduate on time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tennessee, a state with Republican leadership, and Chicago, a city with Democratic leadership, are showing that free community college is possible.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want to spread that idea all across America, so that two years of college becomes as free and universal in America as high school is today.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's stay ahead of the curve.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I want to work with this Congress to make sure those already burdened with student loans can reduce their monthly payments so that student debt doesn't derail anyone's dreams.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thanks to Vice President Biden's great work to update our job training system, we're connecting community colleges with local employers to train workers to fill high-paying jobs like coding, and nursing, and robotics.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Tonight, I'm also asking more businesses to follow the lead of companies like CVS and UPS, and offer more educational benefits and paid apprenticeships -- opportunities that give workers the chance to earn higher-paying jobs even if they don't have a higher education.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as a new generation of veterans comes home, we owe them every opportunity to live the American Dream they helped defend.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Already, we've made strides towards ensuring that every veteran has access to the highest quality care.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're slashing the backlog that had too many veterans waiting years to get the benefits they need.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we're making it easier for vets to translate their training and experience into civilian jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And Joining Forces, the national campaign launched by Michelle and Jill Biden -- (applause) -- thank you, Michelle;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: thank you, Jill -- has helped nearly 700,000 veterans and military spouses get a new job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So to every CEO in America, let me repeat:  If you want somebody who's going to get the job done and done right, hire a veteran.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Finally, as we better train our workers, we need the new economy to keep churning out high-wage jobs for our workers to fill.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Since 2010, America has put more people back to work than Europe, Japan, and all advanced economies combined.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our manufacturers have added almost 800,000 new jobs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some of our bedrock sectors, like our auto industry, are booming.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But there are also millions of Americans who work in jobs that didn't even exist 10 or 20 years ago -- jobs at companies like Google, and eBay, and Tesla.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So no one knows for certain which industries will generate the jobs of the future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we do know we want them here in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We know that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why the third part of middle-class economics is all about building the most competitive economy anywhere, the place where businesses want to locate and hire.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Twenty-first century businesses need 21st century infrastructure -- modern ports, and stronger bridges, faster trains and the fastest Internet.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Democrats and Republicans used to agree on this.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's set our sights higher than a single oil pipeline.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's pass a bipartisan infrastructure plan that could create more than 30 times as many jobs per year, and make this country stronger for decades to come.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's do it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's get it done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's get it done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Twenty-first century businesses, including small businesses, need to sell more American products overseas.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, our businesses export more than ever, and exporters tend to pay their workers higher wages.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But as we speak, China wants to write the rules for the world's fastest-growing region.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That would put our workers and our businesses at a disadvantage.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Why would we let that happen?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should write those rules.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should level the playing field.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why I'm asking both parties to give me trade promotion authority to protect American workers, with strong new trade deals from Asia to Europe that aren't just free, but are also fair.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the right thing to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Look, I'm the first one to admit that past trade deals haven't always lived up to the hype, and that's why we've gone after countries that break the rules at our expense.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But 95 percent of the world's customers live outside our borders.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can't close ourselves off from those opportunities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More than half of manufacturing executives have said they're actively looking to bring jobs back from China.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's give them one more reason to get it done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Twenty-first century businesses will rely on American science and technology, research and development.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want the country that eliminated polio and mapped the human genome to lead a new era of medicine -- one that delivers the right treatment at the right time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In some patients with cystic fibrosis, this approach has reversed a disease once thought unstoppable.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight, I'm launching a new Precision Medicine Initiative to bring us closer to curing diseases like cancer and diabetes, and to give all of us access to the personalized information we need to keep ourselves and our families healthier.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can do this.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I intend to protect a free and open Internet, extend its reach to every classroom, and every community -- (applause -- and help folks build the fastest networks so that the next generation of digital innovators and entrepreneurs have the platform to keep reshaping our world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want Americans to win the race for the kinds of discoveries that unleash new jobs -- converting sunlight into liquid fuel;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: creating revolutionary prosthetics, so that a veteran who gave his arms for his country can play catch with his kids again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Pushing out into the solar system not just to visit, but to stay.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last month, we launched a new spacecraft as part of a reenergized space program that will send American astronauts to Mars.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in two months, to prepare us for those missions, Scott Kelly will begin a year-long stay in space.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So good luck, Captain.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Make sure to Instagram it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're proud of you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, the truth is, when it comes to issues like infrastructure and basic research, I know there's bipartisan support in this chamber.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Members of both parties have told me so.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Where we too often run onto the rocks is how to pay for these investments.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As Americans, we don't mind paying our fair share of taxes as long as everybody else does, too.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But for far too long, lobbyists have rigged the tax code with loopholes that let some corporations pay nothing while others pay full freight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They've riddled it with giveaways that the super-rich don't need, while denying a break to middle-class families who do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This year, we have an opportunity to change that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's close loopholes so we stop rewarding companies that keep profits abroad, and reward those that invest here in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's use those savings to rebuild our infrastructure and to make it more attractive for companies to bring jobs home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's simplify the system and let a small business owner file based on her actual bank statement, instead of the number of accountants she can afford.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And let's close the loopholes that lead to inequality by allowing the top one percent to avoid paying taxes on their accumulated wealth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can use that money to help more families pay for childcare and send their kids to college.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need a tax code that truly helps working Americans trying to get a leg up in the new economy, and we can achieve that together.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can achieve it together.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Helping hardworking families make ends meet.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Giving them the tools they need for good-paying jobs in this new economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Maintaining the conditions of growth and competitiveness.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This is where America needs to go.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I believe it's where the American people want to go.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It will make our economy stronger a year from now, 15 years from now, and deep into the century ahead.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Of course, if there's one thing this new century has taught us, it's that we cannot separate our work here at home from challenges beyond our shores.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My first duty as Commander-in-Chief is to defend the United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In doing so, the question is not whether America leads in the world, but how.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When we make rash decisions, reacting to the headlines instead of using our heads;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: when the first response to a challenge is to send in our military -- then we risk getting drawn into unnecessary conflicts, and neglect the broader strategy we need for a safer, more prosperous world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what our enemies want us to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I believe in a smarter kind of American leadership.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We lead best when we combine military power with strong diplomacy;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: when we leverage our power with coalition building;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: when we don't let our fears blind us to the opportunities that this new century presents.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's exactly what we're doing right now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And around the globe, it is making a difference.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: First, we stand united with people around the world who have been targeted by terrorists -- from a school in Pakistan to the streets of Paris.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We will continue to hunt down terrorists and dismantle their networks, and we reserve the right to act unilaterally, as we have done relentlessly since I took office to take out terrorists who pose a direct threat to us and our allies.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: At the same time, we've learned some costly lessons over the last 13 years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Instead of Americans patrolling the valleys of Afghanistan, we've trained their security forces, who have now taken the lead, and we've honored our troops' sacrifice by supporting that country's first democratic transition.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Instead of sending large ground forces overseas, we're partnering with nations from South Asia to North Africa to deny safe haven to terrorists who threaten America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In Iraq and Syria, American leadership -- including our military power -- is stopping ISIL's advance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Instead of getting dragged into another ground war in the Middle East, we are leading a broad coalition, including Arab nations, to degrade and ultimately destroy this terrorist group.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're also supporting a moderate opposition in Syria that can help us in this effort, and assisting people everywhere who stand up to the bankrupt ideology of violent extremism.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, this effort will take time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It will require focus.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we will succeed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tonight, I call on this Congress to show the world that we are united in this mission by passing a resolution to authorize the use of force against ISIL.  We need that authority.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Second, we're demonstrating the power of American strength and diplomacy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're upholding the principle that bigger nations can't bully the small -- by opposing Russian aggression, and supporting Ukraine's democracy, and reassuring our NATO allies.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last year, as we were doing the hard work of imposing sanctions along with our allies, as we were reinforcing our presence with frontline states, Mr. Putin's aggression it was suggested was a masterful display of strategy and strength.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what I heard from some folks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Well, today, it is America that stands strong and united with our allies, while Russia is isolated with its economy in tatters.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's how America leads -- not with bluster, but with persistent, steady resolve.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In Cuba, we are ending a policy that was long past its expiration date.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When what you're doing doesn't work for 50 years, it's time to try something new.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And our shift in Cuba policy has the potential to end a legacy of mistrust in our hemisphere.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It removes a phony excuse for restrictions in Cuba.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It stands up for democratic values, and extends the hand of friendship to the Cuban people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And this year, Congress should begin the work of ending the embargo.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As His Holiness, Pope Francis, has said, diplomacy is the work of _âÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬ÃâÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬â¥âÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬ÃâÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬Ã¶small steps.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: These small steps have added up to new hope for the future in Cuba.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And after years in prison, we are overjoyed that Alan Gross is back where he belongs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Welcome home, Alan.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're glad you're here.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our diplomacy is at work with respect to Iran, where, for the first time in a decade, we've halted the progress of its nuclear program and reduced its stockpile of nuclear material.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Between now and this spring, we have a chance to negotiate a comprehensive agreement that prevents a nuclear-armed Iran, secures America and our allies -- including Israel, while avoiding yet another Middle East conflict.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There are no guarantees that negotiations will succeed, and I keep all options on the table to prevent a nuclear Iran.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But new sanctions passed by this Congress, at this moment in time, will all but guarantee that diplomacy fails -- alienating America from its allies;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: making it harder to maintain sanctions;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: and ensuring that Iran starts up its nuclear program again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It doesn't make sense.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why I will veto any new sanctions bill that threatens to undo this progress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The American people expect us only to go to war as a last resort, and I intend to stay true to that wisdom.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Third, we're looking beyond the issues that have consumed us in the past to shape the coming century.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No foreign nation, no hacker, should be able to shut down our networks, steal our trade secrets, or invade the privacy of American families, especially our kids.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So we're making sure our government integrates intelligence to combat cyber threats, just as we have done to combat terrorism.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And tonight, I urge this Congress to finally pass the legislation we need to better meet the evolving threat of cyber attacks, combat identity theft, and protect our children's information.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That should be a bipartisan effort.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If we don't act, we'll leave our nation and our economy vulnerable.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If we do, we can continue to protect the technologies that have unleashed untold opportunities for people around the globe.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In West Africa, our troops, our scientists, our doctors, our nurses, our health care workers are rolling back Ebola -- saving countless lives and stopping the spread of disease.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I could not be prouder of them, and I thank this Congress for your bipartisan support of their efforts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But the job is not yet done, and the world needs to use this lesson to build a more effective global effort to prevent the spread of future pandemics, invest in smart development, and eradicate extreme poverty.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the Asia Pacific, we are modernizing alliances while making sure that other nations play by the rules -- in how they trade, how they resolve maritime disputes, how they participate in meeting common international challenges like nonproliferation and disaster relief.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And no challenge -- no challenge -- poses a greater threat to future generations than climate change.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: 2014 was the planet's warmest year on record.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, one year doesn't make a trend, but this does:  14 of the 15 warmest years on record have all fallen in the first 15 years of this century.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've heard some folks try to dodge the evidence by saying they're not scientists;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that we don't have enough information to act.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Well, I'm not a scientist, either.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But you know what, I know a lot of really good scientists at NASA, and at NOAA, and at our major universities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And the best scientists in the world are all telling us that our activities are changing the climate, and if we don't act forcefully, we'll continue to see rising oceans, longer, hotter heat waves, dangerous droughts and floods, and massive disruptions that can trigger greater migration and conflict and hunger around the globe.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The Pentagon says that climate change poses immediate risks to our national security.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should act like it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why, over the past six years, we've done more than ever to combat climate change, from the way we produce energy to the way we use it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we've set aside more public lands and waters than any administration in history.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why I will not let this Congress endanger the health of our children by turning back the clock on our efforts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I am determined to make sure that American leadership drives international action.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In Beijing, we made a historic announcement:  The United States will double the pace at which we cut carbon pollution.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And China committed, for the first time, to limiting their emissions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And because the world's two largest economies came together, other nations are now stepping up, and offering hope that this year the world will finally reach an agreement to protect the one planet we've got.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And there's one last pillar of our leadership, and that's the example of our values.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As Americans, we respect human dignity, even when we're threatened, which is why I have prohibited torture, and worked to make sure our use of new technology like drones is properly constrained.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's why we speak out against the deplorable anti-Semitism that has resurfaced in certain parts of the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's why we continue to reject offensive stereotypes of Muslims, the vast majority of whom share our commitment to peace.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we defend free speech, and advocate for political prisoners, and condemn the persecution of women, or religious minorities, or people who are lesbian, gay, bisexual or transgender.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We do these things not only because they are the right thing to do, but because ultimately they will make us safer.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As Americans, we have a profound commitment to justice.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So it makes no sense to spend $3 million per prisoner to keep open a prison that the world condemns and terrorists use to recruit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Since I've been President, we've worked responsibly to cut the population of Gitmo in half.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now it is time to finish the job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I will not relent in my determination to shut it down.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is not who we are.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's time to close Gitmo.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As Americans, we cherish our civil liberties, and we need to uphold that commitment if we want maximum cooperation from other countries and industry in our fight against terrorist networks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So while some have moved on from the debates over our surveillance programs, I have not.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As promised, our intelligence agencies have worked hard, with the recommendations of privacy advocates, to increase transparency and build more safeguards against potential abuse.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And next month, we'll issue a report on how we're keeping our promise to keep our country safe while strengthening privacy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Looking to the future instead of the past.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Making sure we match our power with diplomacy, and use force wisely.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Building coalitions to meet new challenges and opportunities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Leading -- always -- with the example of our values.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what makes us exceptional.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what keeps us strong.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we have to keep striving to hold ourselves to the highest of standards -- our own.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You know, just over a decade ago, I gave a speech in Boston where I said there wasn't a liberal America or a conservative America;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: a black America or a white America -- but a United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I said this because I had seen it in my own life, in a nation that gave someone like me a chance;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: because I grew up in Hawaii, a melting pot of races and customs;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: because I made Illinois my home -- a state of small towns, rich farmland, one of the world's great cities;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: a microcosm of the country where Democrats and Republicans and Independents, good people of every ethnicity and every faith, share certain bedrock values.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Over the past six years, the pundits have pointed out more than once that my presidency hasn't delivered on this vision.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: How ironic, they say, that our politics seems more divided than ever.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's held up as proof not just of my own flaws -- of which there are many -- but also as proof that the vision itself is misguided, naâÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬ÃâÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬ÃªâÃÂ¬â _âÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬Ã¤ve, that there are too many people in this town who actually benefit from partisanship and gridlock for us to ever do anything about it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know how tempting such cynicism may be.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I still think the cynics are wrong.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I still believe that we are one people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I still believe that together, we can do great things, even when the odds are long.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I believe this because over and over in my six years in office, I have seen America at its best.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've seen the hopeful faces of young graduates from New York to California, and our newest officers at West Point, Annapolis, Colorado Springs, New London.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've mourned with grieving families in Tucson and Newtown, in Boston, in West Texas, and West Virginia.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've watched Americans beat back adversity from the Gulf Coast to the Great Plains, from Midwest assembly lines to the Mid-Atlantic seaboard.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've seen something like gay marriage go from a wedge issue used to drive us apart to a story of freedom across our country, a civil right now legal in states that seven in 10 Americans call home.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So I know the good, and optimistic, and big-hearted generosity of the American people who every day live the idea that we are our brother's keeper and our sister's keeper.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I know they expect those of us who serve here to set a better example.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So the question for those of us here tonight is how we, all of us, can better reflect America's hopes.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've served in Congress with many of you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know many of you well.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There are a lot of good people here, on both sides of the aisle.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And many of you have told me that this isn't what you signed up for -- arguing past each other on cable shows, the constant fundraising, always looking over your shoulder at how the base will react to every decision.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Imagine if we broke out of these tired old patterns.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Imagine if we did something different.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Understand, a better politics isn't one where Democrats abandon their agenda or Republicans simply embrace mine.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A better politics is one where we appeal to each other's basic decency instead of our basest fears.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A better politics is one where we debate without demonizing each other;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: where we talk issues and values, and principles and facts, rather than _âÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬ÃâÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬â¥âÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬ÃâÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬Ã¶gotcha_âÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬ÃâÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬â¥âÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬ÃâÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬Ã moments, or trivial gaffes, or fake controversies that have nothing to do with people's daily lives.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A politics -- a better politics is one where we spend less time drowning in dark money for ads that pull us into the gutter, and spend more time lifting young people up with a sense of purpose and possibility, asking them to join in the great mission of building America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If we're going to have arguments, let's have arguments, but let's make them debates worthy of this body and worthy of this country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We still may not agree on a woman's right to choose, but surely we can agree it's a good thing that teen pregnancies and abortions are nearing all-time lows, and that every woman should have access to the health care that she needs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We still may not agree on a woman's right to choose, but surely we can agree it's a good thing that teen pregnancies and abortions are nearing all-time lows, and that every woman should have access to the health care that she needs.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Yes, passions still fly on immigration, but surely we can all see something of ourselves in the striving young student, and agree that no one benefits when a hardworking mom is snatched from her child, and that it's possible to shape a law that upholds our tradition as a nation of laws and a nation of immigrants.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've talked to Republicans and Democrats about that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's something that we can share.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We may go at it in campaign season, but surely we can agree that the right to vote is sacred;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that it's being denied to too many -- (applause) -- and that on this 50th anniversary of the great march from Selma to Montgomery and the passage of the Voting Rights Act, we can come together, Democrats and Republicans, to make voting easier for every single American.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We may have different takes on the events of Ferguson and New York.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But surely we can understand a father who fears his son can't walk home without being harassed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And surely we can understand the wife who won't rest until the police officer she married walks through the front door at the end of his shift.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And surely we can agree that it's a good thing that for the first time in 40 years, the crime rate and the incarceration rate have come down together, and use that as a starting point for Democrats and Republicans, community leaders and law enforcement, to reform America's criminal justice system so that it protects and serves all of us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's a better politics.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's how we start rebuilding trust.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's how we move this country forward.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what the American people want.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's what they deserve.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I have no more campaigns to run.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My only agenda -- (laughter -- I know because I won both of them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My only agenda for the next two years is the same as the one I've had since the day I swore an oath on the steps of this Capitol -- to do what I believe is best for America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If you share the broad vision I outlined tonight, I ask you to join me in the work at hand.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If you disagree with parts of it, I hope you'll at least work with me where you do agree.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I commit to every Republican here tonight that I will not only seek out your ideas, I will seek to work with you to make this country stronger.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Because I want this chamber, I want this city to reflect the truth -- that for all our blind spots and shortcomings, we are a people with the strength and generosity of spirit to bridge divides, to unite in common effort, to help our neighbors, whether down the street or on the other side of the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want our actions to tell every child in every neighborhood, your life matters, and we are committed to improving your life chances as committed as we are to working on behalf of our own kids.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want future generations to know that we are a people who see our differences as a great gift, that we're a people who value the dignity and worth of every citizen -- man and woman, young and old, black and white, Latino, Asian, immigrant, Native American, gay, straight, Americans with mental illness or physical disability.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Everybody matters.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want them to grow up in a country that shows the world what we still know to be true:  that we are still more than a collection of red states and blue states;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that we are the United States of America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want them to grow up in a country where a young mom can sit down and write a letter to her President with a story that sums up these past six years:  _âÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬ÃâÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬â¥âÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬ÃâÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬Ã¶It's amazing what you can bounce back from when you have to_âÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬ÃâÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬â¥_we are a strong, tight-knit family who's made it through some very, very hard times.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: My fellow Americans, we, too, are a strong, tight-knit family.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We, too, have made it through some hard times.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Fifteen years into this new century, we have picked ourselves up, dusted ourselves off, and begun again the work of remaking America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have laid a new foundation.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A brighter future is ours to write.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let's begin this new chapter together -- and let's start the work right now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thank you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: God bless you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: God bless this country we love.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thank you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. Vice President, Members of Congress, my fellow Americans:Tonight marks the eighth year that I've come here to report on the State of the Union.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And for this final one, I'm going to try to make it a little shorter.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know some of you are antsy to get back to Iowa.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've been there.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I'll be shaking hands afterwards if you want some tips.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I understand that because it's an election season, expectations for what we will achieve this year are low.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But, Mr. Speaker, I appreciate the constructive approach that you and the other leaders took at the end of last year to pass a budget and make tax cuts permanent for working families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So I hope we can work together this year on some bipartisan priorities like criminal justice reform and helping people who are battling prescription drug abuse and heroin abuse.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So, who knows, we might surprise the cynics again.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But tonight, I want to go easy on the traditional list of proposals for the year ahead.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Don't worry, I've got plenty, from helping students learn to write computer code to personalizing medical treatments for patients.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I will keep pushing for progress on the work that I believe still needs to be done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Fixing a broken immigration system.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Protecting our kids from gun violence.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Equal pay for equal work.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Paid leave.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Raising the minimum wage.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: All these things still matter to hardworking families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They're still the right thing to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I won't let up until they get done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But for my final address to this chamber, I don't want to just talk about next year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want to focus on the next five years, the next 10 years, and beyond.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I want to focus on our future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We live in a time of extraordinary change -- change that's reshaping the way we live, the way we work, our planet, our place in the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's change that promises amazing medical breakthroughs, but also economic disruptions that strain working families.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It promises education for girls in the most remote villages, but also connects terrorists plotting an ocean away.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's change that can broaden opportunity, or widen inequality.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And whether we like it or not, the pace of this change will only accelerate.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America has been through big changes before -- wars and depression, the influx of new immigrants, workers fighting for a fair deal, movements to expand civil rights.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Each time, there have been those who told us to fear the future;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: who claimed we could slam the brakes on change;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: who promised to restore past glory if we just got some group or idea that was threatening America under control.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And each time, we overcame those fears.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We did not, in the words of Lincoln, adhere to the "dogmas of the quiet past."

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Instead we thought anew, and acted anew.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We made change work for us, always extending America's promise outward, to the next frontier, to more people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And because we did -- because we saw opportunity where others saw only peril -- we emerged stronger and better than before.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What was true then can be true now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our unique strengths as a nation -- our optimism and work ethic, our spirit of discovery, our diversity, our commitment to rule of law -- these things give us everything we need to ensure prosperity and security for generations to come.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, it's that spirit that made the progress of these past seven years possible.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's how we recovered from the worst economic crisis in generations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's how we reformed our health care system, and reinvented our energy sector;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: how we delivered more care and benefits to our troops and veterans, and how we secured the freedom in every state to marry the person we love.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But such progress is not inevitable.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the result of choices we make together.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we face such choices right now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Will we respond to the changes of our time with fear, turning inward as a nation, turning against each other as a people?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Or will we face the future with confidence in who we are, in what we stand for, in the incredible things that we can do together?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So let's talk about the future, and four big questions that I believe we as a country have to answer -- regardless of who the next President is, or who controls the next Congress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: First, how do we give everyone a fair shot at opportunity and security in this new economy?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Second, how do we make technology work for us, and not against us -- especially when it comes to solving urgent challenges like climate change?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Third, how do we keep America safe and lead the world without becoming its policeman?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And finally, how can we make our politics reflect what's best in us, and not what's worst?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let me start with the economy, and a basic fact: The United States of America, right now, has the strongest, most durable economy in the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're in the middle of the longest streak of private sector job creation in history.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: More than 14 million new jobs, the strongest two years of job growth since the '90s, an unemployment rate cut in half.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our auto industry just had its best year ever.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's just part of a manufacturing surge that's created nearly 900,000 new jobs in the past six years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we've done all this while cutting our deficits by almost three-quarters.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Anyone claiming that America's economy is in decline is peddling fiction.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, what is true -- and the reason that a lot of Americans feel anxious -- is that the economy has been changing in profound ways, changes that started long before the Great Recession hit;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: changes that have not let up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Today, technology doesn't just replace jobs on the assembly line, but any job where work can be automated.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Companies in a global economy can locate anywhere, and they face tougher competition.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: As a result, workers have less leverage for a raise.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Companies have less loyalty to their communities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And more and more wealth and income is concentrated at the very top.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: All these trends have squeezed workers, even when they have jobs;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: even when the economy is growing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's made it harder for a hardworking family to pull itself out of poverty, harder for young people to start their careers, tougher for workers to retire when they want to.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And although none of these trends are unique to America, they do offend our uniquely American belief that everybody who works hard should get a fair shot.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For the past seven years, our goal has been a growing economy that works also better for everybody.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've made progress.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we need to make more.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And despite all the political arguments that we've had these past few years, there are actually some areas where Americans broadly agree.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We agree that real opportunity requires every American to get the education and training they need to land a good-paying job.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The bipartisan reform of No Child Left Behind was an important start, and together, we've increased early childhood education, lifted high school graduation rates to new highs, boosted graduates in fields like engineering.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In the coming years, we should build on that progress, by providing Pre-K for all and offering every student the hands-on computer science and math classes that make them job-ready on day one.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We should recruit and support more great teachers for our kids.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we have to make college affordable for every American.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No hardworking student should be stuck in the red.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've already reduced student loan payments to 10 percent of a borrower's income.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's good.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But now, we've actually got to cut the cost of college.

speaker: Barack Obama
