text: Providing two years of community college at no cost for every responsible student is one of the best ways to do that, and I'm going to keep fighting to get that started this year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the right thing to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But a great education isn't all we need in this new economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We also need benefits and protections that provide a basic measure of security.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's not too much of a stretch to say that some of the only people in America who are going to work the same job, in the same place, with a health and retirement package for 30 years are sitting in this chamber.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For everyone else, especially folks in their 40s and 50s, saving for retirement or bouncing back from job loss has gotten a lot tougher.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Americans understand that at some point in their careers, in this new economy, they may have to retool and they may have to retrain.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But they shouldn't lose what they've already worked so hard to build in the process.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why Social Security and Medicare are more important than ever.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We shouldn't weaken them;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: we should strengthen them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And for Americans short of retirement, basic benefits should be just as mobile as everything else is today.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That, by the way, is what the Affordable Care Act is all about.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's about filling the gaps in employer-based care so that when you lose a job, or you go back to school, or you strike out and launch that new business, you'll still have coverage.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Nearly 18 million people have gained coverage so far.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in the process, health care inflation has slowed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And our businesses have created jobs every single month since it became law.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, I'm guessing we won't agree on health care anytime soon.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Just a guess.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But there should be other ways parties can work together to improve economic security.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Say a hardworking American loses his job -- we shouldn't just make sure that he can get unemployment insurance;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: we should make sure that program encourages him to retrain for a business that's ready to hire him.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If that new job doesn't pay as much, there should be a system of wage insurance in place so that he can still pay his bills.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And even if he's going from job to job, he should still be able to save for retirement and take his savings with him.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's the way we make the new economy work better for everybody.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I also know Speaker Ryan has talked about his interest in tackling poverty.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America is about giving everybody willing to work a chance, a hand up.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I'd welcome a serious discussion about strategies we can all support, like expanding tax cuts for low-income workers who don't have children.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But there are some areas where we just have to be honest -- it has been difficult to find agreement over the last seven years.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And a lot of them fall under the category of what role the government should play in making sure the system's not rigged in favor of the wealthiest and biggest corporations.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it's an honest disagreement, and the American people have a choice to make.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I believe a thriving private sector is the lifeblood of our economy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I think there are outdated regulations that need to be changed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There is red tape that needs to be cut.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There you go!

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Yes!

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But after years now of record corporate profits, working families won't get more opportunity or bigger paychecks just by letting big banks or big oil or hedge funds make their own rules at everybody else's expense.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Middle-class families are not going to feel more secure because we allowed attacks on collective bargaining to go unanswered.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Food Stamp recipients did not cause the financial crisis;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: recklessness on Wall Street did.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Immigrants aren't the principal reason wages haven't gone up;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: those decisions are made in the boardrooms that all too often put quarterly earnings over long-term returns.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's sure not the average family watching tonight that avoids paying taxes through offshore accounts.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The point is, I believe that in this In new economy, workers and start-ups and small businesses need more of a voice, not less.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The rules should work for them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I'm not alone in this.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This year I plan to lift up the many businesses who've figured out that doing right by their workers or their customers or their communities ends up being good for their shareholders.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And I want to spread those best practices across America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's part of a brighter future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fact, it turns out many of our best corporate citizens are also our most creative.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And this brings me to the second big question we as a country have to answer: How do we reignite that spirit of innovation to meet our biggest challenges?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Sixty years ago, when the Russians beat us into space, we didn't deny Sputnik was up there.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We didn't argue about the science, or shrink our research and development budget.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We built a space program almost overnight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And 12 years later, we were walking on the moon.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, that spirit of discovery is in our DNA.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America is Thomas Edison and the Wright Brothers and George Washington Carver.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America is Grace Hopper and Katherine Johnson and Sally Ride.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: America is every immigrant and entrepreneur from Boston to Austin to Silicon Valley, racing to shape a better world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's who we are.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And over the past seven years, we've nurtured that spirit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've protected an open Internet, and taken bold new steps to get more students and low-income Americans online.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've launched next-generation manufacturing hubs, and online tools that give an entrepreneur everything he or she needs to start a business in a single day.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But we can do so much more.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last year, Vice President Biden said that with a new moonshot, America can cure cancer.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Last month, he worked with this Congress to give scientists at the National Institutes of Health the strongest resources that they've had in over a decade.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So tonight, I'm announcing a new national effort to get it done.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And because he's gone to the mat for all of us on so many issues over the past 40 years, I'm putting Joe in charge of Mission Control.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For the loved ones we've all lost, for the families that we can still save, let's make America the country that cures cancer once and for all.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Medical research is critical.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need the same level of commitment when it comes to developing clean energy sources.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Look, if anybody still wants to dispute the science around climate change, have at it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You will be pretty lonely, because you'll be debating our military, most of America's business leaders, the majority of the American people, almost the entire scientific community, and 200 nations around the world who agree it's a problem and intend to solve it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But even if -- even if the planet wasn't at stake, even if 2014 wasn't the warmest year on record -- until 2015 turned out to be even hotter -- why would we want to pass up the chance for American businesses to produce and sell the energy of the future?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Listen, seven years ago, we made the single biggest investment in clean energy in our history.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Here are the results.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In fields from Iowa to Texas, wind power is now cheaper than dirtier, conventional power.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: On rooftops from Arizona to New York, solar is saving Americans tens of millions of dollars a year on their energy bills, and employs more Americans than coal -- in jobs that pay better than average.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're taking steps to give homeowners the freedom to generate and store their own energy -- something, by the way, that environmentalists and Tea Partiers have teamed up to support.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And meanwhile, we've cut our imports of foreign oil by nearly 60 percent, and cut carbon pollution more than any other country on Earth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Gas under two bucks a gallon ain't bad, either.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now we've got to accelerate the transition away from old, dirtier energy sources.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Rather than subsidize the past, we should invest in the future -- especially in communities that rely on fossil fuels.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We do them no favor when we don't show them where the trends are going.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why I'm going to push to change the way we manage our oil and coal resources, so that they better reflect the costs they impose on taxpayers and our planet.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that way, we put money back into those communities, and put tens of thousands of Americans to work building a 21st century transportation system.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, none of this is going to happen overnight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And, yes, there are plenty of entrenched interests who want to protect the status quo.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But the jobs we'll create, the money we'll save, the planet we'll preserve -- that is the kind of future our kids and our grandkids deserve.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it's within our grasp.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Climate change is just one of many issues where our security is linked to the rest of the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why the third big question that we have to answer together is how to keep America safe and strong without either isolating ourselves or trying to nation-build everywhere there's a problem.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I told you earlier all the talk of America's economic decline is political hot air.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Well, so is all the rhetoric you hear about our enemies getting stronger and America getting weaker.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let me tell you something.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The United States of America is the most powerful nation on Earth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Period.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Period.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's not even close.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's not even close.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's not even close.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We spend more on our military than the next eight nations combined.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our troops are the finest fighting force in the history of the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: No nation attacks us directly, or our allies, because they know that's the path to ruin.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Surveys show our standing around the world is higher than when I was elected to this office, and when it comes to every important international issue, people of the world do not look to Beijing or Moscow to lead -- they call us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I mean, it's useful to level the set here, because when we don't, we don't make good decisions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Now, as someone who begins every day with an intelligence briefing, I know this is a dangerous time.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But that's not primarily because of some looming superpower out there, and certainly not because of diminished American strength.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: In today's world, we're threatened less by evil empires and more by failing states.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The Middle East is going through a transformation that will play out for a generation, rooted in conflicts that date back millennia.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Economic headwinds are blowing in from a Chinese economy that is in significant transition.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Even as their economy severely contracts, Russia is pouring resources in to prop up Ukraine and Syria -- client states that they saw slipping away from their orbit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And the international system we built after World War II is now struggling to keep pace with this new reality.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's up to us, the United States of America, to help remake that system.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And to do that well it means that we've got to set priorities.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Priority number one is protecting the American people and going after terrorist networks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Both al Qaeda and now ISIL pose a direct threat to our people, because in today's world, even a handful of terrorists who place no value on human life, including their own, can do a lot of damage.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They use the Internet to poison the minds of individuals inside our country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Their actions undermine and destabilize our allies.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have to take them out.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But as we focus on destroying ISIL, over-the-top claims that this is World War III just play into their hands.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Masses of fighters on the back of pickup trucks, twisted souls plotting in apartments or garages -- they pose an enormous danger to civilians;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: they have to be stopped.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But they do not threaten our national existence.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That is the story ISIL wants to tell.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's the kind of propaganda they use to recruit.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We don't need to build them up to show that we're serious, and we sure don't need to push away vital allies in this fight by echoing the lie that ISIL is somehow representative of one of the world's largest religions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We just need to call them what they are -- killers and fanatics who have to be rooted out, hunted down, and destroyed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's exactly what we're doing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For more than a year, America has led a coalition of more than 60 countries to cut off ISIL's financing, disrupt their plots, stop the flow of terrorist fighters, and stamp out their vicious ideology.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With nearly 10,000 air strikes, we're taking out their leadership, their oil, their training camps, their weapons.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We're training, arming, and supporting forces who are steadily reclaiming territory in Iraq and Syria.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If this Congress is serious about winning this war, and wants to send a message to our troops and the world, authorize the use of military force against ISIL.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Take a vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Take a vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But the American people should know that with or without congressional action, ISIL will learn the same lessons as terrorists before them.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: If you doubt America's commitment -- or mine -- to see that justice is done, just ask Osama bin Laden.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Ask the leader of al Qaeda in Yemen, who was taken out last year, or the perpetrator of the Benghazi attacks, who sits in a prison cell.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When you come after Americans, we go after you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And it may take time, but we have long memories, and our reach has no limits.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our foreign policy hast to be focused on the threat from ISIL and al Qaeda, but it can't stop there.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: For even without ISIL, even without al Qaeda, instability will continue for decades in many parts of the world -- in the Middle East, in Afghanistan, parts of Pakistan, in parts of Central America, in Africa, and Asia.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Some of these places may become safe havens for new terrorist networks.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Others will just fall victim to ethnic conflict, or famine, feeding the next wave of refugees.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The world will look to us to help solve these problems, and our answer needs to be more than tough talk or calls to carpet-bomb civilians.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That may work as a TV sound bite, but it doesn't pass muster on the world stage.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We also can't try to take over and rebuild every country that falls into crisis, even if it's done with the best of intentions.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's not leadership;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that's a recipe for quagmire, spilling American blood and treasure that ultimately will weaken us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the lesson of Vietnam;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: it's the lesson of Iraq -- and we should have learned it by now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Fortunately, there is a smarter approach, a patient and disciplined strategy that uses every element of our national power.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It says America will always act, alone if necessary, to protect our people and our allies;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: but on issues of global concern, we will mobilize the world to work with us, and make sure other countries pull their own weight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's our approach to conflicts like Syria, where we're partnering with local forces and leading international efforts to help that broken society pursue a lasting peace.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we built a global coalition, with sanctions and principled diplomacy, to prevent a nuclear-armed Iran.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And as we speak, Iran has rolled back its nuclear program, shipped out its uranium stockpile, and the world has avoided another war.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's how we stopped the spread of Ebola in West Africa.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our military, our doctors, our development workers -- they were heroic;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: they set up the platform that then allowed other countries to join in behind us and stamp out that epidemic.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Hundreds of thousands, maybe a couple million lives were saved.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's how we forged a Trans-Pacific Partnership to open markets, and protect workers and the environment, and advance American leadership in Asia.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It cuts 18,000 taxes on products made in America, which will then support more good jobs here in America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: With TPP, China does not set the rules in that region;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: we do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: You want to show our strength in this new century?

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Approve this agreement.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Give us the tools to enforce it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the right thing to do.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let me give you another example.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Fifty years of isolating Cuba had failed to promote democracy, and set us back in Latin America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why we restored diplomatic relations opened the door to travel and commerce, positioned ourselves to improve the lives of the Cuban people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So if you want to consolidate our leadership and credibility in the hemisphere, recognize that the Cold War is over -- lift the embargo.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The point is American leadership in the 21st century is not a choice between ignoring the rest of the world -- except when we kill terrorists -- or occupying and rebuilding whatever society is unraveling.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Leadership means a wise application of military power, and rallying the world behind causes that are right.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It means seeing our foreign assistance as a part of our national security, not something separate, not charity.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When we lead nearly 200 nations to the most ambitious agreement in history to fight climate change, yes, that helps vulnerable countries, but it also protects our kids.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When we help Ukraine defend its democracy, or Colombia resolve a decades-long war, that strengthens the international order we depend on.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When we help African countries feed their people and care for the sick, it's the right thing to do, and it prevents the next pandemic from reaching our shores.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Right now, we're on track to end the scourge of HIV/AIDS.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's within our grasp.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And we have the chance to accomplish the same thing with malaria -- something I'll be pushing this Congress to fund this year.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's American strength.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's American leadership.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that kind of leadership depends on the power of our example.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's why I will keep working to shut down the prison at Guantanamo.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is expensive, it is unnecessary, and it only serves as a recruitment brochure for our enemies.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There's a better way.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why we need to reject any politics -- any politics -- that targets people because of race or religion.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let me just say this.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This is not a matter of political correctness.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This is a matter of understanding just what it is that makes us strong.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The world respects us not just for our arsenal;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: it respects us for our diversity, and our openness, and the way we respect every faith.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: His Holiness, Pope Francis, told this body from the very spot that I'm standing on tonight that "to imitate the hatred and violence of tyrants and murderers is the best way to take their place."

speaker: Barack Obama
text: When politicians insult Muslims, whether abroad or our fellow citizens, when a mosque is vandalized, or a kid is called names, that doesn't make us safer.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's not telling it like it is.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's just wrong.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It diminishes us in the eyes of the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It makes it harder to achieve our goals.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It betrays who we are as a country.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: "We the People."

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our Constitution begins with those three simple words, words we've come to recognize mean all the people, not just some;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: words that insist we rise and fall together, and that's how we might perfect our Union.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that brings me to the fourth, and maybe the most important thing that I want to say tonight.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The future we want -- all of us want -- opportunity and security for our families, a rising standard of living, a sustainable, peaceful planet for our kids -- all that is within our reach.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But it will only happen if we work together.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It will only happen if we can have rational, constructive debates.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It will only happen if we fix our politics.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: A better politics doesn't mean we have to agree on everything.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This is a big country -- different regions, different attitudes, different interests.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's one of our strengths, too.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our Founders distributed power between states and branches of government, and expected us to argue, just as they did, fiercely, over the size and shape of government, over commerce and foreign relations, over the meaning of liberty and the imperatives of security.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But democracy does require basic bonds of trust between its citizens.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It doesn't work if we think the people who disagree with us are all motivated by malice.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It doesn't work if we think that our political opponents are unpatriotic or trying to weaken America.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Democracy grinds to a halt without a willingness to compromise, or when even basic facts are contested, or when we listen only to those who agree with us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our public life withers when only the most extreme voices get all the attention.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And most of all, democracy breaks down when the average person feels their voice doesn't matter;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: that the system is rigged in favor of the rich or the powerful or some special interest.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Too many Americans feel that way right now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's one of the few regrets of my presidency -- that the rancor and suspicion between the parties has gotten worse instead of better.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I have no doubt a president with the gifts of Lincoln or Roosevelt might have better bridged the divide, and I guarantee I'll keep trying to be better so long as I hold this office.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But, my fellow Americans, this cannot be my task -- or any President's -- alone.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: There are a whole lot of folks in this chamber, good people who would like to see more cooperation, would like to see a more elevated debate in Washington, but feel trapped by the imperatives of getting elected, by the noise coming out of your base.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: you've told me.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the worst-kept secret in Washington.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And a lot of you aren't enjoying being trapped in that kind of rancor.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But that means if we want a better politics -- and I'm addressing the American people now -- if we want a better politics, it's not enough just to change a congressman or change a senator or even change a President.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have to change the system to reflect our better selves.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I think we've got to end the practice of drawing our congressional districts so that politicians can pick their voters, and not the other way around.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Let a bipartisan group do it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We have to reduce the influence of money in our politics, so that a handful of families or hidden interests can't bankroll our elections.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And if our existing approach to campaign finance reform can't pass muster in the courts, we need to work together to find a real solution -- because it's a problem.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And most of you don't like raising money.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I know;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I've done it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We've got to make it easier to vote, not harder.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need to modernize it for the way we live now.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: This is America: We want to make it easier for people to participate.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And over the course of this year, I intend to travel the country to push for reforms that do just that.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I can't do these things on my own.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Changes in our political process -- in not just who gets elected, but how they get elected -- that will only happen when the American people demand it.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It depends on you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what's meant by a government of, by, and for the people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: What I'm suggesting is hard.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's a lot easier to be cynical;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: to accept that change is not possible, and politics is hopeless, and the problem is all the folks who are elected don't care, and to believe that our voices and actions don't matter.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But if we give up now, then we forsake a better future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Those with money and power will gain greater control over the decisions that could send a young soldier to war, or allow another economic disaster, or roll back the equal rights and voting rights that generations of Americans have fought, even died, to secure.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And then, as frustration grows, there will be voices urging us to fall back into our respective tribes, to scapegoat fellow citizens who don't look like us, or pray like us, or vote like we do, or share the same background.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We can't afford to go down that path.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It won't deliver the economy we want.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It will not produce the security we want.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But most of all, it contradicts everything that makes us the envy of the world.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: So, my fellow Americans, whatever you may believe, whether you prefer one party or no party, whether you supported my agenda or fought as hard as you could against it -- our collective futures depends on your willingness to uphold your duties as a citizen.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To vote.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To speak out.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: To stand up for others, especially the weak, especially the vulnerable, knowing that each of us is only here because somebody, somewhere, stood up for us.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: We need every American to stay active in our public life -- and not just during election time -- so that our public life reflects the goodness and the decency that I see in the American people every single day.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It is not easy.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Our brand of democracy is hard.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: But I can promise that a little over a year from now, when I no longer hold this office, I will be right there with you as a citizen, inspired by those voices of fairness and vision, of grit and good humor and kindness that helped America travel so far.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Voices that help us see ourselves not, first and foremost, as black or white, or Asian or Latino, not as gay or straight, immigrant or native born, not as Democrat or Republican, but as Americans first, bound by a common creed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Voices Dr. King believed would have the final word -- voices of unarmed truth and unconditional love.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And they're out there, those voices.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: They don't get a lot of attention;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: they don't seek a lot of fanfare;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: but they're busy doing the work this country needs doing.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I see them everywhere I travel in this incredible country of ours.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I see you, the American people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And in your daily acts of citizenship, I see our future unfolding.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I see it in the worker on the assembly line who clocked extra shifts to keep his company open, and the boss who pays him higher wages instead of laying him off.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I see it in the Dreamer who stays up late at night to finish her science project, and the teacher who comes in early, and maybe with some extra supplies that she bought because she knows that that young girl might someday cure a disease.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I see it in the American who served his time, and bad mistakes as a child but now is dreaming of starting over -- and I see it in the business owner who gives him that second chance.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: The protester determined to prove that justice matters -- and the young cop walking the beat, treating everybody with respect, doing the brave, quiet work of keeping us safe.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I see it in the soldier who gives almost everything to save his brothers, the nurse who tends to him till he can run a marathon, the community that lines up to cheer him on.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: It's the son who finds the courage to come out as who he is, and the father whose love for that son overrides everything he's been taught.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I see it in the elderly woman who will wait in line to cast her vote as long as she has to;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: the new citizen who casts his vote for the first time;

speaker: Barack Obama
text: the volunteers at the polls who believe every vote should count -- because each of them in different ways know how much that precious right is worth.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's the America I know.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's the country we love.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Clear-eyed.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Big-hearted.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Undaunted by challenge.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Optimistic that unarmed truth and unconditional love will have the final word.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: That's what makes me so hopeful about our future.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: I believe in change because I believe in you, the American people.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: And that's why I stand here confident as I have ever been that the State of our Union is strong.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: Thank you, God bless you.

speaker: Barack Obama
text: God bless the United States of America.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thank you very much.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Mr.Speaker, Mr.Vice President, members of Congress, the first lady of the United States and citizens of America, tonight, as we mark the conclusion of our celebration of Black History Month, we are reminded of our nation's path toward civil rights and the work that still remains to be done.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Recent threats targeting Jewish community centers and vandalism of Jewish cemeteries, as well as last week's shooting in Kansas City, remind us that while we may be a nation divided on policies, we are a country that stands united in condemning hate and evil in all of its very ugly forms.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Each American generation passes the torch of truth, liberty and justice, in an unbroken chain all the way down to the present.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: That torch is now in our hands.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And we will use it to light up the world.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I am here tonight to deliver a message of unity and strength, and it is a message deeply delivered from my heart.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: A new chapter of American greatness is now beginning.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: A new national pride is sweeping across our nation.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And a new surge of optimism is placing impossible dreams firmly within our grasp.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: What we are witnessing today is the renewal of the American spirit.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Our allies will find that America is once again ready to lead.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: All the nations of the world - friend or foe - will find that America is strong, America is proud, and America is free.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: In nine years, the United States will celebrate the 250th anniversary of our founding, 250 years since the day we declared our independence.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: It will be one of the great milestones in the history of the world.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But what will America look like as we reach our 250th year?

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: What kind of country will we leave for our children?

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I will not allow the mistakes of recent decades past to define the course of our future.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: For too long, we've watched our middle class shrink as we've exported our jobs and wealth to foreign countries.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We've financed and built one global project after another, but ignored the fates of our children in the inner cities of Chicago, Baltimore, Detroit and so many other places throughout our land.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We've defended the borders of other nations while leaving our own borders wide open for anyone to cross, and for drugs to pour in at a now unprecedented rate.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And we've spent trillions and trillions of dollars overseas, while our infrastructure at home has so badly crumbled.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Then, in 2016, the earth shifted beneath our feet.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The rebellion started as a quiet protest, spoken by families of all colors and creeds, families who just wanted a fair shot for their children, and a fair hearing for their concerns.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But then the quiet voices became a loud chorus, as thousands of citizens now spoke out together, from cities small and large, all across our country.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Finally, the chorus became an earthquake, and the people turned out by the tens of millions, and they were all united by one very simple, but crucial demand, that America must put its own citizens first, because only then can we truly make America great again.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Dying industries will come roaring back to life.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Heroic veterans will get the care they so desperately need.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Our military will be given the resources its brave warriors so richly deserve.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Crumbling infrastructure will be replaced with new roads, bridges, tunnels, airports and railways, gleaming across our very, very beautiful land.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Our terrible drug epidemic will slow down and ultimately stop.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And our neglected inner cities will see a rebirth of hope, safety and opportunity.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Above all else, we will keep our promises to the American people.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thank you.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: It's been a little over a month since my inauguration, and I want to take this moment to update the nation on the progress I've made in keeping those promises.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Since my election, Ford, Fiat-Chrysler, General Motors, Sprint, Softbank, Lockheed, Intel, Walmart and many others have announced that they will invest billions and billions of dollars in the United States and will create tens of thousands of new American jobs.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The stock market has gained almost $3 trillion in value since the election on Nov.8, a record.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We've saved taxpayers hundreds of millions of dollars by bringing down the price of fantastic - and it is a fantastic - new F-35 jet fighter, and we'll be saving billions more on contracts all across our government.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have placed a hiring freeze on nonmilitary and nonessential federal workers.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have begun to drain the swamp of government corruption by imposing a five-year ban on lobbying by executive branch officials - and a lifetime banâÃÂ¬Ã¥âÃÂ¬Ã

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thank you.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thank you.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And a lifetime ban on becoming lobbyists for a foreign government.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have undertaken a historic effort to massively reduce job-crushing regulations, creating a deregulation task force inside of every government agency and we're imposing a new rule which mandates that for every one new regulation, two old regulations must be eliminated.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We're going to stop the regulations that threaten the future and livelihood of our great coal miners.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have cleared the way for the construction of the Keystone and Dakota Access Pipelines thereby creating tens of thousands of jobs.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And I've issued a new directive that new American pipelines be made with American steel.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have withdrawn the United States from the job-killing Trans-Pacific Partnership.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And with the help of Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, we have formed a council with our neighbors in Canada to help ensure that women entrepreneurs have access to the networks, markets and capital they need to start a business and live out their financial dreams.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: To protect our citizens, I have directed the Department of Justice to form a task force on reducing violent crime.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I have further ordered the Departments of Homeland Security and Justice, along with the Department of State and the director of national intelligence, to coordinate an aggressive strategy to dismantle the criminal cartels that have spread all across our nation.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We will stop the drugs from pouring into our country and poisoning our youth, and we will expand treatment for those who have become so badly addicted.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: At the same time, my administration has answered the pleas of the American people for immigration enforcement and border security.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: By finally enforcing our immigration laws, we will raise wages, help the unemployed, save billions and billions of dollars, and make our communities safer for everyone.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We want all Americans to succeed, but that can't happen in an environment of lawless chaos.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We must restore integrity and the rule of law at our borders.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: For that reason, we will soon begin the construction of a great, great wall along our southern border.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: As we speak tonight, we are removing gang members, drug dealers and criminals that threaten our communities and prey on our very innocent citizens.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Bad ones are going out as I speak, and as I promised throughout the campaign.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: To any in Congress who do not believe we should enforce our laws, I would ask you this one question: What would you say to the American family that loses their jobs, their income or their loved one because America refused to uphold its laws and defend its borders?

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Our obligation is to serve, protect and defend the citizens of the United States.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We are also taking strong measures to protect our nation from radical Islamic terrorism.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: According to data provided by the Department of Justice, the vast majority of individuals convicted of terrorism and terrorism-related offenses since 9/11 came here from outside of our country.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have seen the attacks at home, from Boston to San Bernardino to the Pentagon and, yes, even the World Trade Center.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have seen the attacks in France, in Belgium, in Germany and all over the world.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: It is not compassionate, but reckless to allow uncontrolled entry from places where proper vetting cannot occur.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Those given the high honor of admission to the United States should support this country and love its people and its values.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We cannot allow a beachhead of terrorism to form inside America, and we cannot allow our nation to become a sanctuary for extremists.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: That is why my administration has been working on improved vetting procedures, and we will shortly take new steps to keep our nation safe, and to keep those out who will do us harm.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: As promised, I directed the Department of Defense to develop a plan to demolish and destroy ISIS, a network of lawless savages that have slaughtered Muslims and Christians, and men, women and children of all faiths and all beliefs.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We will work with our allies, including our friends and allies in the Muslim world, to extinguish this vile enemy from our planet.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I have also imposed new sanctions on entities and individuals who support Iran's ballistic missile program, and reaffirmed our unbreakable alliance with the state of Israel.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Finally, I have kept my promise to appoint a justice to the United States Supreme Court, from my list of 20 judges, who will defend our Constitution.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I am greatly honored to have Maureen Scalia with us in the gallery tonight.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thank you, Maureen.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Her late, great husband, Antonin Scalia, will forever be a symbol of American justice.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: To fill his seat, we have chosen Judge Neil Gorsuch, a man of incredible skill and deep devotion to the law.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: He was confirmed unanimously by the Court of Appeals, and I am asking the Senate to swiftly approve his nomination.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Tonight, as I outline the next steps we must take as a country, we must honestly acknowledge the circumstances we inherited.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Ninety-four million Americans are out of the labor force.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Over 43 million people are now living in poverty.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And over 43 million Americans are on food stamps.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: More than one in five people in their prime working years are not working.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have the worst financial recovery in 65 years.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: In the last eight years, the past administration has put on more new debt than nearly all of the other presidents combined.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We've lost more than one-fourth of our manufacturing jobs since Nafta was approved, and we've lost 60,000 factories since China joined the World Trade Organization in 2001.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Our trade deficit in goods with the world last year was nearly $800 billion.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And overseas, we have inherited a series of tragic foreign policy disasters.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Solving these and so many other pressing problems will require us to work past the differences of party.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: It will require us to tap into the American spirit that has overcome every challenge throughout our long and storied history.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But to accomplish our goals at home and abroad, we must restart the engine of the American economy, making it easier for companies to do business in the United States and much, much harder for companies to leave our country.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Right now, American companies are taxed at one of the highest rates anywhere in the world.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: My economic team is developing historic tax reform that will reduce the tax rate on our companies so they can compete and thrive anywhere and with anyone.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: It will be a big, big cut.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: At the same time, we will provide massive tax relief for the middle class.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We must create a level playing field for American companies and our workers - have to do it.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Currently, when we ship products out of America, many other countries make us pay very high tariffs and taxes, but when foreign companies ship their products into America, we charge them nothing or almost nothing.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I just met with officials and workers from a great American company, Harley-Davidson.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: In fact, they proudly displayed five of their magnificent motorcycles, made in the U.S.A., on the front lawn of the White House.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And they wanted me to ride one, and I said, "No, thank you."

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: At our meeting, I asked them, "How are you doing?

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: How is business?"

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: They said that it's good.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I asked them further, "How are you doing with other countries, mainly international sales?"

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: They told me - without even complaining, because they have been so mistreated for so long that they've become used to it - that it's very hard to do business with other countries, because they tax our goods at such a high rate.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: They said that in the case of another country, they taxed their motorcycles at 100 percent.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: They weren't even asking for a change.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But I am.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I believe strongly in free trade, but it also has to be fair trade.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: It's been a long time since we had fair trade.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The first Republican president, Abraham Lincoln, warned that "the abandonment of the protective policy by the American government will produce want and ruin among our people."

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Lincoln was right, and it's time we heeded his advice and his words.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I am not going to let America and its great companies and workers be taken - advantage of us any longer.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: They have taken advantage of our country no longer.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I am going to bring back millions of jobs.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Protecting our workers also means reforming our system of legal immigration.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The current, outdated system depresses wages for our poorest workers and puts great pressure on taxpayers.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Nations around the world, like Canada, Australia and many others, have a merit-based immigration system.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: It's a basic principle that those seeking to enter a country ought to be able to support themselves financially.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Yet in America we do not enforce this rule, straining the very public resources that our poorest citizens rely upon.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: According to the National Academy of Sciences, our current immigration system costs American taxpayers many billions of dollars a year.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Switching away from this current system of lower-skilled immigration, and instead adopting a merit-based system, we will have so many more benefits.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: It will save countless dollars, raise workers' wages and help struggling families, including immigrant families, enter the middle class.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And they will do it quickly, and they will be very, very happy, indeed.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I believe that real and positive immigration reform is possible, as long as we focus on the following goals: to improve jobs and wages for Americans, to strengthen our nation's security and to restore respect for our laws.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: If we are guided by the well-being of American citizens, then I believe Republicans and Democrats can work together to achieve an outcome that has eluded our country for decades.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Another Republican president, Dwight D.Eisenhower, initiated the last truly great national infrastructure program: the building of the interstate highway system.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The time has come for a new program of national rebuilding.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: America has spent approximately $6 trillion in the Middle East, all the while our infrastructure at home is crumbling.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: With the $6 trillion, we could have rebuilt our country twice, and maybe even three times, if we had people who had the ability to negotiate.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: To launch our national rebuilding, I will be asking Congress to approve legislation that produces a $1 trillion investment in infrastructure of the United States, financed through both public and private capital, creating millions of new jobs.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: This effort will be guided by two core principles: Buy American and hire American.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Tonight, I am also calling on this Congress to repeal and replace Obamacare with reforms that expand choice, increase access, lower costs and at the same time provide better health care.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Mandating every American to buy government-approved health insurance was never the right solution for our country.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The way to make health insurance available to everyone is to lower the cost of health insurance, and that is what we are going to do.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Obamacare premiums nationwide have increased by double and triple digits.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: As an example, Arizona went up 116 percent last year alone.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Gov.Matt Bevin of Kentucky just said Obamacare is failing in his state, the state of Kentucky, and it's unsustainable and collapsing.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: One third of the counties have only one insurer, and they're losing them fast, they are losing them so fast.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: They're leaving.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And many Americans have no choice at all.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: There's no choice left.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Remember when you were told that you could keep your doctor and keep your plan?

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We now know that all of those promises have been totally broken.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Obamacare is collapsing, and we must act decisively to protect all Americans.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Action is not a choice;

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: it is a necessity.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: So I am calling on all Democrats and Republicans in Congress to work with us to save Americans from this imploding Obamacare disaster.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Here are the principles that should guide Congress as we move to create a better health care system for all Americans.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: First, we should ensure that Americans with pre-existing conditions have access to coverage and that we have a stable transition for Americans currently enrolled in the health care exchanges.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Secondly, we should help Americans purchase their own coverage, through the use of tax credits and expanded health savings accounts, but it must be the plan they want, not the plan forced on them by our government.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thirdly, we should give our state governors the resources and flexibility they need with Medicaid to make sure no one is left out.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Fourth, we should implement legal reforms that protect patients and doctors from unnecessary costs that drive up the price of insurance and work to bring down the artificially high price of drugs and bring them down immediately.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And finally, the time has come to give Americans the freedom to purchase health insurance across state lines which will create a truly competitive national marketplace that will bring costs way down and provide far better care.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: So important.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Everything that is broken in our country can be fixed.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Every problem can be solved.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And every hurting family can find healing and hope.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Our citizens deserve this, and so much more, so why not join forces and finally get the job done and get it done right?

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: On this and so many other things, Democrats and Republicans should get together and unite for the good of our country and for the good of the American people.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: My administration wants to work with members of both parties to make child care accessible and affordable, to help ensure new parents that they have paid family leave to invest in women's health, and to promote clean air and clean water, and to rebuild our military and our infrastructure.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: True love for our people requires us to find common ground, to advance the common good, and to cooperate on behalf of every American child who deserves a much brighter future.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: An incredible young woman is with us this evening who should serve as an inspiration to us all.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Today is Rare Disease Day, and joining us in the gallery is a rare disease survivor, Megan Crowley.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Megan was diagnosed with Pompe disease, a rare and serious illness, when she was 15 months old.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: She was not expected to live past 5.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: On receiving this news, Megan's dad, John, fought with everything he had to save the life of his precious child.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: He founded a company to look for a cure and helped develop the drug that saved Megan's life.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Today she is 20 years old and a sophomore at Notre Dame.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Megan's story is about the unbounded power of a father's love for a daughter.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But our slow and burdensome approval process at the Food and Drug Administration keeps too many advances, like the one that saved Megan's life, from reaching those in need.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: If we slash the restraints, not just at the FDA but across our government, then we will be blessed with far more miracles just like Megan.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: In fact, our children will grow up in a nation of miracles.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But to achieve this future, we must enrich the mind - and the souls - of every American child.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Education is the civil rights issue of our time.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I am calling upon members of both parties to pass an education bill that funds school choice for disadvantaged youth, including millions of African-American and Latino children.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: These families should be free to choose the public, private, charter, magnet, religious or home school that is right for them.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Joining us tonight in the gallery is a remarkable woman, Denisha Merriweather.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: As a young girl, Denisha struggled in school and failed third grade twice.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But then she was able to enroll in a private center for learning - great learning center - with the help of a tax credit and a scholarship program.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Today, she is the first in her family to graduate, not just from high school, but from college.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Later this year, she will get her master's degree in social work.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We want all children to be able to break the cycle of poverty just like Denisha.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But to break the cycle of poverty, we must also break the cycle of violence.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The murder rate in 2015 experienced its largest single-year increase in nearly half a century.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: In Chicago, more than 4,000 people were shot last year alone, and the murder rate so far this year has been even higher.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: This is not acceptable in our society.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Every American child should be able to grow up in a safe community, to attend a great school and to have access to a high-paying job.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But to create this future, we must work with - not against - not against - the men and women of law enforcement.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We must build bridges of cooperation and trust, not drive the wedge of disunity and it's - really, it's what it is, division.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: It's pure, unadulterated division.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have to unify.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Police and sheriffs are members of our community.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: They're friends and neighbors, they're mothers and fathers, sons and daughters, and they leave behind loved ones every day who worry about whether or not they'll come home safe and sound.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We must support the incredible men and women of law enforcement.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And we must support the victims of crime.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I have ordered the Department of Homeland Security to create an office to serve American victims.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The office is called Voice, Victims of Immigration Crime Engagement.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We are providing a voice to those who have been ignored by our media and silenced by special interests.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Joining us in the audience tonight are four very brave Americans whose government failed them.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Their names are Jamiel Shaw, Susan Oliver, Jenna Oliver and Jessica Davis.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Jamiel's 17-year-old son was viciously murdered by an illegal immigrant gang member who had just been released from prison.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Jamiel Shaw Jr. was an incredible young man with unlimited potential who was getting ready to go to college, where he would have excelled as a great college quarterback.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But he never got the chance.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: His father, who is in the audience tonight, has become a very good friend of mine.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Jamiel, thank you.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thank you.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Also with us are Susan Oliver and Jessica Davis.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Their husbands - Deputy Sheriff Danny Oliver and Detective Michael Davis - were slain in the line of duty in California.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: They were pillars of their community.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: These brave men were viciously gunned down by an illegal immigrant with a criminal record and two prior deportations.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Should have never been in our country.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Sitting with Susan is her daughter, Jenna.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Jenna, I want you to know that your father was a hero and that tonight you have the love of an entire country supporting you and praying for you.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: To Jamiel, Jenna, Susan and Jessica, I want you to know that we will never stop fighting for justice.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Your loved ones will never, ever be forgotten.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We will always honor their memory.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Finally, to keep America safe, we must provide the men and women of the United States military with the tools they need to prevent war - if they must - they have to fight and they only have to win.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I am sending Congress a budget that rebuilds the military, eliminates the defense sequester and calls for one of the largest increases in national defense spending in American history.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: My budget will also increase funding for our veterans.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Our veterans have delivered for this nation, and now we must deliver for them.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The challenges we face as a nation are great.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But our people are even greater.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And none are greater or braver than those who fight for America in uniform.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We are blessed to be joined tonight by Carryn Owens, the widow of U.S.Navy special operator, Senior Chief William "Ryan" Owens.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Ryan died as he lived, a warrior and a hero, battling against terrorism and securing our nation.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I just spoke to our great General [Jim] Mattis just now who reconfirmed that, and I quote, "Ryan was a part of a highly successful raid that generated large amounts of vital intelligence that will lead to many more victories in the future against our enemy."

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Ryan's legacy is etched into eternity.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thank you.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And Ryan is looking down right now.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: You know that.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And he's very happy, because I think he just broke a record.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: For as the Bible teaches us, there is no greater act of love than to lay down one's life for one's friends.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Ryan laid down his life for his friends, for his country and for our freedom.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And we will never forget Ryan.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: To those allies who wonder what kind of a friend America will be, look no further than the heroes who wear our uniform.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Our foreign policy calls for a direct, robust and meaningful engagement with the world.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: It is American leadership based on vital security interests that we share with our allies all across the globe.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We strongly support NATO, an alliance forged through the bonds of two world wars, that dethroned fascism and a Cold War and defeated communism.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But our partners must meet their financial obligations.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And now, based on our very strong and frank discussions, they are beginning to do just that.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: In fact, I can tell you the money is pouring in.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Very nice.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We expect our partners, whether in NATO, in the Middle East or in the Pacific, to take a direct and meaningful role in both strategic and military operations, and pay their fair share of the cost - have to do that.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We will respect historic institutions, but we will respect the foreign rights of all nations.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And they have to respect our rights as a nation, also.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Free nations are the best vehicle for expressing the will of the people, and America respects the right of all nations to chart their own path.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: My job is not to represent the world.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: My job is to represent the United States of America.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But we know that America is better off when there is less conflict, not more.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We must learn from the mistakes of the past.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have seen the war and the destruction that have ravaged and raged throughout the world.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: All across the world.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The only long-term solution for these humanitarian disasters, in many cases, is to create the conditions where displaced persons can safely return home and begin the long, long process of rebuilding.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: America is willing to find new friends, and to forge new partnerships, where shared interests align.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We want harmony and stability, not war and conflict.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We want peace, wherever peace can be found.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: America is friends today with former enemies.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Some of our closest allies, decades ago, fought on the opposite side of these terrible, terrible wars.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: This history should give us all faith in the possibilities for a better world.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Hopefully, the 250th year for America will see a world that is more peaceful, more just, and more free.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: On our 100th anniversary in 1876, citizens from across our nation came to Philadelphia to celebrate America's centennial.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: At that celebration, the country's builders and artists and inventors showed off their wonderful creations.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Alexander Graham Bell displayed his telephone for the first time.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Remington unveiled the first typewriter.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: An early attempt was made at electric light.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thomas Edison showed an automatic telegraph and an electric pen.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Imagine the wonders our country could know in America's 250th year.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Think of the marvels we could achieve if we simply set free the dreams of our people.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Cures to the illnesses that have always plagued us are not too much to hope.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: American footprints on distant worlds are not too big a dream.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Millions lifted from welfare to work is not too much to expect.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And streets where mothers are safe from fear - schools where children learn in peace, and jobs where Americans prosper and grow - are not too much to ask.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: When we have all of this, we will have made America greater than ever before, for all Americans.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: This is our vision.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: This is our mission.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But we can only get there together.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We are one people, with one destiny.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We all bleed the same blood.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We all salute the same great American flag.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And we are all made by the same God.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: When we fulfill this vision, when we celebrate our 250 years of glorious freedom, we will look back on tonight as when this new chapter of American greatness began.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The time for small thinking is over.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The time for trivial fights is behind us.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We just need the courage to share the dreams that fill our hearts, the bravery to express the hopes that stir our souls, and the confidence to turn those hopes and those dreams into action.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: From now on, America will be empowered by our aspirations, not burdened by our fears, inspired by the future, not bound by failures of the past, and guided by a vision, not blinded by our doubts.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I am asking all citizens to embrace this renewal of the American spirit.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I am asking all members of Congress to join me in dreaming big and bold and daring things for our country.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I am asking everyone watching tonight to seize this moment.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Believe in yourselves.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Believe in your future.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And believe, once more, in America.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thank you, God bless you, and God bless the United States.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Mr. Speaker, Mr. Vice President, Members of Congress, the First Lady of the United States, and my fellow Americans:

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Less than one year has passed since I first stood at this podium, in this majestic chamber, to speak on behalf of the American people and to address their concerns, their hopes, and their dreams.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: That night, our new administration had already taken very swift action.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: A new tide of optimism was already sweeping across our land.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Each day since, we have gone forward with a clear vision and a righteous mission -- to make America great again for all Americans.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Over the last year, we have made incredible progress and achieved extraordinary success.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have faced challenges we expected, and others we could never have imagined.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have shared in the heights of victory and the pains of hardship.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We have endured floods and fires and storms.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But through it all, we have seen the beauty of America's soul, and the steel in America's spine.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Each test has forged new American heroes to remind us who we are, and show us what we can be.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We saw the volunteers of the Cajun Navy, racing to the rescue with their fishing boats to save people in the aftermath of a totally devastating hurricane.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We saw strangers shielding strangers from a hail of gunfire on the Las Vegas strip.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We heard tales of Americans like Coast Guard Petty Officer Ashlee Leppert, who is here tonight in the gallery with Melania.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Ashlee was aboard one of the first helicopters on the scene in Houston during the Hurricane Harvey.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Through 18 hours of wind and rain, Ashlee braved live power lines and deep water to help save more than 40 lives.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Ashlee, we all thank you.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thank you very much.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We heard about Americans like firefighter David Dahlberg.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: He's here with us also.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: David faced down walls of flame to rescue almost 60 children trapped at a California summer camp threatened by those devastating wildfires.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: To everyone still recovering in Texas, Florida, Louisiana, Puerto Rico, and the Virgin Islands -- everywhere -- we are with you, we love you, and we always will pull through together, always.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thank you to David and the brave people of California.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Thank you very much, David.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Great job.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Some trials over the past year touched this chamber very personally.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: With us tonight is one of the toughest people ever to serve in this House -- a guy who took a bullet, almost died, and was back to work three and a half months later: the legend from Louisiana, Congressman Steve Scalise.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: I think they like you, Steve.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: We are incredibly grateful for the heroic efforts of the Capitol Police officers, the Alexandria Police, and the doctors, nurses, and paramedics who saved his life and the lives of many others;

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: some in this room.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: In the aftermath -- (applause) -- yes.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Yes.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: In the aftermath of that terrible shooting, we came together, not as Republicans or Democrats, but as representatives of the people.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: But it is not enough to come together only in times of tragedy.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Tonight, I call upon all of us to set aside our differences, to seek out common ground, and to summon the unity we need to deliver for the people.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: This is really the key.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: These are the people we were elected to serve.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Over the last year, the world has seen what we always knew: that no people on Earth are so fearless, or daring, or determined as Americans.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: If there is a mountain, we climb it.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: If there is a frontier, we cross it.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: If there's a challenge, we tame it.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: If there's an opportunity, we seize it.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: So let's begin tonight by recognizing that the state of our Union is strong because our people are strong.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And together, we are building a safe, strong, and proud America.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Since the election, we have created 2.4 million new jobs, including -- (applause) -- including 200,000 new jobs in manufacturing alone.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Tremendous numbers.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: After years and years of wage stagnation, we are finally seeing rising wages.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Unemployment claims have hit a 45-year low.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: It's something I'm very proud of.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: African American unemployment stands at the lowest rate ever recorded.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And Hispanic American unemployment has also reached the lowest levels in history.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Small-business confidence is at an all-time high.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The stock market has smashed one record after another, gaining $8 trillion, and more, in value in just this short period of time.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The great news -- (applause) -- the great news for Americans' 401(k), retirement, pension, and college savings accounts have gone through the roof.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: And just as I promised the American people from this podium 11 months ago, we enacted the biggest tax cuts and reforms in American history.

speaker: Donald J. Trump
